body.text: riṅ ba yin te / de ni sgrib pa źes bya'o //
body.translated_text: [Tibetan] ...is long; that is called an obstruction. //

body.text:
rgyu gaṅ dag gis yoṅs su mya ṅan las 'da' ba'i chos can rnams yoṅs su mya ṅan las ma 'das pa'i rgyu ni bźi po de dag yin no // de dag kyaṅ gaṅ gi tshe saṅs rgyas 'byuṅ ba daṅ dam pa'i chos ṅan pa daṅ rjes su mthun pa'i gdams ṅag rjes su bstan pa rñed ciṅ rgyu de dag kyaṅ med par gyur pa, de'i tshe na dge ba'i rtsa ba dag yoṅs su smin ciṅ rim gyis yoṅs su mya ṅan las 'da' bar yaṅ
'gyur ro //
body.translated_text: [Tibetan] The causes by which those who have the nature to attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final liberation) have not yet attained it — those four are the causes. And when a <s>Buddha</s> arises and instructions concordant with the true <s>Dharma</s> are given, and those causes are also eliminated, then the roots of virtue ripen and one gradually attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. //

body.text: yoṅs su mya ṅan las mi 'da' ba'i chos can rnams ni ṅes pa'i tshogs la gnas pa yin pas / de dag ni rkyen rñed kyaṅ ruṅ ma rñed kyaṅ ruṅ ste / rnam pa thams cad kyi thams cad du yoṅs su mya ṅan las 'da' ba'i skal ba med pa kho na yin no //
body.translated_text: [Tibetan] Those who do not have the nature to attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> abide in the fixed group [of the wrong path]. Whether they encounter conditions or not, in every way and in all respects, they are simply without the fortune of <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. //

body.text:
(I)-A-II-4 Ms.-, Sh.-, W.*60-10, P.3b6, D.3b1, N.4b3, Co.3b2, Ch.396b7
de la yoṅs su mya ṅan las 'da' ba'i chos can rnams kyi gaṅ dag ma tshaṅ źiṅ med la ñe bar ma gyur na yoṅs su mya ṅan las mi 'da' ba'i rkyen rnams gaṅ źe na / smras pa / rkyen gñis te / gñis gaṅ źe na/ gtso bo daṅ dman pa'o //
body.translated_text: [Tibetan] Among those who have the nature to attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, what are the conditions whose absence and non-proximity prevent attainment? It is said: there are two conditions. What two? The principal and the secondary.

body.text:
(I)-A-II-4-a Ms.-, Sh.-, P.3b7, D.3b2, N.4b4, Co.3b3, Ch.396b10
rkyen gtso bo gaṅ źe na / smras pa / 'di lta ste / dam pa'i chos kyi dbaṅ du byas pa'i gźan gyi sgra daṅ / naṅ gi tshul bźin yid la byed pa'o //
body.translated_text: [Tibetan] What is the principal condition? It is said: namely, hearing the voice of another concerning the true <s>Dharma</s>, and internally, methodical attention (<s>yoniśo manasikāra</s>).

body.text:
(I)-A-II-4-b Ms.-, Sh.-, W.*60-28, P.3b8, D.3b2, N.4b5, Co.3b3, Ch.396b11
rkyen dman pa gaṅ źe na / smras pa / rkyen dman pa ni maṅ ste / 'di lta ste / ātmasampat, parasampat, kuśalo dharmacchandah, pravrajyā, śīlasaṃvaraḥ, indriyasaṃvaraḥ, bhojane mātrajñatā, pūrvarātrāpararātraṃ, jāgarikānuyogaḥ, saṃprajānadvihāritā, prāvivekyaṃ, nivaraṇaviśuddhiḥ, samādhisaṃniśrayaś ca //
body.translated_text: [Tibetan/Sanskrit] What is the secondary condition? It is said: the secondary conditions are many, namely: <s>ātmasampat</s> (personal endowment), <s>parasampat</s> (endowment from others), wholesome desire for the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>kuśalo dharmacchandaḥ</s>), going forth (<s>pravrajyā</s>), moral restraint (<s>śīlasaṃvaraḥ</s>), sense restraint (<s>indriyasaṃvaraḥ</s>), moderation in food (<s>bhojane mātrajñatā</s>), wakefulness in the first and last watches of the night (<s>pūrvarātrāpararātraṃ jāgarikānuyogaḥ</s>), dwelling with clear comprehension (<s>saṃprajānadvihāritā</s>), inclination to seclusion (<s>prāvivekyaṃ</s>), purification from hindrances (<s>nivaraṇaviśuddhiḥ</s>), and reliance on <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) (<s>samādhisaṃniśrayaḥ</s>). //

body.text:
(I)-A-II-4-b-(1) Ms.2a1L, Sh.5-3, W.*60-33, P.4a2, D.3b4, N.4b6, Co.3b5, Ch.396b15
de la bdag gi 'byor pa gaṅ źe na / mir gyur pa daṅ / yul dbus su skyes pa daṅ /] indriyair avikalatā, āyatanagataḥ prasādaḥ, aparivṛttakarmāntatā //
body.translated_text: [Tibetan/Sanskrit] What is personal endowment (<s>ātmasampat</s>)? Being born as a human, being born in a central land,] non-deficiency of the sense faculties (<s>indriyair avikalatā</s>), faith directed toward the [appropriate] domain (<s>āyatanagataḥ prasādaḥ</s>), and not having committed irreversible actions (<s>aparivṛttakarmāntatā</s>). //

body.text:
(I)-A-II-4-b-(1)-i Ms-2a1L, Sh.5-3, P.4a3, D.3b5, N.4b7, Co.3b6, Ch.396b17
tatra manuṣyatvaṃ katamat / yathāpīhaikatyo manuṣyāṇāṃ sabhāgatāyāṃ pratyājāto bhavati / puruṣaś ca puruṣendriyeṇa samanvāgataḥ strīś ca / idam ucyate manuṣyatvam //
body.translated_text: What is being human (<s>manuṣyatva</s>)? Here, a certain one is reborn in the common destiny of humans. And a man endowed with male faculties, and a woman — this is called being human (<s>manuṣyatva</s>). //

body.text:
(I)-A-II-4-b-(1)-ii Ms.2a1R, Sh.5-8, P.4a4, D.3b5, N.5a1, Co.3b6, Ch.396b19
āryāyatane pratyājātiḥ katamā / yathāpīhaikatyo madhyeṣu janapadeṣu pratyājāto bhavati, pūrvavad yāvad yatra gatiḥ satpuruṣāṇām / iyam ucyate āryāyatane pratyājātiḥ //
body.translated_text: What is rebirth in a noble domain (<s>āryāyatane pratyājāti</s>)? Here, a certain one is reborn in the central countries, as before, up to where virtuous persons go. This is called rebirth in a noble domain (<s>āryāyatane pratyājāti</s>). //

body.text:
(I)-A-II-4-b-(1)-iii Ms-2a2L, Sh.6-1, W.*60-33, P.4a5, D.3b6, N.5a2, Co.4a1, Ch.396b21
indriyair avikalatā katamā / yathāpīhaikatyo 'jaḍo bhavaty aneḍaka iti vistaraḥ / aṅgapratyaṅgāvikalo vā yadrūpeṇāṅgapratyaṅgāvaikalyena śrotrāvaikalyādikena bhavyaḥ kuśalapakṣasamudāgamāya / idam ucyate indriyāvaikalyam //
body.translated_text: What is non-deficiency of the sense faculties (<s>indriyair avikalatā</s>)? Here, a certain one is not dull, not deaf — thus in detail — or is not deficient in limbs and minor limbs, by whichever kind of deficiency of limbs and minor limbs, such as deficiency of hearing, one would be capable of accomplishing the wholesome side. This is called non-deficiency of the sense faculties (<s>indriyāvaikalya</s>). //

body.text:
(|)-A-II-4-b-(1)-iv Ms.2a3L, Sh.6-6, P.4a7, D.3b7, N.5a3, Co.4a2, Ch.396b25
āyatanagataḥ prasādaḥ katamaḥ / yathāpīhaikatyena tathāgatapravedite dharmavinaye śraddhā pratilabdhā bhavati cetasaḥ prasādaḥ / ayam ucyate āyatanagataḥ prasādaḥ / tatrāyatanaṃ tathāgatapravedito dharmavinayaḥ sarveṣāṃ laukikalokottarāṇāṃ śukladharmāṇām utpattaye / yā punar atra śraddhā tena pūrvaṅgamenādhipatyena sa āyatanagataḥ prasādaḥ / sarvakleśamalakaluṣyāpanayanat //
body.translated_text: What is faith directed toward the [appropriate] domain (<s>āyatanagataḥ prasādaḥ</s>)? Here, a certain one has obtained faith in the <s>Dharma</s>-<s>Vinaya</s> proclaimed by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, a serenity of mind. This is called faith directed toward the [appropriate] domain. Therein, the domain (<s>āyatana</s>) is the <s>Dharma</s>-<s>Vinaya</s> proclaimed by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, for the arising of all mundane and supramundane wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. And whatever faith exists therein — by that as forerunner and ruler, it is faith directed toward the [appropriate] domain, through the removal of all defilement, impurity, and turbidity. //

body.text:
(I)-A-II-4-b-(1)-v Ms.2a4L, Sh.6-13, W.*60-35, P.4b1, D.4a2, N.5a6, Co.4a5, Ch.396c2
aparivṛttakarmāntatā katamā/ yena pañcānām ānantaryāṇāṃ karmaṇāṃ, tadyathā mātṛvadhāt pitṛvadhād arhadvadhāt saṃghabhedāt tathāgatasyāntike duṣṭacittarudhirotpādād anyatamānyatamād ānantaryaṃ karma dṛṣṭa eva dharme na kṛtaṃ bhavati nādhyācaritam iyam ucyate 'parivṛttakarmāntateti / imāni pañcānantaryāṇi karmāṇi kṛtopacitāni dṛṣṭa eva dharme parivartyābhavyo bhavati parinirvāṇāyāryamārgasyotpattaye / tasmād etāni parivṛttakarmāntatety ucyate //
body.translated_text: What is not having committed irreversible actions (<s>aparivṛttakarmāntatā</s>)? When one has not committed or practiced in this very life any of the five actions of immediate retribution (<s>ānantarya karmas</s>), namely: matricide, patricide, killing an <s>arhat</s>, schism of the <s>saṅgha</s>, and maliciously causing blood to flow from the body of the <s>Tathāgata</s> — this is called not having committed irreversible actions. These five actions of immediate retribution, when committed and accumulated, make one incapable in this very life, having reversed [one's course], of attaining <s>parinirvāṇa</s> and the arising of the noble path. Therefore these are called 'irreversible action-limits.' //

body.text: svayam evānena sa ātmabhāva ebhiḥ pañcabhir aṅgaiḥ saṃpādito bhavati / tasmād ātmasaṃpad ity ucyate //
body.translated_text: By oneself alone has this personal existence been accomplished with these five factors. Therefore it is called personal endowment (<s>ātmasampat</s>). //

body.text:
(I)-A-II-4-b-(2) Ms.2a6L, Sh.7-1, W.*61-2, P.4b5, D.4a5, N.5b5, Co,4b1, Ch.396c9
parasampat katamā / tadyathā buddhānām utpādaḥ, saddharmadeśanā, deśitānāṃ dharmāṇām avasthānam, avasthitānāṃ ca dharmāṇām anupravartanam, parataś ca pratyanukampā //
body.translated_text: What is endowment from others (<s>parasampat</s>)? Namely: the arising of <s>Buddhas</s>, the teaching of the true <s>Dharma</s>, the persistence of the <s>dharmas</s> that have been taught, the continued transmission of the <s>dharmas</s> that persist, and compassion from others. //

body.text:
(I)-A-II-4-b-(2)-i Ms.2a6M, Sh.7-4, P.4b6, D.4a6, N.5b3, Co.4b2, Ch.396c11
tatra buddhānām utpādaḥ katamaḥ / yathāpīhaikatyaḥ sarvasattveṣu kalyāṇahitādhyāśayam utpādya prabhūtair duṣkarasahasrair mahatā ca puṇyajñānasambhāreṇa [bskal pa graṅs med pa gsum gyis tha maḥi lus phyi ma]-ātmabhāvapratilambhe bodhimaṇḍe niṣadya, pañca nivaraṇāni prahāya, caturṣu smṛtyupasthāneṣu sūpasthitacittaḥ, saptatriṃśadbodhipakṣyān dharmān bhāvayitvānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbudhyate / ayam ucyate buddhānām utpādaḥ / atītānāgatapratyutpanneṣv adhvasu evam eva [saṅs rgyas bcom ldan 'das thams cad de kho na bźin du 'byuṅ ba yin no //]
body.translated_text: What is the arising of <s>Buddhas</s>? Here, a certain one, having generated the aspiration for the welfare and benefit of all beings, through abundant thousands of difficult deeds and with a great accumulation of merit and knowledge, [after three incalculable aeons, in the last body] — upon attaining the personal existence, sitting at the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>), having abandoned the five hindrances (<s>nivaraṇas</s>), with mind well-established in the four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), having cultivated the thirty-seven factors conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣya dharmas</s>), fully awakens to unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). This is called the arising of <s>Buddhas</s>. In the past, future, and present times, [all Blessed Buddhas arise in exactly the same way. //]

body.text:
(I)-A-II-4-b-(2)-ii Ms-2a8L, Sh.7-12, P.5a2, D.4b2, N.5b5, Co.4b5, Ch.396c18
saddharmadeśanā katamā / ta evaṃ buddhā bhagavanto loka utpadya tasyaiva ca śrāvakā lokānukampām upādāya catvāry āryasatyāny ārabhya duḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgān dharmadeśanāṃ vartayanti, yad uta sūtrageyavyākaraṇagāthodānanidānāvadānetivṛttakajātakavaipulyādbhutadharmopadeśān / iyam ucyate saddharmasya deśanā / sadbhir ayaṃ dharmo niryāto deśitaḥ praśasto buddhaiś ca buddhaśravakaiś ca / [de'i phyir dam pa'i chos te / de bśad pa gaṅ yin pa des ni dam pa'i chos ston pa źes bya'o //]
body.translated_text: What is the teaching of the true <s>Dharma</s> (<s>saddharmadeśanā</s>)? Those very <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, having arisen in the world, and their disciples also, out of compassion for the world, beginning with the four noble truths (<s>āryasatyas</s>) — suffering, origination, cessation, and path — set in motion the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, namely: <s>sūtra</s>, <s>geya</s> (mixed prose and verse), <s>vyākaraṇa</s> (explanations), <s>gāthā</s> (verses), <s>udāna</s> (inspired utterances), <s>nidāna</s> (introductions), <s>avadāna</s> (legends), <s>itivṛttaka</s> (narratives of past events), <s>jātaka</s> (birth stories), <s>vaipulya</s> (extensive teachings), <s>adbhutadharma</s> (marvels), and <s>upadeśa</s> (instructions). This is called the teaching of the true <s>Dharma</s>. This <s>Dharma</s> has been brought forth and taught and praised by virtuous ones — by <s>Buddhas</s> and disciples of <s>Buddhas</s>. [Therefore it is the true Dharma; and the teaching of it is called the teaching of the true Dharma. //]

body.text:
(1)-A-II-4-b-(2)-iii Ms-2b1L, Sh.7-17, P.5a6, D.4b5, N.6a2, Co.5a1, Ch.396c27
deśitānāṃ dharmāṇām avasthānaṃ katamat / deśite saddharme pravartite dharmacakre yāvac ca buddho bhagavān jīvati tiṣṭhati ca parinirvṛte ca buddhe bhagavati yāvatā kālena pratipattir na hīyate saddharmaś ca nāntardhīyate / idam ucyate saddharmasyāvasthānaṃ / [gnas pa de yaṅ don dam pa'i chos mṅon sum du bya ba'i tshul gyis yin par rig par bya'o //]
body.translated_text: What is the persistence of the <s>dharmas</s> that have been taught (<s>deśitānāṃ dharmāṇām avasthānam</s>)? When the true <s>Dharma</s> has been taught and the wheel of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmacakra</s>) has been set in motion — as long as the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, lives and remains, and even after the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, for as long a time as the practice does not decline and the true <s>Dharma</s> does not disappear — this is called the persistence of the true <s>Dharma</s>. [This persistence is to be understood as being in the manner of direct realization of the ultimate Dharma. //]

body.text:
(I)-A-II-4-b-(2)-iv Ms.2b2L, Sh.8-5, P.5a8, D.4b7, N.6a4, Co.5a3, Ch.397a1
avasthitānāṃ dharmāṇām anupravartanaṃ katamat / yat ta evādhigantāraḥ saddharmasya saddharmasākṣātkriyāyai bhavyāṃ pratibalatāṃ janānāṃ viditvā yathādhigatām evānulomikīm avavādānuśāsanīm anupravartayanti / idam ucyate 'vasthitānāṃ dharmāṇām anupravartanam //
body.translated_text: What is the continued transmission of the <s>dharmas</s> that persist (<s>avasthitānāṃ dharmāṇām anupravartanam</s>)? When those very realizers of the true <s>Dharma</s>, having recognized the capability and capacity of beings for the direct realization of the true <s>Dharma</s>, continue to transmit instruction and counsel (<s>avavādānuśāsanī</s>) in accordance with what has been realized. This is called the continued transmission of the <s>dharmas</s> that persist. //

body.text:
(I)-A-II-4-b-(2)-v Ms.2b2R, Sh.8-10, P.5b2, D.5a1, N.6a5, Co.5a3, Ch.397a4
parataḥ pratyanukampā katamā / para ucyante dāyakadānapatayah te yāni tasyānulomikāni jīvitopakaraṇāni taiḥ pratyanukampante, yaduta (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 16

) robes (<s>cīvara</s>), almsfood (<s>piṇḍapāta</s>), lodging (<s>śayanāsana</s>), and medicines and provisions for the sick (<s>glānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāra</s>). This is called compassion from others (<s>parataḥ pratyanukampā</s>). //

body.translated_text: What is compassion from others (<s>parataḥ pratyanukampā</s>)? 'Others' refers to donors and benefactors (<s>dāyakadānapatayaḥ</s>). They show compassion with the requisites for living that are appropriate for that [monastic], namely:

body.text:
(I)-A-II-4-b-(3) Ms.2b3M, Sh.8-15, W.*61-8, P.5b4, D.5a2, N.6a5, Co.5a6, Ch.397a7
kuśalo dharmacchandaḥ katamaḥ / yathāpīhaikatyas tathāgatasya vā tathāgataśrāvakasya vāntikād dharmaṃ śrutvā śraddhāṃ pratilabhate / sa tāṃ pratilabhya, idaṃ pratisaṃśikṣate / "saṃbādho gṛhāvāso rajasām āvāsaḥ / abhyavakāśaṃ pravrajya yan nv ahaṃ sarvaṃ kaḍatravargaṃ dhanadhānyahiraṇyaṃ cotsṛjya svākhyāte dharmavinaye samyag evāgārād anagārikāṃ pravrajeyaṃ, pravrajitvā ca pratipattyā saṃpādayeyam" iti / ya eva samutpannaś chandaḥ kuśaleṣu dharmeṣu, ayam ucyate kuśalo dharmacchandaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is wholesome desire for the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>kuśalo dharmacchandaḥ</s>)? Here, a certain one, having heard the <s>Dharma</s> from the <s>Tathāgata</s> or from a disciple of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, obtains faith. Having obtained it, he reflects thus: "Household life is cramped, a dwelling-place of dust. Going forth is open. Let me abandon all possessions, wealth, grain, gold, and silver, and rightly go forth from home to homelessness in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s>-<s>Vinaya</s>, and having gone forth, accomplish [the goal] through practice." Whatever desire has arisen for wholesome <s>dharmas</s> — this is called wholesome desire for the <s>Dharma</s>. //

body.text:
(I)-A-II-4-b-(4) Ms.2b5L, Sh.9-4, W.*66-10, P.5b8, D.5a5, N.6b2, Co.5b2, Ch.397a14
pravrajyā katamā / yā tam eva kuśalaṃ dharmacchandam adhipatiṃ kṛtvā jñapticaturthena vā karmaṇopasaṃpac chrāmaṇeraśīlasamādānaṃ vā / iyam ucyate pravrajyā //
body.translated_text: What is going forth (<s>pravrajyā</s>)? Having made that very wholesome desire for the <s>Dharma</s> the dominant [motivation], either full ordination (<s>upasaṃpad</s>) through a formal act with a fourth motion, or the undertaking of the <s>śrāmaṇera</s> (novice) precepts. This is called going forth (<s>pravrajyā</s>). //

body.text:
(I)-A-II-4-b-(5) Ms.2b5M, Sh.9-8, W.*61-12, P.6a1, D.5a6, N.6b5, Co.5b3, Ch.397a16
śīlasaṃvaraḥ katamaḥ / sa tathā pravrajitaḥ śīlavān viharati, prātimokṣasaṃvarasaṃvṛtaḥ, ācāragocarasaṃpannaḥ, aṇumātreṣv avadyeṣu bhayadarśī, samādāya śikṣate śikṣāpadeṣu / ayam ucyate śīlasaṃvaraḥ //
body.translated_text: What is moral restraint (<s>śīlasaṃvaraḥ</s>)? Having thus gone forth, one dwells virtuous, restrained by the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint, endowed with proper conduct and resort, seeing danger in the slightest faults, undertaking and training in the training rules (<s>śikṣāpada</s>). This is called moral restraint (<s>śīlasaṃvaraḥ</s>). //

body.text:
(I)-A-II-4-b-(6) Ms.2b6L, Sh.9-13, W.*61-20, P.6a3, D.5a7, N.6b5, Co.5b5, Ch.397a19
indriyasaṃvaraḥ katamaḥ / sa tam eva śīlasaṃvaraṃ niśrityārakṣitasmṛtir bhavati nipakasmṛtiḥ smṛtyārakṣitamānasaḥ samāvasthāvacārakaḥ / sa cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi dṛṣṭvā na nimittagrāhī bhavati, nānuvyaṃjanagrāhī, yato 'dhikaraṇam asya pāpakā akuśalā dharmāś cittam anusraveyuḥ, teṣāṃ saṃvarāya (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 18

children.text: ) pratipadyate, rakṣati cakṣurindriyam, cakṣurindriyeṇa saṃvaram apadyate / sa śrotreṇa śabdān, ghrāṇena gandhān, jihvayā rasān, kāyena spraṣṭavyāni, manasā dharmān vijñāya na nimittagrāhī bhavati nānuvyaṃjanagrāhī, yato 'dhikaraṇam asya pāpakā akuśalā dharmāś cittam anusraveyuḥ, teṣāṃ saṃvarāya pratipadyate, rakṣati mana-indriyaṃ, mana-indriyeṇa saṃvaram āpadyate / ayam ucyate indriyasaṃvaraḥ //
children.translated_text: ) he undertakes [restraint], guards the eye-faculty, and exercises restraint with the eye-faculty. Having cognized sounds with the ear, odors with the nose, tastes with the tongue, tangible objects with the body, and <s>dharmas</s> (mental objects) with the mind, he does not grasp at the general sign nor at the secondary features. Since on account of which evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> would flow into his mind, he undertakes restraint against those, guards the mind-faculty, and exercises restraint with the mind-faculty. This is called <s>indriyasaṃvara</s> (sense-faculty restraint).

body.translated_text: What is sense restraint (<s>indriyasaṃvaraḥ</s>)? Relying on that very moral restraint, one has guarded mindfulness, vigilant mindfulness, with a mind guarded by mindfulness, one who maintains proper conduct. Having seen forms with the eye, one does not grasp at the general sign, does not grasp at the secondary features — [for] from that basis, evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> would flow into the mind — for the restraint of those,

body.text:
(I)-A-II-4-b-(7) Ms.2b8M, Sh.10-4, W.*62-7, P.6a8, D.5b4, N.7a2, Co.6a2, Ch.397b1
bhojane mātrajñatā katamā / sa tathā saṃvṛtendriyaḥ pratisaṃkhyāyāhāram āharati, na darpārthaṃ na madārthaṃ na maṇḍanārthaṃ na vibhūṣaṇārthaṃ, yāvad evāsya kāyasya sthitaye yāpanāyai jighatsoparataye brahmacaryānugrahāya iti / paurāṇāṃ ca vedanāṃ prahāsyāmi, navāṃ ca notpādayiṣyāmi / yātrā ca me bhaviṣyati balaṃ ca sukhaṃ cānavadyatā ca sparśavihāratā ca / iyam ucyate bhojane mātrajñatā //
body.translated_text: What is <s>bhojane mātrajñatā</s> (moderation in food)? He, with his faculties thus restrained, reflecting wisely partakes of food — not for the sake of pride, not for the sake of intoxication, not for the sake of adornment, not for the sake of beautification — but only for the maintenance and sustenance of this body, for the cessation of hunger, and for supporting the holy life, thinking: "I shall put an end to former feelings and not generate new ones. There shall be for me sustenance, strength, well-being, blamelessness, and comfortable dwelling." This is called moderation in food.

body.text:
(I)-A-II-4-b-(8) Ms.3a1M, Sh.10-11, W.*62-10, P.6b3, D.5b6, N.7a4, Co.6a5, Ch.397b7
pūrvarātrāpararātraṃ jāgarikānuyogaḥ katamaḥ / sa tathā bhojane mātrajño divā caṅkramaniṣadyābhyām āvaraṇīyebhyo dharmebhyaś cittaṃ pariśodhayati / sa rātryāḥ prathame yāme caṅkramaniṣadyābhyām āvaraṇīyebhyo dharmebhyaś cittaṃ pariśodhya, tato vihārān nirgamya bahir vihārasya pādau prakṣālya, dakṣiṇena pārśvena siṃhaśayyāṃ kalpayaty pāde pādam ādhāya, ālokasaṃjñī smṛtaḥ saṃprajānann utthānasaṃjñām eva manasikurvan, sa rātryāḥ paścime yāme laghu laghv eva prativibudhya, (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> I 20

children.text: ) caṅkramaniṣadyābhyām āvaraṇīyebhyo dharmebhyaś cittaṃ pariśodhayati. iyam ucyate pūrvarātrāpararātraṃ jāgarikānuyuktatā //
children.translated_text: ) he purifies his mind of obstructive <s>dharmas</s> by walking and sitting. This is called devotion to wakefulness in the first and last watches of the night.

body.translated_text: What is <s>pūrvarātrāpararātraṃ jāgarikānuyoga</s> (devotion to wakefulness in the first and last watches of the night)? He, being thus moderate in food, during the day purifies his mind of obstructive <s>dharmas</s> by walking and sitting. In the first watch of the night, having purified his mind of obstructive <s>dharmas</s> by walking and sitting, then going out from his dwelling, outside the dwelling he washes his feet and, lying down on his right side, prepares the lion's posture, placing foot upon foot, mindful of the perception of light, clearly comprehending, attending to the perception of rising. In the last watch of the night, rising lightly and quickly,

body.text:
(I)-A-II-4-b-(9) Ms.3a3M, Sh.11-10, W.*62-34, P.6b7, D.6a3, N.7b1, Co.6b2, Ch.397b16
saṃprajānadvihāritā katamā / sa tathā jāgarikānuyukto 'bhikramapratikrame saṃprajānadvihārī bhavati, ālokitavyavalokite saṃmiñjitaprasārite sāṃghāṭīcīvarapātradhāraṇe 'śitapītakhāditasvādite nidrāklamavinodane gate sthite niṣaṇṇe śayite jāgṛte bhāṣite tūṣṇīṃbhāve saṃprajānadvihārī bhavati / iyam ucyate saṃprajānadvihāritā //
body.translated_text: What is <s>saṃprajānadvihāritā</s> (dwelling in clear comprehension)? He, thus devoted to wakefulness, is one who dwells in clear comprehension in going forward and returning, in looking ahead and looking aside, in bending and stretching, in wearing the outer robe, robes, and carrying the bowl, in eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting, in dispelling drowsiness and fatigue, in walking, standing, sitting, lying down, being awake, speaking, and being silent — he dwells in clear comprehension. This is called dwelling in clear comprehension.

body.text:
(I)-A-II-4-b-(10) Ms.3a4M, Sh.12-4, W.*63-9, P.7a2, D.6a5, N.7b3, Co.6b4, Ch.397b22
prāvivekyaṃ katamat / sa ebhir dharmaiḥ parikarmabhūmiṃ śodhayitvā viviktāni śayanāsanāny adhyāvasaty araṇyāni vṛkṣamūlāni śūnyāgārāṇi parvatakandaragiriguhāpalālapuṃjābhyavakāśaśmaśānavanaprasthāni prāntāni śayanāsanāni / idam ucyate prāvivekyam //
body.translated_text: What is <s>prāvivekyam</s> (inclination toward seclusion)? He, having purified the preparatory ground with these <s>dharmas</s>, resorts to secluded dwellings — forests, the roots of trees, empty houses, mountain caves, gorges, grottoes, straw-heaps, open spaces, charnel grounds, forest plains — remote dwellings. This is called inclination toward seclusion.

body.text:
(I)-A-II-4-b-(11) Ms.3a5L, Sh.13-1, W.*63-11, P.7a4, D.6a7, N.7b5, Co.6b5, Ch.397b26
nivaraṇaviśuddhiḥ katamā / so 'raṇyagato vā vṛkṣamūlagato vā śūnyāgāragato vā pañcabhyo nivaraṇebhyaś cittaṃ viśodhayati, kāmacchandād vyāpādāt styānamiddhād auddhatyakaukṛtyād vicikitsāyāḥ / sa ebhyo nivaraṇebhyaś cittaṃ viśodhya vinivaraṇam samādhikalyatāyām avasthāpayati / iyam ucyate nivaraṇaviśuddhiḥ //
body.translated_text: What is <s>nīvaraṇaviśuddhi</s> (purification from the hindrances)? He, having gone to the forest, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty house, purifies his mind from the five hindrances: from sensual desire, from ill-will, from sloth-and-torpor, from restlessness-and-remorse, and from doubt. Having purified his mind from these hindrances, he establishes it, free from hindrances, in fitness for <s>samādhi</s> (concentration). This is called purification from the hindrances.

body.text:
(I)-A-II-4-b-(12)-(i),(ii),(iii),(iv) Ms.3a6L, Sh.14-1, W.*63-16, P.7a6, D.6b2, N.7b7, Co.6b7, Ch.397c2
samādhisaṃniśrayaḥ katamaḥ / sa pañca nivaraṇāni prahāya cetasa upakleśakarāṇi saṃkleśakarāṇi /
body.translated_text: What is <s>samādhisaṃniśraya</s> (the basis of concentration)? He, having abandoned the five hindrances, which cause mental corruption and defilement —

body.text: viviktaṃ kāmair viviktaṃ pāpakair akuśalair dharmaiḥ savitarkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ prītisukhaṃ prathamaṃ dhyānam upasaṃpadya viaharati /
body.translated_text: secluded from sensual desires, secluded from evil unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, accompanied by <s>vitarka</s> (initial thought) and <s>vicāra</s> (sustained thought), born of seclusion, with joy and happiness, he enters and dwells in the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation).

body.text: sa vitarkavicārāṇāṃ vyupaśamād adhyātmasaṃprasādāc cetasa ekotībhāvād avitarkam avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ prītisukhaṃ dvitīyaṃ dhyānam upasaṃpadya viharati /
body.translated_text: He, through the subsiding of <s>vitarka</s> (initial thought) and <s>vicāra</s> (sustained thought), with inner tranquility and unification of mind, without <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>, born of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), with joy and happiness, enters and dwells in the second <s>dhyāna</s>.

body.text: sa prīter virāgād upekṣako viharati smṛtaḥ saṃprajānan sukhaṃ ca kāyena pratisaṃvedayate yat tad āryā ācakṣate "upekṣakaḥ smṛtimān sukhavihārīti tṛtīyaṃ dhyānam upasaṃpadya viharati /
body.translated_text: He, with the fading away of joy, dwells equanimous, mindful and clearly comprehending, and experiences happiness with the body — that which the noble ones describe as "equanimous, mindful, dwelling in happiness" — he enters and dwells in the third <s>dhyāna</s>.

body.text: sa sukhasya ca prahāṇād duḥkhasya ca prahāṇāt pūrvam eva ca saumanasyadaurmanasyayor astaṃgamād aduḥkhāsukham upekṣāsmṛtipariśuddhaṃ caturthaṃ dhyānam upasaṃpadya viharati / ayam ucyate samādhisaṃniśrayaḥ //
body.translated_text: He, with the abandoning of happiness and suffering, and with the prior disappearance of elation and dejection, enters and dwells in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, which is neither-painful-nor-pleasant, purified by equanimity and mindfulness. This is called the basis of concentration.

body.text:
(I)-A-II' Ms.3a8R, Sh.15-10, W.'63-21, P.7b4, D.6b6, N.8a5, Co.7a6, Ch.397c11
so 'nayānupūrvyā-uttarottarān viśiṣṭān viśiṣṭatarān viśiṣṭatamān pratyayān ātmasampatpūrvān samādhisaṃniśrayaparyavasānān samudānayati / evaṃ pariśuddhe citte paryavadāte anaṃgaṇe vigatopakleśe ṛjubhūte karmaṇye sthite āniṃjyaprāpte, sacet catvāry āryasatyāny ārabhya teṣāṃ parijñāyai prahāṇāya sākṣātkriyāyai bhāvanāyai parato ghoṣam avavādānuśāsanīṃ labhate, evam asau bhavyo bhavati pratibalaś ca yogavihitasya manaskārasyotpādanāya tatpūrvikāyāś ca samyagdṛṣṭeḥ, yayā catvāry āryasatyāny abhisamāgacchati, vimuktiñ ca paripūrayati, nirupadhiśeṣe ca nirvāṇadhātau parinirvāti / tatra yā samyagdarśanam upādāya vimuktiparipūriḥ nirupadhiśeṣaparinirvāṇaṃ cāyaṃ gotrasamudāgamo veditavyaḥ / tatrātmasaṃpadam upādāya yāvat samādhisaṃniśrayo 'yaṃ hīnaḥ samudāgamapratyayo veditavyaḥ / tatra yaś catuḥsatyadeśanāvavādādhipateyaḥ parato ghoṣo yaś ca yoniśo manaskāraḥ, ayaṃ pradhānaḥ samudāgamapratyayo veditavyaḥ / idam ucyate gotravyavasthānam //
body.translated_text: He, by this sequential progression, brings about increasingly superior, more excellent, and most excellent conditions, preceded by personal attainment and culminating in the basis of concentration. Thus, when his mind is purified, cleansed, unblemished, free from defilement, straight, workable, stable, and having attained imperturbability — if, with regard to the four noble truths, he obtains from another the voice of instruction, exhortation, and guidance for their full understanding, abandonment, direct realization, and cultivation — then he becomes capable and competent to generate the yogically prescribed mental attention and, preceded by that, the right view by which he penetrates the four noble truths, fulfills liberation, and attains final <s>nirvāṇa</s> in the <s>nirvāṇa</s>-element without residue. Therein, the fulfillment of liberation based on right seeing and the final <s>nirvāṇa</s> without residue — this should be understood as the attainment of the <s>gotra</s> (spiritual lineage). Therein, based on personal attainment up to the basis of concentration — this should be understood as the lesser condition for the attainment. Therein, the voice of another consisting of the instruction on the four truths, and the wise mental attention — this should be understood as the chief condition for the attainment. This is called the determination of <s>gotra</s> (spiritual lineage).

body.text:
(I)-A-III Ms.3b3R, Sh.16-7, W.*63-36, P.8a4, D.7a5, N.8b4, Co.7b5, Ch.397c25
gotrasthasya pudgalasya katamāni liṅgāni / āha / yāny aparinirvāṇadharmakasya liṅgāni tadviparyayeṇa gotrasthasya pudgalasya liṅgāni veditavyāni //
body.translated_text: What are the signs of a person established in the <s>gotra</s> (spiritual lineage)? He says: Whatever are the signs of one who is not destined for <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final liberation) — by their opposite, the signs of a person established in the <s>gotra</s> should be understood.

body.text:
(I)-A-III' Ms.3b4M, Sh.16-11, P.8a5, D.7a6, N.8b5, Co.7b6, Ch.397c27
kāni punar aparinirvāṇadharmakaliṅgāni yaiḥ samanvāgato 'parinirvāṇadharmakaḥ pudgalaḥ "aparinirvāṇadharmako 'yam" iti vijñeyaḥ / āha / bahūny aparinirvāṇadharmakaliṅgāni pradeśamātraṃ tu nirdekṣyāmi //
body.translated_text: And what are the signs of one who is not destined for <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, by which a person so endowed is to be known as "this one is not destined for <s>parinirvāṇa</s>"? He says: The signs of one not destined for <s>parinirvāṇa</s> are many, but I shall indicate just a portion.

body.text:
(I)-A-IIl-a Ms.3b5L, Sh.16-15, P.8a7, D.7a7, N.8b6, Co.7b7, Ch.398a1
ihāparinirvāṇadharmakasya pudgalasyādita evālayatṛṣṇā sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā ca sarvabudhdhair āśrayasaṃniviṣṭā aprahāṇadharmiṇī bhavaty anutpīḍyā dūrāgatā pragāḍhasaṃniviṣṭā / idaṃ prathamam agotrasthasya pudgalasya liṅgam //
body.translated_text: Here, for a person not destined for <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, the <s>ālayatṛṣṇā</s> (craving for the substratum) is, from the very beginning, totally and in every way established in the ground of all <s>Buddhas</s>, with the nature of non-abandonment, indestructible, far-reaching, and deeply embedded. This is the first sign of a person not established in the <s>gotra</s>.

body.text:
(I)-A-IIl-b Ms.3b6L, Sh.16-19, P.8b1, D.7b2, N.9a1, Co.8a2, Ch.398a6
punar aparam agotrasthaḥ pudgalaḥ / anekaparyāyeṇa saṃsāradoṣān vicitrān prabhūtāṃś ca śrutvā, nirvāṇaguṇāṃś cānekaparyāyeṇa vicitrān prabhūtāṃś ca śrutvā, parīttam api prapañce saṃsāre doṣadarśanam ādīnavadarśanaṃ saṃvegamātrakaṃ notpāditavān atītam adhvānam upādāya, notpādayiṣyaty anāgatam adhvānam upādāya, notpādayati vartamānam adhvānam upādāya, parīttakalāmātrakam avaramātrakaṃ nirvāṇe tṛṣṇākṣaye virāge nirodhe guṇadarśanam anuśaṃsadarśanaṃ prasādamātrakam atītānāgatapratyutpannam adhvānam upādāya notpāditavān notpādayiṣyati notpādayati / idaṃ dvitīyam agotrasthaṃ liṅgam //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, a person not established in the <s>gotra</s>, having heard in many ways the manifold and abundant faults of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), and having heard in many ways the manifold and abundant qualities of <s>nirvāṇa</s> — has not generated, taking into account past time, even the slightest perception of danger, perception of disadvantage, or mere feeling of urgency regarding <s>prapañca</s> (conceptual proliferation) and <s>saṃsāra</s>; will not generate it, taking into account future time; and does not generate it, taking into account present time; and has not generated, will not generate, and does not generate, taking into account past, future, and present time, even a slight, minimal, lowest perception of quality, perception of benefit, or mere feeling of confidence toward <s>nirvāṇa</s>, the destruction of craving, dispassion, and cessation. This is the second sign of one not established in the <s>gotra</s>.

body.text:
(I)-A-IIl-c Ms.3b7R, Sh.17-9, P.8b4, D.7b5, N.9a4, Co.8a6, Ch.398a17
punar aparam agotrasthaḥ pudgalaḥ / ādita evādhimātreṇāhrikyānapatrāpyeṇa samanvāgato bhavati / yenāyam aghṛṇacittaś cāsaṃkucitacittaś ca prahṛṣṭacittaś ca sarvaṃ pāpam adhyācarati / na ca kadācit tan nidānaṃ vipratisārī bhavati / [gźi des tshe 'di'i zaṅ ziṅ daṅ bcas pa'i bdag ñid ñams pa kho na tsam du mthoṅ bar zad de /] idaṃ tṛtīyam agotrasthaṃ liṅgam //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, a person not established in the <s>gotra</s> is, from the very beginning, endowed with intense shamelessness and lack of moral conscience, by which, with a callous mind, an unshrinking mind, and an elated mind, one commits every evil — and never on account of that does one feel remorse. This is the third sign of one not established in the <s>gotra</s>.

body.text:
(I)-A-IIl-d Ms.4a1L, Sh.17-14, P.8b7, D.7b6, N.9a5, Co.8b1, Ch.398a23
punar aparam agotrasthaḥ pudgalaḥ / sarvākāraparipūrṇe sphuṭe yukte citre gamake duḥkhaṃ vārabhya samudayaṃ vā nirodhaṃ vā mārgaṃ vā saddharme deśyamāne na labhate cetasa āvarjanamātrakam adhimuktimātrakaṃ ca / [spu ziṅ źes byed pa'am / mchi ma bkrug ces byed pa thob par gyur pa lta ci smos te /] atītānāgatapratyutpannam adhvānam upādāya / idaṃ caturtham agotrasthaṃ liṅgam //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, a person not established in the <s>gotra</s>, when the true <s>Dharma</s> is being taught — complete in every aspect, clear, cogent, vivid, and eloquent — concerning <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering), or <s>samudaya</s> (its origin), or <s>nirodha</s> (cessation), or <s>mārga</s> (the path), does not attain even the slightest turning of mind or even the slightest inclination, taking into account past, future, and present time. This is the fourth sign of one not established in the <s>gotra</s>.

body.text:
(I)-A-IIl-e Ms.4a2M, Sh.18-7, P.9a2, D.8a1, N.9b1, Co.8b3, Ch.398b1
punar aparam agotrasthaḥ pudgalaḥ / sacet kadācit karhicit svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajati, sa rājābhinirṇīto vā, corābhinirṇīto vā, ṛṇārto vā bhayārto vājīvikābhayabhīto vā, nātmadamāya, nātmaśamāya, nātmaparinirvāṇāya, (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> I 28

children.text: ) na śrāmaṇyāya, na brāhmaṇyāya, tathā pravarjito 'pi sārdhaṃ gṛhasthapravarjitaiḥ sthitaḥ, praṇidhāya brahmacaryaṃ carati, "devo vā syāṃ devānyataro ve"ti, śikṣāṃ vā pratyākhyāya prahāṇāya varttate / duḥśīlo vā bhavaty antaḥpūtir avasrutaḥ kaśaṃbakajātaḥ śaṃkhasvarasamācāraḥ, aśramaṇaḥ śramaṇapratijñaḥ, abrahmacārī brahmacāripratijñaḥ. atītānāgatapratyutpanneṣv adhvasv agotrasthasya pudgalasyaivam eva pravrajyā veditavyā / na cāśikṣākāmasya pudgalasya pravrajyopasaṃpadbhikṣubhāvaḥ / tad anena paryāyeṇānenābhisandhinārthato [rab tu byuṅ ba ma yin gyi rab tu byuṅ ba'i rtags daṅ cha lugs 'dzin pa tsam gyis rab tu byuṅ ba] iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati / idaṃ pañcamam agotrasthasya pudgalasya liṅgam //
children.translated_text: ) not for <s>śrāmaṇya</s> (the ascetic life), not for <s>brāhmaṇya</s> (the brahminical life). Even having gone forth thus, he remains together with householders and those who have gone forth, and conducts the holy life with an aspiration: "May I become a god or some kind of deity." Or he tends toward giving up the training and abandoning it. Or he becomes immoral, inwardly rotten, corrupt, having the nature of chaff, with conduct like the sound of a conch shell — not an ascetic though professing to be one, not a celibate though professing celibacy. Taking into account past, future, and present time, the going forth of a person not established in the <s>gotra</s> should be understood in just this way. And there is no going forth, full ordination, or <s>bhikṣu</s>-status for one who does not wish to train. By this method, with this intention, in this meaning, one is reckoned as "gone forth" merely by assuming the marks and appearance of one gone forth, without actually being gone forth. This is the fifth sign of a person not established in the <s>gotra</s>.

body.translated_text: Furthermore, a person not established in the <s>gotra</s>, if at any time whatsoever he goes forth in the well-taught <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> (discipline), he has gone forth because he was impelled by a king, or impelled by a thief, or oppressed by debt, or afflicted by fear, or fearing for his livelihood — not for the purpose of self-taming, not for self-pacification, not for one's own <s>parinirvāṇa</s>,

body.text:
(I)-A-IIl-f Ms.4a4M, Sh.18-17, P.9b2, D.8a7, N.9b7, Co.9a3, Ch.398b18
punar aparam agotrasthaḥ pudgalaḥ / yat kiṃcit kuśalaṃ karma karoti kāyena vācā manasā vā, tat sarvaṃ bhavābhiprāyo vā viśiṣṭam āyatipunarbhavam abhiprārthayamānaḥ, bhogābhiprāyo vā viśiṣṭaṃ bhogam abhiprārthayamāno karoti / idaṃ saṣṭham agotrasthasya pudgalasya liṅgam //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, a person not established in the spiritual lineage (<s>agotra</s>): whatever wholesome <s>karma</s> he performs by body, speech, or mind, he performs all of it either with the intention directed toward [continued] existence, aspiring for a superior future rebirth, or with the intention directed toward enjoyments, aspiring for superior enjoyments. This is the sixth mark of a person not established in the spiritual lineage.

body.text: evaṃbhāgīyāni cāsya bahūni liṅgāni saṃvidyante yaiḥ samanvāgato 'parinirvāṇadharmako 'parinirvāṇadharmaka iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati //
body.translated_text: And there exist many marks of this kind, endowed with which one comes to be reckoned as 'one whose nature is not to attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, one whose nature is not to attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.'

body.text:
(I)-A-IV Ms.4a5M, Sh. 19-7, W.*64-6, P.9b5, D.8b3, N. 10a2, Co.9a5, Ch.398b25
tatra katame gotrasthāḥ pudgalāḥ / āha / asti gotrasthaḥ pudgalaḥ / gotra eva sthito nāvatīrṇo na niṣkrāntaḥ, gotrastho 'vatīrṇo na niṣkrāntaḥ, gotrastho 'vatīrṇo niṣkrāntaḥ, mṛdvindriyaḥ, madhyendriyaḥ, tīkṣṇendriyaḥ, rāgacaritaḥ, (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 30

children.text: ) dveṣacaritaḥ, mohacaritaḥ, akṣaṇyopapannaḥ, kṣaṇyopapannaḥ, pramattaḥ, apramattaḥ, mithyāpratipannaḥ, amithyāpratipannaḥ āvṛtaḥ, anāvṛtaḥ, dūre, antike, paripakvaś cāparipakvaś ca, viśuddhaś cāviśuddhaś ca //
children.translated_text: ) one of aversion-temperament (<s>dveṣacarita</s>); one of delusion-temperament (<s>mohacarita</s>); one born in an unfavorable state (<s>akṣaṇyopapanna</s>); one born in a favorable state (<s>kṣaṇyopapanna</s>); one who is heedless (<s>pramatta</s>); one who is heedful (<s>apramatta</s>); one who is wrongly directed (<s>mithyāpratipanna</s>); one who is not wrongly directed (<s>amithyāpratipanna</s>); one who is obstructed (<s>āvṛta</s>); one who is unobstructed (<s>anāvṛta</s>); one who is far; one who is near; one who is matured and one who is not matured; and one who is purified and one who is not purified.

body.translated_text: Therein, what are the persons established in the spiritual lineage (<s>gotrastha</s>)? It is said: There is a person established in the lineage who is merely established in the lineage, not yet entered and not yet set forth; one established in the lineage who has entered but not yet set forth; one established in the lineage who has entered and set forth; one of soft faculties (<s>mṛdvindriya</s>); one of middling faculties (<s>madhyendriya</s>); one of sharp faculties (<s>tīkṣṇendriya</s>); one of passion-temperament (<s>rāgacarita</s>);

body.text:
(I)-A-IV-a Ms.(4a7L), Sh.19-15, P.10a1, D.8b6, N.10a6, Co.9b2, Ch.398c4
tatra katamo gotrasthaḥ pudgalo gotra eva sthito nāvatīrṇo na niṣkrāntaḥ / yathāpīhaikatyaḥ pudgalo lokottaradharmabījaiḥ samanvāgato bhavati / na ca punar adyāpi labhate satpuruṣasaṃsevāṃ vāgamya saddharmaśravaṇaṃ vā tathāgatapravedite dharmavinaye śraddhāṃ, na śīlaṃ samādadāti, na śrutam udgṛhṇāti, na tyāgaṃ bṛṃhayati, na dṛṣṭim ṛjūkaroti / ayaṃ gotra eva sthito nāvatīrṇo na niṣkrāntaḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is a person established in the lineage who is merely established in the lineage, not yet entered and not yet set forth? It is like this: here a certain person is endowed with the seeds of supramundane <s>dharmas</s>, yet he has not up to now obtained the association with a true person (<s>satpuruṣa</s>), nor the hearing of the true <s>Dharma</s> (<s>saddharma</s>), nor faith in the <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> proclaimed by the <s>Tathāgata</s>; he does not undertake moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), does not take up learning (<s>śruta</s>), does not cultivate generosity (<s>tyāga</s>), does not straighten his views (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>). This one is merely established in the lineage, not yet entered, not yet set forth.

body.text:
(I)-A-IV-b Ms.(4b1L), Sh.19-22, P.10a4, D.9a1, N.10b1, Co.9b4, Ch.398c11
katamo gotrastho 'vatīrṇo na niṣkrāntaḥ / [sṅar bśad pa'i nag po'i phyogs las] viparyayeṇa śuklapakṣeṇa gotrasthaś cāvatīrṇaś ca veditavyaḥ / ayaṃ tu viśeṣo no tu lābhī bhavaty āryamārgasya tatphalasya ca kleśavisaṃyogasya //
body.translated_text: What is one established in the lineage who has entered but not yet set forth? By the reverse of [what was previously described as the dark side], through the bright side (<s>śuklapakṣa</s>), one established in the lineage who has entered should be understood. But this is the distinction: he has not yet obtained the noble path (<s>āryamārga</s>), its fruit, and the separation from afflictions (<s>kleśavisaṃyoga</s>).

body.text:
(I)-A-IV-c Ms.4b1M, Sh.20-4, P.10a6, D.9a2, N.10b2, Co.9b5, Ch.398c15
katamo gotrasthaś cāvatīrṇaś ca niṣkrāntaś ca / etad evoktvāyaṃ viśeṣo lābhī bhavaty āryamārgasya tatphalasya ca kleśavisaṃyogasya //
body.translated_text: What is one established in the lineage who has both entered and set forth? Having stated just this, the distinction is: he has obtained the noble path (<s>āryamārga</s>), its fruit, and the separation from afflictions (<s>kleśavisaṃyoga</s>).

body.text:
(I)-A-IV-d Ms.(4b2L), Sh.20-7, P.10a7, D.9a3, N.10b3, Co.9b6, Ch.398c17
tatra mṛdvindriyaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / yasya pudgalasya jñeye vastuny (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 32

children.text: ) ālambane 'tyarthaṃ dhandhavāhīnīndriyaṇi bhavanti mandavahīni vā śrutamayena vā cintāmayena vā bhāvanāmayena vā manasikāreṇa saṃprayuktāni, yaduta śraddhā vīryaṃ smṛtiḥ samādhiḥ prajñā vā na samarthāni na pratibalāni dharmasya vā prativedhāyārthasya vāśu ca prativedhāya tattvasya / ayam ucyate mṛdvindriyaḥ pudgalaḥ //
children.translated_text: with respect to the knowable object, thing, and referent are extremely slow-moving, dull-moving — whether conjoined with attention born from hearing (<s>śrutamaya</s>), from reflection (<s>cintāmaya</s>), or from cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmaya</s>) — namely faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>), concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) — they are not capable, not competent for the penetration of the <s>Dharma</s>, of the meaning, or for the swift penetration of reality (<s>tattva</s>). This is called a person of soft faculties.

body.translated_text: Therein, what is a person of soft faculties (<s>mṛdvindriya</s>)? That person whose faculties

body.text:
(I)-A-IV-e Ms.4b3L, Sh.20-15, P.10b1, D.9a5, N.10b5, Co.10a1, Ch.398c23
tatra madhyendriyaḥ katamaḥ / yasya nātyarthaṃ jñeye vastuny ālambane dhandavāhīnīndriyāṇīti sarvaṃ pūrvavad vistareṇa vaktavyam / ayam ucyate madhyendriyaḥ pudgalaḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is one of middling faculties (<s>madhyendriya</s>)? One whose faculties with respect to the knowable object, thing, and referent are not extremely slow-moving — all the rest should be stated in full as before. This is called a person of middling faculties.

body.text:
(I)-A-IV-f Ms.4b3M, Sh.20-18, P.10b3, D.9a5, N.10b6, Co.10a2, Ch.398c26
tīkṣṇendriyaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / yasya pudgalasya jñeye vastuny ālambane 'dhandhavāhīnīndriyāṇi bhavanty amandavāhīni, śrutamayena vā cintāmayena vā bhāvanāmayena vā manasikāreṇa saṃprayuktāni, yaduta śraddhā viryaṃ smṛtiḥ samādhiḥ prajñā vā śaktāni bhavanti dharmasya prativedhāyārthasya vāśu ca prativedhāya tattvasya / ayam ucyate tīkṣṇendriyaḥ pudgalaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is a person of sharp faculties (<s>tīkṣṇendriya</s>)? That person whose faculties with respect to the knowable object, thing, and referent are not slow-moving and not dull-moving — whether conjoined with attention born from hearing (<s>śrutamaya</s>), from reflection (<s>cintāmaya</s>), or from cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmaya</s>) — namely faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>), concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) — they are capable for the penetration of the <s>Dharma</s>, of the meaning, and for the swift penetration of reality (<s>tattva</s>). This is called a person of sharp faculties.

body.text:
(I)-A-IV-g Ms.4b4M, Sh.21-6, P.10b5, D.9a7, N.11a1, Co.10a4, Ch.399a3
rāgacaritaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / yo raṃjanīya ālambane tīvrarāgaś ca bhavaty āyatarāgaś ca / ayam ucyate rāgacaritaḥ pudgalaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is a person of passion-temperament (<s>rāgacarita</s>)? One who, with respect to an attractive object, has intense passion and extended passion. This is called a person of passion-temperament.

body.text: (I)-A-IV-h Ms.4b5L, Sh.21-6, P.10b7, D.9b1, N.11a2, Co.10a5, Ch.399a3 dveṣacaritaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / yaḥ dūṣaṇīye pratighasthānīya ālambane (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 34

children.text:
)
tīvradveṣaś ca bhavaty āyatadveṣaś ca / ayam ucyate dveṣacaritaḥ pudgalaḥ //
children.translated_text: has intense aversion and extended aversion. This is called a person of aversion-temperament.

body.translated_text: What is a person of aversion-temperament (<s>dveṣacarita</s>)? One who, with respect to an offensive, repugnant object,

body.text:
(I)-A-IV-i Ms.4b5M, Sh.21-12, P.10b7, D.9b2, N.11a2, Co.10a6, Ch.399a8
mohacaritaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / yo jñeye vastuni tīvramohaś ca bhavaty āyatamohaś ca / ayam ucyate mohacaritaḥ pudgalaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is a person of delusion-temperament (<s>mohacarita</s>)? One who, with respect to a knowable thing, has intense delusion and extended delusion. This is called a person of delusion-temperament.

body.text:
(I)-A-IV-j,k,l,m,n,o,p,q Ms.4b5R, Sh.21-15, P.10b8, D.9b3, N.11a2, Co.10a7, Ch.399a11
akṣaṇyopapannapramattamithyāpratipannāvṛtāḥ pūrvavad veditavyāḥ / tadviparyayeṇa kṣaṇyopapannāpramattāmithyāpratipannānāvṛtā veditavyāḥ //
body.translated_text: Those born in unfavorable states, the heedless, the wrongly directed, and the obstructed should be understood as before. By the reverse of those, those born in favorable states, the heedful, the not wrongly directed, and the unobstructed should be understood.

body.text:
(I)-A-IV-r-(1),-(2) Ms.4b6M, Sh.21-18, P.11a2, D.9b4, N.11a3, Co.10b1, Ch.399a14
dūre pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / asti pudgalaḥ kāladūratayā nirvāṇasya dūre, asti prayogadūratayā /
body.translated_text: What is a person who is far? There is a person who is far from <s>nirvāṇa</s> by distance of time; there is one who is far by distance of practice.

body.text: tatra katamaḥ kāladūratayā dūre / anekair jātiśatair anekair jātisahasrair anekair jātiśatasahasrais tataḥ paścād bhavyo [gdod rkyen rñed nas yoṅs su mya ṅan las 'da' ba'i skal pa yod par 'gyur ro /]
body.translated_text: Therein, what is one who is far by distance of time? One who will become capable [of obtaining conditions and attaining parinirvāṇa] only after many hundreds of births, many thousands of births, many hundreds of thousands of births.

body.text: katamaḥ prayogadūratayā dūre / pudgalo gotra eva kevale sthito bhavati nāvatīrṇaḥ, sa bhavyo bhavaty āśu pratyayalābhāya parinirvāṇāya / sa nirvāṇāyānārabdhaprayogatvāt prayogadūratayā dūre na kāladūratayā / ayam ucyate dūre pudgalaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is one who is far by distance of practice? A person who is merely established in the lineage alone, not yet entered — he may be capable of swiftly obtaining conditions and attaining <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. But because he has not yet begun his practice toward <s>nirvāṇa</s>, he is far by distance of practice, not by distance of time. This is called a person who is far.

body.text:
(1)-A-IV-s-(1),-(2) Ms.4b7R, Sh.22-7, P.11a7, D.9b7, N.11b1, Co.10b4, Ch.399a25
āsanne pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / gaṅ zag dus thag ñe bas mya ṅan las 'da' ba (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 36

children.text: ) thag ñe ba yaṅ yod do // sbyor ba thag ñe bas mya ṅan las 'da' ba thag ñe ba yaṅ yod do //
children.translated_text: [by nearness of time, and a person near to nirvāṇa by nearness of practice.]

body.translated_text: What is a person who is near? [A person who is near nirvāṇa]

body.text: de la dus thag ñe bas mya ṅan las 'da' ba thag ñe ba gaṅ źe na / lus daṅ gnas kyi dṅos po tha ma la gnas śiṅ de lus de ñid kyis yoṅs su mya ṅan las 'da' bar byed pa daṅ / skad cig de la bar chad med par ñon moṅs pa spoṅ pa mṅon sum du byed pa gaṅ yin pa ste / de ni dus thag ñe bas mya ṅan las 'da' ba thag ñe ba yin no //
body.translated_text: [Therein, what is one near to nirvāṇa by nearness of time? One who abides in the last state of body and existence, and who with that very body will attain parinirvāṇa, and who at that moment without interruption directly realizes the abandonment of afflictions — this is one near to nirvāṇa by nearness of time.]

body.text: sbyor ba thag ñe bas mya ṅan las 'da' ba thag ñe ba gaṅ źe na / de ni rigs la gnas śiṅ źugs pa gaṅ yin pa ste / de dag gcig tu bsdus pa ni gaṅ zag thag ñe ba źes bya'o //
body.translated_text: [What is one near to nirvāṇa by nearness of practice? One who is established in the lineage and has entered — these, taken together, are called a person who is near.]

body.text:
(I)-A-IV-t Ms.-, Sh.-, P.11b2, D.10a3, N.11b4, Co.10b7, Ch.399b5
aparipakvaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / gaṅ zag gaṅ la gnas nas yoṅs su mya ṅan las 'da' ba daṅ yaṅ dag pa ñid du ṅes pa la 'jug par 'gyur ba'i tha ma'i lus phyi ma ma thob pa gaṅ yin pa ste / ayam ucyate 'paripakvaḥ pudgalaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is a person who is not matured (<s>aparipakva</s>)? [A person who has not yet obtained the last future body, abiding in which one will attain parinirvāṇa and enter into true certainty.] This is called a person who is not matured.

body.text:
(I)-A-IV-u Ms.-, Sh.-, P.11b3, D.10a4, N.11b5, Co.11a1, Ch.399b8
paripakvaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / gaṅ zag gaṅ la gnas nas yoṅs su mya ṅan las 'da' ba daṅ yaṅ dag pa ñid du ṅes pa la 'jug par 'gyur ba'i tha ma'i lus phyi ma thob pa gaṅ yin pa ste / ayam ucyate paripakvaḥ pudgalaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is a person who is matured (<s>paripakva</s>)? [A person who has obtained the last future body, abiding in which one will attain parinirvāṇa and enter into true certainty.] This is called a person who is matured.

body.text:
(I)-A-IV-v Ms.-,Sh.-,P.11b4, D.10a4, N.11b6, Co.11a2, Ch.399b11
aviśuddhaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / gaṅ zag 'phags pa'i lam ma bskyed ciṅ, de'i 'bras bu ñon moṅs pa daṅ bral ba mṅon sum du ma byas pa gaṅ yin pa ste / ayam ucyate 'viśuddhaḥ pudgalaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is a person who is not purified (<s>aviśuddha</s>)? [A person who has not generated the noble path, and who has not directly realized the separation from afflictions that is its fruit.] This is called a person who is not purified.

body.text:
(I)-A-IV-w Ms.-,Sh.-,P.11b5, D.10a5, N.11b6, Co.11a3, Ch.399b13 ḷ
viśuddhaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / de las bzlog pa yin par rig par bya'o //
body.translated_text: What is a person who is purified (<s>viśuddha</s>)? [One should understand it as the reverse of that.]

body.text: de dag ni rigs la gnas pa'i gaṅ zag rnams śes bya ste / 'di lta ste / ma źugs pa rnams gźug par bya ba daṅ / yoṅs su ma smin par rnams yoṅs su smin par (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 38

children.text: ) bya ba daṅ / rnam par ma dag pa rnams rnam par dag par bya ba gaṅ dag gi don du saṅs rgyas bcom ldan 'das rnams 'jig rten du byuṅ źiṅ / chos kyi 'khor lo dag bskor bar mdzad pa daṅ / bslab pa'i gźi rnams 'cha' bar mdzad pa dag yin no //
children.translated_text: those not yet matured who are to be caused to mature, and those not yet purified who are to be caused to become purified — for the sake of whom the Blessed Buddhas arise in the world, turn the wheels of Dharma, and establish the bases of training.]

body.translated_text: [These are to be known as persons established in the spiritual lineage — namely: those not yet entered who are to be caused to enter,

body.text: (bar gyi sdom ni /
body.translated_text: (Intermediate summary verse:

body.text: raṅ bźin daṅ ni de rnams gźag // rtags rnams daṅ ni gaṅ zag dag //
body.translated_text: The nature and the establishment of those, the marks and the persons —

body.text: de dag thams cad mdor bsdus te // rigs kyi sar ni śes par bya //)
body.translated_text: all of these, condensed, are to be known as the stage of the spiritual lineage.)

body.text: ñan thos kyi sa las rigs kyi sa rdzogs so // //
body.translated_text: From the Śrāvakabhūmi, the stage of the spiritual lineage (<s>gotrabhūmi</s>) is complete.

body.text:
(I)-B Ms.-, Sh.-, W.*65-1, P.12a1, D.10b1, N.12a2, Co.11a6, Ch.399b19
[de la 'jug pa'i sa gaṅ źe na / smras pa / yaś cāyam avatārasya svabhāvo yac ca vyavasthānaṃ yāni cemāny avatīrṇānāṃ liṅgāni ye ceme 'vatīrṇāḥ pudgalās tat sarvam abhisaṃkṣipyāvatārabhūmir ity ucyate //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the stage of entry (<s>avatārabhūmi</s>)? It is said: Whatever is the nature of entry, and whatever is the establishment [thereof], and whatever are the marks of those who have entered, and whatever are the persons who have entered — all of this, taken together, is called the stage of entry.

body.text:
(I)-B-I Ms.-, Sh.-, P.12a2, D.10b2, N.12a3, Co.11a7, Ch.399b27
de la 'jug pa'i raṅ bźin gaṅ źe na / 'di la rigs la gnas pa'i gaṅ zag mya ṅan las 'da' ba'i sa bon gyi chos daṅ ldan pa de ni / gaṅ gi tshe saṅs rgyas 'byuṅ ba yod ciṅ yul dbus kyi mi rkun ma ma yin pa dag daṅ kla klo ma yin pa rnams su rgyas par sṅa ma bźin du skyes par gyur na / daṅ po kho nar saṅs rgyas rnams daṅ saṅs rgyas kyi ñan thos rnams la blta ba daṅ druṅ du 'gro ba daṅ bsñen bkur bya ba rñed par 'gyur źiṅ / de dag las chos thos nas daṅ por dad pa thob pa daṅ tshul khrims yaṅ dag par len pa daṅ thos pa 'dzin pa daṅ gtoṅ ba spel ba daṅ lta ba sbyoṅ bar byed do //
body.translated_text: [Therein, what is the nature of entry? Here, a person established in the spiritual lineage, possessing the quality of the seed of nirvāṇa — when there exists the arising of a Buddha, and when he is born among humans in the central lands, not as a thief and not as a barbarian, in full [as before] — at the very outset he obtains seeing, approaching, and attending upon the Buddhas and the disciples of the Buddhas, and having heard the Dharma from them, he first obtains faith, undertakes moral conduct, takes up learning, cultivates generosity, and straightens his views.]

body.text: de'i 'og tu chos yaṅ dag par blaṅs pa'i rgyu de daṅ rkyen des / lus źig ciṅ tshe de yaṅ dag par 'das nas kyaṅ / rnam par smin pa'i skye mched drug gis zin pa'i dbaṅ po khyad par du 'phags pa dag 'thob par 'gyur źiṅ / de'i de dag kyaṅ dad pa śin tu mchog rnams daṅ śin tu gtso bo dag skye ba'i rten du 'gyur ba daṅ / tshul khrims yaṅ dag par blaṅs pa daṅ thos pa gzuṅ ba daṅ gtoṅ ba spel ba daṅ lta ba sbyaṅs pa śin tu mchog daṅ gtso bo daṅ dam par gyur pa dag gi rten du gyur par yaṅ 'gyur ro // dad pa la sogs pa'i chos śin tu mchog daṅ gtso bo daṅ dam par gyur pa gaṅ dag yin pa de dag kyaṅ yaṅ rnam par smin pa gźan gyi rten du 'gyur źiṅ / rnam par smin pa de yaṅ 'jig rten las 'das pa'i chos daṅ rjes su mthun pa'i dge ba gźan dag gi rten du 'gyur te /
body.translated_text: Thereafter, by that cause and condition of rightly undertaking the <s>Dharma</s>, even after the body has perished and the life has passed away, one obtains superior faculties seized by the six sense-spheres of karmic ripening; and those [faculties] become the basis for generating the most supreme and foremost faith, the rightly undertaken moral conduct, the retained learning, the expanded generosity, and the purified views that are most supreme, foremost, and excellent; and those qualities of faith and so forth that are most supreme, foremost, and excellent in turn become the basis for another karmic ripening, and that ripening in turn becomes the basis for other wholesome qualities concordant with supramundane <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: de ltar gcig gi rgyu daṅ rten du gcig gyur pa'i sbyin pa'i stobs bskyed pas / goṅ nas goṅ du gaṅ la gnas na / yoṅs su mya ṅan las 'da' ba daṅ yaṅ dag pa ñid du ṅes pa la 'jug par 'gyur ba'i tha ma'i lus phyi ma thob pa'i bar gyi skye ba khyad par can du 'gro ba gaṅ yin pa de ni 'jug pa źes bya'o //
body.translated_text: Thus, by having generated the power of giving, wherein one thing becomes the cause and basis for another, proceeding from higher to higher — that going to distinguished births up to the point of obtaining the final, last body, abiding in which one enters the certainty of <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (complete liberation) and true reality — this is called 'entry.'

body.text: de ci'i phyir źe na / de de'i tshe na / mya ṅan las 'da' ba thob par bya ba daṅ (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 42

children.text: ) mya ṅan las 'da' ba 'gro bar bya ba daṅ rim gyis 'gro bar bya ba daṅ śin tu mthar thug par bya ba'i phyir lam gaṅ yin pa daṅ lam sraṅ gaṅ yin pa daṅ sgrub pa gaṅ yin pa der źugs pa daṅ yaṅ dag par źugs pa daṅ rab tu źugs pa yin pas na / de'i phyir źugs pa źes bya ste / de ni 'jug pa'i raṅ bźin źes bya'o //
children.translated_text: for the sake of going toward <s>nirvāṇa</s>, for the sake of going gradually, and for the sake of reaching the ultimate end — whichever path, whichever road, whichever practice it may be — one has entered, rightly entered, and fully entered it. Therefore it is called 'entry' — this is called the nature of entry.

body.translated_text: Why is that? Because at that time, for the sake of attaining <s>nirvāṇa</s>,

body.text:
(I)-B-II Ms.-, Sh.-, P.12b5, D.11a3, N.12b5, Co.12a2 Ch.399c17
'jug pa'i rnam par gźag pa gaṅ źe na / rigs yod pa daṅ / 'jug pa yod pa daṅ / yoṅs su smin par byed pa ñid yod pa daṅ / yoṅs su smin pa yod pa ste / źugs pa kho na yin la yoṅs su smin par byed pa ñid kyaṅ ma yin yoṅs su smin pa yaṅ ma yin pa yaṅ yod do / źugs pa yaṅ yin yoṅs su smin par byed pa ñid kyaṅ yin la yoṅs su smin pa ma yin pa yaṅ yod do / źugs pa yaṅ yin yoṅs su smin pa yaṅ yin la yoṅs su smin par byed pa ñid ma yin pa yaṅ yod do / źugs pa yaṅ ma yin yoṅs su smin par byed pa ñid kyaṅ ma yin yoṅs su smin pa yaṅ ma yin pa yaṅ yod do //
body.translated_text: (I)-B-II — What is the classification of entry? There is [one with] lineage, there is [one with] entry, there is [one who is] a ripener, and there is [one who is] ripened. There is also one who has merely entered but is neither a ripener nor ripened. There is also one who has entered and is a ripener but not yet ripened. There is also one who has entered and is ripened but is not a ripener. There is also one who has neither entered, nor is a ripener, nor is ripened.

body.text:
(I)-B-II-1 Ms.-, Sh.-, P.12b8, D.11a5, N.12b7, Co.12a4, Ch.399c21
de la rigs gaṅ źe na / smras pa / sṅa ma bźin no //
body.translated_text: (I)-B-II-1 — Therein, what is the lineage? As stated previously.

body.text:
(I)-B-II-2 Ms.-, Sh.-, P.13a1, D.11a5, N.12b7, Co.12a5, Ch.399c22
de la źugs pa gaṅ źe na / rigs la gnas pa'i gaṅ zag gis sṅon de bźin gśegs pas gsuṅs pa'i chos 'dul ba la dad pa ma thob pa las / daṅ por thob par gyur ciṅ tshul khrims yaṅ dag par len pa daṅ thos pa 'dzin pa daṅ gtoṅ ba spel ba daṅ lta ba sbyoṅ bar byed pa gaṅ yin pa ste / de ni źugs pa źes bya'o //
body.translated_text: (I)-B-II-2 — Therein, what is the entry? When a person abiding in the lineage, who previously had not obtained faith in the <s>dharmavinaya</s> (doctrine and discipline) proclaimed by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, for the first time obtains it, and undertakes moral conduct, retains learning, expands generosity, and purifies views — this is called 'entry.'

body.text:
(I)-B-II-3 Ms.-, Sh.-, P.13a2, D.11a6, N.13a1, Co.12a6, Ch.399c24
yoṅs su smin par byed pa ñid gaṅ źe na / de ltar źugs pa'i gaṅ zag de ñid gaṅ la gnas na / yoṅs su mya ṅan las 'da' ba daṅ yaṅ dag pa ñid du ṅes pa la 'jug par 'gyur ba'i tha ma'i lus phyi ma thob pa ma gtogs pa / źugs pa'i goṅ yan chad nas skye ba goṅ nas goṅ ma dag tu dbaṅ po śin tu mchog daṅ gtso bo daṅ dam pa daṅ śin tu khyad par du 'phags pa dag yaṅ dag par sgrub par (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 44

children.text: ) byed pa gaṅ yin pa ste / de ni yoṅs su smin par byed pa ñid ces bya'o //
children.translated_text: this is called 'ripening.'

body.translated_text: (I)-B-II-3 — What is the ripening? When that very person who has thus entered, abiding in which one enters the certainty of <s>parinirvāṇa</s> and true reality — excepting the obtaining of the final, last body — from the point of entry onward, in progressively higher births, fully accomplishes faculties that are most supreme, foremost, excellent, and highly distinguished —

body.text:
(I)-B-II-4 Ms.-, Sh.-, P.1335, D. 11 b 1, N. 13a3, Co.12b1, Ch.399c29
de la yoṅs su smin pa gaṅ źe na / des gaṅ la gnas na / yoṅs su mya ṅan las 'da' ba daṅ yaṅ dag pa ñid du ṅes pa la 'jug par 'gyur ba'i tha ma'i lus phyi ma thob par gyur pa gaṅ yin pa ste / de ni yoṅs su smin pa źes bya'o //
body.translated_text: (I)-B-II-4 — Therein, what is the ripened? When one has obtained that [body] abiding in which one enters the certainty of <s>parinirvāṇa</s> and true reality — the final, last body — this is called 'ripened.'

body.text:
(I)-B-II-5 Ms.-, Sh.-, P.13a6, D.11b2, N.13a4, Co.12b2, Ch.400a3
de la źugs pa kho na yin la yoṅs su smin par byed pa ñid kyaṅ ma yin yoṅs su smin pa yaṅ ma yin pa gaṅ źe na / de bźin gśegs pas gsuṅs pa'i chos 'dul ba la daṅ por dad pa daṅ lta ba sbyoṅ bar byed pa'i bar ni thob par gyur la / de'i goṅ du ni skye ba gcig tsam yaṅ mṅon par bsgrub par mi byed pa gaṅ yin pa ste / de ni źugs pa kho na yin la yoṅs su smin par byed pa ñid kyaṅ ma yin yoṅs su smin pa yaṅ nia yin pa źes bya'o //
body.translated_text: (I)-B-II-5 — Therein, what is one who has merely entered but is neither a ripener nor ripened? When one has for the first time obtained faith in the <s>dharmavinaya</s> proclaimed by the <s>Tathāgata</s> and up to the purification of views, but beyond that does not accomplish even a single birth [toward progress] — this is called 'one who has merely entered but is neither a ripener nor ripened.'

body.text:
(I)-B-II-6 Ms.-, Sh.-, P.13a8, D.11b3, N.13a6, Co.12b4, Ch.400a6
de la źugs pa yaṅ yin yoṅs su smin par byed pa ñid kyaṅ yin la yoṅs su smin pa ma yin pa gaṅ źe na / de bźin gśegs pas gsuṅs pa'i chos 'dul ba la daṅ por dad pa daṅ lta ba sbyoṅ bar byed pa'i bar yaṅ thob par gyur la / de'i goṅ du skye ba gcig gam gñis sam rab tu maṅ po dag kyaṅ mṅon par sgrub par byed mod kyi / gaṅ la gnas na / yoṅs su mya ṅan las 'da' ba daṅ yaṅ dag pa ñid du ṅes pa la 'jug par 'gyur ba'i tha ma'i lus phyi ma ma thob pa gaṅ yin pa ste / de ni źugs pa yaṅ yin yoṅs su smin par byed pa ñid kyaṅ yin la yoṅs su smin pa ma yin pa źes bya'o //
body.translated_text: (I)-B-II-6 — Therein, what is one who has entered and is a ripener but not yet ripened? When one has for the first time obtained faith in the <s>dharmavinaya</s> proclaimed by the <s>Tathāgata</s> and up to the purification of views, and beyond that accomplishes one, two, or many births and progresses toward distinction, but has not yet obtained the final, last body, abiding in which one attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> and enters the certainty of true reality — this is called 'one who has entered and is a ripener but not yet ripened.'

body.text:
(I)-B-II-7 Ms.-, Sh.-, P.13b4, D.11b6, N.13b1, Co.12b7, Ch.400a12
de la źugs pa yaṅ yin yoṅs su smin pa yaṅ yin la yoṅs su smin par byed pa ñid ma yin pa gaṅ źe na / 'di lta ste / de ltar źugs pa'i gaṅ zag de ñid kyis (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 46

children.text: ) gaṅ la gnas na / yoṅs su mya ṅan las 'da' ba daṅ yaṅ dag pa ñid du ṅes pa la 'jug par 'gyur ba'i tha ma'i lus kyi phyi ma thob ciṅ rñed par gyur pa gaṅ yin pa ste / de ni źugs pa yaṅ yin / yoṅs su smin pa yaṅ yin la / yoṅs su smin par byed pa ñid ma yin pa źes bya'o //
children.translated_text: who has obtained the final, last body, abiding in which one enters the certainty of <s>parinirvāṇa</s> and true reality — this is called 'one who has entered, is ripened, but is not a ripener.'

body.translated_text: (I)-B-II-7 — Therein, what is one who has entered and is ripened but not a ripener? That is, that very person who has thus entered,
