(I)-B-II-8 Ms.6a1L, Sh.-, P.13b6, D.11b7, N.13b3, Co.13a1, Ch.400a19
tatra katamo nāvatīrṇo na paripacyamāno na paripakvaḥ. ['di lta ste / yoṅs
su mya ṅan las 'da' ba'i chos can gyi gaṅ zag rigs kho na la gnas la] nāvatīrṇaḥ, ayam ucyate naivāvatīrṇaḥ pudgalo na paripacyamāno na paripakvaḥ /
body.translated_text: (I)-B-II-8 — Therein, who is one that has neither entered, nor is ripening, nor is ripened? [That is, a person possessing the nature of <s>parinirvāṇa</s> who merely abides in the lineage but] has not entered — this one is called a person who has neither entered, nor is ripening, nor is ripened.

body.text: api tu bhavya eva so 'vatārāya paripākāya / asti punaḥ pudgalo yo 'bhavya evāvatārāya paripākāya vā, tad yathā gotravirahito 'parinirvāṇadharmako yaḥ pudgalaḥ, ayam atyantād evābhavyo 'vatārāya paripākāya vā, kiṃ punaḥ parinirvāṇāya bhavyo bhaviṣyati //
body.translated_text: However, that one is indeed capable of entry and ripening. But there is also a person who is utterly incapable of entry or ripening — namely, a person devoid of the lineage, whose nature is non-<s>parinirvāṇa</s>. Such a person is absolutely incapable of entry or ripening — how much less will one become capable of <s>parinirvāṇa</s>?

body.text:
(I)-B-II-9 Ms.6a2L/13b7M, Sh.25-3, W.* 65-6, P.14a3, D.12a4, N.13b7, Co.13a5, Ch.400a23
tatra sarveṣām eva pudgalānāṃ ṣaḍbhiḥ sthānaiḥ saṃgraho bhavati / katamaiḥ) ṣaḍbhiḥ / bhavyo mṛdukuśalamūlasamanvāgato madhyakuśalamūlasamanvāgato 'dhimātrakuśalamūlasamanvāgato niṣṭhāprāyogiko niṣṭhāgataś ca //
body.translated_text: (I)-B-II-9 — Therein, all persons are comprised under six categories. Which six? One who is capable [but with] mild wholesome roots, one endowed with middling wholesome roots, one endowed with intense wholesome roots, one who is practicing toward the final goal, and one who has reached the final goal.

body.text:
(I)-B-II-9-a Ms.13b7R, Sh.25-7, P.14a4, D.12a5, N.14a1, Co.13a6, Ch.400a28
tatra katamo bhavya eva pudgalaḥ / yo gotrastho na cādyāpi tatprathamatas tathāgatapravedite dharmavinaye śraddhāṃ pratilabhate (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 48

children.text: ) yāvad dṛṣṭiṃ ṛjūkaroti / ayam ucyate bhavya eva pudgalaḥ //
children.translated_text: up to straightening one's views — this one is called a person who is merely capable.

body.translated_text: (I)-B-II-9-a — Therein, who is a person that is merely capable? One who abides in the lineage but has not yet for the first time obtained faith in the <s>dharmavinaya</s> proclaimed by the <s>Tathāgata</s>,

body.text:
(I)-B-II-9-b Ms.14a1L, Sh.25-4, P.14a6, D.12a6, N.14a2, Co.13a7, Ch.400b2
tatra katamo mṛdukuśalamūlasamanvāgataḥ / yo gotrasthas tena tathāgatapravedite dharmavinaye tatprathamataḥ śraddhā pratilabdhā bhavati yāvad drstir ṛjūkṛtā / ayam ucyate mṛdukuśalamūlasamanvāgataḥ pudgalaḥ //
body.translated_text: (I)-B-II-9-b — Therein, who is one endowed with mild wholesome roots? One who, abiding in the lineage, has for the first time obtained faith in the <s>dharmavinaya</s> proclaimed by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, up to having straightened one's views — this one is called a person endowed with mild wholesome roots.

body.text:
(I)-B-II-9-c Ms.14a1R, Sh.26-1, P.14a7, D.12a7, N.14a3, Co.13b1, Ch.400b6
tatra katamo madhyakuśalamūlasamanvāgataḥ / yo gotrasthaḥ pudgalas tatprathamatas tathāgatapravedite dharmavinaye śraddhāṃ pratilabhya yāvad dṛṣṭim ṛjuṃ kṛtvā, tataḥ pareṇaikaṃ vā dve vā saṃbahulāni vā janmāny abhinirvartayati viśeṣāya paraiti / no caramam ātmabhāvaṃ pratilabhate, yatra sthitaḥ parinirvāti samyaktvaṃ ca nyāmam avakrāmati / ayam ucyate madhyakuśalamūlasamanvāgatahpudgalaḥ //
body.translated_text: (I)-B-II-9-c — Therein, who is one endowed with middling wholesome roots? A person who, abiding in the lineage, having for the first time obtained faith in the <s>dharmavinaya</s> proclaimed by the <s>Tathāgata</s> up to having straightened one's views, thereafter generates one, two, or many births and progresses toward distinction, but does not obtain the final self-existence, abiding in which one attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> and enters the certainty of true reality — this one is called a person endowed with middling wholesome roots.

body.text:
(I)-B-II-9-d Ms.14a2L, Sh.26-6, P.14b2, D.12b3, N.14a6, Co.13b3, Ch.400b12
tatra katamo 'dhimātrakuśalamūlasamanvāgataḥ pudgalaḥ / yaḥ pudgalo viśeṣāya paraiti sa caramam ātmabhāvaṃ pratilabhate / yatra sthitaḥ parinirvāti samyaktvaṃ ca nyāmam avakrāmati / ayam ucyate 'dhimātrakuśalamūlasamanvāgataḥ pudgalaḥ //
body.translated_text: (I)-B-II-9-d — Therein, who is a person endowed with intense wholesome roots? A person who progresses toward distinction and obtains the final self-existence, abiding in which one attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> and enters the certainty of true reality — this one is called a person endowed with intense wholesome roots.

body.text:
(I)-B-II-9-e Ms.14a3L, Sh.26-9, P.14b3, D.12b3, N.14a7, Co.13b5, Ch.400b16
tatra katamo niṣṭhāprāyogikaḥ pudgalaḥ / yaḥ pudgalaś caramam ātmabhāvaṃ pratilabhyāsravakṣayāya samyagavavādānuśāsanīṃ saddharmaśravaṇaṃ vā pratilabhya samyag eva prayujyate, na cādyāpi sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā pratipadyata āsravakṣayam anuprāpnoti, na niṣṭhāṃ gacchati / ayam ucyate niṣṭhāprāyogikaḥ pudgalaḥ //
body.translated_text: (I)-B-II-9-e — Therein, who is a person practicing toward the final goal? A person who, having obtained the final self-existence, having received proper instruction and admonition for the destruction of the <s>āśravas</s> (defilements), or having obtained the hearing of the true <s>Dharma</s>, rightly applies oneself, but has not yet in every way, in all respects, by all means practiced to attain the destruction of the <s>āśravas</s>, has not reached the final goal — this one is called a person practicing toward the final goal.

body.text:
(I)-B-II-9-f Ms.14a4L, Sh.26-15, P.14b6, D.12b5, N.14b2, Co.13b7, Ch.400b20
tatra niṣṭhāgataḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / yaḥ samyagavoditaḥ samyaganuśiṣṭo yadutāsravakṣayāya, tathā tathā pratipadyate / yat sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathāsravakṣayam anuprāpnoti, kṛtakṛtyo bhavati paramaśītībhāvaprāptaḥ / ayam ucyate niṣṭhāgataḥ pudgalaḥ //
body.translated_text: (I)-B-II-9-f — Therein, who is a person that has reached the final goal? One who, rightly instructed and rightly admonished for the destruction of the <s>āśravas</s>, practices accordingly, so that in every way, in all respects, by all means one attains the destruction of the <s>āśravas</s>, becomes one whose task is accomplished, having attained the state of supreme coolness — this one is called a person who has reached the final goal.

body.text:
(I)-B-II-9' Ms.14a5L, Sh.26-20, W.*65-14, P.14b8, D.12b6, N.14b6, Co.14a2, Ch.400b25
tatra bhavyajātīyaḥ pudgalo gotraṃ niśritya gotraṃ pratiṣṭhāya mṛdūni kuśalamūlāni pratilabhate, avatīrṇaś ca bhavati / so 'vatīrṇo mṛdūni kuśalamūlāni niśritya pratiṣṭhāya madhyāni kuśalamūlāni pratilabhate, taiś cātmānaṃ paripācayati / sa tathā paripacyamāno madhyāni kuśalamūlāni niśritya pratiṣṭhāyādhimātrāṇi kuśalamūlāni pratilabhate, paripakvaś ca bhavati / so 'dhimātrakuśalamūlahetusamudāgatenātmabhāvapratilambhena yadā saṃbhārañ ca samudānayati, cittaikāgratāñ ca spṛśati, samyaktvañ ca nyāmam avakrāmati, srotaāpattiphalaṃ vā sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ vānāgāmiphalaṃ vā sākṣātkaroti / no tv agraphalam arhattvam sākṣātkaroti / tadā niṣṭhāprāyogika ity ucyate / yadā tu sarvakleśaprahāṇam arhattvam sākṣātkaroti, tadā niṣṭhāgato bhavati /
body.translated_text: Therein, a person of the capable type, relying on and established in the <s>gotra</s> (spiritual lineage), obtains soft roots of wholesomeness and becomes an entrant. Having entered, relying on and established in the soft roots of wholesomeness, he obtains middling roots of wholesomeness and matures himself through them. Being thus matured, relying on and established in the middling roots of wholesomeness, he obtains superior roots of wholesomeness and becomes fully matured. Through the attainment of a personal existence produced by the cause of superior roots of wholesomeness, when he both assembles the requisites and touches one-pointedness of mind and enters into the correct certainty of the right path, he directly realizes the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>), or the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>), or the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>), but does not yet directly realize the highest fruit, <s>arhatship</s>. At that time he is called 'one engaged in the final application.' But when he directly realizes <s>arhatship</s>, the abandonment of all afflictions, then he has reached the final goal.

body.text: saiṣādimadhyaparyavasānā sarvaśrāvakacaryā ṣaḍbhiḥ pudgalavyavasthānaiḥ saṃdarśitā bhavati / tatra gotreṇādiḥ śrāvakacaryāyāḥ (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 52

children.text: ) saṃdarśitaḥ / niṣṭhayā paryavasānam / tadanyena madhyaṃ saṃdarśitam //
children.translated_text: ) has been shown. By the final goal, the end. By the rest, the middle has been shown. //

body.translated_text: This entire career of all <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples), from beginning to middle to end, has been shown through six categories of persons. Therein, by the <s>gotra</s> (lineage) the beginning of the <s>śrāvaka</s> career

body.text:
(I)-B-II-10 Ms.14a8L, Sh.27-2, P.15a7, D.13a4, N.15a2, Co.14a7, Ch.400c12
tatrāvatīrṇānāṃ pudgalānāṃ kiṃ parimāṇaniyatas tulyaś ca sarveṣāṃ kālo bhavati parinirvāṇāya, āhosvid aparimāṇaniyato 'tulyaniścayaḥ sarveṣāṃ kālo bhavati parinirvāṇāya / āha / naiṣāṃ parimāṇaniyataḥ kālo nāpi ca tulyaḥ sarveṣāṃ parinirvāṇāya / api tu yathāyogam eṣāṃ yathāpratyayalābhaṃ parinirvāṇaṃ veditavyam / keṣāṃcic cireṇa, keṣāṃcin nāticireṇa, keṣāṃcit punaḥ kṣipram eva parinirvāṇaṃ bhavati / api tu yo gotrasthaḥ pudgalaḥ sarvaḥ kṣipraṃ parinirvāti, so 'vaśyaṃ trīṇi janmāny abhinirvartayati / ekasminn avatarati, ekasmin paripacyate, ekasmin janmani paripakvo bhavati, tatraiva ca parinirvāti / no cet parinirvāti so 'vaśyaṃ śaikṣaḥ kālaṃ karoti / parañ ca saptabhavān abhinirvartayati / idam ucyate 'vatāravyavasthānam //
body.translated_text: Therein, for persons who have entered, is the time for <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of a fixed measure and equal for all, or is the time for <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of an unfixed measure and unequal determination for all? He says: The time is not of a fixed measure for them, nor is it equal for all for <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. Rather, their <s>parinirvāṇa</s> should be understood as occurring according to their individual fitness and according to their obtaining of conditions. For some it takes a long time, for some not very long, and for some <s>parinirvāṇa</s> occurs swiftly. However, whatever person established in the <s>gotra</s> attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> swiftly, he necessarily completes three births: in one he enters, in one he matures, in one birth he becomes fully matured, and in that very one he attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. If he does not attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, he necessarily dies as a learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>). And he completes at most seven existences. This is called the determination of entry.

body.text:
(I)-B-III-1 Ms.14b2R, Sh.28-14, W.*66-8, P.15b5, D.13b2, N.15a7, Co.14b5, Ch.400c24
avatīrṇasya pudgalasya katamāni liṅgāni / iha gotrasthaḥ pudgalo 'vatīrṇamātra eva yadā janmāntaraparivartenāpi smṛtisaṃpramoṣaṃ pratilabhate / svaśāstari dharmavinaye vā sati, saṃvidyamāne 'pi durākhyāte dharmavinaye svākhyāte 'py anekaparyāyeṇa durākhyātasya dharmavinayasya varṇam stutim ānuśaṃsaṃ śrutvā nāvatarati, na pravrajati / pravrajito 'py avatīrṇo laghu laghv eva pratyudāvartate / prakṛtyaiva cāsya tatrārocakaḥ saṃtiṣṭhate / madhuni jātasyeva ca prāṇakasya śukte prakṣiptasya, kāmopabhogino vā kardame syandanikāyāṃ prakṣiptasya, yathāpi tat pūrvakeṇaiva hetubalādhānena // svākhyātasya vā punar dharmavinayasya naiva varṇastutim ānuśaṃsaṃ śṛṇoti vā / alpamātram avaramātraṃ vā śrutvā, aśrutvā vā, (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 54

children.text: ) laghu laghv evāvatarati pravrajati vā / tathā pravrajitaś cāvatīrṇo na pratyudāvartate / prakṛtyaiva cāsya tatra ruciḥ saṃtiṣṭhate / madhuprāṇakasyeva madhuni, kāmopabhogino vā praṇītāyāṃ kāmacaryāyām / yathāpi tat pūrvakeṇaiva hetubalādhānena / idaṃ prathamam avatīrṇasya pudgalasya liṅgam //
children.translated_text: ) very quickly he enters and goes forth. And having thus gone forth, the one who has entered does not turn back. And by nature, a delight for it remains in him — like a small creature born in honey [placed] in honey, or like one accustomed to sensual pleasures in an excellent sensual practice — just as, indeed, by the force of previous causes. This is the first mark of a person who has entered. //

body.translated_text: What are the marks of a person who has entered? Here, a person established in the <s>gotra</s>, having just entered, when even through change of birth he obtains loss of memory — [yet] when his own teacher's <s>Dharma</s>-<s>Vinaya</s> exists and is present, even though a poorly proclaimed <s>Dharma</s>-<s>Vinaya</s> also exists alongside the well-proclaimed one, having heard in many ways the praise, eulogy, and commendation of the poorly proclaimed <s>Dharma</s>-<s>Vinaya</s>, he does not enter it, does not go forth in it. Even having gone forth, the one who has entered very quickly turns back. And by nature, a distaste for it remains in him — like a small creature born in honey that is thrown into vinegar, or like one accustomed to sensual pleasures who is thrown into a muddy stream — just as, indeed, by the force of previous causes. // But when he hears, or does not hear, even the slightest, lowest praise, eulogy, and commendation of the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s>-<s>Vinaya</s>,

body.text:
(I)-B-IIl-2 Ms.14b5R, Sh.29-14, W.*66-12, P.16a4, D.13b7, N.15b6, Co.15a5, Ch.401a11
punar aparam avatīrṇaḥ pudgalo na ca tāvad visaṃyukto bhavaty apāyākṣaṇagamanīyaiḥ kleśaiḥ, na ca punar akṣaṇeṣūpapadyate / avatīrṇaṃ ca pudgalaṃ sandhāyoktaṃ bhagavatā /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, a person who has entered is not yet separated from the afflictions that lead to rebirth in the lower realms and unfavorable states, yet he is not reborn in unfavorable states. With reference to the person who has entered, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) has said:

children.translated_text: One who has supreme worldly right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>),
even through thousands of births, does not go to an evil destiny. //

body.text: sa punar yadādhimātreṣu kuśalamūleṣu praviṣṭo bhavaty anupūrveṇa paripākagamanīyeṣu tadā nākṣaṇeṣūpapadyate, na tv anyeṣu / idaṃ dvitīyam avatīrṇasya pudgalasya liṅgam //
body.translated_text: But when he has entered into the superior roots of wholesomeness that gradually lead to maturation, then he is not reborn in unfavorable states — but not otherwise. This is the second mark of a person who has entered. //

body.text:
(I)-B-IIl-3 Ms.14b7L, Sh.30-3, P.16a8, D.14a3, N.16a2, Co.14a7, Ch.401a18
punar aparam avatīrṇapudgalo buddhasya vā dharmasya vā saṃghasya vā gunāñ chrutvā, anusmṛtyā vā labhate cetasaḥ prasādam udāraṃ kuśalaṃ naiṣkramyopasaṃhitaṃ, bhūyo bhūyas tenālambanena prasādadravacittatayā aśruprapātān romāṃcāṃś ca pratilabhate / idaṃ tṛtīyam avatīrṇasya pudgalasya liṅgam //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, a person who has entered, having heard the qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>, or of the <s>Dharma</s>, or of the <s>Saṅgha</s>, or through recollection, obtains a serenity of mind that is lofty, wholesome, and connected with renunciation; again and again, by that object, through a mind softened by faith, he experiences tears and goosebumps. This is the third mark of a person who has entered. //

body.text:
(I)-B-IIl-4 Ms.14b8L, Sh.30-9, P.16b2, D.14a4, N.16a3, Co.15b2, Ch.401a22
punar aparam avatīrṇaḥ pudgalaḥ prakṛtyaiva tīvreṇa hrīvyapatrāpyeṇa samanvāgato bhavati, yaduta sarvasāvadyasthānasamudācāreṣu / idaṃ caturtham avatīrṇasya pudgalasya liṅgam //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, a person who has entered is by nature endowed with intense conscience (<s>hrī</s>) and moral dread (<s>vyapatrāpya</s>), namely with respect to all conduct in blameworthy situations. This is the fourth mark of a person who has entered. //

body.text:
(I)-B-IIl-5 Ms.15a1L, Sh.30-13, P.16b3, D.14a5, N.16a4, Co.15b3, Ch.401a26
punar aparam avatīrṇaḥ pudgalaḥ chandiko bhavati / tīvracchanda uddeśe (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 56

children.text: ) svādhyāye paripṛcchāyāṃ yoge manasikāre, kiṃkuśalagaveṣī ca bhavati / idaṃ pañcamam avatīrṇasya pudgalasya liṅgam //
children.translated_text: ) self-study, questioning, practice, and mental attention, and is a seeker of what is wholesome. This is the fifth mark of a person who has entered. //

body.translated_text: Furthermore, a person who has entered is zealous, with intense zeal in recitation,

body.text:
(I)-B-IIl-6 Ms.15a1M, Sh.30-17, P.16b4, D.14a6, N.16a5, Co.15b4, Ch.401a29
punar aparam avatīrṇaḥ pudgalaḥ sarvakarmānteṣv anavadyeṣu sarvasamādāneṣu kuśalapakṣaprayogeṣu dṛḍhārambhaś ca bhavati sthirārambhaś ca niścitārambhaś ca, yaduta samāgamāya / idaṃ ṣaṣṭham avatīrṇasya pudgalasya liṅgam //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, a person who has entered has firm effort, steady effort, and resolute effort in all blameless activities, in all undertakings, and in endeavors toward the wholesome side — that is, for the purpose of attainment. This is the sixth mark of a person who has entered. //

body.text:
(I)-B-IIl-7 Ms.15a2L, Sh.31-1, P.16b6, D.14a7, N.16a6, Co.15b6, Ch.401b4
punar aparam avatīrṇaḥ pudgalo mandarajaskajātīyo bhavati, mandamandaṃ kleśaparyavasthānam utpādayati na ca punaḥ prabandhaṃ sthāpayati, aśaṭhaś ca bhavaty amāyāvī nihatamadamānāhaṃkāro guṇābhiniviṣṭo doṣadveṣṭā / idaṃ saptamam avatīrṇasya pudgalasya liṅgam //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, a person who has entered is of the type with little dust [of defilements]; he generates afflictive states only mildly and gently and does not establish a continuum [of them]; he is not deceitful, not hypocritical, with pride, conceit, and ego-sense destroyed, devoted to qualities and averse to faults. This is the seventh mark of a person who has entered. //

body.text:
(I)-B-IIl-8 Ms.15a3L, Sh.31-6, P.16b8, D.14b2, N.16b1, Co.15b7, Ch.401b8
punar aparam avatīrṇaḥ pudgalo 'saṃlīnacitto bhavaty udāreṣv adhigamyeṣu sthāneṣu nātmānaṃ paribhavati, nāpratibalatāyām avasthāpayati, adhimuktibahulo bhavati / idam aṣṭamam avatīrṇasya pudgalasya liṅgam //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, a person who has entered has an unshrinking mind with respect to lofty, attainable states; he does not disparage himself, does not place himself in a position of incapacity, and is rich in aspiration. This is the eighth mark of a person who has entered. //

body.text: imāny evaṃbhāgīyāni prabhūtāny avatīrṇānāṃ pudgalānāṃ liṅgāni veditavyāni yeṣām etat pradeśamātram ākhyātam //
body.translated_text: These and similar abundant marks of persons who have entered should be understood, of which only a portion has been described here. //

body.text: punar etāni liṅgāni mṛdukuśalamūlasthasyāvatīrṇasya mṛdūni bhavanti, sacchidrāṇy anirantarāṇy apariśuddhāni / madhyakuśalamūlasthitasya madhyāni / adhimātrakuśalamūlasthitasyādhimātrāṇi, niśchidrāṇi nirantarāṇi pariśuddhāni / imāny ucyante "avatīrṇasya pudgalasya liṅgāni" yair liṅgaiḥ samanvāgato 'vatīrṇo 'vatīrṇa iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati / tāni punar etāni gotrasthānām avatīrṇānāṃ ca pudgalānām ānumānikāni liṅgāni (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 58

children.text: ) veditavyāni / buddhā eva tu bhagavantaḥ paramapāramipraptāś ca śrāvakās tāyinas tatra pratyakṣadarśinaḥ, suviśuddhena jñānadarśanena pratyanubhavanti, yaduta gotraṃ cāvatāraṃ ca //
children.translated_text: ) [to be understood thus]. But only the Blessed <s>Buddhas</s> and those disciples who have reached the highest perfection, the protectors, are direct perceivers therein; they directly experience with perfectly purified knowledge-vision both the <s>gotra</s> (lineage) and the entry. //

body.translated_text: Furthermore, these marks, for one who has entered and is established in soft roots of wholesomeness, are soft — with gaps, not continuous, not purified. For one established in middling roots of wholesomeness, they are middling. For one established in superior roots of wholesomeness, they are superior — without gaps, continuous, and purified. These are called 'the marks of a person who has entered,' endowed with which marks one who has entered comes to be reckoned as 'one who has entered.' And furthermore, these marks of persons established in the <s>gotra</s> and of those who have entered are to be understood as inferential marks,

body.text:
(I)-B-IV Ms.15a6L, Sh.32-3, W.*66-18, P.17a7, D.14b7, N.16b6, Co.16a6, Ch.401b26
avatīrṇāḥ pudgalāḥ katame / asty avatīrṇaḥ pudgalo 'vatīrṇa eva na paripacyamāno na paripakvo na niṣkrāntaḥ, asti paripacyamāno na paripakvo na niṣkrāntaḥ, asti paripakvo na niṣkrāntaḥ, asti niṣkrānto na paripakvaḥ / eṣāṃ ca pūrvavad vibhāgo veditavyaḥ // ye 'pi tadanye mṛdvindriyādayaḥ pudgalāḥ gotrabhūmau nirdiṣṭā / teṣām ihāpi yathāyogaṃ vibhāgo veditavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: What are the persons who have entered? There is a person who has entered and is merely entered — not being matured, not matured, and not gone forth. There is one being matured but not matured and not gone forth. There is one matured but not gone forth. There is one gone forth but not matured. The distinction among these should be understood as before. // Whatever persons of soft faculties and so forth have been described in the stage of the spiritual lineage — their distinction here too should be understood as appropriate. //

body.text: tatra yaś cāyam avatārasya svabhāvo yac ca vyavasthānaṃ yāni cemāny avatīrṇānāṃ liṅgāni ye ceme 'vatīrṇāḥ pudgalās tat sarvam abhisaṃkṣipya"avatārabhūmir" ity ucyate //
body.translated_text: Therein, whatever is the nature of entry and whatever is its determination and whatever are these marks of those who have entered and whatever are these persons who have entered — all of that, taken together, is called 'the stage of entry' (<s>avatārabhūmi</s>). //

body.text: uddānam /
body.translated_text: <s>Uddāna</s> (summary verse):

children.text: svabhāvas tadvyavasthānaṃ liṅgaṃ pudgala eva ca /
children.translated_text: The nature and its determination, the marks, and the persons themselves —
all of this, in brief, is to be known as the stage of entry (<s>avatārabhūmi</s>). //

body.text: śrāvakabhūmāv avatārabhūmiḥ samāptā //
body.translated_text: From the <s>Śrāvakabhūmi</s>, the stage of entry (<s>avatārabhūmi</s>) is complete. //

body.text:
(I)-C Ms.15b1M, Sh.33-1, W.*66-25, P.17b4, D.15a4, N.17a3, Co.16b4, Ch.401c11
naiṣkramyabhūmiḥ katamā / āha / yac ca laukikena mārgeṇa vairāgyagamanaṃ, yac ca lokottareṇa mārgeṇa vairāgyagamanaṃ, yaś ca tayoḥ sambhāraḥ, tad ekadhyam abhisaṃkṣipya naiṣkramyabhūmir ity ucyate //
body.translated_text: What is the stage of renunciation (<s>naiṣkramyabhūmi</s>)? He says: Whatever is the attainment of dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) through the worldly path, and whatever is the attainment of dispassion through the supramundane path, and whatever is the requisite for both of these — all of that, taken together, is called the stage of renunciation (<s>naiṣkramyabhūmi</s>). //

body.text:
(I)-C-I Ms.15b2L, Sh.35-7, W.*66-33, P.17b6, D.15a5, N17a4, Co.16b5, Ch.401c18
laukikena mārgeṇa vairāgyagamanaṃ katamat / yathāpīhaikatyaḥ kāmadhātāv audārikadarśī bhavati / prathama eva sa samāpattyupapattike dhyāne vivekaje prītisukhe śāntadarśī bhavati / sa tathādarśī tadbahulavihāri san kāmavairāgyam anuprāpnoti, prathamaṃ ca dhyānam samāpadyate / evaṃ prathamadhyānād ūrdhvam sarvāsv adharimāsu bhūmiṣv audārikadarśi bhavati, sarvāsu coparimāsu bhūmiṣu śāntadarśī, sa tathādarśī tadbahulavihārī samāno yāvad ākiñcanyāyatanād vairāgyam anuprāpnoti naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanaṃ ca samāpadyate / idam ucyate laukikena mārgeṇa vairāgyagamanaṃ, nāsty ata uttari nāto bhūyaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is the attainment of dispassion through the worldly path? Here, a certain one sees the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>) as coarse. In the very first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation absorption) — the attainment-rebirth [level] born of seclusion, with joy and happiness — he sees peace. Seeing thus and dwelling much in that, he attains dispassion from sensual desires and enters the first <s>dhyāna</s>. Likewise, from the first <s>dhyāna</s> upward, he sees all the lower stages as coarse and all the upper stages as peaceful; seeing thus and dwelling much in that, he attains dispassion up to the sphere of nothingness (<s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s>) and enters the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>). This is called the attainment of dispassion through the worldly path — there is nothing beyond this, nothing further. //

body.text:
(I)-C-II Ms.15b3R, Sh.36-2, W.*67-25, P.18a2, D.15b1, N.17a7, Co.17a2, Ch.402a2
lokottareṇa mārgeṇa vairāgyagamanaṃ katamat / yathāpīhaikatyaḥ satpuruṣāṇāṃ darśī, āryadharmeṣu kovidaḥ, ['phag pa'i chos rnams la bzo ba la la], duḥkhaṃ vā duḥkhato yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti, samudayaṃ vā samudayataḥ, nirodhaṃ vā nirodhataḥ, mārgaṃ vā mārgataḥ, śaikṣeṇa jñānadarśanena samanvāgataḥ / tataś cottari mārgaṃ bhāvayaṃs traidhātukebhyo darśanabhāvanāprahātavyebhyo dharmebhya ātmānaṃ visaṃyojayati, vimocayaty evaṃ cāsau traidhātukasamatikrānto bhavati / idam ucyate lokottareṇa mārgeṇa vairāgyagamanam //
body.translated_text: What is the attainment of dispassion through the supramundane path? It is like this: here a certain person sees true persons (<s>satpuruṣas</s>), is learned in the noble <s>dharmas</s>, and truly understands suffering as suffering, origin as origin, cessation as cessation, and the path as path, being endowed with the knowledge and vision of a trainee (<s>śaikṣa</s>). Then, further cultivating the path, he detaches himself from the <s>dharmas</s> in the three realms (<s>traidhātuka</s>) that are to be abandoned through seeing (<s>darśana</s>) and through cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>), and liberates himself. Thus he becomes one who has transcended the three realms. This is called the attainment of dispassion through the supramundane path.

body.text:
(I)-C-III Ms.15b5M/12a1M, Sh.36-11, W.*68-1, P.18a6, D.15b4, N.17b3, Co.17a5, Ch.402a10
tatra saṃbhāraḥ katamaḥ / tadyathā, ātmasaṃpat, parasaṃpat, kuśalo dharmacchandaḥ, śīlasaṃvaraḥ, indriyasaṃvaraḥ, bhojane mātrajñatā, pūrvarātrāpararātraṃ jāgarikānuyuktatā, saṃprajānadvihāritā, kalyāṇamitratā, saddharmaśravaṇacintanā, anantarāyaḥ, tyāgaḥ, śramaṇālaṃkāraś ca, itīme dharmā laukikalokottaravairāgyagamanāya saṃbhāra ity ucyate //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the equipment (<s>saṃbhāra</s>)? Namely: personal attainment (<s>ātmasaṃpat</s>), the attainment of others (<s>parasaṃpat</s>), wholesome desire for the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmacchanda</s>), restraint of moral conduct (<s>śīlasaṃvara</s>), restraint of the sense faculties (<s>indriyasaṃvara</s>), moderation in food, wakefulness during the first and last watches of the night, dwelling with clear comprehension (<s>saṃprajāna</s>), good friendship (<s>kalyāṇamitratā</s>), hearing and reflecting on the true <s>Dharma</s>, freedom from obstacles (<s>anantarāya</s>), generosity (<s>tyāga</s>), and the ornament of the ascetic (<s>śramaṇālaṃkāra</s>) — these <s>dharmas</s> are called the equipment for the attainment of dispassion through the worldly and supramundane [paths].

body.text:
1 (I)-C-III-1,2,3 Ms.12a1R, Sh.37-4, P.18b2, D.15b7, N.17b6, Co.17b1, Ch.402a19 ``
tatra yā cātmasaṃpat parasaṃpat kuśalaś ca dharmacchanda eṣāṃ pūrvavad vibhāgo veditavyaḥ / yad uktaṃ nihīne bījasamudāgamapratyaye //
body.translated_text: Therein, regarding personal attainment, the attainment of others, and wholesome desire for the <s>Dharma</s> — their classification should be understood as before, as stated regarding the inferior seed-condition for arising.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4 Ms.12a2L, Sh.37-7, P.18b3, D.15b7, N.17b6, Co.17b, Ch.402a21
tatra śīlasaṃvaraḥ katamaḥ / yathāpīhaikatyaḥ śīlavān viharati, yāvat samādāya śikṣate śikṣāpadeṣu //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the restraint of moral conduct (<s>śīlasaṃvara</s>)? It is like this: here a certain person dwells as one endowed with moral conduct (<s>śīlavān</s>), up to: he undertakes and trains in the training rules (<s>śikṣāpada</s>).

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-a-(1)-i Ms.12a2R, Sh.37-10, P.18b4, D.16a2, N.18a1, Co.17b3, Ch.402a25
kathaṃ śīlavān viharati / yathāsamātteṣu śikṣāpadeṣv avipannakāyakarmāntaś ca bhavaty avipannavākkarmāntaś ca, akhaṇḍacārī, acchidracāri / evaṃ śīlavān bhavati //
body.translated_text: How does one dwell as endowed with moral conduct? With respect to the training rules as undertaken, one's bodily action is unblemished and one's verbal action is unblemished; one is of unbroken conduct, of conduct without gaps. Thus one is endowed with moral conduct.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-a-(1)-ii Ms.12a3M, Sh.37-14, P.18b6, D.16a3, N.18a2, Co.17b4, Ch.402a27
kathaṃ prātimokṣasaṃvarasaṃvṛto bhavati / saptanaikāyikaṃ śīlaṃ prātimokṣasaṃvara ity ucyate / ta ete nikāyabhedena bahavaḥ saṃvarā bhavanti / asmiṃs tv arthe bhikṣusaṃvaram adhiṣṭhāyāha prātimokṣasaṃvarasaṃvṛtah//
body.translated_text: How is one restrained by the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint? The moral conduct pertaining to seven classes is called the <s>prātimokṣa</s> (individual liberation) restraint. These, by the division of classes, are many restraints. But in this context, establishing the <s>bhikṣu</s> restraint, it is called 'restrained by the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint.'

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-a-(1)-iii Ms.12a4L, Sh.38-2, P.18b8, D.16a4, N.18a3, Co.17b6, Ch.402b2
katham ācārasaṃpanno bhavati / yathāpi tad īryāpathaṃ vetikaraṇīyaṃ vā kuśalapakṣaprayogaṃ vādhiṣṭhāya lokānuvartinā lokānutkrāntena vinayānuvartinā vinayānutkrāntena cācāreṇa samanvāgato bhavati //
body.translated_text: How is one endowed with proper conduct (<s>ācāra</s>)? Whether in regard to deportment, or daily activities, or the application to the wholesome side — one is endowed with conduct that conforms to the world and does not transgress the world, that conforms to the <s>Vinaya</s> (monastic discipline) and does not transgress the <s>Vinaya</s>.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-a-(1)-iii-(a) Ms.12a4R, Sh.38-6, P.19a1, D.16a5, N.18a4, Co.17b7, Ch.402b5
tatreryāpathādhiṣṭhāna ācāraḥ kathaṃ na lokotkrānto na vinayotkrāntaḥ / yathāpi tad yatra caṃkramitavyaṃ yathā caṃkramitavyaṃ tatra tathā caṃkramyate, yena na lokagarhito bhavati na satāṃ samyaggatānāṃ satpuruṣāṇāṃ sahadhārmikāṇāṃ vinayadharāṇāṃ vinayaśikṣitānām avadyo bhavati garhyasthānīyaḥ / yathā caṅkrama evaṃ sthānaṃ niṣadyā śayyā veditavyā //
body.translated_text: Therein, how is the conduct based on deportment neither transgressing the world nor transgressing the <s>Vinaya</s>? Wherever one should walk, and however one should walk, there and thus one walks, in such a way that one is not censured by the world and is not blameworthy or deserving of reproach among true, rightly-conducted persons (<s>satpuruṣas</s>), co-practitioners of the <s>Dharma</s>, and those who uphold and are trained in the <s>Vinaya</s>. As with walking, so should standing, sitting, and lying down be understood.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-a-(1)-iii-(b) Ms.12a5R, Sh.38-14, P.19a4, D.16a7, N.18a7, Co.18a2, Ch.402b13
tatretikaraṇīyādhiṣṭhāna ācāraḥ kathaṃ na lokotkrānto bhavati na vinayotkrāntaḥ / itikaraṇīyam ucyate cīvarācchādanam uccāraprasrāvam udakadantakāṣṭhaṃ grāmapraveśaḥ piṇḍapātanirhāraparibhogaḥ pātranirmādanaṃ sthāpanaṃ ca pādaprakṣālanaṃ śayanāsanaprajñaptiḥ / tasyaiva cābhisaṃkṣepaḥ pātrakarmacīvarakarmeti / yad vā punar evaṃbhāgīyaṃ kiṃcit tad itikaraṇīyam ity ucyate / tac ca yathāyogaṃ yatra kalpayitavyaṃ, yathā ca kalpayitavyaṃ tatra tathā kalpayati / yena laukikānām ananuyojyo bhavaty avigarhitaḥ / vinayadharāṇāṃ vinayaśikṣitānām anapavādyo bhavaty avigarhitaḥ, samyaggatānāṃ sahadhārmikāṇām / evam itikaraṇīyādhiṣṭhāna ācāro lokānutkrānto bhavati vinayānutkrāntaś ca //
body.translated_text: Therein, how is the conduct based on daily activities neither transgressing the world nor transgressing the <s>Vinaya</s>? Daily activities refer to: the wearing of robes, defecation and urination, water and tooth-cleaning sticks, entering the village, collecting, using, and consuming alms-food, washing and storing the bowl, washing the feet, arranging the bedding and seat. These are summarized as bowl-duties and robe-duties. Whatever else is of this kind is called daily activities. And these, as appropriate, wherever they should be arranged, and however they should be arranged, there and thus one arranges them, so that one is not subject to reproach or censure among worldly people, and is not subject to criticism or censure among those who uphold the <s>Vinaya</s>, who are trained in the <s>Vinaya</s>, the rightly-conducted, and the co-practitioners of the <s>Dharma</s>. Thus the conduct based on daily activities conforms to and does not transgress the world and the <s>Vinaya</s>.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-a-(1)-iii-(c) Ms.12b1L, Sh.39-6, P.19b2, D.16b4, N.18b4, Co.18a7, Ch.402b26
tatra kuśalapakṣaprayogādhiṣṭhāna ācāraḥ kathaṃ lokānutkrāntaś ca bhavati vinayānutkrāntaś ca / kuśalapakṣa ucyate tadyathā svādhyāyo gurūṇām sāmīcīkarmopasthānaṃ ca, tathā glānopasthānam, anyo 'nyam anukampācittam upasthāpya cchandadānaṃ, uddeśaḥ / prayogaḥ paripṛcchā dharmaśravaṇadakṣasyānalasasya, vijñānāṃ sabrahmacāriṇāṃ kāyena vaiyāpṛtyakriyā, pareṣāṃ ca kuśalapakṣasamādāpanā dharmadeśanā / pratisaṃlayanapraveśaparyaṅkanibandhaniṣadyā, iti ya evaṃbhāgīyā apy anye dharmā ayam ucyate kuśalapakṣaprayogaḥ / sa evaṃ kuśalapakṣaprayogo yathāyogaṃ yathā parikīrtitaṃ, yatra kalpayitavyaṃ tatra tatha kalpayati / yena nānuyojyo bhavati garhito laukikānāṃ vinayadharāṇāṃ vinayaśikṣitānāṃ satāṃ samyaggatānām satpuruṣāṇāṃ sahadhārmikāṇām / ayam ucyate kuśalapakṣaprayogādhiṣṭhāna ācāro lokānutkrānto vinayānutkrāntaś ca / ya ebhir ākāraiḥ saṃpanna ācāra iyam ucyata ācārasaṃpat / evaṃ cācārasaṃpanno bhavati //
body.translated_text: Therein, how is the conduct based on the application to the wholesome side conforming to and not transgressing the world and the <s>Vinaya</s>? The wholesome side refers to: self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>), the service and attendance upon teachers and preceptors, likewise the attending upon the sick, establishing in one another the mind of compassion and the gift of consent (<s>chandadāna</s>), recitation, the effort of questioning and <s>Dharma</s>-listening for one who is capable and not lazy, the physical rendering of service to knowledgeable co-practitioners of the holy life, the exhorting of others to undertake the wholesome side and the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, entering into seclusion (<s>pratisaṃlayana</s>) and sitting cross-legged — and whatever other <s>dharmas</s> of this kind: this is called the application to the wholesome side. That application to the wholesome side, as appropriate and as proclaimed, wherever it should be arranged, there and thus one arranges it, so that one is not subject to reproach or censure among worldly people, those who uphold the <s>Vinaya</s>, those trained in the <s>Vinaya</s>, the true, the rightly-conducted, the true persons, and the co-practitioners of the <s>Dharma</s>. This is called the conduct based on the application to the wholesome side, conforming to and not transgressing the world and the <s>Vinaya</s>. One who is accomplished in these aspects of conduct — this is called accomplishment in conduct. Thus one becomes accomplished in conduct.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-a-(1)-iv Ms.12b4L, Sh.40-5, P.20a1, D.17a3, N.19a2, Co.18b6, Ch.402c15
kathaṃ ca gocarasaṃpanno bhavati / pañca bhikṣor agocarāḥ / katame pañca / tadyathā ghoṣo veśyaṃ pānāgāro rājakulaṃ caṇḍālakaṭhinam eva pañcamam iti / ya etāṃs tathāgatapratikṣiptān agocarān varjayitvānyatra gocare caraty anavadye tatra kālenaivaṃ gocarasaṃpanno bhavati //
body.translated_text: And how is one accomplished in one's resort (<s>gocara</s>)? There are five non-resorts for a <s>bhikṣu</s>. Which five? Namely: a singing girl's [house], a prostitute's [house], a tavern, a king's court, and a <s>caṇḍāla</s>'s dwelling as the fifth. One who, avoiding these non-resorts prohibited by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, moves about in other resorts that are blameless — that one at the proper time is accomplished in resort.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-a-(1)-v Ms.12b5L, Sh.41-1, P.20a4, D.17a5, N.19a4, Co.19a1, Ch.402c20
katham aṇumātreṣv avadyeṣu bhayadarśī bhavati / aṇumātram avadyam ucyate kṣudrāṇukṣudrāṇi śikṣāpadāni, yeṣv adhyāpattir vyutthānaṃ ca prajñāyate, teṣāṃ yādhyāpattir idam avadyam aṇumātram / punas tathā hi tasyā adhyāpatter alpakṛcchreṇa vyuttiṣṭhate, yena tad aṇumātram ity (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 68

children.text: ) ucyate / tatra kathaṃ bhayadarśī bhavati / "mā haivāham eṣām adhyāpattihetor abhavyo vā syām aprāptasya prāptaye, anadhigatasyādhigamāya, asākṣātkṛtasya sākṣātkriyāyai, apāyago vā syām apāyagāmī, ātmā vā me apavadet, śāstā vā devatā vā vijñā vā sabrahmacāriṇo dharmatayā vigarheyuḥ, digvidikṣu ca me pāpako varṇakīrtiśabdaśloko 'bhyudgacchet" / sa ebhyo dṛṣṭadharmasāṃparāyikebhyas taddhetukebhyo 'niṣṭebhyo dharmebhyo bhayadarśī bhavati / yena tāni kṣudrāṇukṣudrāṇi śikṣāpadāni jīvitahetor api na saṃcintyādhyāpadyate / kadācit karhicit smṛtisaṃpramoṣād adhyāpanno laghu laghv eva yathādharmaṃ pratikaroti vyuttiṣṭhate / evam aṇumātreṣv avadyeṣu bhayadarśī bhavati //
children.translated_text: Therein, how does one see danger? [Thinking:] "May I not, on account of these transgressions, become incapable of attaining what has not been attained, of realizing what has not been realized, of directly knowing what has not been directly known; or may I not become one bound for a lower realm, going to a lower realm; or may my own self reproach me; or may the teacher, or the deities, or wise co-practitioners of the holy life not rightly censure me; and may an evil reputation, fame, and report not spread about me in the [ten] directions." He sees danger in these unwanted <s>dharmas</s> pertaining to the present life and the next, which have that [transgression] as their cause. Because of this, even for the sake of his life, he does not intentionally commit [a transgression of] those minor and secondary training rules. If at some time he does transgress through a lapse of mindfulness, quickly and promptly he makes amends and rehabilitates himself according to the <s>Dharma</s>. Thus he sees danger in the slightest faults.

body.translated_text: How does one see danger in the slightest faults? The slightest fault refers to the minor and secondary training rules, with respect to which transgression and rehabilitation are recognized. The transgression of these is the slightest fault. And moreover, from that transgression one rises with little difficulty, by which it is called 'slightest.'

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-a-(1)-vi Ms.12b8R, Sh.41-19, P.20b3, D.17b4, N.19b3, Co.19a7, Ch.403a5
kathaṃ samādāya śikṣate śikṣāpadeṣu / āha / pūrvam anena prātimokṣasaṃvarasamādāne jñapticaturthena karmaṇopasaṃpadyamānena katipayānāṃ śikṣāpadānāṃ śarīraṃ śrutaṃ, sātirekaṃ ca tadanyam ardhatṛtīyaṃ śikṣāpadaśataṃ prātimokṣasūtroddiṣṭaṃ pratijñayaivopagataṃ "sarvatra śikṣiṣyāmī"ti, ācāryopādhyāyānām antikāc chrutvā, ālaptakasaṃlaptakasaṃstutakasapriyakānām / ardhārdhamāsaṃ ca prātimokṣasūtroddeśataḥ, tataś ca tena sarvaśikṣāpadasamādānāt prātimokṣasaṃvaraḥ pratilabdhaḥ / tata uttarakālaṃ yeṣu śikṣāpadeṣu kuśalo bhavati tāni tāvan nādhyāpadyate / adhyāpannaś ca yathādharmaṃ pratikaroti / yeṣu punaḥ (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 70

children.text: ) śikṣāpadeṣv akuśalo bhavati, avyutpannabuddhiḥ tāni pūrvaṃ pratijñāsamādānena samādattāny etarhi vyutpattikauśalyatayā samādadāti / tebhyaḥ pūrvaṃ yathāparikīrtitebhyaḥ sthānebhya ācāryasya vopādhyāyasya vā pūrvavat, vyutpattikauśalyatayā ca punaḥ samādāya, yathānuśiṣṭo 'nyūnam anadhikaṃ śikṣate teṣu gurugurusthānīyavyapadiṣṭeṣu śikṣāpadeṣu, aviparītagrāhī ca bhavaty arthasya vyañjanasya ca / evaṃ samādāya śikṣate śikṣāpadeṣv ayam / tāvad vibhaṃgaḥ śīlasaṃvarasya vistarakṛtaḥ //
children.translated_text: training rules in which one is unskilled, in which one's understanding is undeveloped — those that were previously undertaken through the pledge, one now undertakes with skill in understanding. From those previously described sources, from the teacher or the preceptor, as before, and with skill in understanding, having undertaken [them] again, one trains as instructed, neither less nor more, in those training rules designated as weighty and of weighty standing; and one is a correct grasper of both meaning and letter. Thus one undertakes and trains in the training rules — this much is the detailed analysis of the restraint of moral conduct.

body.translated_text: How does one undertake and train in the training rules? He says: Previously, when this one was being fully ordained through a <s>jñapticaturtha</s> (motion-and-three-announcements) <s>karman</s> (formal act) for the undertaking of the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint, the substance of a certain number of training rules was heard, and in addition the two hundred and fifty training rules recited in the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> <s>Sūtra</s> were accepted through the pledge "I will train in everything" — having heard from the teachers and preceptors, and from intimate companions, friends, and dear ones. And from the fortnightly recitation of the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> <s>Sūtra</s>, from that, through the undertaking of all training rules, the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint was obtained. Then, in subsequent time, those training rules in which one is skilled, one does not transgress; and having transgressed, one makes amends according to the <s>Dharma</s>. Those

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-a-(2) Ms.13a4M, Sh.42-21, W.*68-34, P.21a3, D.18a3, N.20a2, Co.19b7, Ch.403a22
tatra katamaḥ samāsārthaḥ / tatrāyaṃ samāsārthas trilakṣaṇa eva śīlaskandhaḥ paridīpito bhagavatā, tadyathāvipraṇāśalakṣaṇaḥ, svabhāvalakṣaṇaḥ, svabhāvaguṇalakṣaṇaś ca //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the summary meaning? The summary meaning here is that the aggregate of moral conduct (<s>śīlaskandha</s>) has been illuminated by the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) under just three marks: namely, the mark of non-degeneration, the mark of intrinsic nature, and the mark of the quality of intrinsic nature.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-a-(2)-i
yathā katham iti yat tāvad āha śīlavān viharatīty anena tāvad avipraṇāśalakṣaṇaṃ śīlasaṃvarasyākhyātam //
body.translated_text: How so? First, when he says 'one dwells as endowed with moral conduct' — by this the mark of non-degeneration of the restraint of moral conduct is declared.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-a-(2)-ii
yat punar āha prātimokṣasaṃvarasaṃvṛta ity anena svabhāvalakṣaṇam ākhyātam //
body.translated_text: And when he says 'restrained by the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint' — by this the mark of intrinsic nature is declared.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-a-(2)-iii, iv, v, vi
yat punar āha / ācāragocarasaṃpanna iti, anena param upanidhāya tathā samādattasya prātimokṣasaṃvarasya guṇalakṣaṇam ākhyātam //
body.translated_text: And when he says 'accomplished in conduct and resort' — by this, the mark of the quality of the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint as thus undertaken, in relation to others, is declared.

body.text: tathāpi pare tām ācāragocarasaṃpadam upalabhyāprasannāś ca prasīdanti, prasannānāṃ ca bhavati bhūyobhāvaḥ, prasannāś ca prasannādhikāraṃ kurvanti / na ca manāṃsi pradūṣayanti, nāvarṇaṃ niścārayanti / anyathā śīlasaṃpannasyācāragocarasaṃpannasyāyaṃ parādhipateyo guṇa ānuśaṃsā na bhavet, (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 72
) or by the reverse of that, there would be only fault for him.

body.translated_text: Moreover, others, observing that accomplishment in conduct and resort, those without faith gain faith, and for those with faith there is an increase [of faith], and the faithful perform faithful deeds. And they do not corrupt [others'] minds, and they do not spread a bad report. Otherwise, for one accomplished in moral conduct and accomplished in conduct and resort, this quality and benefit with respect to others would not exist.

body.text: yat punar āha / aṇumātreṣv avadyeṣu bhayadarśī samādāya śikṣate śīkṣāpadeṣv iti, anenādhyātmādhipateyaguṇānuśaṃsalakṣaṇam ākhyātam / tat kasya hetoḥ / yad apy evam ācāragocarasaṃpannaḥ parādhipateyaṃ guṇānuśaṃsaṃ pratilabheta, api tu śīlaṃ vipādayitvā taddhetos tatpratyayam apāyeṣūpapadyate / abhavyatāṃ vāprāptasya prāptaye pūrvavat //
body.translated_text: As for the statement: "Seeing danger in the slightest faults, he trains by undertaking the training rules" — by this, the quality and benefit characterized by the supremacy of self is declared. What is the reason? Even though one endowed with proper conduct and sphere of activity would obtain the quality and benefit of the supremacy of others, nevertheless, having corrupted one's moral conduct, on account of that cause and condition one would be reborn in the lower realms, or would be incapable of attaining the unattained, as before.

body.text: yat punar aṇumātreṣv avadyeṣu bhayadarśī bhavati / prāg evādhimātreṣu samādāya ca śikṣate śikṣāpadeṣu tasmāt taddhetos tatpratyayaṃ kāyasya bhedāt sugatāv upapadyate / bhavyo vā bhavaty aprāptasya prāptaye pūrvavad / anena kāraṇenādhyātmādhipateyo 'yaṃ śīlasaṃvarasya guṇānuśaṃsa ity ucyate //
body.translated_text: Yet the one who sees danger in even the slightest faults — how much more so in the great ones — and who trains by undertaking the training rules, therefore on account of that cause and condition, upon the dissolution of the body, is reborn in a good destination; or one becomes capable of attaining the unattained, as before. For this reason, this is called the quality and benefit of moral restraint characterized by the supremacy of self.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-a-(2)-i' Ms.13b2L, Sh.44-4, P.21b7, D.18b4, N.20b3, Co.20b1, Ch.403b15
aparaḥ punaḥ paryāyaḥ / samāsato bhagavatā samādattaśīlatā paridīpitā, nairyāṇikaśīlatā ca, śīlabhāvanā ca /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, there is another method. In brief, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) has illuminated the undertaking of moral conduct, the moral conduct leading to liberation, and the cultivation of moral conduct.

body.text: tatra yat tāvad āha / "śīlavān viharatī"ty anena samādattaśīlatākhyātā //
body.translated_text: Therein, as for the statement: "One dwells endowed with moral conduct" — by this, the undertaking of moral conduct has been declared.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-a-(2)-ii'
yat punar āha / "prātimokṣasaṃvarasaṃvṛta" ity anena nairyāṇikaśīlatākhyātā / tathā hi prātimokṣasaṃvarasaṃgṛhītaṃ śīlam adhiśīlaṃ śikṣety ucyate / adhiśīlaṃ ca śikṣāṃ niśritya, adhicittaṃ ca, adhiprajñaṃ ca sikṣāṃ bhāvayaty, evam asau sarvaduḥkhakṣayāya niryāto bhavati / yadutādhiśīlaṃ pratiṣṭhāya pūrvaṃgamaṃ kṛtvā tasmāt prātimokṣasaṃvaro nairyāṇikaṃ śīlam ity ucyate //
body.translated_text: As for the statement: "Restrained by the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> restraint" — by this, the moral conduct leading to liberation has been declared. For the moral conduct comprised by the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> restraint is called the higher training in moral conduct. And relying on the higher training in moral conduct, one cultivates the higher training in mind and the higher training in wisdom — thus one proceeds toward the destruction of all suffering. That is, having established oneself in and having made foremost the higher moral conduct — therefore the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> restraint is called moral conduct leading to liberation.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-a-(2)-iii',iv',v',vi'
yat punar āha / "ācāragocarasaṃpanno 'ṇumātreṣv avadyeṣu bhayadarśī samādāya śikṣate śikṣāpadeṣv" ity anena śīlabhāvanākhyātā / ebhir ākārais tat prātimokṣasaṃvaraśīlaṃ bhāvayitavyam / evaṃ ca bhāvitaṃ subhāvitaṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> I 74

body.translated_text: As for the statement: "Endowed with proper conduct and sphere of activity, seeing danger in the slightest faults, he trains by undertaking the training rules" — by this, the cultivation of moral conduct has been declared. By these aspects, that <s>Prātimokṣa</s> moral restraint is to be cultivated. And thus cultivated, it becomes well-cultivated

body.text: sa eṣa ekaḥ śīlasaṃvaraḥ ṣaḍākāradeśanāpratyupasthāno veditavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: This single moral restraint should be understood as set forth through a teaching of six aspects.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-b Ms.13b5L, Sh.44-21, W.*69-22, P.22a6, D.19a3, N.21a1, Co.21a1, Ch.403b29
sa khalu eṣa śīlasaṃvaro daśabhiḥ kāraṇair vipanno veditavyaḥ / viparyayād daśabhiś caiva kāraṇaiḥ saṃpannaḥ //
body.translated_text: Indeed, this moral restraint should be understood as corrupted through ten causes. And by their reverse, through ten causes it is accomplished.

body.text: katamair daśabhiḥ kāraṇair vipanno bhavati / ādita eva durgṛhīto bhavati, atilīno bhavati, atisṛto bhavati, pramādakausīdyaparigṛhīto bhavati, mithyāpraṇihito bhavati, ācāravipattyā parigṛhīto bhavati, ājīvavipattyā parigṛhīto bhavati, antadvayapatito bhavati, anairyāṇiko bhavati, samādānaparibhraṣṭaś ca bhavati //
body.translated_text: Through which ten causes is it corrupted? From the very beginning it is badly grasped; it is too lax; it is too loose; it is seized by heedlessness and laziness; it is wrongly directed; it is seized by corruption of conduct; it is seized by corruption of livelihood; it has fallen into the two extremes; it is not leading to liberation; and it is one who has fallen away from the undertaking.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-b-(1) Ms.13b6M/9b6M, Sh.45-8, P.22b1, D.19a5, N.21a3, Co.21a3, Ch.403c6
tatra katham ādito durgṛhītaṃ śīlaṃ bhavati / yathāpīhaikatyo rājābhinirṇīto vā pravrajitaś, caurābhinirṇīto vā, ṛṇārto vā, bhayārto vā, ajīvikā bhayabhīto vā, na śrāmaṇyāya, na brāhmaṇyāya, nātmaśamāya, nātmadamāya, nātmaparinirvāṇāya / evam ādito durgṛhīto bhavati //
body.translated_text: Therein, how is moral conduct badly grasped from the very beginning? Just as here someone has gone forth because impelled by a king, or impelled by a thief, or oppressed by debt, or afflicted by fear, or fearing for one's livelihood — not for the purpose of the ascetic life, not for the brahminical life, not for self-pacification, not for self-taming, not for one's own <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final liberation). Thus it is badly grasped from the very beginning.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-b-(2) Ms.9b6M, Sh.46-4, P.22b4, D.19a7, N.21a5, Co.21a5, Ch.403c13
katham atilīno bhavati / yathāpīhaikatyo 'lajjī bhavati mandakaukṛtyaḥ, śaithilikaḥ śithilakārī śikṣāpadeṣu / evam atilīno bhavati //
body.translated_text: How is it too lax? Just as here someone is shameless, with little remorse, slack and lax in the training rules. Thus it is too lax.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-b-(3) Ms.9b7L, Sh.46-7, P.22b5, D.19b1, N.21a6, Co.21a6, Ch.403c15
katham atisṛto bhavati / yathāpīhaikatyo durgṛhītagrāhī bhavaty asthānakaukṛtyaḥ / saukṛtyakaraṇīyeṣu sthāneṣu kaukṛtyāyamānaḥ / asthāne pareṣām antike paribhavacittaṃ vāghātaṃ votpādayati pravedayati / evam atisṛtaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: How is it too loose? Just as here someone grasps what is badly grasped, has remorse where there is no cause for it, and where there is cause for well-doing, one generates remorse. And inappropriately, in the presence of others, one gives rise to and experiences a mind of contempt or a mind of harm. Thus it is too loose.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-b-(4) Ms.10a1L, Sh.46-11, P.22b7, D.19b2, N.21a7, Co,21b1, Ch,403c19
kathaṃ pramādakausīdyaparigṛhītaṃ bhavati / yathāpīhaikatyo yām atītam adhvānam upādāyāpattim āpannaḥ, sā cānena smṛtisaṃpramoṣād ekatyā na yathādharmaṃ pratikṛtā bhavati / yathātītam adhvānam upādāya, evam anāgataṃ vartamānam adhvānam upādāya yām āpattim āpanno bhavati, sā cānena smṛtisaṃpramoṣād ekatyā na yathādharmaṃ pratikṛtā bhavati / na ca pūrvam evāpatter āyatyām anadhyāpattaye tīvram autsukyam āpadyate, yan nv "ahaṃ tathā tathā careyaṃ vihareyam, yathā yathā caran viharaṃś cāpattiṃ nādhyāpadyeya" / tathā ca tathā carati viharati yathāpattim adhyāpadyate / so 'nena pūrvāntasahagatenāparāntasahagatena madhyāntasahagatena pūrvakālakaraṇīyena sahānucareṇa ca pramādena samanvāgataḥ nidrāsukhaṃ śayanasukhaṃ pārśvasukhaṃ ca svīkaroti / adakṣaś ca bhavaty alasaḥ, anutthānasaṃpannaḥ, na kartā bhavati vijñānāṃ sabrahmacāriṇāṃ kāyena vaiyāpṛtyam / evaṃ pramādakausīdyaparigṛhītaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: How is it seized by heedlessness and laziness? Just as here someone, taking into account past time, has fallen into an offense, and that offense, due to loss of mindfulness, has in part not been properly corrected. Just as taking into account past time, so too taking into account future and present time, whatever offense one has fallen into, that offense, due to loss of mindfulness, has in part not been properly corrected. And one does not beforehand, prior to the offense, develop intense concern for not falling into offense in the future, thinking: "May I so conduct myself and dwell that, conducting myself and dwelling thus, I would not fall into an offense." Yet one conducts oneself and dwells in such a way that one does fall into offense. Being endowed with this heedlessness — accompanied by the past, the future, and the present, together with what should have been done earlier and with subsequent behavior — one indulges in the pleasure of sleep, the pleasure of lying down, and the pleasure of reclining. And one is unskillful, lazy, devoid of initiative, and does not bodily render service to one's wise co-practitioners in the holy life. Thus it is seized by heedlessness and laziness.

body.text:
(I)-C-iII-4-b-(5) Ms.10a3R, Sh.47-7, P.23a6, D.19b6, N.21b5, Co.21b7, Ch.404a4
kathaṃ mithyāpraṇihitaṃ bhavati / yathāpīhaikatyaḥ praṇidhāya brahmacaryaṃ carati / "anenāhaṃ śīlena vā vratena vā tapasā vā brahmacaryavāsena vā devo vā syāṃ devānyatamo vā" / lābhasatkārakāmo bhavati, parataḥ lābhasatkāraṃ prārthayate, lābhasatkārasya spṛhayati / evaṃ mithyāpraṇihitaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: How is it wrongly directed? Just as here someone conducts the holy life with an aspiration: "By this moral conduct, or by this vow, or by this austerity, or by this life of celibacy, may I become a god or some kind of deity." One desires gain and honor, seeks gain and honor from others, and craves gain and honor. Thus it is wrongly directed.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-b-(6) Ms.10a4M, Sh.47-13, P.23a8, D.20a1, N.21b7, Co.22a1, Ch.404a9
katham ācāravipattyā parigṛhītaṃ bhavati / yathāpīhaikatya īryāpathaṃ vādhiṣṭhāyetikaraṇīyaṃ vā kuśalapakṣaprayogaṃ vā lokotkrāntaś ca bhavati vinayotkrāntaś ca pūrvavad / evam ācāravipattyā parigṛhītaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: How is it seized by corruption of conduct? Just as here someone, either maintaining a deportment, or performing required duties, or engaging in wholesome practices, transgresses worldly norms and transgresses the <s>Vinaya</s> (discipline), as before. Thus it is seized by corruption of conduct.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-b-(7) Ms.10a5M, Sh.47-17, P.23b2, D.20a2, N.22a1, Co.22a2, Ch.404a13
katham ājīvavipattyā parigṛhītaṃ bhavati / yathāpīhaikatyo maheccho bhavaty asaṃtuṣṭo duṣpoṣo durbharajātīyaḥ / sa cādharmeṇa cīvaraṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> I 78

children.text:
) paryeṣate na dharmeṇa, adharmeṇa piṇḍapātaṃ śayanāsanaṃ glānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraṃ paryeṣate na dharmeṇa / sa ca cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaisajyapariṣkārahetor ātmano guṇasaṃbhāvanānimittam aprākṛtaṃ viṭhapitam īryāpathaṃ kalpayati, anuddhatendriyatām acapalendriyatāṃ śāntendriyatāṃ ca pareṣām upadarśayati / yenāsya pare guṇasaṃbhāvanājñātā dātavyaṃ kartavyaṃ manyante, yaduta cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaisajyapariṣkārān / dhvāṅkṣaś ca bhavati mukharaḥ pragalbhaḥ kelāyitā nāmagotrodgṛhītā bahuśruto bhavati dharmadharaḥ / lābhakāraṇād eva ca pareṣāṃ dharmaṃ saṃlapati buddhabhāṣitaṃ vā śrāvakabhāṣitaṃ vā, ātmano vā guṇān bhūtān vā kiṃcid vā punaḥ samāropya svayam eva vaktā bhavati, lāpayati vā paraiḥ / anuttareṇa vopadarśayitā, cīvarārthī vā, anyatamānyatamena vā śrāmaṇakena pariṣkāreṇārthī prabhūtena vāgratareṇa vā / avihanyamāno 'pi prākṛtasya cīvarasyopadarśayitā bhavati, apy evarn śrāddhā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayaḥ cīvareṇa vighātaṃ saṃlakṣayitvā prabhūtaṃ praṇītaṃ cīvaraṃ dātavyaṃ kartavyaṃ maṃsyante / yathā cīvaram evam anyatamānyatamaṃ śrāmaṇakaṃ jīvitapariṣkāram / śrāddhānāṃ ca brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnām antikād yathākāmaṃ vālabhamānaḥ, asatsu vāsaṃvidyamāneṣu bhogeṣv alabhamāna evaṃ coparodhena yācate niṣpiṣya, niṣpiṣyāpi cainān paruṣayaty api / hīnaṃ vā punar labdhvā tathā saṃvidyamāneṣu bhogeṣu taṃ lābhaṃ paṃsayaty avasādayati / saṃmukhaṃ ca dātāraṃ dānapatim evaṃ cāha "haṃ bho, kulaputra, santy eke kulaputrāḥ kuladuhitaraś ca ye tavāntikān nīcakulīnatarāś ca daridratarāś ca / te punar evaṃ caivaṃ ca praṇītadāyino mana-āpadāyinaś ca / kasmāt tvaṃ teṣām antikād uccakulīnataraś cāḍhyataraś ca samāna evam amanā-āpadāyī, cāpraṇītaparīttadāyī ce"ti /
ya ebhir ākāraiḥ kuhanāṃ vā niśritya lapanāṃ vā naimittikatāṃ vā (
children.translated_text: ) not by righteous means; one seeks almsfood, lodging, and medicine and requisites for the sick by unrighteous means, not by righteous means. And for the sake of obtaining robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicine and requisites for the sick, one contrives an artificial, fabricated deportment suggestive of one's own spiritual qualities, and displays to others an appearance of calm faculties, non-agitated faculties, and peaceful faculties — whereby others, perceiving the suggestion of spiritual qualities, consider that gifts should be given, service should be rendered — namely, robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicine and requisites for the sick. And one is a crow-like person, talkative, bold, a jester, one who takes note of names and lineages; one is learned, a bearer of the <s>Dharma</s>; and only for the sake of gain does one discourse the <s>Dharma</s> to others — whether spoken by the <s>Buddha</s> or spoken by the <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) — or one speaks of one's own qualities, whether real or somewhat exaggerated, by oneself or has others speak of them; or one displays by the unsurpassed [method]; and whether one desires robes or some other ascetic requisite, whether more abundant or more excellent. Even when not deprived, one displays one's ordinary robe, [thinking]: "Perhaps faithful <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders, seeing the deficiency in robes, will consider that more abundant and excellent robes should be given and service should be rendered." Just as with robes, so too with any other ascetic requisite for livelihood. And when not obtaining from faithful <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders as one wishes, or when not obtaining due to non-existent and unavailable resources — one begs with annoyance, pressing hard; and even after pressing hard, one speaks harshly to them. Or again, having obtained something inferior even when resources are available, one disparages and belittles that gain. And face to face, one addresses the donor and patron thus: "Ho, sir, good son! There are certain sons and daughters of good family who are of lower birth and poorer than you. Yet they give such excellent gifts and are gratifying in mind. Why then are you, who are of higher birth and wealthier than them, not gratifying in mind and a giver of unexcellent, meager gifts?" One who by these modes, resorting to hypocrisy, or flattery, or hinting, or
<s>Śbh</s> I 80

children.text: ) naiṣpeṣikatāṃ vā lābhena vā lābhaṃ niścikīrṣatāṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārān parataḥ paryeṣate, so 'dharmeṇa / yaḥ punar adharmeṇa so 'sya bhavati mithyājīvaḥ / evaṃ tac chīlam ājīvavipattyā parigṛhītaṃ bhavati //
children.translated_text: ) browbeating, or seeking gain by means of gain, seeks robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicine and requisites for the sick from others — that one does so unrighteously. And whatever one obtains unrighteously — that constitutes one's wrong livelihood. Thus that moral conduct is seized by corruption of livelihood.

body.translated_text: How is it seized by corruption of livelihood? Just as here someone is one of great desires, discontented, hard to nurture, of the type that is difficult to support. And one seeks robes by unrighteous means,

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-b-(8) Ms.10b5M, Sh.49-22, P.24b4, D.21a1, N.22b6, Co.23a1, Ch.404b16
katham antadvayapatitaṃ bhavati / yathāpīhaikatyaḥ kāmasukhallikānuyukto bhavaty adhyavasitaḥ, tān parataḥ pratilabdhān dharmeṇa vādharmeṇa vā cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaisajyapariṣkārān paribhuṅkte, ādīnavādarśī niḥsaraṇam aprajānan / ayam ucyata eko 'ntaḥ / punar aparam ihaikatya ātmaklamathānuyukto bhavaty anekaparyāyeṇātmānam ātāpayati saṃtāpayati kaṣṭavratasamādāyī ca bhavati / tadyathā kaṇṭhakā pāśrayo vā bhavati bhasmāpāśrayo musalāpāśrayaḥ phalakāpāśrayo bhavati / utkuṭukasthito bhavaty utkuṭukaprahāṇayogam anuyuktaḥ / agniparicārako bhavati, yāvat trir apy agniṃ paricarati / udakam adhyāroho bhavati, yāvat trir apy udakam adhyārohati / ekapādakaḥ sthitvā yataḥ sūryas tataḥ parivartate / iti yo vā punar apy evaṃbhāgīya ātmaklamathānuyogaḥ/ ayam ucyate dvitīyo 'ntaḥ / evam antadvayapatitaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: How has it fallen into the two extremes? Just as here someone is devoted to the pursuit of sensual pleasure, attached to it — one enjoys those robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicine and requisites for the sick obtained from others, whether by righteous or unrighteous means, without seeing the danger and not understanding the escape. This is called one extreme. Furthermore, here someone is devoted to self-mortification, torments and afflicts oneself in many ways, and undertakes painful vows — such as one who resorts to thorns, or resorts to ashes, or resorts to a pestle, or resorts to a plank. One stands in the squatting posture and is engaged in the practice of abandonment by squatting. One tends the sacrificial fire, and tends the fire up to three times. One enters the water, and enters the water up to three times. Standing on one foot, one turns toward the sun. And whatever other similar practice belongs to the pursuit of self-mortification — this is called the second extreme. Thus it has fallen into the two extremes.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-b-(9) Ms.11a1R, Sh.50-16, P.25a3, D.21a6, N.23a5, Co.23a6, Ch.404b26
katham anairyāṇikaṃ bhavati / yathāpīhaikatyaḥ śīlaṃ vā vrataṃ vā dṛṣṭyā parāmṛśati / "anenaiva śīlena vā vratena vā śuddhir bhaviṣyati / muktir niryāṇaṃ bhaviṣyatī"ti / sarvaṃ ca śīlam ito bāhyānāṃ surakṣitam api suviśuddham api tad upamayā viśuddhyānairyāṇikam ity ucyate / evam anairyāṇikaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-4-b-(9) — How does it become non-conducive to liberation? Just as here someone grasps at moral conduct or vows through [wrong] views, thinking: "By this very moral conduct or vow alone, purification will come about; liberation and deliverance will come about." And all moral conduct of those outside [the teaching], even if well-guarded, even if well-purified — that is called non-conducive to liberation by way of comparison with [true] purity. Thus it becomes non-conducive to liberation.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-b-(10) Ms.11a2R, Sh.51-4, P.25a6, D.21b1, N.23a6, Co.23b1, Ch.404c1
kathaṃ samādānaparibhraṣṭaṃ bhavati / yathāpīhaikatyaḥ sarveṇa sarvam alajjī bhavati nirapekṣaḥ śrāmaṇye, sa ca bhavati duḥśīlaḥ pāpadharmā antaḥpūtir avasrutaḥ kaśambakajātaḥ śaṃkhasvarasamācāraḥ, aśramaṇaḥ śramaṇapratijñaḥ, abrahmacārī brahmacāripratijñaḥ evam samādānaparibhraṣṭaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-4-b-(10) — How does it become one who has fallen from the undertaking? Just as here someone is completely shameless in every way, without regard for the ascetic life, and he is of bad conduct, evil in nature, inwardly rotten, oozing, arisen from refuse, of conch-shell-sounding conduct — a non-ascetic claiming to be an ascetic, a non-celibate claiming to be celibate. Thus it becomes one who has fallen from the undertaking.

body.text: ebhir daśabhiḥ kāraṇair vipannaṃ śīlaṃ śīlavipattir ity uktā bhagavatā / api ca śīlavyasanam apy uktaṃ bhagavatā / tac caibhyaḥ kāraṇebhyo dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāṃ veditavyaṃ, yā cānairyāṇikatā yaś ca samādānabhraṃśaḥ, tadanyaiś ca kāraṇaiḥ śīlavipattir eva veditavyā //
body.translated_text: Through these ten causes, corrupted moral conduct has been called 'corruption of moral conduct' by the <s>Bhagavat</s>. Moreover, 'calamity of moral conduct' has also been spoken of by the <s>Bhagavat</s>. That should be understood through two of these causes: namely, non-conduciveness to liberation and falling from the undertaking. Through the other causes, it should be understood as corruption of moral conduct alone.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-c Ms.11a4M, Sh.51-16, P.25b3, D.21b4, N.23b3, Co.23b5, Ch.404c10
eṣām eva ca kṛṣṇapaksavyavasthitānāṃ kāraṇānāṃ viparyayeṇa śuklapakṣyaiḥ kāraṇaiḥ śīlasaṃpattir veditavyā śīlaviśuddhiś ca //
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-4-c — By the reverse of these very causes established on the dark side, through the causes of the bright side, the accomplishment of moral conduct and the purification of moral conduct should be understood.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-d Ms.11a4R, Sh.52-1, W.'69-36, P.25b4, D.21b5, N.23b4, Co.23b6, Ch.404c11
kvacit punar bhagavatā śīlaṃ mūlārthenoktam / yathoktam /
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-4-d — In some places the <s>Bhagavat</s> has spoken of moral conduct using the term 'root.' As it is said:

children.translated_text: "One should be well-established in root, delighting in the pacification of the mind,

children.text: saṃyukto ca visaṃyukto dṛṣṭyādṛṣṭyāryapāpayā // iti gāthā //
children.translated_text: connected and disconnected with the noble and evil views." Thus the verse.

body.text: kvacid alaṃkāraśabdenoktaṃ / yathoktaṃ / śīlālaṃkārasaṃpanno bhikṣur vā bhikṣuṇī vā / akuśalaṃ prajahāti kuśalaṃ bhāvayati /
body.translated_text: In some places it is spoken of using the term 'ornament.' As it is said: "A <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) or <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> (nun) accomplished in the ornament of moral conduct abandons the unwholesome and cultivates the wholesome."

body.text: kvacid anulepanaśabdenoktam / yatrāha / śīlānulepanasaṃpanno bhikṣur vā bhikṣuṇī veti pūrvavat /
body.translated_text: In some places it is spoken of using the term 'ointment.' Where it says: "A <s>bhikṣu</s> or <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> accomplished in the ointment of moral conduct" — and so on as before.

body.text: kvacid gandhaśabdenoktam / asti tad ānanda gandhajātam yasyānuvātam api gandho vāti, prativātam apy, anuvātam api prativātam api gandho vāti /
body.translated_text: In some places it is spoken of using the term 'fragrance.' Where it says: "There is, <s>Ānanda</s>, a kind of fragrance whose scent blows with the wind, against the wind, and both with and against the wind."

body.text: kvacid sucaritaśabdenoktam / yatrāha / kāyasucaritasyeṣṭo vipāko dṛṣṭe dharme 'bhisaṃparāye ca evaṃ vāksucaritasya /
body.translated_text: In some places it is spoken of using the term 'good conduct.' Where it says: "The wished-for result of good bodily conduct is in this visible world and in the hereafter; likewise of good verbal conduct."

body.text: kvacid saṃvaraśabdenoktam / yatrāha / dātā dānapatiḥ śīlavān bhavati / saṃvarasthāyy āgamadṛṣṭiḥ phaladarśī //
body.translated_text: In some places it is spoken of using the term 'restraint.' Where it says: "A giver, a lord of giving, is virtuous, established in restraint, possessing the view based on scripture, seeing the fruit."

body.text: api coktam / śīlavān viharati, prātimokṣasaṃvarasaṃvṛta iti vistaraḥ //
body.translated_text: And it is also said: "One lives virtuously, restrained by the <s>prātimokṣa</s> (monastic code) restraint" — and so on in detail.

kena kāraṇena bhagavatā śīlaṃ mūlaśabdenoktaṃ pratiṣṭhārthādhārārtho mūlārthaḥ / tac caitac chīlaṃ sarveṣām eva laukikalokottarāṇāṃ guṇānām anavadyānām agryānāṃ pravarānām sukhāhārāṇāṃ, pratiṣṭhāsthānīyaṃ (

body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-4-d-(1) — For what reason has the <s>Bhagavat</s> spoken of moral conduct using the term 'root'? The meaning of 'root' is the meaning of foundation and support. And this moral conduct serves as the foundation for all worldly and supramundane qualities that are blameless, supreme, excellent, and conducive to happiness,

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-d-(2) Ms.11b2L, Sh.53-4, P.26a7, D.22a6, N.24a5, Co.24a7, Ch.405a7

body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-4-d-(2) — For what reason is moral conduct designated by the term 'ornament'? It is said: Those other ornaments, such as necklaces, bracelets, armlets, rings, or garlands of gold and silver — so long as one is young, a child, dark-haired, endowed with the freshness of youth, those ornaments when worn produce a measure of beauty. But not so for one who is old, aged, greatly advanced in years — whether eighty or ninety — with broken teeth and grey hair; apart from that, when adorned with those ornaments, one appears as if mocked. And when calamity of health, calamity of wealth, or calamity of relatives has befallen, [ornaments] do not bring beauty. But moral conduct produces beauty for all persons at all times. Therefore it is spoken of using the term 'ornament.'

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-d-(3) Ms.11b3R, Sh.54-9, P.26b3, D.22b1, N.24b1, Co.24b3, Ch.405a16

body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-4-d-(3) — For what reason is moral conduct spoken of using the term 'ointment'? Indeed, the wholesome and blameless undertaking of moral conduct removes the burning of body and the burning of mind caused by all undertakings of bad conduct — as sandalwood ointment or camphor ointment [removes burning] for one scorched by heat when the season of the greatest summer heat has arrived. For this reason moral conduct is spoken of using the term 'ointment.'

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-d-(4) Ms.11b4R, Sh.54-15, P.26b6, D.22b3, N.24b3, Co.24b5, Ch.405a21

body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-4-d-(4) — For what reason is moral conduct spoken of using the term 'fragrance'? Indeed, for a virtuous person, fame, glory, renown, and good reputation spread in all directions and sub-directions. Just as the pleasing scent of various

body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-4-d-(5) — For what reason is moral conduct spoken of using the term 'good conduct'? This conduct leads to happiness, leads to heaven, leads to good destinations. This conduct is therefore called 'good conduct.'

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-d-(6) Ms.11b6M, Sh.55-2, P.27a2, D.22b6, N.24b5, Co.25a1, Ch.405a27

body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-4-d-(6) — For what reason is moral conduct spoken of using the term 'restraint'? This <s>dharma</s> is of the nature of cessation, characterized by cessation, of the nature of abstention. Therefore it is spoken of using the term 'restraint.'

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-e Ms.11b7M, Sh.55-4, P.27a3, D.22b7, N.24b6, Co.25a2, Ch.405a29

body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-4-e — Moreover, for this moral restraint there is a threefold examination as a cause of purification. What threefold? Namely: examination of bodily action, examination of verbal action, and examination of mental action.

body.text:

children.translated_text: Śbh I 90

children.text: ) na karoti, nānuprayacchati / sacet punar jānāty avyābādhikaṃ me etat kāyakarma kuśalaṃ pūrvavat, sa karoti tat kāyena karma na pratisaṃharati, anuprayacchati / yad apy anenātītam adhvānam upādāya kāyena karma kṛtaiḥ bhavati / tad apy abhīkṣṇaṃ pratyavekṣate / "kiṃ nu vyābādhikaṃ me etat pūrvavat / sacet sa evaṃ pratyavekṣmāṇo jānāti vyābādhikaṃ me etat" kāyakarma pūrvavat / savijñānāṃ sabrahmacāriṇām antike pratideśayati, yathādharmaṃ pratikaroti / sacet punar evaṃ pratyavekṣamāṇo jānāty avyābādhikaṃ me etat kāyakarma pūrvavat / sa tenaiva prītiprāmodyenāhorātrānuśikṣī bahulaṃ viharaty, evam asya tat kāyakarma supratyavekṣitaṃ ca bhavati, suviśodhitaṃ ca yadutātītānāgatapratyutpanneṣv adhvasu //
children.translated_text: that action, does not proceed with it. But if one knows: "This bodily action of mine is non-harmful, wholesome" — as before — one performs that bodily action, does not withdraw, and proceeds with it. And whatever bodily action one has done in the past — that too one frequently examines: "Is this harmful to me?" — as before. If, examining thus, one knows: "This bodily action of mine was harmful" — as before — one confesses to knowledgeable fellow practitioners and makes amends according to the <s>Dharma</s>. But if, examining thus, one knows: "This bodily action of mine was non-harmful" — as before — one dwells abundantly, training day and night with that very joy and gladness. Thus that bodily action of one's becomes well-examined and well-purified — namely, in the past, future, and present periods.

body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-4-e-(1) — How does one examining these actions purify the moral restraint? Whatever action has been intended to be done with the body, one examines it thus: "Is this bodily action of mine harmful to myself or to others, unwholesome, giving rise to suffering, bearing the fruit of suffering? Or is this bodily action of mine non-harmful to myself and to others, wholesome, giving rise to happiness, bearing the fruit of happiness?" If, examining thus, one knows: "This bodily action of mine is harmful to myself or to others, unwholesome, giving rise to suffering, bearing the fruit of suffering," one withdraws and does not carry out

body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-4-e-(3) — The mind arises dependent on past formations; dependent on future and present formations the mind arises. That mind one frequently examines: "Is this mind of mine harmful?" — as before. So long as [it is harmful], one does not generate [it], one withdraws, one does not proceed with that mental action. But on the bright side, one generates [it], does not withdraw, and proceeds with that mental action. Thus that mental action of one's becomes examined and well-purified — namely, in the past, future, and present periods.

body.translated_text: What is the reason? In the past period, in the future period, and in the present period, whatever

frequently examine, remembering the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s>."

body.translated_text: Therein, the investigating thus: "Is that bodily action, verbal action, mental action harmful to me?" — in detail as before — this is the examination. But the withdrawing from some [actions], confessing, and proceeding with others, dwelling abundantly and training day and night with that very joy and gladness — this is called the purification.

body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-4-f — Therein, for the moral restraint thus purified, ten benefits should be understood.

body.text: katame daśa //

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-f-(1) Ms.8a8R, Sh.59-1, P.28a8, D.24a1, N.26a1, Co.26a4, Ch.405c13
iha śīlavān puruṣapudgalaḥ śīlaviśuddhim ātmanaḥ pratyavekṣamāṇo 'vipratisāraṃ protilabhate / avipratisāriṇaḥ prāmodyaṃ pramuditacittasya prītir jāyate / prītamanasaḥ kāyaḥ praśrabhyate / sa praśrabdhakāyaḥ sukhaṃ vedayate / sukhitasya cittaṃ samādhīyate samāhitacitto yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / yathābhūtaṃ paśyati / yathābhūtaṃ jānan paśyan nirvidyate nirviṇṇo virajyate, virakto vimucyate,vimuktasya vimukto 'smī"ti jñānadarśanaṃ bhavati / yāvan nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvāti / yac chīlavān puruṣapudgalaḥ śīlaviśuddhyadhipateyam avipratisāraṃ pratilabhate / anupūrveṇa yāvan nirvāṇagamanāyāyaṃ prathamaḥ śīlānuśaṃsaḥ //
body.translated_text: Here, a virtuous person, examining his own purity of moral conduct (<s>śīlaviśuddhi</s>), obtains non-remorse (<s>avipratisāra</s>). For one without remorse, joy (<s>prāmodya</s>) [arises]; for one with a joyful mind, rapture (<s>prīti</s>) is born. For one with a rapturous mind, the body becomes tranquil (<s>praśrabdhi</s>). He, with a tranquil body, experiences happiness (<s>sukha</s>). For one who is happy, the mind becomes concentrated (<s>samādhi</s>); with a concentrated mind, he understands as it truly is, he sees as it truly is. Knowing and seeing as it truly is, he becomes disenchanted; being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate; being dispassionate, he is liberated; for one who is liberated, the knowledge-and-vision arises: 'I am liberated' — up to his attaining <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the <s>nirvāṇa</s> element without residue. That a virtuous person, through the dominance of the purity of moral conduct, obtains non-remorse, and gradually up to the attainment of <s>nirvāṇa</s> — this is the first benefit of moral conduct (<s>śīlānuśaṃsa</s>). //

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-f-(2) Ms.8b2M, Sh.60-12, P.28b6, D.24a5, N.26a5, Co.26b1, Ch.405c22
punar aparaṃ śīlavān puruṣapudglaḥ maraṇakālasamaye pratyupasthite, "kṛtaṃ bata me sukṛtaṃ kāyena vācā manasā, na kṛtaṃ bata me duścaritaṃ kāyena pūrvavat" iti "yā gatiḥ kṛtapuṇyānāṃ kṛtakuśalānām kṛtabhayabhīrutrāṇānāṃ tāṃ gatiṃ pretya, gamiṣyāmī"ti dvitīyam avipratisāraṃ pratilabhate sugatigamanāya, avipratisāriṇo hi puruṣapudgalasya bhadrakaṃ maranaṃ bhavati bhadrikā kālakriyā bhadrako 'bhisaṃparāyaḥ / ayaṃ dvitīyaḥ śīlānuśaṃsaḥ //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, a virtuous person, when the time of death approaches: 'Indeed, I have performed good deeds with body, speech, and mind; indeed, I have not performed misconduct with body — as before' — and 'Whatever is the destiny of those who have made merit, who have done what is wholesome, who have made a shelter from fear and terror — to that destiny, after passing away, I shall go' — he obtains the second non-remorse, for going to a good destiny. For a person without remorse, death is auspicious, the passing is auspicious, the future state is auspicious. This is the second benefit of moral conduct. //

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-f-(3) Ms.8b3R, Sh.60-1, P.29a2, D.24b1, N.26b1, Co.26b4, Ch.406a1

body.translated_text: Furthermore, for a virtuous person, in all directions a fair reputation, fame, renown, praise, and acclaim go forth. This is the third benefit of moral conduct. //

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-f-(4) Ms.8b4M, Sh.61-3, P.29a3, D.24b2, N.26b2, Co.26b5, Ch.406a3

body.translated_text: Furthermore, a virtuous person sleeps happily and awakens happily, with a body and mind free from burning. This is the fourth benefit of moral conduct. //

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-f-(5) Ms.8b4R, Sh.61-6, P.29a4, D.24b3, N.26b2, Co.26b6, Ch.406a5

body.translated_text: Furthermore, a virtuous person, when asleep, sees auspicious dreams, not inauspicious ones. This is the fifth benefit of moral conduct. //

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-f-(6) Ms.8b5L, Sh.61-9, P.29a5, D.24b3, N.26b3, Co.26b7, Ch.406a7

body.translated_text: Furthermore, a virtuous person is not afraid and does not tremble — like a wounded person — when [approaching] an assembly, not even with the thought: 'There is indeed something of mine that is blameworthy.' This is the sixth benefit of moral conduct. //

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-4-f-(7) Ms.8b5M, Sh.61-12, P.29a6, D.24b4, N.26b4, Co.27a1, Ch.406a9

children.text: ) iti viditvā mitratāṃ vāpadyate madhyasthatāṃ vā / ayaṃ saptamaḥ śīlānuśaṃsaḥ //

body.translated_text: Furthermore, a virtuous person, even with little effort, easily accomplishes the <s>dharmas</s> conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣya dharmas</s>). This is the ninth benefit of moral conduct. //
