(I)-C-IIl-4-f-(10) Ms.8b7M, Sh.62-5, P.29b4, D.25a2, Co.27a6, N.27a1, Ch.406a21
punar aparaṃ pūrvavat sarvapraṇidhānāni samṛdhyanti / saced ākāṃkṣate "kāmadhātau kṣatriyamahāśālakulānāṃ brāhmaṇamahāśālakulānāṃ vā gṛhapatimahāśālakulānāṃ vā caturmahārājakāyikānāṃ vā devānāṃ, trāyastriṃśānāṃ vā yāmānāṃ tuṣitānāṃ nirmāṇaratīnāṃ paranirmitavaśavartināṃ devānāṃ sabhāgatāyopapadyeya" iti, upapadyate yathāpi tad viśuddhatvāc chīlānāṃ /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, as before, all his aspirations are fulfilled.

body.translated_text: If he wishes: 'Oh, may I attain the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditation absorptions) and dwell happily in this very life! May I be reborn in the common destiny of the gods of the form realm (<s>rūpopaga devas</s>)!'

body.translated_text: If he wishes: 'May I attain those peaceful liberations, transcending [the form realm], and dwell having attained the formless [absorptions]; may I be reborn in the common destiny of the gods of the formless realm!'

body.text: saced ākāṃkṣate "atyantaniṣṭhanirvāṇam adhigaccheyam" ity adhigacchati // tac ca viśuddhatvāc chīlānāṃ sarvatra ca vītarāgatvāt /
body.translated_text: If he wishes: 'May I attain the absolutely final <s>nirvāṇa</s>!' — he attains it. And that is because of the purity of his moral conduct and the absence of passion everywhere.

body.text: ayaṃ daśamaḥ śīlānuśaṃso veditavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: This is to be understood as the tenth benefit of moral conduct. //

body.text: nirdiṣṭaḥ śīlaskandho vibhāgaśaḥ, nirdiṣṭā vipattisaṃpattiḥ, nirdiṣṭāni paryāyanāmāni, nirdiṣṭā pariśuddhipratyavekṣā, nirdiṣṭo 'nuśaṃsaḥ //
body.translated_text: The aggregate of moral conduct (<s>śīlaskandha</s>) has been explained in detail; the failure and accomplishment have been explained; the synonymous names have been explained; the examination of purity has been explained; [and the benefits have been explained].

body.text: sa eṣa sarvākāraparipūrṇaḥ śīlasaṃvaraḥ saṃbhāraparigṛhīta ākhyāta uttano vivṛtaḥ prakāśito, yatrātmakāmaiḥ śrāmaṇyabrāhmaṇyakāmaiḥ kulaputraiḥ śikṣitavyam //
body.translated_text: This moral restraint (<s>śīlasaṃvara</s>), complete in every aspect, included in the requisites, has been declared, made manifest, revealed, and illuminated — wherein those who desire their own welfare, aspiring for the ascetic life (<s>śrāmaṇya</s>) and the brahminical life (<s>brāhmaṇya</s>), should train.

body.text:
uddānam /
vibhaṅgas trividho jñeyaḥ saṃpad daśavidhā bhavet /
paryāyaś ca ṣaḍākāro viśuddhis trividhā matā /
anuśaṃso daśavidhaḥ eṣo 'sau śīlasaṃvaraḥ /
body.translated_text:
<s>Uddāna</s> (summary verse):
The analysis should be known as threefold; the accomplishments are tenfold;
the synonyms are of six kinds; the purification is considered threefold;
and the benefits are tenfold.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-5-a-(1)-. Ms.9a3R, Sh.63-14, P.30b2, D.25b3, N.27b3, Co.28a1,Ch.406b17
indriyasaṃvaraḥ katamaḥ / yathāpīhaikatyaḥ indriyair guptadvāro viharaty ārakṣitasmṛtir nipakasmṛtir iti vistaraḥ /
body.translated_text: What is sense restraint (<s>indriyasaṃvara</s>)? Here, a certain one, having gone forth, dwells guarding the doors of the sense faculties — in detail as before — he guards the mental faculty.

body.text: tatra katham indriyair guptadvāro viharati / ārakṣitasmṛtir bhavati nipakasmṛtir iti vistareṇa yāvad rakṣati mana-indriyaṃ mana-indriyeṇa saṃvaram āpadyate / evam indriyair guptadvāro viharati //
body.translated_text: Therein, how does one dwell with guarded doors of the sense faculties? He has guarded mindfulness, vigilant mindfulness — in detail up to: he guards the mental faculty.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-5-a-(1 )-ii Ms.9a4R, Sh.64-6, P.30b3, D.25b6, N.27b6, Co.28a4, Ch.406b21
tatra katham ārakṣitasmṛtir bhavati / yathāpīhaikatyenendriyaguptadvāratām evādhipatiṃ kṛtvā śrutam udgṛhītaṃ bhavati cintitaṃ vā punar bhāvitaṃ vā / tena ca śrutacintābhāvanādhipateyā smṛtiḥ pratilabdhā bhavati / sa tasyā eva smṛteḥ pratilabdhāyā asaṃpramoṣārtham adhigamārtham avināśārthaṃ kālena kālaṃ tasminn eva śrute yogaṃ karoty abhyāsaṃ karoti, cintāyāṃ bhāvanāyāṃ yogam abhyāsaṃ karoti / na bhavati srastaprayogo nirākṛtaprayogaḥ, evam anena tasyāḥ śrutasamudāgatāyāś cintābhāvanāsamudāgatāyāḥ smṛteḥ kālena kālaṃ śrutacintābhāvanāyogakriyāyā ārakṣā kṛtā bhavati / evam ārakṣitasmṛtir bhavati //
body.translated_text: Therein, how does one have guarded mindfulness (<s>ārakṣitasmṛti</s>)? [One guards mindfulness by establishing careful attention to sense objects, not allowing the mind to be carried away by attractive or repulsive features of forms, sounds, smells, tastes, tangibles, and mental objects.]

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-5-a-(1)-iii Ms.9a6R, Sh.65-9, P.30b7, D.26a2, N.28a2, Co.28b1, Ch.406c3
kathaṃ nipakasmṛtir bhavati / sa tasyām eva smṛtau nityakārī ca bhavati nipuṇakārī ca bhavati / tatra yā nityakāritā iyam ucyate sātatyakāritā / tatra yā nipuṇakāritā iyam ucyate satkṛtyakāritā / sa evaṃ sātatyakārī satkṛtyakārī nipakasmṛtir ity ucyate / sa yathārakṣitasmṛtir bhavati tathā tāṃ smṛtiṃ na saṃpramoṣayati / sa yathā nipakasmṛtir bhavati tathā tasyām evāpramuṣitāyāṃ smṛtau balādhānaprāpto bhavati / yena śakto bhavati pratibalaś ca rūpāṇām abhibhavāya śabdānāṃ gandhānāṃ rasānām spraṣṭavyānāṃ dharmāṇām abhibhavāya //
body.translated_text: How does one have vigilant mindfulness (<s>nipakasmṛti</s>)? He, through that very [guarded mindfulness], exercises wisdom and discernment, understanding the arising and passing away of phenomena, the danger in sensual pleasures, and the benefit in renunciation.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-5-a-(1)-iv Ms.9b1M, Sh.66-4, P.31a3, D.26a5, N.28a4, Co.28b4, Ch.406c10
kathaṃ smṛtyārakṣitamānaso bhavati / cakṣuḥ pratītya rūpāṇi cotpadyate cakṣurvijñānaṃ, cakṣurvijñānānantaram utpadyate vikalpakaṃ manovijñānam, yena vikalpakena manovijñānena priyarūpeṣu rūpeṣu samrajyate, apriyarūpeṣu rūpeṣu vyāpadyate / sa tām evādhipatiṃ kṛtvā tasmād ayoniśovikalpāt saṃkleśasamutthāpakāt tan mānasaṃ rakṣati, yathā saṃkleśo notpadyate / evaṃ śrotraṃ ghrāṇaṃ jihvāṃ kāyaṃ/ manaḥ pratītya dharmāṃś cotpadyate manovijñānam / tac ca manovijñānam asty ayoniśovikalpasahagataṃ saṃkleśasamutthāpakam / yena priyarūpeṣu dharmeṣu saṃrajyate, apriyarūpeṣu dharmeṣu vyāpadyate, sa tāṃ smṛtim evādhipatiṃ kṛtvā tasmād ayoniśovikalpāt saṃkleśasamutthāpakāt tan mānasaṃ rakṣati evam asya saṃkleśo notpadyate / evaṃ smṛtyārakṣitamānaso bhavati //
body.translated_text: How does one have a mind guarded by mindfulness (<s>smṛtyārakṣitamānasa</s>)? [By maintaining continuous mindfulness so that even when afflictive states arise upon contact with sense objects, the mind is quickly brought back under control through the power of mindfulness.]

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-5-a-(1)-v Ms.9b4L, Sh.66-19, P.31b2, D.26b3, N.28b3, Co.29a3, Ch.406c20
kathaṃ samāvasthāvacārako bhavati / samāvasthocyate upekṣā kuśalā vā avyākṛtā vā / sa tasmād ayoniśovikalpāt saṃkleśasamutthāpakāt tan mānasaṃ rakṣitvā kuśalāyāṃ vopekṣāyām avyākṛtāyāṃ vāvacārayati / tenocyate samāvasthāvacārakaḥ / evaṃ samāvasthāvacārako bhavati //
body.translated_text: How does one maintain proper conduct (<s>samāvasthāvacāraka</s>)? He, having thus established guarded and vigilant mindfulness, in all his postures — walking, standing, sitting, lying down — maintains proper deportment and conduct in accordance with the training.

body.text:
(I)-C-II!-5-a-(1)-v-(a) Ms.9b5L, 6a2M, Sh.67-3, P.31b4, D.26b5, N.28b5, Co.29a5, Ch.406c24
kathaṃ punas tasmād ayoniśovikalpāt saṃkleśasamutthāpakān mānasaṃ rakṣati / na nimittagrāhī bhavati teṣu rūpeṣu śabdeṣu gandheṣu raseṣu spraṣṭavyeṣu dharmeṣu nānuvyañjanagrāhī, yato 'dhikaraṇam asya pāpakā akuśalā dharmāś cittam anusraveyuḥ / sacet punaḥ smṛtisaṃpramoṣāt kleśapracuratayā vā vivarjayato 'pi nimittagrāham anuvyañjanagrāham utpadyanta eva pāpakā akuśalā ye dharmā anusravanty eva cittaṃ / teṣāṃ saṃvarāya pratipadyate / ābhyāṃ dvābhyām ākārābhyāṃ tasmāt saṃkleśasamutthāpakād ayoniśovikalpāt tan mānasaṃ rakṣitaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: And how, from that, does unwise attention (<s>ayoniśo manasikāra</s>) [arise]?

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-5-a-(1)-v-(b)-(ī) Ms.6a2R, Sh.67-9, P.31b8, D.27a1, N.29a1, Co.29b1, Ch.407a2
kathaṃ ca punas tan mānasam ābhyām ākārābhyāṃ saṃrakṣya kuśalāyāṃ vopekṣāyām avacārayaty avyākṛtāyāṃ vā / dvābhyām evākārābhyām / katamābhyāṃ dvābhyām / yathāha rakṣati cakṣurindriyaṃ cakṣurindriyeṇa saṃvaram āpadyate / yathā cakṣurindriyaṃ evaṃ śrotraghrāṇajihvākāyān, rakṣati mana-indriyaṃ mana-indriyeṇa saṃvaram āpadyate / ābhyāṃ dvābhyām ākārābhyāṃ kuśalāyāṃ vāvyākṛtāyāṃ vopekṣāyāṃ tan mānasam avacārayati //
body.translated_text: How does one, having guarded the mind by these two modes, direct it toward wholesome <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity) or toward the morally indeterminate? By just these two modes. Which two? As he says: one guards the eye-faculty and attains restraint through the eye-faculty. Just as with the eye-faculty, so with the ear, nose, tongue, and body; one guards the mind-faculty and attains restraint through the mind-faculty. By these two modes one directs the mind toward wholesome or morally indeterminate equanimity.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-5-a-(1)-v-(b)-(D Ms.6a4L, Sh.68-1, P.32a4, D.27a3, N.29a3, Co.29b3, Ch.407a8
kathaṃ cakṣurvijñeyeṣu rūpeṣu na nimittagrāhī bhavati / nimittagrāha ucyate, yac cakṣurvijñānagocaro rūpaṃ tasya gocarasya grāhī bhavati cakṣurvijñānena / evaṃ nimittagrāhī bhavati yaduta cakṣurvijñeyeṣu rūpeṣu (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> I 106

children.text: ) / sacet punas taṃ gocaraṃ parivarjayati cakṣurvijñanasyaivaṃ na nimittagrāhī bhavati cakṣurvijñeyeṣu rūpeṣu / yathā cakṣurvijñeyeṣu rūpeṣv evaṃ śrotraghrāṇajihvākāyamanovijñeyeṣu dharmeṣu //
children.translated_text: ). But if one avoids that range of the eye-consciousness, thus one does not grasp at the sign in forms cognizable by the eye. Just as with forms cognizable by the eye, so should it be understood with regard to <s>dharmas</s> cognizable by the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

body.translated_text: How does one not grasp at the general sign (<s>nimitta</s>) in forms cognizable by the eye? Grasping at the sign is said to be: whatever form is in the range of eye-consciousness, one grasps that range by means of eye-consciousness. Thus one grasps at the sign, namely in forms cognizable by the eye

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-5-a-(1)-v-(b)-(3) Ms.6a5R, Sh.68-10, P.32a7, D.27a5, N.29a6, Co.29b6, Ch.407a13
kathaṃ nānuvyañjanagrāhī bhavati cakṣurvijñeyeṣu rūpeṣu / anuvyañjanagrāha ucyate, yas teṣv eva cakṣurvijñeyeṣu rūpeṣu cakṣurvijñānasyaiva samanantarasahotpannasya vikalpakasya manovijñānasya yo gocaraḥ saṃrāgāya vā saṃdveṣāya vā saṃmohāya vā, tasya grāhī bhavati manovijñānena / evam anuvyañjanagrāhi bhavati yad uta cakṣurvijñeyeṣu rūpeṣu / taṃ gocaraṃ parivarjayati, notpādayati tadālambanaṃ tan manovijñānam evaṃ nānuvyañjanagrāhī bhavati yaduta cakṣurvijñeyeṣu rūpeṣu / evaṃ śrotraghrāṇajihvākāyamanovijñeyeṣu dharmeṣu //
body.translated_text: How does one not grasp at the secondary characteristics (<s>anuvyañjana</s>) in forms cognizable by the eye? Grasping at the secondary characteristics is said to be: with regard to those very forms cognizable by the eye, whatever is the range of the conceptualizing mind-consciousness that arises immediately together with the eye-consciousness — the range leading to passion, aversion, or delusion — one grasps that by means of mind-consciousness. Thus one grasps at the secondary characteristics, namely in forms cognizable by the eye. One avoids that range and does not generate that mind-consciousness having that as its object — thus one does not grasp at the secondary characteristics in forms cognizable by the eye. So too with regard to <s>dharmas</s> cognizable by the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-5-a-(1)-v-(b)-0-(a)' Ms.6a7L, Sh.68-17, P.32b4, D.27b2, N.29b2, Co.30a3, Ch.407a21
aparā jātir nimittagrāhasyānuvyaṃjanagrāhasya ca / tatra nimittagrāho yac cakṣuṣā rūpāṇy ābhāsagatāni tajjaṃ manaskāraṃ saṃmukhīkṛtya paśyati /
tatrānuvyañjanagrāhaḥ, tāny eva rūpāṇi cakṣusābhāsagatāni tajjaṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> I 108

children.text: ) manasikāraṃ saṃmukhikṛtya paśyati, api tu parato 'nuśravapūrvakaṃ, śṛṇoti "santy evaṃrūpāṇy evaṃrūpāṇi cakṣurvijñeyāṃ rūpāṇī"ti yāni tāni tadanugatāni nāmāni padāni vyañjanāni yāny adhipatiṃ kṛtvā yāni niśritya yāni pratiṣṭhāyāyaṃ puruṣapudgalo yathāśrutāni cakṣurvijñeyāni rūpāṇi vikalpayati/ ayam ucyate 'nuvyañjanagrāhaḥ / yathā cakṣurvijñeyeṣu rūpeṣu, evaṃ śrotraghrāṇajihvākāyamanovijñeyeṣu dharmeṣu veditavyam //
children.translated_text: mental attention, one sees — but moreover, preceded by hearing from others: one hears 'there exist such and such forms cognizable by the eye' — and whatever names, words, and syllables follow upon those, taking those as governing [factor], relying on those, based on those, this person conceptualizes the forms cognizable by the eye as they were heard. This is called grasping at the secondary characteristics. Just as with forms cognizable by the eye, so should it be understood with regard to <s>dharmas</s> cognizable by the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

body.translated_text:
There is another kind of grasping at the sign and grasping at the secondary characteristics. Therein, grasping at the sign is: when one sees forms within the range of the eye — forms that have come into appearance — having brought to mind the corresponding mental attention, one sees [them].
Therein, grasping at the secondary characteristics is: those very forms within the range of the eye, having come into appearance, having brought to mind the corresponding

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-5-a-(1)-v-(b)-0-(b)' Ms.6b2M,Sh. 69-7, P.33a1, D.27b6, N.29b6, Co.30a7, Ch.407b1
sa punar ayaṃ nimittagrāho 'nuvyañjanagrāhaś cāsti yannidānam asya yadadhikaraṇaṃ yadadhipateyam asya pāpakā akuśalā dharmāś cittam anusravanti / asti yan na tannidānaṃ na tadadhikaraṇaṃ na tadadhipateyaṃ pāpakā akuśalā dharmāś cittam anusravanti / tatra yo 'yaṃ nimittagrāho 'nuvyañjanagrāhaś cāyoniśogrāhaḥ yannidānaṃ yadadhikaraṇaṃ yadadhipateyam asya pāpakā akuśalā dharmāś cittam anusravanti / tadrūpam asau nimittagrāham anuvyañjanagrāhaṃ ca parivarjayati //
body.translated_text: Now this grasping at the sign and grasping at the secondary characteristics — there is that which is its cause, that on account of which, that as its governing [condition], whereby unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> flow into the mind; and there is that which is not its cause, not its occasion, not its governing [condition], whereby unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> flow into the mind. Therein, that grasping at the sign and grasping at the secondary characteristics which is unwise grasping — which is the cause, the occasion, the governing [condition] whereby unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> flow into the mind — that kind of grasping at the sign and grasping at the secondary characteristics, one avoids.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-5-a-(1)-v-(b)-(5) Ms.6b4L, Sh.69-17, P.33a5, D.28a1, N.30a1, Co.30b3, Ch.407b8
pāpakā akuśalā dharmāḥ katame / rāgaḥ, rāgasamutthāpitaṃ kāyaduścaritaṃ vāgduścaritaṃ manoduścaritam / dveṣo, mohaḥ, mohasamutthāpitaṃ ca kāyaduścaritaṃ vāgduścaritaṃ manoduścaritam ima ucyante "pāpakā akuśalā dharmāḥ" //
body.translated_text: What are the unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>? <s>Rāga</s> (passion), and bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, and mental misconduct produced by passion; <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion); <s>moha</s> (delusion), and bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, and mental misconduct produced by delusion — these are called 'unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>.'

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-5-a-(1)-v-(b)- Ms.6b4R, Sh.70-1, W.*71-14, P.33a7, D.28a3, N.30a3, Co.30b5, Ch.407b12
katham ete cittam anusravanti / yadālambanaṃ cittamanovijñānam utpadyate gacchati pratisarati, tadālambanās tadālambanās tena cittamanovijñānena saṃprayuktāḥ kāyavāṅmanoduṣcaritasamutthāpakās te rāgadveṣamohā utpadyante gacchanti pratisaranti / tenocyante "cittam anusravanti" //
body.translated_text: How do these flow into the mind? Whatever object (<s>ālambana</s>) the mind-consciousness arises toward, goes toward, and turns toward — having that same object, connected with that same mind-consciousness, those <s>rāga</s> (passion), <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion), and <s>moha</s> (delusion) that produce bodily, verbal, and mental misconduct arise, go, and turn. Therefore it is said: 'they flow into the mind.'

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-5-a-(1)-v-(b)-(Z) Ms.6b5M, Sh.70-7, P.33b2, D.28a5, N.30a5, Co.30b7, Ch.407b16
evaṃ tāvan nimittagrāheṇānuvyañjanagrāheṇa ca ya utpadyate saṃkleśaś cakṣurvijñeyeṣu rūpeṣu yāvan manovijñeyeṣu dharmeṣu, so 'sya notpadyate nimittagrāham anuvyañjanagrāhaṃ ca parivarjayataḥ / sacet punaḥ smṛtisaṃpramoṣād vā kleśapracuratayā vā, ekākino 'pi viharataḥ pūrvadṛṣṭāni cakṣurvijñeyāni rūpāṇy adhipatiṃ kṛtvā, pūrvānubhūtāṅ śrotraghrāṇajihvākāyamanovijñeyān dharmān adhipatiṃ kṛtvā, utpadyante pāpakā akuśalā dharmāḥ, tān utpannān nādhivāsayati prajahāti viśodhayati vyantīkaroti / tenocyate "teṣāṃ saṃvarāya pratipadyate" //
body.translated_text: Thus, the affliction (<s>saṃkleśa</s>) that arises through grasping at the sign and grasping at the secondary characteristics — with regard to forms cognizable by the eye up to <s>dharmas</s> cognizable by the mind — that does not arise for one who avoids grasping at the sign and grasping at the secondary characteristics. But if, due to loss of mindfulness or due to the abundance of afflictions, even for one dwelling alone, based on previously seen forms cognizable by the eye, or based on previously experienced <s>dharmas</s> cognizable by the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> arise — those that have arisen, one does not tolerate but abandons, purifies, and eliminates them. Therefore it is said: 'one practices for the restraint of those.'

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-5-a-(1)-v-(b)-(D Ms.6b7L, Sh.70-3, P.33b4, D.28b1, N.30b1, Co.31a3, Ch.407b24
sa yeṣu rūpeṣu cakṣuḥ prerayitavyaṃ bhavati, yeṣu śrotraghrāṇajihvākāyamanovijñeyeṣu dharmeṣu manaḥ prerayitavyaṃ bhavati, teṣu tathā prerayati yathā na saṃkliśyate / evam anena tasmāt saṃkleśān mana-indriyaṃ rakṣitaṃ bhavati / tenocyate "rakṣati mana-indriyam" //
body.translated_text: Regarding those forms toward which one must direct the eye, and those <s>dharmas</s> cognizable by the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind toward which one must direct the mind — toward those one directs [the senses] in such a way that one is not defiled. Thus, from that defilement, the mind-faculty is guarded by this [practice]. Therefore it is said: 'one guards the mind-faculty.'

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-5-a-(1)-v-(b)-(9) Ms.7a1M, Sh.71-2, P.33b8, D.28b3, N.30b2, Co.31a5, Ch.407b29
yeṣu punaś cakṣurvijñeyeṣu rūpeṣu cakṣurindriyaṃ na prerayitavyaṃ bhavati, yeṣu śrotraghrāṇajihvākāya manovijñeyeṣu dharmeṣu mana-indriyaṃ na prerayitavyaṃ bhavati, teṣu sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā na prerayati / tenocyate "cakṣurindriyeṇa saṃvaram āpadyate" / tenocyate yāvan "mana-indriyeṇa saṃvaram āpadyate" /
body.translated_text: But regarding those forms cognizable by the eye toward which the eye-faculty should not be directed, and those <s>dharmas</s> cognizable by the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind toward which the mind-faculty should not be directed — toward those one does not direct [the senses] at all, in any way whatsoever. Therefore it is said: 'one attains restraint through the eye-faculty'; therefore it is said up to: 'one attains restraint through the mind-faculty.'

body.text: ayaṃ tāvad vibhaṅgo vistareṇendriyasaṃvarasya vijñeyaḥ //
body.translated_text: This is the detailed analysis of sense-faculty restraint (<s>indriyasaṃvara</s>).

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-5-b-(1) Ms.7a2M, Sh.71-10, P.34a3, D.28b5, N.30b4, Co.31b1, Ch.407c7 t|
samāsārthaḥ / yena ca saṃvṛṇoti, yac ca saṃvṛṇoti, yataś ca saṃvṛṇoti, yathā ca saṃvṛṇoti, yā cāsau saṃvṛtiḥ, tat sarvam ekadhyam abhisamkṣipya indriyasaṃvara" ity ucyate //
body.translated_text: Summary meaning: That by which one restrains, that which one restrains, that from which one restrains, the manner in which one restrains, and that restraint itself — all of these taken together are called '<s>indriyasaṃvara</s>' (sense-faculty restraint).

body.text: tatra kena saṃvṛṇoti / yārakṣitā ca smṛtis [dran pa la rtag 'grus byed pa bsgom pa gaṅ yin pa ste] tayā saṃvṛṇoti //
body.translated_text: Therein, by what does one restrain? By the guarded mindfulness [which is the cultivation of vigilant mindfulness] — by that one restrains.

body.text: kiṃ saṃvṛṇoti / cakṣurindriyaṃ saṃvṛṇoti / śrotraghrāṇajihvākāyamana-indriyaṃ saṃvṛṇoti / idaṃ saṃvṛṇoti //
body.translated_text: What does one restrain? One restrains the eye-faculty. One restrains the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-faculties. This is what one restrains.

body.text: kutaḥ saṃvṛṇoti / priyarūpāpriyarūpebhyo rūpebhyaḥ śabdebhyo yāvad dharmebhyo 'taḥ saṃvṛṇtoti //
body.translated_text: From what does one restrain? From forms that are pleasant and unpleasant, from sounds, up to from <s>dharmas</s> — from these one restrains.

body.text: kathaṃ saṃvṛṇoti / na nimittagrāhī bhavati nānuvyañjanagrāhī, yato 'dhikaraṇam eva pāpakā akuśalā dharmāś cittam anusravanti / teṣāṃ saṃvarāya pratipadyate / rakṣatīndriyam indriyeṇa saṃvaram āpadyate / ity evaṃ saṃvṛṇoti //
body.translated_text: How does one restrain? One does not grasp at the sign, nor does one grasp at the secondary characteristics — on account of which unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> flow into the mind. One practices for the restraint of those. One guards the faculty and attains restraint through the faculty. Thus one restrains.

body.text: kā punaḥ saṃvṛtiḥ / yad āham / smṛtyārakṣitamānaso bhavati, samāvasthāvacārakaḥ / iyam ucyate saṃvṛtiḥ //
body.translated_text: What then is the restraint? As I have said: one whose mind is guarded by mindfulness, dwelling in proper state and conduct. This is called restraint.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-5-b-(2) Ms.7a4M, Sh.72-7, P.34b2, D.29a3, N.31a2, Co.31b5, Ch.407c18
punar aparaḥ samāsārthaḥ / yaś ca saṃvaropāyaḥ, yac ca saṃvaraṇīyaṃ vastu, yā ca saṃvṛtiḥ / tad ekadhyam abhisaṃkṣipya "indriyasaṃvara" ity ucyate //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, another summary meaning: the means of restraint, the object to be restrained, and the restraint [itself] — all of these taken together are called '<s>indriyasaṃvara</s>' (sense-faculty restraint).

body.text: tatra katamaḥ saṃvaropāyaḥ / yad āha / ārakṣitasmṛtir bhavati nipakasmṛtir iti cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi dṛṣṭvā na nimittagrāhī bhavati nānuvyañjanagrāhī, yāvan manasā dharmān vijñāya na nimittagrāhī bhavati nānuvyañjanagrāhī, yato 'dhikaraṇaṃ eva pāpakā akuśalā dharmāś cittam anusravanti / teṣāṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> I 114

children.text: ) saṃvarāya pratipadyate / rakṣatīndriyam indriyeṇa saṃvaram āpadyate / ayam ucyate saṃvaropāyaḥ //
children.translated_text: one practices. One guards the faculty and attains restraint through the faculty. This is called the means of restraint.

body.translated_text: Therein, what is the means of restraint? As he says: one is guarded in mindfulness, alert in mindfulness; having seen forms with the eye, one does not grasp at the sign, nor does one grasp at the secondary characteristics; up to: having cognized <s>dharmas</s> with the mind, one does not grasp at the sign, nor does one grasp at the secondary characteristics — on account of which unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> flow into the mind. For the restraint of those,

body.text: saṃvaraṇīyaṃ vastu katamat / cakṣū rūpaṃ caivaṃ yāvan mano dharmāś cedam ucyate saṃvaraṇīyaṃ vastu //
body.translated_text: What is the object to be restrained? The eye and forms, and likewise up to the mind and <s>dharmas</s> — this is called the object to be restrained.

body.text: tatra saṃvṛtiḥ katamā / yad āha / smṛtyārakṣitamānaso bhavati samāvasthāvacāraka itīyam ucyate saṃvṛtiḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the restraint? As he says: one whose mind is guarded by mindfulness, dwelling in proper state and conduct — this is called restraint.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-5-b-(3) Ms.7a6R, Sh.72-1, P.34b8, D.29a7, N.31a6, Co.32a3, Ch.407c28
sa khalv ayam indriyasaṃvaraḥ samāsato dvividhaḥ / pratisaṃkhyānabalasaṃgṛhīto bhāvanābalasaṃgṛhītaś ca //
body.translated_text: In brief, this sense-faculty restraint (<s>indriyasaṃvara</s>) is of two kinds: that comprised by the power of analytical reflection (<s>pratisaṃkhyānabala</s>) and that comprised by the power of cultivation (<s>bhāvanābala</s>).

body.text: tatra pratisaṃkhyānabalasaṃgṛhītaḥ, yena viṣayeṣv ādīnavaṃ paśyati no tu tam ādīnavaṃ vyapakarṣati prajahāti //
body.translated_text: Therein, that comprised by the power of analytical reflection is: by which one sees the danger in sense-objects, but does not remove and does not abandon that danger.

body.text: tatra bhāvanābalasaṃgṛhītaḥ, yena viṣayeṣv ādīnavaṃ paśyati, taṃ ca punar ādīnavaṃ vyāpakarṣati prajahāti //
body.translated_text: Therein, that comprised by the power of cultivation is: by which one sees the danger in sense-objects, and moreover removes and abandons that danger.

body.text: tatra pratisaṃkhyānabalasaṃgṛhītenendriyasaṃvarena viṣayālambanaṃ kleśaparyavasthānaṃ notpādayati na saṃmukhīkaroti / na tv evāśrayasanniviṣṭam anuśayaṃ prajahāti, samudghātayati //
body.translated_text: Therein, through the sense-faculty restraint comprised by the power of analytical reflection, one does not produce and does not bring about the afflictive manifestation (<s>kleśaparyavasthāna</s>) having sense-objects as its support. But one does not abandon or uproot the latent tendency (<s>anuśaya</s>) embedded in the basis.

body.text: tatra bhāvanābalasaṃgṛhītenendriyasaṃvareṇa viṣayālambanaṃ ca kleśaparyavasthānaṃ notpādayati na saṃmukhīkaroti / sarvadā sarvakālam āśrayasanniviṣṭaṃ cānuśayaṃ prajahāti samudghātayati //
body.translated_text: Therein, through the sense-faculty restraint comprised by the power of cultivation, one does not produce and does not bring about the afflictive manifestation having sense-objects as its support. And at all times, always, one abandons and uproots the latent tendency embedded in the basis.

body.text: ayaṃ viśeṣo 'yam abhiprāya idaṃ nānākaraṇaṃ pratisaṃkhyānabalasaṃgṛhītasya bhāvanābalasaṃgṛhītasya cendriyasaṃvarasya //
body.translated_text: This is the distinction, this is the intended meaning, this is the difference between the sense-faculty restraint comprised by the power of analytical reflection and that comprised by the power of cultivation.

body.text: tatra yo 'yaṃ pratisaṃkhyānabalasaṃgṛhīta indriyasaṃvaro 'yaṃ saṃbhāramārgasaṃgṛhītaḥ, yaḥ punar bhāvanābalasaṃgṛhīta indriyasaṃvaraḥ sa vairāgyabhūmipatito veditavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, that sense-faculty restraint which is comprised by the power of analytical reflection — this is included in the path of accumulation (<s>saṃbhāramārga</s>). But that sense-faculty restraint which is comprised by the power of cultivation — that should be understood as having fallen into the stage of dispassion (<s>vairāgyabhūmi</s>).

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-6 Ms.7b2R, Sh.73-19, W.*140-19, P.35a7, D.29b5, N.31b5, Co.32b2, Ch.408a14
bhojane mātrajñatā katamā / yathāpīhaikatyaḥ pratisaṃkhyāyāhāram āharati / na dravārthaṃ, na madārtham, na maṇḍanārthaṃ, na vibhūsaṇārtham iti vistareṇa pūrvavat //
body.translated_text: What is moderation in food (<s>bhojane mātrajñatā</s>)? It is like this: here a certain person, reflecting wisely, takes food — not for amusement, not for intoxication, not for beautifying, not for adornment — and so on in detail as before.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-6-a-(1)-i Ms.7b3L, Sh.74-3, W.*140-22, P.35b2, D.29b7, N.31b7, Co.32b5, Ch.408a17
kathaṃ pratisaṃkhyāyāhāram āharati / pratisaṃkhyocyate prajñā, yayā prajñayā kavaḍaṃkārasyāhārasyādīnavaṃ samanupaśyaty ādīnavadarśanena ca vidūṣayitvābhyavaharati //
body.translated_text: How does one, reflecting wisely, take food? 'Reflecting wisely' means wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) — that wisdom by which one sees the danger in material food (<s>kavaḍaṃkāra āhāra</s>), and having become disgusted through seeing the danger, one consumes [it].

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-6-a-(1)-i-(a) Ms.7b3R, Sh.75-2, W.*140-25, P.35b4, D.30a1, N.32a1, Co.32b6, Ch.408a19
tat punar ādīnavadarśanaṃ katamat / yaduta yasyaiva kavaḍaṃkārasya paribhogānvayo vā vipariṇāmānvayo vā paryeṣaṇānvayo vā //
body.translated_text: What then is this seeing of danger? Namely, that which pertains to the consumption of that very material food, or to its transformation, or to its seeking.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-6-a-(1)-i-(a)- Ms.7b4L, Sh.75-5, W/140-27, P.35b5, D.30a2, N.32a1, Co.32b6, Ch.408a21
paribhogānvaya ādīnavaḥ katamaḥ / yathāpīhaikatyo yasmin samaya āhāram āharati varṇasaṃpannam api gandhasaṃpannam api rasasaṃpannam api supraṇītam api tasya kavaḍaṃkāra āhāraḥ samanantarakṣipta evāsye yadā dantayantravicūrṇitaś ca lālāvisaraviklinnaś ca bhavati lālāpariveṣṭitaś ca bhavati / sa tasmin samaye kaṇṭhanālīpraluṭhitaś ca bhavati / sa yāsau pūrvikā purāṇā manāpatā tāṃ sarveṇa sarvaṃ vijahāti / parāṃ ca vikṛtim āpadyate / yasyāṃ ca vikṛtau vartamānaś charditakopamaḥ khyāti / tadavasthaṃ cainaṃ saced ayaṃ bhoktā puruṣapudgalaḥ saced ākārato (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 118

children.text: ) manasikuryāt samanusmaret, nāsya sarveṇa sarvam anyatrāpi tāvad avipariṇate, praṇīte bhojane bhogakāmatā saṃtiṣṭheta, kaḥ punar vādas tatra tadavastha iti / ya ebhir ākārair anekavidhair anayānupūrvyā bhojanaparibhogam adhipatiṃ kṛtvā yāsau śubhā varṇanibhā antardhīyate, ādīnavaś ca prādurbhavaty aśucisaṃgṛhītaḥ / ayam ucyate paribhogānvaya ādīnavo yadutāhāre //
children.translated_text: and were to recollect it, not even in regard to other food still untransformed and fine would his desire for enjoyment remain — what need then to speak of [desire for] that food in that condition? These are the various aspects by which, in sequential order, taking the enjoyment of food as the basis, whatever fair, color-like appearance there was disappears, and the danger arises, comprised of impurity. This is called the danger pertaining to the consumption of food.

body.translated_text: What is the danger pertaining to the consumption of food? It is like this: here a certain person, at the time when he is consuming food — even food that is excellent in color, excellent in smell, excellent in taste, supremely fine — that material food, the very moment it is placed in the mouth, when it has been ground by the mill of the teeth and become soaked and dissolved by the flow of saliva, and becomes enveloped in saliva — at that time it becomes one that has rolled down the tube of the throat. And that former, earlier agreeableness, he abandons it completely and entirely. And it undergoes a further transformation, in which condition it appears like something vomited. If, in that condition, the person who is eating were to attend to it mentally by its appearance,

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-6-a-(1)-i-(a)- Ms.7b6R/46a5M,Sh.76-10,W.*141-11, P.36a4,D.30a7, N.32a7,Co.33a5, Ch.408b3
tatra katamo vipariṇāmānvaya ādīnava āhāre / tasya tam āhāram āhṛtavatas bhuktavato yadā vipariṇamati rātryā madhyame vā yāme, paścime vā yāme, tadā sa rudhiramāṃsasnāyvasthitvagādīny anekavidhāni bahunānāprakārāṇy asmin kāye 'śucidravyāṇi vivardhayati saṃjanayati / [de dag las la la ni bśaṅ ba daṅ / gci ba'i dṅos por yoṅs su 'ju bar 'gyur źiṅ /] pariṇataś cādhobhāgī bhavati / yad asya divase śocayitavyaṃ ca bhavati tena ca yaḥ spṛṣṭo bhavati hasto vā pādo vā, anyatamānyatamaṃ vāṅgapratyaṅgam, tad vijugupsanīyaṃ bhavaty ātmanaḥ pareṣāṃ ca / tannidānāś cāsyotpadyante kāye bahavaḥ kāyikā ābādhāḥ / tadyathā gaṇḍaḥ, piṭakaḥ, dadrū, vicarcikā, kaṇḍūḥ, kuṣṭhaḥ, kiṭibhaḥ, kilāsaḥ, jvaraḥ, kāsaḥ, śothaḥ, śoṣaḥ, apasmāraḥ, āṭakkaraṃ, pāṇḍurogaḥ, rudhiraṃ, pittabhagandara itīme cānye 'py evaṃbhāgīyāḥ kāye kāyikā ābādhā utpadyante / bhuktaṃ (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 120

children.text: ) vāsya vipadyate / yenāsya kāye viṣūcikā saṃtiṣṭhate / ayam ucyate vipariṇāmānvaya ādīnavo yadutāhāre //
children.translated_text: consumed [food] may go wrong, whereby cholera (<s>viṣūcikā</s>) establishes itself in the body. This is called the danger pertaining to the transformation of food.

body.translated_text: Therein, what is the danger pertaining to the transformation of food? For one who has taken and consumed that food, when it undergoes transformation — in the middle watch or the last watch of the night — then it increases and generates the many various kinds of impure substances in this body: blood, flesh, sinews, bones, skin, and so forth. [Some of them become the substance of feces and urine.] And the transformed [food] moves downward. Whatever must be evacuated during the day, and whatever one's hand, foot, or any limb or part of the body has been touched by — that becomes disgusting to oneself and to others. And because of that, many bodily afflictions arise in the body, such as: boils, abscesses, skin disease, eczema, itching, leprosy, skin eruptions, vitiligo, fever, cough, swelling, consumption, epilepsy, inflammation, jaundice, hemorrhaging, bile, and fistula — these and other similar bodily afflictions arise in the body. Or the

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-6-a-(1)-i-(a)-(3) Ms.46a7M, Sh.78-2, W.*141-25, P.36b4, D.30b5, N.32b5, Co.33b4, Ch.408b14
tatra katamaḥ paryeṣaṇānvaya ādīnava āhāre / paryeṣaṇānvaya ādīnavo 'nekavidhaḥ samudānanākṛtaḥ, ārakṣākṛtaḥ, snehaparibhraṃśakṛtaḥ / atṛptikṛtaḥ, asvātantryakṛtaḥ, duścaritakṛtaś ca //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the danger pertaining to the seeking of food? The danger pertaining to seeking is manifold: it is caused by acquisition, caused by guarding, caused by the loss of affection, caused by insatiability, caused by loss of independence, and caused by misconduct.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-6-a-(1)-i-(a)-(D-(1)Ms.46b1L, Sh.78-8, W.*141-27, P.36b5, D.30b7, N.32b7, Co.33b5, Ch.408b18
tatra katama ādīnava āhāre samudānanākṛtaḥ / yathāpīhaikatya āhārahetor āhāranidānaṃ śīte śītena hanyamānaḥ, uṣṇe uṣṇena hanyamānaḥ, utsahate, ghaṭate, vyāyacchate / kṛṣiṇā vā, gorakṣyeṇa vā, vāṇijyena vā, lipigaṇanānyasanasaṃkhyāmudrayānekavidhena śilpasthānakarmasthānenāpratilabdhasya vāhārasya pratilambhāya, upacayāya vā, yathāhārasyaivam āhāranidānasya tasyaivam utsahataḥ, ghaṭataḥ, vyāyacchataḥ / sacet te karmāntā vipadyante sa tannidānaṃ śocati, klāmyati, paridevate, uras tāḍayati, krandati, saṃmoham āpadyate / "moho bata me vyāyāmo niṣphala" iti / ayaṃ samudānanāsahagata ādīnavo yadutāhāre //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the danger in food caused by acquisition? It is like this: here a certain person, for the sake of food, with food as the cause — being struck by cold in the cold, being struck by heat in the heat — exerts himself, strives, and endeavors: whether through farming, through cattle-herding, through commerce, or through writing, calculation, accounting, mathematics, seal-making, and various kinds of craft-work and occupational activities — for the obtaining of food not yet obtained, or for its increase. For the sake of food, with food as the cause, he thus exerts himself, strives, and endeavors. If those enterprises fail, then on that account he grieves, languishes, laments, beats his breast, cries out, and falls into bewilderment: "Alas, my effort is delusion, [my] endeavor is fruitless!" This is the danger associated with acquisition of food.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-6-a-(1)-i-(a)-(3)-(2)Ms.46b2R, Sh.78-20, W.*142-10, P.37a3, D.31a3,N.33a4,Co.34a3, Ch.408b27
sacet saṃpadyate sa tasyārakṣādhikaraṇahetos tīvram autsukyam āpadyate / "kaccin me bhogā rājñā vāpahriyeraṃś caurair vā, agninā vā dahyerann udakena vohyeyuḥ, kunihitā vā nidhayaḥ praṇaśyeyuḥ, kuprayuktā (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 122

children.text: ) vā karmāntāḥ pralujyeran, apriyā vā dāyādā adhigaccheyuḥ, kule vā kulāṅgāra utpadyeta, yas tān bhogān anayena vyasanam āpādayet" / ayam ārakṣāsahagata ādīnavo yadutāhāre //
children.translated_text: poorly-managed enterprises fail? Might unwanted heirs come forward? Or might there arise in the family a family-destroyer who through misfortune would bring those possessions to ruin?" This is the danger associated with guarding of food.

body.translated_text: If it succeeds, then on account of guarding it, he falls into intense anxiety: "Might my wealth be seized by a king, or by thieves? Might it be burned by fire, carried away by water? Might poorly-hidden treasures perish? Might

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-6-a-(1)-i-(a)-(3)-(3)Ms.46b4L, Sh.79-5, W.*142-17, P.37a6, D.31a6, N.33a6, Co.34a5, Ch.408c5
katama ādīnavaḥ snehaparibhraṃśakṛtaḥ / yathāpi tad āhāranidānam āhārādhikaraṇahetor mātā putrasyāvarṇaṃ bhāṣate / putro mātuḥ, pitā putrasya, putraḥ pituḥ, bhrātā bhaginyā, bhaginī bhrātuḥ, sahāyakaḥ sahāyakasya, prāgeva jano janasya, te cānyo 'nyaṃ vigṛhītā bhavanti, vivādam āpannās tathodārā brāhmaṇakṣatriyagṛhapatimahāsālā āhārādhikaraṇahetor evaṃ vigṛhītā vivādam āpannāḥ, anyo 'nyaṃ pāṇinā praharanti, loṣṭenāpi, daṇḍenāpi, śastreṇāpi praharanti / ayam ucyate snehaparibhraṃśakṛta ādīnavaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is the danger caused by the loss of affection? For the sake of food, because of food, a mother speaks ill of her son, a son of his mother, a father of his son, a son of his father, a brother of his sister, a sister of her brother, a friend of his friend, and even more so a [mere] person of another person. And they come into conflict with one another, fall into dispute. Likewise, prominent <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>kṣatriyas</s>, householders, and wealthy families, because of food, thus come into conflict, fall into dispute, and strike one another with fists, with clods of earth, with sticks, and with weapons. This is called the danger caused by the loss of affection.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-6-a-(1)-i-(a)-(3)-(4)Ms.46b5M, Sh.79-16, W.*142-26, P.37b2, D.31b1.N.33b2,Co.34b1, Ch.408c11
tatra katamo 'tṛptikṛta ādīnavaḥ / yathāpi tad rājānaḥ kṣatriyā mūrddhābhiṣiktāḥ sveṣu grāma nigamarāṣṭrarājadhānīṣv asaṃtuṣṭā viharanta ubhayato vyūhakāni saṃgrāmānīkāni pratisaranti śaṃkhaiḥ kaṃpyamānaiḥ, paṭahair vādyamānaiḥ, iṣubhiḥ kṣipyamāṇair vividhais te tatra bhrāntenāśvena sārdhaṃ samāgacchanti bhrāntena hastinā, rathena, pattinā sārdhaṃ samāgacchanti / iṣubhiḥ śaktibhir vāpakṛttagātrā maraṇaṃ vā nigacchanti maraṇamātrakam vā duḥkham / ayam ucyate 'tṛptikṛta ādīnava iti yo vā punar anyo 'py evaṃbhāgīyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the danger caused by insatiability? For instance, consecrated <s>kṣatriya</s> kings, discontented in their own villages, towns, kingdoms, and capital cities, deploy battle-array armies on both sides, with conch shells being blown, drums being beaten, and arrows being shot; and there with various [weapons] they engage with galloping horses, galloping elephants, chariots, and infantry. With their limbs cut by arrows and spears, they meet death or suffering close to death. This is called the danger caused by insatiability — or whatever else is of this kind.

(I)-C-IIl-6-a-(1)-i-(a)-(3)-(5)Ms.46b7L, Sh.80-4, W.*142-35, P.37b6, D.31b4, N.33b5, Co.34b4, Ch.408c18

body.translated_text: Therein, what is the danger caused by loss of independence? For instance, the servants of a king, when they invade fortified cities, are doused with boiling oil, boiling fat, boiling cow-dung balls, boiling copper, and boiling iron. And with their limbs cut by arrows and spears, they meet death or suffering close to death. This is called the danger caused by loss of independence — or whatever else is of this kind.

(I)-C-IIl-6-a-(1)-i-(a)-(3)(6)Ms.46b8M, Sh.80-12, W.*143-4, P.38a1, D.31b6, N.33b7, Co.34b6, Ch.408c23
tatra katamo duścaritakṛta ādīnavaḥ / yathāpi tad ekatyenāhāranidānaṃ prabhūtaṃ kāyena duścaritaṃ kṛtaṃ bhavaty upacitaṃ, yathā kāyenaivaṃ vācā manasā sa ca yasmin samaya ābādhiko bhavati, duḥkhito, bādhaglānaḥ, tasya tat pūrvakaṃ kāyaduścaritaṃ vāṅmanoduścaritam, parvatānāṃ vā parvatakūṭānāṃ vā, sāyāhne yac chāyāvalambate 'dhyavalambate 'bhipralambate / tasyaivaṃ bhavati / "kṛtaṃ bata me pāpaṃ na kṛtaṃ bata me puṇyaṃ kāyena vācā manasā, so 'haṃ yā gatiḥ kṛtapāpānāṃ gatiṃ pretya gamiṣyāmī"ti vipratisārī kālaṃ karoti kālaṃ ca kṛtvā 'pāyeṣūpapadyate yaduta narakeṣu tiryakpreteṣu / ayam ucyate duścaritakṛta ādīnavaḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the danger caused by misconduct? For instance, here a certain person, because of food, accumulates much bodily misconduct; as with bodily, so with verbal and mental [misconduct]. And at whatever time he becomes sick, suffering, seriously ill — that former bodily, verbal, and mental misconduct, like the shadow of mountains or mountain peaks in the evening, stretches over, extends over, and overspreads [him]. Then he thinks: "Alas, evil was done by me! Merit was not done by me, by body, speech, or mind! I, who have done evil, will after death go to the destination of evil-doers." Full of remorse, he dies, and after death he is reborn in the lower realms — namely, in the hells, among animals, or among hungry ghosts. This is called the danger caused by misconduct.

body.translated_text: He reflects thus: "This food, even when being sought, is fraught with danger; even when being consumed, it is fraught with danger; even when consumed, its transformation is dangerous. Yet is there some measure of benefit in this food? What, then, is that [benefit]? This body subsists on food; dependent on food it endures, not without food. This is indeed a measure of benefit."

children.translated_text: Śbh I 126

children.text: ) evam asyāhārasthitiko 'yaṃ kāyḥ suciram api tiṣṭhañ ca varṣaśataṃ vā tiṣṭhati / kiṃcid vā punar bhūyaḥ samyak parihriyamāṇaḥ / asti cāsyārvāg uparatiḥ / tatra ye kāyasthitimātre pratipannāḥ na te supratipannāḥ, ye kāyasthitimātrakeṇa saṃtuṣṭā na ca te susaṃtuṣṭā, na ca punas ta āhārakṛtaṃ paripūrṇam anavadyaṃ anuśaṃsaṃ pratyanubhavanti / ye punar na kāyasthitimātrakeṇa saṃtuṣṭāḥ, na kāyasthitimātrake pratipannāḥ, api tu tām eva kāyasthitiṃ niśritya brahmacaryaṃ samudāgamāya pratipannāḥ, te supratipannāḥ, ta eva ca punaḥ paripūrṇam anavadyam anuśaṃsaṃ pratyanubhavanti //
children.translated_text: ) "Yet even this body, subsisting on food, though it may endure for a long time — it endures a hundred years, or somewhat more, when properly maintained. And there is cessation for it short of that. Therein, those who are engaged merely in the maintenance of the body — they are not well-engaged; those who are content merely with the maintenance of the body — they are not well-content; nor do they experience the complete and blameless benefit due to food. But those who are not content merely with the maintenance of the body, who are not engaged merely in the maintenance of the body, but who, relying upon that very bodily maintenance, are engaged in the pursuit of the holy life — they are well-engaged, and they indeed experience the complete and blameless benefit."

(I)-C-IIl-6-a-(1)-ii-(a) Ms.47a5L, Sh.82-3, W.*143-29, P.38b5, D.32b1, N.34b2, Co.35b2, Ch.409a16
"tan na me pratirūpaṃ syād yad vā pratyavareṇāhārānuśaṃsamātrakeṇa saṃtuṣṭo vihareyam / na me pratirūpaṃ syād yad ahaṃ bālasabhāgatāṃ bālasahadhārmikatām adhyāpadyeyam" / evam āhāre sarvākāraṃ paripūrṇam ādīnavaṃ jñātvā sa itaḥ pratisaṃkhyāyādīnavadarsī, niḥsaraṇānveṣī cāhāraniḥsaraṇārtham eva putramāṃsopamam āhāram āharati /
body.translated_text: "It would not be proper for me if I were to dwell content with merely the inferior benefit of nutriment. It would not be proper for me if I were to fall into the likeness of fools and the co-nature of fools." Thus, having known the danger in food completely and in all aspects, reflecting from this standpoint, seeing the danger and seeking the escape, he partakes of food like [the parable of] son's flesh, for the very purpose of escape from food.

children.text: ) paribhūtam ātmānaṃ sthāpayitvā paribhuñjīya, yathā teṣāṃ kārāḥ kṛtā atyarthaṃ mahāphalāḥ syur mahānuśaṃsā mahādyutayo mahāvistārāḥ, candropamaś ca kulāny upasaṃkrameyaṃ vyavakṛṣya kāyaṃ, vyavakṛṣya cittaṃ hrīmān apragalbhaḥ, anātmotkarsī, aparapansī / yathā svena lābhena sucittaḥ syāṃ sumanāḥ, evaṃ parasyāpi lābhena sucittaḥ syāṃ sumanāḥ / evaṃcittaś ca punaḥ kulāny upasaṃkrameyaṃ, tat kuta etal labhyaṃ pravrajitena parakuleṣu yad dadatu me pare mā na dadatu / satkṛtya, māsatkṛtya, prabhūtaṃ mā stokaṃ, praṇītaṃ mā lūhaṃ, tvaritaṃ mā dhandham / evaṃ caritasya me kulāny upasaṃkrāmataḥ sacet pare na dadyus tenāhaṃ na teṣām antika āghātacittatayā pratighacittatayā vyavadīryeyam / na ca punas tannidānaṃ kāyasya bhedād apāyopapattyā vighātam āpadyeyam / yaduta tām evāghātacittatāṃ pratighacittatām adhipatiṃ kṛtvā saced asatkṛtya na satkṛtya, sacet stokaṃ na prabhūtam / sacel lūhaṃ na praṇītaṃ, saced dhandhaṃ na tvaritaṃ dadyuḥ / tayāhaṃ nāghātacittatayā, pratighacittatayā ca vyavadīryeyam" iti vistareṇa pūrvavat / "imaṃ cāhaṃ kavaḍīkāram āhāraṃ niśritya tathā tathā pratipadyeyaṃ, tāñ ca mātrāṃ prativedyeyam / yena me jīvitendriyanirodhaś (
children.translated_text: ) having established myself in a state worthy of use, should use it in such a way that their deeds would be of exceedingly great fruit, great benefit, great brilliance, and great extent. And I should approach families like the moon — with body withdrawn, with mind withdrawn, modest, not bold, not praising myself, not disparaging others. Just as I would be well-minded and well-pleased with my own gain, so too I would be well-minded and well-pleased with another's gain. And with such a mind I should approach families. But how could this be obtained by a renunciant in the homes of others — that others should give to me or not give; with respect or without respect; abundantly or in small measure; of excellent quality or of poor quality; quickly or slowly? When I, conducting myself thus, approach families — if others do not give, I would not on that account be broken by a mind of hostility or a mind of aversion toward them. Nor on that account, upon the dissolution of the body, would I suffer the harm of rebirth in the lower realms — namely, making that very mind of hostility and mind of aversion the predominant factor. If they should give without respect rather than with respect, if they should give in small measure rather than abundantly, if they should give of poor quality rather than excellent, if they should give slowly rather than quickly — I would not on that account be broken by a mind of hostility and a mind of aversion" — and so on in detail as before. "And relying on this morselled food, I should so practice and realize that measure,
<s>Śbh</s> I 130

children.text: ) ca na syān na ca piṇḍakena klāmyeyam / brahmacaryānugrahaś ca me syād evaṃ ca me śramaṇabhāve pravrajitabhāve sthitasyāyaṃ piṇḍapātaparibhogaḥ pratirūpaś ca pariśuddhaś cānavadyaś ca syād" ebhir ākāraiḥ sa pratisaṃkhyāyāhāram āharati //
children.translated_text: ) so that my life-faculty would not cease, and I would not be fatigued by the almsround. And there would be for me support for the holy life. And for me, abiding thus in the state of an ascetic and one gone forth, this use of almsfood would be proper, pure, and blameless." With these reflections he partakes of food wisely.

body.translated_text: He thinks thus: "These donors and patrons of gifts, having gathered their possessions with difficulty, experiencing the great danger produced by seeking, repeatedly pressing out their skin, flesh, and blood, give to us — namely, out of compassion, desiring a special fruit. For that almsfood thus obtained by us, the proper way of using it would be this: that I,

āhāraḥ punaḥ katamaḥ / catvāra āhārāḥ / kavaḍaṃkāraḥ, sparśaḥ, manaḥsaṃcetanā, vijñānaṃ cāsmiṃs tv arthe kavaḍaṃkāra āhāro 'bhipretaḥ / sa punaḥ katamaḥ / tadyathā manthā vā, apūpā vā, odanakulmāsaṃ vā, sarpiḥ, tailaṃ, madhu, phaṇitaṃ, māṃsaṃ, matsyā, vaIIūrā, lavaṇaṃ, kṣīraṃ, dadhi, navanītam itīmāni cānyāni caivaṃrūpāṇy upakaraṇāni yāni kavaḍāni kṛtvābhyavahriyante / tasmāt kavaḍaṃkāra ity ucyate / āharatīti bhuṇkte, pratiniṣevaty abhyavaharati, khādati, bhakṣayati, svādayati, pibati, cūṣatīti paryāyāḥ //
body.translated_text: What then is food? There are four kinds of nutriment: morselled food, contact, mental volition, and consciousness. But in this context, morselled food is what is intended. And what is that? Namely: barley meal, cakes, boiled rice and porridge, ghee, oil, honey, molasses, meat, fish, beans, salt, milk, curds, butter — these and other such provisions which, having been made into morsels, are ingested. Therefore it is called 'morselled food.' 'He partakes of food' — this means he eats, consumes, ingests, chews, eats up, tastes, drinks, and sucks — these are synonyms.

children.text: ) khādyamāno bādhyamāna uddhatendriyo bhavaty unnatendriyaś ca, drutamānasaḥ, plutamānasaḥ, asthitamānaso 'vyupaśāntamānasaḥ, te punar atyartham āhāram āharanto dravārtham āharantīty ucyate / śrutavāṃs tv āryaśrāvakaḥ pratisaṃkhyānabalika ādīnavadarśī niḥsaraṇaṃ prajānan paribhuṅkte / na tu tathā yathā te kāmopabhogino bhuñjante / tenāha na dravārtham //
children.translated_text: ) being consumed and oppressed, one becomes one of agitated faculties and excited faculties, with a racing mind, a leaping mind, an unsteady mind, an unquiet mind. Those who partake of food excessively are said to partake 'for the sake of sport.' But the learned noble disciple, endowed with the power of wise reflection, seeing the danger, knowing the escape, uses [food] — but not in the way that those sensual enjoyers eat. Therefore he says: 'Not for the sake of sport.'

body.translated_text: "Not for the sake of sport" means: those who partake of food for the purpose of sensual enjoyment — [thinking:] "We, with bodies gratified and sated by food, when the evening time has arrived, when night has come, together with women wearing garlands on their heads, with arms soft as bottle-gourd, with breasts like balls, while playing, delighting, and being entertained — we shall manifest excitement and sport." This 'sport' in the noble <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> refers to evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, namely thoughts connected with sensual desire and connected with sexual intercourse. By these,

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> I 134

children.text: ) iti / "prabhūtabhakṣaṇe ca pratibalā bhaviṣyāmaḥ / bhuktaṃ ca samyak pariṇamiṣyati / doṣāṇāṃ cāpacayaḥ kṛto bhaviṣyati"/ ity ārogyamadārthaṃ, yauvanamadārtham, jīvitamadārthaṃ paribhuñjate /
children.translated_text: ) and we shall be healthy for a long time, and our youth will continue for a long time and will not quickly be overcome by old age that disfigures the body." "And we shall live longer," and "We shall be competent for eating abundantly, and what is eaten will be properly digested, and there will be a reduction of the humors." Thus they eat for the sake of intoxication with health, for the sake of intoxication with youth, and for the sake of intoxication with life.

body.translated_text: "Not for the sake of intoxication, not for the sake of adornment, not for the sake of beautification" means: just as those very sensual enjoyers partake of food for this purpose — [thinking:] "Today we have partaken of food — namely, abundant and to our fill, as much as possible and to our strength; unctuous, virile, nourishing, excellent in color, excellent in smell, and excellent in taste, thoroughly satisfying. When night has passed and dawn has come, we shall be capable and competent for exercise — namely, by means of wrestling, or striking blows, or through habitual exercise, or through rolling on the ground, or through digging the earth, or through arm exercises, or through leg-bracing, or through jumping, or through leaping, or through wheel-exercises. And relying on that exercise, we shall become strong, with well-developed limbs;

body.text: teṣāṃ punar evaṃ bhavati / "kṛtavyāyāmā vayaṃ snātrasaṃvidhānaṃ kariṣyāmo yaduta śucinā toyena gātrāṇi prakṣālayiṣyāmaḥ / prakṣālitagātrāś ca keśāni ca prasādhayiṣyāmaḥ / vividhena cānulepanena, kāyam anūpalipya vividhair vastrair vividhair mālyair vividhair alaṃkāraiḥ kāyaṃ bhūṣayiṣyāmaḥ" / tatra yat snānaprasādhanānulepanam idam ucyate teṣāṃ maṇḍanam / tathā maṇḍanajātānāṃ yad vastramālyābharaṇadhāraṇam idam ucyate vibhūṣaṇam iti / maṇḍanārthaṃ vibhūṣaṇārthaṃ paribhuñjate / ta evaṃ madamattā maṇḍanajātivibhūṣitagātrāḥ / pratyupasthite madhyāhnasamaye sāyāhnasamaye vā bhaktasamaye tṛṣitā bubhukṣitāś ca, pareṇa tarṣeṇa, parayā nandyā, pareṇāmodena, anādīnavadarśino niḥsaraṇam aprajānanto yathopapannam āhāram āharanti / yāvad eva punaḥ punar dravārthaṃ, madārthamṃ, maṇḍanārthaṃ, vibhūṣaṇārthaṃ ca / śrutavāṃs tv āryaśrāvakaḥ pratisaṃkhyānabalika ādīnavadarśī niḥsaranaṃ prajānan paribhuṅkte / na tu tathā yathā te kāmopabhoginaḥ paribhuñjate/ "nānyatremam asaṃniṣevaṇaṃ prahātavyam āhāraṃ pratiniṣevamāṇa eva prahāsyāmī"ti //
body.translated_text: They further think thus: "Having exercised, we shall make arrangements for bathing — namely, we shall wash our limbs with clean water. Having washed our limbs, we shall dress our hair. And having anointed the body with various unguents, we shall adorn the body with various garments, various garlands, and various ornaments." Therein, the bathing, hair-dressing, and anointing — this is called their 'adornment.' And for those thus adorned, the wearing of garments, garlands, and jewelry — this is called 'beautification.' They eat for the sake of adornment and beautification. Those, thus intoxicated, with bodies adorned and beautified — when the midday time or the evening time has arrived, at the time of the meal, being thirsty and hungry, with extreme thirst, with extreme delight, with extreme relish, not seeing the danger and not knowing the escape — they partake of whatever food is available. And again and again [they eat] for the sake of sport, for the sake of intoxication, for the sake of adornment, and for the sake of beautification. But the learned noble disciple, endowed with the power of wise reflection, seeing the danger, knowing the escape, uses [food] — but not in the way that those sensual enjoyers use [it]. "There is no other way — this food that is to be abandoned through non-use, I shall abandon while still using it."

body.translated_text: "Only for the maintenance of this body" means: having eaten or not eaten, whatever constitutes the maintenance of the life of the body. "I, having partaken of this food, shall live, shall not die" — thus one partakes. Therefore he says: 'Only for the maintenance of this body.'

body.translated_text: How does one partake for the sake of sustenance? Sustenance is twofold: there is sustenance with difficulty and there is sustenance without difficulty.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-6-a-(5)-i-(a) Ms.48b4M, Sh.89-2, W.*146-23, P.41b3, D.34b6, N.36b7, Co.38a3, Ch.410a9
kṛcchreṇa yātrā katamā / yadrūpam āhāram āharato jighatsā daurbalyaṃ vā bhavati / duḥkhito vā bāḍhaglānaḥ / adharmeṇa vā piṇḍapātaṃ paryeṣate, na dharmeṇa / raktaḥ paribhuṅkte sakto gṛddho grathito mūrchito 'dhyavasito 'dhyavasāyam āpannaḥ / guruko vāsya kāyo bhavaty akarmaṇyaḥ, aprahāṇakṣamaḥ, yenāsya dhandhaṃ cittaṃ samādhīyate / kṛcchreṇa vāśvāsapraśvāsāḥ pravartante / styānamiddhaṃ vā cittaṃ paryavanahati / iyam ucyate kṛcchreṇa yātrā //
body.translated_text: What is sustenance with difficulty? When one partakes of such food that there is hunger or weakness; or one is afflicted, seriously ill; or one seeks almsfood by unrighteous means, not by righteous means; or one eats with attachment, bound, greedy, entangled, infatuated, resolute, and having reached a state of resolve; or one's body becomes heavy, unworkable, incapable of abandoning [defilements], whereby one's mind enters concentration only slowly; or the breaths come and go with difficulty; or sloth-and-torpor overwhelm the mind. This is called sustenance with difficulty.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-6-a-(5)-i-(b) Ms.48b5M, Sh.89-11, W.M46-32, P.41b7, D.35a2, N.37a3, Co.38a7, Ch.410a16
akṛcchreṇa yātrā katamā / yathāpi tadrūpam āhāram āharato yathā jighatsā daurbalyaṃ vā na bhavati / nābhyadhiko bhavati duḥkhito vā bādhaglānaḥ / dharmeṇa vā piṇḍapātaṃ paryeṣate, na vādharmeṇa / arakto vā paribhuṅkte 'sakto 'gṛdhro 'grathito 'mūrchito 'nadhyavasito 'nadhyavasāyam āpannaḥ / na cāsya kāyo guruko bhavati karmaṇyo bhavati prahāṇakṣamaḥ / yenāsya tvaritaṃ cittaṃ samādhīyate / alpakṛcchreṇāśvasapraśvāsāḥ pravartante / styānamiddhaṃ cittaṃ na paryavanahati / iyam ucyate 'lpakṛcchreṇa yātrā //
body.translated_text: What is sustenance without difficulty? When one partakes of such food that there is neither hunger nor weakness; one is not excessively afflicted or seriously ill; one seeks almsfood by righteous means, not by unrighteous means; one eats without attachment, unbound, without greed, unentangled, uninfatuated, unresolute, and not having reached a state of resolve; and one's body does not become heavy but is workable and capable of abandoning [defilements], whereby one's mind enters concentration quickly; the breaths come and go with little difficulty; and sloth-and-torpor do not overwhelm the mind. This is called sustenance without difficulty.

body.text: tatra yā kṛcchreṇa yātrā tayā jīvitasthitir bhavati, kāyasya sāvadyā sasaṃkliṣṭā / tatra ye 'yam alpakṛcchreṇa yātrā tayā jīvitasthitir bhavati / kāyasya sā ca punar anavadyāsaṃkliṣṭā / tatra śrutavān āryaśrāvakaḥ sāvadyām saṃkliṣṭāṃ yātrāṃ parivarjayati, anavadyām asaṃkliṣṭāṃ yātrāṃ gacchati, pratiṣevate / tenāha yāpanāyai //
body.translated_text: Therein, sustenance with difficulty — the maintenance of life and body thereby is blameworthy and defiled. But sustenance without difficulty — the maintenance of life and body thereby is blameless and undefiled. Therein, the learned noble disciple avoids the blameworthy and defiled sustenance and follows, practices, the blameless and undefiled sustenance. Therefore he says: 'For the sake of sustenance.'

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-6-a-(5)-ii Ms.48b8L, Sh.90-11, W.*147-6, P.42a7, D.35a7, N.37b2, Co.38b6, Ch.410a29
sā punar anavadyāsaṃkliṣṭā yātrā yā pūrvam uktā tāṃ kathaṃ kalpayati / āha / yady "ayaṃ jighatsoparataye, brahmacaryānugrahāye"ti, "paurāṇāṃ ca vedanāṃ prahāsyāmi navāṃ ca notpādayiṣyāmi / yātrā ca me bhaviṣyati / balaṃ ca, sukhaṃ cānavadyatā ca, sparśavihāratā ce"ti / evaṃ pratiṣevamāṇaḥ anavadyām asaṃkliṣṭāṃ yātrāṃ kalpayati //
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-6-a-(5)-ii — Moreover, how does one arrange that blameless, undefiled subsistence which was previously described? It is said: If [one reflects]: "This is for the cessation of hunger, for the support of the holy life," and "I shall put an end to old feelings and shall not generate new ones; and there will be subsistence for me, and strength, and happiness, and blamelessness, and comfortable dwelling" — thus partaking, one arranges a blameless, undefiled subsistence.

body.text: (I)-C-IIl-6-a-(5)-ii-(a) Ms.49a1M, Sh.91-3, W.*147-12, PA2b1, D.35b2, N.37b4, Co.39a1, Ch.410b4 kathaṃ ca punar jighatsoparataya āharati / pratyupasthite bhaktasamaye, utpannāyāṃ kṣudhāyāṃ, yadā paribhuṅkte tasyaiva kṣutparyavasthānasya jighatsādaurbalyasya ca prativigamāya tāñ ca mātrāṃ paribhuṅkte / yathāsya bhuktavato 'kāle punar jighatsādaurbalyaṃ na bādhate, yaduta sāyāhnasamaye vā, abhikrāntāyāṃ vā rajanyāṃ, śvobhūte 'pratyupasthite bhaktasamaye / evaṃ jighatsoparataya āharati //
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-6-a-(5)-ii-(a) — And how does one eat for the cessation of hunger? When mealtime has arrived and hunger has arisen, when one eats, one eats just that measure for the removal of that state of hunger and weakness due to hunger — such a measure that, having eaten, the weakness of hunger does not afflict one again at an improper time, whether in the afternoon, or when the night has advanced, or the next day when mealtime has not yet arrived. Thus one eats for the cessation of hunger.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-6-a-(5)-ii-(b) Ms.49a2M, Sh.91-10, W.*147-19, P.42b4, D.35b4, N.37b6, Co.39a3, Ch.410b10
kathaṃ brahmacaryānugrahāyāharati / tāṃ mātrāṃ paribhuṅkte / tadrūpam āhāram āharati / yenāsya kuśalapakṣe prayuktasya dṛṣṭa eva dharme bhuktasamanantaraṃ tasminn eva vā divase 'gurukaḥ kāyo bhavati / karmaṇyaś ca bhavati, prahāṇakṣamaś ca, yenāsya tvaritatvaritaṃ cittaṃ samādhīyate / alpakṛcchreṇāśvāsapraśvāsāḥ pravartante / styānamiddhaṃ cittaṃ na paryavanahati, yenāyaṃ bhavyo bhavati pratibalaś ca kṣipram eva, aprāptasya prāptaye, anadhigatasyādhigamāya, asākṣātkṛtasya sākṣātkriyāyai / evaṃ brahmacaryānugrahāyāharati //
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-6-a-(5)-ii-(b) — How does one eat for the support of the holy life? One eats that measure and takes in that kind of food by which, while engaged in the wholesome side, in this very life, immediately after eating or on that very day, one's body is not heavy, one is fit for action, capable of striving, by which one's mind quickly becomes concentrated, the breaths proceed with little difficulty, drowsiness and torpor do not overwhelm the mind, by which one becomes capable and able to quickly attain what has not been attained, realize what has not been realized, directly experience what has not been directly experienced. Thus one eats for the support of the holy life.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-6-a-(5)-ii-(c) Ms.49a4M, Sh.91-20, W.*147-28, P.42b8, D.35b7, N.38a2, Co.39a6, Ch.410b17
kathaṃ "paurāṇāṃ vedanāṃ prahāsyāmī"ty āharati / yathāpi tad atītam adhvānam upādāyāmātrayā vā paribhuktaṃ bhavaty apathyaṃ vā, apariṇate vā, yenāsya vividhaḥ kāyika ābādhaḥ samutpanno bhavati / tadyathā kaṇḍūḥ, (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 140

children.text: ) kuṣṭhaḥ kiṭibhaḥ kilāsa iti vistareṇa pūrvavat / tasya cābādhanidāna utpadyante śārīrikā vedanā duḥkhās tīvrāḥ, kharāḥ, kaṭukā, amanāpāḥ / tasyābādhasyopaśamāya tāsāṃ ca tannidānānāṃ duḥkhānāṃ vedanānām upaśamāya hitaṃ pathyam anukūlam ānulomikaṃ vaidyopadiṣṭena vidhinā bhaiṣajyaṃ pratiṣevate / sāṃpreyaṃ cāhāram āharati / yenāsyotpannasyābādhasya tannidānānāṃ ca duḥkhānāṃ vedanānāṃ prahāṇaṃ bhavati / evaṃ "paurāṇāṃ vedanāṃ prahāsyāmī"ty āhāram āharati //
children.translated_text: leprosy, skin disease, vitiligo — and so on in detail as before. And on account of that ailment, there arise bodily feelings of suffering — intense, sharp, bitter, disagreeable. For the subsiding of that ailment and for the subsiding of those painful feelings arisen from that cause, one takes medicine that is beneficial, wholesome, suitable, and concordant, as prescribed by a physician. And one takes appropriate food, by which the arisen ailment and the painful feelings arisen from that cause are abandoned. Thus one eats [thinking] "I shall put an end to old feelings."

body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-6-a-(5)-ii-(c) — How does one eat [thinking] "I shall put an end to old feelings"? Just as in the past, one may have eaten excessively, or unwholesomely, or what was not properly digested, whereby various bodily ailments have arisen — such as itching,

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-6-a-(5)-ii-(d) Ms.49a6M, Sh.92-13, W.*147-38, P.43a4, D.36a3, N.38a5, Co.39b3, Ch.410b27
katham "navāṃ vedanāṃ notpādayiṣyāmī"ty āhāram āharati / sa vartamānam adhvānam upādāya sukhī, arogaḥ, balavān, nāmātrayā vā paribhuṅkte, apathyaṃ vā, apariṇate vā / yenāsyānāgatam adhvānam upādāya śvo vā, uttaraśvo vā, viṣūcikā vā kāye saṃtiṣṭheta / anyatamānyatamo vā kāye kāyika ābādhaḥ samutpadyeta / tadyathā kaṇḍūḥ, kuṣṭhaḥ, kiṭibhaḥ, kilāsa iti vistareṇa pūrvavat / tannidānā utpadyerañ chārīrikā vedanāḥ pūrvavat / evaṃ ca "navāṃ vedanāṃ notpādayiṣyāmī"ty āharati //
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-6-a-(5)-ii-(d) — How does one eat [thinking] "I shall not generate new feelings"? Taking into account the present time, one is happy, healthy, and strong, and one does not eat excessively, or unwholesomely, or what is not properly digested, by which, taking into account the future, tomorrow or the day after, dysentery would establish itself in the body, or some other bodily ailment would arise — such as itching, leprosy, skin disease, vitiligo — and so on in detail as before — and bodily feelings would arise from that cause, as before. Thus one eats [thinking] "I shall not generate new feelings."

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-6-a-(5)-ii-(e) Ms.49b2L, Sh.93-1, W.*148-6, PA3a7, D.36a5, N.38b1, Co.39b5, Ch.410c5
kathaṃ "yātrā me bhaviṣyati balaṃ ca sukhaṃ cānavadyatā ca sparśavihāratā ce"ty āharati / yat tāvad bhuktvā jīvatīty evaṃ yātrā bhavati / yat punar jighatsādaurbalyam apanayati evam asya balaṃ bhavati / yat punaḥ paurāṇāṃ vedanāṃ prajahāti / navāṃ notpādayaty evam asya sukhaṃ bhavati / yat punar dharmeṇa piṇḍapātaṃ paryeṣṭyāraktaḥ paribhuṅkte 'sakta iti vistareṇa pūrvavad evam asyānavadyatā bhavati / yat punar (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 142

children.text: ) bhuktavato na gurukaḥ kāyo bhavati, karmaṇyaś ca bhavati, prahāṇakṣamo vistareṇa pūrvavad evam asya sparśavihāratā bhavati /
children.translated_text: having eaten, one's body is not heavy, one is fit for action, capable of striving — and so on in detail as before — thus there is comfortable dwelling.

body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-6-a-(5)-ii-(e) — How does one eat [thinking] "There will be subsistence for me, and strength, and happiness, and blamelessness, and comfortable dwelling"? First, the fact that having eaten one continues to live — thus there is subsistence. Furthermore, the fact that one removes the weakness of hunger — thus there is strength. Furthermore, the fact that one puts an end to old feelings and does not generate new ones — thus there is happiness. Furthermore, the fact that one seeks almsfood righteously and eats unattached, ungrasping — and so on in detail as before — thus there is blamelessness. Furthermore, the fact that

body.text: tenāha pratisaṃkhyāyāhāram āharati / na dravārthaṃ, na madārthaṃ, na maṇḍanārtham iti vistareṇa pūrvavad ayaṃ tāvad bhojane mātrajñatāyā vistaravibhāgaḥ //
body.translated_text: Therefore it is said: "One eats food with wise reflection — not for amusement, not for intoxication, not for adornment" — and so on in detail as before. This is the detailed analysis of moderation in eating.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-6-b-(1) Ms.49b4L, Sh.93-14, W.M48-17, P,43b4, D.36b2, N.38b5, Co.40a2, Ch.410c15
samāsārthaḥ punaḥ katamaḥ / āha / yaṃ ca paribhuṅkte yathā ca paribhuṅkte 'yaṃ samāsārthaḥ / kaṃ paribhuṅkte / yaduta kavaḍaṃkāram āhāraṃ, manthā vā, apūpā vā, odanakulmāṣaṃ vā vistareṇa pūrvavat / kathaṃ paribhuṅkte / pratisaṃkhyāya paribhuṅkte / na dravārthaṃ, na madārthaṃ, na maṇḍanārtham iti vistareṇa pūrvavat //
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-6-b-(1) — What is the summary meaning? It is said: What one eats and how one eats — this is the summary meaning. What does one eat? Namely, material food — whether gruel, cakes, rice and grain porridge — and so on in detail as before. How does one eat? One eats with wise reflection — not for amusement, not for intoxication, not for adornment — and so on in detail as before.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-6-b-(2) Ms.49b5L, Sh.93-21, W.* 148-23, P.43b7, D.36b5, N.38b7, Co.40a5, Ch.410c19
punar aparaḥ samāsārthaḥ / pratipakṣaparigṛhītaṃ ca paribhuṅkte kāmasukhallikāntavivarjitaṃ cātmaklamathāntavivarjitaṃ ca brahmacaryānugrahāya ca /
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-6-b-(2) — Another summary meaning: One eats [food] that is taken up with the antidote, free from the extreme of pursuing sensual pleasure, free from the extreme of self-mortification, and for the support of the holy life.

body.text: kathaṃ pratipakṣaparigṛhītam / yad āha / pratisaṃkhyāyāhāram āharati /
body.translated_text: How is it taken up with the antidote? As it says: "One eats food with wise reflection."

body.text: kathaṃ kāmasukhallikāntavivarjitaṃ ca / yad āha / na dravārthaṃ na madārthaṃ, na maṇḍanārthaṃ, na vibhūṣaṇārtham iti /
body.translated_text: How is it free from the extreme of pursuing sensual pleasure? As it says: "Not for amusement, not for intoxication, not for adornment, not for embellishment."

body.text: katham ātmaklamathāntavivarjitam / yad āha / "jighatsoparataye, paurāṇāṃ ca vedanāṃ prahāsyāmi / navāṃ ca notpādayiṣyāmi / yātrā ca me bhaviṣyati / balaṃ ca sukhaṃ ce"ti /
body.translated_text: How is it free from the extreme of self-mortification? As it says: "For the cessation of hunger; I shall put an end to old feelings, and I shall not generate new ones; and there will be subsistence for me, and strength, and happiness."

body.text: kathaṃ brahmacaryānugrahāya paribhuṅkte / yad āha / brahamacaryānugrahāya, "anavadyatā ca sparśavihāratā ca me bhaviṣyatī"ti //
body.translated_text: How does one eat for the support of the holy life? As it says: "For the support of the holy life; there will be blamelessness and comfortable dwelling for me."

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-6-b-(3)-(a) Ms.49b6R, Sh.94-11, W.*148-33, P.44a4, D.37a2, N.39a4, Co40b2, Ch.41la1
punar aparaḥ samāsārthaḥ / dvayam idaṃ bhojanaṃ, cābhojanaṃ ca / tatrābhojanaṃ yat sarveṇa sarvam sarvathā kiṃcin na paribhuṅkte / (

and not eating, one dies.

body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-6-b-(3)-(a) — Another summary meaning: This eating is twofold — eating and non-eating. Therein, non-eating is when one does not eat anything at all in every way,

body.text: tatra bhojanaṃ dvividham / samabhojanaṃ, viṣamabhojanaṃ ca / tatra samabhojanaṃ yan nātyalpaṃ nātiprabhūtam, nāpathyam, nāpariṇate na saṃkliṣṭam /
body.translated_text: Therein, eating is twofold — balanced eating and imbalanced eating. Therein, balanced eating is that which is neither too little nor too abundant, neither unwholesome nor indigestible, nor defiled.

body.text: tatra viṣamabhojanaṃ yad atyalpam atiprabhūtaṃ ca, apariṇate vā, apathyaṃ vā, saṃkliṣṭaṃ vā paribhuṅkte /
body.translated_text: Therein, imbalanced eating is eating what is too little or too abundant, or indigestible, or unwholesome, or defiled.

body.text: tatra samabhojane nātyalpabhojane jighatsādaurbalyam anutpannaṃ notpādayati, utpannaṃ prajahāti /
body.translated_text: Therein, by balanced eating that is not too little — the weakness of hunger that has not arisen is not generated, and that which has arisen is abandoned.

body.text: tatra nātiprabhūtabhojanena samabhojanena na gurukaḥ kāyo bhavaty akarmaṇyaḥ, aprahāṇakṣamo vistareṇa pūrvavat /
body.translated_text: Therein, by balanced eating that is not too abundant — the body does not become heavy and unfit for action, incapable of striving — and so on in detail as before.

body.text: tatra pariṇatabhojanena pathyabhojanena samabhojanena paurāṇāṃ ca vedanāṃ prajahāti / navāṃ ca notpādayiṣyaty evam asya yātrā bhavati balaṃ ca, sukhaṃ ca /
body.translated_text: Therein, by balanced eating that is digestible and wholesome — one puts an end to old feelings and will not generate new ones. Thus there is subsistence and strength and happiness for one.

body.text: asaṃkliṣṭabhojanena samabhojanenānavadyatā ca bhavati sparśavihāratā ca /
body.translated_text: By balanced eating that is undefiled — there is blamelessness and comfortable dwelling.

body.text: tatrātyalpabhojanaṃ yena jīvati jighatsādaurbalyaparītaś ca jīvati / atiprabhūtabhojanam / yenāsya gurubhārādhyākrāntaḥ kāyo bhavati / na ca kālena bhaktaṃ pariṇamati /
body.translated_text: Therein, too-little eating is that by which one lives but lives afflicted by the weakness of hunger. Too-abundant eating is that by which one's body becomes overburdened as if by a heavy load, and the food does not digest in due time.

body.text: tatrāpariṇatabhojanena viṣūcikā kāye saṃtiṣṭhate / anyatamānyatamo vā kāye kāyika ābādhaḥ samutpadyate / yathāpariṇatabhojanenaivam apathyabhojanena /
body.translated_text: Therein, by eating what is indigestible, dysentery establishes itself in the body, or some other bodily ailment arises. As with indigestible food, so with unwholesome food.

body.text: tatrāyam apathyabhojane viśeṣaḥ / doṣaḥ pracayaṃ gacchati, kharaṃ cābādhaṃ spṛśati /
body.translated_text: Therein, this is the distinction regarding unwholesome food: the [bodily] humor goes to excess, and one experiences a severe ailment.

body.text:
tatra saṃkliṣṭabhojanenādharmeṇa piṇḍapātaṃ paryeṣya raktaḥ paribhuṅkte, sakto gṛddho grathita iti vistareṇa pūrvavat /
iti yaḥ samabhojanaṃ ca paribhuṅkte / viṣamabhojanaṃ ca parivarjayati / tasmād bhojane samakārīty ucyate / bhojane ca samakāritaiṣā ebhir ākārair ākhyātā, uttānā, vivṛtā, saṃprakāśitā / yaduta pratisaṃkhyāyāhāram āharati / (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 146

children.text: ) na dravārthaṃ, na madārthaṃ, na maṇḍanārthaṃ, na vibhūṣaṇārtham iti vistareṇa pūrvavat //
children.translated_text: not for amusement, not for intoxication, not for adornment, not for embellishment" — and so on in detail as before.

body.translated_text: Therein, by defiled eating — one seeks almsfood unrighteously, attached, and eats clinging, greedy, entangled — and so on in detail as before. Thus one who eats balanced food and avoids imbalanced food — therefore one is called 'moderate in eating.' And this moderation in eating has been explained, disclosed, revealed, and made clear by these aspects — namely: "One eats food with wise reflection,

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-6-b-(3)-(b) Ms.50a5R, Sh.96-1, W.*149-20, P.45a2, D.37b5, N.40a1, Co.41a6, Ch.411a27
tatra yat tāvad āha / "pratisaṃkhyāyāhāram āharati / na dravārthaṃ, na madārthaṃ, na maṇḍanārthaṃ na vibhūṣaṇārtham", yāvad eva,"asya kāyasya sthitaye, yāpanāyai", anena tāvad abhojanaṃ ca pratikṣipati /
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-6-b-(3)-(b) — Therein, the statement: "One eats food with wise reflection — not for amusement, not for intoxication, not for adornment, not for embellishment," up to "for the maintenance and sustenance of this body" — by this, non-eating is rejected.

body.text: yat punar āha / "jighatsoparataye, brahmacaryānugrahāya" vistareṇa yāvat "sparśavihāratāyai", anena viṣamabhojanaṃ pratikṣipati /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the statement: "For the cessation of hunger, for the support of the holy life" — and so on in detail up to "comfortable dwelling" — by this, imbalanced eating is rejected.

body.text: kathaṃ ca punar viṣamabhojanaṃ pratikṣipati / ["bkres pa bsal bar bya ba'i phyir źes gaṅ gsuṅs pa des ni / re źig zas ha caṅ chuṅ ba'i zas ran pa ma yin" pa spoṅ bar byed do] /
body.translated_text: And how is imbalanced eating rejected? ["The statement 'for the removal of hunger' — by this, first of all, balanced eating that is not too little" is what is rejected as improper.]

body.text: yat tāvat āha / "brahmācaryānugrahāya", anenātiprabhūtabhojanaṃ pratikṣipati /
body.translated_text: The statement: "For the support of the holy life" — by this, too-abundant eating is rejected.

body.text: yad āha / "paurāṇāṃ ca vedanāṃ prahāsyāmi, navāṃ ca notpādayiṣyāmī"ty anenāpariṇatabhojanatām apathya bhojanatāṃ ca pratikṣipati /
body.translated_text: The statement: "I shall put an end to old feelings, and I shall not generate new ones" — by this, eating what is indigestible and eating what is unwholesome are rejected.

body.text: yad āha / "yātrā ca me bhaviṣyati, balaṃ", anena nātyalpabhojanatāṃ nātiprabhūtabhojanatāṃ ca darśayati /
body.translated_text: The statement: "There will be subsistence for me, and strength" — by this, eating neither too little nor too abundantly is shown.

body.text: yad āha / "sukhaṃ ca me bhaviṣyatī"ty anena pariṇatabhojanatāṃ pathyabhojanatāṃ ca darśayati /
body.translated_text: The statement: "There will be happiness for me" — by this, eating what is digestible and eating what is wholesome are shown.

body.text: yad āha / "anavadyatā ca me bhaviṣyati, sparśavihāratā ce"ty anenāsaṃkliṣṭabhojanatāṃ darśayati /
body.translated_text: The statement: "There will be blamelessness for me, and comfortable dwelling" — by this, eating what is undefiled is shown.

body.text: yo 'sāv adharmeṇa piṇḍapātaṃ paryeṣya raktaḥ paribhuṅkte / sakto vistareṇa pūrvavat / sa saṃkliṣṭaś ca paribhuṅkte, sāvadyatā cāsya bhavati / tasyaiva ca kuśalapakṣaprayuktasya pratisaṃlayane, yoge, manasikāre, uddeśasvādhyāye, arthacintāyāṃ ta eva pāpakā akuśalā vitarkāś cittam anusravanti / ye 'sya tanniṃnām, tatpravaṇāṃ, tatprāgbhārām (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 148

children.text: ) cittasantatiṃ pravartayanti / yenāsya sparśavihāro na bhavati /
children.translated_text: mental continuum to incline toward them, slope toward them, and tend toward them — whereby he does not have comfortable dwelling (<s>sparśavihāra</s>).

body.translated_text: One who, having sought alms-food by unrighteous means, partakes of it with attachment, clinging — in detail as before. He partakes in a defiled manner, and there is blameworthiness for him. And when that very one is engaged in the wholesome side — in seclusion, in meditation, in mental attention, in recitation, in self-study, in reflecting on the meaning — those very evil unwholesome thoughts flow into his mind, which cause his

body.text: sā ceyaṃ dvividhā sparśāvihāratā / atiprabhūtabhojanaparivarjanāc ca yenāsya na gurukaḥ kāyo bhavaty akarmaṇyaḥ, aprahāṇakṣama iti vistareṇa pūrvavat / āhāre cāsvādākaraṇād yenāsya vitarkasaṃkṣobhakṛtāsparśavihāratā na bhavati /
body.translated_text: And this non-comfortable-dwelling is of two kinds: through the avoidance of excessive eating, whereby one's body is not heavy and unfit for action, incapable of striving — in detail as before; and through not savoring food, whereby the non-comfortable-dwelling caused by the disturbance of [unwholesome] thoughts does not arise.

body.text: tad evaṃ sati sarvair ebhiḥ padair bhojane samakāritā vyākhyātā bhavati / iyam ucyate bhojane mātrajñatā // vistarataḥ saṃkṣepataś ca //
body.translated_text: This being so, moderation in eating has been explained through all these terms. This is called moderation in food (<s>bhojane mātrajñatā</s>) — in detail and in summary.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-7-a-(1)-i Ms.50b3R, Sh.97-16, P.45b7, D.38b1, N.40b5, Co.42a3, Ch.411c6
pūrvarātrāpararātraṃ jāgarikāyogasyānuyuktatā katamā / tatra katamaḥ pūrvarātraḥ / katamo 'pararātraḥ / katamo jāgarikāyogaḥ / katamā jāgarikāyogasyānuyuktatā //
body.translated_text: What is the application to the practice of wakefulness during the first and last watches of the night? Therein, what is the first watch of the night? What is the last watch? What is the practice of wakefulness? What is the application to the practice of wakefulness?

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-7-a-(1)-ii Ms.50b4L, Sh.98-3, W.*71-28, P.45b8, D.38b2, N.40b6, Co.42a4, Ch.411c8
tatrāyaṃ sāyāhnaṃ pūrvarātraḥ, sāyāhnaṃ sūryasyāstaṃgamanam upādāya, yo rātryāḥ pūrvabhāgaḥ sātirekaṃ praharam / apararātraḥ katamaḥ / yo rātryā aparabhāgaḥ sātirekaṃ praharam /
body.translated_text: Therein, the 'first watch' is the evening, reckoning from the time of the setting of the sun — the first portion of the night, somewhat more than one watch. What is the 'last watch'? The latter portion of the night, somewhat more than one watch.

body.text: tatrāyaṃ jāgarikāyogaḥ / yad āha / divā caṅkramaniṣadyābhyām āvaraṇīyebhyo dharmebhyaś cittaṃ pariśodhayati / rātryāḥ prathame yāme caṅkramaniṣadyābhyām āvaraṇīyebhyo dharmebhyaś cittaṃ pariśodhayati / pariśodhya, bahir vihārasya pādau prakṣālya, vihāraṃ praviśya, dakṣiṇena pārśvena śayyāṃ kalpayati pāde pādam ādhāya, ālokasaṃjñī smṛtaḥ saṃprajānann utthānasaṃjñām eva manasikurvan, sa rātryāḥ paścime yāme laghu laghv eva prativibudhya, caṅkramaniṣadyābhyām āvaraṇīyebhyo dharmebhyaś cittaṃ pariśodhayati /
body.translated_text: Therein, this is the practice of wakefulness: as he says, 'During the day, by walking meditation and seated meditation, one purifies the mind from obstructive <s>dharmas</s>. During the first watch of the night, by walking meditation and seated meditation, one purifies the mind from obstructive <s>dharmas</s>.
