Having purified [it], outside the dwelling one washes one's feet, enters the dwelling, and lies down on the right side, placing foot upon foot, mindful of the perception of light, with clear comprehension, attending to the perception of rising. In the last watch of the night, quickly and promptly awakening, by walking meditation and seated meditation, one purifies the mind from obstructive <s>dharmas</s>.'

body.text: tatreyaṃ jāgarikāyogasyānuyuktatā / yathāpi tad buddhasya bhagavataḥ śrāvako jāgarikāyogasya śrotā tatra ca śikṣitukāmo bhavati / tathābhūtasyāsya "yaj jāgarikāyogam ārabhya buddhānujñātaṃ jāgarikāyogaṃ saṃpādayiṣyāmī"ti yaś chando vīryo vyāyāmo niṣkramaḥ parākramaḥ sthāna ārambha utsāha utsūdhir aprativāṇiś cetasaḥ (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 152
ness, and mental engagement, and continuity [there is — this is the application].

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the application to the practice of wakefulness: just as a disciple of the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, is a hearer of the practice of wakefulness and wishes to train in it — for such a person, [thinking:] 'I shall, with respect to the practice of wakefulness, fulfill the practice of wakefulness authorized by the <s>Buddha</s>' — whatever desire, vigor, effort, exertion, perseverance, firmness, enterprise, enthusiasm, energy, unrelenting-

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-7-a-(2)-i-(a)-(d) Ms.50b7M, Sh.99-9, W.*71-37, P.46a8, D.39a2, N.41a5, Co.42b3, Ch.411c22
tatra kathaṃ divā caṅkramaniṣadyābhyām āvaraṇīyebhyo dharmebhyaś cittaṃ pariśodhayati / "divā" ucyate sūryasyābhyudgamanasamayam upādāya yāvad astaṃgamanasamayāt / "caṅkrama" ucyata āyate vipulamāpite pṛthivīpradeśe gamanapratyāgamanapratisaṃyuktaṃ kāyakarma / "niṣadyā" ucyate yathāpīhaikatyo mañce vā pīṭhe vā tṛṇasaṃstare vā niṣīdati, paryaṅkam ābhujya, ṛjuṃ kāyaṃ praṇidhāyābhimukhīṃ smṛtim upasthāpya / āvaraṇāny ucyante pañca nivaraṇāni / āvaraṇīyā dharmā ye nivaraṇasthānīyā dharmā nivaraṇāhārakāḥ / te punaḥ katame / kāmacchandaḥ, vyāpādaḥ, styānamiddham, auddhatyakaukṛtyam, vicikitsā, śubhatā pratighanimittam andhakāro jñātijanapadāmaravitarkaḥ paurāṇasya ca hasitakrīḍitaramitaparivāritasyānusmṛtiḥ, trayaś cādhvānaḥ, tryadhvagatā cāyoniśodharmacintā //
body.translated_text: Therein, how does one during the day purify the mind from obstructive <s>dharmas</s> by walking meditation and seated meditation? 'During the day' means reckoning from the time of the rising of the sun until the time of its setting. 'Walking meditation' means bodily action involving going and returning on a long, wide, prepared stretch of ground. 'Seated meditation' means one who sits on a bed, a chair, or a grass mat, cross-legged, holding the body upright, establishing mindfulness before oneself. 'Obstructions' means the five hindrances (<s>nīvaraṇa</s>). 'Obstructive <s>dharmas</s>' means the <s>dharmas</s> that serve as the basis for the hindrances and that feed them. And what are those? Sensual desire (<s>kāmacchanda</s>), ill-will (<s>vyāpāda</s>), sloth-and-torpor (<s>styānamiddha</s>), restlessness-and-remorse (<s>auddhatyakaukṛtya</s>), doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>), the [perception of] beauty, the sign of aversion, darkness, thoughts about relatives, country, and immortals, and the recollection of past laughter, play, sport, and company, and the three time-periods, and unwise reflection on <s>dharmas</s> pertaining to the three time-periods.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-7-a-(2)-i-(d)-(1) Ms.51a2R, Sh.100-7, P.46b6, D.39a6, N.41b3, Co.43a1, Ch.412a5
ebhyaḥ kathaṃ caṅkrameṇa cittaṃ pariśodhayati / katibhyaś ca pariśodhayati / styānamiddhāt styānamiddhāhārakāc cāvaraṇāt pariśodhayati / ālokanimittam anena sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca sugṛhītaṃ bhavati sumanasikṛtam sujuṣṭaṃ supratividdham / sa ālokasahagatena suprabhāsasahagatena cittena channe vā, abhyavakāśe vā, caṅkrame caṅkramyamāṇaḥ anyatamānyatamena prasadanīyenālambanena cittaṃ saṃdarśayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati / (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 154

children.text: ) yaduta buddhānusmṛtyā va, dharmasaṃghaśīlatyāgadevatānusmṛtyā vā / kaye vā punar anena styānamiddhādīnavapratisaṃyuktā dharmāḥ śrutā bhavanty udgṛhītā dhṛtāḥ / tadyathā sūtraṃ geyaṃ vyākaraṇaṃ gāthodānanidānāvadānetivṛttakajātakavaipulyādbhutadharrnopadeśāḥ / yeṣu styānamiddham anekaparyāyeṇa vigarhitaṃ vijugupsitam / styānamiddhaprahāṇaṃ punaḥ stutaṃ varṇitaṃ praśastam / tān vistareṇa svareṇa svādhyāyaṃ karoti / pareṣāṃ vā prakāśayati, arthaṃ vā cintayati tulayaty upaparīksate, diśo vā vyavalokayati, candranakṣatragrahatārāsu vā dṛṣṭiṃ cārayati, udakena mukham ākledayati / evam asya tat styānamiddhaparyavasthānam anutpannaṃ ca notpadyate, utapannaṃ ca prativigacchati / evam anena tasmād āvaraṇīyād dharmāc cittaṃ pariśodhitaṃ bhavati //
children.translated_text: namely, through recollection of the <s>Buddha</s>, or through recollection of the <s>Dharma</s>, the <s>Saṃgha</s>, moral conduct, generosity, or deities. Or again, by him, <s>dharmas</s> connected with the danger of sloth-and-torpor have been heard, taken up, and retained — such as <s>sūtra</s>, <s>geya</s>, <s>vyākaraṇa</s>, <s>gāthā</s>, <s>udāna</s>, <s>nidāna</s>, <s>avadāna</s>, <s>itivṛttaka</s>, <s>jātaka</s>, <s>vaipulya</s>, <s>adbhutadharma</s>, and <s>upadeśa</s> — in which sloth-and-torpor is condemned, criticized, and disparaged in many ways, and the abandonment of sloth-and-torpor is praised, extolled, and commended. Those he recites aloud in full, or explains to others, or reflects on the meaning, examines it, investigates it, or he looks at the directions, or casts his gaze upon the moon, stars, planets, and constellations, or moistens his face with water. Thus, the mental state of sloth-and-torpor that has not arisen does not arise, and that which has arisen recedes. Thus, by him, the mind has been purified from that obstructive <s>dharma</s>.

body.translated_text: From these, how does one purify the mind by walking meditation? And from how many does one purify it? One purifies it from sloth-and-torpor, from the obstruction that feeds sloth-and-torpor. The perception of light has been well and properly grasped, well attended to, well applied, and well penetrated by him. With a mind accompanied by light, accompanied by brilliant clarity — whether under cover or in the open — while walking in the walking meditation area, with one or another gladdening object, one causes the mind to see, arouses, and gladdens [it] —

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-7-a-(2)-i-(d)-(1)-(2) Ms.51a6M, Sh.101-7, P.47a7, D.39b7, N,42a3, Co,43b2, Ch.412a23
tatra niṣadyayā katamebhya āvaraṇīyebhyo dharmebhyaś cittaṃ pariśodhayati / kathaṃ ca punaḥ pariśodhayati / āha / caturbhya āvaraṇīyebhyo dharmebhyaḥ pariśodhayati, kāmacchandād vyāpādād auddhatyakaukṛtyād vicikitsāyās tadāhārakebhyaś ca dharmebhyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, from which obstructive <s>dharmas</s> does one purify the mind by seated meditation? And how does one purify it? He says: One purifies it from four obstructive <s>dharmas</s> — from sensual desire (<s>kāmacchanda</s>), ill-will (<s>vyāpāda</s>), restlessness-and-remorse (<s>auddhatyakaukṛtya</s>), doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>), and from the <s>dharmas</s> that feed them.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-7-a-(2)-i-(d)-(1)-(2)-i Ms.51b1L, Sh.101-10, P.47b1, D,40a1, N.42a4, Co.43b3, Ch.412a26
sa utpanne vā kāmacchandaparyavasthāne prativinodanāyānutpanne vā dūrīkaraṇāya, niṣadya paryaṅkam ābhujya, ṛjuṃ kāyaṃ praṇidhāya pratimukhaṃ smṛtim upasthāpya, vinīlakaṃ vā vipūyakaṃ vā vipaḍumakaṃ vā vyādhmātakaṃ vikhāditakaṃ vā vilohitakaṃ vāsthiṃ vā śaṃkalikāṃ vānyatamānyatamaṃ bhadrakaṃ samādhinimittaṃ manasikaroti / ye vā punar anena dharmāḥ kāmarāgaprahāṇam evārabhya kāmacchandaprahāṇāyodgṛhītā bhavanti, dhṛtā vacasā parijitā manasānvīkṣitā dṛṣṭyā supratividdhāḥ / tadyathā sūtraṃ geyaṃ vyākaraṇam iti vistareṇa pūrvavat / ye 'nekaparyāyeṇa kāmarāgaṃ kāmacchandaṃ kāmālayaṃ kāmaniyantiṃ kāmādhyavasānaṃ vigarhanti vivarṇayanti vijugupsayanti / kāmarāgaprahāṇam (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 156

children.text: ) anekaparyāyeṇa stuvanti varṇayanti praśaṃsanti / tān dharmāṃs tathā niṣaṇṇo yoniśo manasikaroti / evam asyānutpannaṃ ca kāmacchandaparyavasthānaṃ notpadyate, utpannaṃ ca kāmacchandaparyavasthānaṃ prativigacchati //
children.translated_text: is praised, extolled, and commended in many ways — those <s>dharmas</s>, while thus seated, one wisely attends to. Thus the mental state of sensual desire that has not arisen does not arise, and the mental state of sensual desire that has arisen recedes.

body.translated_text: When the mental state of sensual desire has arisen, for its removal, or when it has not arisen, for its distancing — one sits cross-legged, holds the body upright, establishes mindfulness before oneself, and attends to one or another auspicious sign of concentration (<s>samādhinimitta</s>) — whether the blue-black [corpse], or the festering, or the bloated, or the split open, or the gnawed, or the blood-smeared, or bones, or the chain of bones. Or again, those <s>dharmas</s> that have been taken up for the purpose of abandoning sensual passion and sensual desire — from the <s>sūtras</s>, <s>geyas</s>, <s>vyākaraṇas</s>, and so on in detail as before — in which sensual passion, sensual desire, sensual attachment, sensual delight, and sensual determination are condemned, criticized, and disparaged in many ways; and the abandonment of sensual passion

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-7-a-(2)-i-(d)-(1)-(2)-ii Ms.51b3L, Sh.102-8, P.47b8, D.40a7, N.42b3, Co.44a2, Ch.412b11
tatra vyāpāde 'yaṃ viśeṣaḥ / tathā niṣaṇṇo maitrīsahagatena cittenāvaireṇāsapathenāvyābādhena vipulena mahadgatenāpramāṇena subhāvitenaikāṃ diśām adhimucya spharitvopasaṃpadya viharati / tathā dvitīyāṃ tathā tṛtīyāṃ tathā caturthīm ity ūrdhvam adhas tiryak sarvam anantaṃ lokam spharitvopasaṃpadya viharati / śeṣaṃ pūrvavat //
body.translated_text: Therein, regarding ill-will (<s>vyāpāda</s>), this is the distinction: while thus seated, with a mind accompanied by <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), without enmity, without hostility, without harm — vast, great, immeasurable, and well-cultivated — one resolves upon one direction, pervades and dwells in it. Likewise the second, the third, and the fourth direction; above, below, across — the entire infinite world one pervades and dwells in. The rest is as before.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-7-a-(2)-i-(d)-(1)-(2)-iii Ms.51b4R, Sh.102-15, P.48a3, D.40b2, N.42b5, Co.44a4, Ch.412b16
tatrauddhatyakaukṛtye viśeṣaḥ / tadyathā niṣaṇṇo 'dhyātmam eva cittaṃ sthāpayati saṃsthāpayati saṃniṣpādayaty ekotīkaroti samādhatte / śeṣaṃ pūrvavat //
body.translated_text: Therein, regarding restlessness-and-remorse (<s>auddhatyakaukṛtya</s>), this is the distinction: while thus seated, one internally settles, stabilizes, brings to one-pointedness, and concentrates the mind. The rest is as before.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-7-a-(2)-i-(d)-(1)-(2)-iv Ms.51b5M,W.*72-8,Sh.102-19,P.48a4,DAOb3, N.42b5,Co.44a5, Ch.412b18
tatra vicikitsānivaraṇe viśeṣaḥ / tathā san niṣaṇṇo 'tītam adhvānaṃ nāyoniśo manasikaroti, anāgataṃ pratyutpannam adhvānaṃ nāyoniśo manasikaroti / "kiṃ nv aham abhūvam atīte 'dhvani, āhosvin nāham atīte 'dhvani, ko nv aham abhūvaṃ, kathaṃ nv aham abhūvam atīte 'dhvani / ko nv ahaṃ bhaviṣyāmy anāgate 'dhvani, kathaṃ bhaviṣyāmy anāgate 'dhvani / ke santaḥ ke bhaviṣyāmaḥ / ayaṃ sattvaḥ kuta āgataḥ, itaś cyutaḥ kutragāmī bhaviṣyati" sa ityevaṃrūpam ayoniśomanasikāraṃ varjayitvā yoniśo manasikaroti, atītam apy adhvānam anāgataṃ pratyutpannam apy adhvānam /
body.translated_text: Therein, regarding the hindrance of doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>), this is the distinction: while thus seated, one does not unwisely attend to the past time-period, nor to the future or present time-period: "Did I exist in the past, or did I not exist in the past? What was I? How was I in the past? What will I be in the future? How will I be in the future? Being what, what shall we become? This being — where did it come from? And having departed from here, where will it go?" Abandoning such unwise attention, one wisely attends — to the past, the future, and the present time-periods.

body.text: sa dharmamātraṃ paśyati vastumātraṃ sac ca sato 'sac cāsato hetumātraṃ (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 158

children.text: ) phalamātraṃ, nāsadbhūtaṃ samāropaṃ karoti, na sadvastu nāśayaty apavadati, bhūtaṃ bhūtato jānāti / yadutānityato vā duḥkhato vā śūnyato vānātmato vānityeṣu duḥkheṣu śūnyeṣv anātmasu dharmeṣu / sa evaṃ yoniśo manasikurvan, buddhe 'pi niṣkāṅkṣo bhavati nirvicikitsaḥ, dharme saṃghe duḥkhe samudaye nirodhe mārge hetau hetusamutpanneṣu dharmeṣu niṣkāṅkṣo bhavati nirvicikitsaḥ / śeṣaṃ pūrvavat //
children.translated_text: merely effects. One does not superimpose what is not real, does not deny and reject what is real, and knows what is real as it really is — namely, as impermanent, as suffering, as empty, as not-self — in <s>dharmas</s> that are impermanent, suffering, empty, and not-self. Thus wisely attending, one becomes free from doubt and free from uncertainty regarding the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, the <s>Saṃgha</s>, suffering, its origin, cessation, the path, the cause, and <s>dharmas</s> arisen from causes. The rest is as before.

body.translated_text: One sees merely <s>dharmas</s>, merely things, what exists as existing and what does not exist as not existing, merely causes,

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-7-a-(2)-i-(d)-(1)-(2)-i',ii',iii',iv' Ms.52a2M, Sh.103-18, PA8b4, D.41a2, N.43a3, Co.44b4, Ch.412c4
tatra vyāpāde vaktavyam / yo 'nena pratighaṃ pratighanimittaṃ cārabhya, tasya ca prahāṇāya, dharmā udgṛhītā iti vistaraḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, regarding ill-will, it should be stated: whatever <s>dharmas</s> have been taken up by him with reference to aversion and the sign of aversion, and for its abandonment — in detail.

body.text: auddhatyakaukṛtye vaktavyam / anenauddhatyakaukṛtyam ārabhya, tasya ca prahāṇāya, dharmā udgṛhītā iti vistareṇa pūrvavat /
body.translated_text: Regarding restlessness-and-remorse, it should be stated: whatever <s>dharmas</s> have been taken up by him with reference to restlessness-and-remorse, and for its abandonment — in detail as before.

body.text: vicikitsāyāṃ vaktavyam / ye 'nena vicikitsām ārabhya, tasyāś ca prahāṇāya, dharmā udgṛhītā iti vistareṇa pūrvavat /
body.translated_text: Regarding doubt, it should be stated: whatever <s>dharmas</s> have been taken up by him with reference to doubt, and for its abandonment — in detail as before.

body.text: evam anena kāmacchandanivaraṇād vyāpādastyānamiddhauddhatyakaukṛtyavicikitsānivaraṇāc cittaṃ viśodhitaṃ bhavati, tadāhārakebhyaś ca dharmebhya āvaraṇīyebhyaḥ / tenāha / caṅkramaniṣadyābhyām āvaraṇīyebhyo dharmebhyaś cittaṃ pariśodhayati /
body.translated_text: Thus by this, his mind has been purified from the hindrance of sensual desire (<s>kāmacchanda-nivaraṇa</s>), from the hindrance of ill-will (<s>vyāpāda</s>), sloth-and-torpor (<s>styāna-middha</s>), restlessness-and-remorse (<s>auddhatya-kaukṛtya</s>), and doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>), and from the <s>dharmas</s> that nourish and obstruct them. Therefore he says: 'By walking meditation and sitting, he purifies the mind from obstructive <s>dharmas</s>.'

body.text: sā khalv eṣā dharmādhipateyāvaraṇīyebhyo dharmebhyaś cittasya pariśodhanākhyāta //
body.translated_text: This is the purification of the mind from obstructive <s>dharmas</s>, explained as having the <s>Dharma</s> as its authority. //

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-7-a-(2)-i-(d)-(2) Ms.52a4R, Sh.104-11, P.49a1, D.41a6, N.43b2, Co.45a1, Ch.412c13
asti punar ātmādhipateyā lokādhipateyā cāvaraṇīyebhyo dharmebhyaś cittapariśodhanā /
body.translated_text: There is also the purification of the mind from obstructive <s>dharmas</s> having oneself as authority and having the world as authority.

body.text: ātmādhipateyā katamā / yathāpi tadutpanne 'nyatamānyatamasmin nivaraṇe, ātmata evāpratirūpatāṃ viditvā, utpannaṃ nivaraṇaṃ nādhivāsayate prajahāti vinodayati vyantīkaroti, tena nivaraṇenātmānaṃ lajjāyamānaḥ, cetasa (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 160

children.text: ) upakleśakareṇa prajñādaurbalyakareṇa vighātapakṣyeṇa / evam asāv ātmānam evādhipatiṃ kṛtvā, āvaraṇīyebhyo dharmebhyaś cittaṃ pariśodhayati /
children.translated_text: ) a cause of weakness of wisdom, and belonging to the side of obstruction. Thus, having made oneself the authority, one purifies the mind from obstructive <s>dharmas</s>.

body.translated_text: What is the purification having oneself as authority? When any one of the hindrances has arisen, having recognized for oneself its unsuitability, one does not tolerate the arisen hindrance but abandons it, removes it, and eliminates it, being ashamed before oneself on account of that hindrance, [recognizing it] as a cause of mental defilement,

body.text: kathaṃ lokam adhipatiṃ kṛtvā āvaraṇīyebhyo dharmebhyaś cittaiḥ pariśodhayati / ihāsya nivaraṇe samutpanna utpattikāle vā pratyupasthita evaṃ bhavati, "ahaṃ ced anutpannaṃ nivaraṇam utpādayeyaṃ, śāstā me 'pavaded devatā api vijñā api sabrahmacāriṇo dharmatayā vigarheyur" iti / sa lokam evādhipatiṃ kṛtvā, anutpannaṃ ca nivaraṇaṃ notpādayati, utpannaṃ ca prajahāti / evaṃ lokam adhipatiṃ kṛtvā, āvaraṇīyebhyo dharmebhyaś cittaṃ pariśodhayati //
body.translated_text: How does one purify the mind from obstructive <s>dharmas</s> having made the world the authority? Here, when a hindrance has arisen or is about to arise at the time of its arising, he thinks thus: 'If I were to generate an unarisen hindrance, the Teacher would reprove me, wise deities also, and fellow practitioners of the holy life would rightly censure me.' Having thus made the world the authority, he does not generate the unarisen hindrance and abandons the arisen one. Thus, having made the world the authority, he purifies the mind from obstructive <s>dharmas</s>. //

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-7-a-(2)-ii-(a) Ms.52a8M, Sh.105-12, P.49a8, D.41b4, N.43b8, Co.45a6, Ch.412c27
śayanāsanapratiguptyarthaṃ punar "lokācāraś cānuvṛtto bhaviṣyatī"ti / yāvad rātryāḥ prathame yāme caṅkramaniṣadyābhyām āvaraṇīyebhyo dharmebhyaś cittaṃ pariśodhayati / āvaraṇīyebhyo dharmebhyaś cittaṃ pariśodhya, bahir vihārasya pādau prakṣālayati / prakṣālya, vihāraṃ praviśya śayyāṃ kalpayati / yāvad eva svapnaupacayikānāṃ mahābhūtānām upacayāya / upacito 'yaṃ kāyaḥ karmaṇyataraś ca bhaviṣyati, anukūlataraś ca sātatyena nipake kuśalapakṣaprayoge //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, regarding the purpose of protecting his lodging: 'Worldly convention too shall be followed.' During the first watch of the night, by walking meditation and sitting, he purifies the mind from obstructive <s>dharmas</s>. Having purified the mind from obstructive <s>dharmas</s>, he goes outside the dwelling and washes his feet. Having washed them, he enters the dwelling and prepares his bed — just for the replenishment of the great elements that are accumulated during sleep. This body, thus replenished, will become more fit for action and more suitable for constant, vigilant endeavor in the wholesome side. //

body.text: (I)-C-IIl-7-a-(2)-ii-(b) Ms.52b1R, Sh.105-24, W.*72-30, P.49b4, D.41b7, N.44a3, Co.45b2, Ch.413a3 kena kāraṇena daksiṇena pārśvena śayyāṃ kalpayati / siṃhasya prāṇinaḥ sādharmyeṇa / kiṃ punar atra sādharmyam / siṃhaḥ prāṇī sarveṣāṃ tiryagyonigatānāṃ prāṇināṃ vikrānta utsāhī dṛḍhaparākramaḥ / bhikṣur api jāgarikāyogānuyukta ārabdhavīryo viharati vikrānta utsāhī dṛḍhaparākramaḥ / atas tasya siṃhopamaiva śayyā pratirūpā bhavati, no tu pretaśayyā devaśayyā, na kāmabhogiśayyā / tathā hi te sarva eva kusīdā hīnavīryā mandabalaparākramāḥ / (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 162

children.text: ) api tu dharmataiṣā yad dakṣiṇena pārśvena siṃhopamāṃ śayyāṃ kalpayato na tathā gātrāṇāṃ vikṣepo bhavati, na ca śayānasya smṛtisaṃpramoṣo bhavati, na ca gāḍhaṃ svapiti, pāpakāṃś ca svapnān na paśyati / anyathā tu śayyāṃ kalpayato viparyayeṇa sarve doṣā veditavyāḥ / tenāha / pāde pādam ādhāya dakṣiṇena pārśvena śayyāṃ kalpayati //
children.translated_text: ) Moreover, it is a natural law that when one prepares the lion's posture lying on the right side, there is not such scattering of the limbs, nor does one who is lying down lose mindfulness, nor does one sleep deeply, and one does not see evil dreams. But if one prepares one's bed otherwise, all the opposite faults should be understood. Therefore he says: 'Placing foot upon foot, he prepares his bed on the right side.' //

body.translated_text: For what reason does he prepare his bed on the right side? By analogy with the lion, the living being. And what is the analogy here? The lion, the living being, is the most valiant, energetic, and of firm prowess among all beings born in the animal realm. Likewise, a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) engaged in the practice of wakefulness dwells with aroused vigor, valiant, energetic, and of firm prowess. Therefore the lion's posture is fitting for him, but not the posture of a ghost, nor of a god, nor of a sensualist. For all those are lazy, of inferior vigor, and of weak prowess.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-7-a-(2)-ii-(c) Ms.52b4L, Sh.106-16, P.50a2, D.42a4, N.44b1, Co,45b7, Ch.413a13
katham ālokasaṃjñi śayyāṃ kalpayati / ālokanimittam anena sūdgṛhītaṃ bhavati sumanasikṛtaṃ sujuṣṭaṃ supratividdham / tad eva manasikurvan sa prabhāsahagatena cittena śayyāṃ kalpayati / suptasyāpi cāsya yena na bhavati cetaso 'ndhakārāyitatvam / evam ālokasaṃjñī śayyāṃ kalpayati //
body.translated_text: How does one prepare one's bed with the perception of light (<s>ālokasaṃjñī</s>)? The sign of light has been well-grasped, well-attended to, well-practiced, and well-penetrated by him. Attending to that very [sign], he prepares his bed with a mind accompanied by radiance. Even when asleep, there is no darkness of mind for him. Thus one prepares one's bed with the perception of light. //

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-7-a-(2)-ii-(d) Ms.52b5L, Sli. 106-21, P.5Oa4, D.42a6, N.44b2, Co.46a2, Ch.413a17
kathaṃ smṛtaḥ śayyāṃ kalpayati / ye 'nena dharmāḥ śrutā bhavanti cintitā vā bhāvitā vā kuśalā arthopasaṃhitāḥ, tadanvayāsya smṛtir yāvat svapanakāle 'nuvartinī bhavati / yayāsya suptasyāpi ta eva dharmā jāgrato tvābhilapanti, teṣv eva ca dharmeṣu taccittaṃ bahulam anuvicarati / iti yathāsmṛtyā yathāsmṛtaḥ kuśalacittaḥ śayyāṃ kalpayati, avyākṛtacitto vā / evaṃ smṛtaḥ śayyāṃ kalpayati //
body.translated_text: How does one prepare one's bed mindfully (<s>smṛta</s>)? Whatever <s>dharmas</s> have been heard, reflected upon, or cultivated by him — wholesome ones connected with meaning — the mindfulness following upon those continues in him up to the time of falling asleep. By that [mindfulness], even when asleep, those very <s>dharmas</s> that one has while awake speak to him, and in those very <s>dharmas</s> the mind mostly ranges. Thus, with whatever mindfulness and in whatever way mindful, with a wholesome mind, he prepares his bed — or with an indeterminate mind. Thus one prepares one's bed mindfully. //

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-7-a-(2)-ii-(e) Ms.52b6L, Sh.107-7, P.50a7, D.42b1, N,44b4, Co.46a4, Ch.413a23
kathaṃ saṃprajānan śayyāṃ kalpayati / suptasyāsya tathā smṛtasya yasmin samaye 'nyatamānyatamenopakleśena cetasaḥ saṃkleśo bhavati / sa (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 164

children.text: ) utpadyamānam eva taṃ saṃkleśaṃ samyag eva prajānāti, nādhivāsayati, prajahāti, pratividhyati, pratyudāvartayati mānasam / tenocyate saṃprajānan śayyāṃ kalpayati //
children.translated_text: ) as soon as that defilement arises, correctly understands it, does not tolerate it, abandons it, counteracts it, and turns back the mind. Therefore it is said: 'He prepares his bed with clear comprehension.' //

body.translated_text: How does one prepare one's bed with clear comprehension (<s>saṃprajānan</s>)? When, for one thus mindful while asleep, at whatever time there is mental defilement through any one of the afflictions, he,

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-7-a-(2)-ii-(f) Ms.52b7L, Sh.107-14, P.50b1, D.42b2, N.44b6, Co.46a6, Ch,413a27
kathaṃ utthānasaṃjñām eva manasikurvan śayyāṃ kalpayati / sa vīryasaṃpragṛhītaṃ cittaṃ kṛtvā śayyāṃ kalpayati / supratibuddhikayā suhrasvamiddhaḥ / tadyathāraṇyako mṛgaḥ, no tu sarveṇa sarvaṃ middhāvakramaṇanimnaṃ cittaṃ karoti, na tatpravaṇaṃ, na tatprāgbhāram /
body.translated_text: How does one prepare one's bed attending to the perception of arising (<s>utthānasaṃjñā</s>)? He prepares his bed with a mind that has been seized by vigor, easily awakened, sleeping lightly — like a deer in the forest — and does not in every way make the mind inclined toward sloth-and-torpor, nor disposed toward it, nor leaning toward it.

body.text: api cāsyaivaṃ bhavati / "aho batāhaṃ buddhānujñātāṃ jāgarikāṃ sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā saṃpādayeyam" iti / tasyāś ca saṃpādanārthaṃ bhrśaṃ ghanarasena prayogeṇa chandagato viharaty abhiyuktaś ca /
body.translated_text: Moreover, he thinks thus: 'Oh, may I in every way and completely fulfill the wakefulness approved by the <s>Buddhas</s>!' And for the purpose of fulfilling that, he dwells with intense and dense effort, with the desire [to fulfill it], and is diligent.

body.text: api cāsyaivaṃ bhavati / "yathāham adya jāgarikārtham ārabdhavīryo vyahārṣaṃ, kuśalānāṃ ca dharmāṇāṃ bhāvanāyai dakṣo 'nalasa utthānasaṃpannaḥ / śvaḥ prabhāte, nirgatāyāṃ ca rajanyāṃ, bhūyasyā mātrayārabdhavīryo vihariṣyāmy utthānasaṃpanna" iti /
body.translated_text: Moreover, he thinks thus: 'Just as today I have aroused vigor for the purpose of wakefulness and have been skillful, not lazy, endowed with effort in the cultivation of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> — so tomorrow morning, when the night has passed, I shall dwell with even greater measure of aroused vigor, endowed with effort.'

body.text: tatraikayotthānasaṃjñayā na gāḍhaṃ svapiti / yenāyaṃ śaknoti laghu laghv evotthānakāla utthātuṃ, na kālātikrāntaṃ pratibudhyati / dvitīyayotthānasaṃjñayā buddhānujñātāṃ siṃhaśayyāṃ kalpayaty anyūnām anadhikām / tṛtīyayotthānasaṃjñayā cchandaṃ na sraṃsayati / smṛtisaṃpramoṣe saty uttaratrottaratra samādānāya prayukto bhavati / evam utthānasaṃjñām eva manasikurvan śayyāṃ kalpayati //
body.translated_text: Therein, by the first perception of arising, one does not sleep deeply, by which one is able to rise very quickly at the time of arising and does not awaken past the proper time. By the second perception of arising, one prepares the lion's posture approved by the <s>Buddhas</s>, neither too little nor too much. By the third perception of arising, one does not let go of one's zeal; when there is loss of mindfulness, one is engaged in undertaking [the practice] again and again in ever higher [degrees]. Thus one prepares one's bed attending to the perception of arising. //

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-7-a-(2)-iii Ms.53a2M, Sh.108-12, W.*72-4, P.50b8, D.43a1, N.45a5, Co.46b5, Ch.413b14
sa rātryāḥ paścime yāme laghu laghv eva prativibudhya caṅkramaniṣadyābhyām āvaraṇīyebhyo dharmebhyaś cittaṃ pariśodhayatīti / rātryāḥ paścimo yāma ucyate, yo 'pararātraḥ sātirekaṃ praharam / sa cāyam ālokasaṃjñī smṛtaḥ saṃprajānann utthānasaṃjñām eva manasikurvan rātyāḥ madhyamaṃ yāmaṃ sātirekaṃ praharaṃ middham avakrāmayitvā, yasmim samaye vyuttiṣṭhate tatra tasmim samaye vyuttiṣṭhate karmaṇyakāyo bhavati, utthāya nādhimātreṇa styānamiddhaparyavasthānenābhibhūtaḥ / yena nāsyottiṣṭhato dhandhāyitatvaṃ vā syād mandāyitatvaṃ vālasyakausīdyaṃ vā / asati vā punas tasmin dhandhāyitatve mandāyitatva ālasyakausīdye laghu laghv evotthānaṃ bhavaty ābhogamātrāt / caṅkramaniṣadyābhyāṃ āvaraṇīyebhyo dharmebhyaś cittasya pariśuddhiḥ pūrvavad veditavyā / ayaṃ tāvat pūrvarātrāpararātraṃ jāgarikāyogasyānuyuktatāvistaravibhāgaḥ //
body.translated_text: He, in the last watch of the night, having very quickly awakened, purifies the mind from obstructive <s>dharmas</s> by walking meditation and sitting. The last watch of the night is said to be the latter part of the night, slightly more than one <s>prahara</s> (watch period). And this one, with the perception of light, mindful, with clear comprehension, attending to the perception of arising, having allowed sloth to set in during the middle watch of the night for slightly more than one <s>prahara</s> — at whatever time he arises, at that very time upon arising, his body becomes fit for action. Having arisen, he is not overcome by excessive sloth-and-torpor. By which there would be no sluggishness, no dullness, no laziness or indolence for him upon arising. Or, in the absence of that sluggishness, dullness, laziness, and indolence, the arising occurs very quickly, merely by intention. The purification of the mind from obstructive <s>dharmas</s> by walking meditation and sitting should be understood as before. This, then, is the detailed analysis of the engagement in the practice of wakefulness in the first and last watches of the night. //

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-7-b-(1) Ms.53a4R, Sh.109-6, P.51a6, D.43a6, N.45b2, Co.47a2, Ch.413b24
samāsārthāḥ punaḥ katame / iha jāgarikāyogam anuyuktasya puruṣapudgalasya catvāri samyakkaraṇīyāni bhavanti / katamāni catvāri / yāvaj jāgrati tāvat kuśalapakṣaṃ na riñcati, sātatyena nipake kuśaladharmabhāvanāyām / kālena ca śayyāṃ kalpayati, nākālena / suptaś cāsaṃkliṣṭacitto (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 168

children.text: ) middham avakrāmayati, na saṃkliṣṭacittaḥ / kālena ca prativibudhyate, notthānakālam ativartate / [nam gyi cha stod daṅ / nam gyi cha smad la mi ñal bar sbyor ba'i rjes su brtson pa'i skyes bu gaṅ zag gis yaṅ dag par bya ba ni bźi po de dag yin no /] itīmāni catvāri samyakkaraṇīyāny ārabhya bhagavatā śrāvakāṇāṃ jāgarikāyogānuyuktatā deśitā //
children.translated_text: ) one allows sloth to set in, not with a defiled mind. And one awakens at the proper time and does not exceed the time for arising. [These four are what should be properly done by a person engaged in the practice of wakefulness during the first and last watches of the night.] These are the four things to be properly done, in reference to which the <s>Bhagavān</s> has taught the engagement in the practice of wakefulness for <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples). //

body.translated_text: What are the summary meanings? Here, for a person engaged in the practice of wakefulness, there are four things to be properly done. What four? As long as one is awake, one does not abandon the wholesome side, [being engaged] constantly and vigilantly in the cultivation of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. And one prepares one's bed at the proper time, not at an improper time. And while asleep, with an undefiled mind,

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-7-b-(2) Ms.53a6M, Sh.109-16,W.*73-13, P.51b3, D.43b2, N.45b6, Co.47a6, Ch.413c4
kathaṃ ca punar deśitaḥ / yat tāvad āha / "divā caṅkramaniṣadyābhyām āvaraṇīyebhyo dharmebhyaś cittaṃ pariśodhayati / evaṃ rātryāḥ prathamayāmaṃ caṅkramaniṣadyābhyām āvaraṇiyebhyo dharmebhyaś cittaṃ pariśodhayatī"ty anena tāvat prathamaṃ samyakkaraṇīyam ākhyātam / yaduta yāvaj jāgrati tāvat kuśalapakṣaṃ na riñcati / udyukto sātatyena nipake kuśaladharmabhāvanāyām /
body.translated_text: And how has it been taught? First, the statement: 'During the day, by walking meditation and sitting, he purifies the mind from obstructive <s>dharmas</s>. Likewise, during the first watch of the night, by walking meditation and sitting, he purifies the mind from obstructive <s>dharmas</s>' — by this, the first thing to be properly done has been explained: namely, that as long as one is awake, one does not abandon the wholesome side, being diligent, constantly and vigilantly in the cultivation of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: yasmāt punar āha / "bahir vihārasya pādau prakṣālya, vihāraṃ praviśya dakṣiṇena pārśvena śayyāṃ kalpayati / pāde pādam ādhāye"ty anena dvitīyam samyakkaraṇīyam ākhyātam / yaduta kālena śayyāṃ kalpayati, nākālena /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the statement: 'Having washed his feet outside the dwelling, he enters the dwelling and prepares his bed on the right side, placing foot upon foot' — by this, the second thing to be properly done has been explained: namely, that one prepares one's bed at the proper time, not at an improper time.

body.text: yat punar āha / "ālokasaṃjñī smṛtaḥ saṃprajānann utthānasaṃjñām eva manasikurvan śayyāṃ kalpayatī"ty anena tṛtīyaṃ samyakkaraṇīyam ākhyātam / yadutāsaṃkliṣṭacitto middham avakrāmayati, na saṃkliṣṭacitta iti/
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the statement: 'With the perception of light, mindful, with clear comprehension, attending to the perception of arising, he prepares his bed' — by this, the third thing to be properly done has been explained: namely, that one allows sloth to set in with an undefiled mind, not with a defiled mind.

body.text: yat punar āha / "rātryāḥ paścime yāme laghu laghv eva prativibudhya, caṅkramaniṣadyābhyām āvaraṇīyebhyo dharmebhyaś cittaṃ pariśodhayatī"ty (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 170

children.text:
) anena caturthaṃ samyakkaraṇīyam ākhyātam / yaduta kālena prativibudhyati, notthānakālam ativartate /
iti tatra yad uktam / "ālokasaṃjñī smṛtaḥ saṃprajānan vyutthānasaṃjñām eva manasikurvan śayyāṃ kalpayatī"ty / ato dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyām asaṃkliṣṭacitto middham avakrāmayati, yaduta smṛtyā, saṃprajanyena / dvābhyāṃ punaḥ kāraṇābhyāṃ, kālena prativibudhyate, no tu kālam ativartate, yadutālokasaṃjñayotthānasaṃjñayā ca /
children.translated_text: By this the fourth proper action has been explained — namely, one awakens in due time, one does not let the time for rising pass. Thus therein, the statement: "With the perception of light, mindful and clearly comprehending, cultivating the perception of arising, one arranges one's bed" — by two causes one falls asleep with an undefiled mind, namely: by mindfulness and by clear comprehension. By two further causes one awakens in due time and does not let the time pass, namely: by the perception of light and by the perception of arising.

body.translated_text: Furthermore, the statement: 'In the last watch of the night, having very quickly awakened, by walking meditation and sitting, he purifies the mind from obstructive <s>dharmas</s>' — by this,

body.text: kathaṃ punaḥ / smṛtyā kuśalam ālambanaṃ parigṛhya svapiti / saṃprajanyena tasmāt kuśalād ālambanāc cyavamānaṃ saṃkliśyamānaṃ ca cittaṃ laghu laghv eva samyak prajānāti / evam asyābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyām asaṃkliṣṭacittasya śayyā bhavati /
body.translated_text: And how? By mindfulness, one falls asleep having grasped a wholesome object. By clear comprehension, one quickly and rightly discerns a mind that is slipping from that wholesome object and becoming defiled. Thus by these two causes one's sleep is with an undefiled mind.

body.text: tatrālokasaṃjñayotthānasaṃjñayā ca na gāḍhaṃ svapiti, nāsya dūrānugatam tanmiddhaparyavasthānaṃ bhavati / ity ābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāṃ kālena prativibudhyate, notthānakālam ativartate /
body.translated_text: Therein, by the perception of light and by the perception of arising, one does not sleep deeply, and the overwhelming of sleep does not go far. Thus by these two causes one awakens in due time and does not let the time for rising pass.

body.text: ayaṃ jāgarikāyogānuyuktasya samāsārthaḥ / yaś ca pūrvako vistaravibhāgaḥ, yaś cāyaṃ samāsārthaḥ, iyam ucyate pūrvarātrāpararātraṃ jāgarikāyogānuyuktatā// //
body.translated_text: This is the summary meaning for one devoted to the practice of wakefulness. Both the earlier detailed analysis and this summary meaning — this is called the practice of being devoted to wakefulness in the first and last watches of the night.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-8-a-(1) Ms.53b4L, Sh.111-11, P-52b3, D.44a7, N.46b3, Co.48a4, Ch.413c29
saṃprajānadvihāritā katamā / yathāpīhaikatyo 'bhikramapratikrame saṃprajānadvihārī bhavati / ālokitavyavalokite saṃmiñjitaprasārite saṃghāṭīcīvarapātradhāraṇe / aśite pīte khādite svādite, gate sthite niṣaṇṇe śayite, jāgṛte, bhāṣite tūṣṇīṃbhāve, nidrāklamaprativinodane saṃprajānadvihāri bhavati //
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-8-a-(1) — What is clear comprehension in conduct? Just as here someone conducts himself with clear comprehension in going forward and returning; in looking and gazing around; in bending and extending [the limbs]; in wearing the outer robe, inner robe, and bowl; in eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting; in going, standing, sitting, and lying down; in being awake; in speaking and remaining silent; in dispelling drowsiness and fatigue — one conducts oneself with clear comprehension.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-8-a-(2)-i Ms.53b5L, Sh.112-1, P.52b5, D.44b1, N.46b5, Co.48a6, Ch.414a7
tatra katamo 'bhikramaḥ / pratikramaḥ katamaḥ / abhikramapratikrame saṃprajānadvihāratā katamā /
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-8-a-(2)-i — Therein, what is going forward? What is returning? What is clear comprehension in conduct regarding going forward and returning?

body.text: tatrābhikramaḥ / yathāpīhaikatyo grāmaṃ vopasaṃkrāmati, grāmāntaraṃ vā kulaṃ vā kulāntaraṃ vā vihāraṃ vā vihārāntaraṃ vā /
body.translated_text: Therein, going forward is: just as here someone approaches a village, or another village, or a family, or another family, or a monastery, or another monastery.

body.text: tatra pratikramaḥ / yathāpīhaikatyo grāmad vā pratinivartate, grāmāntarād vā kulād vā kulāntarād vā vihārād vā vihārāntarād vā /
body.translated_text: Therein, returning is: just as here someone turns back from a village, or from another village, or from a family, or from another family, or from a monastery, or from another monastery.

body.text: tatra saṃprajānadvihāritā / abhikramamāṇo "'bhikramāmī"ti samyag eva prajānāti / pratikramamāṇaḥ "pratikramāmī"ti samyag eva prajānāti / "atra mayābhikramitavyaṃ, atra mayā punar nābhikramitavyam" iti samyag eva prajānāti / "ayaṃ vā me 'bhikramaṇakālaḥ, ayaṃ nābhikramaṇakāla" iti samyag eva prajānāti / idam asyocyate saṃprajanyam /
body.translated_text: Therein, clear comprehension in conduct is: when going forward, one rightly knows: "I am going forward." When returning, one rightly knows: "I am returning." One rightly knows: "Here I should go forward, here I should not go forward." One rightly knows: "This is the time for my going forward, this is not the time for going forward." This is called one's clear comprehension.

body.text: sacet tena saṃprajanyena samanvāgataḥ / abhikramamāṇaḥ prajānāty "abhikramāmī"ti / yatra cānenābhikramitavyaṃ bhavati tatra cābhikramati / kālena cābhikramati nākālena / yathā cābhikramitavyaṃ bhavati tadrūpayā (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 174

children.text: ) caryayācāreṇākalpeneryāpathena tathābhikrāmati / iyam asyocyate saṃprajānadvihāritā, yadutābhikramapratikramayoḥ //
children.translated_text: conduct, manner, propriety, and deportment, so one goes forward. This is called one's clear comprehension in conduct — namely, in going forward and returning.

body.translated_text: If one is endowed with that clear comprehension — when going forward, one knows: "I am going forward"; and where one should go forward, there one goes forward; and one goes forward at the proper time, not at an improper time; and as one should go forward, with the proper

body.text:
(|)-C-|||-8-a-(2)-ii Ms.53b8M, Sh.113-7, P.53a4, D.44b7, N.47a3, Co.48b5, Ch.414a23
tatra katamad ālokitam / katamad vyavalokitam / katamālokitavyavalokitesaṃprajānadvihāritā /
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-8-a-(2)-ii — Therein, what is looking? What is gazing around? What is clear comprehension in conduct regarding looking and gazing around?

body.text: tasyāsya pūrvaparikīrtiteṣu vastuṣv abhikramataḥ pratikramataś ca / yad abuddhipūrvakam aprayatnapūrvakam acchandapūrvakam antarāle cakṣuṣā rūpadarśanam / idam ucyata ālokitam /
body.translated_text: For one going forward and returning in the previously enumerated situations, whatever seeing of forms with the eye that occurs casually, without deliberation, without effort, without intention — this is called looking.

body.text: yat punar teṣūpasaṃkrāntapratikrāntasya buddhipūrvakaṃ prayatnapūrvakaṃ chandapūrvakaṃ cakṣuṣā rūpadarśanam / tadyathā rājñāṃ rājamātrāṇāṃ naigamānāṃ jānapadānāṃ vā brāhmaṇānāṃ gṛhapatināṃ dhanināṃ śreṣṭhinām sārthavāhānām, tadanyeṣāṃ bāhyakānāṃ layanānāṃ mārutānām avarakāṇāṃ prāsādānāṃ harmyatalānām iti / yad vā punar anyeṣāṃ lokacitrāṇāṃ darśanam / idam ucyate vyavalokitam /
body.translated_text: But whatever seeing of forms with the eye that occurs while approaching and departing, with deliberation, with effort, with intention — such as [seeing] kings, royal ministers, townspeople, country-folk, or <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, householders, the wealthy, guild-leaders, caravan-leaders, or the dwellings of other outsiders, wind-shelters, walled enclosures, palaces, and terraces — or again, whatever seeing of other worldly spectacles — this is called gazing around.

body.text: yat punar ālokitaṃ ca vyavalokitaṃ ca svalakṣaṇataḥ samyag eva prajānāti / yac cāvalokayitavyaṃ yac ca vyavalokayitavyaṃ tad api samyag eva prajānāti / yadālokayitavyaṃ yadā vyavalokayitavyaṃ tad api samyag eva prajānāti / yathālokayitavyaṃ yathā vyavalokayitavyaṃ tad api samyag eva (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 176
knows. This is called one's clear comprehension.

body.translated_text: Furthermore, whatever one rightly knows — both looking and gazing around — according to their own characteristics, and what should be looked at and what should be gazed upon — that too one rightly knows; and when one should look and when one should gaze around — that too one rightly knows; and how one should look and how one should gaze around — that too one rightly

body.text: sa tena saṃprajanyena samanvāgataḥ / saced ālokayamāno vyavalokayamāno jānāty "ālokayāmi vyavalokayāmī"ti / yac cālokayitavyaṃ vyavalokayitavyaṃ tad ālokayati vyavalokayati / yadālokayitavyaṃ vyavalokayitavyaṃ tadālokayati vyavalokayati / yathālokayitavyaṃ vyavalokayitavyaṃ tathālokayati vyavalokayati / iyam asyocyate saṃprajānadvihāritā yadutālokitavyavalokite //
body.translated_text: One endowed with that clear comprehension — if, when looking and gazing around, one knows: "I am looking, I am gazing around"; and what should be looked at and gazed upon, that one looks at and gazes upon; and when it should be looked at and gazed upon, then one looks and gazes; and as it should be looked at and gazed upon, so one looks and gazes — this is called one's clear comprehension in conduct, namely, in looking and gazing around.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-8-a-(2)-iii Ms.54a4M, Sh.114-11, P.53b6, DA5a7, N.47b4, Co.49a6, Ch.414b11
tatra katamat saṃmiñjitam, katamat prasāritaṃ, katamā saṃmiñjitaprasārite saṃprajānadvihāritā / sa tathālokayamāno vyavalokayamānaś ca, abhikramapūrvakaṃ pratikramapūrvakaṃ ca, yat pādau vā saṃmiñjayati prasārayati, bāhū vā saṃmjayati prasārayati, hastau vā saṃmiñjayati prasārayati, anyatamānyatamaṃ vāṅgapratyaṅgaṃ saṃmiñjayati prasārayati / idam ucyate saṃmiñjitaprasāritam /
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-8-a-(2)-iii — Therein, what is bending? What is extending? What is clear comprehension in conduct regarding bending and extending? When one thus looks and gazes around, and in the course of going forward and returning, one bends or extends the feet, bends or extends the arms, bends or extends the hands, or bends or extends any limb or part of the body — this is called bending and extending.

body.text:
sa cet saṃmiñjitaprasāritaṃ svalakṣaṇataḥ samyag eva prajānāti / saṃmiñjayitavyaṃ prasārayitavyaṃ ca samyag eva prajānāti / yadā ca saṃmiñjayitavyaṃ yadā prasārayitavyaṃ tad api samyag eva prajānāti / yathā ca saṃmiñjayitavyaṃ yathā prasārayitavyaṃ tad api samyag eva prajānāti / idam asyocyate saṃprajanyam /
sa tena saṃprajanyena samanvāgataḥ / sa cet saṃmiñjayamānaḥ prasārayamāno jānāti, "saṃmiñjayāmi prasārayāmī"ti / yac ca saṃmiñjayitavyaṃ prasārayitavyaṃ saṃmiñjayati prasārayati / yadā ca saṃmiñjayitavyaṃ prasārayitavyaṃ tadā saṃmiñjayati prasārayati / yathā (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 178

children.text: ) ca saṃmiñjayitavyaṃ prasārayitavyaṃ tathā saṃmiñjayati prasārayati / iyam asyocyate saṃprajānadvihāritā yaduta saṃmiñjitaprasārite //
children.translated_text: it should be bent and extended, so one bends and extends — this is called one's clear comprehension in conduct, namely, in bending and extending.

body.translated_text: If one rightly knows bending and extending according to their own characteristics; and rightly knows what should be bent and what should be extended; and when it should be bent and when extended — that too one rightly knows; and how it should be bent and how extended — that too one rightly knows — this is called one's clear comprehension. One endowed with that clear comprehension — if, when bending and extending, one knows: "I am bending, I am extending"; and what should be bent and extended, one bends and extends; and when it should be bent and extended, then one bends and extends; and as

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-8-a-(2)-iv Ms.54a7M, Sli.115-11, P.54a7, D.45b6, N.48a3, Co.49b5, Ch.414b22
tatra katamat saṃghāṭīdhāraṇaṃ, katamac cīvaradhāraṇaṃ, katamat pātradhāraṇaṃ, katamā saṃghāṭīcīvarapātradhāraṇe saṃprajānadvihāritā /
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-8-a-(2)-iv — Therein, what is wearing the outer robe? What is wearing the inner robe? What is using the bowl? What is clear comprehension in conduct regarding wearing the outer robe, inner robe, and bowl?

body.text: yat tāvad asya jyeṣṭaṃ cīvaraṃ ṣaṣṭikhaṇḍaṃ vā navatikhaṇḍaṃ vā, dviguṇasīvitaṃ vaikaguṇasīvitaṃ vā / iyam ucyate saṃghāṭī / tasya prāvaraṇaṃ paribhogaḥ samyag eva pariharaṇaṃ dhāraṇam ity ucyate /
body.translated_text: First, one's <s>saṃghāṭī</s> (outer robe) is one's largest robe, of sixty or ninety patches, double-sewn or single-sewn — this is called the <s>saṃghāṭī</s>. Its wearing, use, and proper maintenance is called 'wearing.'

body.text: yat punar asya madhyaṃ vā kanīyo vādhiṣṭhānikaṃ vā cīvaram atirekacīvaraṃ vā vikalpanārhaṃ vikalpitaṃ vā / tac cīvaram ity ucyate / tasya prāvaraṇaṃ paribhogaḥ samyag eva pariharaṇaṃ dhāraṇam ity ucyate /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, one's middle or smaller authorized robe, or an extra robe eligible for or having received designation — that is called 'robe' (<s>cīvara</s>). Its wearing, use, and proper maintenance is called 'wearing.'

body.text: yat punar asyādhiṣṭānikam āyasaṃ vā mṛnmayaṃ vā bhaikṣabhājanam / idam ucyate pātram / tasya paribhogaḥ samyag eva pariharaṇaṃ dhāraṇam ity ucyate /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, one's authorized alms-vessel, whether of iron or of clay — this is called the 'bowl' (<s>pātra</s>). Its use and proper maintenance is called 'wearing.'

body.text: sacet punar ayaṃ tāṃ saṃghāṭīṃ cīvaraṃ pātraṃ dhāraṇaṃ vā svalakṣaṇataḥ samyag eva prajānāti / yac ca saṃghāṭīcīvarapātradhāraṇaṃ kalpikam akalpikaṃ vā tad api samyag eva prajānāti / yadā ca saṃghāṭīcīvarapātradhāraṇaṃ dhārayitavyaṃ tad api samyag eva prajānāti / yathā ca dhārayitavyaṃ tad api samyag eva prajānāti / idam asyocyate saṃprajanyam /
body.translated_text: If one rightly knows the wearing of the <s>saṃghāṭī</s>, robe, and bowl according to their own characteristics; and whether the wearing of the <s>saṃghāṭī</s>, robe, and bowl is proper or improper — that too one rightly knows; and when the <s>saṃghāṭī</s>, robe, and bowl should be worn — that too one rightly knows; and how they should be worn — that too one rightly knows — this is called one's clear comprehension.

body.text: sa tena saṃprajanyena samanvāgataḥ sacet saṃghāṭīṃ cīvaraṃ pātraṃ dhārayamāṇo jānāti "dhārayāmī"ti / yac ca dhārayitavyaṃ tad dhārayati / yadā (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 180

children.text: ) ca dhārayitavyaṃ tadā dhārayati / yathā ca dhārayitavyaṃ tathā dhārayati / iyam asyocyate saṃprajānadvihāritā yaduta saṃghāṭīcīvarapātradhāraṇe //
children.translated_text: it should be worn, then one wears; and as it should be worn, so one wears — this is called one's clear comprehension in conduct, namely, in wearing the outer robe, inner robe, and bowl.

body.translated_text: One endowed with that clear comprehension — if, when wearing the <s>saṃghāṭī</s>, robe, and bowl, one knows: "I am wearing [them]"; and what should be worn, one wears; and when

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-8-a-(2)-v Ms.45b4R, Sh.116-19, P.55a1, D,46a6, N.48b3, Co.50a5, Ch.414c11
tatra katamad aśitaṃ, katamat pītaṃ, katamat khāditaṃ, katamat svāditaṃ, katamāśitapītakhāditasvādite saṃprajānadvihāritā /
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-8-a-(2)-v — Therein, what is eating? What is drinking? What is chewing? What is tasting? What is clear comprehension in conduct regarding eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting?

body.text: yaḥ kaścit piṇḍapātaparibhogaḥ sarvaṃ tad aśitam ity ucyate /
body.translated_text: Whatever partaking of alms-food — all of that is called 'eating.'

body.text: tasya punar dvidhābhedaḥ, khāditaṃ svāditaṃ ca / tatra khāditaṃ, manthā vā, apūpo vā, odanakulmāṣaṃ veti, yad vā punar anyatamam ābhisaṃskārikam annaṃ vikṛtaṃ bhojyaṃ prāṇasaṃdhāraṇam / idam ucyate khāditam, aśitam apīdam /
body.translated_text: That has a twofold division — chewing and tasting. Therein, chewing: gruel, or cakes, or rice and grain porridge, or again any prepared, processed food that sustains life — this is called 'chewing,' and this is also 'eating.'

body.text: svāditaṃ katamat / tadyathā kṣīraṃ dadhi navanītam sarpis tailaṃ madhu phāṇitaṃ māṃsaṃ matsyā vaIIūrā lavaṇaṃ vanaphalaṃ vā bhakṣaprakāraṃ vā / idam ucyate svāditam, aśitam apīdam/
body.translated_text: What is tasting? Such as: milk, curd, butter, ghee, oil, honey, molasses, meat, fish, venison, salt, forest fruits, or various types of confections — this is called 'tasting,' and this is also 'eating.'

body.text: yat punaḥ pīyate khaṇḍarasaṃ vā, śarkarārasaṃ vā, kāñcikaṃ vā, dadhimaṇḍaṃ vā, śuktaṃ vā, takraṃ vā, antataḥ pānīyam api / idam ucyate pītam /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, what is drunk — whether a preparation of raw sugar, or of refined sugar, or rice-gruel, or whey of yogurt, or vinegar, or buttermilk, or at the very least even water — this is called 'drinking.'

body.text: aśitapītakhāditasvāditaṃ svalakṣaṇataḥ samyag eva prajānāti / yac cāśitavyaṃ pātavyaṃ khāditavyaṃ svāditavyaṃ tad api samyag eva prajānāti / yadā cāśitavyaṃ pātavyaṃ khāditavyaṃ svāditavyaṃ tad api samyag eva prajānāti / yathā cāśitavyaṃ pātavyaṃ khāditavyaṃ svāditavyaṃ tad api samyag eva prajānāti / idam asyocyate saṃprajanyaṃ /
body.translated_text: One rightly knows eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting according to their own characteristics; and what should be eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted — that too one rightly knows; and when it should be eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted — that too one rightly knows; and how it should be eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted — that too one rightly knows — this is called one's clear comprehension.

body.text: sa tena saṃprajanyena samanvāgato 'śnanaḥ pibamānaḥ khādamānaḥ svādayamānaḥ sa cej jānāty "aśnāmi pibāmi khādāmi svādayāmī"ti / yac (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 182

children.text: ) cāśitavyaṃ pātavyaṃ khāditavyaṃ svāditavyaṃ tad aśnāti yāvat svādayati / yadā cāśitavyaṃ yāvat svādayitavyaṃ tadāśnāti yāvat svādayati / yathā cāśitavyaṃ yāvat svādayitavyaṃ tathāśnāti yāvat svādayati / iyam asyocyate saṃprajānadvihāritā yadutāśitapītakhāditasvādite //
children.translated_text: ) what is to be eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted — one eats and so on up to tastes. When it is to be eaten and so on up to tasted — then one eats and so on up to tastes. And in the manner that it is to be eaten and so on up to tasted — so one eats and so on up to tastes. This is called one's dwelling in clear comprehension, namely, regarding what is eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted.

body.translated_text: One endowed with that clear comprehension — eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting — if one knows: "I am eating, I am drinking, I am chewing, I am tasting"; and what

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-8-a-(2)-vi Ms.55a2M, Sh.118-7,W.*74-1, P.55b6, D.46b7, N.49a5, Co.50b6,Ch.415a5
tatra katamad gatam, katamat sthitam, kataman niṣaṇṇam, katamac chayitaṃ, katamaj jāgrtam, katamad bhāṣitam, katamas tūṣṇīṃbhāvaḥ, katamā nidrāklamaprativinodanā, katamā gate sthite niṣaṇṇe śayite jāgrte bhāṣite tūṣṇīṃbhāve nidrāklamaprativinodanāyāṃ saṃprajānadvihāritā /
body.translated_text: Therein, what is 'going,' what is 'standing,' what is 'sitting,' what is 'lying down,' what is 'being awake,' what is 'speaking,' what is 'silence,' what is 'dispelling drowsiness and fatigue,' and what is dwelling in clear comprehension with regard to going, standing, sitting, lying down, being awake, speaking, silence, and dispelling drowsiness and fatigue?

body.text: yathāpīhaikatyaś caṅkrame vā caṅkramyate, sahadhārmikāṇāṃ vopasaṃkrāmati, adhvānaṃ vā pratipadyate / idam asyocyate gatam /
body.translated_text: Just as here someone walks on the walking path, or approaches co-practitioners in the <s>Dharma</s>, or sets out on a journey. This is called one's 'going.'

body.text: yathāpīhaikatyaś caṅkrame vā tiṣṭhati, sahadhārmikāṇāṃ vā puratas tiṣṭhaty ācāryāṇām upādhyāyānāṃ gurūṇāṃ gurusthānīyānām / idam ucyate sthitam /
body.translated_text: Just as here someone stands on the walking path, or stands before co-practitioners in the <s>Dharma</s>, before teachers, preceptors, elders, and those in the place of elders. This is called 'standing.'

body.text:
yathāpīhaikatyo mañce vā pīṭhe vā tṛṇasaṃstarake vā saṃniviśati vā saṃniṣīdati vā, paryaṅkam ābhujya, ṛjuṃ kāyaṃ praṇidhāya, pratimukhīṃ smṛtim upasthāpya / idam ucyate niṣaṇṇam /
yathāpīhaikatyo bahir vihārasya pādau prakṣālya vihāraṃ praviśya dakṣiṇena pārśvena siṃhaśayyāṃ kalpayati, pāde pādam ādhāya, mañce vā pīṭhe vā tṛṇasaṃstarake vā, araṇye vā vṛkṣamūle vā śunyāgāre vā / idam ucyate śayitam /
body.translated_text: Just as here someone settles or sits down on a bed, a seat, or a straw mat, crossing the legs, setting the body upright, and establishing mindfulness before oneself. This is called 'sitting.' Just as here someone, outside the dwelling washes one's feet, enters the dwelling, and lying on the right side prepares the lion's posture, placing foot upon foot, on a bed, a seat, or a straw mat, in the forest, at the root of a tree, or in an empty house. This is called 'lying down.'

body.text: yathāpīhaikatyo divā caṅkramaṇiṣadyābhyām āvaraṇīyebhyo dharmebhyaś cittaṃ pariśodhayati, evaṃ rātryāḥ prathame yāme paścime yāme / idam ucyate jāgṛtam /
body.translated_text: Just as here someone during the day purifies the mind of obstructive <s>dharmas</s> by walking and sitting, and likewise in the first watch and the last watch of the night. This is called 'being awake.'

body.text: yathāpīhaikatyas tathā jāgarikāyogānuyukto 'nuddiṣṭāṃś ca dharmān (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> I 184

children.text: ) uddiśati paryavāpnoti, tadyathā sūtraṃ geyaṃ vyākaraṇam iti vistareṇa pūrvavat / uddiṣṭeṣu ca dharmeṣu vacasā paricayaṃ karoti, yaduta vistareṇa svādhyāyakriyayā, pareṣāṃ vā vistareṇa saṃprakāśayati, kālena kālam ālapati pratisaṃmodayati vijñaiḥ sabrahmacaribhiḥ sārdhaṃ tadanyair vā gṛhasthair yadutodyojanapariṣkārārtham / idam ucyate bhāṣitam /
children.translated_text: ) masters them — namely: <s>sūtra</s>, <s>geya</s> (songs), <s>vyākaraṇa</s> (explanations) — and so on in detail as before. And regarding the <s>dharmas</s> that have been taught, one familiarizes oneself verbally — namely, by means of extensive recitation — or explains them in detail to others; from time to time one converses and exchanges greetings with wise co-practitioners in the holy life, or with other householders, namely for the purpose of encouragement and preparation. This is called 'speaking.'

body.translated_text: Just as here someone, thus devoted to the practice of wakefulness, teaches <s>dharmas</s> not yet taught and

body.text: yathāpīhaikatyo yathāśrutānāṃ yathā paryavāptānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ vacasā parijitānām ekākī rahogato 'rthaṃ cintayati tulayaty upaparīkṣate / pratisaṃlīno vā punar bhavaty adhyātmam eva cittaṃ sthāpayati / saṃsthāpayaty avasthāpayaty upasthāpayati damayati śamayati vyupaśamayaty ekotīkaroti samādhatte vipaśyanāyāṃ vā yogaṃ koroti / ayam ucyate tūṣṇīṃbhāvaḥ* /
body.translated_text: Just as here someone, alone and secluded, contemplates, weighs, and examines the meaning of the <s>dharmas</s> as heard and mastered, as conquered by speech. Or one is withdrawn, establishing the mind inwardly, fixing it, stabilizing it, applying it, taming it, calming it, thoroughly calming it, unifying it, and concentrating it; or one practices the yoga of <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight meditation). This is called 'silence.'

body.text: yathāpīhaikatyo grīṣmasamaye pratyupasthita uttamagrīṣmaparidāhakāle vartamāne, uṣṇena vā bādhyate śrānto vā bhavati, klāntasyotpadyate 'kāle nidrāklamaḥ svapitukāmaḥ / ayam ucyate nidrāklamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Just as here someone, when the summer season has arrived and the time of the greatest summer heat is present, is oppressed by the heat or is exhausted — for the fatigued one there arises at an improper time drowsiness and fatigue, and one wishes to sleep. This is called 'drowsiness and fatigue.'

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-8-a-(2)-vii Ms.55b3L, Sh.120-8, P.56b7, D.47b4, N.50a2, Co.51b4, Ch.415b7
sacet punar ayaṃ gataṃ yāvan nidrāklamavinodanāṃ tatsvalakṣaṇataḥ samyag eva prajānāti / yatra ca gantavyaṃ yāvan nidrāklamaḥ prativinodayitavyaḥ, tad api samyag eva prajānāti / yadā ca gantavyaṃ yāvad yadā nidrāklamaḥ prativinodayitavyaḥ, tad api samyag eva prajānāti / yathā ca gantavyaṃ bhavati yathā ca yāvan nidrāklamaḥ prativinodayitavyaḥ, tad api samyag eva prajānāti / idam asyocyate saṃprajanyam /
body.translated_text: If then one properly knows going up to the dispelling of drowsiness and fatigue according to their own characteristics; and where one should go up to where drowsiness and fatigue should be dispelled — that too one properly knows; and when one should go up to when drowsiness and fatigue should be dispelled — that too one properly knows; and how one should go and how drowsiness and fatigue should be dispelled — that too one properly knows. This is called one's clear comprehension.

body.text: sa tena saṃprajanyena samanvāgato gacchan yāvan nidrāklamam (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> I 186

children.text: ) prativinodayan sa cej jānti, "gacchāmi yāvan nidrāklamaṃ prativinodayāmī"ti / yatra ca gantavyaṃ bhavati yatra ca yāvan nidrāklamaḥ prativinodhyitavyo bhavati, tatra gacchati tatra yāvan nidrāklamaṃ prativinodayati / yadā ca gantavyaṃ bhavati yadā ca yāvan nidrāklamaḥ prativinodayitavyo bhavati, tadā gacchati tadā yāvan nidrāklamaṃ prativinodayati / yathā ca gantavyaṃ bhavati yathā yāvan nidrāklamaḥ prativinodayitavyo bhavati, tathā gacchati tathā yāvan nidrāklamaṃ prativinodayati / iyam asyocyate saṃprajānadvihāritā yaduta gatasthitaniṣaṇṇaśayitajāgṛtabhāṣitatūṣṇīṃbhāvanidrāklamaprativinodanāyām //
children.translated_text: ) if one knows: "I am going" up to "I am dispelling drowsiness and fatigue"; and where one should go and where drowsiness and fatigue should be dispelled — there one goes, there one dispels drowsiness and fatigue; and when one should go and when drowsiness and fatigue should be dispelled — then one goes, then one dispels drowsiness and fatigue; and in the manner one should go and in the manner drowsiness and fatigue should be dispelled — so one goes, so one dispels drowsiness and fatigue. This is called one's dwelling in clear comprehension, namely, regarding going, standing, sitting, lying down, being awake, speaking, silence, and the dispelling of drowsiness and fatigue.

body.translated_text: One endowed with that clear comprehension, while going up to while dispelling drowsiness and fatigue —

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-8-a-(3)-i Ms.55b5R, Sh.121-3, P.57a6, D.48a2, N.50a7, Co.52a2, Ch.415b20
saṃprajānadvihāritāyāḥ katamānupūrvī, katamā vastuvibhāvanā / yathāpīhaikatyo yaṃ yam eva grāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vopaniśritya viharati /
body.translated_text: What is the sequence of dwelling in clear comprehension, and what is the elucidation of the subject? Just as here someone dwells in dependence on a village or a market town.

body.text: tasyaivaṃ bhavati / "mayā khalv ayaṃ grāmo vā nigamo vā piṇḍāyopasaṃkramitavyaḥ / piṇḍāya caritvā punar eva vihāraṃ pratiniṣkramitavyam / santi punar atra kulāni grāme vā nagare vā yāni mayā nopasaṃkramitavyāni, tāni punaḥ katamāni / tadyathā ghoṣaṃ' pānāgāraṃ veśyaṃ rājakulaṃ caṇḍālakaṭhinam / yāni vā punaḥ kulāny ekāntena pratihatāny apratyudāvartāni /
body.translated_text: One thinks thus: "I must indeed approach that village or market town for alms. Having gone for alms, I must return again to the dwelling. But there are families in the village or town that I should not approach — and which are those? Namely: a cattle-pen, a tavern, a brothel, a royal palace, and an outcaste settlement. And also those families which are entirely opposed and unreceptive.

body.text: santi ca punaḥ kulāni yāni mayopasaṃkramitavyāni / tadyathā kṣatriyamahāsālakulāni vā brāhmaṇamahāsalakulāni vā gṛhapatimahāsālakulāni vā naigamakulāni vā jānapadakulāni vā dhanikulāni vā śreṣṭhikulāni vā sārthavāhakulāni vā /
body.translated_text: But there are families that I should approach — namely: families of great <s>Kṣatriya</s> (warrior) households, or families of great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> (priestly) households, or families of great householder households, or townspeople families, or country families, or wealthy families, or merchant families, or caravan-leader families.

body.text: yāni vā kulāni mayopasaṃkramitavyāni tāni nātisāyam upasaṃkramitavyāni tāni vikālam / na ca kāryavyagreṣu dāyakadānapatiṣu, na krīḍāratimaṇḍanayogam anuyukteṣu, na grāmyadharmāya pravṛtteṣu, na kupiteṣu / tathā copasaṃkramitavyāni yathopasaṃkrāmann ahaṃ na bhrāntena hastinā sārdhaṃ samāgaccheyaṃ na bhrāntena rathena punaś caṇḍenāśvena na caṇḍayā gavā na caṇḍena kukkureṇa / na gahanaṃ na kaṇṭakavāṭaṃ vā mardeyaṃ, na śvabhre palvale prapāte prapateyam / na syandanikāyāṃ na (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> I 190

children.text: ) gūthakaṭhikke / candropamaś ca kulāny upasaṃkrameyaṃ hrīmān apragalbho vyavakṛṣya kāyaṃ vyavakṛṣya cittaṃ na lābhakāmo na satkārakāmaḥ / yathā svena lābhena sucittaḥ sumanās tathā parasyāpi lābhena sucittaḥ sumanā anātmotkarṣy aparapaṃsako 'nukaṃpācitto dayācittaḥ / evaṃ ca punar upasaṃkramitavyāni / tat kuta etal labhyaṃ pravrajitena parakuleṣu yad dadatu me pare mā na dadatu, yāvat tvaritaṃ mā dhandham iti vistareṇa / upasaṃkramya ca me pratigrahe mātrā karaṇīyā / na ca lābhahetoḥ kuhanā karaṇīyā lapanā naimittikatā naiṣpeṣikatā lābhena lābhaniścikīrṣatā karaṇīyā / sa ca lābho 'raktena paribhoktavyaḥ, asaktenāgṛddhenāgrathitenāmūdhitenānadhyavasitenādhyavasāyam anāpannena" //
children.translated_text: ) a refuse heap. And I should approach families like the moon — modest, not bold, with body withdrawn, with mind withdrawn, not desiring gain, not desiring honor. Just as I would be well-minded and well-pleased with my own gain, so too I would be well-minded and well-pleased with another's gain — not praising myself, not disparaging others, with a mind of compassion and a mind of sympathy. And I should approach [families] in this manner. But how could this be obtained by a renunciant in the homes of others — that others should give to me or not give; and so on in detail up to: quickly or slowly. And having approached, I should observe moderation in accepting. And for the sake of gain, I should not resort to hypocrisy, flattery, hinting, browbeating, or seeking gain by means of gain. And that gain should be used without attachment, without clinging, without greed, without entanglement, without infatuation, without resolve, and without having reached a state of resolve."

body.translated_text: And those families that I should approach — I should not approach them too late in the evening or at an improper time; not when the donors and patrons are busy with their affairs; not when they are engaged in the pursuit of play, amusement, and adornment; not when they are engaged in vulgar behavior; not when they are angry. And I should approach in such a way that, while approaching, I would not encounter a mad elephant, or a mad chariot, or a fierce horse, or a fierce cow, or a fierce dog; I should not tread upon a thicket or a thorn-hedge; I should not fall into a pit, a swamp, or a precipice; not into a drain, not into

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-8-a-(3)-ii Ms. 56a6M, Sh.122-20, W.*74,17*;20**, P.58a5, D.48b7, N.51a5, Co.53a1, Ch.415c20
yāni ca rūpāṇi tatropasaṃkramatopasaṃkrāntena vā draṣṭavyāni bhavanti na tāny ekatyāni draṣṭavyāni tāni caikatyāni draṣṭavyāni / tatra yāni na draṣṭavyāni teṣūtkṣiptacakṣuṣā bhavitavyaṃ susaṃvṛtendriyeṇa / yāni punar draṣṭavyāni teṣu sūpasthitāṃ smṛtim upasthāpya / (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> I 192

children.text: ) kathaṃrūpāṇi punā rūpāṇi nāvalokayitavyāni / tadyathā naṭo nartako hāsako lāsaka iti / yad vā punar anyac cāraṇajātaṃ nṛtte vā gīte vā vādite vā pravṛttam / tathā mātṛgrāmo viśeṣeṇa punaḥ śiśur udāravarṇo rañjanīya iti / yāni ca punā rūpāṇi dṛṣṭāni brahmacaryopaghātāya brahmacaryāntarāyāya, pāpakānāṃ cākuśalānāṃ vitarkāṇāṃ samudācārāya saṃvarteran / tadrūpāṇi rūpāṇi nāvalokayitavyāni, na vyavalokayitavyāni /
children.translated_text: ) What kind of visible forms should not be looked at? Namely: an actor, a dancer, a comedian, a performer — or any other traveling entertainers engaged in dance, song, or music. Likewise, women especially — a young woman, one of fair complexion, one who is captivating. And whatever visible forms that, if seen, would be detrimental to the holy life, obstructive to the holy life, and would lead to the arising of evil, unwholesome thoughts — such visible forms should not be looked at, should not be gazed upon.

body.translated_text: Whatever visible forms are to be seen while approaching or having approached — some of those should not be looked at, and some should be looked at. Therein, regarding those that should not be looked at, one should keep one's eyes cast down and one's faculties well restrained. But regarding those that should be looked at, one should establish well-established mindfulness.

body.text: "kathaṃrūpāṇi punā rūpāṇi draṣṭavyāni" / tadyathā jīrṇaṃ vā vṛddhaṃ vā mahaIIakaṃ vā khurukhurupraśvāsakāyaṃ purataḥprāgbhārakāyaṃ daṇḍam avaṣṭabhya pravepamānena kāyena, ābādhikaṃ vā duḥkhitaṃ bāḍhaglānam ādhmātapādam ādhmātahastam ādhmātodaram ādhmātamukhaṃ pāṇḍukachavivarṇam, dardrūlaṃ vā kacchūlaṃ vā kuṣṭhitaṃ vā duḥkhitahatagātram, pakvagātram upahatendriyaṃ, mṛtaṃ vā kālagatam ekāhamṛtaṃ vā dvyahamṛtaṃ vā saptāhamṛtaṃ vā, kākaiḥ kuraraiḥ khādyamānaṃ, gṛdhraih śvabhiḥ sṛgālair vividhair vā tiryagjātigataiḥ prāṇibhir bhakṣyamāṇam abhinirhriyamāṇaṃ vā / mañca āropyopari vitānena prasāritena purataḥ pṛṣṭhataś ca mahājanakāyena rodamānena krandamānena bhasmāvakīrṇapramuktakeśena tathā śokajātaṃ duḥkhajātaṃ paridevajātaṃ daurmanasyajātam upāyāsajātaṃ, yan "mayā draṣṭavyam" ity evaṃrūpāṇi cānyāni caivaṃbhāgīyāni rūpāṇi draṣṭavyāni, yāni brahmacaryānugrahāya kuśalānāṃ ca vitarkāṇāṃ samudācārāya saṃvartante //
body.translated_text: "What kind of visible forms should be looked at?" Namely: one who is aged, old, greatly advanced in years, with a body wheezing and gasping for breath, with a body bent forward, supporting oneself with a staff and trembling in body; or one who is sick, suffering, seriously ill, with swollen feet, swollen hands, swollen abdomen, swollen face, pale, of discolored skin; or one with skin disease, or with scabies, or with leprosy, with afflicted and damaged limbs, with decayed limbs, with impaired faculties; or one who is dead, who has passed away — dead one day, or two days, or seven days — being devoured by crows and hawks, being eaten by vultures, dogs, jackals, and various creatures of the animal realm, or being carried out [for cremation]; or placed upon a bier with a canopy spread above, with a great crowd of people before and behind weeping and wailing, with ashes scattered and hair unbound — thus stricken by grief, stricken by suffering, stricken by lamentation, stricken by dejection, stricken by despair — [thinking:] "This is what I should look at." Such visible forms and other similar ones should be looked at — those which conduce to the support of the holy life and to the arising of wholesome thoughts.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-8-a-(3)-iii Ms.56b5R, Sh.124-6, P.59a1, D.49b2, N.52a1, Co.53b3, Ch.416a10
na kāyapracālakam upasaṃkramitavyaṃ na bāhupracālakaṃ na śīrṣapracālakaṃ noccagghikayā na hastāvalagnikayā na soḍhaukikayā / nānanujñātenāsane niṣattavyaṃ, nāpratyavekṣyāsanam, na sarvakāyam samavadhāya, na pāde pādam ādhāya, na sakthni sakthinā, nābhisaṃkṣipya pādau, nābhivikṣipya pādau //
body.translated_text: One should not approach [families] swinging the body, not swinging the arms, not swinging the head; not with laughter, not with hands hanging loosely, not with a haughty bearing. One should not sit on a seat without being invited, nor without examining the seat, nor settling the whole body [heavily], nor placing foot upon foot, nor thigh upon thigh, nor drawing in the feet, nor spreading the feet apart.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-8-a-(3)-iv Ms.56b6R, Sh.124-12, P.59a4, D.49b4, N.52a3, Co.53b5, Ch.416a15
nodguṇṭhikayā kṛtena, noccastikayā, na vitastikayā, na paryastikayā, parimaṇḍalaṃ cīvaraṃ prāvṛtya, nātyutkṛṣṭaṃ nātyapakṛṣṭam, na hastiśuṇḍakaṃ na tālavṛntakaṃ na nāgaphaṇakaṃ na kulmāṣapiṇḍikaṃ cīvaraṃ prāvaritavyam / nānāgate khādanīye pātram upanāmayitavyaṃ, na ca khādanīyabhojanīyasyopari dhārayitavyam / nānāstīrṇe pṛthivīpradeśe prapāte prāgbhāre pātraṃ sthāpayitavyam //
body.translated_text: One should not wear the robe with a hood, nor excessively raised, nor in a forearm-length manner, nor thrown over [the shoulder]. The robe should be wrapped evenly — neither too high nor too low — not like an elephant's trunk, not like a palm-leaf fan, not like a serpent's hood, not like a ball of porridge. One should not hold out the bowl when the food has not yet arrived, and one should not hold it above the food and drink. One should not place the bowl on uneven ground, or on a slope, or on an overhanging ledge.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-8-a-(3)-v Ms.57a2L, Sh.124-19, P.59a7, D.49b6, N.52a6, Co.53b7, Ch.416a20
sāvadānaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ paribhoktavyam / naudanena sūpikaṃ praticchādayitavyam, na sūpikenaudanam / nātittinikāyogam anuyuktena paribhoktavyam / nātisthūlaṃ nātiparīttaṃ parimaṇḍalam ālopa ālopayitavyam / na hastāvalehakaṃ na pātrāvalehakam, na hastasaṃdhūnakaṃ na pātrasaṃdhūnakam, na kavaḍacchedakam, piṇḍapātaṃ paribhoktavyam //
body.translated_text: One should partake of almsfood attentively. One should not cover the curry with rice, nor the rice with curry. One should not eat intent on an excessive quantity. The morsel should be formed evenly — neither too large nor too small. One should not eat almsfood by licking the hand, or licking the bowl, or shaking the hand, or shaking the bowl, or breaking off pieces of the morsel.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-8-a-(3)-vi Ms.57a3L, Sh.125-6, P.59b2, D.50a1, N.52b1, Co.54a2, Ch.416a25
"vihāragatenāpi me tebhyaḥ kulebhyaḥ pratyāgatena pratiniṣkrāntena divā vā rātrau vā prātipaudgalike caṅkrame caṅkramitavyaṃ, na parakye 'viśvāsye 'pravārite 'nuddiṣṭe / na śrāntakāyena na klāntakāyena, anauddhatyābhinigṛhīte citte, kuśalapakṣaprayukte nākuśalamanasikārānugate (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> I 200

children.text: ) 'ntargatair indriyair abahirgatena mānasena, nātidrutaṃ nāticapalaṃ naikāntena gamanapratyāgamanapratisaṃyuktena, kālena kālaṃ gacchatā kālena kālaṃ tiṣṭhatā /
children.translated_text: with faculties turned inward, with mind not turned outward, not too hastily, not too restlessly, not exclusively occupied with going and coming back, going from time to time and standing from time to time;

body.translated_text: "Having returned to the monastery and come back from those families, whether by day or by night, one should walk on one's own personal walking-path — not on another's, not on an untrusted one, not on an uninvited one, not on an undesignated one. Not with a weary body, not with an exhausted body, with a mind restrained from agitation, applied to the wholesome side, not following unwholesome mental attention,

body.text: tathā sve vihāre sve parigaṇe svakyāṃ kuṭikāyām uddeśikāyāṃ prātipaudgalikāyāṃ, na parakyāyām aviśvāsyāyām apravāritāyām / tathā mañce vā pīṭhe vā tṛṇasaṃstaraṇe vā, araṇye vā vṛkṣamūle vā śūnyāgāre vā niṣattavyaṃ, paryaṅkam ābhujya, ṛjuṃ kāyaṃ praṇidhāya, pratimukhīṃ smṛtim upasthāpya //
body.translated_text: likewise, in one's own monastery, in one's own group, in one's own cell — a designated one, a personal one — not another's, not an untrusted one, not an uninvited one. Likewise, on a bed or a chair or a grass mat, or in the forest, or at the root of a tree, or in an empty dwelling, one should sit down, crossing the legs, keeping the body upright, and establishing mindfulness before one.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-8-a-(3)-vii Ms.57a5M, Sh.125-20, P.59b7, D.50a6, N.52b5, Co.54a6, Ch.416b8
rātryā madhyame yāme svapitavyam / divā pūrvakaṃ ca yāmam kuśalapakṣeṇātināmayitavyam / evaṃ ca punaḥ svapitavyaṃ, ālokasaṃjñinā smṛtena saṃprajānenotthānasaṃjñām eva manasikurvatā, rātryāḥ paścime yāme laghu laghv eva prativibudhya //
body.translated_text: One should sleep during the middle watch of the night. During the daytime and the first watch [of the night], one should spend the time with the wholesome side. And one should sleep thus: with the perception of light, mindful, clearly comprehending, attending to the perception of rising, and during the last watch of the night, one should awaken quickly and promptly.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-8-a-(3)-viii Ms.57a6M, Sh.126-3, P.60a1, D.50a7, N.52b6, Co.54b1, Ch.416b11
bhāṣye vā svādhyāyakriyāyāṃ vā yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ, prahāṇe vā pratisaṃlayane, dharmacintāyām / lokāyatāś ca mantrā vivarjayitavyāḥ, citrākṣarāś citrapadavyañjanā anarthopasaṃhitāḥ, ye nābhijñāyai na saṃbodhāya na nirvāṇāya saṃvartante / ye vā punar dharmās tathāgatabhāṣitā gambhīrā gambhīrābhāsāḥ śūnyatāpratisaṃyuktā idaṃpratyayatāpratītyasamutpādānulomās te satkṛtyodgṛhītavyāḥ dṛḍhaṃ ca sthiraṃ ca sūdgṛhītāś ca na nāśayitavyāḥ, pratipattyāḥ saṃpādanārthaṃ, na lābhasatkārahetoḥ / te ca punar dharmā vacasā suparijitāḥ kartavyāḥ / na ca saṅgaṇikāyā atināmayitavyam na karmārāmatayā na bhāṣyārāmatayā, kālena ca kalam upasthitayā smṛtyā vijñasya sabrahmacāriṇa ālapitavyāḥ saṃlapitavyāḥ pratisaṃmodayitavyāḥ / paripṛcchanajātīyena ca bhavitavyaṃ, kiṃkuśalagaveṣiṇā, anupālambhacittena, mitavādinā, yuktabhāṇinā, [gnam por smra ba daṅ] praśāntabhāṇinā ca, pareṣāṃ dhārmyāṃ kathāṃ kathayitukāmena / tūṣṇīṃbhāvena ca ye pāpakā akuśalā vitarkā na (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> I 204

children.text: ) vitarkayitavyāḥ / na cāyoniśodharmacintāprayuktena / [mṅon pa'i ṅa rgyal can du mi bya ba daṅ / khyad par rtogs pa cuṅ zad tsam daṅ / ṅan ṅon tsam gyi bar ma dor sgyid lug par mi bya ba daṅ / bsaṃ par mi bya ba'i gnas rnams yoṅs su spaṅ bar bya ba daṅ / dus dus su źi gnas daṅ / lhag mthoṅ la brtson par bya ba daṅ / spoṅ ba la dga' ba daṅ / rgyun du chud par bya ba la brtson pa daṅ / gus par bya ba la brtson par bya'o sñam pa daṅ //
children.translated_text: ), nor should one be engaged in unwise reflection on <s>dharmas</s>. [One should not be conceited; one should not, upon gaining even a small special attainment or the slightest disillusionment, become complacent or weary; one should completely abandon the occasions for what should not be contemplated; from time to time one should strive in <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight); one should delight in abandonment; one should strive diligently in continuous training; and one should strive in respectful conduct.]

body.translated_text: One should apply oneself to speech, or to the practice of recitation, or to the practice of abandonment in seclusion, to reflection on the <s>Dharma</s>. <s>Lokāyata</s> (worldly) treatises should be avoided — those with fanciful letters, fanciful words and syllables, connected with what is unprofitable, which do not conduce to higher knowledge, to awakening, or to <s>nirvāṇa</s>. But those <s>dharmas</s> spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s> that are profound, that appear profound, that are connected with emptiness, that are in accordance with conditionality and dependent origination — those should be taken up with respect, firmly and stably grasped, and not lost, for the purpose of accomplishing practice, not for the sake of gain and honor. And those <s>dharmas</s> should be well-mastered verbally. One should not spend time in socializing, nor in delight in work, nor in delight in talk. With mindfulness established from time to time, one should address, converse with, and exchange greetings with wise co-practitioners of the holy life. One should be of the nature of asking questions, seeking what is wholesome, with a mind free from fault-finding, speaking moderately, speaking appropriately, speaking peacefully, and wishing to discourse on <s>Dharma</s> topics to others. In silence, one should not engage in unwholesome thoughts

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-8-a-(3)-ix Ms.-, Sh.-, P.60b2, D.50b7, N.53a7, Co.55a1, Ch.416b29
bdag dpyid ka'i tsha bas gduṅs pa'm / de ltar brtson pa daṅ / 'bad pa daṅ / rtsol ba'm / ruṅ ba'i bya ba cuṅ zad byed pas yoṅs su ṅal ba'i rgyu daṅ / yoṅs su ṅal ba'i gźi las dus ma yin par gñid kyi sñom pa skye bar gyur na / de'i don du ci nas kyaṅ myur ba myur ba kho nar de med par 'gyur źiṅ / dus yun riṅ por dge ba'i phyogs ñams par mi 'gyur ba daṅ / dge ba'i phyogs kyi bar chad du mi 'gyur bar bya ba'i phyir / yud tsam źig gñid bsaṅ bar bya ste / der yaṅ bdag gi sgo bcad pa'm / dge sloṅ yod na ltar gźug pa'm / 'dul ba'i bsruṅ ba daṅ / 'dul ba'i cho gas chos gos kyis bciṅs la / gnas dben par 'dug ste / gñid bsaṅ bar bya'o sñam du sems pa yin te / des na de'i gñid kyi sñom pa rnam pa thams cad kyi thams cad du med par 'gyur ro //
body.translated_text: [If, being consumed by the heat of spring, or through such exertion, effort, and striving, or when even a small measure of appropriate activity causes weariness — if, from a cause and basis of weariness, drowsiness arises at an improper time — for the purpose of quickly and promptly eliminating that, and so that the wholesome side is not impaired for a long time, and so that there is no obstruction to the wholesome side, one should briefly rest in sleep. And therein, having closed one's door, or in the presence of a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) as witness, with the guarding and discipline of the <s>Vinaya</s>, having wrapped oneself in the <s>dharma</s>-robe, one should sit in a secluded place and rest in sleep — thus one should intend. Thereby, that drowsiness is completely eliminated in every way.]

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-8-a-(4) Ms.-, Sh.-, P.60b6, D.51a3, N.53b3, Co.55a4, Ch.416c7
de ni 'di lta ste / rgyu ba daṅ spyod pa las brtsams nas / śes bźin du (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> I 206

children.text: ) spyod pa ñid kyi go rims yin te / dan po kho nar de ltar tshul bźin yid la byed pa daṅ / śes rab daṅ ldan pa'i sems mṅon par 'du byed pa gaṅ yin pa de ni de'i śes bźin źes bya'o //
children.translated_text: whatever mental formation arises that is endowed with wise attention and wisdom — that, in this context, is called 'clear comprehension.'

body.translated_text: [This is the sequential arrangement of clear comprehension (<s>saṃprajanya</s>) itself in relation to deportment and conduct. First of all,

body.text: de ltar śes bźin daṅ ldan pas rgyu ba daṅ spyod pa thams cad mi ñuṅ bar sgrub par byed pa gaṅ yin pa de ni śes bźin du spyod pa ñid ces bya'o //
body.translated_text: Whatever one who is thus endowed with clear comprehension accomplishes in all deportment and conduct without deficiency — that is called 'acting with clear comprehension.'
