body.text: de la 'gro ba daṅ / ldog pa daṅ / chuṅ zad bltas pa daṅ / rnam par bltas pa daṅ / bskum pa daṅ / brkyaṅ ba daṅ / snam sbyar daṅ / chos gos daṅ / lhuṅ bzed bcaṅ ba gaṅ yin pa daṅ / zos pa daṅ / 'thuṅs pa daṅ / 'chos pa daṅ / myaṅs pa gaṅ yin pa de la śes bźin du spyod pa gaṅ yin pa de ni groṅ du rgyu ba daṅ ldan pa la śes bźin du spyod pa ñid ces bya'o //
body.translated_text: Therein, whatever involves going, returning, looking briefly, looking around, bending, stretching, wearing the inner robe, the <s>dharma</s>-robe, and holding the bowl, and whatever involves eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting — clear comprehension with respect to those is called 'acting with clear comprehension in connection with going about in the village.'

body.text: de la soṅ ba daṅ / sdod pa daṅ / 'dug pa daṅ / ñal ba daṅ / mi ñal ba daṅ / smra ba daṅ / mi smra ba gaṅ yin pa daṅ / gñid kyi sñom pa bsaṅ ba gaṅ yin pa de la śes bźin du spyod pa gaṅ yin pa de ni gtsug lag khaṅ na spyod pa daṅ ldan pa la śes bźin du spyod pa ñid ces bya ste /
body.translated_text: Therein, whatever involves walking, standing, sitting, lying down, not lying down, speaking, not speaking, and resting from drowsiness — clear comprehension with respect to those is called 'acting with clear comprehension in connection with conduct in the monastery.'

body.text: de ni re źig śes bźin du spyod pa ñid kyi rnam par dbye ba rgyas pa yin par rig par bya'o //
body.translated_text: This should be understood as the detailed classification of acting with clear comprehension.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-8-b-(1) Ms.-, Sh.-, P.61a3, D.51b1, N.53b7, Co.55b2, Ch.416c17
don mdor bsdu ba gaṅ źe na / rgyu ba daṅ ldan pa'i las rnam pa lṅa daṅ / spyod pa daṅ ldan pa'i las rnam pa lṅa daṅ / rgyu ba daṅ ldan pa daṅ / spyod pa daṅ ldan pa'i las la śes bźin du spyod pa rnam pa bźi gaṅ yin pa de ni don mdor bsdu ba źes bya'o //
body.translated_text: What is the summary meaning? Whatever five kinds of actions connected with going about, and five kinds of actions connected with conduct, and whatever four kinds of clear comprehension in actions connected with going about and conduct — that is called the summary meaning.

body.text: de la rgyu ba daṅ ldan pa'i las rnam pa lṅa gaṅ źe na / 'di lta ste / lus kyi las daṅ / mig gi las daṅ / yan lag daṅ / ñiṅ lag thams cad kyi las daṅ / chos gos daṅ / lhuṅ bzed kyi las daṅ / bsod sñoms kyi las te / de ni rgyu ba daṅ ldan pa'i las rnam pa lṅa źes bya'o //
body.translated_text: What are the five kinds of actions connected with going about? Namely: bodily action, action of the eye, action of all major and minor limbs, action of the <s>dharma</s>-robe and bowl, and action of almsfood — these are called the five kinds of actions connected with going about.

body.text: de la re źig ldog pa daṅ 'gro ba źes bya ba gaṅ gsuṅs pa des ni rgyu ba daṅ ldan pa'i lus kyi las bstan to // "chuṅ zad bltas pa daṅ / rnam par bltas pa" źes gaṅ gsuṅs pa des ni rgyu ba daṅ ldan pa'i mig gi las bstan to // (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> I 208

children.text: ) "bskum pa daṅ / brkyaṅ ba" źes bya ba gaṅ gsuṅs pa des ni rgyu ba daṅ ldan pa'i yan lag daṅ ñiṅ lag thams cad kyi las bstan to // "snam sbyar daṅ / chos gos daṅ / lhuṅ bzed bcaṅ ba" źes gaṅ gsuṅs pa des ni rgyu ba daṅ ldan pa'i chos gos daṅ / lhuṅ bzed kyi las bstan to // "zos pa daṅ / 'thuṅs pa daṅ / 'chos pa daṅ / myaṅs pa" źes gaṅ gsuṅs pa des ni rgyu ba daṅ ldan pa'i bsod sñoms kyi las bstan to //
children.translated_text: What was stated as 'bending and stretching' — by that, the action of all major and minor limbs connected with going about is shown. What was stated as 'wearing the inner robe, the <s>dharma</s>-robe, and holding the bowl' — by that, the action of the <s>dharma</s>-robe and bowl connected with going about is shown. What was stated as 'eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting' — by that, the action of almsfood connected with going about is shown.

body.translated_text: Therein, first, what was stated as 'returning and going' — by that, the bodily action connected with going about is shown. What was stated as 'looking briefly and looking around' — by that, the action of the eye connected with going about is shown.

body.text: spyod pa daṅ ldan pa'i las rnam pa lṅa gaṅ źe na / 'di lta ste / lus kyi las daṅ / ṅag gi las daṅ / yid kyi las daṅ / ñin mo'i las daṅ / mtshan mo'i las te / de ni spyod pa daṅ ldan pa'i las rnam pa lṅa źes bya'o //
body.translated_text: What are the five kinds of actions connected with conduct? Namely: bodily action, verbal action, mental action, daytime action, and nighttime action — these are called the five kinds of actions connected with conduct.

body.text: de la re źig "soṅ ba daṅ / sdod pa daṅ / 'dug pa" źes gaṅ gsuṅs pa des ni spyod pa daṅ ldan pa'i lus kyi las bstan to // "smra ba" źes gaṅ gsuṅs pa des ni spyod pa daṅ ldan pa'i ṅag gi las bstan to // "ñal ba daṅ / mi smra ba daṅ / gñid kyi sñom pa bsaṅ ba" źes gaṅ gsuṅs pa des ni spyod pa daṅ ldan pa'i yid kyi las bstan to // "mi ñal ba" źes gaṅ gsuṅs pa des ni spyod pa daṅ ldan pa'i ñin mo'i las daṅ / mtshan mo'i las daṅ / lus kyi las daṅ / ṅag gi las kyaṅ bstan to // "ñal ba" źes gaṅ gsuṅs pa des ni spyod pa daṅ ldan pa'i mtshan mo'i las daṅ yid kyi las kho nar yaṅ bstan te / de ni spyod pa daṅ ldan pa'i las rnam pa lṅa yin par rig par bya'o //
body.translated_text: Therein, first, what was stated as 'walking, standing, and sitting' — by that, the bodily action connected with conduct is shown. What was stated as 'speaking' — by that, the verbal action connected with conduct is shown. What was stated as 'lying down, not speaking, and resting from drowsiness' — by that, the mental action connected with conduct is shown. What was stated as 'not lying down' — by that, the daytime action, nighttime action, bodily action, and verbal action connected with conduct are also shown. What was stated as 'lying down' — by that, only the nighttime action and mental action connected with conduct are shown — these should be understood as the five kinds of actions connected with conduct.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-8-b-(2) Ms.-, Sh.-, P.61b6, D.52a1, N.54b1, Co.56a3, Ch.417a6
de la rgyu ba daṅ ldan pa daṅ / spyod pa daṅ ldan pa'i las la śes bźin du spyod pa rnam pa bźi gaṅ źe na / daṅ po kho nar "las 'di lta bu źig brtsam mo" źes rgyu ba'i las sam / spyod pa'i las śig rtsoṃ par byed pa na / las de ñid la dran pa ñe bar gźag ciṅ / bag yod par spyod la / las de dran pas yoṅs su zin ciṅ bag yod pas kyaṅ yoṅs su zin pas / gźi gaṅ la phyogs gaṅ du / dus gaṅ gi tshe ji sñed cig rnam pa gaṅ gis ji ltar brtag par bya ba'i gźi de la / phyogs der dus de'i tshe / de sñed cig rnam pa des de ltar rtog par byed ciṅ rab tu śes par byed pa ste / de ltar rtog par byed ciṅ / rab tu śes par byed pa na tshe 'di ñid la kha na ma tho ba med pa daṅ / lhuṅ ba med pa (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 210

children.text: ) daṅ / 'gyod pa med pa daṅ / yid la gcags pa med pa daṅ / rjes su gduṅ ba med par 'gyur ba daṅ / tshe phyi ma la yaṅ kha na ma tho ba med ciṅ lus źig ste / śi ba'i 'og tu ṅan son ṅan 'gro log par ltuṅ ba sems can dmyal ba rnams su skye bar mi 'gyur ba daṅ / ma thob pa thob par bya ba'i tshogs kyi rgyu byas par 'gyur ba yin no //
children.translated_text: no remorse, no mental anguish, no torment; and in the next life, with the body broken apart after death, one does not arise in the lower realms, evil destinies, downfalls, or hells; and it serves as a cause for the equipment of attaining what has not been attained.]

body.translated_text: [Therein, what are the four kinds of clear comprehension in actions connected with going about and conduct? First of all, when one is about to begin some action involving going about or conduct, one intends: "I shall undertake such-and-such an action." Then, for that very action, one establishes mindfulness and acts with heedfulness. And since that action is grasped by mindfulness and also grasped by heedfulness — regarding whatever basis, in whatever direction, at whatever time, to whatever extent, and in whatever manner it should be examined — on that basis, in that direction, at that time, to that extent, in that manner, one examines and clearly comprehends. And while thus examining and clearly comprehending, in this very life there is no blameworthiness and no transgression,

body.text: de ni śes bźin du spyod pa ñid kyi don mdor bsdus pa yin te / rnam par dbye ba rgyas par sṅa ma gaṅ yin pa daṅ / don mdor bsdu ba gaṅ yin pa de ni śes bźin du spyod pa ñid ces bya'o //
body.translated_text: [This is the summary meaning of acting with clear comprehension itself. Both the detailed classification that was stated previously and the summary meaning — that is called 'acting with clear comprehension.']

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-9-a-(1) Ms.-, Sh.-,W.*74-24(Englisḥ tr.),P.62a4,D.52a6,N.54b6,Co.56a7, Ch.417a19
de la dge ba'i bśes gñen gaṅ źe na / rgyu rnam pa brgyad kyis rnam pa thams cad yoṅs su rdzogs pa'i dge ba'i bśes gñen yin par rig par bya'o //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is a good spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>)? One should understand that through eight causes, a good spiritual friend is complete in every aspect.

body.text: brgyad gaṅ źe na / 'di ltar 'di na la la daṅ po kho nar tshul khrims la gnas pa yin pa daṅ / maṅ du thos pa yin pa daṅ / rtog pa daṅ ldan pa yin pa daṅ / rjes su sñiṅ brtse ba daṅ ldan pa yin pa daṅ / yid yoṅs su mi skyo ba yin pa daṅ / bzod pa daṅ ldan pa yin pa daṅ / mi 'jigs pa daṅ ldan pa yin pa daṅ / tshig gi bya ba daṅ ldan pa yin no //
body.translated_text: What are the eight? It is like this: here a certain person first of all is established in moral conduct, is one of great learning, is endowed with realization, is endowed with compassion, is of unwearied mind, is endowed with patience, is endowed with fearlessness, and is endowed with skill in speech.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-9-a-(1)-i Ms.-, Sh.-, P.62a6, D.52b1, N.55a1, Co.56b2, Ch.417b1
de la ji ltar na tshul khrims la gnas pa yin źe na / rgyas par sṅa ma bźin du tshul khrims daṅ ldan par gnas pa daṅ / so sor thar ba'i sdom pas bsdams pa daṅ / dge sbyoṅ gi lam 'dod pa daṅ / bram ze'i lam 'dod pa daṅ / bdag dul bar bya ba daṅ / bdag źi bar bya ba daṅ / bdag yoṅs su mya ṅan las 'da' bar bya ba'i phyir źugs pa yin te / de ltar na tshul khrims la gnas pa yin no //
body.translated_text: Therein, how is one established in moral conduct? In detail as before: one dwells endowed with moral conduct, restrained by the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint, desiring the way of the ascetic, desiring the way of the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, having gone forth for the purpose of self-taming, self-pacification, and one's own <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. Thus one is established in moral conduct.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-9-a-(1)-ii Ms.57b2R, Sh.127-2, P.62a8, D.52b3, N.55a2, Co.56b3, Ch.417b5
ji ltar na maṅ du thos pa yin źe na / des chos tshaṅs par spyod pa daṅ / thog mar dge ba / bar du dge ba / tha mar dge ba / don bzaṅ po / tshig 'bru bzaṅ po / ma 'dres pa / yoṅs su rdzogs pa / yoṅs su dag pa / yoṅs su byaṅ ba gaṅ dag yin pa de dag mṅon par brjod pas mṅon par rjod par byed pa daṅ / evaṃrūpā anena bahavo dharmā udgṛhītā bhavanti dhṛtā vacasā parijitā manasā cānvīkṣitā dṛṣṭyā supratividdhāḥ / evaṃ bahuśruto bhavati //
body.translated_text: How is one of great learning? By him, those <s>dharmas</s> of the holy life that are good at the beginning, good in the middle, good at the end, having good meaning, good words, unmixed, complete, pure, and purified — those he proclaims by way of exposition. And many <s>dharmas</s> of such kind have been taken up by him, retained, mastered verbally, investigated mentally, and well penetrated by view. Thus one is of great learning.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-9-a-(1)-iii Ms.57b3L, Sh.129-1, P.62b3, D.52b5, N.55a4, Co.56b5, Ch.417b9
katham adhigantā bhavati / lābhī bhavaty anityasaṃjñāyā anitye duḥkhasaṃjñāyā duḥkhe 'nātmasaṃjñāyā āhāre pratikūlasaṃjñāyāḥ sarvaloke 'nabhiratisaṃjñāyā ādīnavasaṃjñāyāḥ prahāṇasaṃjāyā virāgasaṃjñāyā nirodhasaṃjñāyā maraṇasaṃjñāyā aśubhasaṃjñāyā vinīlakasaṃjñāyā vipūyakasaṃjñāyā vipaḍumakasaṃjñāyā vyādhmātakasaṃjñāyā vikhāditakasaṃjñāyā vilohitakasaṃjñāyā vikṣiptakasaṃjñāyā asthisaṃjñāyāḥ śūnyatāpratyavekṣaṇasaṃjñāyāḥ / lābhī bhavati prathamasya dhyānasya dvitīyasya tṛtīyasya caturthasyākāśānantyāyatanavijñānānantyāyatanākiṃcanyāyatananaivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanasya maitryāḥ karuṇāyā muditāyā upekṣāyāḥ srotaāpattiphalasya sakṛdāgāmiphalasyānāgāmiphalasya carddhiviṣayasya pūrvanivāsasya divyasya śrotrasya cyutyupapādasya cetaḥparyāyasyārhattvasyāṣṭavimokṣadhyāyitvasya / śakto bhavati pratibalaś ca pareṣāṃ tribhiḥ prātihāryair avavaditum, ṛddhiprātihāryeṇa, ādeśanāprātihāryeṇa, anuśāsanāprātihāryeṇa / evam adhigantā bhavati //
body.translated_text: How is one an attainer? One has obtained the perception of impermanence regarding the impermanent, the perception of suffering regarding suffering, the perception of not-self, the perception of repulsiveness regarding food, the perception of non-delight in all the world, the perception of danger, the perception of abandonment, the perception of dispassion, the perception of cessation, the perception of death, the perception of the impure, the perception of the blue-black [corpse], the perception of the festering, the perception of the bloated, the perception of the split open, the perception of the gnawed, the perception of the blood-smeared, the perception of the scattered, the perception of bones, the perception of investigation of emptiness. One has obtained the first <s>dhyāna</s>, the second, the third, the fourth; the sphere of infinite space, the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception; <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy), <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity); the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpatti</s>), the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmi</s>), the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmi</s>); the domain of supernatural powers (<s>ṛddhi</s>), knowledge of past lives (<s>pūrvanivāsa</s>), the divine ear, [knowledge of] death and rebirth, knowledge of others' minds, and <s>arhatship</s>; and mastery of the eight liberations (<s>aṣṭavimokṣa</s>). One is capable and competent to admonish others by three miracles: the miracle of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhiprātihārya</s>), the miracle of mind-reading (<s>ādeśanāprātihārya</s>), and the miracle of instruction (<s>anuśāsanāprātihārya</s>). Thus one is an attainer.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-9-a-(1)-iv Ms.57b5M, Sh.129-16, P.63a3, D.53a4, N.55b4, Co.57a5, Ch.417b22
katham anukampako bhavati / pareṣām antike kāruṇiko bhavati dayāpannah / arthakāmo bhavati hitakāmaḥ sukhakāmaḥ sparśakāmo yogakṣemakāmaḥ / evam anukampako bhavati //
body.translated_text: How is one compassionate? One is compassionate toward others, sympathetic, desirous of their welfare, desirous of their benefit, desirous of their happiness, desirous of their comfort, and desirous of their security. Thus one is compassionate.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-9-a-(1)-v Ms.57b5R, Sh.129-20, P.63a5, D.53a5, N.55b5, Co.57a6, Ch.417b25
katham aparikhinnamānaso bhavati / saṃdarśako bhavati samādāpakaḥ samuttejakaḥ saṃpraharṣakaḥ / ayāsī catasṛnāṃ parṣadāṃ dharmadeśanāyai dakṣo bhavaty analasa utthānasaṃpanna ārabdhavīryajātīyaḥ / evam aparikhinnamānaso bhavati //
body.translated_text: How is one of unwearied mind? One is a shower, a persuader, an encourager, and a gladdener. One is untiring in teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to the four assemblies; one is capable, not lazy, endowed with initiative, and of the nature of aroused vigor. Thus one is of unwearied mind.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-9-a-(1)-vi Ms.57b6R, Sh.130-2, P.63a7, D.53a7, N.55b7, Co.57b1, Ch.417b29
kathaṃ kṣamāvān bhavati / ākruṣṭo na pratyākrośati / roṣito na pratiroṣayati / tādito na pratitāḍayati / bhaṇḍito na pratibhaṇḍayati / ākoṭānapratyākoṭānakṣamo bhavati / pragāḍheṣv api bandhaneṣu rodhaneṣu tāḍaneṣu kutsaneṣu tarjaneṣu chedaneṣv ātmāparādhī bhavati / karmavipākaṃ ca pratisarati / na pareṣām antike kupyati / nāpy anuśayaṃ vahati / iti vimānito 'pi vivarṇito 'pi vijugupsito 'pi na vikṛtim āpadyate / nānyatrārthāyaiva cetayate / kṣamaś ca bhavati śītasyoṣṇasya jighatsāyāḥ pipāsāyā daṃśamaśakavātātapasarīsṛpasaṃsparśānām / parato duruktānām durāgatānāṃ vacanapathānām utpannānāṃ śārīrikāṇāṃ vedanānāṃ duḥkhānāṃ tīvrāṇāṃ kharāṇāṃ kaṭukānām amanaāpānāṃ prāṇahāriṇīnāṃ kṣamo bhavaty adhivāsanajātīyaḥ / evaṃ kṣamāvān bhavati //
body.translated_text: How is one patient (<s>kṣamāvān</s>)? When reviled, one does not revile in return; when provoked, one does not provoke in return; when struck, one does not strike in return; when abused, one does not abuse in return. One is capable of enduring blows and retorts. Even in the case of severe binding, imprisonment, beating, humiliation, threats, and cutting — one blames oneself, and one recalls the ripening of <s>karma</s>. One does not become angry toward others, nor does one harbor resentment. Even when despised, criticized, or treated with disgust, one does not undergo any change, and one does not think about anything other than the very purpose [of the teaching]. One is patient with cold, heat, hunger, thirst, the contact of flies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and serpents; with harsh words and unwelcome speech from others; and with arisen bodily feelings that are painful, intense, sharp, bitter, disagreeable, and life-threatening — one is patient and of the nature of forbearance. Thus one is patient.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-9-a-(1)-vii Ms.58a2L, Sh.130-18, P.63b5, D.53b5, N.56a5, Co.57b6, Ch.417c9
kathaṃ viśārado bhavati / asaṃlīnacittaḥ parṣadi dharmaṃ deśayaty agadgadasvaro 'saṃpramuṣitasmṛtipratibhānaḥ / na cāsya śāradyahetoḥ śāradyanidānaṃ bhayaṃ vākrāmati samāviśati / nāpi kakṣābhyāṃ svedo mucyate romakūpebhyo vā / evaṃ viśārado bhavati //
body.translated_text: How is one fearless (<s>viśārada</s>)? One teaches the <s>Dharma</s> before the assembly with an unshrunken mind, with an unfaltering voice, with mindfulness and eloquence unimpaired. And on account of that fearlessness, neither fear nor trembling enters or overcomes one. Nor does sweat issue from one's armpits or pores. Thus one is fearless.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-9-a-(1)-viii Ms.58a2R, Sh.131-4, P.63b6, D.53b6, N.56a6, Co.57b6, Ch.417c13
kathaṃ vākkaraṇenopeto bhavati / pauryā vācā samanvāgato bhavati, valgvā, vispaṣṭayā, vijñeyayā, śravaṇīyayā, apratikūlayā, aniśritayā, aparyantayā / evaṃ vākkaraṇenopeto bhavati kalyāṇavākyaḥ //
body.translated_text: How is one endowed with skill in speech? One is endowed with speech that is urbane, pleasant, clear, intelligible, audible, inoffensive, independent, and unlimited. Thus one is endowed with skill in speech, one of beautiful words.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-9-a-(2) Ms.58a3M, Sh.131-9, W.*74-33, P.63b8, D.57b7, N.56a7, Co.58a1, Ch.417c17
sa ebhir aṣṭābhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ samanvāgataś codako bhavati, smārakaḥ avavādakaḥ, anuśāsakaḥ, dharmadeśakaḥ //
body.translated_text: One endowed with these eight qualities becomes one who admonishes, who reminds, who advises, who instructs, and who teaches the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-9-a-(2)-i Ms.58a3R, Sh.131-12, P.64a1, D.54a1, N.56b1, Co.58a1, Ch.417c18
kathaṃ cokado bhavati / yad utādhiśīle ca śīlavipattyā, adhyācara ācāravipattyā, dṛṣṭena śrutena pariśaṅkayā codayati, bhūtena nābhūtena kālena nākālenārthopasaṃhitena nānarthopasaṃhitena ślakṣṇena na paruṣeṇa mitravattayā na dveṣāntareṇa / evaṃ codako bhavati //
body.translated_text: How does one admonish? One admonishes regarding higher moral conduct and the failure of moral conduct, regarding higher conduct and the failure of conduct — by what is seen, by what is heard, by suspicion — truthfully and not untruthfully, at the proper time and not at an improper time, in connection with the purpose and not in connection with what is purposeless, gently and not harshly, with the disposition of a friend and not from inner hostility. Thus one admonishes.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-9-a-(2)-ii Ms.58a4R, Sh.131-18, W.*75-1, P.64a3, D.54a3, N.56b3, Co.58a3, Ch.417c23
kathaṃ smārako bhavati / āpattiṃ vā smārayati dharmaṃ vārthaṃ vā / katham āpattim smārayati / yathāpi tadāpattim adhyāpadyamāno na smarati tam enaṃ smārayati, "āyuṣmann amuṣmin deśe, amuṣmin vastuni, amuṣmin kāle, evaṃrūpaṃ caivaṃrūpām āpattim āpanna" iti / evam āpattiṃ smārayati /
body.translated_text: How does one remind? One reminds of an offense, or of a <s>dharma</s>, or of a meaning. How does one remind of an offense? When someone who has committed an offense does not remember it, one reminds him: "Venerable one, in such-and-such a place, regarding such-and-such a matter, at such-and-such a time, you committed such-and-such an offense." Thus one reminds of an offense.

body.text: kathaṃ dharmaṃ smārayati / yathāpi tacchrutānugṛhitān dharmān ekākī na smarati, smartum icchati / tadyathā sūtraṃ geyaṃ vyākaraṇam iti vistareṇa pūrvavan na smarati tam enaṃ smārayati / utsmāraṇikāṃ vāsyānuprayacchati, āpṛcchanaparipṛcchanikāṃ vā / evaṃ dharmaṃ smārayati /
body.translated_text: How does one remind of a <s>dharma</s>? When someone alone does not remember the <s>dharmas</s> supported by learning, and wishes to remember them — such as <s>sūtra</s>, <s>geya</s>, <s>vyākaraṇa</s> — in detail as before — and does not remember, one reminds him. Or one provides a mnemonic aid, or a [format of] questioning and cross-questioning. Thus one reminds of a <s>dharma</s>.

body.text: katham arthaṃ smārayati / yathāpi tadarthaṃ vismarati tam enaṃ smārayati / punar api pratinavīkaroti, uttānīkaroti, deśayati, saṃprakāśayati, yac cāpi kuśalam arthopasaṃhitaṃ brahmacaryopasaṃhitaṃ cirakṛtaṃ cirabhāṣitam apy anusmārayitā bhavati / evaṃ smārako bhavati //
body.translated_text: How does one remind of a meaning? When someone forgets a meaning, one reminds him. Furthermore, one renews, clarifies, explains, and illuminates [the meaning]. And whatever wholesome thing connected with the purpose, connected with the holy life, was done long ago or spoken long ago — one reminds [of that] as well. Thus one is a reminder.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-9-a-(2)-iii Ms.58a7M, Sh.132-16, P.64b1, D.54b1, N.57a1, Co.58b1, Ch.418a8
katham avavādako bhavati / prāvivekye pratisaṃlayane yoge manasikāre śamathavipaśyanāyāṃ kālena kālam ānulomikam avavādaṃ pravartayati / kālena ca kālaṃ tatpratisaṃyuktāṃ kathāṃ karoti / tadyathā cetovinivaraṇasāṃpreyagāminīṃ śīlakathāṃ vā samādhikathāṃ vā prajñākathāṃ vā vimuktikathāṃ vā vimuktijñānadarśanakathāṃ vālpecchākathāṃ vā saṃtuṣṭikathāṃ vā prahāṇakathāṃ virāgakathāṃ nirodhakathām apacayakathām asaṃsargakathām daṃpratyayatāpratītyasamutpādānuIomāṃ kathāṃ karoti / evam avavādako bhavati //
body.translated_text: How does one advise? Regarding seclusion, retreat, meditation, mental attention, and <s>śamatha-vipaśyanā</s> (calm and insight), one gives timely and appropriate advice from time to time. And from time to time one gives discourse connected with that — namely: discourse that removes the mental hindrances and leads to the good destination — discourse on moral conduct, discourse on concentration, discourse on wisdom, discourse on liberation, discourse on the knowledge and vision of liberation, discourse on fewness of desires, discourse on contentment, discourse on abandonment, discourse on dispassion, discourse on cessation, discourse on diminishment, discourse on non-association, and discourse in accordance with specific conditionality and dependent origination. Thus one advises.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-9-a-(2)-iv Ms.58b2L, Sh.133-3, P.64b5, D.54b4, N.57a4, Co.58b4, Ch.418a15
katham anuśāsako bhavati / dharmeṇa vinayena śāstuḥ śāsane samanuśāsako (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 222

children.text: ) bhavati / ācāryo vopādhyāyo vā sahadhārmiko vā gurur vā gurusthānīyo vānyatamānyatamasminn adhikaraṇe 'trisṛtaṃ vyatikrāntaṃ viditvā, kālena kālam avasādayati daṇḍakarmānuprayacchati pravāsayati cainaṃ / punar api ca dharmeṇa samaye pratisaṃstarasāmīcīsaṃjñapitiṃ pratigṛhṇāti saṃgrāhakaś ca bhavati / karaṇīye cākaraṇīye vādhyācārānadhyācārād adhyācīrṇe 'nadhyācīrṇe ca śāsty anuśāsti / evam anuśāsako bhavati //
children.translated_text: one becomes [an instructor]. Whether a teacher, a preceptor, a fellow practitioner of the <s>Dharma</s>, an elder, or one occupying the position of an elder — knowing that in a particular case [a rule] has been transgressed beyond the three [occasions], one from time to time censures, administers disciplinary action, and banishes that person. And again, in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>, at the proper occasion, one receives the acknowledgment of reconciliation and propriety, and one becomes a gatherer [of the community]. In what should be done and what should not be done, in what has been transgressed and what has not been transgressed regarding conduct and non-conduct, one instructs and governs. Thus one becomes an instructor.

body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-9-a-(2)-iv — How does one become an instructor? One who properly instructs in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>, the <s>Vinaya</s> (discipline), and the teaching of the Teacher —

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-9-a-(2)-v Ms.58b3M, Sh.133-13, P.64b8, D.54b6, N.57a7, Co.58b7, Ch.418a23
kathaṃ ca dharmadeśako bhavati / kālena kālaṃ pūrvakālakaraṇīyāṃ kathāṃ karoti, tadyathā dānakathāṃ śīlakathām svargakathām / kāmeṣv ādīnavaniḥsaraṇān vyavadānapakṣān dharmān vistareṇa saṃprakāśayati / kālena kālaṃ sāmutkarṣikīṃ caturāryasatyapratisaṃyuktāṃ kathāṃ kathayati / duḥkhaṃ vārabhya samudayaṃ vā nirodhaṃ vā mārgaṃ vā / sattvaparipākāya vā sattvavyavadānāya vā saddharmasya vā cirasthitaye / yuktaiḥ padavyañjanaiḥ sahitair ānulomikair ānucchavikair aupāyikaiḥ pratirūpaiḥ pradakṣiṇair nipakasyāṅgasaṃbhāraiḥ /
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-9-a-(2)-v — And how does one become a teacher of <s>Dharma</s>? From time to time one gives the preliminary discourse, such as a discourse on giving, a discourse on moral conduct, a discourse on heaven. One illuminates in detail the <s>dharmas</s> on the side of purification — the danger in sensual pleasures and the escape from them. From time to time one gives an exalting discourse connected with the Four Noble Truths — regarding suffering, or its origin, or its cessation, or the path; for the ripening of beings, or for the purification of beings, or for the long endurance of the true <s>Dharma</s>; with suitable words and syllables that are connected, concordant, fitting, skillful, proper, auspicious — the requisite collection for one who is wise.

body.text: tāṃ ca punaḥ kathāṃ kālena karoti, satkṛtyānupūrvam anusaṃdhim anusahitaṃ harṣayan rocayan toṣayann utsāhayann anavasādayaṃs ca yuktāṃ sahitām avyavakīrṇāṃ dhārmikīṃ yathāparṣan maitracitto hitacitto 'nukampācitto 'niśrito lābhasatkāraśloke na cātmānam utkarṣayati, na parān paṃsayati / evaṃ dharmadeśako bhavati //
body.translated_text: And one gives that discourse at the proper time, respectfully, in due order, with coherence, in a connected manner — gladdening, delighting, satisfying, encouraging, and not causing despondency — a discourse that is well-composed, coherent, undispersed, and righteous, appropriate to the assembly, with a mind of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), a mind of benevolence, a mind of compassion, not dependent on gain, honor, and fame, not exalting oneself, not disparaging others. Thus one becomes a teacher of <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-9-a-(3) Ms.58b6L, Sh.134-9, P.65a7, D.55a5, N.57b6, Co.59a5, Ch.418b7
yaś caibhir aṣṭābhir aṅgaiḥ samanvāgato bhavati, evaṃ ca kālena kālaṃ codako bhavati smārako 'vavādako 'nuśāsako dharmadeśakah, tasmāt sa kalyāṇamitra ity ucyate / ayaṃ tāvat kalyāṇamitratāyā vistaravibhāgaḥ//
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-9-a-(3) — One who is endowed with these eight qualities, and who from time to time is an urger, a reminder, an admonisher, an instructor, and a teacher of <s>Dharma</s> — therefore that one is called a <s>kalyāṇamitra</s> (spiritual friend). This is the detailed analysis of spiritual friendship.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-9-b Ms.58b6R, Sh.134-14, P.65b1, D.55a6, N 57b7, Co.59a7, Ch.418b10
samāsārthaḥ punaḥ katamaḥ / saced ayaṃ mitrasuhṛdanukampaka ādita eva hitakāmo bhavati, sukhakāmaś ca / tac ca punar hitasukhaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti, aviparyasto bhavaty aviparītadṛṣṭiḥ / pratibalas ca bhavaty upāyakuśalaḥ yad utāsyaiva hitasukhasya samudāgamāyopasaṃhārāya / dakṣas ca bhavaty analasa utthānasaṃpanna ārabdhavīryajātīyaḥ, yad uta tam eva hitasukhopasaṃhāram ārabhya / ebhiś caturbhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ sarvākāraparipūrṇaḥ / samāsataḥ kalyāṇamitro veditavyaḥ / ayaṃ ca punaḥ kalyāṇamitratāyāḥ samāsārthaḥ /
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-9-b — What is the summary meaning? If this friend, companion, and sympathizer is from the very beginning desirous of benefit and desirous of happiness; and furthermore, one truly understands that benefit and happiness as it really is, being undistorted, of undistorted view; and one is capable and skillful in means for the accomplishment and bringing about of that very benefit and happiness; and one is adept, not lazy, endowed with initiative, of the nature of aroused energy, with respect to undertaking that very bringing about of benefit and happiness — by these four causes, complete in all aspects, one should be understood in summary as a <s>kalyāṇamitra</s>. And this is the summary meaning of spiritual friendship.

body.text: yaś ca pūrvako vistaravibhāgo yaś cāyaṃ samāsārtha iyam ucyate kalyāṇamitratā //
body.translated_text: Both the earlier detailed analysis and this summary meaning — this is called spiritual friendship.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-10-a-(1) Ms.59a2R, Sh.135-6, W.*75-6, P.65b5, D.55b3, N.58a4, Co.59b3, Ch.418b19
saddharmaśravaṇacintanā katamā / saddharma ucyate buddhaiś ca buddhaśrāvakaiś ca sadbhiḥ samyaggataiḥ satpuruṣair ākhyāto deśita uttāno vivṛtaḥ saṃprakāśitaḥ /
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-10-a-(1) — What is hearing and reflecting on the true <s>Dharma</s>? The true <s>Dharma</s> is called that which has been proclaimed, taught, disclosed, revealed, and made clear by the <s>Buddhas</s> and the disciples of the <s>Buddha</s>, by the good, the rightly-gone, the true persons.

body.text: sa punaḥ katamaḥ / tadyathā sūtraṃ geyaṃ vyākaraṇam iti vistareṇa pūrvavad dvādaśāṅgavacogatam saddharma ity ucyate //
body.translated_text: And what is it? Namely: <s>sūtra</s>, <s>geya</s>, <s>vyākaraṇa</s> — and so on in detail as before — that which is contained in the twelve divisions of the word. This is called the true <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: (I)-C-IIl-10-a-(1)-i Ms.59a3M, Sh.136-1, W.*75-18, P.66a1, D.55b6, N.58a7, Co.59b6, Ch.418b23 tatra sūtraṃ katamat / yat tatra tatra bhagavatā tāṃs tān vineyāṃs tāni tāni vineyacāritāni cārabhya skandhapratisaṃyuktā vā kathā kṛtā, dhātupratisaṃyuktā vā kathā kṛtā, dhātusaṅgaṇapratisayuktā vā, āyatanapratisaṃyuktā vā, pratītyasamutpādapratisaṃyuktā vā, āhārasatyapratisaṃyuktā vā, śrāvakapratyekabuddhatathāgatapratisaṃyuktā vā, smṛtyupasthānasamyakprahāṇa rddhipādendriyabalabodhyaṅgamārgāṅgapratisaṃyuktā vā, aśubhānāpānasmṛtiśikṣāvetyaprasādapratisaṃyuktā kathā kṛtā / sā ca kathā saṃgītikāraiḥ parigṛhya śāsanacirasthitaye yathāyogam (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 228

children.text: ) anupūrveṇa racitānupūrveṇa samāyuktā pratirūpair nāmakāyapadakāyavyañjanakāyair, yad uta teṣāṃ teṣām arthānāṃ sūcanāya kuśalānām arthopasaṃhitānāṃ brahmacaryopasaṃhitānām / idam ucyate sūtram //
children.translated_text: composed in due sequence with proper groups of names, groups of phrases, and groups of syllables — namely, for the indication of those various meanings, which are wholesome, connected with meaning, connected with the holy life — this is called <s>sūtra</s>.

body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-10-a-(1)-i — Therein, what is <s>sūtra</s> (discourse)? Whatever discourse the <s>Bhagavat</s> has given in various places, regarding various persons to be trained, in connection with various conducts of those to be trained — whether a discourse connected with the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), or a discourse connected with the <s>dhātus</s> (elements), or connected with the classification of elements, or connected with the <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), or connected with <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), or connected with nutriment and truth, or connected with <s>śrāvakas</s>, <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Tathāgatas</s>, or connected with the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness), <s>samyakprahāṇas</s> (right strivings), <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of spiritual power), <s>indriyas</s> (faculties), <s>balas</s> (powers), <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening), and <s>mārgāṅgas</s> (path-factors), or a discourse connected with the <s>aśubha</s> (unpleasant), <s>ānāpānasmṛti</s> (mindfulness of breathing), the training rules, and the verified grounds of confidence. And that discourse, taken up by the compilers of the collection for the long endurance of the teaching, arranged in due order, appropriately

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-10-a-(1)-ii Ms.59a5R, Sh.137-3, W.'76-16, P.66a6, D.56a3, N.58b4, Co.60a4, Ch.418c5
geyaṃ katamat / yasyānte paryavasāne gāthābhigītā, yac ca sūtraṃ neyārtham / idam ucyate geyam //
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-10-a-(1)-ii — What is <s>geya</s> (mixed verse and prose)? That at whose end and conclusion verses are sung; and whatever <s>sūtra</s> is of provisional meaning — this is called <s>geya</s>.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-10-(1)-iii Ms.59a6L, Sh.137-5, W.V6-20, P.66a7, D.56a4, N.58b5, Co.60a4, Ch.418c7
vyākaraṇaṃ katamat / yasmiñ chrāvakebhyo 'bhyatītakālagata upapattau vyākriyate, yac ca sūtraṃ nītārtham / idam ucyate vyākaraṇam //
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-10-a-(1)-iii — What is <s>vyākaraṇa</s> (declaration)? That in which the <s>śrāvakas</s> receive a declaration regarding their future rebirth in a past time; and whatever <s>sūtra</s> is of definitive meaning — this is called <s>vyākaraṇa</s>.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-10-(1)-iv Ms.59a6M, Sh.137-8, W.*76-26, P.66a8, D.56a4, N.58b5, Co.60a5, Ch.418c9
gāthā katamā / yā na gadyena bhāṣitā, api tu pādopanibandhena dvipadā vā tripadā vā catuṣpadā vā pañcapadā vā ṣaṭpadā vā / iyam ucyate gāthā //
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-10-a-(1)-iv — What is <s>gāthā</s> (verse)? That which is not spoken in prose but is composed in verse-feet — of two feet, three feet, four feet, five feet, or six feet — this is called <s>gāthā</s>.

body.text: (I)-C-IIl-10-a-(1)-v Ms.59a7L, Sh.137-11, W.*76-32, P.66b1, D.56a5, N.58b6, Co.60a6, Ch.418c12 udānaṃ katamat / yat pudgalasya nāma gotram aparikīrtayitvānuddiśya bhāṣitam āyatyāṃ vā saddharmacirasthitaye śāsanacirasthitaye (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 230
this is called <s>udāna</s>.

body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-10-a-(1)-v — What is <s>udāna</s> (inspired utterance)? That which is spoken without naming or identifying a person's name and clan, for the long endurance of the true <s>Dharma</s> and the teaching in the future —

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-10-a-(1)-vi Ms.5937M, Sh.138-2, W.*77-1, P.66b2, D.56a6, N.58b7, Co.60a7, Ch.418c14
nidānaṃ katamat / yat pudgalasya nāma gotraṃ parikīrtayitvoddiśya bhāṣitam, yac ca kiṃcid vinayapratisaṃyuktaṃ sotpattikaṃ sanidānaṃ prātimokṣasūtram / idam ucyate nidānam //
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-10-a-(1)-vi — What is <s>nidāna</s> (narrative occasion)? That which is spoken after naming and identifying a person's name and clan; and whatever is connected with the <s>Vinaya</s>, having an origin, having a cause — the <s>prātimokṣa</s> (monastic code) sūtra — this is called <s>nidāna</s>.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-10-a-(1)-vii Ms.59b1L, Sh.138-6, W.*77-9, P.66b3, D.56a7, N.59a1, Co.60b1, Ch.418c17
avadānaṃ katamat / yat sadṛṣṭāntakam udāhṛtam, yena dṛṣṭāntena yasya prakṛtasyārthasya vyavadānaṃ bhavati / idam ucyate 'vadānam //
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-10-a-(1)-vii — What is <s>avadāna</s> (parable)? That which is narrated with an illustration, by which illustration the purification of a given subject-matter is effected — this is called <s>avadāna</s>.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIi-10-a-(1)-viii Ms.59b1M, Sh.138-9, W.*77-15, P.66b4, D.56b1, N.59a2, Co.66b1, Ch.418c18
vṛttakaṃ katamat / yat kiṃcit pūrvayogapratisaṃyuktam / idam ucyate vṛttakam //
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-10-a-(1)-viii — What is <s>vṛttaka</s> (event narrative)? Whatever is connected with a former connection [in a previous life] — this is called <s>vṛttaka</s>.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-10-a-(1)-ix Ms.59b1R, Sh.138-11, W.*77-20, P.66b5, D.56b1, N.59a2, Co.60b2, Ch.418c20
jātakaṃ katamat / yad atītam adhvānam upādāya tatra tatra bhagavataś cyutyupapādeṣu bodhisattvacaryā duṣkaracaryākhyātā / idam ucyate jātakam //
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-10-a-(1)-ix — What is <s>jātaka</s> (birth story)? Whatever relates, with reference to the past, the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct and difficult conduct of the <s>Bhagavat</s> in his various deaths and rebirths — this is called <s>jātaka</s>.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-10-a-(1)-x Ms.59b2M, Sh.138-14, P.66b6, D.56b2, N.59a3, Co.60b4, Ch.418c22
vaipulyaṃ katamat / yatra bodhisattvānāṃ mārgo deśyate 'nuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye daśabalānāvaraṇajñānasamudāgamāya / idam ucyate vaipulyam //
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-10-a-(1)-x — What is <s>vaipulya</s> (extensive discourse)? That in which the path of <s>bodhisattvas</s> is taught for the unsurpassed perfect awakening, for the accomplishment of the ten powers and unobstructed knowledge — this is called <s>vaipulya</s>.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-10-a-(1)-xi Ms.59b2R, Sh.139-1, W.*77-26, P.66b7, D.56b3, N.59a4, Co.60b4, Ch.418c25
adbhutā dharmāḥ katame / yatra buddhānāṃ ca buddhaśrāvakāṇāṃ ca bhikṣūṇāṃ ca bhikṣuṇīnāṃ ca śikṣamāṇānāṃ śrāmaṇerāṇāṃ śrāmaṇerikāṇām upāsakānām upāsikānāṃ sādhāraṇāsādhāraṇāś ca tadanyaprativiśiṣṭāś cāścaryādbhutasaṃmatā guṇaviśeṣā ākhyātāḥ / ima ucyante 'dbhutā dharmāḥ //
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-10-a-(1)-xi — What are <s>adbhutadharmāḥ</s> (marvelous events)? That in which the special qualities, regarded as wonderful and marvelous, common and uncommon, and surpassing others, of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the disciples of the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> (nuns), <s>śikṣamāṇās</s> (female probationers), <s>śrāmaṇeras</s> (male novices), <s>śrāmaṇerikās</s> (female novices), <s>upāsakas</s> (male lay followers), and <s>upāsikās</s> (female lay followers) are proclaimed — these are called <s>adbhutadharmāḥ</s>.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-10-a-(1)-xii Ms.59b3R, Sh.139-7, W.*77-36, P.67a2, D.56b5, N.59a6, Co.60b6, Ch.419a1
upadeśāḥ katame / sarvamātṛkābhidharmaḥ sūtrāntaniṣkarṣaḥ sūtrāntavyākhyānam upadeśa ity ucyate //
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-10-a-(1)-xii — What is <s>upadeśa</s> (instruction)? The entire <s>mātṛkā</s> (matrix) <s>Abhidharma</s>, the extraction from the <s>sūtrāntas</s>, the explanation of the <s>sūtrāntas</s> — this is called <s>upadeśa</s>.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-10-a-(2) Ms.59b4L, Sh.139-10, W.*78-4, P.67a3, D.56b6, N.59a7, Co.60b6, Ch.419a3
tac caitad dvādaśāṅgavacogatam, asti sūtram, asti vinayaḥ asty abhidharmaḥ / tatra yat tāvad āha, sūtraṃ geyaṃ vyākaraṇaṃ gāthodānāvadānavṛttakajātakavaipulyādbhutadharmā iti, idaṃ tāvat sūtram / yat punar āha, nidānam iti, ayam ucyate vinayaḥ / yat punar āha, upadeśā iti, ayam ucyate 'bhidharmaḥ /
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-10-a-(2) — And this twelve-fold division of the word — there is <s>sūtra</s>, there is <s>Vinaya</s>, and there is <s>Abhidharma</s>. Therein, the statement: "<s>sūtra</s>, <s>geya</s>, <s>vyākaraṇa</s>, <s>gāthā</s>, <s>udāna</s>, <s>avadāna</s>, <s>vṛttaka</s>, <s>jātaka</s>, <s>vaipulya</s>, <s>adbhutadharmāḥ</s>" — this is the <s>sūtra</s> [basket]. The statement: "<s>nidāna</s>" — this is called the <s>Vinaya</s>. The statement: "<s>upadeśāḥ</s>" — this is called the <s>Abhidharma</s>.

body.text: tac caitad dvādaśāṅgavacogataṃ piṭakatrayasaṃgṛhītaṃ sadbhiḥ samyaggatair deśitaṃ saddharma ity ucyate //
body.translated_text: And this twelve-fold division of the word, comprised in the three baskets, taught by the good, the rightly-gone — this is called the true <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-10-a-(3) Ms.59b5M, Sh.139-17, W.*78-12, P.67a7, D.57a1, N.59b3, Co.61a2, Ch.419a10
tasya śravaṇaṃ saddharmaśravaṇam / tat punaḥ katamat / yathāpīhaikatyaḥ sūtradharo vā bhavati, vinayadharo vā, mātṛkādharo vā, sūtravinayadharo vā, sūtrābhidharmadharo vā, vinayamātṛkādharo vā, sūtravinayamātṛkādharo vā / idam ucyate saddharmaśravaṇam /
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-10-a-(3) — The hearing of that is hearing the true <s>Dharma</s>. And what is it? Just as here someone is a bearer of the <s>sūtras</s>, or a bearer of the <s>Vinaya</s>, or a bearer of the <s>mātṛkā</s>, or a bearer of the <s>sūtra</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, or a bearer of the <s>sūtra</s> and <s>Abhidharma</s>, or a bearer of the <s>Vinaya</s> and <s>mātṛkā</s>, or a bearer of the <s>sūtra</s>, <s>Vinaya</s>, and <s>mātṛkā</s> — this is called hearing the true <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: tat punaḥ śravaṇaṃ dvividham / vyañjanaśravaṇam arthaśravaṇaṃ ca //
body.translated_text: That hearing is twofold: hearing the letter and hearing the meaning.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-10-b-(1) Ms.59b6L,Sh.140-6,W.*78-18,**78-20f.67a8,D.57a3N.59b4,Co.61a4,Ch.419a17
cintanā katamā / yathāpīhaikatyas tān eva yathāśrutān dharmān ekākī rahogataḥ, ṣaḍ acintyāni sthānāni tadyathā, ātmacintāṃ sattvacintāṃ lokacintāṃ sattvānāṃ karmavipākacintāṃ dhyāyināṃ dhyāyiviṣayaṃ buddhānāṃ buddhaviṣayaṃ varjayitvā, svalakṣaṇataḥ sāmānyalakṣaṇataś ca cintayati //
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-10-b-(1) — What is reflection? Just as here someone, alone, in seclusion, regarding those very <s>dharmas</s> as they were heard — avoiding the six unthinkable subjects, namely: reflection on the self, reflection on sentient beings, reflection on the world, reflection on the karmic ripening of beings, the domain of meditators' meditation, and the domain of the <s>Buddhas</s>' [knowledge] — reflects on them according to their own characteristics and according to their general characteristics.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-10-b-(2) Ms.59b7L, Sh.140-12, W.*78-31, P.67b3, D.57a5, N.59b6, Co.61a6, Ch.419a22
sā punaś cintā dvividhā / gaṇanākārā saha gaṇanāyogena dharmāṇām / tulanākārā yuktyā guṇadoṣopaparīkṣaṇākārā / sacet skandhapratisaṃyuktāṃ deśanāṃ cintayati, saced anyatamānyatamāṃ pūrvanirdiṣṭāṃ deśanāṃ cintayati, ābhyāṃ dvābhyām ākārābhyāṃ cintayati //
body.translated_text: (I)-C-III-10-b-(2) — That reflection is twofold: of the nature of enumeration, together with the application of enumeration to <s>dharmas</s>; and of the nature of weighing, of the nature of examining merits and faults by reasoning. If one reflects on a teaching connected with the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), or if one reflects on any other previously indicated teaching, one reflects by these two modes.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIMO-b-(2)-i Ms.59b7R, Sh.140-16, P.67b5, D.57a6, N.60a1, Co.61b1, Ch.419a27
yathā punaḥ katham iti / rūpam ucyate daśa rūpīṇy āyatanāni yac ca dharmāyatanaparyāpannaṃ rūpam sa ca rūpaskandhaḥ / tisro vedanā vedanāskandhaḥ / ṣaṭ saṃjñākāyāḥ saṃjñāskandhaḥ / ṣaṭ cetanākāyāh saṃskāraskandhaḥ / ṣaḍ vijñānakāyā vijñānaskandhaḥ / ity evaṃ gaṇanāsaṃkhyākārayā skandhadeśanāṃ cintayati / uttarottaraprabhedena yena vā punar asyāḥ saṃkhyāgaṇanākārāyāś cintāyā apramāṇaḥ praveśanayo veditavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: How, then, and in what manner? Form (<s>rūpa</s>) is said to be the ten material sense bases (<s>āyatana</s>) and whatever form is included in the <s>dharmāyatana</s> — that is the form aggregate (<s>rūpaskandha</s>). Three [kinds of] feeling constitute the feeling aggregate (<s>vedanāskandha</s>). Six groups of perception constitute the perception aggregate (<s>saṃjñāskandha</s>). Six groups of volition constitute the formations aggregate (<s>saṃskāraskandha</s>). Six groups of consciousness constitute the consciousness aggregate (<s>vijñānaskandha</s>). Thus one reflects on the teaching of the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>) by the mode of counting and enumeration. Through progressively further analysis, the mode of entry into this reflection by counting and enumeration should be understood as immeasurable. //

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-10-b-(2)-ii Ms.60a2L, Sh.141-7, W.78-37, P.68a1, D.57b2, N.60a4, Co.61b3, Ch.419b5
kathaṃ yuktyupaparīkṣākārayā cintayā skandhadeśanāṃ cintayati / catasṛbhir yuktibhir upaparīkṣate /
body.translated_text: How does one reflect on the teaching of the aggregates by the mode of investigation through reasoning (<s>yukti</s>)? One investigates by means of four types of reasoning.

body.text: katamābhiś catasṛbhiḥ / yad utāpekṣāyuktyā, kāryakaraṇayuktyā, upapattisādhanayuktyā, dharmatāyuktyā //
body.translated_text: Which four? Namely: the reasoning of dependence (<s>apekṣāyukti</s>), the reasoning of function (<s>kāryakaraṇayukti</s>), the reasoning of evidential establishment (<s>upapattisādhanayukti</s>), and the reasoning of the nature of things (<s>dharmatāyukti</s>). //

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-10-b-(2)-ii-(a) Ms.60a2R, Sh.141-11, W.*79-8, P.68a2, D.57b3, N.60a5, Co.61b4, Ch.419b8
apekṣāyuktiḥ katamā / dvividhāpekṣā, utpattyapekṣā prajñaptyapekṣā ca / tatrotpattyapekṣā yair hetubhir yaiḥ pratyayaiḥ skandhānāṃ prādurbhāvo bhavati, tasyāṃ skandhotpattau te hetavas te pratyayā apekṣyante / yair nāmakāyapadakāyavyañjanakāyaiḥ skandhānāṃ prajñaptir bhavati, tasyām (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 238

children.text: ) skandhaprajñaptau te nāmakāyapadakāyavyañjanakāyā apekṣyante / iyam ucyate skandheṣūtpattyapekṣā prajñaptyapekṣā ca / yā cotpattyapekṣā yā ca prajñaptyapekṣā sā yuktir yoga upāyaḥ skandhotpattaye skandhaprajñaptaye / tasmād apekṣāyuktir ity ucyate //
children.translated_text: ) designation of the aggregates, those name-groups, sentence-groups, and syllable-groups are depended upon. This is called the dependence regarding arising and the dependence regarding designation in the aggregates. And whatever is the dependence regarding arising and whatever is the dependence regarding designation — that reasoning, method, and means is for the arising and designation of the aggregates. Therefore it is called the reasoning of dependence. //

body.translated_text: What is the reasoning of dependence (<s>apekṣāyukti</s>)? Dependence is twofold: dependence regarding arising and dependence regarding designation. Therein, dependence regarding arising: whatever causes and whatever conditions bring about the manifestation of the aggregates — in that arising of the aggregates, those causes and conditions are depended upon. Whatever name-groups, sentence-groups, and syllable-groups bring about the designation of the aggregates — in that

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-10-b-(2)-ii-(b) Ms.60a4M, Sh.142-3, W.*79-15, P.68a7, D.57b6, N.60b1, Co.61b7, Ch.419b16
kāryakaraṇayuktiḥ katamā / yad utpannānāṃ skandhānāṃ svena hetunā svena pratyayena tasmiṃs tasmin svakāryakaraṇe viniyogaḥ / tadyathā, cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi draṣṭavyāni, śrotreṇa śabdāḥ śrotavyāḥ, yāvan manasā dharmā vijñeyā iti / rūpeṇa cakṣuṣo gocare 'vasthātavyam, śabdena śrotrasya, evaṃ yāvad dharmair manas iti / yad vā punar anyad apy evaṃbhāgīyaṃ, tatra tatra dharmāṇām anyonyaṃ kāryakaraṇe prati yuktir yoga upāyaḥ / iyam ucyate kāryakaraṇayuktiḥ //
body.translated_text: What is the reasoning of function (<s>kāryakaraṇayukti</s>)? Each aggregate has its own function: the function of the form aggregate is to serve as the basis for experience; the function of feeling is to experience; the function of perception is to take signs; the function of formations is to construct; and the function of consciousness is to cognize. When each aggregate performs its own function, the reasoning that establishes this is called the reasoning of function. //

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-10-b-(2)-ii-(c) Ms.60a5R, Sh.142-12, W.*79-17, P.68b3, D.58a1, N.60b4, Co.62a3, Ch.419b23
upapattisādhanayuktiḥ katamā / anityāḥ skandhā iti, pratītyasamutpannā duḥkhāḥ śūnyā anātmāna iti tribhiḥ pramāṇair upaparīkṣate / yad utāptāgamena pratyakṣeṇānumānena ca / ebhis tribhiḥ pramāṇair upapattiyuktaiḥ satāṃ hṛdayagrāhakair vyavasthāpanā sādhanā kriyate / yad uta skandhānityatāyā vā pratītyasamutpannatāyā vā duḥkhatāyā vā (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 240

children.text: ) śūnyatāyā vanātmatāyā vā / iyam ucyata upapattisādhanayuktiḥ //
children.translated_text: ) whether regarding emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) or selflessness (<s>anātmatā</s>), this is called the reasoning of evidential establishment. //

body.translated_text: What is the reasoning of evidential establishment (<s>upapattisādhanayukti</s>)? When the teaching of the aggregates is investigated through three kinds of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) — namely, direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), inference (<s>anumāna</s>), and reliable testimony (<s>āgama</s>) — and is not contradicted,

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-10-b-(2)-ii-(d) Ms.60a7L, Sh.143-4, W.*79-19, P.68b6, D.58a4, N.60b6, Co.62a5, Ch.419b28
dharmatāyuktiḥ katamā / kena kāraṇena tathābhūtā ete skandhāḥ, tathābhūto lokasaṃniveśaḥ / kena kāraṇena kharalakṣaṇā pṛthivī dravalakṣaṇā āpa uṣṇalakṣaṇaṃ tejaḥ samudīraṇalakṣaṇo vāyuḥ / kena kāraṇenānityāḥ skandhāḥ kena kāraṇena śāntaṃ nirvāṇam iti / tathā kena kāraṇena rūpaṇalakṣanaṃ rūpam, anubhavanalakṣaṇā vedanā, saṃjānanālakṣaṇā saṃjñā, abhisaṃskaraṇalakṣaṇāḥ saṃskārāḥ, vijānanālakṣaṇaṃ vijñānam iti / prakṛtir eṣāṃ dharmāṇām iyam, svabhāva eṣa īdṛśaḥ, dharmataiṣā / yaiva cāsau dharmatā saivātra yuktir yoga upāyaḥ / evaṃ vaitat syāt, anyathā vā, naiva vā syāt, sarvatraiva ca dharmataiva pratisaraṇaṃ dharmataiva yuktiḥ / cittanidhyāpanāya cittasaṃjñāpanāya / iyam ucyate dharmatāyuktiḥ /
body.translated_text: What is the reasoning of the nature of things (<s>dharmatāyukti</s>)? The very nature of things — that form is of such nature, feeling is of such nature, and likewise for the other aggregates — [the fact that their nature is simply thus and not otherwise] — this established nature of things is called the reasoning of the nature of things.

body.text: evaṃ catasṛbhir yuktibhiḥ skandhadeśanopaparīkṣyate yāvat punar anyā kācid deśaneti //
body.translated_text: Thus by these four types of reasoning, the teaching of the aggregates is investigated, and indeed whatever other teachings [are likewise investigated]. //

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-10-b-(3) Ms.60b2M, Sh.143-18, P.69a4, D.58b1, N.61a4, Co.62b3, Ch.419c10
yaivam ābhyāṃ dvābhyām ākārābhyāṃ gaṇanāsaṃkhyākārayā ca yuktyupaparīkṣaṇākārayā ca samyagupanidhyāpanā tasyās tasyā deśanāyāḥ sā cintā //
body.translated_text: One who thus reflects on the teaching of the true <s>Dharma</s> through these two modes of reflection — the mode of counting-enumeration and the mode of reasoning-investigation — develops the understanding born of reflection (<s>cintāmayī prajñā</s>), and on the basis of that, the understanding born of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmayī prajñā</s>). //

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-10-c Ms.60b3L, Sh.143-21, P.69a5, D.58b2, N.61a5, Co.62b4, Ch.419c14
iyam ucyate saddharmaśravaṇacintā//
body.translated_text: This is called the reflection on the true <s>Dharma</s> (<s>saddharma</s>). //

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-11-a Ms.60b3L, Sh.144-1, W.*80-12, P.69a6, D.58b2, N.61a5, Co.62b4, Ch.419c15
anantarāyaḥ katamaḥ / anantarāyo dvividhaḥ / adhyātmam upādāya bahirdhā ca / tatrādhyātmaṃ bahirdhā copādāyāntarāyaṃ vakṣyati / tadviparyayeṇānantarāyo veditavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is the obstacle (<s>antarāya</s>)? The obstacles are twofold: those arising from internal [factors] and those arising from external [factors].

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-11-a-(1) Ms.60b3M, Sh.144-5, P.69a7, D.58b3, N.61a6, Co.62b5, Ch.419c17
adhyātmam upādāyāntarāyaḥ katamaḥ / yathāpīhaikatyaḥ pūrvam eva kṛtapuṇyo na bhavati / so 'kṛtatvāt puṇyānāṃ na lābhī bhavati kālena kālam ānulomikānāṃ jīvitapariṣkārāṇām, yaduta cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇām / tīvrarāgo bhavaty āyatarāgaḥ, tīvradveṣa āyatadveṣaḥ, tīvramoha āyatamohaḥ / pūrvaṃ vānenābādhasaṃvartanīyāni karmāṇi kṛtāni bhavanti / yaddhetor ābādhabahulo bhavati / dṛṣṭa eva dharme viṣamacārī bhavati / yenāsyābhīkṣṇaṃ vāto vā kupyati pittaṃ vā śleṣmaṃ vā, viṣūcikā vā kāye saṃtiṣṭhate / bhojanaguruko bhavati bahvartho bahukṛtyo gaṇasaṃnipātabahulo bhavati / karmārāmo vā bhāṣyārāmo vā nidrārāmaḥ saṅgaṇikārāmaḥ saṃsargārāmaḥ prapañcārāmaḥ / ātmasaṃpragrāhakaś capalaḥ pramattaḥ kudeśavāsī vā / ity evaṃbhāgīyā antarāyā adhyātmam upādāya veditavyāḥ //
body.translated_text: What are the obstacles arising from internal [factors]? Illness, mental disturbance, lack of faith, laziness, indulgence in sense pleasures, wrong view, not taking delight in the true <s>Dharma</s>, and lack of progress even after entering the true <s>Dharma</s> — these are obstacles arising from internal factors. [Explained in detail:] when one is afflicted with illness, suffering, and severe sickness, one cannot apply oneself to practice.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-11-a-(2) Ms.60b6M, Sh.144-21, P.69b5, D.58b7, N.61b3, Co.63a2, Ch.419c29
bahirdhopādāyāntarāyāḥ katame / yathāpi tad asatpuruṣāpāśrayaḥ, yato na labhate kālena kālam ānulomikīm avavādānuśāsanīṃ, kudeśe vā vasati / yatrāsya vāsaṃ kalpayato divā vauvilako bhavati prabhūtaḥ, rātrau voccaśabdo mahāśabdo mahājanakāyasya nirghosaḥ / tīvrakaṭukaś ca vātātapasaṃsparśo manuṣyād amanuṣyād api bhayam / ayam evaṃbhāgīyo bahirdhopādāyāntarāyo veditavyaḥ / ayaṃ tāvad vistaravibhāgaḥ //
body.translated_text: What are the obstacles arising from external [factors]? Involvement with householders, involvement with work and duties, involvement with travel, the arising of dangers such as famine, the arising of fear from robbers and enemies, not obtaining the requisites — robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicines — these are obstacles arising from external factors.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-11-b Ms.60b7M, Sh.145-8, W/80-14, P.69b8, D.59a3, N.61b6, C0.63a4, Ch.420a7
samāsārthaḥ punaḥ katamaḥ / samāsatas trividho 'ntarāyaḥ / prayogāntarāyaḥ prāvivekyāntarāyaḥ pratisaṃlayanāntarāyaś ca /
body.translated_text: What is the summary meaning? The obstacles are threefold: the obstacle to practice (<s>prayogāntarāya</s>), the obstacle to seclusion (<s>prāvivekyāntarāya</s>), and the obstacle to meditative retreat (<s>pratisaṃlayanāntarāya</s>).

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-11-b-(1) Ms.61a1L, Sh.145-11, P.70a1, D.59a3, N.61b6, Co.63a5, Ch.420a9
tatra prayogāntarāyaḥ katamaḥ / yenāntarāyeṇa samavahitena saṃmukhībhūtenāśakto bhavaty apratibalaḥ sarveṇa sarvaṃ kuśalapakṣaprayoge /
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the obstacle to practice?

body.text: sa punaḥ katamaḥ / yad ābādhako bhavati duḥkhito bāḍhaglānaḥ / (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 248

children.text: ) abhīkṣṇam asya vāto vā kupyate pittaṃ va śleṣmaṃ vā viṣūcikā vāsya kāye saṃtiṣṭhate / api tv asya daśaty ahir vṛściko vā śatapadī vā manuṣyo vainaṃ viheṭhayaty amanuṣyo vā / na ca lābhī bhavati cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇām / ayam evaṃbhāgīyaḥ prayogāntarāyo veditavyaḥ //
children.translated_text: ) Frequently, wind (<s>vāta</s>) becomes disturbed for him, or bile (<s>pitta</s>), or phlegm (<s>śleṣman</s>), or cholera establishes itself in his body. Moreover, various bodily ailments arise for him, and he has no access to medicine, or no strength to endure [the treatment].

body.translated_text: It is this: when one is afflicted, suffering, severely ill.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-11-b-(2) Ms.61a2M, Sh.145-21, P.70a5, D.59a6, N.62a1, Co.63b1, Ch.420a16
prāvivekyāntarāyaḥ katamaḥ / yad bhojanaguruko bhavati / bahvartho bahukṛtyo bahukaraṇīyaḥ karmārāmaratiṃ rato bhavati / teṣu teṣv itikaraṇīyeṣu prasṛtamānasaḥ / bhāṣyārāmo bhavati / śaktaḥ pratibalaḥ san prāvivekye prahāṇe pratisaṃlayane bhāvanāyām uddeśasvādhyāyamātrakeṇa saṃtuṣṭaḥ / nidrārāmo bhavati / styānamiddhaparyavasthitaḥ kusīdajātīyo nidrāsukhaṃ pārśvasukhaṃ śayanasukhaṃ ca svīkaroti / saṅgaṇikārāmo bhavati / sārdhaṃ gṛhasthapravrajitai rājakathāṃ vā karoti, corakathāṃ vānnakathāṃ vā pānakathāṃ vā vastrakathāṃ vā veśyākathāṃ vā vīthīkathāṃ vā janapadamahāmātrākhyānakathāṃ vā lokākhyānakathāṃ vā samudrākhyānakathāṃ vā / ity evaṃbhāgīyayānarthopasaṃhitayā kathayā kālam atināmayati /
body.translated_text: What is the obstacle to seclusion (<s>prāvivekyāntarāya</s>)? When one has gone forth and dwells in the forest or in secluded places, yet

body.text: tatra cābhirato bhavaty abhīkṣṇañ ca gaṇasaṃnipātabahulo bhavati / teṣu teṣv adhikaraṇeṣu vyākṣiptamānaso bhavati vyākulamānasaḥ / (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 250

children.text: ) saṃsargārāmo bhavati / gṛhasthapravrajitānām asamavahitānāṃ ca [mthoṅ bar 'dod ciṅ / phrad pa rnams daṅ 'bral bar mi 'dod pa daṅ] / prapañcārāmo bhavati / prapañcarato 'vakramaṇīyeṣu pūrvaṃgamaḥ prāvivekyeṣu nikṣiptadhuraḥ / ima evaṃbhāgīyā dharmāḥ pravivekāntarāyo veditavyaḥ / yaiḥ samavahitaiḥ saṃmukhībhūtair na sukaraṃ bhavaty araṇyavanaprasthāni prāntāni śayanāsanāny adhyāvasitum, araṇyāni vā vṛkṣamūlāni vā śūnyāgārāṇi vā //
children.translated_text: ) one becomes fond of social contact; [one desires to see and meet with householders, the ordained, and the inattentive ones —

body.translated_text: one takes delight therein and frequently becomes involved in assemblies. In those various matters, one's mind becomes distracted,

body.text:
(I)-C-III-11-b-(3) Ms.61a6M, Sh.147-2, P.70b6, D.59b5, N.62b2, Co.63b7, Ch.420b5
pratisaṃlayanāntarāyaḥ katamaḥ / tadyathā pratisaṃlayanam ucyate śamatho vipaśyanā ca / tatrāsti śamathāntarāyaḥ, asti vipaśyanāntarāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is the obstacle to meditative retreat (<s>pratisaṃlayanāntarāya</s>)? When one who has entered retreat becomes distracted by various obstacles — concerns about clothing, food, shelter, and other requisites — and is unable to maintain continuous and uninterrupted practice.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-11-b-(3)-i Ms.61b1L, Sh.147-4, P.70b7, D.59b6, N.62b2, Co.64a1, Ch.420b7
tatra śamathāntarāyaḥ katamaḥ / pramādo 'deśavāsaś ca / yathāsya pramattasya styānamiddhaṃ vā cittaṃ paryavanahati, śamathamātraṃ vāsvādayati, līnatvāya vā cittam upanāmayati, andhakārāyitatvaṃ vā cetaso bhavati / yadrūpeṇa cādeśavāsena manuṣyakṛto vāmanuṣyakṛto vā parataḥ saṃghaṭṭo bhavati / yenāsya cittaṃ bahirdhā vikṣipyate / ayaṃ śamathāntarāyaḥ pratisaṃlayanāntarāyo veditavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the obstacle to <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding)? Heedlessness and dwelling in an unfavorable place. Just as for the heedless one, sloth-and-torpor overwhelms the mind, or one merely savors the taste of calm, or one inclines the mind toward laxity, or there is a state of darkness in the mind. And by dwelling in an unfavorable place, there arises disturbance from others — whether caused by humans or non-humans — by which one's mind is scattered outwardly. This obstacle to <s>śamatha</s> should be understood as the obstacle to seclusion.

body.text: (I)-C-IIl-11-b-(3)-ii Ms.61b2L, Sh.147-12, P.71a2, D.60a1, N.62b5, Co.64a4, Ch.420b13 vipaśyanāntarāyaḥ katamaḥ / yadutātmasaṃpragrāhaś cāpalyaṃ ca //
body.translated_text: What is the obstacle to <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight)? Namely, self-aggrandizement and restlessness.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-11-b-(3)-ii-(a) Ms.61b2M, Sh.147-14, P.71a2, D.60a1, N.62b5, Co.64a4, Ch.420b14
tatrātmasaṃpragraho yathāpi tad "aham asty uccakulaḥ pravrajito 'līnaḥ, anye ca bhikṣavo na tathe"ty ātmānam utkarṣayati saṃpragṛhṇāti, parāṃś ca paṃsayati / evam "ādhyakulapravrajito 'dīnaḥ", evam "abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ", evaṃ "bahuśrutaḥ śrutādhāraḥ śrutasaṃnicayaḥ", evam "aham asmi kalyāṇavākyo vākkaraṇenopetaḥ, anye ca bhikṣavo na tathe"ty ātmānam utkarṣayati saṃpragṛhṇāti, parāṃś ca paṃsayati /
body.translated_text: Therein, self-aggrandizement is as follows: 'I am one gone forth from a high family, I am not lax, while other <s>bhikṣus</s> are not like that' — thus one exalts oneself, grasps at oneself, and disparages others. Likewise: 'I am one gone forth from a wealthy family, not impoverished'; likewise: 'I am handsome, good-looking, inspiring confidence'; likewise: 'I am learned, a bearer of what has been heard, one who has accumulated learning'; likewise: 'I am one of fine speech, endowed with eloquence, while other <s>bhikṣus</s> are not like that' — thus one exalts oneself, grasps at oneself, and disparages others.

body.text: sa ātmānaṃ saṃpragṛhṇān ye te bhavanti bhikṣavaḥ sthavirā rātrijñā abhyavacīrṇabrahmacaryās tān na kālena kālaṃ paripṛcchati paripraśnī karoti / te cāsya na kālena kālam avivṛtāni ca sthānāni vivṛṇvanti, vivṛtāni ca sthānāny uttānīkurvanti, na ca gambhīram arthapadaṃ sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca prajñayā pratividhya saṃprakāśayanti yāvad eva jñānadarśanasya viśuddhaye / evamasya sa ātmasaṃpragraha āntarāyiko bhavati yaduta vipaśyanāyāḥ /
body.translated_text: One who grasps at oneself in this way does not from time to time approach and question those <s>bhikṣus</s> who are elders, who know the [watches of the] night, who have practiced the holy life extensively. And those [elders] do not from time to time open up for him what is unopened, make clear what is opened, or illuminate well and thoroughly with wisdom a profound matter of meaning, for the sake of the purification of knowledge and vision. Thus his self-aggrandizement becomes an obstacle, namely to <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight).

body.text: punar aparam alpamātrakasyāvaramātrakasya jñānadarśanamātrakasya sparśavihāramātrakasya lābhī bhavati / sa tena jñānamātrakeṇa darśanamātrakeṇa (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> I 254

children.text: ) sparśavihāramātrakeṇātmānam utkarṣayati saṃpragṛhṇāti / sa ātmānaṃ saṃpragṛhṇaṃs tāvatā saṃtuṣṭo bhavati, nottari vyāyacchate / evam asyāntarāyaḥ kṛto bhavaty ātmasaṃpragraheṇa yaduta vipaśyanāyāḥ //
children.translated_text: that mere contact-dwelling, one exalts oneself and grasps at oneself. One who thus grasps at oneself becomes satisfied with just that much and does not strive further. Thus an obstacle has been created for him by self-aggrandizement, namely to <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight).

body.translated_text: Furthermore, one obtains only a small measure, a lesser measure of knowledge and vision, a mere contact-dwelling. With that mere knowledge, that mere vision,

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-11-b-(3)-ii-(b) Ms.61b6M, Sh.148-13, P.71b3, D.60b1, N.63a5, Co.64b4, Ch.420b29
capalo vā punar anupaśāntendriyo bhavaty uddhatendriya unnatendriyaḥ / sa dūṣitacittī bhavati durbhāṣitabhāṣī duṣkṛtakarmakārī, na sthiraṃ dharmāṃś cintayati, na dṛḍhaṃ cintayati / yena vipaśyanāṃ na pūrayati na viśodhayati / evam asya cāpalyam antarāyo bhavati yaduta vipaśyanāyā iti //
body.translated_text: Or again, the restless one is one of unquiet faculties, of agitated faculties, of excited faculties. Such a one is of corrupted intention, a speaker of ill speech, a doer of wrongful deeds; one does not reflect on <s>dharmas</s> steadily, does not reflect firmly. Whereby one does not fulfill or purify <s>vipaśyanā</s>. Thus one's restlessness becomes an obstacle, namely to <s>vipaśyanā</s>.

body.text: (I)-C-IIl-11-b-(3)-iii Ms.62a1M, Sh.148-20, W.*80-19, P.71b6, D.60b3, N.63a7, Co.64b6, Ch.420c5 dvau dharmau śamathāntarāyau / yaduta pramādo 'deśavāsaś ca / dvau dharmau vipaśyanāntarāyau / yadutātmasaṃpragrahaś cāpalyam ca /
body.translated_text: Two <s>dharmas</s> are obstacles to <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding): namely, heedlessness and dwelling in an unfavorable place. Two <s>dharmas</s> are obstacles to <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight): namely, self-aggrandizement and restlessness.

body.text: iti yaś ca śamathāntarāyaḥ / yaś ca vipaśyanāntarāyaḥ / ayam ucyate pratisaṃlayanāntarāyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus, both the obstacle to <s>śamatha</s> and the obstacle to <s>vipaśyanā</s> — this is called the obstacle to seclusion.

body.text: ayaṃ ca punar antarāyasya samāsārtha iti //
body.translated_text: And this is the summary meaning of the obstacle.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-11-c Ms.62a2L, Sh.149-2, P.71b8, D.60b4, N.63b1, Co.64b7, Ch.420c9
yaś cāyaṃ samāsārtho yaś ca pūrvako vistaravibhāgas tad ekadhyam abhisaṃkṣipyāntarāya ity ucyate / asya cāntarāyasya viparyayeṇānantarāyo (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> I 256

children.text: ) veditavya iti / ya eṣām antarāyāṇām abhāvo vigamo 'saṅgatir asamavadhanam / ayam ucyate 'nantarāyaḥ //
children.translated_text: should be understood. That which is the absence, the removal, the non-occurrence, the non-conjunction of these obstacles — this is called 'absence of obstacle.'

body.translated_text: Both this summary meaning and the previous detailed analysis — taken together, they are called 'obstacle.' And by the reverse of this obstacle, the absence of obstacle

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-12-a Ms.62a3L, Sh.149-8, W.*80-30, P.72a2, D.60b5, N.63b3, Co.65a1, Ch.420c11
tyāgaḥ katamaḥ / yad dānam anavadyaṃ cittālaṃkārārthaṃ cittapariṣkārārthaṃ yogasaṃbhārārtham uttamārthasya prāptaye dadāti /
body.translated_text: What is generosity (<s>tyāga</s>)? That blameless giving, for the purpose of adorning the mind, for the purpose of purifying the mind, for the purpose of the equipment of the practice, one gives for the attainment of the supreme goal.

body.text: tatra ko dadāti / kutra dadāti / kiṃ dadāti / kena dadāti / kathaṃ dadāti / kasmād dadāti / yenāsya dānam anavadyaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: Therein: who gives? Where does one give? What does one give? By what does one give? How does one give? Why does one give? — by which one's giving becomes blameless.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-12-a-(1) Ms.62a3L, Sh.151-1, P.72a4, D.60b7, N.63b4, Co.65a3, Ch.420c16
āha / dātā dānapatir dadāti / tatra katamo dātā katamo dānapatiḥ / yaḥ svair eva pāṇibhir dadāti, ayam ucyate dātā / yasya svakaṃ dīyate tac ca dātukāmasya nādātukāmasya, ayam ucyate dānapatiḥ //
body.translated_text: He says: the giver, the lord of giving, gives. Therein, who is the giver and who is the lord of giving? One who gives with one's own hands — this one is called the giver. One whose own [property] is given, and who wishes to give, not one who does not wish to give — this one is called the lord of giving.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-12-a-(2) Ms.62a3L, Sh.151-5, W.*81-4, P.72a5, D.61a1, N.63b6, Co.65a4, Ch.420c18
tatra kutra dadāti / āha / caturṣu dadāti / duḥkhitāya, wpakāriṇe, iṣṭāya, viśiṣṭāya ca /
body.translated_text: Therein, to whom does one give? He says: one gives to four [kinds of recipients]: to the suffering, to the benefactor, to the beloved, and to the distinguished.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-12-a-(2)-i Ms.62a4R, Sh.151-7, P.72a6, D.61a2, N.63b6, Co.65a5, Ch.420c19
tatra duḥkhitāyeti / kṛpaṇā vā, vanīyakā vā, adhvagā vā, yācanakā (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> I 258

children.text: ) vā, andhā va, badhirā vā, anāthā vā, apratisaraṇā vā, upakaraṇavikalā iti / ye vā punar anye 'py evaṃbhāgīyāḥ / ima ucyante duḥkhitāḥ //
children.translated_text: or the blind, or the deaf, or the orphaned, or the unprotected, or those lacking requisites — and whoever else is of this kind. These are called 'the suffering.'

body.translated_text: Therein, 'to the suffering' means: the destitute, or travelers, or wayfarers, or beggars,

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-12-a-(2)-ii Ms.62a4R, Sh.151-11, P.72a8, D.61a3, N.64a1, Co.65a6, Ch.420c23
upakāriṇaḥ katame / tadyathā mātāpitaram, āpāyakaṃ, poṣakam, saṃvardhakam iti / ye vā punar aṭavīkāntarād uttārayanti, durbhikṣād vā, paracakrabhayād vā, bandhanād vā, ābādhād vā / hitopadeśakāś cāsya bhavanti, sukhopadeśakā hitasukhopasaṃhārakāḥ, utpannotpanneṣu cādhikaraṇeṣu sahāyakāḥ sahanandinaḥ sahaśokāḥ, āpatsu cainaṃ na parityajantīti / ye vā punar anye 'py evaṃbhāgīyāḥ / ima ucyanta upakāriṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: Who are the benefactors? Such as: mother and father, nurse, nourisher, and rearer; or those who rescue one from a wilderness, or from a famine, or from danger of invading armies, or from bondage, or from illness; and those who counsel one for one's welfare and happiness, who are concerned with one's welfare and happiness, who are companions in arising circumstances, who rejoice and grieve together, and who do not abandon one in misfortune — and whoever else is of this kind. These are called 'the benefactors.'

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-12-a-(2)-iii Ms.62a6R, Sh.151-19, P.72b4, D.61a5, N.64a3, Co.65b1, Ch.421a1
iṣṭāḥ katame / ye saṃstutāḥ, yeṣām asyāntike bhavati prema vā gauravaṃ vā / bhaktivādo vā alaptakāḥ saṃstutakāḥ sapriyakāś ca bhavantīti / ye vā punar anye 'py evaṃbhāgīyāḥ / ima ucyanta iṣṭāḥ //
body.translated_text: Who are the beloved? Those with whom one is familiar, toward whom one has affection or reverence; those who are devoted, who are intimate, familiar, and dear — and whoever else is of this kind. These are called 'the beloved.'

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-12-a-(2)-iv Ms.62a7M, Sh.151-23, P.72b5, D.61a7, N.64a4, Co.65b2, Ch.421a4
viśiṣṭāḥ katame / te śramaṇabrāhmaṇāḥ {MS śravaṇa-}, sādhurūpa saṃmatāḥ, avyābādhyāḥ, avyābādhyaratāḥ, vigatarāgāḥ, rāgavinayāya pratipannāḥ, vigatadveṣāḥ, dveṣavinayāya pratipannāḥ, vigatamohāḥ, mohavinayāya pratipannā iti / ye vā punar anye 'py evaṃbhāgīyāḥ ima ucyante viśiṣṭāḥ //
body.translated_text: Who are the distinguished? Those <s>śramaṇas</s> (ascetics) and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> (priests) who are regarded as virtuous, who are non-injurious, who delight in non-injury, who are free from passion or who are practicing for the discipline of passion, who are free from aversion or who are practicing for the discipline of aversion, who are free from delusion or who are practicing for the discipline of delusion — and whoever else is of this kind. These are called 'the distinguished.'

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-12-a-(3) Ms.62b1L, Sh.152-6, W.*81-10, P.72b8, D.61b1, N.64a6, Co.65b4, Ch.421a9
tatra kiṃ dadātīty āha / samāsataḥ sattvasaṃkhyātam asattvasaṃkhyātaṃ ca vastu dadāti /
body.translated_text: Therein, what does one give? He says: in brief, one gives material things classified as sentient-being-counted and non-sentient-being-counted.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-12-a-(3)-i Ms.62b1M, Sh.152-8, P.72b8, D.61b2, N.64a7, Co.65b5, Ch.421a11
tatra sattvasaṃkhyātaṃ vastu katamat / tadyathā putradāraṃ dāsīdāsakarmakarapauruṣeyaṃ hastyaśvagaveḍakakukkuṭastrīpuruṣadārakadārikam iti / yad vā punar anyad apy evaṃbhāgīyaṃ vastu / adhyātmaṃ vā punar upādāya karacaraṇaśiromāṃsarudhiravasādīny anuprayacchati / idam api sattvasaṃkhyātaṃ dānaṃ yatra bodhisattvabodhāḥ saṃdṛśyante / asmiṃs tv arthe nedaṃ dānam abhipretam / yeṣu tu sattveṣv asyaiśvaryaṃ bhavati, vaśitā ca prabhaviṣṇutā ca, arhati ca tān sattvān pareṣāṃ pratipādayitum / pratipādayaṃś cātmānam anavadyaṃ karoti / na taddhetos tatpratyayaṃ pare manāṃsi pradūṣayanti / ye ca sattvāḥ pareṣu pratipāditās te na vyāpāditā bhavanti /
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the material thing classified as sentient-being-counted? Such as: sons, wives, female and male servants, workers, and employees; elephants, horses, cattle, goats, roosters, women, men, boys, and girls — and whatever other material thing is of this kind. Or further, with regard to one's own body, one gives up hands, feet, head, flesh, blood, fat, and so forth. This too is giving classified as sentient-being-counted, where the awakenings of <s>bodhisattvas</s> are seen. But in this context, such giving is not intended. Rather, with regard to those sentient beings over whom one has mastery, authority, and power, one is entitled to hand over those beings to others. And in handing them over, one makes oneself blameless. Others do not corrupt their minds on account of that cause and condition. And those beings handed over to others are not harmed.

body.text: idam ucyate navadyam sattvasaṃkhyātavastudānam //
body.translated_text: This is called blameless giving of material things classified as sentient-being-counted.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-12-a-(3)-ii Ms.62b3R, Sh.152-21, P.73a6, D.61b6, N.64b4, Co.66a2, Ch.421a21
asattvasaṃkhyātaṃ vastu katamat / tadyathā dhanavastu dhānyavastu deśavastu //
body.translated_text: What is the material thing classified as non-sentient-being-counted? Such as: wealth, grain, and property.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-12-a-(3)-ii-(a) Ms.62b4L, Sh.153-2, P.73a6, D.61b6, N.64b4, Co.66a2, Ch.421a23
tatra dhanavastu katamat / tadyathā maṇimuktāvaidūryaśaṃkhaśilāpravāḍāśmagarbhamusāragalvajātarūparajatalohitikādakṣiṇāvartam iti / yad vā punar anyad apy evaṃbhāgīyaṃ ratnaṃ vā hiraṇyaṃ vā rūpyaṃ vā vastraṃ vā bhāṇḍopaskaraṃ vā gandhajātaṃ vā mālyajātaṃ vā / idam ucyate dhanavastus //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is wealth? Such as: gems, pearls, <s>vaidūrya</s> (beryl), conch shells, crystal, coral, cat's eye, <s>musāragalva</s> (a type of coral), gold, silver, <s>lohitikā</s> (red gem), and right-spiraling [conch] — and whatever other kind of jewel, or gold, or silver, or cloth, or household goods and utensils, or fragrant substances, or garlands. This is called wealth.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-12-a-(3)-ii-(b) Ms.62b5L, Sh.153-8, P.73b1, D.62a1, N.64b6, Co. 66a4, Ch.421a27
dhānyaṃ katamat / yat kiṃcid bhojyaṃ vā peyaṃ vā / tadyathā yavā vā, śālir vā, godhūmā vā, kolā vā, kulatthā vā, tilā vā, māṣā vā, ikṣuraso vā, [dar ba daṅ,] mṛdvīkāraso veti / yad vā punar anyad 9) apy evaṃbhāgīyam / idam ucyate dhānyam //
body.translated_text: What is grain? Whatever is edible or drinkable: such as barley, rice, wheat, jujubes, horse-gram, sesame, black gram, sugarcane juice, [<s>darba</s> grass,] and grape juice — and whatever else is of this kind. This is called grain.

body.text:
(I)-C-III-12-a-(3)-ii-(c) Ms.62b6L, Sh. 153-13, P.73b2, D.62a2, N.64b7, Co.66a5, Ch.421 b1
deśavastu katamat / tadyathā kṣetravastu, gṛhavastu, āpaṇavastu, puṇyaśālāvihārapratiṣṭhāpanam iti / yad vā punar anyad apy evaṃbhāgīyam / idam ucyate deśavastu /
body.translated_text: What is property? Such as: field property, house property, shop property, and the establishment of merit-halls and monasteries — and whatever else is of this kind. This is called property.

body.text: tatra yac ca sattvāsattvasaṃkhyātaṃ vastu, idaṃ dadātīti //
body.translated_text: Therein, whatever material thing is classified as sentient-being-counted and non-sentient-being-counted — this is what one gives.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-12-a-(4) Ms.62b6R, Sh.153-18, P.73b4, D.62a4, N.65a2, Co.66a7, Ch.421b5
kena dadātīti / yā cālobhasahagatā cetanā cittābhisaṃskāro manaskarma / yac ca tatsamutthāpitaṃ kāyakarma vākkarma deyavastuparityāgāya svasantāne vā parasantāne vā / anena dadāti //
body.translated_text: By what does one give? By the volition (<s>cetanā</s>) accompanied by non-greed, which is a mental formation, a mental action; and by the bodily action and verbal action produced thereby, for the relinquishment of the thing to be given, whether in one's own continuum or in another's continuum. By this one gives.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-12-a-(5) Ms.62b7R, Sh.154-1, P.73b6, D.62a5, N.65a3, Co.66b1, Ch.421b7
tatra kathaṃ dadātīti / śraddhayā dadāti / āgamadṛṣṭiḥ phaladarśī (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> I 266

children.text: ) satkṛtya dadāti / praṇatacittaḥ svahastaṃ dadāty anapaviddham / kālena dadāti yathaitat pareṣām upayogyaṃ syāt / parān anupahatya dadāti / dharmeṇa samayenāsāhasena samudānayitvā śuci dadāti / praṇītaṃ kalpikaṃ dadāti / yena na pare sāvadyā bhavanti, nātmā / abhīkṣṇaṃ dadāti / vinīya mātsaryamalaṃ saṃnidhimalaṃ ca dānaṃ dadāti / pūrvam eva dānāt sumanā dadaṃś cittaṃ prasādayati dattvā cāvipratisārī bhavati / evaṃ dadāti //
children.translated_text: ) one gives with respect; with a humble mind one gives with one's own hand, unimpaired; one gives at the proper time so that it may be useful to others; one gives without harming others; having gathered [wealth] righteously, by proper agreement, and without violence, one gives what is pure; one gives what is excellent and proper — that by which neither others nor oneself become blameworthy; one gives repeatedly; having removed the stain of jealousy and the stain of hoarding, one gives the gift; even before giving, one is well-pleased, clarifies the mind while giving, and after giving is without regret. Thus one gives.

body.translated_text: Therein, how does one give? One gives with faith (<s>śraddhā</s>). With a view based on tradition, seeing the fruit,

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-12-a-(6) Ms.63a2L, Sh.154-11, W.*81-16, P.74a3, D.62b1, N.65a7, Co.66b4, Ch.421b17
kasmād dadāti / āha / kāruṇyād vā dadāti yaduta duḥkhiteṣu / kṛtajñatayā dadāti yadutopakāriṣu / premṇā gauraveṇa bhaktyā dadāti yaduteṣṭeṣu / Iaukikalokottaraviśeṣaprārthanayā dadāti yaduta viśiṣṭeṣu / tasmād dadātīty ucyate //
body.translated_text: Why does one give? It is said: Out of compassion one gives — namely, to those in suffering. Out of gratitude one gives — namely, to benefactors. Out of love, respect, and devotion one gives — namely, to those who are dear. With the aspiration for worldly and supramundane distinction one gives — namely, to those who are distinguished. Therefore it is said: 'One gives.'

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-12-b Ms.63a3L, Sh.154-16, P.74a5, D.62b3, N.65b1, Co.66b6, Ch.421b21
ebhir ākārair ato 'sya gṛhiṇo vā pravrajitasya vā cittālaṃkārārthaṃ cittapariṣkārārthaṃ yogasaṃbhārārtham uttamārthasya prāptaye tad dānam, anavadyaṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text: By these aspects, that gift of a householder or of one gone forth, for the purpose of adorning the mind, for the purpose of purifying the mind, for the purpose of accumulating the equipment of yoga, for the attainment of the highest goal — that gift becomes blameless.

body.text: ayam ucyate tyāgaḥ //
body.translated_text: This is called generosity.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-13-a Ms. 63aM3,Sh. 155-1, W.*81-26, P.74a7, D.62b4,N.65b3,Co.66b7,Ch.421b25
śramaṇālaṃkāraḥ katamaḥ / tadyathaikatyaḥ śrāddho bhavati, aśaṭhaḥ, alpābādhaḥ, ārabdhavīryajātīyaḥ, prājñaḥ, alpecchaḥ, saṃtuṣṭaḥ, supoṣaḥ, subharaḥ, dhutaguṇasamanvāgataḥ, prāsādikaḥ, mātrajñaḥ, satpuruṣadharmasamanvāgataḥ, paṇḍitaliṅgasamanvāgataḥ, kṣamaḥ, sūrataḥ, peśalaś ca bhavati //
body.translated_text: What is the ornament of the ascetic? Namely: a certain one is faithful, non-deceitful, of few illnesses, of the type that has aroused energy, wise, of few desires, contented, easy to nurture, easy to support, endowed with the ascetic qualities, inspiring confidence, knowing the proper measure, endowed with the qualities of a good person, endowed with the marks of a wise person, patient, gentle, and skillful.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-13-a-(1) Ms.63aM4,Sh. 155-8, P.74b1, D.62b5, N.65b4, Co.67a2, Ch.421c5
kathaṃ śrāddho bhavati / prasādabahulo bhavati, avakalpanābahulaḥ, vimuktibahulaḥ, chandikaś ca kuśaleṣu dharmeṣu / sa śāstari prasīdati, na kāṅkṣati, na vicikitsati / śāstāraṃ satkaroti, gurukaroti, mānayati, pūjayati / satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvopaniśritya viharati / yathā śāstary evaṃ dharme sabrahmacāriṣu śikṣāyām avavādānuśāsanyāṃ pratisaṃstare 'pramāde samādhau / evaṃ śrāddho bhavati //
body.translated_text: How is one faithful? One is abundant in confidence, abundant in non-fabrication, abundant in liberation, and eager regarding wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. One has confidence in the Teacher, does not doubt, does not waver. One honors the Teacher, reveres, respects, and venerates him. Having honored, revered, respected, and venerated him, one dwells in dependence [on him]. Just as toward the Teacher, so too toward the <s>Dharma</s>, toward co-practitioners in the holy life, toward the training, toward instruction and admonition, toward hospitality, toward diligence, and toward <s>samādhi</s> (concentration). Thus one is faithful.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-13-a-(2) Ms.63a5R,Sh.155-16, P.74b5, D.63a1, N.65b7, Co.67a5, Ch.421c12
katham aśaṭho bhavati / ṛjuko bhavati, ṛjukajātīyaḥ / yathābhūtam ātmānam āviṣkartā bhavati, śāstur antike vijñānāṃ ca sabramacāriṇām / evam aśaṭho bhavati //
