body.translated_text: How is one non-deceitful? One is straightforward, of a straightforward nature. One is a revealer of oneself as one truly is — in the presence of the Teacher and of wise co-practitioners in the holy life. Thus one is non-deceitful.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-13-a-(3) Ms.63a6M,Sh. 156-3, P.74b6, D.63a2, N.66a1, Co.67a6, Ch.421c14
katham alpābādho bhavati / arogajātīyaḥ samayā pācanyā grahaṇyā samanvāgato bhavati, nātyuṣṇayā, nātiśītayā, avyābādhayā, ṛtusukhayā/ yayāsyāśitapītakhāditāsvāditāni samyak sukhena paripākaṃ gacchanti / evam alpābādho bhavati //
body.translated_text: How is one of few illnesses? One is of a healthy nature, endowed with a properly balanced digestion — neither too hot nor too cold, free from affliction, comfortable in the seasons — whereby what one eats, drinks, chews, and tastes is properly and comfortably digested. Thus one is of few illnesses.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-13-a-(4) Ms.63a7L,Sh. 156-8, P.74b8, D.63a3, N.66a2, Co.67a7, Ch.421c18
katham ārabdhavīryajātīyo bhavati / sthāmavān viharati, vīryavān, utsāhī, dṛḍhaparākramaḥ, anikṣiptadhuraḥ kuśaleṣu dharmeṣu / dakṣaś ca bhavati, analasaḥ, utthānasaṃpannaḥ / kartā bhavati vijñānāṃ sabrahmacāriṇāṃ kāyena vaiyāpṛtyam / evam ārabdhavīryajātīyo bhavati //
body.translated_text: How is one of the type that has aroused energy? One dwells with strength, energy, zeal, firm exertion, and without abandoning the burden regarding wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. One is skillful, not lazy, endowed with initiative; one bodily renders service to wise co-practitioners in the holy life. Thus one is of the type that has aroused energy.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-13-a-(5) Ms.63b1L,Sh.156-13, P.75a2, D.63a4, N.66a4, Co.67b2, Ch.421c22
kathaṃ prājño bhavati / medhāsmṛtibuddhisaṃpanno bhavati / adhandhendriyaḥ, amūḍhendriyaḥ, aneḍakaḥ, ahastasaṃvācikaḥ pratibalaḥ subhāṣitadurbhāṣitānāṃ dharmāṇām artham ājñātum iti / sahajayāpi buddhyā (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> I 272

children.text: ) samanvāgato bhavati / prāyogikayāpi buddhyā samanvāgato bhavati / evaṃ prājño bhavati //
children.translated_text: ) and one is also endowed with acquired wisdom. Thus one is wise.

body.translated_text: How is one wise? One is endowed with intelligence, memory, and wisdom; one's faculties are not dull, not confused; one is not mute, not one who communicates only by hand; one is capable of understanding the meaning of well-spoken and ill-spoken <s>dharmas</s>. One is endowed with innate wisdom,

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-13-a-(6) Ms.63b1R,Sh.156-19, P.75a4, D.63a6, N.66a6, Co.67b3, Ch.421c26
katham alpeccho bhavati / yāvadbhir guṇaiḥ samanvāgato bhavaty alpecchatām ādiṃ kṛtvā, taiḥ parato jñātuṃ na samanveṣate, kaścin me pare na jānīyuḥ, "alpeccha" iti vā, "evaṃguṇayukta" iti / evam alpeccho bhavati //
body.translated_text: How is one of few desires? Whatever qualities one is endowed with, beginning with having few desires — by those one does not seek to be known by others, [thinking:] "Let no one know me as 'one of few desires' or as 'endowed with such qualities.'" Thus one is of few desires.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-13-a-(7) Ms.63b2M,Sh. 157-1, P.75a6, D.63a7, N.66a7, Co.67b5, Ch.421c28
kathaṃ saṃtuṣṭo bhavati / itaretareṇa cīvarapiṇḍapātena śayanāsanena tuṣṭo bhavati, saṃtuṣṭaḥ / so 'labdhvā cīvaraṃ lūhaṃ vā praṇītaṃ vā notkaṇṭhati, na paritasyati / labdhvā ca punar araktaḥ paribhuṅkte 'sakta iti vistareṇa pūrvavat / yathā cīvaram evaṃ piṇḍapātaḥ śayanāsanam / evaṃ saṃtuṣṭo bhavati //
body.translated_text: How is one contented? One is satisfied and content with whatever robe and almsfood and lodging [comes one's way]. Not having obtained a robe, whether coarse or fine, one does not feel distress or anxiety. And having obtained it, one uses it without attachment, without clinging — and so on in detail as before. As with the robe, so too with almsfood and lodging. Thus one is contented.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-13-a-(8) Ms.63b3M,Sh. 157-7, P.75a8, D.63b2, N.66b2, Co.67b6, Ch.422a5
kathaṃ supoṣo bhavti / ātmāsyaikaḥ poṣyo bhavati / na tu pare, tadyathā dārakā vā manuṣyā veti, ye vā punar anye 'pi ke cid / yeṣām arthāya yān paryeṣṭim āpadyeta, pare cainaṃ dāyakadānapatayo duṣpoṣyam iti paśyeran / evaṃ supoṣo bhavati //
body.translated_text: How is one easy to nurture? Only oneself is to be nurtured — not others, such as children or [other] people, or anyone else on whose account one would undertake a search [for requisites], and others — the donors and patrons — would see one as difficult to nurture. Thus one is easy to nurture.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-13-a-(9) Ms.63b4L,Sh.157-12, P.75b2, D.63b3, N.66b3, Co.68a1, Ch.422a7
kathaṃ subharo bhavati / alpenāpi yāpayati / lūhenāpi yāpayati / evaṃ subharo bhavati //
body.translated_text: How is one easy to support? One manages even with little; one manages even with what is coarse. Thus one is easy to support.

body.text: (I)-C-IIl-13-a-(10) Ms.63b4M,Sh.157-14, W.* 82-1, P.75b3, D.63b3, N.66b4, Co.68a1, Ch.422a9 kathaṃ dhutaguṇasamanvāgato bhavati / prāptapiṇḍapātiko bhavati, sāvadānapiṇḍapātikaḥ / ekāsanikaḥ / khalupaścādbhaktikaḥ / traicīvarikaḥ / nāmatikaḥ / pāṃsukūlikaḥ / āraṇyakaḥ / vṛkṣamūlikaḥ / ābhyavakāśikaḥ / śmāśānikaḥ / naiṣadyikaḥ / )yāthāsaṃstarikaḥ / ta ete piṇḍapātaṃ cīvaraṃ śayanāsanam ārabhya dvādaśakā dhutaguṇā bhavanti trayodaśakā vā /
body.translated_text: How is one endowed with the ascetic qualities (<s>dhutaguṇa</s>)? One is a regular alms-gatherer, a careful alms-gatherer; one eats at a single sitting; one who eats only after all [food] has been received; one who uses only three robes; one who uses wool; one who uses rag-robes; one who dwells in the forest; one who dwells at the root of a tree; one who dwells in the open air; one who dwells in a charnel ground; one who sits [and does not lie down]; one who uses whatever bedding is available. These are the twelve or thirteen ascetic qualities pertaining to almsfood, robes, and lodging.

body.text: tatra piṇḍapātikatvaṃ bhidyamānaṃ dvidhā bhavati, prāptapiṇḍapātikaḥ sāvadānapiṇḍapātikaś ca //
body.translated_text: Therein, the practice of gathering alms, being divided, becomes twofold: the regular alms-gatherer and the careful alms-gatherer.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-13-a-(10)-i Ms.-,Sh. 158-7, P.75b5, D.63b6, N.66b6, Co.68a4, Ch.422a15
tatra prāptapiṇḍapātikaḥ katamaḥ / ['dris pa'i khyim dag nas] yathālabdhaṃ yathopasaṃpannaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuṅkte //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the regular alms-gatherer? One who eats whatever almsfood is obtained, whatever is available, from the families [one visits].

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-13-a-(10)-ii Ms.63b5R, Sh.158-7,W.*82-13,P.75b7,D.63b6, N.66b7,Co.68a4,Ch.422a 17
sāvadānapiṇḍapātikaḥ katamaḥ / veśmānuveśya kulāni bhikṣitvā paryaṭitvā yathālabdhaṃ yathopasaṃpannaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuṅkte / no tv uccaiḥ śuṇḍāṃ praṇidhāya kulāny upasaṃkrāmati / "ato 'haṃ lapsye praṇītaṃ khādanīyam bhojanīyaṃ yāvadāptam" /
body.translated_text: What is the careful alms-gatherer? One who, going from house to house, begs and wanders among the families, and eats whatever almsfood is obtained, whatever is available. But one does not approach families raising one's nose high [with expectation, thinking:] "From there I shall obtain excellent food and eatables to my fill."

body.text: tatra piṇḍapātikatvam aviśeṣeṇārabhya dvādaśa bhavanti prabhedaṃ punar ārabhya trayodaśa //
body.translated_text: Therein, taking the practice of alms-gathering without distinction, there are twelve; but taking their subdivisions, there are thirteen.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-13-a-(10)-iii Ms.63b6R, Sh.158-14, P.76a1, D.64a1, N.67a2, Co.68a6, Ch.422a21
tatraikāsanikatvaṃ katamat / ekasminn āsane niṣaṇṇo yāvat paribhoktavyaṃ tāvat paribhuṅkte / vyutthitaś ca punas tasmād āsanān na paribhuṅkte / idam ucyate ekāsanikatvam //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the practice of eating at a single sitting? Having sat down at one seat, one eats as much as is to be eaten. And having risen from that seat, one does not eat again. This is called the practice of eating at a single sitting.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-13-a-(10)-iv Ms.63b7M,Sh.158-18, P.76a2, D.64a2, N.67a3, Co.68a7, Ch.422a23
khalupaścādbhaktikatvaṃ katamat / bhojanārthaṃ niṣaṇṇas tāvan na paribhuṅkte, yāvat sarvabhojanaṃ pratīcchati, yāvatā jānāti śakṣyāmi yāpayitum / yataś ca punar jānīte "na me 'ta uttari bhojanena kṛtyaṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> I 278

children.text: ) bhaviṣyatī"ti, tataḥ sarvaṃ parigṛhyārabhate paribhoktum / evaṃ khalupaścādbhaktiko bhavati //
children.translated_text: ) beyond this" — then, having accepted everything, one begins to eat. Thus one practices eating only after all [food] has been received.

body.translated_text: What is the practice of eating only after all [food] has been received? Having sat down for the purpose of eating, one does not eat until one has accepted all the food — as much as one knows one will be able to manage with. And when one knows: "I shall have no further need for food

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-13-a-(10)-v Ms.64a1M,Sh.159-2, P.76a4, D.64a3, N.67a4, Co.68b1, Ch.422a28
kathaṃ traicīvariko bhavati / tribhiś ca cīvarair yāpayati, sāṃghāṭinā, uttarāsaṃgena, antarvāsena ca / trayāṇāṃ cīvarāṇām atirekam uttaraṃ na dhārayati / evaṃ traicīvariko bhavati //
body.translated_text: How does one practice wearing only three robes? One manages with three robes: the outer robe (<s>sāṃghāṭī</s>), the upper robe (<s>uttarāsaṃga</s>), and the inner garment (<s>antarvāsa</s>). One does not keep any additional robe beyond the three. Thus one practices wearing only three robes.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-13-a-(10)-vi Ms.64a1R,Sh.159-6, P.76a5, D.64a5, N.67a6, Co.68b2, Ch.422b2
kathaṃ nāmatiko bhavati / yat kiṃcic cīvaraṃ dhārayati tricīvaraṃ vā, atirekacīvaraṃ vā / sarvaṃ tad aurṇikaṃ dhārayati / na tv anyat / evaṃ nāmatikaṃ dhārayati //
body.translated_text: How does one practice using wool? Whatever robe one wears — whether the three robes or any additional robe — one wears it all made of wool, not of anything else. Thus one practices using wool.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-13-a-(10)-vii Ms.64a2M,Sh.159-10, P.76a6, D.64a5, N.67a6, Co.68b3, Ch.422b5
kathaṃ pāṃsukūliko bhavati / yac cīvaraṃ parair muktaṃ bhavaty ucchiṣṭaṃ choritaṃ rathyāyāṃ vā, vīthyāṃ vā, catvare vā, śrṅgāṭake vā, pathi vā, utpathe vā, uccārasaṃsṛṣṭaṃ vā prasrāvasaṃsṛṣṭaṃ vā, uccāraprasrāvapūyarudhirakheṭaprakṣitaṃ vā / tato yad aśuci tad apanīya, sāram ādāya, śodhayitvā sīvitvā vivarṇīkṛtya dhārayati / evaṃ pāṃsukūliko bhavati //
body.translated_text: How does one practice using rag-robes? Whatever robe has been discarded by others, abandoned, thrown away — on a road, or in a lane, or at a crossroads, or at a four-way intersection, or on a path, or off the path — soiled with excrement or urine, or smeared with excrement, urine, pus, blood, or phlegm — from that, having removed what is impure, taking the usable part, washing it, sewing it, and dyeing it, one wears it. Thus one practices using rag-robes.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-13-a-(10)-viii Ms.64a3M,Sh.159-17, P.76b1, D.64a6, N.67b1, Co.68b5, Ch.422b9
katham āraṇyako bhavati / araṇyavanaprasthāni prāntāni śayanāsanāny adhyāvasati, yāni vyavakṛṣṭāni grāmanigamānām / evam āraṇyako bhavati //
body.translated_text: How does one practice dwelling in the forest? One resorts to remote dwellings in forests and woodland plains, which are secluded from villages and market towns. Thus one practices dwelling in the forest.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-13-a-(10)-ix Ms.64a3R,Sh. 159-20, P.76b2, D.64a7, N.67b1, Co.68b6, Ch.422b12
kathaṃ vṛkṣamūliko bhavati / vṛkṣamūle vāsaṃ kalpayati vṛkṣamūlaṃ niśritya / evaṃ vṛksamūliko bhavati //
body.translated_text: How does one practice dwelling at the root of a tree? One arranges one's dwelling at the root of a tree, depending on the root of a tree. Thus one practices dwelling at the root of a tree.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-13-a-(10)-x Ms.64a[margin],Sh. 160-3, P.76b3, D.64b1, N.67b2, Co.68b6, Ch.422b14
katham ābhyavakāśiko bhavati / abhyavakāśe vāsaṃ kalpayati, anavacchanne vivṛte deśe / evam ābhyavakāśiko bhavati //
body.translated_text: How does one practice dwelling in the open air? One arranges one's dwelling in the open air, in an uncovered, exposed place. Thus one practices dwelling in the open air.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-13-a-(10)-xi Ms.64a[margin],Sh. 160-6, P.76b3, D.64b1, N.67b3, Co.68b7, Ch.422b15
kathaṃ śmāśāniko bhavati / śmaśāne vāsaṃ kalpayati, yatra mṛtamṛto janakāyo 'bhinirhriyate / evaṃ śmāśāniko bhavati //
body.translated_text: How does one practice dwelling in a charnel ground? One arranges one's dwelling in a charnel ground, where dead bodies of the deceased are carried out. Thus one practices dwelling in a charnel ground.

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-13-a-(10)-xii Ms.64a4L,Sh. 160-9, P.76b4, D.64b2, N.67b3, Co.68b7, Ch.422b17
kathaṃ naiṣadyiko bhavati / mañce vā pīṭhe vā tṛṇasaṃstare vā niṣadyayā kālam atināmayati / no tu mañcaṃ vā pīṭhaṃ vā kuḍyaṃ vā vṛkṣamūlaṃ vā tṛṇasaṃstaraṃ vā niśritya pṛṣṭhaṃ vā pārśvaṃ vā dadāti / evaṃ naiṣadyiko bhavati //
body.translated_text: How does one become a sitter (<s>naiṣadyika</s>)? One passes the time sitting on a bed, a bench, or a grass mat. But one does not lean one's back or side against a bed, a bench, a wall, the root of a tree, or a grass mat. Thus one becomes a sitter. //

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-13-a-(10)-xiii Ms.64a5L,Sh.160-15, P.76b5, D.64b3, N.67b4, Co.69a1, Ch.422b21
kathaṃ yāthāsaṃstariko bhavati / yasmin tṛṇasaṃstare vā parṇasaṃstare vā śayyāṃ kalpayati / tṛṇasaṃstaraṃ vā parṇasaṃstaraṃ vā sakṛd yathaiva saṃstṛtaṃ bhavati tathaiva śayyāṃ kalpayati / no tu punar vikopayaty abhisaṃskaroti ca / evaṃ yāthāsaṃstariko bhavati //
body.translated_text: How does one become one who uses [bedding] just as it is spread (<s>yāthāsaṃstarika</s>)? Whatever grass mat or leaf mat upon which one prepares one's bed — just as the grass mat or leaf mat was first spread, in that very way one prepares one's bed. One does not rearrange it or reshape it. Thus one becomes one who uses [bedding] just as it is spread. //

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-13-a-(10)-a Ms.64a5R,Sh.160-20,W.82-18,**82-29, P.76b7, D.64b4, N.67b5, Co.69a2, Ch.422b24
kenaite dhutaguṇā ucyante / tadyathā, ūrṇā vā karpāsaṃ vā yasmin samaye dhutaṃ bhavati saṃkṛttaṃ vicūrṇaṃ tasmin samaye mṛdu ca bhavati laghu ca karmaṇyaṃ ca, yaduta sūtrābhinirhāre vā tūlābhinirhāre vā /
body.translated_text: Why are these called ascetic qualities (<s>dhutaguṇa</s>)? Just as, when wool or cotton is shaken (<s>dhuta</s>), carded, and pulverized, at that time it becomes soft, light, and workable — namely for the production of thread or for the production of stuffing —

body.text: evam evehaikatyasya piṇḍapātapātarāgeṇa piṇḍapāte cittaṃ saktaṃ bhavati saṃsaktaṃ, cīvararāgeṇa cīvare cittam saktaṃ bhavati saṃsaktam, śayanāsanarāgeṇa śayanāsane cittaṃ saktaṃ bhavati saṃsaktam / sa ebhir dhutaguṇair viśodhayaty ṛjūkaroti, mṛdu karmaṇyam ārjavam āsravaṃ vidheyam, yaduta brahmacaryavāsāya /
body.translated_text: even so, here, a certain person's mind is attached and clinging to almsfood through passion for almsfood; the mind is attached and clinging to robes through passion for robes; the mind is attached and clinging to lodgings through passion for lodgings. He, through these ascetic qualities, purifies, straightens, makes soft and workable, makes upright, tractable, and compliant [the mind with respect to] its outflows — that is, for the purpose of dwelling in the holy life.

body.text: tenocyante dhutaguṇā iti //
body.translated_text: Therefore they are called ascetic qualities (<s>dhutaguṇa</s>). //

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-13-a-(10)-b Ms.64b2M, Sh.161-9,P.77a3, D.64b7, N.68a2, Co.69a5, Ch.422c4
tatra piṇḍapātarāgo dvividho 'ntarāyaḥ / praṇitabhojanarāgaḥ prabhūtabhojanarāgaś ca / tatra praṇītabhojanarāgasya prahāṇāya piṇḍapātikaḥ / prabhūtabhojanarāgasya prahāṇāyaikāsanikaḥ khalupaścādbhaktikaś ca bhavati /
body.translated_text: Therein, passion for almsfood is a twofold obstacle: passion for refined food and passion for abundant food. Therein, for the abandonment of passion for refined food, one becomes an almsfood-eater (<s>piṇḍapātika</s>). For the abandonment of passion for abundant food, one becomes a one-meal-eater (<s>ekāsanika</s>) and indeed one who eats after [the proper time] (<s>khalupaścādbhaktika</s>).

body.text: cīvararāgo trividho 'ntarāyaḥ / prabhūtacīvararāgaś cīvare mṛdusaṃsparśarāgaḥ praṇītacīvararāgaś ca / tatra prabhūtacīvararāgasya prahāṇāya traicīvariko bhavati / cīvare mṛdusaṃsparśarāgasya prahāṇāya nāmatiko bhavati / praṇītacīvararāgasya prahāṇāya pāṃśukūliko bhavati /
body.translated_text: Passion for robes is a threefold obstacle: passion for abundant robes, passion for the soft touch of robes, and passion for refined robes. Therein, for the abandonment of passion for abundant robes, one becomes a three-robe wearer (<s>traicīvarika</s>). For the abandonment of passion for the soft touch of robes, one becomes a felt-robe wearer (<s>nāmatika</s>). For the abandonment of passion for refined robes, one becomes a rag-robe wearer (<s>pāṃśukūlika</s>).

body.text: śayanāsanarāgaś caturvidho 'ntarāyaḥ / tadyathā saṃsargarāgaḥ, pratiśrayarāgaḥ, pārśvasukhaśayanasukharāgaḥ, āstaraṇapratyāstaraṇopacchādanarāgaḥ / tatra saṃsargarāgasya prahāṇāyāraṇyako bhavati / pratiśrayarāgasya prahāṇāya vṛkṣamūlika ābhyavakāśikaḥ śmāśāniko bhavati / api ca śmāśānikatvaṃ mithunarāgasya prahāṇāya bhavati / pārśvasukhaśayanasukharāgasya prahāṇāya naiṣadyiko bhavati / āstaraṇapratyāstaraṇopacchādanarāgasya prahāṇāya yāthāsaṃstariko bhavati / evaṃ (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 286
) one becomes endowed with the ascetic qualities (<s>dhutaguṇa</s>). //

body.translated_text: Passion for lodgings is a fourfold obstacle, namely: passion for company, passion for shelter, passion for the pleasure of [lying on] one's side and the pleasure of sleeping, and passion for bedding, covers, and blankets. Therein, for the abandonment of passion for company, one becomes a forest-dweller (<s>āraṇyaka</s>). For the abandonment of passion for shelter, one becomes a tree-root dweller (<s>vṛkṣamūlika</s>), an open-air dweller (<s>ābhyavakāśika</s>), or a charnel-ground dweller (<s>śmāśānika</s>). Moreover, charnel-ground dwelling is for the abandonment of passion for sexual intercourse. For the abandonment of passion for the pleasure of [lying on] one's side and sleeping, one becomes a sitter (<s>naiṣadyika</s>). For the abandonment of passion for bedding, covers, and blankets, one becomes one who uses [bedding] just as it is spread (<s>yāthāsaṃstarika</s>). Thus,

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-13-a-(11) Ms.64b5L, Sh.162-7, P.77b3, D.65a5, N.68a7, Co.69b4, Ch.422c18
kathaṃ prāsādiko bhavati / prāsādikenābhikramapratikrameṇa samanvāgato bhavati, ālokitavyavalokitena saṃmiñjitaprasāritena sāṃghāṭīcīvarapātradhāraṇena / evaṃ prāsādiko bhavati //
body.translated_text: How does one become gracious (<s>prāsādika</s>)? One is endowed with gracious approaching and departing, with [proper] looking ahead and looking around, with bending and stretching, and with wearing the outer robe (<s>sāṃghāṭī</s>), the robe, and carrying the bowl. Thus one becomes gracious. //

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-13-a-(12) Ms.64b5R,Sh.162-11, P.77b4, D.65a6, N.68b1, Co.69b5, Ch.422c20
kathaṃ mātrajño bhavati / iha śrāddhā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo svarthaṃ pravārayanti, yad uta cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ / tatra pratigrahe mātrāṃ jānāti evaṃ mātrajño bhavati //
body.translated_text: How does one become moderate (<s>mātrajña</s>)? Here, faithful householders and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> invite [the monk] for his own benefit — namely with robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and provisions for the sick. Therein, one knows the measure in accepting. Thus one becomes moderate. //

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-13-a-(13) Ms.65a1L,Sh.162-15, P.77b6, D.65a7, N.68b3, Co.69b6, Ch.422c22
kathaṃ satpuruṣadharmasamanvāgato bhavati / uccakulapravrajito vā sann āḍhyakulapravrajito vābhirūpo vā darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko bahuśruto vākkaraṇenopetaḥ / anyatamānyatamasya vā jñānamātrakasya darśanamātrakasparśavihāramātrakasya lābhī sann etena nātmānam utkarṣayati parāṃś ca paṃsayati / [chos daṅ rjes su mthun pa'i chos 'ba' źig bsgrub par bya ba kho na yin par rig nas /] nānyatra (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 288
) practicing the <s>Dharma</s> in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>. Thus one becomes endowed with the <s>dharmas</s> of a virtuous person. //

body.translated_text: How does one become endowed with the <s>dharmas</s> of a virtuous person (<s>satpuruṣadharma</s>)? Whether one has gone forth from a noble family or from a wealthy family, whether one is handsome, attractive, and gracious, whether one is of great learning and endowed with eloquence, or whether one has obtained any one of the [attainments] — a mere knowledge, a mere seeing, or a mere contact-dwelling — by this one does not exalt oneself or disparage others. [Knowing that one should accomplish only the <s>dharma</s> that accords with the <s>Dharma</s>,] nothing other than

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-13-a-(14) Ms.65a2M,Sh.162-22, P.78a1, D.65b2, N.68b5, Co.70a1, Ch.422c28
kathaṃ paṇḍitaliṅgasamanvāgato bhavati / karmalakṣaṇo bālaḥ karmalakṣaṇaḥ paṇḍitaḥ / yathā katham iti / bālo duścintitacintī bhavati, durbhāṣitabhāsī duṣkṛtakarmakārī / paṇḍitaḥ punaḥ sucintitacintī bhavati, subhāṣitabhāṣī sukṛtakarmakārī / evaṃ paṇḍitaliṅgasamanvāgato bhavati //
body.translated_text: How does one become endowed with the marks of a wise person (<s>paṇḍitaliṅga</s>)? A fool is characterized by his actions, and a wise person is characterized by his actions. How so? A fool thinks badly thought [thoughts], speaks badly spoken [words], and performs badly done actions. But a wise person thinks well-thought [thoughts], speaks well-spoken [words], and performs well-done actions. Thus one becomes endowed with the marks of a wise person. //

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-13-a-(15) Ms.65a3M,Sh.163-6, P.78a4, D.65b4, N.68b7, Co.70a3, Ch.423a4
kathaṃ kṣamo bhavati / ākruṣṭo na pratyākrośati / roṣito na pratiroṣayati / tāḍito na pratitāḍayati / bhaṇḍito na pratibhaṇḍayati / sa cāyuṣmān kṣamo bhavati śītasyoṣṇasya jighatsāyāḥ pipāsāyā daṃśamaśakavātātapasarīsṛpasaṃsparśāṇām, parato duruktānāṃ durāgatānāṃ vacanapathānām / śārīrikāṇāṃ vedanānāṃ duḥkhānāṃ tīvrāṇāṃ kharāṇāṃ kaṭukānām amana-āpānāṃ prāṇahāriṇīnāṃ kṣamo bhavaty adhivāsanajātīyaḥ / evaṃ kṣamo bhavati //
body.translated_text: How does one become patient (<s>kṣama</s>)? When reviled, one does not revile in return; when provoked to anger, one does not provoke in return; when struck, one does not strike in return; when abused, one does not abuse in return. And this venerable one is patient with cold, heat, hunger, thirst, the contact of gadflies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and serpents, with harsh and unwelcome speech from others, and with bodily feelings that are painful, intense, sharp, bitter, disagreeable, and life-threatening — one is patient and of the nature of forbearance. Thus one becomes patient. //

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-13-a-(16) Ms.65a4R,Sh.163-15, P.78a7, D.65b6, N.69a2, Co.70a5, Ch.423a9
katham sūrato bhavati / yathāpi tan maitreṇa kāyakarmaṇā samanvāgato bhavati, maitreṇa vākkarmaṇā, maitreṇa manaskarmaṇā, śāstur antike vijñānāṃ ca sabrahmacāriṇām / sādhāraṇaparibhogī ca bhavati, apratibhogī ca bhavaty apratiguptabhojī, lābhair dhārmikair dharmapratilabdhaiḥ, (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 290

children.text: ) pātragataiḥ pātraparyāpannaiḥ/ śīlasāmānyagataś ca bhavati, dṛṣṭisāmānyagataś ca / sa ebhiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ saṃrañjanīyair dharmaiḥ samanvāgataḥ priyakaraṇair gurukaraṇair avivādakaraṇaiḥ, sukhasaṃvāsyo bhavati, aviheṭhanajātīyaḥ / abhinandanti cainaṃ vijñāḥ sabrahmacāriṇa ekavyavasāyam / evam sūrato bhavati //
children.translated_text: ) that have come into one's bowl and belong to one's bowl. And one has moral conduct in common and views in common. Endowed with these six <s>dharmas</s> that inspire affection — that produce friendliness, that produce respect, that prevent quarrels — one becomes pleasant to live with, of the nature that does not cause distress. And wise fellow practitioners delight in one, being of one resolve. Thus one becomes gentle. //

body.translated_text: How does one become gentle (<s>sūrata</s>)? One is endowed with friendly bodily action, friendly verbal action, and friendly mental action — toward the Teacher and toward one's wise fellow practitioners of the holy life. And one shares in common [one's requisites] and does not eat secretly or in hiding, [sharing] with righteous and lawfully obtained gains,

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-13-a-(17) Ms.65a6R,Sh. 164-3, P.78b3, D.66a2, N.69a5, Co.70b5, Ch.423a18
kathaṃ peśalo bhavati / vigatabhṛkuṭir bhavaty uttānamukhavarṇaḥ, smitapūrvaṃgamaḥ, pūrvābhibhāṣī, priyavādī, saṃgrahaśīlaḥ, śuddhasantānaḥ / evaṃ peśalo bhavati //
body.translated_text: How does one become amiable (<s>peśala</s>)? One has an unfurrowed brow, an open facial expression, begins with a smile, speaks first, speaks pleasantly, is of a gathering nature, and is of pure disposition. Thus one becomes amiable. //

body.text:
(I)-C-IIl-13-b Ms.65a7M,Sh. 164-6, P.78b5, D.66a3, N.69a6, Co.70b3, Ch.423a20
sa ebhir dharmaiḥ samanvāgato dharmakāmo bhavati, guṇakāmaḥ / na Iābhasatkārakīrtiślokakāmaḥ / na samāropikayā mithyādṛṣṭyā samanvāgato bhavati, nāpy apavādikayā / asantaṃ dharmaṃ na samāropayati / santaṃ dharmaṃ nāpavadati / sa "yat tad bhavati kavitaṃ kāveyaṃ citrākṣaraṃ cihnapadavyañjanaṃ lokāyatapratisaṃyuktam, tan nirarthakam" iti viditvā, ārāt parivarjayati, na teneyate, na tena prīyate /
body.translated_text: Endowed with these <s>dharmas</s>, one becomes desirous of the <s>Dharma</s>, desirous of qualities, not desirous of gain, honor, fame, and renown. One is not endowed with the false view of superimposition, nor with that of denial. One does not superimpose a non-existent <s>dharma</s>. One does not deny an existent <s>dharma</s>. Having understood that 'whatever is composed, poetic, with ornate letters, with signs and marks and characteristics, connected with worldly philosophy (<s>lokāyata</s>) — that is meaningless,' one avoids it from afar, is not led by it, does not delight in it.

body.text: na cotsadaṃ pātracīvaraṃ dhārayati / gṛhasthaiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃsargaṃ parivarjayati kleśavardhanam / āryaiḥ saha saṃsargaṃ karoti jñānaviśodhakam / na ca mitrakulāni karoti pratigṛhṇāti / "mā me tato nidānaṃ bhaviṣyaty anekaparyāyeṇa vyākṣepād vyāpāro vā teṣāṃ vā punar vipariṇāmād anyathībhāvād utpatsyante śokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsā" iti /
body.translated_text: And one does not wear excessively [elaborate] bowl and robe. One avoids contact with householders that increases afflictions. One cultivates contact with noble ones (<s>āryas</s>) that purifies knowledge. And one does not make or accept patron-families, [thinking:] 'May there not arise for me, from that cause, in many ways, distraction or involvement [with them]; or again, from their change and alteration, grief, lamentation, suffering, mental anguish, and distress may arise.'

body.text: utpannotpannāṃś ca kleśopakleśān nādhivāsayati, prajahati, vinodayati, vyantīkaroti / "mā me 'tonidānam utpadyate dṛṣṭadhārmikaṃ vā duḥkhaṃ sāṃparāyikaṃ ve"ti /
body.translated_text: And whatever afflictions and secondary afflictions have arisen — one does not tolerate them but abandons them, removes them, and eliminates them, [thinking:] 'May there not arise for me from that cause either suffering in this life or suffering in the life to come.'

body.text: śraddhādeyaṃ ca na vinipātayati, acyutaśīlaḥ, abhraṣṭavrataḥ, śraddhādeyaṃ paribhuṅkte / na ca śraddhādeyaṃ pratikṣipati / na śikṣāṃ pratyākhyāti /
body.translated_text: And one does not waste what has been given in faith; one is of unbroken moral conduct, of unfailing observances; one enjoys what has been given in faith. And one does not reject what has been given in faith. One does not renounce the training.

body.text: ātmadoṣāntaraskhalitagaveṣī vā bhavati / praticchannakalyāṇo vivṛtapāpakaḥ / paradoṣāntaraskhaliteṣu nābhogaḥ / saṃcintya cāpattir nāpadyate jīvitahetor api / āpannaś ca laghu laghv eva yathādharmaṃ (

children.translated_text: Śbh I 294

children.text: ) pratikaroti / itikaraṇīyeṣu ca dakṣo bhavaty analasaḥ svayaṃkārī / na parataḥ kāyaparicaryāṃ paryeṣate /
children.translated_text: ) one makes amends. And in duties to be done, one is capable, not lazy, acting by oneself. One does not seek bodily service from others.

body.translated_text: One is a seeker of one's own faults and slips. One conceals one's virtues and reveals one's faults. One pays no attention to the faults and slips of others. And one does not intentionally commit an offense, not even for the sake of one's life. And having committed one, very quickly, according to the <s>Dharma</s>,

body.text: buddhānāṃ ca buddhaśrāvakāṇāṃ cācintyam anubhāvaṃ, gambhīrāṃ ca deśanām adhimucyate, na pratikṣipati, "tathāgatā eva jānakāḥ paśyakāḥ, nāham" iti viditvā, na ca svayaṃdṛṣṭiparāmarśasthāyī bhavaty asamañjasagrāhī duḥpratiniḥsargamantrī /
body.translated_text: And one has conviction in the inconceivable power of the <s>Buddhas</s> and the disciples of the <s>Buddhas</s>, and in their profound teaching; one does not reject it, knowing: 'The <s>Tathāgatas</s> alone are the knowers and seers, not I.' And one does not remain fixed in clinging to one's own views, grasping what is unfitting, and being one whose counsel is difficult to relinquish.

body.text: sa ebhir guṇair yukta evaṃvihārī evaṃśikṣamāṇaḥ śramaṇālaṃkāreṇālaṃkṛtaḥ śobhate / tadyathā kaś cid eva puruṣo yuvā maṇḍanajātīyaḥ kāmopabhogī snātānulipto 'vadātavastraprāvṛto vividhair bhūṣaṇair alaṃkṛtaḥ śobhate, tadyathā harṣair vā keyūrair vāṅgulimudrikayā vā jātarūparajatamālayā vā / evam eva sa ebhir vividhaiḥ śramaṇālaṃkārair guṇair alaṃkṛto bhāsate tapati virocate / tasmāc chramaṇālaṃkāra ity ucyate / ayam ucyate śramaṇālaṃkāraḥ //
body.translated_text: Endowed with these qualities, dwelling thus and training thus, one is adorned with the ornament of the ascetic (<s>śramaṇālaṃkāra</s>) and shines. Just as a certain young man, of the nature to adorn himself, a sensualist, bathed and anointed, draped in white garments, adorned with various ornaments, shines — such as necklaces, armlets, finger-rings, or garlands of gold and silver — even so, he, adorned with these various qualities that are the ornaments of the ascetic, shines, blazes, and radiates. Therefore it is called the ornament of the ascetic. This is called the ornament of the ascetic (<s>śramaṇālaṃkāra</s>). //

body.text: // uddānam //
body.translated_text: // <s>Uddāna</s> (summary verse) //

children.translated_text: Faithful, non-deceitful, seldom-ill, vigor, wisdom, fewness of desires, contentment,
ease of maintenance, ease of support, ascetic [qualities], graciousness, moderation,
[endowed with] virtuous-person [qualities], wise-person marks, patience, gentleness, and amiability. // [1]
There would be personal and external endowments, desire, moral conduct, senses, likewise,
food, and also wakefulness, dwelling with clear comprehension. // [2]
Likewise, the good spiritual friend, hearing and reflecting on the true <s>Dharma</s>,
absence of obstacles, generosity, and last of all, the ornament [of the ascetic]. // [3]

children.text: laukikaṃ caiva vairāgyaṃ tathā lokottareṇa ca /
children.translated_text: And worldly dispassion, and likewise by the supramundane [path],

children.text: tayoś caiva hi saṃbhāro bhūmir naiṣkramyasaṃjñitā // [4]
children.translated_text: and indeed the requisites of both — [this] stage is called 'renunciation' (<s>naiṣkramya</s>). // [4]

body.text: // yogācārabhūmau śrāvakabhūmisaṃgṛhītāyāṃ prathamaṃ yogasthānam //
body.translated_text: // From the <s>Yogācārabhūmi</s>, in the section included in the <s>Śrāvakabhūmi</s>, the first stage of practice (<s>yogasthāna</s>). //

body.text:
(II)-A-I Ms.66a2L, Sh.169-1, W.83-13, P.80a2, D.67a4, N.70b2, Co.71b2, Ch.424a1
tatra kati pudgalā ye 'syāṃ naiṣkramyabhūmau yathādeśitāyāṃ yathāparikīrtitāyāṃ niṣkrāmanti / kathaṃ ca pudgalānāṃ vyavasthānaṃ bhavati / katamad ālambanam / katamo 'vavādaḥ / katamā śikṣā / katame śikṣānulomikā dharmāḥ / katamo yogabhraṃśaḥ / katame yogāḥ / katamo manaskāraḥ / katamad yogakaraṇīyam / kati yogācārāḥ / katamā yogabhāvanā / katamad bhāvanāphalam / kati pudgalaparyāyāḥ / kati mārāḥ / kati mārakarmāṇi / katham ārambho viphalo bhavati //
body.translated_text: Therein, how many persons go forth in this stage of renunciation (<s>naiṣkramyabhūmi</s>), as taught and proclaimed? And how is the classification of persons established? What is the object? What is the admonition? What is the training? What are the <s>dharmas</s> conforming to the training? What is the falling away from practice? What are the practices? What is the mental attention? What is the task of practice? How many are the practitioners of yoga? What is the cultivation of yoga? What is the fruit of cultivation? How many are the classes of persons? How many are the <s>Māras</s>? How many are the deeds of <s>Māra</s>? How does effort become fruitless?

body.text:
(II)-A-II-1-a Ms.66a3R, Sh.169-14, W.84-1, P.80a7, D.67a7, N.70b5, Co.71b7, Ch.424a17
tatra pudgalā aṣṭāviṃśatiḥ / katame 'ṣṭāviṃśatiḥ / tadyathā mṛdvindriyaḥ / tīkṣṇendriyaḥ / utsadarāgaḥ / utsadadveṣaḥ / utsadamohaḥ / utsadamānaḥ / utsadavitarkaḥ / samaprāptaḥ / mandarajaskajātīyaḥ / pratipannakaḥ / phalasthaḥ / śraddhānusārī / dharmānusārī / śraddhādhimuktaḥ / dṛṣṭiprāptaḥ / kāyasākṣī / saptakṛdbhavaparamaḥ / kulaṃkulaḥ / ekavīcikaḥ / antarāparinirvāyī / upapadyaparinirvāyī / anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī / sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī / ūrdhvaṃsrotā / (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 4

one liberated at a [certain] time (<s>samayavimukta</s>); one of unshakable nature (<s>akopyadharmā</s>); one liberated through wisdom (<s>prajñāvimukta</s>); and one liberated in both ways (<s>ubhayatobhāgavimukta</s>).

body.translated_text: Therein, there are twenty-eight persons. Which twenty-eight? Namely: one of soft faculties (<s>mṛdvindriya</s>); one of sharp faculties (<s>tīkṣṇendriya</s>); one with predominance of passion (<s>utsadarāga</s>); one with predominance of aversion (<s>utsadadveṣa</s>); one with predominance of delusion (<s>utsadamoha</s>); one with predominance of pride (<s>utsadamāna</s>); one with predominance of discursive thought (<s>utsadavitarka</s>); one of equal attainment (<s>samaprāpta</s>); one of slight dust [on the eyes] (<s>mandarajaска</s>); one on the path (<s>pratipannaka</s>); one established in the fruit (<s>phalastha</s>); a faith-follower (<s>śraddhānusārī</s>); a <s>Dharma</s>-follower (<s>dharmānusārī</s>); one liberated through faith (<s>śraddhādhimukta</s>); one who has attained the view (<s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s>); a body-witness (<s>kāyasākṣī</s>); one with seven births at most (<s>saptakṛdbhavaparama</s>); one reborn from family to family (<s>kulaṃkula</s>); a one-seeder (<s>ekavīcika</s>); one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the intermediate state (<s>antarāparinirvāyī</s>); one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> upon rebirth (<s>upapadyaparinirvāyī</s>); one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> without effort (<s>anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī</s>); one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> with effort (<s>sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī</s>); one whose stream goes upward (<s>ūrdhvaṃsrotas</s>);

body.text:
(II)-A-II-1-a-(1) Ms.66a5M, Sh.170-7, P.80b4, D.67b4, N.71a2, Co.72a4, Ch.424a25
tatra mṛdvindriyaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / yasya pudgalasya mṛdūnīndriyāṇi dhandhavāhīni mandavāhīni jñeye vastunīti pūrvavat / sa punar dvividho veditavyaḥ / ādita eva mṛdvindriyagotro paribhāvitendriyaś ca //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is a person of soft faculties (<s>mṛdvindriya</s>)? That person whose faculties are soft, slow-moving, and dull-moving with respect to the knowable object and thing — as before. He should be understood as being of two kinds: one who is of the lineage of soft faculties from the very beginning, and one whose faculties have been [subsequently] cultivated.

body.text:
(II)-A-II-1-a-(2) Ms.66a6L, Sh.170-12, P.80b6, D.67b5, N.71a3, Co.72a5, Ch.424a28
tīkṣṇendriyaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / yasya pudgalasya tīkṣṇānīndriyāṇy adhandhavāhīni bhavanty amandavāhīni jñeye vastunīti pūrvavat / sa punar dvividho veditavyaḥ / ādita eva tīkṣṇendriyagotraḥ paribhāvitendriyaś ca //
body.translated_text: What is a person of sharp faculties (<s>tīkṣṇendriya</s>)? That person whose faculties are sharp, not slow-moving, and not dull-moving with respect to the knowable object and thing — as before. He should be understood as being of two kinds: one who is of the lineage of sharp faculties from the very beginning, and one whose faculties have been [subsequently] cultivated.

body.text:
(II)-A-II-1-a-(3) Ms.66a6R, Sh.170-17, P.80b7, D.67b6, N.71a5, Co.72a6, Ch.424b4
rāgotsadaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / yena pudgalena pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu rāga āsevito bhāvito bahulīkṛtaḥ, sa tena hetunā tena pratyayenaitarhi rañjanīye vastuni tīvrarāgaś ca bhavaty āyatarāgaś ca / ayam ucyate rāgotsadaḥ pudgalaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is a person with predominance of passion (<s>rāgotsada</s>)? A person who, in previous births, has practiced, cultivated, and made much of passion — by that cause and that condition, now, with respect to an attractive object, has intense passion and extended passion. This is called a person with predominance of passion.

body.text:
(II)-A-II-1-a-(4) Ms.66a7M, Sh.171-1, P.81a1, D.67b7, N.71a6, Co.72b1, Ch.424b8
dveṣotsadaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / yena pudgalena dveṣaḥ pūrvam anyāsu (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 6

children.text: ) jātiṣv āsevito bhāvito bahulīkṛtaḥ, tena ca hetunā tena pratyayenaitarhi dveṣaṇīye vastuni tīvradveṣaś ca bhavaty āyatadveṣaś ca / ayam ucyate dveṣotsadaḥ pudgalaḥ //
children.translated_text: births, has practiced, cultivated, and made much of aversion — by that cause and that condition, now, with respect to an offensive object, has intense aversion and extended aversion. This is called a person with predominance of aversion.

body.translated_text: What is a person with predominance of aversion (<s>dveṣotsada</s>)? A person who, in previous

body.text:
(II)-A-II-1-a-(5) Ms.66a8L, Sh.171-6, P.81a3, D.68a1, N.71a7, Co.72b2, Ch.424b11
mohotsadaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / yena pudgalena pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu moha āsevito bhāvito bahulīkṛtaḥ, tena ca hetunā tena pratyayenaitarhi mohanīye vastuni tīvramohaś ca bhavaty āyatamohaś ca / ayam ucyate mohotsadaḥ pudgalaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is a person with predominance of delusion (<s>mohotsada</s>)? A person who, in previous births, has practiced, cultivated, and made much of delusion — by that cause and that condition, now, with respect to a deluding object, has intense delusion and extended delusion. This is called a person with predominance of delusion.

body.text:
(II)-A-II-1-a-(6) Ms.66b1L, Sh.171-11, P.81a5, D.68a3, N.71b2, Co.72b3, Ch.424b15
mānotsadaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / yena pudgalena pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu māna āsevito bhāvito bahulīkṛtaḥ, tena ca hetunā tena ca pratyayenaitarhi mananīye vastuni tīvramānaś ca bhavaty āyatamānaś ca / ayam ucyate mānotsadaḥ pudgalaḥ//
body.translated_text: What is a person with predominance of pride (<s>mānotsada</s>)? A person who, in previous births, has practiced, cultivated, and made much of pride — by that cause and that condition, now, with respect to an object conducive to conceit, has intense pride and extended pride. This is called a person with predominance of pride.

body.text:
(II)-A-II-1-a-(7) Ms.66b1R, Sh.171-16, P.81a7, D.68a4, N.71b3, Co.72b4, Ch.424b18
vitarkotsadaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / yena pudgalena pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu vitarka āsevito bhāvito bahulīkṛtaḥ, tena ca hetunā tenaiva pratyayenaitarhi vitarkasthānīye vastuni tīvravitarkaś ca bhavaty āyatavitarkaś ca / ayam ucyate vitarkotsadaḥ pudgalaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is a person with predominance of discursive thought (<s>vitarkotsada</s>)? A person who, in previous births, has practiced, cultivated, and made much of discursive thought — by that cause and that condition, now, with respect to an object conducive to discursive thought, has intense discursive thought and extended discursive thought. This is called a person with predominance of discursive thought.

body.text:
(II)-A-II-1-a-(8) Ms.66b2R, Sh.171-21, P.81b1, D.68a5, N.71b4, Co.72b6, Ch.424b22
samaprāptaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / yena pudgalena pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu rāgo dveṣo moho māno vitarko nāsevito bhāvito bahulīkṛtaḥ / na caite dharmā ādīnavato dṛṣṭā vidūṣitāḥ saṃtīritāḥ / sa tena hetunā tena pratyayena rañjanīye vā vastuni dveṣaṇīye mohanīye manyanīye vitarkanīye na tīvrarāgo bhavati nāpy āyatarāgaḥ / na cāsya na samudācarati rāgo yaduta tena vastuna / yathā rāga evaṃ dveṣo moho māno vitarkaḥ / ayam ucyate samaprāptaḥ pudgalaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is a person of equal attainment (<s>samaprāpta</s>)? A person who, in previous births, has not practiced, cultivated, or made much of passion, aversion, delusion, pride, or discursive thought; and these <s>dharmas</s> have not been seen as dangerous, have not been become disgusted with, have not been stirred up. By that cause and that condition, with respect to an attractive, offensive, deluding, conceiting, or thought-provoking object, one does not have intense passion, nor extended passion — yet passion does arise with respect to that object. As with passion, so with aversion, delusion, pride, and discursive thought. This is called a person of equal attainment.

body.text:
(II)-A-II-1-a-(9) Ms.66b4L, Sh.172-8, P.81b5, D.68b2, N.72a1, Co.73a2, Ch.424b29
mandarajaskaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / yena pudgalena pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu na rāga āsevito bhāvito bahulīkṛtaḥ / ādīnavataś ca bahulaṃ dṛṣṭo bhavati vidūṣitaḥ saṃtīritaḥ / sa tena hetunā tena pratyayenaitarhi rañjanīye vastuni samavahite saṃmukhībhūte 'dhimātre pracura ulbaṇe dhandhaṃ rāgam utpādayati / madhye parītte naivotpādayati / yathā rāga evaṃ dveṣo moho māno vitarko veditavyaḥ / ayam ucyate mandarajaskaḥ pudgalaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is a person of slight dust [on the eyes] (<s>mandarajaska</s>)? A person who, in previous births, has not practiced, cultivated, or made much of passion, and has frequently seen [passion] as dangerous, has become disgusted with it, and has stirred it up. By that cause and that condition, now, with respect to an attractive object, when it is present and faces one, when it is intense, abundant, and excessive — one generates passion only sluggishly. When it is moderate or slight, one does not generate it at all. As with passion, so should aversion, delusion, pride, and discursive thought be understood. This is called a person of slight dust [on the eyes].

body.text:
(II)-A-II-1-a-(10) Ms.66b5R, Sh.172-17, P.82a1, D.68b4, N.72a3, Co.73a5, Ch.424c5
pratipannakaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / āha / pratipannakāḥ pudgalāś catvāraḥ / katame catvāraḥ / tadyathā srota-āpattiphalapratipannakaḥ, sakṛdāgāmiphalapratipannakaḥ, anāgāmiphalapratipannakaḥ, arhattvaphalapratipannakaś ca / ayam ucyate pratipannakaḥ pudgalaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is a person on the path (<s>pratipannaka</s>)? He says: there are four persons on the path. Which four? Namely: one on the path to the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>), one on the path to the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>), one on the path to the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>), and one on the path to the fruit of <s>arhatship</s>. This is called a person on the path.

body.text:
(II)-A-II-1-a-(11) Ms.66b6R, Sh.173-2, P.82a3, D.68b5, N.72a5, Co.73a6, Ch.424c8
phalasthaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / āha / srota-āpannaḥ, sakṛdāgāmī, anāgāmī, arhan / ayam ucyate phalasthaḥ pudgalaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is a person established in the fruit (<s>phalastha</s>)? He says: a stream-enterer (<s>srotaāpanna</s>), a once-returner (<s>sakṛdāgāmī</s>), a non-returner (<s>anāgāmī</s>), and an <s>arhat</s>. This is called a person established in the fruit.

body.text:
(II)-A-II-1-a-(12) Ms.66b7L, Sh.175-1, P.82a5, D.68b7, N.72a6, Co.73b1, Ch.424c11
śraddhānusārī pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / yaḥ pudgalaḥ parato 'vavādānuśāsanīṃ paryeṣate / tadbalena ca pratipadyate yaduta phalasyādhigamāya / no tūdgṛhīteṣu dharmeṣu paryavāpteṣu cintiteṣu tuliteṣūpaparīkṣiteṣu svayam eva śakto bhavati pratibalas tān dharmān bhāvanākāreṇānusartum / nānyatra pudgalānusāriṇyā śraddhayā pratipadyate / tasmāc chraddhānusārīty ucyate //
body.translated_text: What is a faith-follower (<s>śraddhānusārī</s>)? A person who seeks admonition and instruction from another, and by that power practices — namely, for the attainment of the fruit. But with respect to the <s>dharmas</s> that have been taken up, mastered, reflected upon, weighed, and examined — one is not capable or competent by oneself to follow those <s>dharmas</s> in the mode of cultivation. One practices not otherwise than through faith that follows after persons. Therefore one is called a faith-follower.

body.text:
(II)-A-II-1-a-(13) Ms.66b8M, Sh.175-8, P.82a8, D.69a2, N.72b1, Co.73b3, Ch.424c16
dharmānusārī pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / yaḥ pudgalo yathāśruteṣu dharmeṣu paryavāpteṣu cintiteṣu tuliteṣūpaparīkṣiteṣu svayam eva śakto bhavati pratibalas tān dharmān bhāvanākāreṇānusartum / no tu parato 'vavādānuśāsanīṃ paryeṣate, yaduta phalasyādhigamāya / ayam ucyate dharmānusārī pudgalaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is a <s>Dharma</s>-follower (<s>dharmānusārī</s>)? A person who, with respect to the <s>dharmas</s> as heard, mastered, reflected upon, weighed, and examined — is capable and competent by oneself to follow those <s>dharmas</s> in the mode of cultivation. One does not seek admonition and instruction from another, namely for the attainment of the fruit. This is called a <s>Dharma</s>-follower.

body.text:
(II)-A-II-1-a-(14) Ms.67a1M, Sh.175-14, P.82b2, D.69a3, N.72b3, Co.73b4, Ch.424c20
śraddhādhimuktaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / āha / sa eva śraddhānusārī pudgalo yasmin samaye śrāmaṇyaphalam adhigacchati sparśayati sākṣātkaroti parato 'vavādānuśāsanīm āgamya, tasmin samaye śraddhādhimukta ity ucyate //
body.translated_text: What is a person liberated through faith (<s>śraddhādhimukta</s>)? He says: that very faith-follower, at the time when he attains, contacts, and directly realizes the fruit of the ascetic life, having relied on the admonition and instruction of another — at that time he is called 'liberated through faith.'

body.text:
(II)-A-II-1-a-(15) Ms.67a2L, Sh.176-4, P.82b4, D.69a4, N.72b4, Co.73b6, Ch.424c23
dṛṣṭiprāptaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / āha / sa eva dharmānusārī pudgalo yasmin samaye śrāmaṇyaphalam adhigacchati sparśayati sākṣātkaroti parato nāvavādānuśāsanīm āgamya, tasmin samaye dṛṣṭiprāpta ity ucyate //
body.translated_text: What is a person who has attained the view (<s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s>)? He says: that very <s>Dharma</s>-follower, at the time when he attains, contacts, and directly realizes the fruit of the ascetic life, not having relied on the admonition and instruction of another — at that time he is called 'one who has attained the view.'

body.text:
(II)-A-II-1-a-(16) Ms.67a2R, Sh.177-3, P.82b5, D.69a5, N.72b5, Co.73b7, Ch.424c25
kāyasākṣī pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / yo 'yaṃ pudgalo 'nulomapratilomam aṣṭau vimokṣān samāpadyate vyuttiṣṭhate ca / kāyena ca sākṣātkṛtya bahulaṃ viharati / na ca sarveṇa sarvam āsravakṣayam anuprāpnoti / ayam ucyate kāyasākṣī pudgalaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is a body-witness (<s>kāyasākṣī</s>)? A person who enters into and emerges from the eight liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>) in forward and reverse order, and who, having directly realized [them] with the body, dwells abundantly [therein]; yet one does not fully attain the destruction of the outflows (<s>āsravakṣaya</s>) in every respect. This is called a body-witness.

body.text:
(II)-A-II-1-a-(17) Ms.67a3M, Sh.177-8, W.84-25, P.82b7, D.69a7, N.72b7, Co.74a1, Ch.424c27
saptakṛdbhavaparamaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / yo 'yaṃ pudgalas trayāṇām saṃyojanānāṃ prahāṇāt satkāyadṛṣṭeḥ śīlavrataparāmarśasya vicikitsāyāḥ srota-āpanno bhavati / avinipātadharmā niyataḥ saṃbodhiparāyaṇaḥ saptakṛdbhavaparamaḥ saptakṛtvo devāṃś ca manuṣyāṃś ca saṃdhāvya saṃsṛtya duḥkhasyāntaṃ karoti / ayam ucyate saptakṛdbhavaparamaḥ pudgalaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is a person with seven births at most (<s>saptakṛdbhavaparama</s>)? A person who, through the abandonment of the three fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>) — the view of the perishable aggregate (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), attachment to rules and vows (<s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>), and doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>) — becomes a stream-enterer (<s>srotaāpanna</s>), one whose nature is not to fall into lower realms, who is determined, who is bound for awakening (<s>saṃbodhiparāyaṇa</s>), with seven births at most — having run through and wandered among <s>devas</s> and humans seven times, one makes an end of suffering. This is called a person with seven births at most.

body.text:
(II)-A-II-1-a-(18) Ms.67a4M, Sh.178-1, P.83a2, D.69b2, N.73a2, Co.74a3, Ch.425a2
kulaṃkulaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / [smras pa / rigs nas rigs su skye ba ni gñis te / lha'i rigs nas rigs su skye ba daṅ / mi'i rigs nas rigs su skye ba'o // de la lha'i rigs nas rigs su skye ba ni / lha rnams kyi rigs nas rigs su mtshams sbyar źiṅ / 'khor nas sdug bsṅal mthar byed pa gaṅ yin pa'o / de la mi'i rigs nas rigs su skye ba ni / mi rnams kyi rigs nas rigs su mtshams sbyar źiṅ / 'khor nas sdug bsṅal mthar byed pa gaṅ yin pa ste] / ubhāv api srota-āpannau pudgalau veditavyau //
body.translated_text: What is a person reborn from family to family (<s>kulaṃkula</s>)? [He says: one reborn from family to family is of two kinds: one reborn from family to family among the gods, and one reborn from family to family among humans. Therein, one reborn from family to family among the gods is one who, linking up from family to family of the gods, wandering in the cycle, makes an end of suffering. Therein, one reborn from family to family among humans is one who, linking up from family to family of humans, wandering in the cycle, makes an end of suffering.] Both should be understood as stream-enterer (<s>srotaāpanna</s>) persons.

body.text:
(II)-A-II-1-a-(19) Ms.67a4R, Sh.178-3, P.83a5, D.69b4, N.73a4, Co.74a6, Ch.425a6
tatraikavīcikaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / yasya sakṛdāgāminaḥ pudgalasyānāgāmiphalapratipannakasya kāmāvacarāṇāṃ kleśānām adhimātramadhyakleśāḥ prahīṇā bhavanti / mṛdukāś caike 'vaśiṣṭā bhavanti / sakṛc ca kāmāvacaradevabhavam abhinirvartya tatraiva parinirvāti / na punaḥ sakṛd āgacchatīmaṃ lokam / ayam ucyata ekavīcikaḥ pudgalaḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the <s>ekavīcika</s> (one-intervener) person? That person who is a <s>sakṛdāgāmin</s> (once-returner), practicing for the fruit of the <s>anāgāmin</s> (non-returner) — whose intense and middling defilements among the defilements belonging to the desire realm have been abandoned, and some mild ones remain — who, having produced existence once as a <s>deva</s> (god) in the desire realm, attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final liberation) right there, and does not come again to this world. This is called the <s>ekavīcika</s> (one-intervener) person.

body.text:
(II)-A-II-1-a-(20) Ms.67a5R, Sh.178-10, P.83a7, D.69b5, N.73a6, Co.74a7, Ch.425a11
antarāparinirvāyī pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / āha / antarāparinirvāyiṇaḥ pudgalās trayaḥ / eko 'ntarāparinirvāyī pudgalaś cyutamātra evāntarābhavābhinirvṛttikāle 'ntarābhavam abhinirvartayati / abhinirvṛtte samakālam eva parinirvāti / tadyathā parīttaḥ śakalikāgnir utpanna eva parinirvāti /
body.translated_text: What is the <s>antarāparinirvāyin</s> (one who attains parinirvāṇa in the intermediate state) person? He says: there are three types of <s>antarāparinirvāyin</s> persons. The first <s>antarāparinirvāyin</s> person — at the very moment of death, at the time of the production of the intermediate existence (<s>antarābhava</s>), produces the intermediate existence and at the very same time of its production attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — just as a small spark of fire is extinguished the very moment it arises.

body.text:
dvitīyo 'ntarāparinirvāyī pudgalo 'ntarābhavam abhinirvartayati / abhinirvṛtte 'ntarābhave tatrastha eva kālāntareṇa parinirvāti / no tu yenopapattibhavas tenādyāpy upanato bhavati / tadyathā, ayoguḍānāṃ vāyaḥsthālānāṃ vā dīptāgnisaṃprataptānām ayoghanair hanyamānānām ayaḥprapāṭikotpataty eva parinirvāti /
tṛtīyo 'ntarāparinirvāyī pudgalo 'ntarābhavam abhinirvartya yenopapattibhavas tenopanamati / upanataś ca punar anupapanna eva parinirvāti / tadyathāyasprapāṭikotpatya pṛthivyām apatitaiva parinirvāti /
body.translated_text:
The second <s>antarāparinirvāyin</s> person produces the intermediate existence, and having been established in that intermediate existence, after some time attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> there itself — but does not yet approach the birth-existence where [rebirth would occur]. Just as, when iron balls or iron pans heated by blazing fire are struck with iron hammers, a spark flies up and is extinguished right there.
The third <s>antarāparinirvāyin</s> person, having produced the intermediate existence, approaches toward the birth-existence where [rebirth would occur], but while approaching, before actually being reborn, attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — just as a spark, having flown up, is extinguished before falling to the ground.

body.text: ta ime trayo 'ntarāparinirvāyiṇaḥ pudgalā ekadhyam abhisaṃkṣipyāntarāparinirvāyī pudgala ity ucyate //
body.translated_text: These three types of <s>antarāparinirvāyin</s> persons, taken together, are called the <s>antarāparinirvāyin</s> (one who attains parinirvāṇa in the intermediate state) person.

body.text:
(II)-A-II-1-a-(21) Ms.67b2M, Sh.180-13, P.83b7, D.70a4, N.73b5, Co.74b6, Ch.425a22
upapadyaparinirvāyī pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / ya upapannamātra eva parinirvāti / ayam ucyata upapadyaparinirvāyī pudgalaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is the <s>upapadyaparinirvāyin</s> (one who attains parinirvāṇa upon rebirth) person? One who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> at the very moment of being reborn. This is called the <s>upapadyaparinirvāyin</s> person.

body.text:
(II)-A-II-1-a-(22) Ms.67b2R, Sh.180-15, P.84a1, D.70a5, N.73b6, Co.74b7, Ch.425a24
anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / 13) yo 'nabhisaṃskāreṇāprayatnenākhedena mārgaṃ saṃmukhīkṛtya tatropapannaḥ parinirvāti / ayam ucyate 'nabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī pudgalaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is the <s>anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyin</s> (one who attains parinirvāṇa without exertion) person? One who, without deliberate effort, without exertion, without fatigue, having brought the path to the fore, attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> being reborn there. This is called the <s>anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyin</s> person.

body.text:
(II)-A-II-1-a-(23) Ms.67b3L, Sh.181-3, P.84a2, D.70a6, N.73b7, Co. 75a1, Ch.425a27
sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / yo 'bhisaṃskāreṇa prayatnena khedena mārgaṃ saṃmukhīkṛtya tatropapannaḥ parinirvāti / ayam ucyate sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī pudgalaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is the <s>sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyin</s> (one who attains parinirvāṇa with exertion) person? One who, with deliberate effort, with exertion, with fatigue, having brought the path to the fore, attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> being reborn there. This is called the <s>sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyin</s> person.

body.text:
(II)-A-II-1-a-(24) Ms.67b3R, Sh.181-7, P.84a4, D.70a7, N.74a1, Co. 75a3, Ch.425a29
ūrdhvaṃsrotāḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / yaḥ pudgalo 'nāgāmī prathame dhyāna upapannaḥ sa na tatrastha eva parinirvāti / api tu tasmāc cyavitvottarottaram upapattyāyatanam abhinirvartayan yāvad akaniṣṭhān vā devān gacchati, naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanaṃ vā / ayam ucyata ūrdhvaṃsrotāh pudgalaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is the <s>ūrdhvaṃsrotas</s> (upstream-goer) person? That <s>anāgāmin</s> (non-returner) person who, having been reborn in the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation absorption), does not attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> there itself, but rather, departing from there, produces one after another higher realm of rebirth, going up to the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> <s>devas</s> (gods) or to the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>). This is called the <s>ūrdhvaṃsrotas</s> (upstream-goer) person.

body.text:
(II)-A-II-1-a-(25) Ms.67b4R, Sh.182-6, P.84a6, D.70b2, N.74a3, Co. 75a4, Ch.425b5
samayavimuktaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / yo mṛdvindriyagotraḥ pudgalo laukikebhyo dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārebhyaḥ parihīyate / cetayati vā maraṇāya / anurakṣate vā vimuktim / atyarthāpramādacaryām anuyukto bhavati, yadutaitām evāparihāṇim adhipatiṃ kṛtvā / tanmātro vāsya kuśalapakṣo bhavati, no tu teṣāṃ teṣāṃ rātriṃdivasānāṃ kṣaṇalavamuhūrtānām atyayād atyarthaṃ viśeṣāya paraiti / yāvan na tīvram abhiyogaṃ karoti / ayam ucyate samayavimuktaḥ pudgalaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is the <s>samayavimukta</s> (one liberated on occasion) person? That person who is of the class with mild faculties, who falls away from the worldly pleasant abidings in the visible life. One either intends to die [to prevent falling], or one guards one's liberation, or one is devoted to the practice of extreme diligence — namely, taking this very non-falling-away as the governing [concern]. And one's wholesome side remains at just that measure, and does not advance greatly toward distinction with the passing of those nights and days, moments and instants and hours — as long as one does not make an intense effort. This is called the <s>samayavimukta</s> (one liberated on occasion) person.

body.text:
(II)-A-II-1-a-(26) Ms.67b6L, Sh.183-1, P.84b2, D.70b4, N.74a6, Co. 75a7, Ch.425b11
akopyadharmā pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / etadviparyayeṇākopyadharmā pudgalo veditavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is the <s>akopyadharman</s> (one whose attainments are unshakable) person? By the reverse of the preceding, the <s>akopyadharman</s> person should be understood.

body.text:
(II)-A-II-1-a-(27) Ms.67b6M, Sh.183-3, P.84b3, D.70b5, N.74a6, Co. 75a7, Ch.425b12
prajñāvimuktaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / yaḥ pudgalaḥ sarveṇa sarvam āsravakṣayam anuprāpnoti / no tv aṣṭau vimokṣān kāyena sākṣātkṛtvopasaṃpadya viharati / ayam ucyate prajñāvimuktaḥ pudgalaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is the <s>prajñāvimukta</s> (one liberated by wisdom) person? That person who attains the destruction of all <s>āsravas</s> (defilements) completely and in every way, but does not directly realize and dwell in the attainment of the eight <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations) with the body. This is called the <s>prajñāvimukta</s> person.

body.text:
(II)-A-II-1-a-(28) Ms.67b7L, Sh.183-7, P.84b4, D.70b6, N.74b1, Co.75b1, Ch.425b15
ubhayatobhāgavimuktaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / yaḥ pudgalaḥ sarveṇa sarvam āsravakṣayam anuprāpnoti / aṣṭau vimokṣān kāyena sākṣātkṛtvopasaṃpadya viharati / tasya kleśāvaraṇāc ca cittaṃ muktaṃ bhavati, vimokṣāvaraṇāc ca / ayam ucyata ubhayatobhāgavimuktaḥ pudgalaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is the <s>ubhayatobhāgavimukta</s> (one liberated in both ways) person? That person who attains the destruction of all <s>āsravas</s> (defilements) completely and in every way, and who directly realizes and dwells in the attainment of the eight <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations) with the body. That one's mind is liberated from the obstacle of defilements (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>) and from the obstacle to liberation (<s>vimokṣāvaraṇa</s>). This is called the <s>ubhayatobhāgavimukta</s> (one liberated in both ways) person.

body.text:
(II)-A-II-2-a Ms.68a1M, Sh.184-1, W.85-5, P.84b6, D.70b7, N.74b2, Co.75b3, Ch.425b20
pudgalavyavasthānaṃ katamat / ekādaśabhiḥ prabhedaiḥ pudgalavyavasthānaṃ veditavyam / katamair ekādaśabhiḥ / tadyathā indriyaprabhedena, nikāyaprabhedena, caritaprabhedena, praṇidhānaprabhedena, pratipatprabhedena, mārgaphalaprabhedena, prayogaprabhedena, samāpattiprabhedena, upapattiprabhedena, parihāṇiprabhedena, āvaraṇaprabhedena ca //
body.translated_text: What is the classification of persons (<s>pudgalavyavasthāna</s>)? The classification of persons should be understood through eleven categories. Which eleven? Namely: by the category of faculties, by the category of community, by the category of temperament, by the category of aspiration, by the category of practice, by the category of path-fruit, by the category of application, by the category of attainment, by the category of rebirth, by the category of falling away, and by the category of obstacles.

body.text:
-II-2-a-(1) Ms.68a2L, Sh.184-7, P.85a1, D.71a2, N.74b4, Co.75b5, Ch.425b25
indriyaprabhedena tāvat / mṛdvindriyatīkṣṇendriyapudgalayor vyavasthānam //
body.translated_text: First, by the category of faculties: the classification of persons with mild faculties and those with keen faculties.

body.text:
-II-2-a-(2) Ms.68a2L, Sh. 184-9, P.85a2, D.71a3, N.74b5, Co.75b5, Ch.425b27
nikāyaprabhedena saptavidhaṃ pudgalavyavasthānam / bhikṣur bhikṣuṇī śikṣamāṇā śrāmaṇeraḥ śrāmaṇery upāsaka upāsikā ca //
body.translated_text: By the category of community: there is a sevenfold classification of persons — <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk), <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> (nun), <s>śikṣamāṇā</s> (female probationer), <s>śrāmaṇera</s> (male novice), <s>śrāmaṇerī</s> (female novice), <s>upāsaka</s> (male lay follower), and <s>upāsikā</s> (female lay follower).

body.text:
-II-2-a-(3) Ms.68a2M, Sh. 184-12, P.85a3, D.71a3, N.74b6, Co.75b6, Ch.425c1
tatra caritaprabhedena saptānāṃ pudgalānāṃ vyavasthānam / yo 'yaṃ rāgotsadaḥ pudgalaḥ sa rāgacaritaḥ / yo dveṣotsadaḥ sa dveṣacaritaḥ / yo mohotsadaḥ sa mohacaritaḥ / yo mānotsadaḥ sa mānacaritaḥ / yo vitarkotsadaḥ sa vitarkacaritaḥ / yaḥ samaprāptaḥ sa samabhāgacaritaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, by the category of temperament: there is a classification of seven persons. The person who has an excess of <s>rāga</s> (passion) is of passionate temperament. One who has an excess of <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion) is of aversive temperament. One who has an excess of <s>moha</s> (delusion) is of deluded temperament. One who has an excess of <s>māna</s> (pride) is of proud temperament. One who has an excess of <s>vitarka</s> (discursive thought) is of discursive temperament. One who has attained balance is of balanced temperament.

body.text: yo mandarajaskaḥ sa mandacarito veditavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: One who has little dust [on one's eyes] should be understood as of mild temperament.

body.text:
-II-2-a-(3)-i Ms.68a3M, Sh.185-1, P.85a6, D.71a5, N.75a1, Co.76a1, Ch.425c8
tatra rāgacaritasya pudgalasya katamāni liṅgāni / iha rāgacaritaḥ pudgalaḥ parītte sarvanihīne rañjanīye vastuni ghanam adhimātraṃ rāgaparyavasthānam utpādayati / kaḥ punar vādo madhyapraṇīte / tac ca punā rāgaparyavasthānaṃ saṃtatyā cirakālam avasthāpayati / dīrghakālam anubaddho bhavati /
body.translated_text: Therein, what are the signs of the person of passionate temperament? Here, the person of passionate temperament, even in regard to a minor, inferior, and trivial object of delight, produces an intense and strong manifestation of passionate obsession. How much more so in regard to middling or excellent [objects]. And furthermore, that passionate obsession persists in a continuous stream for a long time; one is attached for a long duration.

body.text: tena paryavasthānena rañjanīyair dharmair abhibhūyate / no tu śaknoti rañjanīyān dharmān abhibhavitum / snigdhendriyaś ca bhavaty akharendriyaḥ, akarkaśendriyaḥ, aparuṣendriyaḥ / nātyarthaṃ pareṣāṃ viheṭhanajātīyo yaduta kāyena vācā durvivejyaś ca bhavati duḥsaṃvejyaś ca / hīnādhimuktikaś ca bhavati / dṛḍhakarmāntaḥ / sthirakarmāntaḥ / dṛḍhavrataḥ / sthiravrataḥ / sahiṣṇuś ca bhavaty upakaraṇeṣu pariṣkāreṣu lolupajātīyas tadgurukaś ca, saumanasyabahulaś ca bhavaty ānandībahulo vigatabhṛkuṭir uttānamukhavarṇaḥ smitapūrvaṃgamaḥ / ity evaṃbhāgīyāni rāgacaritasya pudgalasya liṅgāni veditavyāni //
body.translated_text: One is overcome by that obsession in regard to delightful <s>dharmas</s>, but is not able to overcome the delightful <s>dharmas</s>. One's faculties are smooth, not harsh, not rough, not coarse. One is not excessively of the nature of harming others, whether by body or speech. One is hard to alarm and hard to arouse [spiritually]. One is of low aspiration. One is firm in one's actions, steady in one's actions, firm in one's vows, steady in one's vows. One is patient and tolerant, of the nature of craving for requisites and possessions, giving them great weight. One is predominantly joyful, predominantly delighted, without furrowed brow, with an open and bright facial expression, and smiling as a forerunner [of speech]. Such and similar signs of the person of passionate temperament should be understood.

body.text:
-II-2-a-(3)-ii Ms.68a6L, Sh.185-17, P.85b6, D.71b4, N.75a6, Co.76a6, Ch.425c19
tatra dveṣacaritasya pudgalasya liṅgāni katamāni / iha dveṣacaritaḥ pudgalo (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> II 26

children.text: ) dveṣaṇīye vastuni parīttena pratighavastunimittena ghanaṃ prabhūtaṃ pratighaparyavasthānam utpādayati / kaḥ punar vādo madhyādhimātreṇa / tasya ca pratighaparyavasthānasya dīrghakālaṃ saṃtatim avasthāpayati / cirakālam anubaddho bhavati / pratighaparyavasthānena sa dveṣaṇīyair dharmair abhibhūyate / no tu dveṣaṇīyān dharmāñ chaknoty abhibhavitum / rūkṣendriyaś ca bhavati / kharendriyaḥ karkaśendriyaḥ paruṣendriyaś ca bhavati / atyarthaṃ ca pareṣāṃ viheṭhanajātīyo bhavati yaduta kāyena vācā / suvivejyaś ca bhavati susaṃvejyaḥ / dhvāṅkṣo bhavati mukharaḥ, pragalbhaḥ, anadhimuktibahulaḥ / na dṛḍhakarmanto na sthirakarmanto na dṛḍhavrato na sthiravrataḥ / daurmanasyabahulaś ca bhavaty upāyāsabahulaḥ / akṣamo bhavaty asahiṣṇuḥ, vilomanajātīyaḥ, apradakṣiṇagrāhī duṣpratyāneyajātīyaḥ, upanāhabahulaḥ / krūrāśayaś caṇḍaś ca bhavaty ādāśī pratyakṣaravādī so 'lpamātram apy uktaḥ sann abhiṣajyate, kupyati, vyāpadyate madguḥ pratitiṣṭhati kopaṃ saṃjanayati / vikṛtabhṛkuṭiś ca bhavati / anuttānamukhavarṇaḥ, parasaṃpattidveṣṭā, īrṣyābahulaḥ / ity evaṃbhāgīyāni dveṣacaritasya pudgalasya liṅgāni veditavyāni //
children.translated_text: in regard to an object of aversion, even with a minor cause and sign of hostility, produces an intense and abundant manifestation of hostile obsession. How much more so with middling or strong [causes]. And that hostile obsession persists in a continuous stream for a long duration; one is attached for a long time. One is overcome by the hostile obsession in regard to hateful <s>dharmas</s>, but is not able to overcome the hateful <s>dharmas</s>. One's faculties are dry, harsh, rough, and coarse. One is excessively of the nature of harming others, whether by body or speech. One is easily alarmed and easily aroused [spiritually]. One is crow-like, talkative, bold, predominantly lacking aspiration. One is not firm in one's actions, not steady in one's actions, not firm in one's vows, not steady in one's vows. One is predominantly displeased and distressed. One is impatient, intolerant, of contrary nature, grasping inauspiciously, of the nature that is hard to lead back, predominantly bearing grudges. One is of cruel disposition, fierce, hostile, retorting word for word — even when spoken to only slightly, one takes offense, becomes angry, becomes hostile, is like a cormorant, stands in opposition, and generates wrath. One's brow is furrowed, one's facial expression is not open, one hates the success of others, and is predominantly envious. Such and similar signs of the person of aversive temperament should be understood.

body.translated_text: Therein, what are the signs of the person of aversive temperament? Here, the person of aversive temperament,

body.text:
-II-2-a-(3)-iii Ms.68b1R, Sh.186-16, P.86a7, D.72a3, N.75b6, Co.76b5, Ch.426a4
tatra katamāni mohacaritasya pudgalasya liṅgāni / iha mohacaritaḥ pudgalo mohasthānīye vastuni parītte ghanaṃ prabhūtaṃ mohaparyavasthānam utpādayati / prāg eva madhyādhimātre / dīrghaṃ ca kālaṃ tasya mohaparyavasthānasya saṃtatim avasthāpayati / tena ca anubaddho bhavati / sa mohanīyair dharmair abhibhūyate / no tu mohanīyān dharmāñ chaknoty abhibhavitum / dhandhendriyaś ca bhavati / jaḍendriyaś ca bhavati, mandendriyaś ca śithilakāyakarmāntaḥ, śithilavākkarmāntaḥ, duścintitacintī, durbhāṣitabhāṣī, duṣkṛtakarmakārī, alaso 'nutthānasaṃpannaḥ, mandabhāṣī, durmedhaḥ, muṣitasmṛtiḥ, asaṃprajānadvihārī, vāmagrāhī, durvivejyaḥ, duḥsaṃvejyaḥ, hīnādhimuktikaḥ / jaḍa eḍamūko hastasaṃvācikaḥ / apratibalaḥ subhāṣitadurbhāṣitānāṃ dharmāṇām artham ājñātum / pratyayahāryaś ca bhavati parahāryaḥ parapraṇeyaḥ / ity evaṃbhāgīyāni mohacaritasya pudgalasya liṅgāni veditavyāni //
body.translated_text: Therein, what are the signs of a person of deluded character? Here, a person of deluded character, regarding an object that is a basis for delusion, even if slight, generates a thick and abundant mental obsession of delusion — how much more so regarding a moderate or intense [object]. One maintains the continuity of that mental obsession of delusion for a long time, and is bound by it. One is overpowered by <s>dharmas</s> conducive to delusion, but is unable to overpower the <s>dharmas</s> conducive to delusion. One's faculties are sluggish, one's faculties are dull, one's faculties are dim. One's bodily actions are slack, one's verbal actions are slack. One thinks badly-thought thoughts, speaks badly-spoken words, does badly-done deeds. One is lazy, devoid of initiative, slow of speech, of poor intelligence, with confused mindfulness, not dwelling in clear comprehension. One grasps perversely, is difficult to instruct, difficult to arouse spiritually, and of inferior inclination. One is dull, mute, communicating only by hand, incapable of understanding the meaning of well-spoken and ill-spoken <s>dharmas</s>. One is carried away by conditions, led by others, directed by others. Such and similar should be understood as the signs of a person of deluded character.

body.text:
-II-2-a-(3)-iv Ms.68b4M, Sh.187-13, P.86b7, D.72b1, N.76a5, Co.77a4, Ch.426a16
tatra katamāni mānacaritasya pudgalasya liṅgāni / iha mānacaritaḥ pudgalo mānasthānīye vastuni parītte 'pi ghanaṃ prabhūtamṃ mānaparyavasthānam utpādayati / kaḥ punar vādo madhyādhimātre / tasya ca mānaparyavasthānasya (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> II 30

children.text: ) dīrghakālaṃ saṃtatim avasthāpayati / tena cānubaddho bhavati / sa mānasthānīyair dharmair abhibhūyate / no tu mānasthānīyān dharmāñ chaknoty abhibhavitum / uddhatendriyaś ca bhavaty unnatendriyaś ca kāyamaṇḍanānuyogam anuyuktaś ca bhavati/ adhimātram unnatāṃ ca vācaṃ bhāṣate nāvanatām / mātāpitṛjñātigurusthānīyānāṃ ca na kālena kālaṃ yathānurūpām apacitiṃ kartā bhavati / stabdho bhavati, apraṇatakāyo nābhivādanavandanapratyutthānāñjalisāmīcīkarmaśīlaḥ / ātmapragrāhako bhavaty ātmotkarṣaparapaṃsakaḥ / lābhakāmaḥ satkārakāmaḥ kīrtiśabdaślokakāmaḥ / utplāvanābhāṇḍo durvivejyaś ca bhavati duḥsaṃvejyaḥ / udārādhimuktiś ca bhavati / mandakāruṇyaḥ / adhimātraṃ cātmasattvajīvapoṣapuruṣapudgaladṛṣṭimanyubahalo bhavati, upanāhī ca / ity evaṃbhāgīyāni mānacaritasya pudgalasya liṅgāni veditavyāni //
children.translated_text: ) one maintains the continuity for a long time, and is bound by it. One is overpowered by <s>dharmas</s> that are bases for pride, but is unable to overpower the <s>dharmas</s> that are bases for pride. One's faculties are agitated and excited. One is engaged in the pursuit of adorning the body. One speaks in an excessively elevated manner, never in a humble manner. One does not from time to time render appropriate service to mother, father, relatives, and those in the position of elders. One is rigid, with an unbent body, not given to the practice of greeting, salutation, rising, making the <s>añjali</s> (palms-joined gesture), and respectful acts. One is a grasper of self, one who exalts oneself and disparages others. One desires gain, desires honor, desires fame and renown and praise. One is a vessel of pretension, difficult to instruct, and difficult to arouse spiritually. One is of lofty inclination but of little compassion. One is abundantly endowed with the view of a self, being, soul, nourisher, person, and individual, intensely so, and is resentful and grudging. Such and similar should be understood as the signs of a person of prideful character.

body.translated_text: Therein, what are the signs of a person of prideful character? Here, a person of prideful character, regarding an object that is a basis for pride, even if slight, generates a thick and abundant mental obsession of pride — how much more so regarding a moderate or intense [object]. Of that mental obsession of pride,

body.text:
-II-2-a-(3)-v Ms.68b8R, Sh.188-15, P.87a7, D.72b7, N.76b4, Co.77b3, Ch.426b1
tatra katamāni vitarkacaritasya pudgalasya liṅgāni / iha vitarkacaritaḥ pudgalo vitarkasthānīye vastuni parītte 'pi ghanaṃ prabhūtaṃ vitarkaparyavasthānam utpādayati / kaḥ punar vādo madhyādhimātre / tac ca paryavasthānaṃ dīrghakālam avasthāpayati / tena cānubaddho (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> II 32

children.text: ) bhavati / sa vitarkasthānīyair dharmair abhibhūyate / no tu vitarkasthānīyān dharmāñ chaknoty abhibhavitum / asthirendriyaś ca bhavati capalendriyaś cañcalendriyo vyākulendriyaḥ / tvaritakāyakarmāntas tvaritavākkarmāntaḥ / durvivejyo duḥsaṃvejyaḥ / prapañcārāmaḥ prapañcarataḥ / kāṅkṣābahulo vicikitsābahulaḥ / chandikaś ca bhavaty asthiravrato 'niścitavrataḥ / asthirakarmānto 'niścitakarmāntaḥ / śaṃkābahulaḥ pramuṣitasmṛtiḥ / vivekānabhirato vikṣepabahulaḥ / lokacitreṣu chandarāgānusṛtaḥ, dakṣo 'nalasa utthānasaṃpannaḥ / ity evaṃbhāgīyāni vitarkacaritasya pudgalasya liṅgāni veditavyāni /
children.translated_text: ) One is overpowered by <s>dharmas</s> that are bases for discursive thought, but is unable to overpower the <s>dharmas</s> that are bases for discursive thought. One's faculties are unstable, agitated, restless, and disturbed. One's bodily actions are hasty, one's verbal actions are hasty. One is difficult to instruct and difficult to arouse spiritually. One delights in conceptual proliferation, is attached to conceptual proliferation. One is abundant in doubt and uncertainty. One is eager but unsteady in one's vows, undecided in one's vows; unsteady in one's actions, undecided in one's actions; abundant in suspicion, with confused mindfulness. One does not delight in seclusion and is abundant in distraction. One follows after desire and passion for the manifold things of the world, yet is skillful, not lazy, and endowed with initiative. Such and similar should be understood as the signs of a person of discursive character.

body.translated_text: Therein, what are the signs of a person of discursive character? Here, a person of discursive character, regarding an object that is a basis for discursive thought, even if slight, generates a thick and abundant mental obsession of discursive thought — how much more so regarding a moderate or intense [object]. One maintains the continuity of that obsession for a long time, and is bound by it.

body.text: idaṃ caritaprabhedena pudgalavyavasthānaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text: This should be understood as the classification of persons by distinction of character.

body.text:
-II-2-a-(4) Ms.69a3L, Sh.189-11, P.87b8, D.73a6, N.77a3, Co.78a2, Ch.426b14
tatra81 praṇidhānaprabhedena pudgalavyavasthānam / asti pudgalaḥ śrāvakayāne kṛtapraṇidhānaḥ, asti pratyekabuddhayāne, asti mahāyāne / tatra yo 'yaṃ pudgalaḥ śrāvakayāne kṛtapraṇidhānaḥ sa syāc chrāvakagotraḥ, syāt pratyekabuddhagotraḥ, syān mahāyānagotraḥ / tatra yo 'yaṃ pudgalaḥ pratyekāyāṃ bodhau kṛtapraṇidhānaḥ so 'pi syāt pratyekabuddhagotraḥ, syāc chrāvakagotraḥ, syān mahāyānagotraḥ / tatra yo 'yaṃ pudgalo mahāyāne kṛtapraṇidhānaḥ so 'pi syāc chrāvakagotraḥ, syāt pratyekabuddhagotraḥ, syān mahāyānagotraḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the classification of persons by distinction of aspiration? There is a person who has made an aspiration in the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> (disciples' vehicle), there is one in the <s>Pratyekabuddhayāna</s> (solitary buddhas' vehicle), and there is one in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (great vehicle). Therein, a person who has made an aspiration in the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> may be of the <s>śrāvaka</s> lineage, or of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> lineage, or of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> lineage. Therein, a person who has made an aspiration for solitary awakening may also be of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> lineage, or of the <s>śrāvaka</s> lineage, or of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> lineage. Therein, a person who has made an aspiration in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> may also be of the <s>śrāvaka</s> lineage, or of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> lineage, or of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> lineage.

body.text: tatra yo 'yaṃ śrāvakagotraḥ pudgalaḥ pratyekāyāṃ bodhāv anuttarāyāṃ vā samyaksaṃbodhau kṛtapraṇidhānaḥ, sa śrāvakagotratvād avaśyam ante kāle (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> II 34

children.text: ) tatpraṇidhānaṃ vyāvartya śrāvakayānapraṇidhāna evāvatiṣṭhate / evaṃ pratyekabuddhayānagotro mahāyānagotro veditavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: ) turn away from that aspiration and settle in the aspiration for the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> alone. Similarly, one of the <s>Pratyekabuddhayāna</s> lineage and one of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> lineage should be understood.

body.translated_text: Therein, a person of the <s>śrāvaka</s> lineage who has made an aspiration for solitary awakening or for unsurpassed perfect awakening — that one, being of the <s>śrāvaka</s> lineage, will inevitably in the end

body.text: tatra bhavaty eṣāṃ pudgalānāṃ praṇidhānasaṃcāraḥ praṇidhānavyatikaraḥ / no tu gotrasaṃcāraḥ, gotravyatikaraḥ / asmiṃs tv arthe śrāvakayānapraṇidhānāḥ śrāvakagotrāś caite pudgalā veditavyāḥ / evaṃ praṇidhānaprabhedena pudgalavyavasthānaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: Therein, for these persons there may be a shift of aspiration, a crossing over of aspiration; but there is no shift of lineage, no crossing over of lineage. In this context, these persons should be understood as having the aspiration for the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> and as being of the <s>śrāvaka</s> lineage. Thus the classification of persons by distinction of aspiration is [established].

body.text:
-II-2-a-(5) Ms.69a6L, Sh.190-8, Choi.162-6, P.88b1, D.73b5, N.77b2, Co.78b1, Ch.426c2
kathaṃ pratipatprabhedena pudgalavyavasthānaṃ bhavati / eṣāṃ yathoddiṣṭānāṃ yathāparikīrtitānāṃ pudgalānāṃ catasṛbhiḥ pratipadbhir niryāṇaṃ bhavati / katamābhiś catasṛbhiḥ / asti pratipad duḥkhā dhandhābhijñā/ asti pratipad duḥkhā kṣiprābhijñā / asti pratipat sukhā dhandhābhijñā / asti pratipat sukhā kṣiprābhijñā /
body.translated_text: How is the classification of persons by distinction of practice? For these persons as described and enumerated, the going forth is by means of four practices. Which four? There is the practice that is painful with slow higher knowledge; there is the practice that is painful with swift higher knowledge; there is the practice that is pleasant with slow higher knowledge; and there is the practice that is pleasant with swift higher knowledge.

body.text: tatra mṛdvindriyasya pudgalasya mauladhyānālābhino yā pratipad iyam ucyate duḥkhā dhandhābhijñā / tatra tīkṣṇendriyasya pudgalasya mauladhyānālābhino yā pratipad iyam ucyate duḥkhā kṣiprābhijñā / tatra mṛdvindriyasya pudgalasya mauladhyānalābhino yā pratipad iyam ucyate sukhā dhandhābhijñā / tatra tīkṣṇendriyasya pudgalasya mauladhyānalābhino yā pratipad iyam ucyate sukhā kṣiprābhijñā / evaṃ pratipatprabhedena pudgalavyavasthānaṃ veditavyam /
body.translated_text: Therein, for a person of mild faculties who has not obtained the fundamental <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), that practice is called painful with slow higher knowledge. For a person of sharp faculties who has not obtained the fundamental <s>dhyāna</s>, that practice is called painful with swift higher knowledge.
