For a person of mild faculties who has obtained the fundamental <s>dhyāna</s>, that practice is called pleasant with slow higher knowledge. For a person of sharp faculties who has obtained the fundamental <s>dhyāna</s>, that practice is called pleasant with swift higher knowledge. Thus the classification of persons by distinction of practice should be understood.

body.text:
-II-2-a-(6) Ms.69a8M, Sh.190-22, P.88b7, D.74a1, N.77b6, Co.78b5, Ch.426c13
tatra kathaṃ mārgaphalaprabhedena pudgalavyavasthānaṃ veditavyam / tadyathā caturṇāṃ pratipannakānāṃ srota-āpattiphalapratipannakasya, sakṛdāgāmiphalapratipannakasya, anāgāmiphalapratipannakasya, arhattvaphalapratipannakasya / (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> II 36

children.text: ) caturṇāṃ ca phalasthānāṃ, srota-āpannasya, sakṛdāgāmino, 'nāgāmino, 'rhataś ca / ye pratipannakamārge vartante te pratipannakās teṣāṃ pratipannakamārgeṇa vyavasthānam / ye tatphalaśrāmaṇyaphalavyavasthitās teṣāṃ mārgaphalavyavasthānam / evaṃ mārgaphalaprabhedena pudgalavyavasthānaṃ bhavati //
children.translated_text: ) and of the four who are established in the fruit — the stream-enterer, the once-returner, the non-returner, and the <s>arhat</s> (worthy one). Those who abide on the path of practice — they are the practitioners, and their classification is by the path of practice. Those who are established in the fruit of their <s>śrāmaṇya</s> (ascetic life) — their classification is by path and fruit. Thus the classification of persons by distinction of path and fruit is [established].

body.translated_text: Therein, how should the classification of persons by distinction of path and fruit be understood? Namely: of the four who are practicing — the one practicing toward the fruit of stream-entry, the one practicing toward the fruit of once-returning, the one practicing toward the fruit of non-returning, and the one practicing toward the fruit of <s>arhatship</s> (worthy-ship);

body.text:
-II-2-a-(7) Ms.69b1R, Sh.191-10, P.89a4, D.74a5, N.78a3, Co.79a2, Ch.426c22
kathaṃ prayogaprabhedena pudgalavyavasthānaṃ bhavati / tadyathā śraddhānusāridharmānusāriṇā / no yaḥ pudgalaḥ śraddhānusāreṇa prayuktaḥ sa śraddhānusārī / yo dharmeṣu aparapratyayavinayānusāreṇa prayuktaḥ sa dharmānusārī / evaṃ prayogaprabhedena pudgalavyavasthānaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: How is the classification of persons by distinction of mode of application? Namely: of the faith-follower and the <s>Dharma</s>-follower. A person who is engaged in following faith is not [merely] a faith-follower; rather, one who is engaged in following the <s>Dharma</s> without depending on another's guidance is a <s>Dharma</s>-follower. Thus the classification of persons by distinction of mode of application is [established].

body.text:
-II-2-a-(8) Ms.69b2R, Sh.191-15, P.89a6, D.74a7, N.78a5, Co.79a3, Ch.426c27
tatra katham samāpattiprabhedena pudgalavyavasthānaṃ bhavati / tadyathā kāyasākṣy aṣṭau vimokṣān kāyena sākṣātkṛtvopasaṃpadya viharati / na ca sarveṇa sarvam āsravakṣayam anuprāpto bhavati / rūpī rūpāṇi paśyati / adhyātmam arūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyati / śubhaṃ vimokṣaṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> II 38

children.text: ) kāyena sākṣātkṛtvopasaṃpadya viharati / akāśānantyāyatanam, vijñ snānantyāyatanam, ākiñcanyāyatanam, naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanam, )saṃjñāvedayitanirodham anulomapratilomaṃ samāpadyate ca, vyuttiṣṭhate ca / evaṃ samāpattiprabhedena pudgalavyavasthānaṃ bhavati //
children.translated_text: ) [Then:] The sphere of infinite space, the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception — one enters into and arises from the cessation of perception and feeling, both in forward and reverse order. Thus the classification of persons by distinction of attainment is [established].

body.translated_text: Therein, how is the classification of persons by distinction of attainment? Namely: the body-witness, who, having realized the eight liberations with the body, enters into and dwells in them, but has not in every way attained the destruction of the <s>āśravas</s> (defilements). [The eight liberations are:] Possessing form, one sees forms. Without the perception of form internally, one sees forms externally. One enters into and dwells in the liberation of the beautiful.

body.text:
-II-2-a-(9) Ms.69b4L, Sh.192-3, P.89b3, D.74b3, N.78b1, Co.79a7, Ch.427a6
katham upapattiprabhedena pudgalavyavasthānaṃ bhavati / tadyathā saptakṛdbhavaparamasya, kulaṃkulasya, ekavīcikasya, antarāparinirvāyiṇaḥ, upapadyaparinirvāyiṇaḥ, anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyiṇaḥ, sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyiṇaḥ, ūrdhvaṃsrotasaś ca / evam upapattiprabhedena pudgalavyavasthānaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: How is the classification of persons by distinction of rebirth? Namely: one who has at most seven existences, one who goes from family to family, one who has one more intervening [birth], one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the intermediate state, one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> upon rebirth, one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> without effort, one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> with effort, and one who goes upstream. Thus the classification of persons by distinction of rebirth is [established].

body.text:
-II-2-a-(10) Ms.69b5L, Sh.192-7, P.89b6, D.74b5, N.78b3, Co.79b2, Ch.427a10
kathaṃ parihāṇiprabhedena pudgalavyavasthānaṃ bhavati / tadyathā samayavimuktasyārhato yo bhavyo dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārebhyaḥ parihāṇāya / aparihāṇiprabhedena punar vyavasthānam / akopyadharmakasyārhato yo na bhavyo dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārebhyaḥ parihāṇāya / evam aparihāṇiprabhedena pudgalavyavasthānaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: How is the classification of persons by distinction of decline? Namely: of a time-liberated <s>arhat</s> who is capable of declining from the pleasant dwellings in the present life. The classification by distinction of non-decline: of an <s>arhat</s> whose <s>dharma</s> is unshakable, who is not capable of declining from the pleasant dwellings in the present life. Thus the classification of persons by distinction of non-decline is [established].

body.text:
-II-2-a-(11) Ms.69b6L, Sh.192-13, P.90a1, D.74b7, N.78b5, Co.79b4, Ch.427a14
tatra katham āvaraṇaprabhedena pudgalavyavasthānaṃ bhavati / tadyathā prajñāvimuktasyobhayatobhāgavimuktasyārhataḥ / tatra prajñāvimukto 'rhan kleśāvaraṇavimuktaḥ, na samāpattyāvaraṇāt / ubhayatobhāgavimuktas tv arhan kleśāvaraṇāc ca vimuktaḥ samāpattyāvaraṇāc ca / tasmād ubhayatobhāgavimukta (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> II 40

children.text: ) ity ucyate / evam āvaraṇaprabhedena pudgalavyavasthānaṃ bhavati //
children.translated_text: ). Thus the classification of persons by distinction of obstruction is [established].

body.translated_text: Therein, how is the classification of persons by distinction of obstruction? Namely: of the wisdom-liberated <s>arhat</s> and the both-ways-liberated <s>arhat</s>. Therein, the wisdom-liberated <s>arhat</s> is freed from the obstruction of afflictions but not from the obstruction of attainments. But the both-ways-liberated <s>arhat</s> is freed from both the obstruction of afflictions and the obstruction of attainments. Therefore one is called 'both-ways-liberated'

body.text:
-II-2-b Ms.69b7L, Sh.192-19, P.90a4, D.75a2, N.79a1, Co.79b6, Ch.427a20
ebhiḥ prabhedair yathoddiṣṭair yathoddiṣṭānāṃ pudgalānāṃ yathākramaṃ vyavasthānaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text: By these distinctions as enumerated, the classification of the enumerated persons should be understood in due order.

body.text:
(II)-A-II-3 Ms.69b7M, Sh.192-21, Sa.4-2, W.86-1, P.90a5, D.75a3, N.79a2, Co.79b7, Ch.427a22
tatrālambanaṃ katamat / āha / catvāry ālambanavastūni / katamāni catvāri / vyāpy ālambanam, caritaviśodhanam ālambanam, kauśalyālambanam, kleśaviśodhanaṃ cālambanam //
body.translated_text: (II)-A-II-3 — Therein, what is the object? It is said: There are four object-substrata. Which four? The all-pervading object, the object for purifying conduct, the object of skill, and the object for purifying the afflictions.

body.text:
-II-3-a-(1) Ms.69b7R, Sh.193-4, Sa.4-6, P.90a6, D.75a4, N.79a3, Co.80a1, Ch.427a24
tatra vyāpy ālambanaṃ katamat / āha / tad api caturvidham / tadyathā avikalpaṃ pratibimbam, nirvikalpaṃ pratibimbaṃ, vastuparyantatā, kāryapariniṣpattiś ca //
body.translated_text: -II-3-a-(1) — Therein, what is the all-pervading object? It is said: That too is fourfold, namely: the discursive image, the non-discursive image, the limit of things, and the accomplishment of the purpose.

body.text:
-II-3-a-(1)-i Ms.69b8M, Sh.193-7, Sa.4-10, P.90a8, D.75a5, N.79a4, Co.80a2, Ch.427a27
tatra savikalpaṃ pratibimbaṃ katamat / yathāpīhaikatyaḥ saddharmaśravaṇaṃ vāvavādānuśāsanīṃ vā niśritya, dṛṣṭaṃ vā, śrutaṃ vā, parikalpitaṃ vopādāya jñeyavastusabhāgaṃ pratibimbam samāhitabhūmikair vipaśyanākārair vipaśyati, vicinoti, pravicinoti, parivitarkayati, parimīmāṃsāṃ āpadyate /
body.translated_text: -II-3-a-(1)-i — Therein, what is the discursive image? Just as here someone, relying on hearing the true <s>Dharma</s>, or on instruction and admonition, takes up what has been seen, or heard, or imagined, and by means of the modes of <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) belonging to the level of concentration, one examines, investigates, thoroughly investigates, deliberates, and arrives at assessment — with respect to an image that resembles the knowable object.

body.text: tatra jñeyaṃ vastu / tadyathāśubhā vā, maitrī vā, idaṃpratyayatāpratītyasamutpādo vā, dhātuprabhedo vā, ānāpānasmṛtir vā, skandhakauśalyaṃ vā, dhātukauśalyam āyatanakauśalyaṃ, pratītyasamutpādakauśalyaṃ, sthānāsthānakauśalyam, adhobhūmīnām audārikatvaṃ, uparibhūmīnāṃ śāntatvaṃ, duḥkhasatyam, samudayasatyaṃ, nirodhasatyaṃ, mārgasatyam / idam ucyate jñeyaṃ vastu /
body.translated_text: Therein, the knowable object is: such as the <s>aśubhā</s> (contemplation of the unpleasant), or <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), or the conditionality of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), or the analysis of <s>dhātus</s> (elements), or <s>ānāpānasmṛti</s> (mindfulness of breathing), or skill in the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), skill in the <s>dhātus</s> (elements), skill in the <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), skill in <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), skill in what is possible and impossible, the coarseness of the lower realms, the peacefulness of the higher realms, the truth of suffering, the truth of origination, the truth of cessation, the truth of the path — this is called the knowable object.

body.text: tasyāsya jñeyavastuno 'vavādānuśāsanīṃ vāgamya, saddharmaśravaṇam vā, tanniśrayeṇa samāhitabhūmikaṃ manaskāraṃ saṃmukhīkṛtya, tān eva dharmān (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 44

children.text: ) adhimucyate tad eva jñeyaṃ vastv adhimucyate / tasya tasmin samaye pratyakṣānubhāvika ivādhimokṣaḥ pravartate jñeyavastuni / na taj jñeyaṃ vastu pratyakṣībhūtaṃ bhavati samavahitaṃ saṃmukhībhūtam / na ca punar anyat tajjātīyaṃ dravyam / api tv adhimokṣānubhavaḥ sa tādṛśo manaskārānubhavaḥ samāhitabhūmikaḥ, yena tasya jñeyasya vastuno 'nusadṛśaṃ tad bhavati pratibhāsam / yena tad ucyate jñeyavastusabhāgaṃ pratibimbam iti / yad ayaṃ yogī santīrayaṃs tasmin prakṛte jñeye vastuni parīkṣye guṇadoṣāvadhāraṇaṃ karoti / idam ucyate savikalpaṃ pratibimbam //
children.translated_text: At that time, one's resolution operates as if it were a direct experience with respect to the knowable object. But that knowable object has not become directly perceived, set before one, and face-to-face. Nor is it another real substance of the same kind. Rather, it is such an experience of resolution, such an experience of mental engagement belonging to the level of concentration, by which there arises an appearance similar to that knowable object. Therefore it is called 'an image resembling the knowable object.' When this <s>yogī</s> (meditator), exploring that given knowable object under investigation, makes a determination of merits and faults — this is called the discursive image.

body.translated_text: For that knowable object of one's, relying on instruction and admonition, or on hearing the true <s>Dharma</s>, based on that, having brought to the fore a mental engagement belonging to the level of concentration, one resolves upon those very <s>dharmas</s>, one resolves upon that very knowable object.

body.text:
-II-3-a-(1)-ii Ms.70a4L, Sh. 194-21, Sa.6-4, W.86-9, P.91a4, D.75b5, N.79b5, Co.80b3, Ch.427b15
nirvikalpaṃ pratibimbaṃ katamat / ihāyaṃ yogī pratibimnanimittam udgṛhya na punar vipaśyati, vicinoti, prativicinoti, parivitarkayati, parimīmāṃsām āpadyate / api tu tad evālambanam amukto śamathākāreṇa tac cittaṃ śamayati / yaduta navākārayā cittasthityādhyātmam eva cittaṃ sthāpayati, saṃsthāpayati, avasthāpayati, upasthāpayati, damayati, śamayati, vyupaśamayati, ekotīkaroti, samādhatte / tasya tasmin samaye nirvikalpaṃ (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 46

children.text: ) tat pratibimbam ālambanaṃ bhavati / yatrāsāv ekāṃśenaikāgrāṃ smṛtim avasthāpayati, tad ālambanam / no tu vipaśyati, vicinoti, prativicinoti, parivitarkayati, parimīmāṃsām āpadyate /
children.translated_text: image becomes the object — that upon which one fixes one-pointed, single-minded <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness), that is the object. But one does not examine, investigate, thoroughly investigate, deliberate, or arrive at assessment.

body.translated_text: -II-3-a-(1)-ii — What is the non-discursive image? Here this <s>yogī</s>, having grasped the sign of the image, no longer examines, investigates, thoroughly investigates, deliberates, or arrives at assessment. Rather, taking that very object, without releasing it, one calms the mind by the mode of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) — namely, by the nine modes of mental stability, one inwardly fixes the mind, steadies it, settles it, establishes it, tames it, calms it, thoroughly calms it, unifies it, and concentrates it. At that time, the non-discursive

body.text: tac ca pratibimbaṃ pratibimbam ity ucyate / [tiṅ ṅe 'dzin gyi mtshan ma daṅ / tiṅ ṅe 'dzin gyi spyod yul gyi yul daṅ / tiṅ ṅe 'dzin gyi thabs daṅ / tiṅ ṅe 'dzin gyi sgo daṅ / yid la byed pa'i rten daṅ / naṅ du rnam par rtog pa'i lus daṅ / snaṅ brñan źes kyaṅ bya ste] / itīmāni tasya jñeyavastusabhāgasya pratibimbasya paryāyanāmāni veditavyāni //
body.translated_text: And that image is called 'image.' [The sign of concentration, the domain of the sphere of concentration, the means of concentration, the door of concentration, the basis of mental engagement, the body of internal conceptualization, and the image — thus these] should be understood as the synonyms of that image resembling the knowable object.

body.text:
-II-3-a-(1)-iii Ms.70a6L, Sh.195-13, Sa.7-6, P.91b3, D.76a3, N.80a3, Co,81a1, Ch.427b28
vastuparyantatā katamā / yālambanasya yāvadbhāvikatā yathāvadbhāvikatā ca /
body.translated_text: -II-3-a-(1)-iii — What is the limit of things? It is the extensiveness and the trueness of the object.

body.text: tatra yāvadbhāvikatā katamā / yasmāt pareṇa nāsti rūpaskandho vā, vedanāskandho vā, saṃjñāskandho vā, saṃskāraskandho vā, vijñānaskandho veti sarvasaṃskṛtavastusaṃgrahaḥ pañcabhir dharmaiḥ / sarvadharmasaṃgraho dhātubhir āyatanaiḥ sarvajñeyavastusaṃgrahaś cāryasatyaiḥ / iyam ucyate yāvadbhāvikatā /
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the extensiveness? Beyond which there is nothing further — the aggregate of form, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of volitional formations, the aggregate of consciousness — the inclusion of all conditioned things under five <s>dharmas</s>; the inclusion of all <s>dharmas</s> under the <s>dhātus</s> (elements) and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases); and the inclusion of all knowable things under the Noble Truths — this is called extensiveness.

body.text: tatra yathāvadbhāvikatā katamā / yālambanasya bhūtatā tathatā / catasṛbhir yuktibhir yuktyupetatā / yadutāpekṣāyuktyā, kāryakāraṇayuktyā, upapattisādhanayuktyā, dharmatāyuktyā ca / iti yā cālambanasya yāvadbhāvikatā yā ca (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 48

children.text: ) yathāvadbhāvikatā tad ekadhyam abhisaṃkṣipya vastuparyantatety ucyate //
children.translated_text: the extensiveness and the trueness of the object — combining those into one, it is called 'the limit of things.'

body.translated_text: Therein, what is the trueness? It is the reality and suchness of the object, the accordance with four types of reasoning — namely, the reasoning of dependency, the reasoning of cause and effect, the reasoning of proof by evidence, and the reasoning of the nature of things. Thus whatever is

body.text:
-II-3-a-(1)-iv Ms.70b1R, Sh.196-12, Sa.8-8, P.92a1, D.76a7, N.80b1, Co.81a5, Ch.427c8
tatra kāryapariniṣpattiḥ katamā / yad asya yogina āsevanānvayād bhāvanānvayād bahulīkārānvayāc chamathavipaśyanāyā yah pratibimbālambano manaskāraḥ sa paripūryate / tatparipūryāś cāśrayaḥ parivartate / sarvadauṣṭhulyāni ca pratipraśrabhyante / āśrayaparivṛtteś ca pratibimbam atikramya tasminn eva jñeye vastuni nirvikalpaṃ pratyakṣaṃ jñānadarśanam utpadyate / prathamadhyānasamāpattuḥ prathamadhyānalābhinaḥ prathamadhyānagocare, dvitīyatṛtīyacaturthadhyānasamāpattuś caturthadhyānalābhinaś caturthadhyānagocare, ākāśānantyāyatanavijñānānantyāyatanākiñcanyāyatananaivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanasamāpattus taIIābhinas tadgocare / iyam ucyate kāryapariniṣpattiḥ //
body.translated_text: -II-3-a-(1)-iv — Therein, what is the accomplishment of the purpose? When, through repeated practice, cultivation, and frequent application, the mental engagement of this <s>yogī</s> that takes the image as its object in <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) reaches fulfillment, and from that fulfillment the basis undergoes transformation, and all forms of unsuitability are calmed, and through the transformation of the basis, having transcended the image, with respect to that very knowable object, non-discursive, direct knowledge and vision arises — [whether of] the attainment of the first <s>dhyāna</s>, for one who has obtained the first <s>dhyāna</s>, in the domain of the first <s>dhyāna</s>; the attainment of the second, third, and fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, for one who has obtained the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, in the domain of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>; [or] the attainment of the sphere of infinite space, the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, and the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, for one who has obtained those, in those domains — this is called the accomplishment of the purpose.

body.text: tāny etāni bhavanti catvāry ālambanavastūni sarvatragāni sarveṣv ālambaneṣv anugatāni / atītānāgatapratyutpannaiḥ samyaksambuddhair deśitāni / tenaitad vyāpy ālambanam ity ucyate /
body.translated_text: These are the four object-substrata, which are all-pervading, running through all objects, taught by the perfectly awakened ones of past, future, and present. Therefore this is called the all-pervading object.

body.text: api caitad ālambanam śamathapakṣyaṃ vipaśyanāpakṣyaṃ sarvavastukam bhūtavastukaṃ, hetuphalavastukaṃ ca / tena tad vyāpīty ucyate / yat tāvad t āha "savikalpaṃ pratibimbam" itīdam atra vipaśyanapakṣyasya / yat punar āha "nirvikalpaṃ pratibimbam" itīdam atra śamathapakṣyasya / yat punar āha "vastuparyantate" tīdam atra sarvavastukatāyā bhūtavastukatāyāś ca / yad āha "kāryapariniṣpattir" itīdam atra hetuphalasaṃbandhasya //
body.translated_text: Moreover, this object belongs to the side of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding), belongs to the side of <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), encompasses all things, [encompasses] real things, and [encompasses] cause-and-effect things. Therefore it is called 'all-pervading.' The statement: 'the discursive image' — this belongs here to the side of <s>vipaśyanā</s>. The statement: 'the non-discursive image' — this belongs here to the side of <s>śamatha</s>. The statement: 'the limit of things' — this belongs here to the totality of all things and the reality of things. The statement: 'the accomplishment of the purpose' — this belongs here to the connection of cause and effect.

body.text:
-II-3-a-(2)-i Ms.70b5R, Sh.197-17, Sa.9-13, W.86-32, P.92b5, D.77a1, N.81a3, Co.81b7, Ch.427c27
yathoktaṃ bhagavatāyuṣmantaṃ revatam ārabhya /
body.translated_text: -II-3-a-(2)-i — As spoken by the <s>Bhagavat</s> with reference to the venerable <s>Revata</s>:

body.text: "evam anuśrūyate", āyuṣmān revato bhagavantaṃ praśnam aprākṣīt /
body.translated_text: "Thus it has been heard." The venerable <s>Revata</s> asked the <s>Bhagavat</s> a question:

body.text: "kiyati, bhadanta, bhikṣur yogī yogācāra ālambane cittam upanibadhnāti. katamasminn ālambane cittam upanibadhnātī"ti / "kathaṃ punar ālambane cittam upanibaddhaṃ sūpanibaddhaṃ bhavati" //
body.translated_text: "In how many [objects], Venerable Sir, does a <s>bhikṣu</s>, a <s>yogī</s> and practitioner of <s>yoga</s>, fix the mind on an object? On which object does one fix the mind?" "And how does the mind, fixed on an object, become well-fixed?"

body.text:
-II-3-a-(2)-ii-(a) Ms.70b6M, Sh. 198-4, Sa.10-4, W.'86-37, P.92b8, D.77a2, N.81a4, Co.82a2, Ch.428a3
bhagavān āha / "sādhu, sādhu, revata, sādhu khalu tvaṃ revata, etam arthaṃ pṛcchasi / tena hi śṛṇu sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuru, bhāṣiṣye / iha, revata, bhikṣur yogī yogācāraś caritaṃ vā viśodhayitukāmaḥ, kauśalyaṃ vā kartukāmaḥ, āsravebhyo vā cittaṃ vimocayitukāmaḥ, anurūpe cālambane cittam upanibadhnāti, pratirūpe ca samyag eva copanibadhnāti, tatra cānirākṛtadhyāyī bhavati /
body.translated_text: -II-3-a-(2)-ii-(a) — The <s>Bhagavat</s> said: "Good, good, <s>Revata</s>! It is good indeed that you ask this question. Then listen well and thoroughly, pay attention, I shall speak. Here, <s>Revata</s>, a <s>bhikṣu</s>, a <s>yogī</s> and practitioner of <s>yoga</s>, wishing to purify conduct, or wishing to develop skill, or wishing to liberate the mind from the <s>āśravas</s> (defilements), fixes the mind on a suitable object, on a proper object, and fixes it rightly — and therein one is an unobstructed meditator.

body.text: katham anurūpa ālambane cittam upanibadhnāti / saced revata, bhikṣur yogī yogācāro rāgacarita eva sann aśubhālambane cittam upanibadhnāti / evam anurūpa ālambane cittam upanibadhnāti, dveṣacarito vā punar maitryām / mohacarito vedaṃpratyayatāpratītyasamutpāde, mānacarito vā dhātuprabhede / saced revata, sa bhikṣur yogī yogācāro vitarkacarita eva sann ānāpānasmṛtau (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 52

children.text: ) cittam upanibadhnāti / evaṃ so 'nurūpa ālambane cittam upanibadhnāti /
children.translated_text: Thus one fixes the mind on a suitable object.

body.translated_text: How does one fix the mind on a suitable object? If, <s>Revata</s>, a <s>bhikṣu</s>, a <s>yogī</s> and practitioner of <s>yoga</s>, is of passionate temperament, one fixes the mind on the object of the <s>aśubhā</s> (unpleasant). Thus one fixes the mind on a suitable object. If of hateful temperament, [one fixes the mind] on <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness). If of deluded temperament, on the conditionality of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination). If of conceited temperament, on the analysis of <s>dhātus</s> (elements). If, <s>Revata</s>, that <s>bhikṣu</s>, the <s>yogī</s> and practitioner of <s>yoga</s>, is of discursive temperament, one fixes the mind on <s>ānāpānasmṛti</s> (mindfulness of breathing).

body.text: sacet sa revata, bhikṣuḥ saṃskārāṇāṃ svalakṣaṇe saṃmūdha ātmasattvajīvajantupoṣapudgalavastusaṃmūḍhaḥ skandhakauśalye cittam upanibadhnāti / hetusaṃmūdho dhātukauśalye, pratyayasaṃmūdha āyatanakauśalye, anityaduḥkhānātmasaṃmūḍhaḥ pratītyasamutpādasthānāsthānakauśalye, kāmadhātor vā vairāgyaṃ kartukāmaḥ, kāmānām audārikatve rūpāṇāṃ śāntatve, rūpebhyo vā vairāgyaṃ kartukāmo rūpāṇām audārikatva ārūpyaśāntatāyāṃ ca cittam upanibadhnāti / sarvatra vā satkāyān nirvettukāmaḥ, vimoktukāmaḥ, duḥkhasatye samudayasatye, nirodhasatye, mārgasatye cittam upanibadhnāti / evaṃ hi, revata, bhikṣur yogī yogacāro 'nurūpa ālambane cittam upanibadhnāti //
body.translated_text: If, <s>Revata</s>, that <s>bhikṣu</s> is confused about the own-characteristics of formations, confused about self, being, life, creature, nurturer, person, and substance — one fixes the mind on skill in the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates). If confused about causes, on skill in the <s>dhātus</s> (elements). If confused about conditions, on skill in the <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases). If confused about impermanence, suffering, and non-self, on skill in <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) and in what is possible and impossible. If wishing to become dispassionate toward the desire-realm, [one fixes the mind] on the coarseness of sensual pleasures and the peacefulness of forms. If wishing to become dispassionate toward the form-realm, [one fixes the mind] on the coarseness of forms and the peacefulness of the formless [realm]. If wishing to become disenchanted with and liberated from all embodied existence, one fixes the mind on the truth of suffering, the truth of origination, the truth of cessation, and the truth of the path. Thus, <s>Revata</s>, a <s>bhikṣu</s>, a <s>yogī</s> and practitioner of <s>yoga</s>, fixes the mind on a suitable object.

body.text:
-II-3-a-(2)-2-ii-(b) Ms.71a5M, Sh.199-(9), Sa.11-13, P.93b7, D.77b5, N.82a1, Co.82b5, Ch.428a28
kathaṃ ca revata, bhikṣur yogī yogācāraḥ pratirūpa ālambane cittam upanibadhnāti / iha revata, bhikṣur yad yad eva jñeyaṃ vastu vicetukāmo bhavati, pravicetukāmaḥ parivitarkayitukāmaḥ parimīmāṃsayitukāmaḥ, tac ca tena pūrvam eva dṛṣṭaṃ vā bhavati, śrutaṃ vā mataṃ vā vijñātaṃ vā / sa tad eva dṛṣṭam adhipatiṃ kṛtvā śrutaṃ mataṃ vijñātam adhipatiṃ kṛtvā samāhitabhūmikena manaskāreṇa manasikaroti / vikalpayaty adhimucyate / sa na tad eva jñeyaṃ vastu samavahitaṃ saṃmukhībhūtaṃ paśyaty api tu tatpratirūpakam asyotpadyate tatpratibhāsaṃ vā, jñānamātraṃ vā, darśanamātraṃ vā, pratismṛtamātraṃ vā yadālambanam ayaṃ bhikṣur yogī yogācāraḥ kālena kālaṃ cittam saṃśamayati, kālena kālam adhiprajñe dharmavipaśyanāyāṃ (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 54

children.text: ) yogaṃ karoti / evaṃ hi sa revata, bhikṣur yogī yogācāraḥ pratirūpa ālambane cittam upanibadhnāti //
children.translated_text: ) he practices yoga. Thus indeed, <s>Revata</s>, a <s>bhikṣu</s>, a yogī, a practitioner of yoga, binds the mind to the appropriate object.

body.translated_text: -II-3-a-(2)-ii-(b) — And how, <s>Revata</s>, does a <s>bhikṣu</s>, a <s>yogī</s> and practitioner of <s>yoga</s>, fix the mind on a proper object? Here, <s>Revata</s>, a <s>bhikṣu</s>, whatever knowable object one wishes to examine, thoroughly examine, deliberate upon, and assess — that has been previously seen, or heard, or cognized, or known by that person. Taking that very thing seen as the basis, or that heard, cognized, or known as the basis, one mentally engages it with a mental engagement belonging to the level of concentration; one conceptualizes and resolves upon it. That person does not see that very knowable object as set before one and face-to-face; rather, there arises for one its semblance, or its appearance, or a mere knowing, or a mere seeing, or a mere recollection — and taking that as the object, this <s>bhikṣu</s>, the <s>yogī</s> and practitioner of <s>yoga</s>, from time to time calms the mind, and from time to time [engages] in the insight contemplation of <s>dharmas</s> with higher wisdom,

body.text:
-II-3-a-(2)-2-ii-(c) Ms.71a7R, Sh.199-(19), Sa.12-13, P.94a6, D.78a3, N.82a6, Co.83a3, Ch.428b10
kathaṃ ca revata, bhikṣur yogī yogācāraḥ samyag evālambane cittam upanibadhnāti / saced ayaṃ revata, bhikṣur yogī yogācāra ālambane cittam upanibadhnāti yāvad anena jñeyaṃ jñātavyaṃ bhavati, tac ca yathābhūtam aviparītam / evaṃ hi, revata, bhikṣur yogī yogācāraḥ samyag evālambane cittam upanibadhnāti //
body.translated_text: And how, <s>Revata</s>, does a <s>bhikṣu</s>, a yogī, a practitioner of yoga, correctly bind the mind to the object? If, <s>Revata</s>, a <s>bhikṣu</s>, a yogī, a practitioner of yoga binds the mind to the object insofar as the knowable is to be known by him, and that [known] as it truly is, without distortion — thus indeed, <s>Revata</s>, a <s>bhikṣu</s>, a yogī, a practitioner of yoga correctly binds the mind to the object.

body.text:
-II-3-a-(2)-2-ii-(d) Ms.71a8M, Sh.200-2, Sa.13-6, P.94b1, D.78a5, N.82b1, Co.83a5, Ch.428b15
kathaṃ ca revata, bhikṣur yogī yogācāro 'nirākṛtadhyāyī bhavati / sacet sa revata, bhikṣur yogī yogācāra evam ālambane samyak prayujyamānaḥ sātatyaprayogī ca bhavati satkṛtyaprayogī ca kālena ca kālaṃ śamathanimittaṃ bhāvayati pragrahanimittam upekṣānimittam āsevanānvayād bhāvanānvayād bahulīkārānvayāt sarvadauṣṭhulyānāṃ pratipraśrabdher āśrayapariśuddhim anuprāpnoti sparśayati sākṣātkaroti / jñeyavastupratyavekṣatayā cālambanapariśuddhiṃ rāgavirāgāc cittapariśuddhim avidyāvirāgāj jñānapariśuddhim adhigacchati sparśayati sākṣātkaroti / evaṃ hi, sa revata, bhikṣur (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 56
a yogī, a practitioner of yoga, becomes one who meditates without rejection.

body.translated_text: And how, <s>Revata</s>, does a <s>bhikṣu</s>, a yogī, a practitioner of yoga become one who meditates without rejection? If, <s>Revata</s>, a <s>bhikṣu</s>, a yogī, a practitioner of yoga, thus correctly applied to the object, is one who applies himself continuously and one who applies himself respectfully, and from time to time cultivates the sign of calm (<s>śamathanimittā</s>), the sign of exertion (<s>pragrahanimittā</s>), and the sign of equanimity (<s>upekṣānimittā</s>) — through the course of practice, through the course of cultivation, through the course of making much of [it], through the subsiding of all states of unsuitability (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>), one attains, contacts, and directly realizes the purification of the basis (<s>āśrayapariśuddhi</s>). And through the review of the knowable objects and things, one attains the purification of the object; through dispassion from passion, the purification of the mind; through dispassion from ignorance, the purification of knowledge — one attains, contacts, and directly realizes [them]. Thus indeed, <s>Revata</s>, a <s>bhikṣu</s>,

body.text: yataś ca revata, bhikṣur asminn ālambane cittam upanibadhnāti, evaṃ cālambane cittam upanibadhnāti, evam asya tac cittam ālambane sūpanibaddhaṃ bhavati" //
body.translated_text: "And since, <s>Revata</s>, a <s>bhikṣu</s> binds the mind to this object, and thus binds the mind to the object — thus his mind becomes well-bound to the object."
Therein, a verse:

children.translated_text: The yogī, moving among the signs, knower of the meaning of all beings,
meditating on the reflection, steadfast, attains purity.

body.text: tatra yat tāvad āha "nimitteṣu caran yogī"ty anena tāvac chamathanimitte pragrahanimitta upekṣānimitte satatakāritā satkṛtyakāritā cākhyātā / yat punar āha "sarvabhūtārthavedaka" ity anena vastuparyantatākhyātā / yat punar āha "bimbadhyāyī sātatika" ity anena savikalpaṃ nirvikalpaṃ ca pratibimbam ākhyātam / yat punar āha "pāriśuddhiṃ nigacchatī"ty anena kāryapariniṣpattir ākhyātā //
body.translated_text: Therein, when he says 'the yogī moving among the signs' — by this, steady and respectful practice with respect to the sign of calm, the sign of exertion, and the sign of equanimity is declared. When he says 'knower of the meaning of all beings' — by this, exhaustiveness regarding objects is declared. When he says 'meditating on the reflection, steadfast' — by this, both the conceptual and the non-conceptual reflection are declared. When he says 'attains purity' — by this, the accomplishment of the result is declared.

body.text: punar api coktaṃ bhagavatā /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, it has been said by the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

children.text: cittanimittasya kovidaḥ pravivekasya ca vindate rasam /
children.translated_text: "Skilled in the sign of the mind, and finding the taste of seclusion,

children.text: dhyāyī nipakaḥ pratismṛto bhuṅkte prītisukhaṃ nirāmiṣam //
children.translated_text: the meditator, wise, mindful, enjoys non-material joy and happiness."

body.text: tatra yat tāvad āha "cittanimittasya kovida" ity anena savikalpaṃ nirvikalpaṃ ca pratibimbaṃ nimittaśabdenākhyātam, vastuparyantatā kovidaśabdena / yat punar āha "pravivekasya ca vindate rasam" itya anenālambane samyak (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 58

children.text: ) prayuktasya prahāṇārāmatā bhāvanārāmatā cākhyātā / yat punar āha "dhyāyī nipakaḥ pratismṛta" ity anena śamathavipaśyanāyā bhāvanāsātatyam ākhyātam / yat punar āha "bhuṅkte prītisukhaṃ nirāmiṣam" ity anena kāryapariniṣpattir ākhyātā /
children.translated_text: for one correctly applied to the object are declared. When he says 'the meditator, wise, mindful' — by this, the continuity of the cultivation of <s>śamatha</s> (calm) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) is declared. When he says 'enjoys non-material joy and happiness' — by this, the accomplishment of the result is declared.

body.translated_text: Therein, when he says 'skilled in the sign of the mind' — by this, both the conceptual and the non-conceptual reflection are declared by the word 'sign,' and exhaustiveness regarding objects by the word 'skilled.' When he says 'finds the taste of seclusion' — by this, the delight in abandonment and the delight in cultivation

body.text: tad evaṃ saty etad vyāpy ālambanam āptāgamaviśuddhaṃ veditavyaṃ yuktipatitaṃ ca / idam ucyate vyāpy ālambanam //
body.translated_text: This being so, this all-encompassing object (<s>vyāpyālambana</s>) should be understood as purified by authoritative tradition and as falling within reason. This is called the all-encompassing object.

body.text:
-II-3-b Ms.71b6R, Sh.202-3, P.95b2, D.79a2, N.83a6, Co.83a3, Ch.428c18
tatra caritaviśodhanam ālambanaṃ katamat / tadyathā, aśubhā, maitrī, idaṃpratyayatāpratītyasamutpādaḥ, dhātuprabhedaḥ, ānāpānasmṛtiś ca //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the object for purifying temperament (<s>caritaviśodhana ālambana</s>)? Namely: the contemplation of impurity (<s>aśubhā</s>), loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), specific conditionality and dependent origination (<s>idaṃpratyayatā-pratītyasamutpāda</s>), the analysis of elements (<s>dhātuprabhedа</s>), and mindfulness of breathing (<s>ānāpānasmṛti</s>).

body.text:
-II-3-b-(1)-i
tatrāśubhā katamā / āha / ṣaḍvidhāśubhā / tadyathā pratyaśubhatā, duḥkhāśubhatā, avarāśubhatā, āpekṣiky aśubhatā, kleśāśubhatā, prabhaṃgurāśubhatā ca //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the contemplation of impurity? He says: the impurity is sixfold. Namely: direct impurity (<s>pratyaśubhatā</s>), impurity of suffering (<s>duḥkhāśubhatā</s>), inferior impurity (<s>avarāśubhatā</s>), relative impurity (<s>āpekṣikī aśubhatā</s>), impurity of defilements (<s>kleśāśubhatā</s>), and impurity of fragility (<s>prabhaṅgurāśubhatā</s>).

body.text:
-II-3-b-(1)-i-(a) Ms.72a1L, Sh.203-1, P.95b5, D.79a5, N.83b1, Co.84a5, Ch.428c22
tatra pratyaśubhatā katamā / āha / pratyaśubhatādhyātmam upādāya bahirdhā copādāya veditavyā //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is direct impurity (<s>pratyaśubhatā</s>)? He says: direct impurity should be understood with reference to internal [factors] and with reference to external [factors].

body.text:
-II-3-b-(1)-i-(a)
tatrādhyātmam upādāya / tadyathā keśā, romāṇi, nakhā, dantā, rajaḥ, (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 60

children.text: ) malaṃ, tvak, māṃsaṃ, asthi, snāyu, sirā, )vṛkkā, hṛdayaṃ, plīhakaṃ, klomam, antrāṇi, antraguṇaḥ, āmāśayaṃ, pakvāśayaṃ, yakṛt, purīṣam, aśru, svedaḥ, kheṭaḥ, śiṅghāṇakaṃ, vasā, lasīkā, majjā, medaḥ, pittaṃ, śleṣmā, pūyaḥ, śoṇitam, mastakaṃ, mastakaluṅgaṃ, prasrāvaḥ //
children.translated_text: filth, skin, flesh, bones, sinews, veins, kidneys, heart, spleen, lungs, intestines, mesentery, stomach, bowels, liver, excrement, tears, sweat, phlegm, mucus, fat, lymph, marrow, grease, bile, mucus, pus, blood, brain, brain membrane, and urine.

body.translated_text: Therein, with reference to internal: namely, head hair, body hair, nails, teeth, dust,

body.text:
-II-3-b-(1)-i-(a) Ms.7232L, Sh.203-11, P.96a2, D.79a7, N.83b5, Co.84b1, Ch.428c28
tatra bahirdhopādāyāśubhā katamā / tadyathā vinīlakaṃ vā, vipūyakaṃ vā, vipaṭumakaṃ vā, vyādhmātakaṃ vā, vikhāditaṃ vā, vilohitakaṃ vā, vikṣiptakaṃ vā, asthi vā, śaṅkalikā vā, asthiśaṅkalikā vā, uccārakṛtaṃ vā, prasrāvakṛtaṃ vā, kheṭakṛtaṃ vā, śiṅghāṇakakṛtaṃ vā, rudhiramrakṣitaṃ vā, pūyamrakṣitaṃ vā, gūthakaṭhiIIaṃ vā, syandanikā vā / ity evaṃbhāgīyā bahirdhopādāya pratyaśubhatā veditavyā / yā cādhyātmam upādāya yā ca bahirdhopādāyāśubhatā, iyam ucyate pratyaśubhatā //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the impurity with reference to external? Namely: the blue-black [corpse], or the festering, or the bloated, or the swollen, or the gnawed, or the blood-smeared, or the scattered, or bones, or a chain of bones, or a skeleton, or what is soiled by feces, or soiled by urine, or soiled by phlegm, or soiled by mucus, or smeared with blood, or smeared with pus, or a lump of dung, or a discharge. Such and similar is the direct impurity with reference to external. Whatever impurity is with reference to internal and whatever is with reference to external — this is called direct impurity.

body.text:
-II-3-b-(1)-i-(b)
tatra duḥkhāśubhatā katamā / yad duḥkhavedanīyaṃ sparśaṃ pratītyotpadyate kāyikacaitasikam asātaṃ vedayitaṃ vedanāgatam iyam ucyate duḥkhāśubhatā //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the impurity of suffering (<s>duḥkhāśubhatā</s>)? Whatever unpleasant bodily and mental feeling arises dependent on contact to be felt as suffering — this is called the impurity of suffering.

body.text:
-II-3-b-(1)-(c) Ms.72a4L, Sh.204-6, P.96a7, D.79b4, N.84a2, Co.84b5, Ch.429a7
tatrāvarāśubhatā katamā / yat sarvanihīnaṃ vastu, sarvanihīno dhātus tadyathā kāmadhātuḥ, yasmāt punar hīnataraś cāvarataraś ca pratikruṣṭataraś cānyo dhātur nāsti / iyam ucyata avarāśubhatā //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is inferior impurity (<s>avarāśubhatā</s>)? Whatever is the most inferior object, the most inferior realm — namely the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>) — since there is no other realm more inferior, more lowly, or more wretched than it. This is called inferior impurity.

body.text:
-II-3-b-(1)-i-(d)
tatrāpekṣiky aśubhatā katamā / tadyathā tad ekatyaṃ vastu śubham api sad anyac chubhataram apekṣyāśubhataḥ khyāti / tadyathārūpyān apekṣya rūpadhātur aśubhataḥ khyāti / satkāyanirodhaṃ nirvāṇam apekṣya yāvad bhavāgram aśubhatve saṃkhyāṃ gacchati / iyam evaṃbhāgīyāpekṣiky aśubhatā //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is relative impurity (<s>āpekṣikī aśubhatā</s>)? For instance, a certain object, even though it may be beautiful, appears impure in relation to something more beautiful. For instance, the form realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>) appears impure in relation to the formless realms (<s>ārūpya</s>). In relation to <s>nirvāṇa</s>, the cessation of the personal aggregate (<s>satkāya</s>), everything up to the peak of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>) comes to be reckoned as impure. Such and similar is relative impurity.

body.text:
-II-3-b-(1)-(e) Ms.72a5M, Sh.204-16, P.96b4, D.79b7, N.84a5, Co.85a1, Ch.429a15
tatra kleśāśubhatā katamā / traidhātukāvacarāṇi sarvāṇi saṃyojanabandhanānuśayopakleśaparyavasthānāni kleśāśubhatety ucyate //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the impurity of defilements (<s>kleśāśubhatā</s>)? All fetters, bonds, latent tendencies, secondary defilements, and mental engulfments pertaining to the three realms — this is called the impurity of defilements.

body.text:
-II-3-b-(1)-i-(f)
tatra prabhaṃgurāśubhatā katamā / yā pañcānām upādānaskandhānām anityatā, adhruvatā, anāśvāsikatā, vipariṇāmadharmatā / iyam ucyate prabhaṃgurāśubhatā /
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the impurity of fragility (<s>prabhaṅgurāśubhatā</s>)? Whatever is the impermanence, instability, unreliability, and nature of change of the five aggregates of clinging (<s>upādānaskandha</s>). This is called the impurity of fragility.

body.text: itīyam aśubhatā rāgacaritasya viśuddhaya ālambanam //
body.translated_text: Thus this impurity is the object for the purification of one of passionate temperament.

body.text:
-II-3-b-(1 )-ii Ms.72a6M, Sh.204-21, P.96b7, D.80a1, N.84a7, Co.85a3, Ch.429a19
tatra rāgas tadyathā adhyātmaṃ kāmeṣu kāmacchandaḥ kāmarāgaḥ, bahirdhā kāmeṣu maithunacchando maithunarāgaḥ, viṣayacchando viṣayarāgaḥ, (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 64

children.text: ) rūpacchando rūparāgaḥ, satkāyacchandaḥ satkāyarāgaś cety ayaṃ pañcavidho rāgaḥ / tasya pañcavidhasya rāgasya prahāṇāya prativinodanāyāsamudācārāya ṣaḍvidhāśubhatālambanam //
children.translated_text: the desire for form, the passion for form (<s>rūparāga</s>); the desire for the personal aggregate, the passion for the personal aggregate (<s>satkāyarāga</s>) — this is fivefold passion. For the abandonment, removal, and non-manifestation of this fivefold passion, the sixfold impurity serves as the object.

body.translated_text: Therein, passion is as follows: internally, in regard to sensual pleasures — the desire for sensual pleasures, the passion for sensual pleasures (<s>kāmarāga</s>); externally, in regard to sensual pleasures — the desire for sexual intercourse, the passion for sexual intercourse (<s>maithunarāga</s>); the desire for sense objects, the passion for sense objects;

body.text:
-l|-3-b-(1)-ii-(a)
tatrādhyātmam upādāya pratyaśubhatālambanenādhyātmaṃ kāmeṣu kāmacchandāt kāmarāgāc cittaṃ viśodhayati //
body.translated_text: Therein, through the object of direct impurity with reference to internal, one purifies the mind from the desire for sensual pleasures and the passion for sensual pleasures with reference to internal.

body.text:
-II-3-b-(1 )-ii-(b)-1,-2,-3,-4 Ms.72a7R, Sh.205-9, P.97a3, D.80a4, N.84b3, Co.85a7, Ch.429a25
tatra bahirdhopādāya pratyaśubhatālambanena bahirdhā kāmeṣu maithunacchandād maithunarāgāc caturvidhā rāgapratisaṃyuktād varṇarāgasaṃsthānarāgasparśarāgopacārarāgapratisaṃyuktāc cittaṃ viśodhayati /
body.translated_text: Therein, through the object of direct impurity with reference to external, one purifies the mind from the fourfold passion connected with the desire for sexual intercourse and the passion for sexual intercourse with reference to external sensual pleasures — namely, from passion connected with color, passion connected with form, passion connected with touch, and passion connected with behavior.

body.text: tatra yadā vinīlakaṃ vā, vipūyakaṃ vā, vipaṭumakaṃ vā, vyādhmātakaṃ vā, vikhāditakaṃ vā manasikaroti, tadā varṇarāgāc cittaṃ viśodhayati /
body.translated_text: Therein, when one attends to the blue-black [corpse], or the festering, or the bloated, or the swollen, or the gnawed — then one purifies the mind from passion connected with color.

body.text: yadā punar vilohitakaṃ manasikaroti, tadā saṃsthānarāgāc cittaṃ viśodhayati /
body.translated_text: When one attends to the blood-smeared — then one purifies the mind from passion connected with form.

body.text: yadā punar asthi vā śaṅkalikāṃ vāsthiśaṅkalikāṃ vā manasikaroti, tadā sparśarāgāc cittaṃ viśodhayati /
body.translated_text: When one attends to bones, or a chain of bones, or a skeleton — then one purifies the mind from passion connected with touch.

body.text: yadā vikṣiptakaṃ manasikaroti, tadopacārarāgāc cittaṃ viśodhayati /
body.translated_text: When one attends to the scattered [corpse] — then one purifies the mind from passion connected with behavior.

body.text: evaṃ sa maithunarāgāc cittaṃ viśodhayati //
body.translated_text: Thus one purifies the mind from the passion for sexual intercourse.

body.text:
-II-3-b-(1)-ii-(b)-1',-2',-3',-4' Ms.72b1R, Sh.205-20, P.97b1, D.80b1, N.84b7, Co.85b4, Ch.429b6
ata eva bhagavatā bahirdhopādāya pratyaśubhatā sā catasṛṣu śivapathikāsu vyavasthāpitā / yā yaivānena śivapathikā dṛṣṭā bhavati / ekāhamṛtā vā saptāhamṛtā vā kākaiḥ kuraraiḥ khādyamānā gṛdhraiḥ śvabhiḥ sṛgālaiḥ /

children.text: tatra tatremam eva kāyam upasaṃharati / ayam api me kāya evaṃbhāvī, evaṃbhūtaḥ, evaṃdharmatām anatītaḥ iti / anena tāvad vinīlakam upādāya yāvad vikhāditakam ākhyātam /
children.translated_text: Therein, one draws the comparison with this very body: "This body of mine too is of such a nature, will become such, has not passed beyond this nature." By this, from the blue-black [corpse] up to the gnawed has been declared.

body.translated_text: For this very reason, the Blessed One has established the direct impurity with reference to external in the four charnel-ground [contemplations]. Whatever charnel ground has been seen by him — a [corpse] dead one day or dead seven days — being devoured by crows and hawks, being eaten by vultures, dogs, and jackals.

body.text: yat punar āha "yānena śivapathikā dṛṣṭā bhavati / apagatatvaṅmāṃsaśoṇitasnāyūpanibaddhe"ty anena vilohitakam ākhyātam /
body.translated_text: When he says: "whatever charnel ground has been seen — stripped of skin, flesh, blood, and held together by sinews" — by this, the blood-smeared has been declared.

body.text: yat punar āha / "yāny eva śivapathikāsthānāni dṛṣṭāni bhavantī"ti [des ni rus goṅ daṅ / keṅ rus daṅ / rus pa'i keṅ rus bstan to /]
body.translated_text: When he says: "whatever bones of the charnel ground have been seen" — [by this, the skeleton and the chain of bones and the bone-chain are shown.]

body.text: yat punar āha / "[des lag pa'i rus pa dag kyaṅ logs śig / rkaṅ pa'i rus pa dag kyaṅ logs śig / loṅ bu'i rus pa dag kyaṅ logs śig / pus mo'i rus pa dag kyaṅ logs śig (D., Co. add la) / rtsib logs kyi rus pa dag daṅ / dpuṅ pa'i rus pa dag daṅ / lag ṅar gyi rus pa daṅ] / pṛṣṭhīvaṃśaḥ, hanucakram, dantamālā, śiraḥkapālaṃ, tathā bhinnapratibhinnāni, ekavārṣikāṇi dvivārṣikāṇi yāvat saptavārṣikāṇi śvetāni śaṃkhanibhāni, kapotavarṇāni pāṃsucūrṇavyatimiśrāṇi dṛṣṭāni bhavantī"ty anena vikṣiptakam ākhyātam / evaṃ pratyaśubhatālambanena bahirdhopādāya caturvidhā rāgapratisaṃyuktād maithunarāgāc cittaṃ viśodhayati //
body.translated_text: When he says: ["the bones of the hands are scattered, the bones of the feet are scattered, the bones of the shins are scattered, the bones of the knees are scattered, the rib bones and the shoulder bones and the forearm bones and] the spinal column, the jaw-bone, the row of teeth, the skull-cap — likewise broken and shattered, one year old, two years old, up to seven years old, white, conch-like, pigeon-colored, mixed with dust and powder, have been seen" — by this, the scattered [corpse] has been declared. Thus, through the object of direct impurity with reference to external, one purifies the mind from the fourfold passion connected with the passion for sexual intercourse.

body.text:
-II-3-b-(1)-ii-c,-d,-e Ms.72b4R, Sh.206-19, P.98a3, D.81a1, N.85a7, Co.86a3, Ch.429b24
tatra duḥkhatāśubhatālambanenāvarāśubhatālambanena ca viṣayapratisaṃyuktāt kāmarāgāc cittaṃ viśodhayati /
body.translated_text: Therein, by the objects of contemplation of the unpleasant as suffering and the unpleasant as inferior, one purifies the mind from sensual desire (<s>kāmarāga</s>) connected with sense-objects.

body.text: tatropekṣāśubhatālambanena rūparāgāc cittaṃ viśodhayati" /
body.translated_text: Therein, by the object of contemplation of the unpleasant as equanimity, one purifies the mind from desire for form (<s>rūparāga</s>).

body.text: tatra kleśāśubhatālambanena prabhaṃgurāśubhatālambanena cā bhavāgram upādāya satkāyachandarāgāc cittaṃ viśodhayati /
body.translated_text: Therein, by the objects of contemplation of the unpleasant as affliction and the unpleasant as perishable, beginning from the peak of existence, one purifies the mind from desire-and-passion for the individual existence (<s>satkāyachandarāga</s>).

body.text: idaṃ tāvad rāgacaritasya caritaviśodhanam ālambanam / saṃbhavaṃ praty etad ucyate / sarvaṃ sarvākāram aśubhatālambanaṃ saṃgṛhītaṃ bhavati / asmiṃs tv arthe pratyaśubhataivābhipretā / tadanyā tv aśubhatā tadanyasyāpi caritasya viśuddhaya ālambanam //
body.translated_text: This is the object of contemplation for purifying the temperament of the person of passionate temperament. This is stated with respect to its [complete] range. All modes of the object of the unpleasant are comprehended. But in this context, only the contemplation of the unpleasant itself is intended. Yet other kinds of unpleasantness are also objects for the purification of other temperaments.

body.text:
-II-3-b-(2) Ms.72b6M, Sh.207-7, Mai.277, P.98a8, D.81a4, N.85b4, Co.86a7, Ch.429c3
tatra maitrī katamā / yo mitrapakṣe vā, amitrapakṣe vā, udāsīnapakṣe vā, hitādhyāśayam upasthāpya mṛdumadhyādhimātrasya sukhasyopasaṃhārāyādhimokṣaḥ samāhitabhūmikaḥ / tatra yo mitrapakṣo 'mitrapakṣa udāsīnapakṣaś cedam ālambanam / tatra yo hitādhyāśayaḥ, sukhopasaṃhārāya cādhimokṣaḥ samāhitabhūmiko 'yam ālambaka iti / yac cālambanaṃ yaś cālambakas tad ekadhyam abhisaṃkṣipya maitrīty ucyate //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness)? Having established a benevolent intention toward those in the category of friends, or those in the category of enemies, or those in the category of the indifferent, the resolve to bring about mild, middling, and intense happiness, operating on the level of concentration. Therein, those in the category of friends, enemies, and the indifferent — this is the object. Therein, the benevolent intention and the resolve to bring about happiness, operating on the level of concentration — this is the one who takes the object. Both the object and the one who takes the object, taken together, are called '<s>maitrī</s>' (loving-kindness).

body.text: tatra yat tāvad āha "maitrīsahagatena cittene"ty anena tāvat triṣu pakṣeṣu mitrapakṣe, amitrapakṣe, udāsīnapakṣe hitādhyāśaya ākhyātaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, when he first says 'with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness' — by this, the benevolent intention toward the three categories — the friend category, the enemy category, and the indifferent category — is declared.

body.text: yat punar āha "avaireṇāsapatnenāvyābādhene"ty anena tasyaiva hitādhyāśayasya trividhaṃ lakṣaṇam ākhyātam / tatrāvairatayā hitādhyāśayaḥ, (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> II 70

children.text: ) sā punar avairatā dvābhyāṃ padābhyām ākhyātā, asapatnatayā, avyābādhatayā ca / tatrāpratyanīkabhāvasthānārthenāsapatnatā / apakārāviceṣṭanārthenāvyābādhatā /
children.translated_text: and that non-enmity is declared by two terms: non-rivalry and non-harming. Therein, non-rivalry means standing in a position of non-opposition. Non-harming means abstaining from injurious action.

body.translated_text: And when he says 'without enmity, without rivalry, without harming' — by this, the threefold characteristic of that very benevolent intention is declared. Therein, by non-enmity the benevolent intention [is shown],

body.text: yat punar āha / "vipulena mahadgatenāpramāṇene"ty anena mṛdumadhyādhimātrasya sukhasyopasaṃhāra ākhyātaḥ kāmāvacarasya, prathamadvitīyadhyānabhūmikasya vā, tṛtīyadhyānabhūmikasya vā /
body.translated_text: And when he says 'vast, great, immeasurable' — by this, the bringing about of mild, middling, and intense happiness is declared — [happiness] belonging to the desire realm, or to the level of the first and second <s>dhyānas</s> (meditation absorptions), or to the level of the third <s>dhyāna</s>.

body.text: yat punar āha / "adhimucya spharitvopasaṃpadya viharatī"ty anena sukhopasaṃhārāyādhimokṣaḥ samāhitabhūmika ākhyātaḥ sa punar eṣa sukhopasaṃhāro hitādhyāśayaparigṛhīta ādhimokṣikamanaskārānugataḥ /
body.translated_text: And when he says 'having resolved, pervading, attaining, one dwells' — by this, the resolve for the bringing about of happiness, operating on the level of concentration, is declared. And this bringing about of happiness, comprised by the benevolent intention, follows the mental attention of resolving.

body.text: aduḥkhāsukhite mitrapakṣe, amitrapakṣe, udāsīnapakṣe sukhakāme veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: It should be understood [as directed toward] the friend category, the enemy category, and the indifferent category who are neither suffering nor happy but who desire happiness.

body.text: yas tu duḥkhito vāduḥkhito vā punar mitrapakṣo 'mitrapakṣa udāsīnapakṣo vā / tatra yo duḥkhitaḥ sa karuṇāyā ālambanam / yaḥ sukhitaḥ sa muditāyā ālambanam, iyam ucyate maitrī /
body.translated_text: But whoever in the friend category, the enemy category, or the indifferent category is suffering or not suffering — therein, one who is suffering is the object of <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion). One who is happy is the object of <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy). This is called <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness).

body.text: tatra vyāpādacaritaḥ pudgalo maitrīṃ bhāvayan sattveṣu yo vyāpādas taṃ pratanūkaroti / vyāpādāc cittaṃ pariśodhayati //
body.translated_text: Therein, the person of aversive temperament, cultivating <s>maitrī</s>, attenuates the ill-will toward beings. One purifies the mind from ill-will.

body.text:
-II-3-b-(3) Ms.73a4M, Sh. 210-3, P.99a7, D.81b7, N.86a7, Co.87a3, Ch.430a4
tatredaṃpratyayatāpratītyasamutpādaḥ katamaḥ / yat triṣv adhvasu saṃskāramātraṃ dharmamātraṃ vastumātraṃ hetumātraṃ phalamātraṃ yuktipatitaṃ yadutāpekṣāyuktyā kāryakaraṇayuktyopapattisādhanayuktyā dharmatāyuktyā ca, dharmāṇām eva dharmāhārakatvaṃ niṣkārakavedakatvaṃ ca / idam ucyata (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> II 72

children.text: ) idaṃpratyayatāpratītyasamutpādālambanam / yad ālambanaṃ manasikurvan mohādhikaḥ pudgalo mohacarito mohaṃ prajahāti tanūkaroti mohacaritāc cittaṃ viśodhayati //
children.translated_text: the object of conditionality and dependent origination. The person who has an excess of delusion, of deluded temperament, by attending to this object, abandons and attenuates delusion, and purifies the mind from the deluded temperament.

body.translated_text: Therein, what is conditionality and dependent origination (<s>idaṃpratyayatāpratītyasamutpāda</s>)? That which, in the three times, is mere formations, mere <s>dharmas</s>, mere things, mere causes, mere fruits, falling within reason — namely, by the reasoning of dependency, by the reasoning of the performance of function, by the reasoning of the establishment of proof, and by the reasoning of <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of things) — the fact that <s>dharmas</s> alone produce <s>dharmas</s>, and there is no agent or experiencer. This is called

body.text:
-II-3-b-(4) Ms.73a5L, Sh.211-1, P.99b3, D.82a3, N.86b3, Co.87a6, Ch.430a12
tatra dhātuprabhedaḥ katamaḥ / tadyathā ṣaḍdhātavaḥ pṛthivīdhātur abdhātus tejodhātur vāyudhātur ākāśadhātur vijñānadhātuś ca //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the analysis of elements (<s>dhātuprabhedha</s>)? Namely, the six elements: the earth element (<s>pṛthivīdhātu</s>), the water element (<s>abdhātu</s>), the fire element (<s>tejodhātu</s>), the wind element (<s>vāyudhātu</s>), the space element (<s>ākāśadhātu</s>), and the consciousness element (<s>vijñānadhātu</s>).

body.text:
-II-3-b-(4)-i Ms.73a6M, Sh.211-4, P.99b4, D.82a3, N.86b4, Co.87a6, Ch.430a13
tatra pṛthivīdhātur dvividhaḥ / ādhyātmiko bāhyaś ca /
body.translated_text: Therein, the earth element is twofold: internal and external.

body.text: tatrādhyātmiko yad asmin kāye 'dhyātmaṃ pratyātmaṃ khakkhaṭam kharagatam upagatam upādattam /
body.translated_text: Therein, the internal [earth element] is whatever in this body, internally, pertaining to oneself, is solid, solidified, appropriated, and taken up.

body.text: bāhyaḥ punaḥ pṛthivīdhātur yad bāhyaṃ khakkhaṭaṃ kharagatam anupagatam anupādattam /
body.translated_text: The external earth element is whatever externally is solid, solidified, not appropriated, and not taken up.

body.text: sa punar ādhyātmikapṛthivīdhātuḥ katamaḥ / tadyathā keśā, romāṇi, nakhā, dantā, rajaḥ, malaṃ, tvak, māṃsam, asthi, snāyu, sirā, vṛkkā, hṛdayaṃ, plīhakaṃ, klomakam, antrāṇi, antraguṇāḥ, āmāśayaḥ, pakvāśayaḥ, yakṛt, purīṣam / ayam ucyata ādhyātmikaḥ pṛthivīdhātuḥ /
body.translated_text: What then is the internal earth element? Namely: hair of the head, hair of the body, nails, teeth, dust, dirt, skin, flesh, bones, sinews, veins, kidneys, heart, spleen, lungs, intestines, mesentery, stomach, lower stomach, liver, and feces. This is called the internal earth element.

body.text: sa punar bāhyaḥ pṛthivīdhātuḥ katamaḥ / kāṣṭhāni vā, loṣṭāni vā, śarkarā vā, kaṭhiIIā vā, vṛkṣā vā, parvatāgrā veti, yo vā punar anyo 'py evaṃbhāgīyaḥ / ayam ucyate bāhyaḥ pṛthivīdhātuḥ //
body.translated_text: What then is the external earth element? Pieces of wood, clods of earth, gravel, pebbles, trees, and mountain peaks — and whatever else is of this kind. This is called the external earth element.

body.text:
-II-3-b-(4)-ii Ms.73b1R, Sh.213-2, P.100a2, D.82a7, N 87a1, Co.87b3, Ch.430a21
abdhātuḥ katamaḥ / abdhātur dvividhaḥ / ādhyātmiko bāhyaś ca /
body.translated_text: What is the water element (<s>abdhātu</s>)? The water element is twofold: internal and external.

body.text: tatrādhyātmiko 'bdhātuḥ " katamaḥ / yad adhyātmaṃ pratyātmaṃ snehaḥ snehagatam āpo 'bgatam upagatam upādattam / tadyathā aśru, svedaḥ, khetaḥ, śiṃghāṇakaḥ, vasā, lasīkā, majjā, medaḥ, pittaṃ, śleṣmā, pūyaḥ, śoṇitaṃ, mastakam, mastakaluṃgam, prasrāvaḥ / ayam ucyata ādhyātmiko 'bdhātuḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the internal water element? Whatever internally, pertaining to oneself, is moisture, has become liquid, is water, has become watery, is appropriated and taken up. Namely: tears, sweat, saliva, mucus, fat, lymph, marrow, grease, bile, phlegm, pus, blood, brain, brain membrane, and urine. This is called the internal water element.

body.text: bāhyo 'bdhātuḥ katamaḥ / yad bāhyam āpo 'bgatam, snehaḥ snehagatam anupagatam anupādattam / tat punar utso vā, sarāṃsi vā, taḍāgā vā, nadyo vā, prasravaṇāni veti, yo vā punar anyo 'py evaṃbhāgīyaḥ / ayam ucyate bāhyo 'bdhātuḥ //
body.translated_text: What is the external water element? Whatever externally is water, has become watery, is moisture, has become liquid, is not appropriated and not taken up. That is: springs, lakes, reservoirs, rivers, and streams — and whatever else is of this kind. This is called the external water element.

body.text:
-II-3-b-(4)-iii Ms.73b3M, Sh.214-3, P.100a7, D.82b3, N.87a4, Co.87b6, Ch.430b1
tejodhātuḥ katamaḥ / tejodhātur dvividha ādhyātmiko bāhyaś ca /
body.translated_text: What is the fire element (<s>tejodhātu</s>)? The fire element is twofold: internal and external.

body.text: tatrādhyātmikas tejodhātuḥ katamaḥ / yad adhyātmaṃ pratyātmaṃ tejas tejogatam ūṣmoṣmāgatam upagatam upādattam / tadyathā yad asmin kāye tejo yenāyaṃ kāya ātapyate, saṃtapyate, paritapyate / yena cāśitapītakhāditasvāditaṃ samyak sukhena paripākaṃ gacchati / yasya cotsadatvāj jvārito jvārita iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati / ayam ucyata ādhyātmikas tejodhātuḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the internal fire element? Whatever internally, pertaining to oneself, is heat, has become fiery, is warmth, has become warm, is appropriated and taken up. Namely: whatever heat in this body by which this body is heated, burns, and is consumed; by which what has been eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted is properly and easily digested; and from the excess of which one comes to be reckoned as 'feverish, feverish.' This is called the internal fire element.

body.text: bāhyas tejodhātuḥ katamaḥ / yad bāhyaṃ tejas tejogatam ūṣmoṣmāgatam anupagatam anupādattam / tat punar yan manuṣyā araṇīsahagatakebhyo gomayacūrṇebhyaḥ samanveṣante / yad utpannaṃ grāmam api dahati, (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> II 76

children.text: ) grāmapradeśam api, nagaraṃ vā, nagarapradeśaṃ vā, janapadaṃ vā, janapadapradeśaṃ vā, dvīpaṃ vā, kakṣaṃ vā, dāvaṃ vā, kāṣṭhaṃ vā, tṛṇaṃ vā, gomayaṃ vā dahan paraitīti, yo vā punar anyo 'py evaṃbhāgīyaḥ / ayam ucyate bāhyas tejodhātuḥ //
children.translated_text: or a part of a village, or a city, or a part of a city, or a country, or a part of a country, or an island, or a thicket, or a forest, or wood, or grass, or cow-dung — burning, it passes on. And whatever else is of this kind. This is called the external fire element.

body.translated_text: What is the external fire element? Whatever externally is heat, has become fiery, is warmth, has become warm, is not appropriated and not taken up. That is: what humans seek from cow-dung powder by means of fire-sticks; which, once arisen, burns a village,

body.text:
-II-3-b-(4)-iv Ms.73b6L, Sh.215-7, W.87-20, P.100b6, D.82b7, N.87b2, Co.88a4, Ch.430b11
tatra vāyudhātuḥ katamaḥ / vāyudhātur dvividhaḥ, ādhyātmiko bāhyaś ca /
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the wind element (<s>vāyudhātu</s>)? The wind element is twofold: internal and external.

body.text: tatrādhyātmiko vāyudhātur yad apy adhyātmaṃ pratyātmaṃ vāyur vāyugataṃ laghutvaṃ samudīraṇatvam upagatam upādattam / sa punaḥ katamaḥ / santy asmin kāya ūrdhvaṃgamā vāyavaḥ, adhogamā vāyavaḥ, pārśvaśayā vāyavaḥ, kukṣiśayā vāyavaḥ, pṛṣṭhiśayā vāyavaḥ vāyvaṣṭhīlā vāyavaḥ, kṣurakapippalakaśastrakā vāyavaḥ, viṣūcikā vāyavaḥ, āśvāsapraśvāsā vāyavaḥ, aṅgapratyaṅgānusāriṇo vāyavaḥ / ayam ucyata ādhyātmiko vāyudhātuḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, the internal wind element is whatever internally, pertaining to oneself, is wind, has become airy, is lightness, is agitation, is appropriated and taken up. What then is that? There are in this body upward-moving winds, downward-moving winds, winds dwelling in the sides, winds dwelling in the abdomen, winds dwelling in the back, winds like thorns, winds like razor-blades, peppercorns, and knives, winds of cholera, in-breaths and out-breaths, and winds pervading the limbs and minor limbs. This is called the internal wind element.

body.text: bāhyo vāyudhātuḥ katamaḥ / yad bāhyaṃ vāyur vāyugataṃ laghutvaṃ, samudīraṇatvam anupagatam anupādattam / sa punaḥ katamaḥ / santi bahirdhā pūrvā vāyavaḥ, dakṣiṇā vāyavaḥ, uttarā vāyavaḥ, paścimā vāyavaḥ, sarajaso vāyavaḥ, arajaso vāyavaḥ, parīttā mahadgatā vāyavaḥ, viśvā vāyavaḥ, vairambhā vāyavaḥ, vāyumaṇḍalakavāyavaḥ / bhavati ca samayo yasmin mahān vāyuskandhaḥ samudāgato vṛkṣāgrān api (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> II 78

children.text: ) pātayati, kuḍyāgrān api pātayati, parvatāgrān api pātayati / pātayitvā nirupādāno nirgacchati / yaṃ sattvāś cīvarakarṇakena vā paryeṣante, tālavṛntena vā, vidhamanakena veti, yo vā punar anyo 'py evaṃbhāgīyaḥ / ayam ucyate bāhyo vāyudhātuḥ //
children.translated_text: topples even wall-tops, topples even mountain-peaks. Having toppled them, without support it passes away. [It is also] that which beings seek with the corner of a robe, or with a palm-leaf fan, or with a bellows — and whatever else is of this kind. This is called the external wind element.

body.translated_text: What is the external wind element? Whatever externally is wind, has become airy, is lightness, is agitation, is not appropriated and not taken up. What then is that? There are external eastern winds, southern winds, northern winds, western winds, dusty winds, dustless winds, minor and great winds, whirlwind winds, winds of the wind-circle. And there comes a time when a great mass of wind arises that topples even treetops,

body.text:
-II-3-b-(4)-v Ms.74a2R, Sh.217-1, P.101a7, D.83a7, N.88a1, Co.88b3, Ch.430b26
ākāśadhātuḥ katamaḥ / yac cakṣuḥsauṣiryaṃ vā, śrotrasauṣiryaṃ vā, ghrāṇasauṣiryaṃ vā, mukhasauṣiryaṃ vā, kaṇṭhasauṣiryaṃ veti, yena vābhyavaharati, yatra vābhyavaharati, yena vābhyavahriyate, adhobhāgena pragharatīti, yo vā punar anyo 'py evaṃbhāgīyaḥ / ayam ucyata ākāśadhātuḥ //
body.translated_text: What is the space element (<s>ākāśadhātu</s>)? The cavity of the eye, the cavity of the ear, the cavity of the nose, the cavity of the mouth, the cavity of the throat — and that by which one ingests, where one ingests, and that which is ingested, and what passes out below. And whatever else is of this kind. This is called the space element.

body.text:
-II-3-b-(4)-vi Ms.74a3R, Sh.218-6, P.101b1, D.83b1, N.88a3, Co.88b4, Ch.430b28
vijñānadhātuḥ katamaḥ / yac cakṣurvijñānaṃ śrotraghrāṇajihvākāyamanovijñānam / tat punaś cittaṃ mano vijñānaṃ ca / ayam ucyate vijñānadhātuḥ //
body.translated_text: What is the consciousness element (<s>vijñānadhātu</s>)? The eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, and mind-consciousness. That, further, is mind, <s>manas</s>, and consciousness. This is called the consciousness element.

body.text:
-II-3-b-(4)' Ms.74a4L, Sh.218-9, P.101b2, D.83b2, N.88a4, Co.88b4, Ch.430c1
tatra mānacaritaḥ pudgala imaṃ dhātuprabhedaṃ manasikurvan kāye piṇḍasaṃjñāṃ vibhāvayati, aśubhasaṃjñāṃ ca pratilabhate, na ca punas tenonnatiṃ gacchati, mānaṃ pratanūkaroti / tasmāc caritāc cittaṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> II 80

children.text: ) viśodhayati / ayam ucyate dhātuprabhedaḥ / mānacaritasya pudgalasya caritaviśodhanam ālambanam //
children.translated_text: This is called the analysis of elements — the object for purifying the temperament of the person of proud temperament.

body.translated_text: Therein, the person of proud temperament, attending to this analysis of elements, dispels the perception of a compact [self] in the body, and obtains the perception of the unpleasant, and does not again become puffed up. One attenuates pride. From that temperament, one purifies the mind.

body.text:
-II-3-b-(5) Ms.74a5L, Sh.219-1, W.88-15, P.101b5, D.83b4, N.88a6, Co.88b7, Ch.430c5
tatrānāpānasmṛtiḥ katamā / āśvāsapraśvāsālambanā smṛtir iyam ucyata ānāpānasmṛtiḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is mindfulness of breathing (<s>ānāpānasmṛti</s>)? Mindfulness with the in-breath and out-breath as its object — this is called mindfulness of breathing.

body.text:
-II-3-b-(5)-i-(a) Ms.74a5M, Sh.220-1, W.*86-16, P. 101 b6, D.83b4, N.88a6, Co. 89a1, Ch.430c7
tatra dvāv āśvāsau / katamau dvau / āśvāso 'ntarāśvāsaś ca / dvau praśvāsau / katamau dvau / praśvāso 'ntarapraśvāsaś ca /
body.translated_text: Therein, there are two in-breaths. Which two? The in-breath and the intermediate in-breath. [And] two out-breaths. Which two? The out-breath and the intermediate out-breath.

body.text: tatrāśvāso yaḥ praśvāsasamanantaram antarmukho vāyuḥ pravartate yāvan nābhīpradeśāt /
body.translated_text: Therein, the inhalation (<s>āśvāsa</s>) is the inward-directed air (<s>vāyu</s>) that proceeds immediately after the exhalation, extending down to the region of the navel.

body.text: tatrāntarāśvāso ya uparate 'sminn āśvāse na tāvat praśvāsa utpadyate, yadantarāle viśrāmasthānasahagata itvarakālīnas tadanusadṛśo vāyur utpadyate / ayam ucyate 'ntarāśvāsaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, the intermediate inhalation (<s>antarāśvāsa</s>) is when, after this inhalation has ceased and before the exhalation arises, in the interval there arises an air accompanied by a resting-place, of brief duration, similar [to the inhalation]. This is called the intermediate inhalation.

body.text: yathāśvāso 'ntarāśvāsaś caivaṃ praśvāso 'ntarapraśvāsaś ca veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Just as the inhalation and the intermediate inhalation, so the exhalation (<s>praśvāsa</s>) and the intermediate exhalation (<s>antarapraśvāsa</s>) should be understood.

body.text: tatrāyaṃ viśeṣo bahirmukho vāyuḥ pravartata iti vaktavyam, nābhīdeśam upādāya, yāvan mukhāgrān nāsikāgrāt, tato vā punar bahiḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, this is the distinction: the outward-directed air proceeds — it should be stated — from the region of the navel, extending up to the tip of the mouth and the tip of the nose, and from there outward. //

body.text:
-II-3-b-(5)-i-(b) Ms.74a7R, Sh.220-15, W.88-38, P.102a3, D.84a1, N.88b3, Co.89a5, Ch.430c16
dvāv āśvāsapraśvāsanidānau / katamau dvau / tadākṣepakaṃ ca karma, nābhīpradeśasauṣiryaṃ ca, tato vā punar uttari yat kāyasauṣiryam //
body.translated_text: There are two causes of inhalation and exhalation. What two? The <s>karma</s> (action) that impels them, and the hollowness of the navel region — and furthermore, beyond that, whatever hollowness of the body. //

body.text:
-II-3-b-(5)-i-(c) Ms.74b1L, Sh.221-1, W.89-4, P.102a4, D.84a2, N.88b4, Co.89a6, Ch.430c18
dvāv āśvāsapraśvāsayoḥ saṃniśrayau / katamau dvau / kāyaś cittaṃ ca / tat kasya hetoḥ / kāyasaṃniśritāś cittasaṃniśritāś cāśvāsapraśvāsāḥ pravartante / te ca yathāyogaṃ sacet kāyasaṃniśritā eva pravarteran, asaṃjñisamāpannānāṃ, nirodhasamāpannānām asaṃjñisattveṣu deveṣūpapannānāṃ sattvānāṃ pravarteran / sacec cittasaṃniśritā eva pravarteran, tenārūpyasamāpannopapannānām sattvānāṃ pravarteran /
body.translated_text: There are two supports of inhalation and exhalation. What two? The body and the mind. What is the reason? Inhalations and exhalations proceed supported by the body and supported by the mind. If they were to proceed supported by the body alone, according to fitness, then they would proceed for those who have attained the attainment without perception (<s>asaṃjñisamāpanna</s>), for those who have attained the cessation attainment (<s>nirodhasamāpanna</s>), and for beings reborn among the gods without perception (<s>asaṃjñisattva</s>). If they were to proceed supported by the mind alone, then they would proceed for beings who have attained or are reborn in the formless attainments.

body.text: sacet kāyasaṃniśritāś cittasaṃniśritāḥ pravarteraṃs te ca na yathāyogaṃ, tena caturthadhyānasamāpannopapannānām sattvānāṃ kalalagatānāṃ cārbudagatānāṃ peśīgatānām sattvānāṃ pravarteran / na ca pravartante / tasmād āśvāsapraśvāsāḥ kāyasaṃniśritāś cittasaṃniśritāś ca pravartante te ca yathāyogam //
body.translated_text: If they were to proceed supported by the body and supported by the mind but not according to fitness, then they would proceed for beings who have attained or are reborn in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, and for beings at the <s>kalala</s> (embryonic), <s>arbuda</s> (blistered), and <s>peśī</s> (lump) stages [of embryonic development]. But they do not proceed [for those]. Therefore, inhalations and exhalations proceed supported by the body and supported by the mind, and indeed according to fitness. //

body.text:
-II-3-b-(5)-i-(d) Ms.74b3M, Sh.221-16, W.90-1, P.102b3, D.84a6, N.89a2, Co.89b3, Ch.430c26
dve āśvāsapraśvāsayor gatī / katame dve / āśvāsayor adhogatiḥ, praśvāsayor ūrdhvagatiḥ //
body.translated_text: There are two directions of inhalation and exhalation. What two? For inhalation, the downward direction; for exhalation, the upward direction. //

body.text:
-II-3-b-(5)-i-(e) Ms.74b3R, Sh.221-18, W.90-4, P.102b4, D.84a7, N.89a3, Co.89b4, Ch.430c28
dve āśvāsapraśvāsayor bhūmī / katame dve / audārikaṃ ca sauṣiryaṃ, sūkṣmaṃ ca sauṣiryam /
body.translated_text: There are two kinds of hollowness for inhalation and exhalation. What two? Coarse hollowness and subtle hollowness.

body.text: tatraudārikaṃ sauṣiryaṃ nābhīpradeśam upādāya yāvan mukhanāsikādvāram / mukhanāsikādvāram upādāya yāvan nābhīpradeśasauṣiryam /
body.translated_text: Therein, the coarse hollowness extends from the navel region up to the opening of the mouth and nose. From the opening of the mouth and nose, extending outward —

body.text: sūkṣmasauṣiryaṃ katamat / sarvakāyagatāni romakūpāni //
body.translated_text: What is subtle hollowness? The hair-pores throughout the entire body. //

body.text:
-II-3-b-(5)-i-(f) Ms.74b4M, Sh.222-3, W.90-15, P.102b6, D.84b2, N.89a4, Co.89b6, Ch.431a3
catvāry āśvāsapraśvāsānāṃ paryāyanāmāni / katamāni catvāri / vāyavaḥ, ānāpānāḥ, āśvāsapraśvāsāḥ, kāyasaṃskārāś ceti / tatrānyair vāyubhiḥ (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 84

children.text: ) sādhāraṇaṃ paryāyanāmaikaṃ yaduta vāyur iti / asādhāraṇāni tadanyāni trīṇi //
children.translated_text: ) One common synonym, namely 'air' (<s>vāyu</s>). The other three are uncommon [i.e., specific]. //

body.translated_text: There are four synonymous names for inhalation and exhalation.

body.text:
-II-3-b-(5)-i-(g) Ms.74b5L, Sh.222-8, W.*90-19, P.102b8, D.84b3, N.89a6, Co.89b7, Ch.431a6
dvāv apakṣālāv āśvāsaprāśvāsaprayuktasya / katamau dvau / atiśithilaprayogatā ca, atyavaṣṭabdhaprayogatā ca /
body.translated_text: There are two faults in the practice [of mindfulness of breathing]. What two? Too loose a practice and too tight a practice.

body.text: tatrātiśithilaprayogatayā kausīdyaprāptasya styānamiddhaṃ vā cittaṃ paryavanahati, bahirdhā vā vikṣipyate / tathātyavaṣṭabdhaprayuktasya kāyavaiṣamyam votpadyate cittavaiṣamyaṃ vā /
body.translated_text: Therein, through excessively loose practice, having become lazy, sloth-and-torpor either overwhelm the mind, or the mind is scattered outward, or [both defects arise].

body.text: kathaṃ kāyavaiṣamyam utpadyate / balābhinigraheṇāśvāsapraśvāsān abhiniṣpīḍayataḥ kāye viṣamā vāyavaḥ pravartante / ye 'sya tatprathamatas teṣu teṣv aṅgapratyaṅgeṣu sphuranti / ye sphurakā ity ucyante / te punaḥ sphurakā vāyavo vivardhamānā rujakā bhavanti / ye 'sya teṣu teṣv aṅgapratyaṅgeṣu rujām utpādayanti / idam ucyate kāyavaiṣamyam /
body.translated_text: How does bodily imbalance arise? By forcefully suppressing the inhalations and exhalations, uneven winds arise in the body. From that, wind disorders arise in the body, and various bodily ailments arise.

body.text: kathaṃ cittavaiṣamyam utpadyate / cittaṃ vāsya vikṣipyate / pragāḍhena vā daurmanasyopāyāsenābhibhūyate / evaṃ cittavaiṣamyam utpadyate //
body.translated_text: How does mental imbalance arise? The mind becomes scattered, or one is overcome by intense mental anguish and distress, or [both].

body.text:
-II-3-b-(5)-ii Ms.75a1M, Sh.223-1, W.90-24, P.103a6, D.84b7, N.89b3, Co.90a5, Ch.431a17
asyāḥ khalv ānāpānasmṛteḥ pañcavidhaḥ paricayo veditavyaḥ / tadyathā gaṇanāparicayaḥ skandhāvatāraparicayaḥ pratītyasamutpādāvatāraparicayaḥ satyāvatāraparicayaḥ ṣoḍaśākāraparicayaś ca //
body.translated_text: Now, this practice of mindfulness of breathing (<s>ānāpānasmṛti</s>) has five stages. What five? Counting (<s>gaṇanā</s>), following (<s>anugama</s>), placement (<s>sthāpanā</s>), examination (<s>upalakṣaṇā</s>), and transformation (<s>vivartanā</s>).

body.text:
-II-3-b-(5)-ii-(a) Ms.75a2L, Sh.223-5, W.90-31, P.103a8, D.85a2, N.89b5, Co.90a6, Ch.431a21
tatra gaṇanāparicayaḥ katamaḥ / samāsataś caturvidho gaṇanāparicayaḥ (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 86
) Namely: counting one-by-one, counting two-by-one, forward counting, and reverse counting. //

body.translated_text: Therein, what is counting (<s>gaṇanā</s>)?

body.text:
-II-3-b-(5)-ii-(a)-(1) Ms.75a2R, Sh.223-8, P.103b1, D.85a3, N.89b6, Co.90a7, Ch.431a24
tatraikaikagaṇanā katamā / yadāśvāsaḥ praviṣṭo bhavati, tadāśvāsapraśvāsālambanopanibaddhayā smṛtyaikam iti gaṇayati / yadāśvāse niruddhe praśvāsa utpadya nirgato bhavati tadā dvitīyaṃ gaṇayati, evaṃ yāvad daśa gaṇayati / eṣā hi gaṇanā saṃkhyā nātisaṃkṣiptā nātivistarā / iyam ucyata ekaikagaṇanā //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is counting one-by-one? One counts the inhalation as one, the exhalation as two, the [next] inhalation as three, the exhalation as four — thus, counting each one by one, up to ten. This is called counting one-by-one.

body.text:
-II-3-b-(5)-ii-(a)-(2) Ms.75a3R, Sh.223-14, P.103b4, D.85a4, N.89b7, Co.90b2, Ch.431a28
dvayaikagaṇanā katamā / yadāśvāsaḥ praviṣṭo bhavati niruddhaś ca praśvāsa utpanno bhavati nirgataś ca, tadaikam iti gaṇayati / anena gaṇanāyogena yāvad daśa gaṇayati / iyam ucyate dvayaikagaṇanā / āśvāsaṃ ca praśvāsaṃ cedaṃ dvayam ekadhyam abhisaṃkṣipyaikam iti gaṇayati, tenocyate dvayaikagaṇanā //
body.translated_text: What is counting two-by-one? One counts the inhalation and the exhalation together as one, the [next] inhalation and exhalation together as two — thus, counting pairs as one, up to ten. This is called counting two-by-one.

body.text:
-II-3-b-(5)-ii-(a)-(3) Ms.75a4R, Sh.223-20, P.103b6, D.85a6, N.90a2, Co.90b4, Ch.431b3
anulomagaṇanā katamā / anayaivaikaikagaṇanayā dvayaikagaṇanayā vānulomaṃ yāvad daśa gaṇayati / iyam ucyate 'nulomagaṇanā //
body.translated_text: What is forward counting? Beginning from one, one counts forward, namely: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten. This is called forward counting.

body.text:
-II-3-b-(5)-ii-(a)-(4) Ms.75a5L, Sh.224-2, P. 103b7, D.85a6, N.90a3, Co.90b4, Ch.431 b6
pratilomagaṇanā katamā / pratilomaṃ daśa upādāya navāṣṭau sapta ṣaṭ pañca yāvad ekaṃ gaṇayati / iyam ucyate pratilomagaṇanā /
body.translated_text: What is reverse counting? Beginning from ten, one counts in reverse, namely: ten, nine, eight, seven, six, five, four, three, two, one. This is called reverse counting.

body.text: yadā sa ekaikagaṇanāṃ niśritya dvayaikagaṇanāṃ vā, anulomagaṇanāyāṃ, pratilomagaṇanāyāṃ ca kṛtaparicayo bhavati, na cāsyāntarāc cittaṃ vikṣipyate, avikṣiptacittaś ca gaṇayati, tadāsyottaragaṇanāviśeṣo vyapadiśyate //
body.translated_text: When one, relying on counting one-by-one or counting two-by-one, in forward counting and in reverse counting, has become practiced,

body.text:
-II-3-b-(5)-ii-(a)-(5) Ms.75a6L, Sh.224-10, P.104a2, D.85b1, N.90a5, Co.90b6, Ch.431b12
katamo gaṇanāviśeṣaḥ / ekaikagaṇanayā vā, dvayaikagaṇanayā vā, dvayam ekaṃ kṛtvā gaṇayati / tatra dvayaikagaṇanayā catvāra āśvāsapraśvāsā ekaṃ (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 88

children.text: ) bhavati, ekaikagaṇanayā punar āśvāsaḥ praśvāsaś " caikaṃ bhavati / evaṃ yāvad daśa gaṇayati / evam uttarottaravṛddhyā yāvac chatam apy ekaṃ kṛtvā gaṇayati / tadā śataikagaṇanayānupūrveṇa yāvad daśa gaṇayati / evam asya gaṇanāprayutkasya yāvad daśaikaṃ kṛtvā gaṇayati / yāvac ca daśa paripūrayati / tayā daśaikagaṇanayā na cāsyāntarāc cittaṃ vikṣipyate / iyatā tena gaṇanāparicayaḥ kṛto bhavati /
children.translated_text: ) In counting one-by-one, the inhalation and the exhalation are each one. Thus one counts up to ten. Thus

body.translated_text: What is the purpose of counting?

body.text: tasya ca gaṇanāprayuktasya saced antarāc cittaṃ vikṣipyate, tadā punaḥ pratinivartyādito gaṇayitum ārabhate 'nulomaṃ vā, pratilomaṃ vā / yadā cāsya gaṇanāparicayāt tac cittaṃ svarasenaiva vāhimārgasamārūḍham āśvāsapraśvāsālambanopanibaddham avyavacchinnaṃ nirantaraṃ, pravartamāna āśvāse pravṛttigrāhakam, niruddha āśvāse nivṛttigrāhakaṃ praśvāsaśūnyāvasthāgrāhakaṃ, pravṛtte praśvāse pravṛttigrāhakaṃ, nivṛtte punar nivṛttigrāhakam āśvāsaśūnyāvasthāgrāhakam avikaṃpyam avicalam avikṣepākāram, sābhirāmaṃ ca pravartate /
body.translated_text: if, while engaged in counting, the mind becomes scattered in the interval, then one should turn back and begin counting again from the start.

body.text: iyatā gaṇanābhūmisamatikramo bhavati / punas tadāgaṇayitavyaṃ bhavati / nānyatrāśvāsapraśvāsālambanaṃ cittam upanibadhyate / āśvāsapraśvāsā anugantavyāś cābhilakṣayitavyāś ca sāntarāśvāsapraśvāsāḥ sapravṛttinivṛttyavasthāḥ / ayam ucyate gaṇanāparicayaḥ //
body.translated_text: To this extent, the stage of counting is transcended. After that, there is nothing more to count. One should not attend to any object other than the object of inhalation and exhalation.

body.text:
Ms.75b2L, Sh.225-12, P.104b6, D.86a2, N.90b6, Co,91b1, Ch.431c4
sa khalv eṣa gaṇanāparicayo mṛdvindriyāṇāṃ vyapadiśyate / teṣām etad (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 90

children.text: ) vyākṣepasthānaṃ bhavati cittasthitaye cittanirataye / anyathā gaṇanām antareṇa teṣāṃ styānamiddhaṃ vā cittaṃ paryavanaheta, bahirdhā vā cittaṃ vikṣipyeta, gaṇanāprayuktānāṃ tu teṣām etan na bhavati /
children.translated_text: ) a basis for steadying the mind and preventing distraction — for the stability and fixation of the mind. Otherwise, without counting, sloth-and-torpor

body.translated_text: This practice of counting is, for those of soft faculties,
