These ten perceptions, when practiced, cultivated, and frequently applied, conduce to the abandonment of the tenfold obstacle to training, the ten <s>dharmas</s> opposing the training.

body.text: tatra dharmālokaḥ, arthālokaḥ, śamathālokaḥ, vipaśyanālokaś ca / etān ālokān adhipatiṃ kṛtvā ālokasaṃjñā / asminn artha abhipretā dharmacintāyogamanasikārāḥ paripanthasya prahāṇāya //
body.translated_text: Therein, the light of <s>Dharma</s>, the light of meaning, the light of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding), and the light of <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) — making these lights the governing [factor] constitutes the perception of light. In this meaning, the mental attentions of <s>Dharma</s>-reflection and yogic practice are intended for the abandonment of the obstacle.

body.text:
-II-6-b Ms.81b4R, Sh.270-15, W.*92-12, Choi.158-12, P.122b5, D.100a3, N.105b2, Co.104b6, Ch.437a15
tatrāpare daśa śikṣānulomikā dharmā veditavyāḥ / katame daśa / tadyathā pūrvako hetuḥ / ānulomika upadeśaḥ / yoniśaḥ prayogaḥ / sātatyasatkṛtyakāritā / tīvracchandatā / yogabalādhānatā / kāyacittadauṣṭhulyapratiprasrabdhiḥ / abhīkṣṇapratyavekṣā / aparitamanā / nirabhimānatā ca /
body.translated_text: Therein, another ten <s>dharmas</s> in conformity with the training should be understood. Which ten? Namely: prior cause (<s>pūrvako hetu</s>), conforming instruction (<s>ānulomika upadeśa</s>), methodical application (<s>yoniśaḥ prayoga</s>), continuous and respectful practice (<s>sātatyasatkṛtyakāritā</s>), intense aspiration (<s>tīvracchandatā</s>), exertion of the power of practice (<s>yogabalādhānatā</s>), alleviation of bodily and mental unsuitability (<s>kāyacittadauṣṭhulyapratiprasrabdhi</s>), frequent self-examination (<s>abhīkṣṇapratyavekṣā</s>), non-contentment (<s>aparitamanā</s>), and absence of conceit (<s>nirabhimānatā</s>).

body.text: tatra pūrvako hetuḥ katamaḥ / yaḥ pūrvam indriyaparipāka indriyasamudāgamaś ca /
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the prior cause? The previous maturation of faculties and the arising of faculties.

body.text: tatrānulomika upadeśo ya upadeśo 'viparītaś cānupūrvikaś ca /
body.translated_text: Therein, conforming instruction is instruction that is both non-erroneous and sequential.

body.text: tatra yoniśaḥ prayogo yathaivāvavāditas tathaiva prayujyate / tathā prayujyamānaḥ samyagdṛṣṭim utpādayati /
body.translated_text: Therein, methodical application is when one practices exactly as one has been instructed. Practicing thus, one generates right view.

body.text: tatra sātatyasatkṛtyakāritā yadrūpeṇa prayogeṇa avandhyaṃ ca kālaṃ karoti kuśalapakṣeṇa / kṣipram eva kuśalapakṣaṃ samudānayati /
body.translated_text: Therein, continuous and respectful practice is that form of application by which one makes one's time fruitful through the wholesome side, and quickly accomplishes the wholesome side.

body.text: tatra tīvracchandatā yathāpi tad uttare vimokṣaspṛhām utpādayati / "kadāsvid ahaṃ tad āyatanam upasaṃpadya vihariṣyāmi yad āryā āyatanam upasaṃpadya viharantī"ti /
body.translated_text: Therein, intense desire is when one generates longing for the higher liberation: "When indeed shall I enter and dwell in that sphere in which the noble ones dwell, having entered and dwelled?"

body.text: tatra yogabalādhānatā dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāṃ yogabalādhānaprāpto bhavati / prakṛtyaiva ca tīkṣṇendriyatayā, dīrghakālābhyāsaparicayena ca /
body.translated_text: Therein, application of the power of yoga — one attains the application of the power of yoga through two causes: through having naturally sharp faculties, and through long-term practice and familiarization.

body.text: tatra kāyacittadauṣṭhulyapratiprasrabdhir yathāpi tac chrāntakāyasya klāntakāyasyotpadyate kāyadauṣṭhulyaṃ cittadauṣṭhulyam / tad īryāpathāntarakalpanayā pratiprasrambhayati / ativitarkitenātivicāritenotpadyate kāyacittadauṣṭhulyam, tadādhyātmaṃ cetaḥ śamathānuyogena pratiprasrambhayati /
body.translated_text: Therein, the relaxation of bodily and mental rigidity — just as for one whose body is exhausted and fatigued, there arises bodily rigidity and mental rigidity; one relaxes that by changing the deportment. Through excessive initial thought and excessive sustained thought, bodily and mental rigidity arise — one relaxes that internally by the practice of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) of the mind.

body.text: cittābhisaṃkṣepeṇa cittalayena styānamiddhaparyavasthānenotpadyate kāyacittadauṣṭhulyam / tad adhiprajñaṃ dharmavipaśyanayā, prasadanīyena ca manaskāreṇa prasrambhayati / prakṛtyaiva cāprahīṇakleśasya kleśapakṣaṃ kāyacittadauṣṭhulyam avigataṃ bhavati / sadānuṣaktaṃ tat samyaṅmārgabhāvanayā pratiprasrambhayati /
body.translated_text: Through the contraction of mind, sinking of mind, and the mental obsession of sloth-and-torpor, bodily and mental rigidity arise — one relaxes that through the higher wisdom, the <s>dharma</s>-insight (<s>dharmavipaśyanā</s>), and by means of a gladdening mental attention. And for one whose afflictions have not been abandoned, the bodily and mental rigidity belonging to the affliction side naturally remains, constantly attached — one relaxes that through the cultivation of the right path.

body.text: tatrābhīkṣṇapratyavekṣā abhīkṣṇaṃ śīlāny ārabhya kukṛtaṃ pratyavekṣate sukṛtaṃ ca / akṛtaṃ ca pratyavekṣate, kṛtaṃ ca / kukṛtāc cākṛtād vyāvartate / sukṛtāc cākṛtān na pratyudāvartate / kukṛtāc ca kṛtāt pratyudāvartate / sukṛtāc ca kṛtān na pratyudāvartate / tathā kleśānāṃ prahīṇāprahīṇānāṃ mīmāṃsāmanaskāram adhipatiṃ kṛtvā abhīkṣṇaṃ pratyavekṣate /
body.translated_text: Therein, frequent examination — one frequently examines with regard to moral conduct what has been badly done and what has been well done; one examines what has not been done and what has been done. One turns away from what has been badly done and not done; one does not turn away from what has been well done and not done. One turns away from what has been badly done and done; one does not turn away from what has been well done and done. Similarly, making examination and reflection the predominant factor regarding afflictions — whether abandoned or not abandoned — one frequently examines.

body.text: tatra prahīṇatāṃ jñātvā [yid bde bar 'gyur la / ma spaṅs bar śes na] punaḥ punas tam eva mārgaṃ bhāvayati /
body.translated_text: Therein, having known that [an affliction] has been abandoned, [one is joyful; and having known that it has not been abandoned,] one again and again cultivates that very path.

body.text: tatrāparitamanā / yat kālāntareṇa jñātavyaṃ draṣṭavyaṃ prāptavyaṃ tad ajānato 'paśyato 'nadhigacchataḥ paritamanā utpadyate, caitasikaḥ klamaḥ, caitasiko vighātaḥ / tām utpannāṃ nādhivāsayati prajahāti /
body.translated_text: Therein, freedom from discontent — what is to be known, seen, and attained over time, when not knowing, not seeing, not attaining it, discontent arises — mental fatigue, mental frustration. That which has arisen, one does not tolerate but abandons it.

body.text: tatra nirabhimānatā / adhigame prāptau sparśanāyāṃ nirabhimāno bhavati / aviparītagrāhī, prāpte prāptasaṃjñī, adhigate 'dhigatasaṃjñī sākṣātkṛte sākṣatkṛtasaṃjñī /
body.translated_text: Therein, freedom from conceit — regarding attainment, obtainment, and realization, one is free from conceit. One is a non-erroneous grasper — regarding what has been attained, one has the perception of attainment; regarding what has been realized, one has the perception of realization; regarding what has been directly experienced, one has the perception of direct experience.

body.text: itīme daśa dharmāḥ śikṣākāmasya yogina ādimadhyaparyavasānam upādāya śikṣām anulomayanti, na vilomayanti / tenocyante śikṣānulomikā iti //
body.translated_text: These ten <s>dharmas</s>, for a practitioner who wishes to train, from beginning through middle to end, conform to the training, do not oppose it. Therefore they are called 'conforming to the training.'

body.text:
(II)-A-II-7-a Ms.82a5R, Sh.273-1, W.92-23, P.124a4, D.101a4, N.106b3, Co.105b6, Ch.437b23
tatra katamo yogabhraṃśaḥ / āha / catvāro yogabhraṃśāḥ / katame catvāraḥ / asti yogabhraṃśa ātyantikaḥ / asti tāvatkālikaḥ / asti prāptiparihāṇikaḥ / asti mithyāpratipattikṛtaḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the failure of yoga? It is said: There are four failures of yoga. Which four? There is a failure of yoga that is absolute; there is one that is temporary; there is one consisting in the decline from attainment; and there is one caused by wrong practice.

body.text:
-II-7-a-(1),-(2),-(3) Ms.82a6M, Sh.273-5, P.124a4, D.101a5, N.106b4, Co.105b7, Ch.437b26
tatrātyantiko yogabhraṃśo 'gotrasthānāṃ pudgalānāṃ veditavyaḥ / te hy aparinirvāṇadharmakatvād atyantaparibhraṣṭā eva yogād bhavanti /
body.translated_text: Therein, the absolute failure of yoga is to be understood for persons not established in the <s>gotra</s> (spiritual lineage). For they, being of a nature not destined for <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, are absolutely fallen from yoga.

body.text: tatra tāvatkālikaḥ / tadyathā gotrasthānāṃ parinirvāṇadharmakāṇāṃ pratyayavikalānām, te hi dūram api param api gatvā avaśyam eva pratyayān āsādayiṣyanti / yogaṃ ca saṃmukhīkṛtya bhāvayitvā parinirvāsyanti / tenaiṣa teṣāṃ tāvatkālika eva yogabhraṃśo bhavati /
body.translated_text: Therein, the temporary [failure]: namely, for persons established in the <s>gotra</s>, destined for <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, but lacking conditions — they, even having gone far and to the very limit, will inevitably encounter the conditions; and having directed themselves to and cultivated the yoga, they will attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. Therefore this failure of yoga for them is merely temporary.

body.text: tatra prāptiparihāṇiko yogabhraṃśaḥ / yathāpīhaikatye prāptād adhigatāj jñānadarśanasparśavihārāt parihīyante //
body.translated_text: Therein, the failure of yoga consisting in the decline from attainment — just as here certain ones decline from the attained, realized knowledge, vision, and contact-dwelling.

body.text:
-II-7-a-(4) Ms.82a7R, Sh.273-15, P.124b2, D.101b1, N.107a1, Co.106a3, Ch.437c5
tatra mithyāpratipattikṛto yogabhraṃśaḥ / yathāpīhaikatyo 'yoniśaḥ prayujyamāno nārādhako bhavati yogasya, nārādhayati nyāyyaṃ dharmaṃ kuśalam / yathāpīhaikatyo bahukleśo bhavati, prabhūtarajaskajātīyaḥ paṭuvijñānaś ca bhavati paṭubuddhiḥ sahajayā buddhyā samanvāgataḥ sa śrutam udgṛhṇāti śrutaṃ paryavāpnoty alpaṃ vā, prabhūtaṃ vā / araṇye vā punar viharati, āgatāgatānāṃ ca gṛhipravrajitānām, ṛjukānām, ṛjukajātīyānāṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> II 148

children.text: ) dharmadeśanayā cittam ārādhayati kuhanānucaritayā ca ceṣṭayā kāyavākpratisaṃyuktayā / tasya tena hetubhāvena tena pratyayenotpadyate lābhasatkāraślokaḥ / sa jñāto bhavati mahāpuṇyo lābhī bhavati cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇām, satkṛtaś ca bhavati, gurukṛtaḥ, rājñāṃ rājamātrāṇām, yāvat sārthavāhānām, arhatsaṃmataḥ / tasyānvāvartante śrāvakāḥ, gṛhiṇaḥ, pravrajitā api, anvāvṛtteṣu gredhaṃ nigamayaty āvartate bāhulyāya /
children.translated_text: ) and by hypocritical behavior connected with body and speech, one wins over their minds. By that cause and condition, gain, honor, and fame arise for one. One becomes known as one of great merit, obtains robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicine and requisites for the sick; one is honored and revered by kings and royal ministers, and so on up to caravan-leaders, and is regarded as an <s>arhat</s>. Disciples follow one — householders and even renunciants. When they follow, one develops greed and turns toward proliferation.

body.translated_text: Therein, the failure of yoga caused by wrong practice — just as here someone, practicing unmethodically, is not a successful practitioner of yoga, does not succeed in the right, wholesome <s>dharma</s>. Just as here someone is one of many afflictions, of a nature abundant in passion, yet is of keen consciousness, of keen intelligence, endowed with innate wisdom — one grasps what has been heard, masters what has been heard, whether little or much. Or further, one dwells in the forest, and by teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to incoming householders and renunciants who are straightforward and of a straightforward nature,

body.text: tasyaivaṃ bhavati / "santi me śrāvakāḥ, gṛhipravrajitā ye, mayi saṃbhāvanā jātā yeṣām arhatsaṃmatas te cen mām upasaṃkramya yoge manasikāre śamathavipaśyanāyāṃ praśnaṃ pṛccheyuḥ / teṣāṃ cāhaṃ pṛṣṭo vyākuryāṃ na jānāmīty evaṃ sati yā saṃbhāvanā sā ca hīyet, na ca syām arhatsaṃmataḥ, yan nv ahaṃ svayam eva cintayitvā tulayitvopaparīkṣya yogaṃ vyavasthāpayeyam" / sa etam evārtham adhipatiṃ kṛtvā lābhasatkārābhigṛddha ekākī rahogataḥ svayam eva cintayitvā tulayitvopaparīkṣya yogaṃ vyavasthāpayati /
body.translated_text: One thinks thus: "I have disciples — householders and renunciants — for whom respect has arisen toward me, who regard me as an <s>arhat</s>. If they should approach me and ask questions about yoga, mental attention, <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding), and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), and if I, when asked, should respond 'I do not know' — then the respect [they have] would diminish, and I would no longer be regarded as an <s>arhat</s>. Rather, I should by myself, having thought, weighed, and examined, establish a [system of] yoga." Making this very purpose the predominant factor, greedy for gain and honor, alone and secluded, by oneself having thought, weighed, and examined, one establishes a [system of] yoga.

body.text: sa cāsya yogo na sūtre 'vatarati na vinaye saṃdṛśyate / dharmatāṃ ca vilomayati / sa ye te bhikṣavaḥ sūtradharā, vinayadharā, mātṛkādharās teṣaṃ tad yogasthānaṃ vinigūhati na prakāśayati / ye 'py asya śravakā (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> II 150

children.text: ) bhavanti gṛhiṇaḥ, pravrajitāś ca, tān api yogapratiguptaya ājñāpayati /
children.translated_text: ) householders and renunciants — one instructs them too to keep the yoga secret.

body.translated_text: And this yoga of one's does not accord with the <s>sūtras</s> and is not found in the <s>Vinaya</s> (discipline), and it contradicts the nature of <s>dharma</s>. One conceals that yogic position from those <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) who are bearers of the <s>sūtras</s>, bearers of the <s>Vinaya</s>, and bearers of the <s>Mātṛkā</s> (Abhidharma), and does not make it public. And whatever disciples one has —

body.text: tat kasya hetoḥ / "mā haiva te sūtradharā, vinayadharā, mātṛkādharā, etad yogasthānaṃ śrutvā sūtre 'vatārayeyuḥ, tac ca nāvataret / vinaye saṃdarśayeyuḥ, tac ca na saṃdṛśyet / dharmatayā upaparīkṣeyuḥ, tac ca dharmatāṃ virodhayet / te ca tato nidānam apratītā bhaveyur apratītavacanaiś ca māṃ codayeyuḥ / adhikaraṇāni cotpādayeyuḥ" /
body.translated_text: For what reason? "Lest those bearers of the <s>sūtras</s>, bearers of the <s>Vinaya</s>, and bearers of the <s>Mātṛkā</s>, having heard this yogic position, should try to find it in the <s>sūtras</s> — and it would not be found; should try to see it in the <s>Vinaya</s> — and it would not be seen; should examine it by the nature of <s>dharma</s> — and it would contradict the nature of <s>dharma</s>. And they, on that account being unconvinced, would challenge me with words of disbelief and would bring up disciplinary proceedings."

body.text: "evam ahaṃ punar api na satkṛtaḥ syāṃ na gurukṛtaḥ, rājñāṃ rājāmātrāṇāṃ yāvad dhanināṃ śreṣṭhināṃ sārthavāhānām, na ca punar lābhī syāṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇām" iti /
body.translated_text: "Thus I would again be neither honored nor revered by kings and royal ministers, and so on up to the wealthy, merchants, and caravan-leaders; nor would I again be an obtainer of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicine and requisites for the sick."

body.text: sa tām eva lābhasatkārakāmatām adhipatiṃ kṛtvā adharme dharmasaṃjñī, vinidhāya saṃjñāṃ rucim adharmaṃ dharmato dīpayati saṃprakāśayati /
body.translated_text: One, making that very desire for gain and honor the predominant factor, having the perception of <s>dharma</s> regarding what is non-<s>dharma</s>, having established one's perception and inclination, illuminates and proclaims non-<s>dharma</s> as <s>dharma</s>.

body.text: tatra ye 'sya dṛṣṭyanumatam āpadyante te 'py adharme dharmasaṃjñino bhavanti mandatvān momuhatvāt te 'dharme dharmasaṃjñino yathānuśiṣṭā api pratipadyamānā mithyāpratipannā eva te veditavyāḥ / ayam evaṃrūpo mithyāpratipattikṛto yogabhraṃśaḥ saddharmapratirūpako hy asaddharmaḥ saddharmasyāntardhānāya /
body.translated_text: Therein, those who come to adopt the view-agreement of that one — they too have the perception of <s>dharma</s> regarding what is non-<s>dharma</s>, due to their dullness and confusion. Those who have the perception of <s>dharma</s> regarding non-<s>dharma</s> — even though they practice as instructed, they should be understood as wrongly practiced. This kind of failure of yoga caused by wrong practice is a counterfeit of the true <s>Dharma</s>, for it is false <s>dharma</s> [leading] to the disappearance of the true <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: itīme catvāro yogabhraṃśā dhyāyinā bhikṣuṇā yogācāreṇa parijñeyā varjayitavyāḥ //
body.translated_text: These four failures of yoga are to be fully known and avoided by the meditating <s>bhikṣu</s>, the yoga-practitioner.

body.text:
(II)-A-II-8-a Ms-82b7M, Sh.275-23, W.92-31, Choi.163-1, P.125b8, D.102b2, N.108a3, Co.107a4, Ch.438a16
tatra yogaḥ katamaḥ / āha / caturvidho yogaḥ / tadyathā śraddhā chando vīryam upāyaś ca //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is yoga? It is said: Yoga is fourfold — namely: faith, aspiration, energy, and skillful means.

body.text:
-II-8-a-(1) Ms.82b7R, Sh.276-2, W.92-32, Choi.163-9, P.126a1, D.102b3, N.108a3, Co.107a4, Ch.438a17
tatra śraddhā dvyākārā dvividhādhiṣṭhānā, abhisaṃpratyayākārā prasādākārā ca, dharmayuktivicāraṇādhiṣṭhānā pudgalānubhāvādhimuktyadhiṣṭhānā ca //
body.translated_text: Therein, faith is of two aspects and has two kinds of basis: the aspect of conviction and the aspect of confidence; the basis of investigation of <s>dharma</s>-logic and the basis of inclination through the influence of persons.

body.text:
-II-8-a-(2) Ms.82b8L, Sh.276-5, W/92-35, Choi.163-10, 7, P.126a2, D.102b4, N.108a4, Co.107a5, Ch.438a20
chando 'pi caturvidhaḥ / tadyathā prāptaye yathāpīhaikatya uttare vimokṣaspṛhām utpādayati, vistareṇa pūrvavat / paripṛcchāyai yathāpīhaikatyaḥ spṛhām utpādayaty ārāmaṃ gamanāya, vijñānāṃ sabrahmacāriṇāṃ yogajñānām antikam aśrutasya śravaṇāya, śrutasya ca paryavadānāya / saṃbhārasamudāgamāya cchando yathāpīhaikatyaḥ śīlasaṃvarapāriśuddhaye, indriyasaṃvarapāriśuddhaye, bhojane mātrajñatāyām, jāgarikānuyoge, saṃprajānadvihāritāyām uttarottarāṃ spṛhām utpādayati / anuyogāya cchando yathāpīhaikatyaḥ sātatyaprayogatāyāṃ satkṛtyaprayogatāyāṃ ca mārgabhāvanāyāṃ spṛhām utpādayaty abhilāṣaṃ kartukāmatām / ity ayaṃ caturvidhaś chandaḥ / yaduta prāptaye paripṛcchanāyai saṃbhārasamudāgamāya anuyogāya ca //
body.translated_text: Aspiration too is fourfold — namely: for attainment — just as here someone generates longing for the higher liberation, and so on in detail as before. For inquiry — just as here someone generates longing to go to a park, to the presence of wise co-practitioners in the holy life who know yoga, for the purpose of hearing what has not been heard and for the purification of what has been heard. For the accomplishment of the accumulations — just as here someone generates ever-higher longing for the purification of moral restraint, for the purification of sense-faculty restraint, for moderation in food, for the practice of wakefulness, and for dwelling in clear comprehension. For devoted practice — just as here someone generates longing, desire, and the wish to act with regard to continuous application and respectful application in the cultivation of the path. This is the fourfold aspiration — namely: for attainment, for inquiry, for the accomplishment of the accumulations, and for devoted practice.

body.text:
-II-8-a-(3) Ms.83a1R, Sh.276-20, W.*93-1, Choi.164-8, P.126a8, D.102b7, N.108b1, Co.107b2, Ch.438b1
tatra vīryam api caturvidhaṃ tadyathā śravaṇāya, cintanāyai, bhāvanāyai, āvaraṇapāriśuddhaye ca /
body.translated_text: Therein, energy too is fourfold — namely: for hearing, for reflection, for cultivation, and for the purification of obstructions.

body.text: tatra śravaṇāya vīryaṃ / yad aśrutaṃ ca śṛṇvataḥ, paryavadāpayataḥ, cetaso 'bhyutsāhaḥ, avinyastaprayogatā / evaṃ yathāśrutānāṃ dharmāṇām ekākino rahogatasyārtham, cintayatas tulayata upaparīkṣamāṇasya / evaṃ pratisaṃlayanapraviṣṭasya kālena kālaṃ śamathavipaśyanāṃ bhāvayataḥ / evam ahorātrānuyuktasya caṃkramaniṣadyābhyāṃ nivaraṇebhyaś cittaṃ viśodhayataḥ, yaś cetaso 'bhyutsāhaḥ, avinyastaprayogatā //
body.translated_text: Therein, energy for hearing — when, while hearing what has not been heard, while mastering [it], there is mental enthusiasm and non-relaxation of effort. Similarly, when one, alone and secluded, contemplates, weighs, and examines the meaning of the <s>dharmas</s> as heard. Similarly, when one, having entered withdrawal, from time to time cultivates <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight). Similarly, when one, engaged day and night, purifies the mind of the hindrances through walking and sitting — that mental enthusiasm and non-relaxation of effort.

body.text:
-II-8-a-(4) Ms.83a3M, Sh.277-10, W.*93-3, Choi.165-1, P.126b5, D.103a4, N.108b5, Co.107b5, Ch.438b9
tatropāyo 'pi caturvidhaḥ / tadyathā śīlasaṃvaram indriyasaṃvaram adhipatiṃ kṛtvā sūpasthitasmṛtitā tathā copasthitasmṛter apramādaś cetasa ārakṣā / kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ niṣevaṇā / tathā vāpramattasyādhyātmaṃ cetaḥśamathayogaḥ / adhiprajñaṃ ca dharmavipaśyanā //
body.translated_text: Therein, the method (<s>upāya</s>) is also fourfold. Namely: having the restraint of moral conduct and the restraint of the sense faculties as the basis — well-established mindfulness and, for one of established mindfulness, heedfulness and the guarding of the mind; the practice of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>; likewise, for the heedful one, the yoga of internal mental calm (<s>cetaḥśamatha</s>); and, with higher wisdom, the investigation of <s>dharmas</s> through insight (<s>dharmavipaśyanā</s>).

body.text: sa cāyaṃ yogaś caturvidhaḥ / ṣoḍaśākāro bhavati //
body.translated_text: And this fourfold yoga has sixteen aspects.

body.text:
-II-8-b Ms.83a4M, Sh.277-16, W.93-23, Choi.165-10, P.126b8, D.103a6, N.108b7, Co.107b7, Ch.438b13
tatra śraddhayā prāptavyam artham abhisaṃpratyeti / prāptim (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 156

children.text: ) abhisaṃpratyayāt kartukāmatām utpādayati kuśaleṣu dharmeṣu / sa evaṃ kartukāmo 'horātrānuyukto viharati / utsāhī dṛḍhaparākramaḥ / tac ca vīryam upāyaparigṛhītam aprāptasya prāptaye, anadhigatasyādhigamāya asākṣātkṛtasya sākṣātkriyāyai saṃvartate / tasmād ime catvāro dharmā yoga ity ucyate41 //
children.translated_text: ment, one generates the desire to act with regard to wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. Thus desiring to act, one dwells devoted day and night, enthusiastic, of firm perseverance. And that vigor, being accompanied by method, conduces to the attainment of the unattained, to the realization of the unrealized, and to the direct experience of the directly unexperienced. Therefore these four <s>dharmas</s> are called yoga.

body.translated_text: Therein, through faith one believes in the goal to be attained. From believing in the attain-

body.text:
(II)-A-II-9-a Ms.83a5R, Sh.278-1, W.94-1, P.127a3, D.103b1, N.109a2, Co.108a2,Ch.438b19
tatra manasikāraḥ katamaḥ / catvāro manaskārāḥ / katame catvāraḥ / tadyathā balavāhanaḥ, sacchidravāhanaḥ, niśchidravāhanaḥ, anābhogavāhanaś ca //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is mental attention (<s>manasikāra</s>)? There are four mental attentions. Which four? Namely: forceful application (<s>balavāhana</s>), application with gaps (<s>sacchidravāhana</s>), application without gaps (<s>niśchidravāhana</s>), and effortless application (<s>anābhogavāhana</s>).

body.text:
-II-9-a-(1) Ms.83a6R, Sh.278-8, W.94-3, P.127a4, D.103b2, N.109a3, Co.108a3, Ch.438b21
tatra balavāhano manaskāraḥ katamaḥ / tadyathā ādikarmikasyādhyātmam eva cittaṃ sthāpayataḥ saṃsthāpayataś ca dharmān pravicinvataḥ, yāvan manaskāraṃ na prāpnoti, tāvad asya balavāhano manaskāro bhavati / balād avaṣṭabhya tac cittam ekāgratāyām avasthāpayati / tenocyate balavāhana iti //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the mental attention of forceful application? When a beginner (<s>ādikarmika</s>) is internally settling and stabilizing the mind and investigating <s>dharmas</s>, for as long as he has not yet attained [proper] mental attention — that long his mental attention is of forceful application. By force he holds that mind in one-pointedness. Therefore it is called 'forceful application.'

body.text:
-II-9-a-(2) Ms.83a7M, Sh.279-5, W.94-8, P. 127a6, D. 103b3, N. 109a5, Co. 108a4, Ch.438b25
tatra sacchidravāhano manaskāraḥ katamaḥ / yo labdhamanaskārasyordhvaṃ laukikena mārgeṇa gacchato lokottareṇa vā yo lakṣaṇapratisaṃvedī manaskāraḥ / tathā hi samādhis tatra cintayā vyavakīryate, naikāntena bhāvanākāreṇa pravartate //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the mental attention of application with gaps? For one who has attained mental attention, going higher through the worldly path or the supramundane path — the mental attention that perceives characteristics. For therein, concentration is interspersed with reflection, and does not proceed exclusively in the mode of cultivation.

body.text:
-II-9-a-(3) Ms.83a8L, Sh.279-10, W.94-11, P.127b1, D.103b5, N.109a6, Co.108a5, Ch.438b28
tatra niśchidravāhano manaskāraḥ katamaḥ / lakṣaṇapratisaṃvedino manaskārād ūrdhvaṃ yāvat prayoganiṣṭhān manasikārāt //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the mental attention of application without gaps? From the mental attention that perceives characteristics onwards, up to the mental attention of the culmination of practice.

body.text:
-II-9-a-(4) Ms.83a8M, Sh.279-12, W.94-13, P.127b2, D.103b5, N.109a7, Co.108a6, Ch.438c1
tatrānābhogavāhano manaskāraḥ katamaḥ / yaḥ prayoganiṣṭhāphalo manaskāraḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the mental attention of effortless application? The mental attention that is the fruit of the culmination of practice.

body.text:
-II-9-b-(1),(2),(3),(4) Ms.83a8R, Sh.279-14, P.127b3, D.103b6, N.109a7, Co.108a7, Ch.438c3
apare catvāro manaskārāḥ / tadyathā ānulomikaḥ, prātipakṣikaḥ, prasadanīyaḥ, pratyavekṣaṇīyaś ca /
body.translated_text: There are another four mental attentions. Namely: conforming (<s>ānulomika</s>), opposing (<s>prātipakṣika</s>), gladdening (<s>prasadanīya</s>), and reviewing (<s>pratyavekṣaṇīya</s>).

body.text: tatrānulomiko manaskāraḥ / yenālambanaṃ vidūṣayati samyakprayogaṃ cārabhate, no tu kleśaṃ prajahāti /
body.translated_text: Therein, the conforming mental attention is that by which one becomes disgusted with the object and commences correct practice, but does not yet abandon the defilement.

body.text: tatra prātipakṣikaḥ / yena kleśaṃ prajahāti /
body.translated_text: Therein, the opposing is that by which one abandons the defilement.

body.text: tatra prasadanīyaḥ / yena līnaṃ cittaṃ pragrāhakair nimittair abhipramodayati saṃpraharṣayati pragṛhṇāti /
body.translated_text: Therein, the gladdening is that by which, when the mind is sunken, one delights, encourages, and uplifts it with signs that uplift.

body.text: tatra pratyavekṣaṇīyo manaskāraḥ / tadyathā mīmāṃsāmanaskāraḥ, yam adhipatiṃ kṛtvā prahīṇāprahīṇatāṃ kleśānāṃ pratyavekṣate //
body.translated_text: Therein, the reviewing mental attention is like the mental attention of investigation (<s>mīmāṃsā</s>), having which as the basis, one reviews whether defilements have been abandoned or not abandoned.

body.text:
-II-9-c Ms.83b2L, Sh.280-4, P. 127b8, D. 104a2, N. 109b4, Co. 108b3, Ch.438c10
tatrālambanaṃ manasikurvatā kati nimittāni manasikartavyāni bhavanti / āha / catvāri / tadyathālambananimittaṃ nidānanimittaṃ parivarjanīyaṃ nimittaṃ niṣevaṇīyaṃ ca nimittam //
body.translated_text: Therein, for one attending to the object, how many signs are to be attended to? He says: four. Namely: the sign of the object (<s>ālambananimitta</s>), the sign of the cause (<s>nidānanimitta</s>), the sign to be avoided (<s>parivarjanīyanimitta</s>), and the sign to be practiced (<s>niṣevaṇīyanimitta</s>).

body.text:
-II-9-c-(1) Ms.83b2R, Sh.280-7, P.128a1, D.104a3, N.109b5, Co.108b4, Ch.438c12
tatrālambananimittam / yaj jñeyavastusabhāgaṃ pratibimbaṃ pratibhāsaḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, the sign of the object: the reflection that is a likeness of the knowable object — the mental appearance.

body.text:
-II-9-c-(2) Ms.83b3L, Sh.280-10, P.128a2, D.104a3, N.109b5, Co.108b4, Ch.438c13
tatra nidānanimittam / tadyathā samādhisaṃbhāropacayaḥ, ānulomika (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 162

children.text: ) upadeśaḥ, bhāvanāsahagatas tīvracchandaḥ saṃvejanīyeṣu dharmeṣu saṃvegaḥ, vikṣepāvikṣepaparijñāvadhānam, parataś cāsaṃghaṭṭo manuṣyakṛto vāmanuṣyakṛto vā śabdakṛto vā vyāyāmakṛto vā / tathā vipaśyanāpūrvaṃgamo 'dhyātmaṃ cittābhisaṃkṣepa uttaptatarāyā vipaśyanāyā uttaratra nidānanimittam / tathā śamathapūrvaṃgamā vipaśyanā uttaptatarasya śamathasyottaratra nidānanimittam //
children.translated_text: instruction, intense desire accompanied by cultivation, a sense of urgency regarding <s>dharmas</s> that cause urgency, awareness of the recognition of distraction and non-distraction, and from others, non-disturbance whether caused by humans or non-humans, by sounds or by exertion. Likewise, insight preceded by the internal concentration of the mind — this is the causal sign for more intense insight further on. Likewise, insight preceded by calm — this is the causal sign for more intense calm further on.

body.translated_text: Therein, the sign of the cause: the accumulation of the equipment for concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), conforming

body.text:
-II-9-c-(3)-i,ii,iii,iv Ms.83b4M, Sh.280-19, P.128a6, D.104a6, N.110a1, Co.108b6, Ch.438c19
tatra parivarjanīyanimittaṃ caturvidham / tadyathā layanimittam auddhatyanimittaṃ saṅganimittaṃ vikṣepanimittaṃ ca /
body.translated_text: Therein, the sign to be avoided is of four kinds. Namely: the sign of sinking (<s>layanimitta</s>), the sign of restlessness (<s>auddhatyanimittā</s>), the sign of attachment (<s>saṅganimitta</s>), and the sign of distraction (<s>vikṣepanimitta</s>).

body.text: tatra layanimittam / yenālambananimittena nidānanimittena cittaṃ līnatvāya paraiti /
body.translated_text: Therein, the sign of sinking: that object-sign or causal sign by which the mind tends toward sinking.

body.text: tatra auddhatyanimittam / yenālambananimittena nidānanimittena cittam uddhanyate /
body.translated_text: Therein, the sign of restlessness: that object-sign or causal sign by which the mind becomes restless.

body.text: tatra saṅganimittam / yenālambananimittena nidānanimittena cittam ālambane rajyate saṃrajyate saṃkliśyate /
body.translated_text: Therein, the sign of attachment: that object-sign or causal sign by which the mind becomes attached, passionately attached, and defiled with respect to the object.

body.text: tatra vikṣepanimittam / yenālambananimittena nidānanimittena cittaṃ bahirdhā vikṣipyate /
body.translated_text: Therein, the sign of distraction: that object-sign or causal sign by which the mind is scattered outwardly.

body.text: tāni punar nimittāni yathā samāhitāyāṃ bhūmau //
body.translated_text: Those signs are as [established] in the stage of concentration.

body.text:
-II-9-d Ms.83b6L, Sh.281-8, P.128b2, D.104b2, N.110a4, Co.109a2, Ch.438c26
ebhir manaskārair ālambanam adhimucyataḥ katy adhimokṣā bhavanti / āha / navādhimokṣāḥ / tadyathā prabhāsvaraś cāprabhāsvaraś ca jaḍaḥ paṭuḥ parītto mahadgato 'pramāṇaḥ pariśuddho 'pariśuddhaś ceti /
body.translated_text: For one who thus resolves upon the object through these mental attentions, how many resolutions (<s>adhimokṣa</s>) are there? He says: nine resolutions. Namely: luminous and non-luminous, dull and acute, limited and great, immeasurable, purified, and unpurified.

body.text: tatra prabhāsvaro 'dhimokṣaḥ / ya ālokanimitte sūdgṛhīta ālokasahagataḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, the luminous resolution: one that is well-grasped in the sign of light, accompanied by light.

body.text: tatrāprabhāsvaro 'dhimokṣaḥ / tadyathā ālokanimitte 'nudgṛhīte 'ndhakārasahagataḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, the non-luminous resolution: when the sign of light is not grasped, accompanied by darkness.

body.text: tatra jaḍo 'dhimokṣaḥ / yo mṛdvindriyasantānapatitaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, the dull resolution: one that falls within the continuum of soft faculties.

body.text: tatra paṭur adhimokṣaḥ / yas tīkṣṇendriyasantānapatitaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, the acute resolution: one that falls within the continuum of sharp faculties.

body.text: tatra parītto 'dhimokṣaḥ / yaḥ parīttaśraddhāchandasahagataḥ parīttālambanaś ca / iti manaskāraparīttatayā cālambanaparīttatayā ca parītto 'dhimokṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, the limited resolution: one that is accompanied by limited faith and desire, and having a limited object. Thus, through the limitedness of the mental attention and the limitedness of the object, the resolution is limited.

body.text: tatra mahadgato 'dhimokṣaḥ / tadyathā yo mahadgataśraddhāchandasahagataḥ, mahadgataṃ vālambanam adhimucyate yo 'dhimokṣaḥ / iti manaskāramahadgatatayā cālambanamahadgatatayā ca mahadgato 'dhimokṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, the great resolution: one that is accompanied by great faith and desire, or one that resolves upon a great object. Thus, through the greatness of the mental attention and the greatness of the object, the resolution is great.

body.text: tatrāpramāṇo 'dhimokṣaḥ / apramāṇaśraddhāchandasahagataḥ, anantam vā aparyantam ālambanam adhimucyate yo 'dhimokṣaḥ / iti manaskārāpramāṇatayā cālambanāpramāṇatayā cāpramāṇo 'dhimokṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, the immeasurable resolution: one accompanied by immeasurable faith and desire, or one that resolves upon an infinite, limitless object. Thus, through the immeasurability of the mental attention and the immeasurability of the object, the resolution is immeasurable.

body.text: tatra pariśuddho 'dhimokṣaḥ / yaḥ subhāvitaḥ pariniṣpannaḥ paryavasānagataḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, the purified resolution: one that is well-cultivated, accomplished, and has reached its culmination.

body.text: apariśuddho vā punaḥ yo na subhāvito na pariniṣpanno na paryavasānagataḥ //
body.translated_text: And the unpurified: one that is not well-cultivated, not accomplished, and has not reached its culmination.

body.text:
(II)-A-II-10 Ms.84a1R, Sh.283-2, W.*95-4, P.129a3, D.104b7, N.110b4, Co.109b2, Ch.439a16
tatra kati yogasya yogakaraṇīyāni / āha / catvāri / katamāni catvāri / tadyathāśrayanirodhaḥ, āśrayaparivartaḥ, ālambanaparijñānam, ālambanābhiratiś ca /
body.translated_text: Therein, how many are the tasks of yoga (<s>yogakaraṇīya</s>)? He says: four. Which four? Namely: the cessation of the basis (<s>āśrayanirodha</s>), the transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparivarta</s>), the full knowledge of the object (<s>ālambanaparijñāna</s>), and delight in the object (<s>ālambanābhirati</s>).

body.text: tatrāśrayanirodhaḥ prayogamanasikārabhāvanānuyuktasya yo dauṣṭhulyasahagata āśrayaḥ so 'nupūrveṇa nirudhyate, prasrabdhisahagataś cāśrayaḥ parivartate / ayam āśrayanirodho 'yam āśrayaparivarto yogakaraṇīyam /
body.translated_text: Therein, the cessation of the basis: for one devoted to the practice of mental attention and cultivation, the basis that is accompanied by unsuitability (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>) gradually ceases, and the basis accompanied by tranquility (<s>prasrabdhi</s>) is transformed. This is the cessation of the basis and the transformation of the basis — the task of yoga.

body.text: tatrālambanaparijñānam ālambanābhiratiś ca / asty ālambanaparijñānam ālambanābhiratir āśrayanirodhaparivartapūrvaṃgamam, yac cālambanaparijñānam ālambanābhiratiṃ cādhipatiṃ kṛtvāśrayo nirudhyate parivartate ca / asty ālambanaparijñānam ālambanābhiratir āśrayaviśuddhipūrvaṃgamam āśrayaśuddhim adhipatiṃ kṛtvā suviśuddham ālambanajñānaṃ kāryapariniṣpattikāle pravartate, abhiratiś ca /
body.translated_text: Therein, the full knowledge of the object and the delight in the object: there is a full knowledge of the object and a delight in the object that are preceded by the cessation and transformation of the basis; and there is a cessation and transformation of the basis that take the full knowledge of the object and the delight in the object as their governing [factor]. There is a full knowledge of the object and a delight in the object preceded by the purification of the basis — having the purification of the basis as the governing [factor], at the time of the accomplishment of the result, the thoroughly purified knowledge of the object and the delight [in it] proceed.

body.text: tenocyate catvāri yogasya yogakaraṇīyānīti //
body.translated_text: Therefore it is said that there are four tasks of yoga.

body.text:
(II)-A-II-11-a-(1),(2),(3) Ms.84a4R, Sh.284-4, W.95-11, P.129b2, D.105a5, N.111a2, Co.109b6, Ch.439b1
tatra kati yogācārāḥ / āha / trayaḥ / tadyathā ādikarmikaḥ, kṛtaparicayaḥ, atikrāntamanaskāraś ca /
body.translated_text: Therein, how many are the practitioners of yoga (<s>yogācāra</s>)? He says: three. Namely: the beginner (<s>ādikarmika</s>), the experienced (<s>kṛtaparicaya</s>), and the one who has transcended mental attention (<s>atikrāntamanaskāra</s>).

body.text: tatrādikarmiko yogācāro manaskārādikarmikaḥ kleśaviśuddhyādikarmikaś ca /
body.translated_text: Therein, the beginner practitioner of yoga is a beginner with respect to mental attention and a beginner with respect to the purification from defilements.

body.text: tatra manaskārādikarmikas tatprathamakarmika ekāgratāyāṃ yāvan manaskāraṃ na prāpnoti cittaikāgratāṃ na spṛśati /
body.translated_text: Therein, the beginner with respect to mental attention is one who is a first-time practitioner in one-pointedness, who has not yet attained mental attention and has not yet touched one-pointedness of mind.

body.text: tatra kleśaviśuddhyādikarmikaḥ / adhigate 'pi manaskāre kleśasya cittaṃ viśodhayitukāmasya yaIIakṣaṇapratisaṃvedino manaskārasyārambhaḥ pratigrahaś cābhyāsaḥ / ayaṃ kleśaviśuddhyādikarmikaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, the beginner with respect to the purification from defilements: even when mental attention has been attained, for one who wishes to purify the mind from defilement, the commencement, undertaking, and practice of the mental attention that perceives characteristics — this is the beginner with respect to the purification from defilements.

body.text: tatra kṛtaparicayaḥ katamaḥ / lakṣaṇapratisaṃvedinaṃ manaskāram sthāpayitvā tadanyeṣu ṣaṭsu manaskāreṣu prayoganiṣṭhāparyanteṣu kṛtaparicayo bhavati /
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the experienced (<s>kṛtaparicaya</s>)? Setting aside the mental attention that perceives characteristics, in the other six mental attentions up to the culmination of practice, one becomes experienced.

body.text: tatrātikrāntamanaskāraḥ prayoganiṣṭhāphale manaskāre veditavyaḥ / atikrānto 'sau bhavati prayogabhāvanāmanaskāram, sthito bhavati bhāvanāphale / tasmād atikrāntamanaskāra ity ucyate //
body.translated_text: Therein, the one who has transcended mental attention should be understood as being in the mental attention that is the fruit of the culmination of practice. He has transcended the mental attention of the practice of cultivation, and is established in the fruit of cultivation. Therefore he is called 'one who has transcended mental attention.'

body.text:
-11-11-b-(1),(2),(3) Ms.84a7M, Sh.284-23, P.130a1, D.105b3, N.111a7, Co.110a3, Ch.439b15
api ca kuśalaṃ dharmacchandam upādāya prayujyamāno yāvan nirvedhabhāgīyāni kuśalamūlāni notpādayati tāvad ādikarmiko bhavati /
body.translated_text: Moreover, relying on wholesome desire for the <s>Dharma</s>, when one who is practicing has not yet generated the wholesome roots conducive to penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>) — that long one is a beginner.

body.text: yadā punar nirvedhabhāgīyāny utpādayati, tadyathā ūṣmagatāni mūrdhānaḥ (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 170

children.text: ) satyānulomāḥ kṣāntayo laukikā agradharmāḥ, tadā kṛtaparicayo bhavati /
children.translated_text: the conforming patient acceptances of the truths (<s>satyānulomakṣānti</s>), and the worldly supreme <s>dharmas</s> (<s>laukikāgradharmā</s>) — then one is experienced.

body.translated_text: When one generates the [roots] conducive to penetration, namely the heat (<s>ūṣmagata</s>), the peaks (<s>mūrdhāna</s>),

body.text: yadā punaḥ samyaktvaṃ nyāmam avakrāmati satyāny abhisamāgacchaty aparapratyayo bhavaty ananyaneyaḥ śāstuḥ śāsane, tadātikrāntamanaskāro bhavati / parapratyayaṃ manaskāram atikramyāparapratyaye sthitaḥ / tasmād, atikrāntamanaskāra ity ucyate //
body.translated_text: When one enters into the certainty of correctness (<s>samyaktvaniyāma</s>), realizes the truths, becomes one who is not dependent on another, and cannot be led astray in the <s>Śāstā's</s> (Teacher's) teaching — then one has transcended mental attention. Having transcended the mental attention that depends on another, one is established in the state of not depending on another. Therefore one is called 'one who has transcended mental attention.'

body.text:
(II)-A-II-12-a-(1) Ms.84b1L, Sh.285-11, W.96-14, P.130a6, D.105b6, N.111b4, Co.110a6, Ch.439b22
tatra yogabhāvanā katamā / āha / dvividhā / tadyathā saṃjñābhāvanā bodhipakṣyā bhāvanā ca /
body.translated_text: (II)-A-II-12-a-(1) — Therein, what is yoga cultivation? It is said: It is twofold, namely: cultivation of perceptions and cultivation of the factors conducive to awakening.

body.text: tatra saṃjñābhāvanā katamā / tadyathā laukikamārgaprayuktaḥ sarvāsv adharimāsu bhūmiṣv ādīnavasaṃjñāṃ bhāvayati / nirvāṇāya vā punaḥ prayuktaḥ prahāṇadhātau virāgadhātau nirodhadhātau śāntadarśī prahāṇasaṃjñāṃ virāgasaṃjñāṃ nirodhasaṃjñāṃ ca bhāvayati / śamathāya vā punaḥ prayukta ūrdhvamadhaḥsaṃjñāṃ śamathapakṣyāṃ bhāvayati / vipaśyanāyāṃ prayuktaḥ paścātpuraḥsaṃjñāṃ vipaśyanāpakṣyāṃ bhāvayati //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the cultivation of perceptions? Such as: one engaged in the worldly path cultivates the perception of danger in all the lower realms. Or again, one engaged toward <s>nirvāṇa</s>, seeing peace in the element of abandonment, the element of dispassion, and the element of cessation, cultivates the perception of abandonment, the perception of dispassion, and the perception of cessation. Or again, one engaged in <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) cultivates the perception of above-and-below, belonging to the side of calm abiding. One engaged in <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) cultivates the perception of behind-and-in-front, belonging to the side of insight.

body.text:
-II-12-a-(2) Ms.84b2R, Sh.287-2, P.130b1, D.106a2, N.111b7, Co.110b1, Ch.439b28
tatrordhvamadhaḥsaṃjñī imam eva kāyaṃ yathāsthitaṃ yathāpraṇihitam ūrdhvaṃ pādatalād adhaḥ keśamastakāt pūrṇaṃ nānāvidhasyāśuceḥ pratyavekṣate / santy asmin kāye keśā romāṇīti pūrvavat /
tatra paścātpuraḥsaṃjñī / yathāpi tad ekatyena pratyavekṣaṇānimittam eva sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca sūdgṛhītaṃ bhavati sumanasīkṛtam sujuṣṭaṃ supratividdham / tadyathā sthito niṣaṇṇaṃ pratyavekṣate, niṣaṇṇo vā nipannam, purato vā gacchantaṃ pṛṣṭhato gacchan pratyavekṣate / sā khalv eṣā traiyadhvikānāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ pratītyasamutpannānāṃ vipaśyanākārā pratyavekṣā paridīpitā /
body.translated_text: -II-12-a-(2) — Therein, one with the perception of above-and-below examines this very body, as it is situated, as it is positioned — from the soles of the feet upward, from the top of the head downward — as full of various impurities: "In this body there are head-hairs, body-hairs" — and so on as before. Therein, one with the perception of behind-and-in-front: just as when someone has well and thoroughly grasped the sign for examination, well attended to it, well practiced it, well penetrated it — such as when standing, one examines one who is sitting; or sitting, one who is lying down; or going behind, one examines one going in front — this indeed is the insight-mode examination of formations of the three times that have arisen dependently, which is here illuminated.

body.text: tatra yat tāvad āha "sthito niṣaṇṇaṃ pratyavekṣata" ity anena paridīpitaṃ vartamānena manaskāreṇa_ anāgataṃ jñeyaṃ pratyavekṣate / vartamānāpi (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 174

children.text: ) manaskārāvasthā utpannā "sthite"ty ucyate / anāgatā punar jñeyāvasthā anutpannatvād utpādābhimukhatvāc ca "niṣaṇṇe"ty ucyate /
children.translated_text: state of mental engagement that has arisen is called 'standing.' But the future state of the knowable, being unarisen yet facing arising, is called 'sitting.'

body.translated_text: Therein, the statement: "Standing, one examines one who is sitting" — by this it is illuminated that with a present mental engagement one examines a future knowable object. Even the present

body.text: yat punar āha "niṣaṇṇo vā nipannaṃ pratyavekṣata" ity anena pratyutpannena manaskāreṇātītasya jñeyasya pratyavekṣaṇā paridīpitā / pratyutpannā hi manaskārāvasthā nirodhābhimukhā "niṣaṇṇe"ty ucyate / atītā punar niruddhatvāj jñeyāvasthā "nipanne"ty ucyate /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the statement: "Sitting, one examines one who is lying down" — by this the examination of a past knowable by a present mental engagement is illuminated. For the present state of mental engagement, facing cessation, is called 'sitting.' But the past state of the knowable, having ceased, is called 'lying down.'

body.text: yat punar āha "purato vā gacchantaṃ pṛṣṭhato gacchan pratyavekṣata" ity anena pratyutpannena manaskāreṇānantaraniruddhasya manaskārasya pratyavekṣā paridīpitā / tatra ya utpannotpanno manasikāro 'nantaraniruddhah sa purato yāyī /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the statement: "Going behind, one examines one going in front" — by this the examination of the immediately ceased mental engagement by a present mental engagement is illuminated. Therein, whatever mental engagement has arisen and immediately ceased — that is 'the one going in front.'

body.text: tatra yo 'nantarotpanno 'nantarotpanno manaskāro navanavo 'nantaraniruddhasyānantaraniruddhasya grāhakaḥ sa pṛṣṭhato yāyī /
body.translated_text: Therein, whatever mental engagement has immediately arisen, newly and freshly — which grasps the one that has immediately and successively ceased — that is 'the one going behind.'

body.text: tatra śamathaṃ ca vipaśyanāṃ ca bhāvayaṃs tadubhayapakṣyām ālokasaṃjñāṃ bhāvayati / iyaṃ saṃjñābhāvanā //
body.translated_text: Therein, cultivating both <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), one cultivates the perception of light belonging to both sides. This is the cultivation of perceptions.

body.text:
II-12-b Ms.84b7M, Sh.288-19, W.*97-1, P.131a5, D.106b3, N.112b2, Co.111a2, Ch.439c18
tatra bodhipakṣyabhāvanā katamā / yaḥ saptatriṃśatāṃ bodhipakṣyāṇāṃ dharmāṇām abhyāsaḥ paricaya āsevanā bhāvanā bahulīkāra iyam ucyate bodhipakṣyabhāvanā / tadyathā caturṇām smṛtyupasthānānām, caturṇāṃ (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 176

children.text: ) samyakprahāṇānām, caturṇām ṛddhipādānām, pañcanām indriyāṇām, pañcānāṃ balānām, saptānāṃ bodhyaṅgānām, āryāṣṭāṅgasya mārgasya /
children.translated_text: <s>samyakprahāṇas</s> (right strivings), of the four <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of spiritual power), of the five <s>indriyas</s> (faculties), of the five <s>balas</s> (powers), of the seven <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening), and of the noble eightfold path.

body.translated_text: -II-12-b — Therein, what is the cultivation of the factors conducive to awakening? The practice, familiarization, repeated engagement, cultivation, and frequent application of the thirty-seven <s>dharmas</s> conducive to awakening — this is called cultivation of the factors conducive to awakening. Namely: of the four <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness), of the four

body.text: kāyasmṛtyupasthānasya vedanācittadharmasmṛtyupasthānasya /
body.translated_text: Of the foundation of mindfulness on the body, of the foundation of mindfulness on feelings, mind, and <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: anutpannānāṃ pāpakānām akuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām anutpādāya cchandaiḥ janayati vyāyacchate vīryam ārabhate cittaṃ pragṛhṇāti pradadhātīti samyakprahāṇasya, utpannānāṃ pāpakānām akuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ prahāṇāya, anutpannānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām utpādāya, utpannānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām sthitaye 'saṃmoṣāya bhāvanāparipūraye bhūyobhāvavṛddhivipulatāyai chandaṃ janayati vyāyacchate vīryam ārabhate cittaṃ pragṛhṇāti pradadhātīti samyakprahāṇasya /
body.translated_text: For the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, one generates desire, strives, arouses energy, exerts the mind, and applies oneself — this is the right striving; for the abandonment of arisen evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>; for the arising of unarisen wholesome <s>dharmas</s>; for the stability, non-confusion, development, fulfillment, increase, growth, and abundance of arisen wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, one generates desire, strives, arouses energy, exerts the mind, and applies oneself — this is the right striving.

body.text: chandasamādhiprahāṇasaṃskārasamanvāgatasya ṛddhipādasya, vīryacittamīmāṃsāsamādhiprahāṇasaṃskārasamanvāgatasya ṛddhipādasya /
body.translated_text: Of the basis of spiritual power endowed with the concentration of desire and the formations of striving; of the basis of spiritual power endowed with the concentration of energy, mind, and investigation and the formations of striving.

body.text: śraddhāvīryasmṛtisamādhiprajñendriyasya /
body.translated_text: Of the faculty of faith, energy, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom.

body.text: śraddhāvīryasmṛtisamādhiprajñābalānām /
body.translated_text: Of the powers of faith, energy, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom.

body.text: smṛtisaṃbodhyaṅgasya dharmapravicayavīryaprītipraśrabdhisamādhyupekṣāsaṃbodhyaṅgasya ca /
body.translated_text: Of the awakening-factor of mindfulness; of the awakening-factor of investigation of <s>dharmas</s>, energy, joy, tranquility, concentration, and equanimity.

body.text: samyagdṛṣṭeḥ samyaksaṃkalpasya samyagvākkarmāntājīvānām samyagvyāyāmasya samyaksmṛteḥ samyaksamādheś ca //
body.translated_text: Of right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration.

body.text:
-II-12-b-(1)-i-(a) Ms.85a3R, Sh.291-5, W.97-22, P.132a1, D.107a4, N.113a3, Co.111b3, Ch.440a13
tatra katamaḥ kāyaḥ / katamā kāye kāyānupaśyanā / katamā smṛtiḥ / katamāni smṛter upasthānāni / āha /
body.translated_text: -II-12-b-(1)-i-(a) — Therein, what is the body? What is the contemplation of the body in the body? What is <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness)? What is the establishment of mindfulness? It is said:

body.text: kāyaḥ pañcatriṃśatividhaḥ / tadyathā ādhyātmiko bāhyaś ca, indriyasaṃgṛhīto 'nindriyasaṃgṛhītaś ca, sattvasaṃkhyāto 'sattvasaṃkhyātaś ca, dauṣṭhulyasahagataḥ praśrabdhisahagataś ca, bhūtakāyo bhautikakāyaś ca, nāmakāyo rūpakāyaś ca, nārakas tairyagyonikaḥ paitṛviṣayiko mānuṣyako divyaś ca, savijñānako 'vijñānako vā, antaḥkāyo bahiḥkāyaś ca, vipariṇato 'vipariṇataś ca, strīkāyaḥ puruṣakāyaḥ paṇḍakakāyaś ca, mitrakāyo 'mitrakāya udāsīnakāyaś ca, hīnakāyo madhyakāyaḥ praṇītakāyaś ca, dahrakāyo yūnakāyo vṛddhakāyaś ca / ayaṃ tāvat kāyasya prabhedaḥ //
body.translated_text: The body is of thirty-five kinds, namely: internal and external; included among the faculties and not included among the faculties; counted as sentient-being and not counted as sentient-being; accompanied by unsuitability and accompanied by tranquility; the primary-element body and the derived-element body; the name-body and the form-body; of hell-beings, of animals, of the realm of the departed, of humans, and of gods; with consciousness and without consciousness; the inner body and the outer body; transformed and untransformed; the female body, the male body, and the neuter body; the body of a friend, the body of an enemy, and the body of one who is indifferent; the inferior body, the middling body, and the excellent body; the body of a child, the body of a youth, and the body of an elder. This is the classification of the body.

body.text:
-II-12-b-(1)-i-(b) Ms.85a5R, Sh.292-11, P.132a7, D.107b1, N.113a7, Co.111b7, Ch.440a21
tatrānupaśyanā trividhā / yā kāyam adhipatiṃ kṛtvā śrutamayī vā prajñā cintāmayī vā bhāvanāmayī vā, yayā prajñayā sarvaṃ kāyaṃ sarvākāraṃ samyag evopaparīkṣate saṃtīrayaty anupraviśaty anubudhyate //
body.translated_text: -II-12-b-(1)-i-(b) — Therein, the contemplation is threefold: whatever wisdom — born of hearing, or born of reflection, or born of cultivation — which, taking the body as the basis, with all aspects, rightly examines, explores, penetrates, and comprehends the entire body.

body.text:
-II-12-b-(1)-i-(c) Ms.85a6M, Sh.292-15, P.132b1, D.107b2, N.113b1, Co.112a1, Ch.440a23
tatra smṛtir yad asya kāyam adhipatiṃ kṛtvā ye dharmā udgṛhītās teṣām eva ca dharmāṇāṃ yo 'rthaś cintito ye ca bhāvanayā sākṣātkṛtāḥ, tatra vyañjane cārthe ca sākṣātkriyāyāṃ ca taccetaso 'saṃmoṣaḥ, "sūdgṛhītā vā ma ete dharmāḥ", "na ve"ti, "sūpalakṣitā vā tatra tatra prajñayā", "na ve"ti, "susaṃsparśitāḥ tatra tatra vimuktyā", "na ve"ti smṛtir upasthitā bhavati / (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 180
This is the establishment of mindfulness.

body.translated_text: -II-12-b-(1)-i-(c) — Therein, <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) is: with the body as the basis, whatever <s>dharmas</s> have been grasped [through learning], whatever meaning of those <s>dharmas</s> has been reflected upon, and whatever has been directly experienced through cultivation — regarding the letter, the meaning, and the direct experience — the non-forgetfulness of that mind: "Have these <s>dharmas</s> been well-grasped by me," "or not?" "Have they been well-discerned here and there by wisdom," "or not?" "Have they been well-touched here and there by liberation," "or not?" — mindfulness is established.

body.text:
-II-12-b-(1)-i-(d) Ms.85a7M, Sh.293-6, P. 132b5, D. 107b5, N. 113b4, Co. 112a3, Ch.440a29
api ca smṛtyārakṣāyai smṛter upasthānaṃ viṣayāsaṃkleśāyālambanopanibandhāya ca /
body.translated_text: -II-12-b-(1)-i-(d) — Moreover, the establishment of mindfulness is for the guarding of mindfulness, for non-defilement regarding objects, and for the binding of the mind to the object.

body.text: tatra smṛtyārakṣā yathoktaṃ pūrvam ev"ārakṣitasmṛtir bhavati nipakasmṛtir" iti /
body.translated_text: Therein, guarding by mindfulness — as previously stated: "One has guarded mindfulness, one has careful mindfulness."

body.text: tatra viṣayāsaṃkleśāya / yathoktaṃ "smṛtyārakṣitamānasaḥ samāvasthācārako" "na nimittagrāhī nānuvyañjanagrāhī" yāvad vistareṇa "rakṣati mana-indriyaṃ mana-indriyeṇa saṃvaram āpadyate" /
body.translated_text: Therein, for non-defilement regarding objects — as stated: "With a mind guarded by mindfulness, conducting oneself properly, not grasping at signs, not grasping at secondary features" — and so on in detail up to "one guards the mind-faculty, one undertakes the restraint of the mind-faculty."

body.text: tatrālambanopanibandhāya / yathoktaṃ caturvidha ālambane smṛtim upanibadhnataḥ / tadyathā vyāpiny ālambane caritaviśodhane kauśalyālambane kleśaviśodhane vā /
body.translated_text: Therein, for the binding of the mind to the object — as stated: One binds mindfulness to four types of objects, namely: the all-pervading object, the object for purifying conduct, the object of skill, and the object for purifying the afflictions.

body.text: ebhis tribhir ākārair yā sūpasthitasmṛtitā, idam ucyate smṛter upasthānam //
body.translated_text: By these three aspects, the well-established state of mindfulness — this is called the establishment of mindfulness.

body.text:
-II-12-b-(1)-ii Ms.85b1R, Sh.293-18, P.133a3, D.108a1, N.114a1, Co.112b7, Ch.440b8
tatra vedanā katamā / tadyathā sukhā duḥkhā aduḥkhāsukhā ca vedanā / tatra sukhāpi kāyikī duḥkhāpy aduḥkhāsukhāpi / yathā kāyikī, evaṃ caitasikī / sukhāpi sāmiṣā duḥkhāpy aduḥkhāsukhāpi / evaṃ nirāmiṣāpi, evaṃ gardhāśritā, naiṣkramyāśritā vedanā sukhāpi duḥkhāpy aduḥkhāsukhāpi /
body.translated_text: -II-12-b-(1)-ii — Therein, what is feeling? Such as: pleasant, painful, and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. Therein, pleasant [feeling] is also bodily; painful is also; neither-painful-nor-pleasant is also. As bodily, so too mental. Pleasant [feeling] is also with-material; painful is also; neither-painful-nor-pleasant is also. So too without-material. So too based on desire; based on renunciation — pleasant feeling is also, painful is also, neither-painful-nor-pleasant is also.

body.text: saiṣā ekaviṃśatividhā vedanā bhavati, navavidhā vā //
body.translated_text: This feeling is of twenty-one kinds, or of nine kinds.

body.text:
-II-12-b-(1)-iii Ms.85b2R, Sh.294-7, W.97-39, P.133a7, D.108a4, IM.114a4, Co.113a2, Ch. 440b13
tatra cittaṃ katamat / tadyathā sarāgaṃ cittaṃ vigatarāgaṃ sadveṣaṃ vigatadveṣaṃ samohaṃ vigatamohaṃ saṃkṣiptaṃ vikṣiptaṃ līnaṃ pragṛhītam uddhatam anuddhataṃ vyupaśāntam avyupaśāntaṃ samāhitam asamāhitaṃ subhāvitam asubhāvitaṃ suvimuktaṃ cittam asuvimuktaṃ cittam / tad etad abhisamasya viṃśatividhaṃ cittaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: -II-12-b-(1)-iii — Therein, what is the mind? Such as: a mind with attachment, a mind free from attachment; with hatred, free from hatred; with delusion, free from delusion; contracted, distracted; lax, exerted; agitated, unagitated; calmed, uncalmed; concentrated, unconcentrated; well-cultivated, not well-cultivated; well-liberated mind, not well-liberated mind. This mind, combining them, is of twenty kinds.

body.text:
-II-12-b-(1)-iv Ms.85b3R, Sh.294-13, P.133b2, D.108a6, N.114a7, Co.112b5, Ch.440b18
tatra dharmāḥ katame / rāgo rāgavinayaś ca, dveṣo dveṣavinayaś ca, moho mohavinayaś ca, saṃkṣepo vikṣepo layaḥ pragraha auddhatyam anauddhatyaṃ vyupaśamo 'vyupaśamaḥ, susamāhitatā na susamāhitatā subhāvitamārgatā na subhāvitamārgatā suvimuktatā na suvimuktatā ca / itīme kṛṣṇaśuklapakṣavyavasthitā viṃśatidharmā veditavyāḥ saṃkleśavyavadānapakṣyāḥ //
body.translated_text: -II-12-b-(1)-iv — Therein, what are the <s>dharmas</s>? Passion and the discipline of passion; hatred and the discipline of hatred; delusion and the discipline of delusion; contraction, distraction, laxity, exertion, agitation, non-agitation, calm, non-calm, well-concentrated, not well-concentrated, well-cultivated path, not well-cultivated path, well-liberated, and not well-liberated. These twenty <s>dharmas</s>, established in the dark and bright sides, should be understood as belonging to the side of defilement and the side of purification.

body.text:
-II-12-b-(1)-ii' Ms.85b5L, Sh.295-8, P.133b6, D.108b2, N.114b3, Co.112b7, Ch.440b23
tatra sukhā vedanā yat sukhavedanīyam sparśaṃ pratītyotpadyate sātaṃ veditaṃ vedanāgatam / sā punar yā pañcavijñānasaṃprayuktā sā kāyikī, yā punar manovijñānasaṃprayuktā sā caitasikī /
body.translated_text: -II-12-b-(1)-ii' — Therein, pleasant feeling is that agreeable sensation belonging to the domain of feeling, which arises dependent on a contact that is to be felt as pleasant. That which is associated with the five sense-consciousnesses is bodily; that which is associated with mind-consciousness is mental.

body.text: yathā sukhavedanīyam evaṃ duḥkhavedanīyam aduḥkhāsukhavedanīyam sparśaṃ pratītyotpadyate 'sātaṃ naiva sātaṃ nāsātaṃ veditaṃ vedanāgatam / idam ucyate duḥkhā aduḥkhāsukhā vedanā / sā punar yā pañcavijñānakāyasaṃprayuktā sā kāyikī, yā manovijñānasaṃprayuktā sā caitasikī /
body.translated_text: As with contact to be felt as pleasant, so too dependent on contact to be felt as painful or to be felt as neither-painful-nor-pleasant, there arises a disagreeable or neutral sensation belonging to the domain of feeling. This is called painful and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. That which is associated with the five sense-consciousness bodies is bodily; that which is associated with mind-consciousness is mental.

body.text: yā nirvāṇānukūlā nairvedhikī atyantaniṣṭhatāyā atyantavimalatāyā atyantabrahmacaryaparyavasānāyai saṃvartate sā nirāmiṣā / yā punar dhātupatitā bhavapatitā sā sāmiṣā / yā punā rūpārūpyapratisaṃyuktā vairāgyānukūlā vā sā naiṣkramyāśritā / yā punaḥ kāmapratisaṃyuktā na ca vairāgyānukūlā sā gardhāśritā //
body.translated_text: That which is conducive to <s>nirvāṇa</s>, penetrative, leading to ultimate finality, ultimate purity, and the culmination of the absolute holy life — that is without-material. That which has fallen into the realms, fallen into existence — that is with-material. That which is connected with the form and formless [realms] or is conducive to dispassion — that is based on renunciation. That which is connected with sensual pleasures and is not conducive to dispassion — that is based on desire.

body.text:
-II-12-b-(1)-iii' Ms.85b7R, Sh.296-13, P.134a6, D.109a1, N.115a1, Co.113a6, Ch.440c5
tatra sarāgaṃ cittaṃ yad rañjanīye vastuni rāgaparyavasthitam / vigatarāgaṃ yad rāgaparyavasthānāpagatam / sadveṣaṃ yad dveṣaṇīye vastuni dveṣaparyavasthitam / vigatadveṣaṃ yad dveṣaparyavasthānāpagatam / tatra saṃmohaṃ yan mohanīye vastuni mohaparyauasthitam / vigatamohaṃ yad mohaparyavasthānāpagatam /
body.translated_text: Therein, a mind with passion (<s>sarāga citta</s>) is one that is overcome by the state of passion regarding a passion-inducing object. A mind free from passion (<s>vigatarāga</s>) is one freed from the state of passion. A mind with aversion (<s>sadveṣa</s>) is one that is overcome by the state of aversion regarding an aversion-inducing object. A mind free from aversion (<s>vigatadveṣa</s>) is one freed from the state of aversion. Therein, a mind with delusion (<s>saṃmoha</s>) is one that is overcome by the state of delusion regarding a delusion-inducing object. A mind free from delusion (<s>vigatamoha</s>) is one freed from the state of delusion.

body.text:
tāny etāni ṣaṭ cittāni cārasahagatāni veditavyāni / tatra trīṇi saṃkleśapakṣyāṇi trīṇi saṃkleśaprātipakṣikāṇi /
tatra saṃkṣiptacittaṃ yac chamathākāreṇādhyātmālambanopanibaddham / vikṣiptaṃ yad bahirdhā pañcasu kāmaguṇeṣv anuvisṛtam /
body.translated_text:
These six mind-states should be understood as accompanied by [mental] movement. Therein, three belong to the side of defilement and three are counteragents to defilement.
Therein, a contracted mind (<s>saṃkṣipta citta</s>) is one that is internally bound to an object in the mode of calm (<s>śamatha</s>). A distracted mind (<s>vikṣipta</s>) is one that has gone outward into the five strands of sensual pleasure.

body.text: tatra līnaṃ cittaṃ yat styānamiddhasahagatam / pragṛhītaṃ yat prasadanīyenālambanena saṃpraharṣitam / uddhataṃ cittaṃ yad atisaṃpragrahād auddhatyaparyavasthitam / anuddhataṃ cittaṃ yat pragrahakāle cābhisaṃkṣepakāle copekṣāprāptam /
body.translated_text: Therein, a sunken mind (<s>līna citta</s>) is one accompanied by sloth-and-torpor. An uplifted mind (<s>pragṛhīta</s>) is one stimulated by a gladdening object. An agitated mind (<s>uddhata citta</s>) is one that, through excessive exertion, is overcome by restlessness. A non-agitated mind (<s>anuddhata citta</s>) is one that, at the time of exertion and the time of restraint, has attained equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>).

body.text: tatra vyupaśāntaṃ cittaṃ yan nivaraṇebhyo vimuktam / avyupaśāntaṃ punar yad avimuktam /
body.translated_text: Therein, a pacified mind (<s>vyupaśānta citta</s>) is one freed from the hindrances. An unpacified mind (<s>avyupaśānta</s>) is one not freed.

body.text: tatra samāhitaṃ cittaṃ yan nivaraṇavimokṣān mauladhyānapraviṣṭam / asamāhitaṃ yad apraviṣṭam /
body.translated_text: Therein, a concentrated mind (<s>samāhita citta</s>) is one that, through liberation from the hindrances, has entered a fundamental <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation absorption). An unconcentrated mind (<s>asamāhita</s>) is one that has not entered.

body.text: tatra subhāvitaṃ cittaṃ yat tasyaiva samādher dīrghakālaparicayān nikāmalābhī bhavaty akṛcchralābhy āśusaṃpattā / tatra na subhāvitam cittam etadviparyayeṇa veditavyam /
body.translated_text: Therein, a well-cultivated mind (<s>subhāvita citta</s>) is one that, through long familiarity with that very <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), easily obtains it, obtains it without difficulty, and attains it swiftly. Therein, a mind not well-cultivated should be understood as the reverse of this.

body.text: tatra suvimuktaṃ cittaṃ yat sarvataś cātyantataś ca vimuktam / na suvimuktaṃ cittaṃ yan na sarvato nāpy atyantato vimuktam /
body.translated_text: Therein, a well-liberated mind (<s>suvimukta citta</s>) is one that is liberated from everything and definitively. A mind not well-liberated is one that is not liberated from everything nor definitively.

body.text: itīmāni caturdaśa cittāni vihāragatāni veditavyāni / tatra nivaraṇaviśuddhibhūmim ārabhya vihāragatāny aṣṭau cittāni / saṃkṣiptaṃ vitkṣiptaṃ yāvad vyupaśāntam avyupaśāntam iti / kleśaviśuddhiṃ punar ārabhya vihāragatāni ṣaṭ cittāni / yāvat suvimuktaṃ cittaṃ na suvimuktam iti /
body.translated_text: These fourteen mind-states should be understood as pertaining to [meditative] dwelling. Therein, beginning from the level of purification from hindrances, there are eight mind-states pertaining to dwelling — contracted, distracted, up to pacified and unpacified. But beginning from the purification of afflictions, there are six mind-states pertaining to dwelling — up to well-liberated and not well-liberated.

body.text: yat punaḥ saty adhyātmaṃ nivaraṇe "asti me nivaraṇam" iti jānāti, asati nivaraṇe "nāsti me nivaraṇam" iti janāti / yathā cānutpannasya nivaraṇasyotpādo bhavati tad api prajānāti, yathā cotpannasya vigamo bhavati tad api prajānāti /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, when there is internally a hindrance, one knows: 'There is a hindrance in me.' When there is no hindrance, one knows: 'There is no hindrance in me.'

body.text: tatra sati cakṣuḥsaṃyojane yāvan manaḥsaṃyojane "asti me yāvan manaḥsamyojanam" iti, asati yāvan manaḥsaṃyojane "nāsti me yāvan manaḥsaṃyojanam" iti prajānāti / yathā cānutpannasya yāvan manaḥsaṃyojanasyotpādo bhavati tad api prajānāti, yathā cotpannasya nirodho bhavati tad api prajānāti /
body.translated_text: Therein, when there is a fetter of the eye and so on up to a fetter of the mind, [one knows:] 'There is a fetter of the mind in me.' When there is no fetter up to the fetter of the mind, [one knows:] 'There is no fetter of the mind in me.'

body.text: saty adhyātmam smṛtisaṃbodhyaṅge "asti me smṛtisaṃbodhyaṅgam" iti prajānāti, asati "nāsti me" prajānāti / yathā cānutpannasya smṛtisaṃbodhyaṅgasyotpādo bhavati tad api prajānāti, yathā cotpannasya sthitir bhavaty asaṃmoṣo bhāvanāparipūribhūyobhāvavṛddhivipulatā tad api prajānāti /
body.translated_text: When there is internally the awakening factor of mindfulness (<s>smṛtisaṃbodhyaṅga</s>), one understands: 'There is the awakening factor of mindfulness in me.' When it is absent, one understands: 'There is no [awakening factor of mindfulness] in me.'

body.text: yathā smṛtisaṃbodhyaṅgam evaṃ dharmapravicayavīryaprītipraśrabdhisamādhyupekṣāsaṃbodhyaṅgaṃ veditavyam iti //
body.translated_text: Just as the awakening factor of mindfulness, so the awakening factors of investigation of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmapravicaya</s>), vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), rapture (<s>prīti</s>), tranquility (<s>praśrabdhi</s>), concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), and equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>) should be understood in the same way.

body.text:
-II-12-b-(1)-iv' Ms.86a7M, Sh.299-13, P.135b4, D.110a2, N.116a4, Co.114a7, Ch.441a13
yad evaṃ svabhāvanidānādīnavapratipakṣākāraiḥ saṃkliṣṭadharmaparijñānam idaṃ śarīraṃ dharmasmṛtyupasthānasya //
body.translated_text: When one thus knows the nature of these [mental states], with the arising of attention directed toward their arising and ceasing, one dwells observing <s>dharmas</s> in <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmeṣu dharmānudarśī</s>).

body.text:
-II-12-b-(1)-v Ms.86a7R, Sh.299-15, P.135b5, D.110a3, N.116a5, Co.114a7, Ch.441a14
yathā kāye kāyānupaśyanā smṛtyupasthānam uktam evaṃ vedanāyāṃ citte dharmeṣu yathāyogaṃ veditavyam /
body.translated_text: Just as one dwells observing the body in the body (<s>kāye kāyānudarśī</s>), so also regarding feelings, mind, and <s>dharmas</s> — there are three modes of observing.

body.text: tatra katham adhyātmaṃ kāye kāyānudarśī viharati, kathaṃ bahirdhā, katham adhyātmabahirdhā /
body.translated_text: Therein, how does one dwell observing the body in the body internally (<s>adhyātma</s>), how externally (<s>bahirdhā</s>), and how both internally and externally (<s>adhyātmabahirdhā</s>)?

body.text: yadā adhyātmaṃ pratyātmaṃ sattvasaṃkhyāte kāye kāyānupaśyī viharati, evam adhyātmaṃ kāye kāyānudarśī viharati /
body.translated_text: When one dwells observing the body in the body internally — with respect to one's own personal body reckoned as a being — thus one dwells observing the body in the body internally.

body.text: yadā bahirdhā asattvasaṃkhyātaṃ rūpam ālambanīkaroti, evaṃ bahirdhā kāye kāyānudarśī viharati /
body.translated_text: When one takes as object the external form not reckoned as a being, thus one dwells observing the body in the body externally.

body.text: yadā bahirdhā parakyaṃ sattvasaṃkhyātaṃ rūpam ālambanīkaroti, evam adhyātmabahirdhā kāye kāyānudarśī viharati /
body.translated_text: When one takes as object the form belonging to another, external, reckoned as a being, thus one dwells observing the body in the body both internally and externally.

body.text:
tatrādhyātmaṃ rūpam upādāya svakyaṃ sattvasaṃkhyātaṃ yā utpannā vedanā cittaṃ dharmās tān ālambanīkurvann adhyātmaṃ vedanāsu citte dharmeṣu dharmānudarśī viharati /
bāhyam asattvasaṃkhyātaṃ rūpam upādāya yā utpannā vedanā cittaṃ dharmās tān ālambanīkurvan bahirdhā vedanāyāṃ citte dharmeṣu dharmānudarśī viharati /
body.translated_text: Therein, taking internal form — one's own, reckoned as a being — whatever feelings, mind, and <s>dharmas</s> have arisen in dependence on that, taking those as object, one dwells observing feelings in feelings, mind in mind, and <s>dharmas</s> in <s>dharmas</s> internally.

body.text: bahirdhā bāhyaṃ rūpaṃ sattvasaṃkhyātam upādāya yā utpannā vedanā cittaṃ dharmās tān ālambanīkurvann adhyātmabahirdhā vedanāyāṃ citte dharmeṣu dharmānudarśī viharati //
body.translated_text: Taking external form, reckoned as a being, whatever feelings, mind, and <s>dharmas</s> have arisen in dependence on that, taking those as object, one dwells observing [them] externally.

body.text:
-II-12-b-(1)-v-(a) Ms.86b2R, Sh.300-15, P.136a5, D.110b2, N.116b4, Co.114b6, Ch.441a29
aparaḥ paryāyaḥ / indriyasaṃgṛhītaṃ rūpam ālambanīkurvann adhyātmaṃ kāye kāyānupaśyī viharati / anindriyasaṃgṛhītaṃ rūpam anupagatam anupādattam ālambanīkurvan bahirdhā kāye kāyānudarśī viharati / anindriyasaṃgṛhītam eva rūpam adhyātmam upagatam upādattaṃ rūpam ālambanīkurvann adhyātmabahirdhā kāye kāyānupaśyī viharati / evaṃ pūrvaṃ trividhaṃ rūpam upādāya yā utpannā vedanā cittaṃ dharmās tān yathāyogam ālambanīkurvaṃs tathādarśī viharatīti veditavyam //
body.translated_text: Another method: taking internal form as the basis, and external form not reckoned as a being as the object — thus one dwells observing the body in the body both internally and externally.

body.text:
-II-12-b-0)-v-(b) Ms.86b4L, Sh.301-6, P.136b1, D.110b4, N.116b6, Co.115a1, Ch.441b6
aparaḥ paryāyaḥ / yat samāhitabhūmikaṃ praśrabdhisahagataṃ rūpam ālambanīkaroty evam adhyātmaṃ kāye kāyānudarśī viharati / yat svakyam evādhyātmam asamāhitabhūmikaṃ dauṣṭhulyasahagataṃ rūpam ālambanīkaroty evaṃ bahirdhā kāye kāyānupaśyī viharati / parakyaṃ dauṣṭhulyasahagataṃ praśrabdhisahagataṃ ca rūpam ālambanīkurvann adhyātmabahirdhā (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 192

children.text: ) kāye kāyānudarśī viharaty evaṃ tad upādāyotpannā vedanā cittaṃ dharmā yathāyogaṃ veditavyāḥ //
children.translated_text: ) one dwells observing the body in the body. The feelings, mind, and <s>dharmas</s> arisen in dependence on that should be understood accordingly. //

body.translated_text: Another method: taking the body's own form and external form together as the object,

body.text:
-II-12-b-(1)-v-(c) Ms.86b5M, Sh.301-14, P.136b5, D.110b7, N.117a2, Co.115a4, Ch.441b13
aparaḥ paryāyaḥ / adhyātmaṃ bhūtarūpam ālambanīkurvann adhyātmaṃ kāye kāyānudarśī viharati / bāhyaṃ bhūtarūpam ālambanīkurvan bahirdhā kāye kāyānudarśī viharati / tac ca bhūtarūpam upādāya yad utpannam indriyaviṣayasaṃgṛhītam upādāyarūpaṃ cālambanīkurvann adhyātmabahirdhā kāye kāyānudarśī viharati / evaṃ tad upādāya yā utpannā vedanā cittaṃ dharmās te 'pi yathāyogaṃ veditavyāḥ //
body.translated_text: Another method: taking the inner body of the hair of the head, body hair, nails, teeth and so forth as the object — as to their characteristics of the unpleasant, as to their aspects of impurity — one dwells observing the body in the body internally.

body.text:
-II-12-b-(1)-v-(d) Ms.86b6R, Sh.301-21, P.136b8, D.111a2, N.117a5, Co.115a6, Ch.441b19
aparaḥ paryāyaḥ / yadā savijñānakaṃ kāyam adhyātmam ālambanīkaroty evam adhyātmaṃ kāye kāyānudarśī viharati / avijñānakaṃ rūpaṃ sattvasaṃkhyātaṃ vinīlakādiṣv avasthāsv ālambanīkurvan bahirdhā kāye kāyānudarśī viharati / avijñānakasya ca rūpasyātīte kāle savijñānatāṃ savijñānakasya ca rūpasyānāgate kāle 'vijñānatāṃ tulyadharmatāṃ samadharmatām ālambanīkurvann adhyātmabahirdhā kāye kāyānudarśī viharati /
body.translated_text: Another method: taking the outer body in its changed and unchanged states, with the aspects of the blue-black [corpse] and so forth, as the object,

body.text: evaṃ tad upādāya yā utpannā vedanā cittaṃ dharmās te 'pi yathāyogaṃ veditavyāḥ //
body.translated_text: the feelings, mind, and <s>dharmas</s> arisen in dependence on that should also be understood accordingly. //

body.text: aparaḥ paryāyaḥ / ātmano 'ntaḥkāyaṃ keśaromanakhādibhir ākārair ālambanīkurvann adhyātmaṃ kāye kāyānudarśī viharati / pareṣām antaḥkāyaṃ keśaromanakhādibhir ākārair ālambanīkurvan bahirdhā kāye kāyānudarśī viharati / ātmanaś ca bahiḥkāyam avipariṇataṃ vinīlakādibhir ākāraiḥ (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 194

children.text: ) pareṣāṃ ca bahiḥkāyaṃ vipariṇatam avipariṇataṃ ca vinīlakādibhir ākārais tulyadharmatayālambanīkurvann adhyātmabahirdhā kāye kāyānudarśī viharati /
children.translated_text: ) And taking the outer body of others, in its changed and unchanged states, with the aspects of the blue-black [corpse] and so forth, as the object — by the equality of nature — one dwells observing [the body] both internally and externally.

body.translated_text: Another method: taking one's own inner body as the object, with aspects such as hair of the head, body hair, nails and so forth, one dwells observing the body in the body internally.

body.text: tad upādāya yā utpannā vedanā cittaṃ dharmās te 'pi yathāyogaṃ veditavyāḥ /
body.translated_text: The feelings, mind, and <s>dharmas</s> arisen in dependence on that should also be understood accordingly.

body.text: ity evaṃbhāgīyāḥ kāyavedanācittadharmaprabhedena bahavaḥ paryāyā veditavyāḥ / ime tu katipayāḥ paryāyāḥ saṃprakāśitāḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, many methods of this kind should be understood, differentiated into body, feelings, mind, and <s>dharmas</s>. But these are only a few methods explained as a portion.

body.text:
Ms.87a2L, Sh.303-4, W.*98-5, P.137b2, D.111b2, N.117b5, Co.115b5, Ch.441c6
tatra caturṇāṃ viparyāsānāṃ pratipakṣeṇa bhagavatā catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni vyavasthāpitāni /
body.translated_text: Therein, the four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) are established as counteragents to the four inversions (<s>viparyāsa</s>).

body.text: tatrāśucau śucīti viparyāsapratipakṣeṇa kāyasmṛtyupasthānaṃ vyavasthāpitam / tathā hi bhagavatā kāyasmṛtyupasthānabhāvanāyām aśubhāpratisamyuktāś catasraḥ śivapathikā deśitāḥ, yā asya bahulaṃkurvanmanasikurvataḥ, aśucau śucīti viparyāsaḥ prahīyate /
body.translated_text: Therein, the foundation of mindfulness of the body (<s>kāyasmṛtyupasthāna</s>) is established as the counteragent to the inversion of [perceiving] the pure in the impure (<s>aśucau śuci</s>). For the <s>Bhagavān</s> has taught the contemplation of the body primarily by means of the unpleasant aspects — through internal aspects such as hair and so forth, and external aspects such as the blue-black [corpse] and so forth.

body.text: tatra duḥkhe sukham iti viparyāsapratipakṣeṇa vedanāsmṛtyupasthānaṃ vyavasthāpitam / vedanāsu vedanānudarśī viharan "yat kiṃcid veditam idam atra duḥkhasye"ti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti, evam asya yo duḥkhe sukham iti viparyāsaḥ sa prahāyate /
body.translated_text: Therein, the foundation of mindfulness of feelings (<s>vedanāsmṛtyupasthāna</s>) is established as the counteragent to the inversion of [perceiving] happiness in suffering (<s>duḥkhe sukham</s>). By observing feelings in feelings, one recognizes the three types of feelings and the suffering of conditioned existence (<s>saṃskāraduḥkhatā</s>) that pervades [all of them].

body.text: tatra anitye nityam iti viparyāsapratipakṣeṇa cittasmṛtyupasthānaṃ vyavasthāpitam / tasya sarāgādicittaprabhedena teṣāṃ teṣāṃ rātriṃdivasānām atyayāt kṣaṇalavamuhūrtānām anekavidhānāṃ bahunānāprakāratāṃ (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 196

children.text: ) cittasyopalabhya yo 'nitye nityam iti viparyāsaḥ sa prahīyate /
children.translated_text: ) and apprehending the impermanent nature of the mind, the inversion of [perceiving] permanence in the impermanent is abandoned.

body.translated_text: Therein, the foundation of mindfulness of the mind (<s>cittasmṛtyupasthāna</s>) is established as the counteragent to the inversion of [perceiving] permanence in the impermanent (<s>anitye nityam</s>). By observing that mind with its mind-states such as with-passion and so forth,

body.text: tatrānātmany ātmeti viparyāsapratipakṣeṇa dharmasmṛtyupasthānaṃ vyavasthāpitam / tasya yeṣām ātmadṛṣṭyādikānāṃ saṃkleśānāṃ sadbhāvād yeṣām anātmadṛṣṭyādikānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām asadbhāvāt skandheṣv ātmadarśanaṃ bhavati, nānyasya, svalakṣaṇataḥ sāmānyalakṣaṇataś ca dharmān dharmānudarśino yathābhūtaṃ paśyataḥ, yo 'nātmany ātmeti viparyāsaḥ sa prahīyate //
body.translated_text: Therein, the foundation of mindfulness of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmasmṛtyupasthāna</s>) is established as the counteragent to the inversion of [perceiving] self in the not-self (<s>anātmany ātma</s>). By observing those [dharmas] in which the view of self arises,

body.text:
-II-12-b-(1)-v-(f) Ms.87a6L, Sh.305-1, P.138a4, D.112a1, N.118a6, Co.116a5, Ch.441c22
aparaḥ paryāyaḥ / prāyeṇa hi loka evaṃ pravṛttaḥ / skandheṣu skandhamātraṃ dharmamātraṃ yathābhūtam aprajānan yathā "kāya āśritaḥ, yadāśritaś ca sukhaduḥkham upabhuñje", dharmādharmābhyām saṃkliśyate vyavadāyate ca / tatrātmana āśrayavastusaṃmohāpanayanārthaṃ kāyasmṛtyupasthānaṃ vyavasthāpitam / tasyaivātmano 'nubhavanavastusaṃmohāpanayanārthaṃ vedanāsmṛtyupasthānaṃ vyavasthāpitam / yatraiva ca te citte manasi vijñāna ātmagrāheṇa saṃmūḍhā ātmavastusaṃmohāpanayanārthena cittasmṛtyupasthānaṃ vyavasthāpitam / tasyaiva ca cittasaṃkleśavyavadānavastusaṃmohāpanayanārthaṃ dharmasmṛtyupasthānaṃ vyavasthāpitam //
body.translated_text: Another method: Generally the world is constituted thus.
