Not knowing the aggregates as merely aggregates, merely <s>dharmas</s>, as they really are — [thinking:] 'there is a body on which [something] depends, and depending on it one experiences happiness and suffering' — one is defiled and purified through <s>dharma</s> (wholesome action) and <s>adharma</s> (unwholesome action). Therein, for the purpose of removing the confusion about the basis-object of the self, the foundation of mindfulness of the body (<s>kāyasmṛtyupasthāna</s>) is established. For the purpose of removing the confusion about the object of experience of that very self, the foundation of mindfulness of feelings (<s>vedanāsmṛtyupasthāna</s>) is established. And that very mind, thought, consciousness in which they are confused by grasping at a self — for the purpose of removing the confusion about the object of the self, the foundation of mindfulness of the mind (<s>cittasmṛtyupasthāna</s>) is established. And for the purpose of removing the confusion about the objects of defilement and purification of that very mind, the foundation of mindfulness of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmasmṛtyupasthāna</s>) is established.

body.text:
-II-12-b-(1)-v-(g) Ms.87a7R, Sh.305-10, W.98-22, P.138b2, D.112a5, N.118b3, Co.116b2, Ch.441c29
aparaḥ paryāyaḥ / yatra ca karma karoti, yadarthaṃ ca karoti, yaś ca karma karoti, yena ca karoti, tat sarvam ekadhyam abhisaṃkṣipya catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni vyavasthāpitāni, tatra kāye karoti vedanārthaṃ cittaṃ kuśalākuśalair dharmaiḥ //
body.translated_text: Another method: Where one performs action, for what purpose one performs action, who performs action, and by what one performs action — all of these taken together, the four foundations of mindfulness are established. Therein, one acts in the body, for the purpose of feeling, [by] the mind, through wholesome and unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text:
-II-12-b-(1)-v-(h) Ms.87b1R, Sh.306-4, P.138b4, D.112a7, N.118b4, Co.116b4, Ch.442a5
aparaḥ paryāyaḥ / yatra ca saṃkliśyate viśudhyate yataś ca yaś ca yena kliśyate viśudhyate, tad ekadhyam abhisaṃkṣipya catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni vyavasthāpitāni, tatra kāye saṃkliśyate viśudhyate ca vedanābhyaś cittaṃ dharmaiḥ saṃkliśyate viśudhyate ca //
body.translated_text: Another method: Where one is defiled and purified, from what, who, and by what one is defiled and purified — all of these taken together, the four foundations of mindfulness are established. Therein, in the body one is defiled and purified; from feelings, [by] the mind, through <s>dharmas</s>, one is defiled and purified.

body.text:
-II-12-b-(1)-vi Ms.87b2M, Sḥ 306-10, P.138b7, D.112b2, N.118b7, Co.116b6, Ch.442a10
tatra smṛtyupasthānam iti ko 'rthaḥ / āha / yatra ca smṛtim upasthāpayati yena ca smṛtim upasthāpayati tad ucyate smṛtyupasthānam / yatra smṛtim upasthāpayati tad ālambanasmṛtyupasthānam / yena smṛtim upasthāpayati tatra yā prajñā smṛtiś ca samādhisaṃgrāhikā tat svabhāvasmṛtyupasthānam / tadanye tatsaṃprayuktāś cittacaitasikā dharmāḥ saṃsargasmṛtyupasthānam /
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the meaning of 'foundation of mindfulness' (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>)? He says: that in which one establishes mindfulness and that by which one establishes mindfulness — that is called the foundation of mindfulness. That in which one establishes mindfulness — that is the object-foundation of mindfulness. That by which one establishes mindfulness — therein, the wisdom and the mindfulness that comprise concentration — that is the intrinsic-nature-foundation of mindfulness. Other mental and mental-concomitant <s>dharmas</s> associated with those — that is the associated-foundation of mindfulness.

body.text: api ca kāyavedanācittadharmādhipateyo yo mārgaḥ samutpannaḥ kuśalaḥ sāsravo 'nāsravaś ca tat smṛtyupasthānam / sa punaḥ śrutamayaś cintāmayo bhāvanāmayaś ca / tatra śrutacintāmayaḥ sāsrava eva, bhāvanāmayaḥ syāt sāsravaḥ syād anāsravaḥ //
body.translated_text: Moreover, the path that has arisen governed by body, feelings, mind, and <s>dharmas</s>, which is wholesome, defiled (<s>sāsrava</s>) or undefiled (<s>anāsrava</s>) — that is the foundation of mindfulness. And that is born of hearing, born of reflection, and born of cultivation. Therein, what is born of hearing and reflection is defiled alone; what is born of cultivation may be defiled or may be undefiled.

body.text:
-II-12-b-(2) Ms.87b4M, Sh.307-5, P.139a5, D.112b6, N.119a4, Co.117a3, Ch.442a26
sa evaṃ caturṣu smṛtyupasthāneṣu kṛtaparicaya audārikaudārikaṃ viparyāsam apanīya kuśalākuśaladharmābhijñaḥ / tadanantaram "anutpannānāiḥ pāpakānām akuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām anutpādāya, utpannānāṃ prahāṇāya, anutpannānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām utpādāya, utpannānām sthitaya" iti vistareṇa pūrvavad yāvac cittaṃ pragṛhṇāti pradadhāti //
body.translated_text: One thus familiarized with the four foundations of mindfulness, having removed the coarser and coarser perversions, knowing wholesome and unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> — immediately thereafter, 'for the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, for the abandonment of arisen ones, for the arising of unarisen wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, for the stability of arisen ones' — and so on in detail as before, up to: one takes hold of and applies the mind.

body.text:
-II-12-b-(2)-i-(a) Ms.87b5M, Sh.307-12, P.139a8, D.113a2, N.119a6, Co.117a5, Ch442b2
tatra katame pāpakā akuśalā dharmāḥ / yat kāmāvacaraṃ kliṣṭaṃ kāyakarma vākkarma manaskarma kāyavāṅmanoduścaritasaṃgṛhītam, ye ca tatsamutthāpakāḥ kleśās te punar ye 'samavahitā asaṃmukhībhūtās te 'nutpannāḥ, ye samavahitāḥ saṃmukhībhūtās ta utpannāḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, what are the evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>? The defiled bodily action, verbal action, and mental action belonging to the desire realm, included in bodily, verbal, and mental misconduct, and the defilements that produce them. Among those, the ones that are not assembled and not brought to the fore — those are unarisen. The ones that are assembled and brought to the fore — those are arisen.

body.text: tatra kuśalā dharmā ye tatprātipakṣikā dharmā duścaritaprātipakṣikā nivaraṇaprātipakṣikāḥ saṃyojanaprātipakṣikā vā / te 'py anutpannās tathaiva veditavyā utpannāś ca yathā pāpakā akuśalā dharmāḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, the wholesome <s>dharmas</s> are those that are their antidotes — antidotes to misconduct, antidotes to hindrances, and antidotes to fetters. Those too, the unarisen, should be understood in the same way, and the arisen, in the same way as the evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text:
-II-12-b-(2)-i-(b)-(1) Ms.87b6R, Sh.308-5, P.139b4, D.113a5, N.119b3, Co.117b1, Ch.442b8
tatra yadānutpannānāṃ pāpakānām akuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām anutpādāya spṛhām utpādayati praṇidhatte "sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā notpādayiṣyāmī"ti, evaṃ chandaṃ janayati / utpannān vā punaḥ samavahitān "sarveṇa sarvaṃ nādhivāsayiṣyāmi prahāsyāmi prativinodayiṣyāmi" /
body.translated_text: Therein, when for the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> one generates the desire, one resolves: 'in every way, in every manner, I shall not produce [them]' — thus one generates the aspiration. Or, regarding arisen ones that are assembled: 'in every way, in every manner, I shall not tolerate [them], I shall abandon [them], I shall dispel [them].'

body.text: yad anutpanneṣu pāpakeṣv akuśaleṣu dharmeṣu pūrvam evānutpādāya spṛhām utpādayati praṇidhatte nādhivāsayitukāmo bhavati, ayam anutpannānām (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> II 202

children.text: ) anutpādāya cchandaḥ / yad votpannān nādhivāsayati prahāṇayati, ayam utpannānāṃ prahāṇāya cchandaḥ //
children.translated_text: And when, regarding arisen ones, one does not tolerate and abandons [them] — this is the aspiration for the abandonment of the arisen.

body.translated_text: When, regarding unarisen evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, one first generates the desire for their non-arising and resolves, being unwilling to tolerate [them] — this is the aspiration for the non-arising of the unarisen.

body.text:
-II-12-b-(2)-i-(b)-(2) Ms.88a2L, Sh.308-14, P.139b7, D.113a7, N.119b5, Co.117b4, Ch.442b14
te punaḥ pāpakā akuśalā dharmā atītavastvālambanā vā anāgatavastvālambanā vā vartamānaviṣayālambanā votpadyante, te bhavanti parokṣaviṣayālambanāḥ pratyakṣaviṣayālambanāś ca / ye 'tītānāgatavastvālambanās te parokṣaviṣayālambanāḥ, ye vartamānaviṣayālambanās te pratyakṣaviṣayālambanāḥ //
body.translated_text: Moreover, those evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> arise having past things as their object, or future things as their object, or present objects as their object. They are of two kinds: having remote objects and having immediate objects. Those having past and future things as objects have remote objects; those having present objects have immediate objects.

body.text:
-II-12-b-(2)-i-(b)-(3) Ms.88a2R, Sh.308-20, P.140a2, D.113b2, N.119b7, Co.117b5, Ch.442b18
tatra parokṣaviṣayālambanānāṃ pāpakānām akuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām anutpannānām anutpādāya, utpannānāṃ ca prahāṇāya vyāyacchate / pratyakṣaviṣayālambanānāṃ punar anutpannānām anutpādāyotpannānāṃ ca prahāṇāya vīryam ārabhate /
body.translated_text: Therein, for the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> that have remote objects, and for the abandonment of arisen ones, one strives. For the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> that have immediate objects, and for the abandonment of arisen ones, one initiates vigor.

body.text: tathā hi teṣāṃ dṛḍhatareṇa vīryārambheṇānutpattiḥ prahāṇaṃ vā bhavati / api ca mṛdumadhyānāṃ paryavasthānānām anutpannānām anutpādāya, utpannānāṃ prahāṇāya uyāyacchate / adhimātrāṇāṃ paryavasthānānām anutpannānām anutpādāya, utpannānāṃ ca prahānāya vīryam ārabhate /
body.translated_text: For indeed, through a firmer initiation of vigor, their non-arising or abandonment comes about. Moreover, for the non-arising of unarisen mild and middling obsessions, and for the abandonment of arisen ones, one strives. For the non-arising of unarisen intense obsessions, and for the abandonment of arisen ones, one initiates vigor.

body.text: saced atīta ālambane carati, tathā carati yathāsya tenālambanena kleśo notpadyate / sacet punaḥ smṛtisaṃpramoṣād utpadyate nādhivāsayati prajahāti vinodayati vyantīkaroti / yathātīta ālambana evam anāgate 'pi veditavyam / (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> II 204

children.text: ) evam ayam anutpannānāṃ pāpakānām akuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām anutpādāyotpannānāṃ ca prahāṇāya "vyāyacchata" ity ucyate /
children.translated_text: Thus, for the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> and for the abandonment of arisen ones, it is said: 'one strives.'

body.translated_text: If one is engaged with a past object, one conducts oneself in such a way that a defilement does not arise through that object. But if through a lapse of mindfulness one does arise, one does not tolerate it, one abandons, dispels, and eliminates it. As with a past object, so should it be understood with a future one also.

body.text: saced ayaṃ vartamāna ālambane carati, tathā tathā carati yathā tenālambanena kleśo notpadyate / sacet punaḥ smṛtisaṃpramoṣād utpadyata utpannaṃ nādhivāsayati prajahāti vinodayati vyantīkaroti / evam anutpannānāṃ pāpakānām akuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām anutpādāyotpannānāṃ ca prahāṇāya "vīryam ārabhata" ity ucyate //
body.translated_text: If one is engaged with a present object, one conducts oneself in such a way that a defilement does not arise through that object. But if through a lapse of mindfulness one arises, one does not tolerate the arisen [defilement], one abandons, dispels, and eliminates it. Thus, for the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> and for the abandonment of arisen ones, it is said: 'one initiates vigor.'

body.text:
-II-12-b-(2)-i-(b)-(4) Ms.88a6M, Sh.309-19, P.140b2, D.114a1, N.120a6, Co.118a4, Ch.442c7
santi pāpakā akuśalā dharmā ye saṃkalpavaśenotpadyante na viṣayabalena, santi ye saṃkalpabalena ca viṣayabalena ca /
body.translated_text: There are evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> that arise by the force of intention alone, not by the force of the object; and there are some that arise by both the force of intention and the force of the object.

body.text: tatra saṃkalpavaśenotpadyante na uiṣayabalena, tadyathā viharato 'tītānāgatālambanena ya utpadyante /
body.translated_text: Therein, those that arise by the force of intention alone, not by the force of the object — such as those that arise while dwelling with past and future objects.

body.text: tatra saṃkalpavaśena ca viṣayabalena cotpadyante, tadyathā carato vartamānenālambanenotpadyante, avaśyaṃ tatrāyoniśaḥsaṃkalpo bhavati //
body.translated_text: Therein, those that arise by both the force of intention and the force of the object — such as those that arise while engaged with a present object. Inevitably, there is also unwise intention in that case.

body.text:
Ms.88a7M, Sh.310-4, P.140b5, D.114a3, N.118a6, Co.120b2, Ch.442c13
tatra ye saṃkalpabalenotpadyante teṣām anutpannānām anutpādāya, utpannānāṃ ca prahāṇāya vyāyacchate / tatra ye viṣayabalena saṃkalpabalena cotpadyante teṣām anutpannānām anutpādāya, utpannānāṃ ca prahāṇāya vīryam ārabhate //
body.translated_text: Therein, for the non-arising of unarisen ones that arise by the force of intention, and for the abandonment of arisen ones, one strives. Therein, for the non-arising of unarisen ones that arise by the force of the object and the force of intention, and for the abandonment of arisen ones, one initiates vigor.

body.text:
-II-12-b-(2)-i-(c) Ms.88a8M, Sh.310-10, P.140b7, D.114a4, N.118b1, Co.120b3, Ch.442c17
tatr"ānutpannānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām utpādāya cchandaṃ janayatī"ti / ye kuśalā dharmā apratilabdhā asaṃmukhībhūtāś ca teṣāṃ pratilambhāya saṃmukhībhāvāya ca spṛhām utpādayati cittaṃ praṇidhatte, tīvrā pratilabdhukāmatā saṃmukhīkartukāmatā cāsya pratyupasthitā bhavati / ayam "anutpannānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām utpattaye chandaḥ" /
body.translated_text: Therein, 'for the arising of unarisen wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, one generates the aspiration' — those wholesome <s>dharmas</s> that have not been obtained and have not been brought to the fore — for their obtainment and for bringing them to the fore, one generates the desire, one resolves the mind; an intense wish to obtain and to bring to the fore has presented itself. This is 'the aspiration for the arising of unarisen wholesome <s>dharmas</s>.'

body.text: "utpannānāṃ ca kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām sthitaye 'saṃmoṣāya bhāvanāparipūraye chandaṃ janayatī"ti, "utpannāḥ kuśalā dharmā" ye pratilabdhāḥ saṃmukhībhūtāś ca / tatra pratilambhāvigamaṃ pratilabdhāpārihāṇim adhikṛtyāha "sthitaya" iti / saṃmukhībhāvād adhandhāyitatvam adhikṛtyāha "asaṃmoṣāye"ti / teṣām eva ca kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ pratilabdhānāṃ saṃmukhībhūtānām āsevanānvayāt pariniṣpattiṃ niṣṭhāgamanam adhikṛtyāha "bhāvanāparipūraya" iti / tatra ca spṛhām utpādayati cittaṃ praṇidhatte tīvrā cāsya sthitikāmatā asaṃmoṣakāmatā bhāvanāparipūrikāmatā pratyupasthitā bhavati / ayam ucyata "utpannānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ sthitaye 'saṃmoṣāya bhāvanāparipūraye chandaḥ" //
body.translated_text: 'And for the stability, the non-loss, the fulfillment of cultivation of arisen wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, one generates the aspiration' — 'arisen wholesome <s>dharmas</s>' are those that have been obtained and brought to the fore. Therein, referring to the non-disappearance and non-deterioration of what has been obtained, he says 'for stability.' Referring to the non-sluggishness of what has been brought to the fore, he says 'for non-loss.' And referring to the completion and culmination through the continuation of practice of those very wholesome <s>dharmas</s> that have been obtained and brought to the fore, he says 'for the fulfillment of cultivation.' And therein, one generates the desire, one resolves the mind, and an intense wish for stability, non-loss, and fulfillment of cultivation has presented itself. This is called 'the aspiration for the stability, non-loss, and fulfillment of cultivation of arisen wholesome <s>dharmas</s>.'

body.text:
Ms.88b3M, Sh.311-7, P.141a6, D.114b2, N.118b6, Co.121a2, Ch.443a2
tatra "vyāyacchata" iti pratilabdhānāṃ saṃmukhībhāvāya / "vīryam ārabhate" 'pratilabdhānāṃ pratilambhāya /
body.translated_text: Therein, 'one strives' for the bringing to the fore of those already obtained. 'One initiates vigor' for the obtainment of those not yet obtained.

body.text: tatra "vyāyacchata" utpannānāṃ sthitaye 'saṃmoṣāya / "vīryam ārabhate" bhāvanāparipūraye /
body.translated_text: Therein, 'one strives' for the stability and non-loss of the arisen. 'One initiates vigor' for the fulfillment of cultivation.

body.text: api ca mṛdumadhyānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām anutpannānām utpādāya, utpannānāṃ ca sthitaye 'saṃmoṣāya vyāyacchate / adhimātrāṇāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām anutpannānām utpādāya, utpannānāṃ ca yāvad bhāvanāparipūraye vīryam ārabhate /
body.translated_text: Moreover, for the arising of unarisen mild and middling wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, and for the stability and non-loss of arisen ones, one strives. For the arising of unarisen intense wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, and for [everything] up to the fulfillment of cultivation of arisen ones, one initiates vigor.

body.text: tatra "cittaṃ pragṛhṇāti" / yadā tac cittaṃ śamathabhāvanāyām ekāgratāyāṃ prayuktaṃ bhavati, anutpannānāṃ pāpakānām akuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām anutpādāya, (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> II 208

children.text: ) evaṃ vistareṇa yāvad utpannānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ sthitaye 'saṃmoṣāya bhāvanāparipūraye tac ca tathādhyātmam abhisaṃkṣiptaṃ līnatvāya paraiti, līnatvābhiśaṅki caivaṃ paśyati / tadānyatamānyatamena pragrāhakeṇa nimittena prasadanīyena pratigṛhṇāti saṃharṣayati / evaṃ cittaṃ pragṛhṇāti /
children.translated_text: and so on in detail up to: for the stability, non-loss, and fulfillment of cultivation of arisen wholesome <s>dharmas</s> — and when that [mind], having become contracted internally, tends toward laxity, and one apprehends the tendency toward laxity — then by means of some uplifting sign that is gladdening, one grasps, encourages, and delights [the mind]. Thus one 'takes hold of the mind.'

body.translated_text: Therein, 'one takes hold of the mind' — when that mind, engaged in the practice of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) cultivation, in one-pointedness, for the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>,

body.text: kathaṃ "pradadhāti" / punar uddhatam auddhatyābhiśaṅki vā pragrahakāle paśyati, tadā punar apy adhyātmam abhisaṃkṣipati śamathāya praṇidadhāti //
body.translated_text: How does one "settle"? Again, when one sees [the mind as] restless or suspects restlessness, at the time of restraint, then again one inwardly contracts [the mind] and settles it for the sake of calm.

body.text:
-II-12-b-(2)-i-(d) Ms.88b7M, Sh.312-10, W.*98-32, P.141b6, D.115a1, N.121b1, Co.119a5, Ch.443a17
tāny etāni bhavanti catvāri samyakprahāṇāni / kṛṣṇapakṣyāṇāṃ dharmāṇām anutpannānām anutpādāya, utpannānāṃ ca prahāṇāya cchando vyāyāmo vīryārambhaś cittapragrahaḥ pradadhanam ime dve samyakprahāṇe / śuklapakṣyāṇāṃ dharmāṇām anutpannānām utpādāya, vistareṇa dve samyakprahāṇe veditavye / tadyathā kṛṣṇapakṣyāṇām /
body.translated_text: These then are the four right exertions: For the non-arising of unarisen dark-side <s>dharmas</s>, and for the abandonment of arisen ones — the desire, effort, energetic striving, mental seizing, and settling — these are two right exertions. For the arising of unarisen bright-side <s>dharmas</s> — and in detail, two right exertions should be understood, as with the dark-side ones.

body.text: tatraikaṃ saṃvaraṇaprahāṇam, yad "utpannānāṃ pāpakānām akuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ prahāṇāya cchandaṃ janayatī"ti vistareṇa /
body.translated_text: Therein, one is the exertion of restraint — which is: "One generates desire for the abandonment of arisen evil unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>" and so on in detail.

body.text: dvitīyaṃ prahāṇaprahāṇam, yad "anutpannānām anutpādāya cchandaṃ janayatī"ti vistareṇa / utpannaṃ hi saṃvarayitavyaṃ pāpakaṃ vastu, anutpannaṃ ca yat tad asamudācārataḥ prahīṇam eva tad asaṃmukhībhāvataḥ prahātavyaṃ iti kṛtvā, prahīṇasya praḥāṇaṃ prahāṇaprahāṇam /
body.translated_text: The second is the exertion of abandonment — which is: "One generates desire for the non-arising of unarisen ones" and so on in detail. For an arisen evil thing is to be restrained, and an unarisen one — which has been abandoned in the sense of non-occurrence — is to be abandoned in the sense of non-confrontation. The abandonment of what has [already] been abandoned is the exertion of abandonment.

body.text: tatra bhāvanāprahāṇam ekam / yad āha / "anutpannānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām utpādāye"ti vistareṇa yāvac "cittaṃ pragṛhṇāti pradadhātī"ti /
body.translated_text: Therein, one is the exertion of cultivation — which says: "For the arising of unarisen wholesome <s>dharmas</s>" and so on in detail up to: "one seizes the mind and settles it."

body.text:
tathā hi kuśalā dharmā āsevyamānā bhāvyamānā, apratilabdhāś ca pratilabhyante, pratilabdhāś ca saṃmukhīkriyante /
tatrānurakṣaṇāprahāṇam ekam / yad āha / "utpannānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ sthitaye" vistareṇa yāvac "cittaṃ pragṛhṇāti, pradadhāti" / tathā hi pratilabdheṣu saṃmukhīkṛteṣu ca kuśaleṣu dharmeṣu yā pramādavarjanā apramādaniṣevaṇā ca sā kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ sthitaye, asaṃmoṣāya, bhāvanāparipūraye saṃvartate / evam utpannāḥ kuśalā dharmā anurakṣitā bhavanti / ayaṃ tāvat samyakprahāṇānāṃ vistaravibhāgaḥ //
body.translated_text: For indeed, wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, when practiced and cultivated, are obtained when not yet obtained, and when obtained, they are brought to the forefront. Therein, one is the exertion of guarding — which says: "For the stability of arisen wholesome <s>dharmas</s>" and so on in detail up to: "one seizes the mind and settles it." For indeed, with regard to wholesome <s>dharmas</s> that have been obtained and brought to the forefront, the avoidance of heedlessness and the cultivation of diligence — this conduces to the stability, non-loss, and fulfillment of cultivation of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. Thus arisen wholesome <s>dharmas</s> become guarded. This, for now, is the detailed analysis of the right exertions.

body.text:
-II-12-b-(2)-ii Ms.89a3R, Sh.313-14, P.142a8, D.115b2, N.122a2, Co.119b5, Ch.443b8
samāsārthaḥ punaḥ katamaḥ / āha / kṛṣṇaśuklapakṣikasya tyāgādānavastuno 'dhyāśayasaṃpat prayogasaṃpac ca paridīpitā bhavati / tatrādhyāśayasaṃpac chandajananatayā, prayogasaṃpat punar vyāyāmavīryārambhacittapragrahapradadhanaiḥ / etāvac ca yoginā karaṇīyam / yat prahātavyasya vastunaḥ prahāṇāya prāptavyasya ca vastunaḥ prāptaye pūrvam eva spṛhājātena bhavitavyam, paryavasthānaprahāṇāya vīryam ārabdhavyam anuśayaprahāṇāya ca, kālena kālaṃ śamathapragrahopekṣānimittāni bhāvayitavyāni (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> II 212

children.text: ) / paryavasthānaprahāṇānuśayaprahāṇāya ca ye pratipakṣikā dharmāḥ kuśalās te samudānayitavyāḥ / tac caitat sarvaṃ caturbhiḥ samyakprahāṇaiḥ paridīpitaṃ bhavati / ayaṃ samāsārthaḥ //
children.translated_text: ) And for the abandonment of active defilements and latent tendencies, one must accomplish those wholesome <s>dharmas</s> that are their antidotes. And all of this has been illuminated through the four right exertions. This is the summary meaning.

body.translated_text: What then is the summary meaning? It is said: The endowment of superior intention and the endowment of application have been illuminated with regard to the matter of abandoning and adopting the dark and bright sides. Therein, the endowment of superior intention is through the generation of desire; the endowment of application is through effort, energetic striving, mental seizing, and settling. And this is what is to be done by the yogin: For the abandonment of the matter to be abandoned and for the attainment of the matter to be attained, one must first of all be one in whom longing has arisen; one must arouse energy for the abandonment of active defilements and for the abandonment of latent tendencies; and from time to time one must cultivate the signs of calm, restraint, and equanimity.

body.text:
-II-12-b-(3) Ms.89a6M, Sh.314-5, P.142b5, D.115b6, N.122a6, Co.120a2, Ch.443b18
tatra catvāraḥ samādhayaḥ / tadyathā chandasamādhiḥ, vīryasamādhiḥ, cittasamādhiḥ, mīmāṃsāsamādhiś ca /
body.translated_text: Therein, the four concentrations: namely, the concentration based on desire (<s>chandasamādhi</s>), the concentration based on energy (<s>vīryasamādhi</s>), the concentration based on mind (<s>cittasamādhi</s>), and the concentration based on investigation (<s>mīmāṃsāsamādhi</s>).

body.text: tatra cchandam adhipatiṃ kṛtvā yaḥ pratilabhyate samādhir ayaṃ chandasamādhiḥ / vīryam, cittam, mīmāṃsām adhipatiṃ kṛtvā yaḥ pratilabhyate samādhir ayaṃ mīmāṃsāsamādhiḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, the concentration obtained by making desire the predominant factor — this is the concentration based on desire. The concentration obtained by making energy, mind, or investigation the predominant factor — this is the concentration based on investigation.

body.text:
-II-12-b-(3)-i-(a) Ms.89a7R, Sh.315-4, P.142b7, D.115b7, N.122b1, Co.120a4, Ch.443b23
yadā tāvad ayaṃ chandam eva kevalaṃ janayati / chandajātaś ca tān pāpakān akuśalān dharmān svabhāvato nidānata ādīnavataḥ pratipakṣataś ca samyag evopanidadhyāti, ekāgrāṃ smṛtiṃ pravartayati / evaṃ kuśalān dharmān svabhāvato nidānato 'nuśaṃsato niḥsaraṇataḥ samyag evopanidadhyāti, ekāgrāṃ smṛtim avasthāpayati, tadbahulākārād ekāgratām spṛśati paryavasthānasamudācāradūrīkaraṇayogena / na tv adyāpy anuśayaṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> II 214

children.text: ) samudghātayati pāpakānām akuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām / ayam apy ucyate chandādhipateyaḥ //
children.translated_text: ) of evil unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>. This too is called the [concentration with] desire as predominant.

body.translated_text: When one generates merely desire — and having generated desire, one properly attends to those evil unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> from the standpoint of their nature, their cause, their danger, and their antidote, and establishes one-pointed mindfulness. Similarly, one properly attends to wholesome <s>dharmas</s> from the standpoint of their nature, their cause, their benefit, and their escape, and establishes one-pointed mindfulness — from the frequent application of this, one touches one-pointedness through the practice of distancing from the arising of active defilements. But one does not yet uproot the latent tendencies

body.text:
-II-12-b-(3)-i-(b) Ms.89b2M, Sh.316-10, P.143a3, D.116a3, N.122b4, Co.120a7, Ch.443b29
sa atīte vānāgatapratyutpanne vā punar ālambane pāpakākuśaladharmasthānīye mṛdumadhyādhimātrakleśaparyavasthānīye, anutpannasya vānutpādāya, utpannasya vā prahāṇāya, vyāyacchamāno vīryam ārabhamāṇaḥ / tatrālambane vicarataḥ, tasya vālambanasya svabhāvato nidānata ādīnavataḥ pratipakṣataś ca samyag upanidhyāyataḥ, ekāgrāṃ smṛtim upasthāpayataḥ, yat tadbahulavihāriṇaś cittaikāgratā utpadyate paryavasthānasamudācāradūrīkaraṇayogena / na tv adyāpy anuśayaṃ samudghātayati pāpakānām akuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām / ayaṃ vīryādhipateyaḥ samādhiḥ //
body.translated_text: One, with regard to objects that are bases for evil unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> — whether past, future, or present — and that are bases for mild, moderate, or intense afflictions of defilement, for the non-arising of the unarisen and for the abandonment of the arisen, exerting oneself and arousing energy — while examining that object, while properly attending to that very object from the standpoint of its nature, cause, danger, and antidote, while establishing one-pointed mindfulness — for one who frequently dwells thus, the one-pointedness of mind that arises through the practice of distancing from the arising of active defilements — but one does not yet uproot the latent tendencies of evil unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> — this is the concentration with energy as predominant.

body.text:
-II-12-b-(3)-i-(c) Ms.89b4M, Sh.316-19, P.143a7, D.116a6, N.122b7, Co.120b3, Ch.443c8
līnaṃ vā punaś cittaṃ pragṛhṇataḥ, pragṛhītaṃ cittaṃ samādadhataḥ, kālena ca kālam adhyupekṣito yat pāpakākuśalān dharmān pāpakākuśaladharmasthānīyānvayān, kuśalākuśalān dharmān kuśalākuśalasthānīyāṃś ca dharmān svabhāvato nidānata ādīnavato 'nuśaṃsataḥ pratipakṣato niḥsaraṇataḥ, samyag upanidhyāyataḥ, ekāgrāṃ smṛtim upasthāpayataḥ, (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> II 216

children.text: ) tadbahulavihāriṇo yā utpadyante cittasyaikāgratā / vistareṇa yāvat / ayam ucyate cittādhipateyaḥ samādhiḥ //
children.translated_text: ) for one who frequently dwells thus, the one-pointedness of mind that arises — and so on in detail — this is called the concentration with mind as predominant.

body.translated_text: Furthermore, when one seizes a sunken mind, when one settles a mind that has been seized, when from time to time one exercises equanimity, and when with regard to evil unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> and objects that are bases for evil unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, and wholesome-unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> and objects that are their bases, one properly attends from the standpoint of their nature, cause, danger, benefit, antidote, and escape, and establishes one-pointed mindfulness —

body.text:
-II-12-b-(3)-i-(d) Ms.89b5R, Sh.317-8, P.143b3, D.116b2, N.123a3, Co.120b6, Ch.443c15
tatra ye pāpakākuśaladharmasthānīyā dharmā bhavanty ayoniśomanasikurvataḥ / ta eva kuśaladharmasthānīyā bhavanti yoniśomanasikurvataḥ / tasyaivaṃ paryavasthāneṣu dūrīkṛteṣu, paryavasthānapratipakṣikeṣu ca samādhipramukheṣu dharmeṣv utpanneṣu, te pāpakā akuśalā dharmā na samudācaranti /
body.translated_text: Therein, those <s>dharmas</s> that are bases for evil unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> when one attends unwisely — those very same become bases for wholesome <s>dharmas</s> when one attends wisely. For one whose active defilements have been distanced, and for whom <s>dharmas</s> headed by concentration, which are antidotes to active defilements, have arisen — those evil unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> no longer occur.

body.text: tasyaivaṃ bhavati / "kiṃ sataḥ saṃvidyamānān pāpakān akuśalān dharmān na pratisaṃvedayāmy āhosvid asato 'saṃvidyamānān yan nv ahaṃ parimīmāṃseyam" / sa mīmāṃsāmanaskāram adhipatiṃ kṛtvā prahīṇāprahīṇatāṃ mīmāṃsate, samyag evopanidhyāyati, ekāgrām smṛtim upasthāpayati / tadbahulavihārī ca spṛśati cittasyaikāgratām / yena nirabhimāno bhavati / "paryavasthānamātrakān me cittaṃ vimuktaṃ na tu sarveṇa sarvam anuśayebhyaḥ, tatpratipakṣāś ca me samādhipramukhāḥ kuśalā dharmāḥ pratilabdhā, bhāvitā, na tv anuśayaprātipakṣikā" iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / ayam asyocyate mīmāṃsāsamādhiḥ //
body.translated_text: One thinks thus: "Do I not experience evil unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> because they exist and are present, or because they do not exist and are not present? Let me investigate." Making the mental attention of investigation the predominant factor, one investigates whether [afflictions] have been abandoned or not abandoned, properly attends, and establishes one-pointed mindfulness. And one who frequently dwells thus touches one-pointedness of mind — whereby one becomes free from conceit: "My mind is freed only from active defilements, but not entirely and in every way from latent tendencies. And those wholesome <s>dharmas</s> headed by concentration that are their antidotes have been obtained by me and cultivated, but they are not yet antidotes to the latent tendencies" — thus one knows according to reality. This is called one's concentration based on investigation.

body.text:
-II-12-b-(3)-i-(e) Ms.90a1R, Sh.318-5, P.144a2, D.116b7, N.123b2, Co.121a4, Ch.443c29
sa taṃ caturvidhaṃ samādhim adhipatiṃ kṛtvā paryavasthāneṣu dūrīkṛteṣu, sarveṇa sarvam anuśayasamudghātāya pāpakānām akuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ tatprātipakṣikāṇāñ ca kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ samudāgamāya punar api chandaṃ janayati vyāyacchata iti vistareṇa caturbhiḥ samyakprahāṇaiḥ prayujyate //
body.translated_text: One, making that fourfold concentration the predominant factor, when active defilements have been distanced — for the complete uprooting of all latent tendencies of evil unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> and for the accomplishment of those wholesome <s>dharmas</s> that are their antidotes — one again generates desire, exerts oneself, and so on in detail — one engages with the four right exertions.

body.text:
-II-12-b-(3)-ii-(a) Ms.90a2R, Sh.318-10, W*.99-1, P.144a4, D.117a2, N.123b4, Co.121a5, Ch.444a4
tathāprayuktasya tathābhūtasyāṣṭau praḥāṇasaṃskārā bhavanti / ye 'syānuśayasamudghātāya ca pravartante samādhiparipūraye ca /
body.translated_text: For one thus engaged and so constituted, there are eight factors of abandonment, which operate for the uprooting of latent tendencies and for the fulfillment of concentration.

body.text: tadyathā chandaḥ "kadācit samādhiṃ paripūrayiṣyāmi, anuśayāṃś ca prahāsyāmi pāpakānām akuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām" /
body.translated_text: Namely: desire — "At some point I shall fulfill concentration and abandon the latent tendencies of evil unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>."

body.text: vyāyāmo yāvat pratipakṣabhāvanāyām avinyastaprayogatā /
body.translated_text: Effort — up to: non-relaxation of application in the cultivation of the antidote.

body.text: śraddhā yā avinyastaprayogasya viharata uttare 'dhigame śraddadhānatā, abhisaṃpratyayaḥ /
body.translated_text: Faith — the confidence and conviction of one who dwells without relaxation of application, regarding the higher attainment.

body.text:
tatra praśrabdhir yac chraddhāprasādapūrvaṃgamaṃ prāmodyaṃ prītiḥ, prītamanasaś cānupūrvā pāpakākuśaladharmapakṣasya dauṣṭhulyasya pratipraśrabdhiḥ /
tatra smṛtir yā navākārā, navākārāyāś cittasthiteḥ śamathapakṣyāyāḥ saṃgrāhikā /
body.translated_text: Therein, tranquility — which is the gladness and joy preceded by the confidence of faith; and the sequential relaxation of the rigidity belonging to the side of evil unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> for one whose mind is joyful. Therein, mindfulness — which is the nine-aspected [mindfulness] that collects the nine-aspected fixation of mind belonging to the calm-abiding side.

body.text: tatra saṃprajanyam yā vipaśyanāpakṣyā prajñā /
body.translated_text: Therein, clear comprehension — which is the wisdom belonging to the insight side.

body.text: tatra cetanā yaś cittābhisaṃskāraḥ prahīṇāprahīṇatāṃ mīmāṃsamānasya yaś cittābhisaṃskāraḥ śamathavipaśyanānukūlaḥ kāyakarma vākkarma samutthāpayati /
body.translated_text: Therein, volition — which is the mental formation; for one investigating whether [defilements] have been abandoned or not, it is the mental formation that, in conformity with calm abiding and insight, produces bodily action and verbal action.

body.text: tatropekṣā yātitānāgatapratyutpanneṣu pāpakākuśaladharmasthānīyeṣu carataś cittāsaṃkleśā cittasamatā / ābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāṃ prahīṇatām anuśayānāṃ paricchinatti jānāti / yaduta viṣayaviparokṣayā cetanayā viṣayāviparokṣayā copekṣayā /
body.translated_text: Therein, equanimity — which is the non-defilement of mind, the evenness of mind, while one moves among objects past, future, and present that are bases for evil unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>. By these two causes, one discerns and knows the state of abandonment of latent tendencies — namely: by the volition that does not turn away from the object, and by the equanimity that does not turn away from the object.

body.text: ime 'ṣṭau prahāṇasaṃskārā bhavanti //
body.translated_text: These are the eight factors of abandonment.

body.text:
-II-12-b-(3)-ii-(b) Ms.90a6M, Sh.320-17, W.*99-21, P.144b4, D.117b1, N.124a3, Co.121b5, Ch.444a21
sa caiṣo 'ṣṭaprahāṇasaṃskārayogo bhavaty anuśayasamudghātāya / tatra chandaś chanda eva, yo vyāyāma idaṃ vīryam, yā śraddhā sā śraddhā, yā ca praśrabdhir yā ca smṛtir yac ca saṃprajanyaṃ yā ca cetanā yā copekṣā ayam upāyaḥ / tad idaṃ sarvam abhisamasya, ye ca pūrvakāś chandasamādhayaḥ, ye ceme prahāṇasaṃskārāḥ prahīṇeṣv anuśayeṣu pariniṣpanne samādhau, chandasamādhiprahāṇasaṃskārasamanvāgata ṛddhipāda ity ucyate / vīryacittamīmāṃsāsamādhiprahāṇasaṃskārasamanvāgata ṛddhipāda ity ucyate /
body.translated_text: This practice of the eight factors of abandonment is for the uprooting of latent tendencies. Therein, desire is desire itself; effort is energy; faith is faith; tranquility, mindfulness, clear comprehension, volition, and equanimity — this is the skillful means. Taking all of this together — the prior concentrations based on desire, and these factors of abandonment — when the latent tendencies have been abandoned and the concentration has been completed, [the whole] endowed with the concentration based on desire and the factors of abandonment is called a <s>ṛddhipāda</s> (basis of supernatural power). [Similarly,] endowed with the concentrations based on energy, mind, and investigation, and the factors of abandonment, it is called a <s>ṛddhipāda</s>.

body.text:
-II-12-b-(3)-iii Ms.90b1L, Sh.321-5, W.100-1, P.144b8, D.117b4, N.124a7, Co.121b7, Ch.444a29
kena kāraṇena ṛddhipāda ity ucyate / āha / tadyathā yasya pādaḥ saṃvidyate so 'bhikramapratikramaparākramasamartho bhavati / evam eva yasyaite dharmāḥ saṃvidyante, eṣa ca samādhiḥ saṃvidyate paripūrṇaḥ, sa evaṃ pariśuddhe citte, paryavadāte, anaṅgaṇe, vigatopakleśe, ṛjubhūte, karmaṇyasthite, āniñjyaprāpte, abhikramapratikramaparākramasamartho bhavati, lokottarāṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ prāptaye sparśanāyai / eṣā hi parā ṛddhiḥ parā samṛddhiḥ, yaduta lokottarā dharmāḥ / tenocyata ṛddhipāda iti //
body.translated_text: For what reason is it called 'basis of supernatural power' (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>)? He says: Just as one who has a foot is capable of stepping forward, stepping backward, and striding forth — so too one in whom these <s>dharmas</s> and this concentration exist in completeness, with a mind thus purified, cleansed, unblemished, free from secondary defilements, straightened, workable, stable, and having attained imperturbability — one is capable of stepping forward, stepping backward, and striding forth for the attainment and realization of supramundane <s>dharmas</s>. For this is the supreme supernatural power, the supreme prosperity — namely, the supramundane <s>dharmas</s>. Therefore it is called 'basis of supernatural power.'

body.text:
-II-12-b-(4)-i-(a) Ms.90b2R, Sh.321-15, P.145a3, D.117b7, N.124b3, Co.122a3, Ch.444b8
sa evaṃ samādhipratiṣṭhitaḥ samādhiṃ niśrityādhicittaṃśikṣāyām adhiprajñaṃśikṣāyāṃ yogaṃ karoti / tatrāsya yogaṃ kurvataḥ pareṣāṃ cādhigame śāstuḥ śrāvakāṇāṃ ca yo 'bhisaṃpratyayaḥ prasādaḥ / śraddadhānatā adhipatyarthena śraddhendriyam ity ucyate /
body.translated_text: Thus established in concentration and relying on concentration, one practices yoga in the training of the higher mind (<s>adhicittaśikṣā</s>) and in the training of higher wisdom (<s>adhiprajñāśikṣā</s>). Therein, for one practicing yoga, the belief, confidence, and faith in the attainment of others — of the <s>Śāstā</s> (Teacher) and the <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) — in the sense of sovereignty, is called the faculty of faith (<s>śraddhendriya</s>).

body.text: kutra punar asyādhipatyam / āha / lokottaradharmotpattipramukhānāṃ vīryasmṛtisamādhiprajñānām utpattaya ādhipatyam / ye 'pi te vīryādayas teṣām api lokottaradharmotpattaya ādhipatyam / yāvat pratipattaya ādhipatyam / yāvat prajñāyā lokottaradharmotpattaya ādhipatyam / tenaitāni śraddhādīni pañcendriyāṇi bhavanti //
body.translated_text: Where does its sovereignty lie? He says: sovereignty over the arising of vigor, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom, preceded by the arising of supramundane <s>dharmas</s>. And those very [factors] beginning with vigor have sovereignty over the arising of supramundane <s>dharmas</s> — up to sovereignty over the practice. Up to: the sovereignty of wisdom over the arising of supramundane <s>dharmas</s>. Therefore these five, beginning with faith, are faculties (<s>indriya</s>).

body.text:
-II-12-b-(4)-i-(b) Ms.90b4M, Sh.322-11, P. 145a8, D.118a4, N.124b6, Co.122a7, Ch.444b17
yā punaḥ pūrveṇāparaṃ viśeṣādhigamaṃ saṃjānatas tadanusāreṇa taduttaralokottaradharmādhigamāyābhisaṃpratyayaḥ prasādaḥ śraddadhānatā / sā anavamṛdyatārthena śraddhābalam ity ucyate / kena punar na śakyate 'vamṛditum / asaṃhāryā sā śraddhā devena vā, māreṇa vā, brahmaṇā vā, kenacid vā punar loke sahadharmeṇa, kleśaparyavasthānena vā / tena sānavamṛdyety ucyate / tatpramukhās tatpūrvaṃgamā ye vīryādayas te 'pi balānīty ucyante / taiḥ sa balair balavān sarvaṃ mārabalaṃ vijitya prayujyata āsravāṇāṃ kṣayāya / tasmād balānīty ucyante //
body.translated_text: And the belief, confidence, and faith — knowing the successive attainment of distinction after the previous [attainment], and in accordance with that, for the attainment of the further supramundane <s>dharmas</s> — in the sense of being uncrushed, is called the power of faith (<s>śraddhābala</s>). By what can it not be crushed? That faith is unconquerable by a <s>deva</s>, by <s>Māra</s>, by <s>Brahmā</s>, or by anyone in the world, whether by a counter-argument (<s>sahadharma</s>) or by the overwhelming force of a defilement (<s>kleśaparyavasthāna</s>). Therefore it is called 'uncrushed.' Those [factors] beginning with vigor that are preceded by and have as their forerunners [faith] — they too are called powers. Endowed with those powers, being powerful, having conquered the entire host of <s>Māra</s>, one practices for the destruction of the <s>āsravas</s> (defilements). Therefore they are called powers.

body.text:
-II-12-b-(4)-ii Ms.90b6M, Sh.323-7, W.*100-22, P.145b3, D.118a7, N.125a3, Co.122b3, Ch.444b26
tatra yac ca śraddhendriyaṃ yac ca śraddhābalaṃ caturṣv etad avetyaprasādeṣu draṣṭavyam / tat kasya hetoḥ / yo 'sau samyaktvanyāmāvakrāntasyāvetyaprasādaḥ sa taddhetukas tatpratyayas tannidānaḥ / tasmād dhetuphalasaṃbandhena tasyās tad adhipatiphalam iti kṛtvā tatra draṣṭavyam ity uktaṃ bhagavatā, na tu taccharīratā tallakṣaṇatā /
body.translated_text: Therein, the faculty of faith and the power of faith should be seen in the four kinds of unwavering confidence (<s>avetyaprasāda</s>). For what reason? That unwavering confidence of one who has entered the certainty of correctness (<s>samyaktvaniyāma</s>) has that [faith] as its cause, that as its condition, that as its basis. Therefore, by the connection of cause and effect, that being the dominant fruit of it, it is said by the <s>Bhagavān</s> to be seen therein — not that [faith] is identical with or has the characteristic of [the unwavering confidence].

body.text: tatra vīryendriyaṃ caturṣu samyakprahāṇeṣu draṣṭavyam / tat kasya hetoḥ / yāni katamāni samyakprahāṇāni / yāni darśanaprahātavyakleśaprahāṇāya prāyogikāṇi samyakprahāṇāni, tāny atra samyakprahāṇāny abhipretāni / tāni hy atyantatāyai pāpakānām akuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ prahāṇāya saṃvartante /
body.translated_text: Therein, the faculty of vigor should be seen in the four right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>). For what reason? Whatever are the right efforts — those right efforts that are preliminary to the abandonment of defilements to be abandoned by seeing — those are the right efforts intended here. For they conduce to the ultimate abandonment of evil unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: tatra smṛtīndriyaṃ caturṣu smṛtyupasthāneṣu draṣṭavyam / itīmāni catvāri smṛtyupasthānāny aśeṣaviparyāsaprahāṇāya saṃvartante /
body.translated_text: Therein, the faculty of mindfulness should be seen in the four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>). These four foundations of mindfulness conduce to the abandonment of all distortions without remainder.

body.text: tatra samādhīndriyaṃ caturṣu dhyāneṣu draṣṭavyam / yāni dhyānāny anāgāmitāyāṃ prāyogikāṇi /
body.translated_text: Therein, the faculty of concentration should be seen in the four <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions) — those <s>dhyānas</s> that are preliminary to the state of non-returning (<s>anāgāmitā</s>).

body.text:
tatra prajñendriyaṃ caturṣv āryasatyeṣu draṣṭavyam / iti yat satyajñānaṃ caturṇām āryasatyānām abhisamayāya saṃvartate śrāmaṇyaphalaprāptaye /
yathendriyāṇy evaṃ balāni veditavyāni //
body.translated_text: Therein, the faculty of wisdom should be seen in the four noble truths (<s>āryasatya</s>). The knowledge of the truths conduces to the realization of the four noble truths and to the attainment of the fruits of the ascetic life. As with the faculties, so should the powers be understood.

body.text:
-II-12-b-(4)-iii Ms.91a2R, Sh.324-8, W.*101-5, P.146a3, D.118b6, N.125b2, Co.123a2, Ch.444c10
sa eṣām indriyāṇām eteṣāṃ ca balānām āsevanānvayād bhāvanānvayād bahulīkārānvayān nirvedhabhāgīyāni kuśalamūlāny utpādayati mṛdumadhyādhimātrāṇi / tadyathoṣmagatāni mūrdhānaḥ satyānulomāḥ kṣāntayo laukikāgradharmāḥ /
body.translated_text: Through the course of practicing, cultivating, and making much of these faculties and powers, one generates the wholesome roots conducive to penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya kuśalamūla</s>) — mild, middling, and intense. Namely: the heat (<s>ūṣmagata</s>), the peaks (<s>mūrdhāna</s>), the conforming patient acceptances of the truths (<s>satyānulomakṣānti</s>), and the worldly supreme <s>dharmas</s> (<s>laukikāgradharma</s>).

body.text: tadyathā kaścid eva puruṣo 'gnināgnikāryaṃ kartukāmo 'gninārthy adharāraṇyām uttarāraṇiṃ pratiṣṭhāpyābhimathnann utsahate ghaṭate vyāyacchate / tasyotsahato ghaṭato vyāyacchataś ca tatprathamato 'dharāraṇyām ūṣmā jāyate / saiva coṣmābhivardhamānā ūrdhvam āgacchati /
body.translated_text: Just as a certain man, wishing to produce fire and desiring fire, places the upper fire-stick upon the lower fire-stick and rubs — he exerts himself, strives, and endeavors. For him, while exerting, striving, and endeavoring, heat is first generated in the lower fire-stick. And that same heat, increasing, rises upward.

body.text: bhūyasyā mātrayābhivardhamānā nirarciṣam agniṃ pātayati, agnipatanasamanantaram eva cārcir jāyate / yathārciṣotpannayā jātayā saṃjātayāgnikāryaṃ karoti / yathābhimanthanavyāyāma evaṃ pañcānām indriyāṇām āsevanā draṣṭavyā / yathādharāraṇyā tatprathamata evoṣmagataṃ bhavaty, evam ūṣmagatāni draṣṭavyāni / pūrvaṃgamāni nimittabhūtāny agnisthānīyānām anāsravāṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ kleśaparidāhakānām utpattaye / yathā tasyaivoṣmaṇa ūrdhvam āgamanam evaṃ mūrdhāno draṣṭavyāḥ / yathā dhūmaprādurbhāva evaṃ satyānulomāḥ kṣāntayo draṣṭavyāḥ / yathāgneḥ patanaṃ nirarciṣa evaṃ laukikāgradharmā draṣṭavyāḥ / yathā tadanantaram arciṣa utpāda evaṃ lokottarānāsravā dharmā draṣṭavyāḥ / ye laukikāgradharmasaṃgṛhītānāṃ pañcānām indriyāṇāṃ samanantaram utpadyante //
body.translated_text: Increasing further in measure, it produces flameless fire; and immediately upon the falling of the fire, a flame arises. Just as with the arisen flame one performs the work of fire — so should the practice of the five faculties be seen as like the rubbing exertion. Just as the heat first arises in the lower fire-stick — so should the heat stage (<s>ūṣmagata</s>) be seen: as forerunners, serving as signs for the arising of the undefiled <s>dharmas</s> that stand in the place of fire, which burn away defilements. Just as the rising upward of that very heat — so should the peaks (<s>mūrdhāna</s>) be seen. Just as the appearance of smoke — so should the conforming patient acceptances of the truths (<s>satyānulomakṣānti</s>) be seen. Just as the falling of flameless fire — so should the worldly supreme <s>dharmas</s> (<s>laukikāgradharma</s>) be seen. Just as the arising of the flame immediately thereafter — so should the supramundane undefiled <s>dharmas</s> be seen, which arise immediately after the five faculties comprised in the worldly supreme <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text:
-II-12-b-(5) Ms.91a6R, Sh.325-17, P.146b5, D.119a6, N.126a4, Co.123b2, Ch.444c29
te punaḥ katame / āha / saptabodhyaṅgāni / yo 'sau yathābhūtāvabodhaḥ samyaktvanyāmāvakrāntasya pudgalasya tasyaitāny aṅgāni / sa hi yathābhūtāvabodhaḥ saptāṅgaparigṛhītaḥ, tribhiḥ śamathapakṣyaiḥ, tribhir vipaśyanāpakṣyaiḥ, ekenobhayapakṣyeṇa / tasmād bodhyaṅgānīty ucyante /
body.translated_text: And what are those? He says: the seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>). That awakening as it truly is (<s>yathābhūtāvabodha</s>) of a person who has entered the certainty of correctness (<s>samyaktvaniyāma</s>) — these are its factors. For that awakening as it truly is is accompanied by seven factors: three on the side of calm (<s>śamathapakṣya</s>), three on the side of insight (<s>vipaśyanāpakṣya</s>), and one on the side of both.

body.text: tatra yaś ca dharmavicayaḥ, yac ca vīryam, yā ca prītir itīmāni trīṇi vipaśyanāpakṣyāṇi / tatra yā ca prasrabdhiḥ, yaś ca samādhiḥ, yā copekṣā (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 230

children.text: ) itīmāni trīṇi śamathapakṣyāṇi / smṛtir ubhayapakṣyā sarvatragety ucyate / sa tasmin samaye tatprathamato bodhyaṅgalābhāc chaikṣo bhavati dṛṣṭapadaḥ //
children.translated_text: — these three are on the side of calm. Mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>) is on the side of both, pervading all — so it is said. At that time, from the very first obtaining of the factors of awakening, one becomes a trainee (<s>śaikṣa</s>), one who has seen the path (<s>dṛṣṭapada</s>).

body.translated_text: Therein, the investigation of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmavicaya</s>), vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), and joy (<s>prīti</s>) — these three are on the side of insight. Therein, tranquility (<s>prasrabdhi</s>), concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), and equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>)

body.text:
-II-12-b-(6) Ms.91b1R, Sh.326-10, P.147a1, D.119b2, N.126a7, Co.123b5, Ch.445a8
darśanaprahātavyāś cāsya kleśāḥ prahīṇā bhavanti, bhāvanāprahātavyāś cāvaśiṣṭāḥ / sa teṣāṃ prahāṇāya triskandham āryāṣṭāṅgaṃ mārgaṃ bhāvayati /
body.translated_text: And his defilements to be abandoned by seeing are abandoned, and those to be abandoned by cultivation remain. For their abandonment, one cultivates the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅga mārga</s>) comprised of three aggregates.

body.text: tatra yā ca samyagdṛṣṭir, yaś ca samyaksaṃkalpaḥ, yaś ca samyagvyāyāmaḥ, ayaṃ prajñāskandhaḥ / tatra ye samyakvākkarmāntājīvāḥ, ayaṃ śīlaskandhaḥ / tatra yā ca samyaksmṛtiḥ, yaś ca samyaksamādhiḥ, ayaṃ samādhiskandhaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>), right intention (<s>samyaksaṃkalpa</s>), and right effort (<s>samyagvyāyāma</s>) — this is the aggregate of wisdom (<s>prajñāskandha</s>). Therein, right speech, right action, and right livelihood — this is the aggregate of moral conduct (<s>śīlaskandha</s>). Therein, right mindfulness (<s>samyaksmṛti</s>) and right concentration (<s>samyaksamādhi</s>) — this is the aggregate of concentration (<s>samādhiskandha</s>).

body.text: kena kāraṇenāryāṣṭāṅgo mārga ity ucyate / āha / āryasya śaikṣasya dṛṣṭapadasyāyaṃ mārga iyaṃ pratipad aṣṭābhir aṅgaiḥ saṃgṛhītaḥ, apariśeṣaḥ sarvakleśaprahāṇāya vimuktisākṣātkriyāyai / tenocyata āryāṣṭāṅgo mārgaḥ //
body.translated_text: For what reason is it called the noble eightfold path? He says: this is the path, this is the practice of the noble trainee (<s>śaikṣa</s>) who has seen the path, comprised of eight factors, which is complete for the abandonment of all defilements and for the direct realization of liberation. Therefore it is called the noble eightfold path.

body.text:
-II-12-b-(6)-i Ms.91b3M, Sh.327-13, P.147a5, D.119b6, N.126b4, Co.124a2, Ch.445a15
tatra yaś ca bodhyaṅgakāle tattvāvabodhaḥ pratilabdhaḥ, pratilabhya ca yat tasyaiva prajñayā vyavasthānaṃ karoti yathādhigatasyāvabodhasya, tad ubhayam ekadhyam abhisaṃkṣipya samyagdṛṣṭir ity ucyate /
body.translated_text: Therein, the awakening to reality obtained at the time of the factors of awakening, and the establishment by means of that very wisdom of what has been realized — both taken together are called right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>).

body.text: tāṃ samyagdṛṣṭim adhipatiṃ kṛtvā yan naiṣkramyasaṃkalpaṃ saṃkalpayaty avyāpādasaṃkalpam avihiṃsāsaṃkalpam / ayam ucyate samyaksaṃkalpaḥ /
body.translated_text: Having right view as the governing [factor], one conceives the intention of renunciation (<s>naiṣkramyasaṃkalpa</s>), the intention of non-ill-will (<s>avyāpādasaṃkalpa</s>), and the intention of non-harming (<s>avihiṃsāsaṃkalpa</s>). This is called right intention (<s>samyaksaṃkalpa</s>).

body.text: sacet tāvad vitarkeṣu cittaṃ krāmati, sa evaṃrūpān vitarkān vitarkayati / sacet punaḥ kathāyāṃ cittaṃ krāmati, samyagdṛṣṭim adhipatiṃ kṛtvā tenaiva kuśalāt saṃkalpād dharmyāṃ kathāṃ kathayati / sāsya bhavati samyagvāk /
body.translated_text: If the mind turns to thoughts, one thinks such thoughts [as are wholesome]. If the mind turns to conversation, having right view as the governing [factor], from that very wholesome intention, one speaks <s>Dharma</s>-conversation. This becomes one's right speech (<s>samyagvāk</s>).

body.text: sacec cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārair arthī (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 232

children.text: ) bhavati, tatparyeṣaṇāṃ vāpadyate / so 'bhikramapratikrame saṃprajānadvihārī bhavaty ālokitavyavalokite, saṃmiñjitaprasārite sāṃghāṭīcīvarapātradhāraṇe 'śitapītakhāditāsvādite / vihāragato vā punaḥ paryeṣiteṣu cīvarādiṣu gate sthite niṣaṇṇe yāvan nidrāklamaprativinodane saṃprajānadvihārī bhavati / ayam asyocyate samyakkarmāntaḥ /
children.translated_text: or if one is engaged in their seeking — in stepping forward and stepping backward, one dwells with clear comprehension; in looking briefly and looking around, in bending and stretching, in wearing the outer robe, inner robe, and holding the bowl, in eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting. Or again, having returned to the monastery, in the sought robes and so forth, in going, standing, sitting, up to the dispelling of drowsiness and fatigue, one dwells with clear comprehension. This is called one's right action (<s>samyakkarmānta</s>).

body.translated_text: If one is in need of robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicine and requisites for the sick,

body.text: sa tac cīvaraṃ yāvad bhaiṣajyapariṣkāraṃ dharmeṇa paryeṣate / yāvan mithyājīvakarakadharmavivarjitaḥ / so 'sya bhavati samyagājīvaḥ /
body.translated_text: One seeks those robes, up to medicine and requisites, by righteous means — up to: one is free from the <s>dharmas</s> that constitute wrong livelihood. This is one's right livelihood (<s>samyagājīva</s>).

body.text: ye punar viratisaṃgṛhītāḥ samyagvākkarmāntājīvāḥ, te 'nena pūrvam eva manaskāralābhād bodhyaṅgair eva saha labdhā bhavanti /
body.translated_text: The right speech, right action, and right livelihood comprised in abstinence — these are obtained by him from the very first, at the time of attaining mental attention, together with the factors of awakening.

body.text: yo 'py āryakāntāni śīlāny ucyante / kena kāraṇena / dīrghakālaṃ hy etad āryāṇāṃ satāṃ samyaggatānām iṣṭaṃ kāntaṃ priyaṃ mana-āpaṃ "kaccid ahaṃ tad vāgduścaritasya kāyaduścaritasya mithyājīvasyākaraṇaṃ saṃvaraṃ pratilabheyam" / yad asya dīrgharātram iṣṭaṃ kāntaṃ priyaṃ mana-āpaṃ tad anena tasmin samaye pratilabdhaṃ bhavati / tasmād āryakāntam ity ucyate / tathā hi sa labdheṣv āryakānteṣu śīleṣu, na saṃprajāno mrṣāṃ vācaṃ bhāṣate, na saṃcintya prāṇinaṃ jīvitād vyaparopayati, nādattam ādatte, (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 234

children.text: ) na kāmeṣu mithyā carati, na cādharmeṇa cīvarādīni paryeṣate / iti tāny āryakāntāni śīlāny adhipatiṃ kṛtvā mārgabhāvanākāle yā vāk pravartate yac ca kāyakarma yaś cājīvaḥ, te 'pi samyagvākkarmāntājīvā ity ucyante /
children.translated_text: does not engage in sexual misconduct, and does not seek robes and so forth by unrighteous means. Thus, having the moral conduct beloved by the noble ones as the governing [factor], at the time of cultivating the path, the speech that proceeds, the bodily action, and the livelihood — these too are called right speech, right action, and right livelihood.

body.translated_text: These are also called the moral conduct beloved by the noble ones (<s>āryakānta śīla</s>). For what reason? For a long time, this has been desired, wanted, cherished, and agreeable to the noble ones, the true, the rightly-conducted: "May I indeed obtain the non-commission and restraint from that misconduct of speech, misconduct of body, and wrong livelihood." That which has long been desired, wanted, cherished, and agreeable — that is obtained by him at that time. Therefore it is called 'beloved by the noble ones.' For indeed, having obtained the moral conduct beloved by the noble ones, one does not knowingly speak falsehood, does not intentionally deprive a living being of life, does not take what is not given,

body.text:
tasya samyagdṛṣṭisamyaksaṃkalpavākkarmāntājīvasanniśrayeṇa bhāvanāprayuktasya yac chando vīryo vyāyāmo niṣkramaḥ parākramasthāmārambhaś cetasaḥ saṃpragrahaḥ sātatyam / ayam ucyate samyagvyāyāmaḥ /
yac catvāri smṛtyupasthānāny adhipatiṃ kṛtvāviparyāsasaṃgṛhītā smṛtir navākārā navākāracittasthitisaṃgrāhikā / iyam ucyate samyaksmṛtiḥ samyaksamādhiś ca //
body.translated_text: For one devoted to cultivation, relying on right view, right intention, right speech, right action, and right livelihood — whatever desire, vigor, effort, exertion, perseverance, strength, enterprise, and mental engagement, and continuity [there is] — this is called right effort (<s>samyagvyāyāma</s>). And whatever mindfulness, having the four foundations of mindfulness as the governing [factor], comprised in non-distortion, of nine aspects, gathering the nine-aspect stability of mind — this is called right mindfulness (<s>samyaksmṛti</s>) and right concentration (<s>samyaksamādhi</s>).

body.text:
-II-12-b-(6)-ii Ms.92a4L, Sh.330-1, P.148a7, D.120b6, N.127b5, Co.125a3, Ch.445b16
tad etat sarvam abhisamasyāryāṣṭāṅgo mārgaś cārakaraṇīye ca vihārakaraṇīye cāvasthitaḥ / tatra samyagvākkarmāntājīvāś cārakaraṇīye / vihārakaraṇīyaṃ punar dvividham / śamatho vipaśyanā ca / tatra yā ca samyagdṛṣṭiḥ, yaś ca samyaksaṃkalpaḥ, yaś ca samyagvyāyāma iyaṃ vipaśyanā / tatra yā ca samyaksmṛtir yaś ca samyaksamādhir ayaṃ śamathaḥ /
body.translated_text: -II-12-b-(6)-ii — All of this, taken together, shows that the noble eightfold path is established both in the domain of conduct and in the domain of dwelling. Therein, right speech, right action, and right livelihood are in the domain of conduct. The domain of dwelling is twofold: <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight). Therein, right view, right intention, and right effort — this is <s>vipaśyanā</s>. Right mindfulness and right concentration — this is <s>śamatha</s>.

body.text: evaṃ pariśuddhān vākkarmāntājīvān niśritya śamathavipaśyanāṃ bhāvayati kālena kālaṃ niravaśeṣasaṃyojanaprahāṇaṃ sākṣātkaroty agraphalam arhattvaṃ (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 236

children.text: ) prāpnoti / prākarṣikaś ca bhāvanāmārgaḥ kālāntarābhyāsena kleśān prajahāti / jñānamātrapratibaddhas tu darśanamārgo jñānotpattimātrakeṇa kleśān prajahāti / anena kāraṇena vākkarmāntājīvā bhāvanāmārge vyavasthāpitāḥ /
children.translated_text: ). The cultivation path is gradual and abandons afflictions through practice over a period of time. But the path of seeing, dependent merely on knowledge, abandons afflictions merely through the arising of knowledge. For this reason, speech, action, and livelihood have been established in the cultivation path.

body.translated_text: Thus, relying on purified speech, action, and livelihood, one cultivates <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s>, and from time to time directly realizes the abandonment of all fetters without remainder, and attains the final fruit, <s>arhatship</s>

body.text: iti ya evam eṣām anayānupūrvyā saptatriṃśatāṃ bodhipakṣyāṇāṃ dharmāṇām abhyāsaḥ paricayaḥ / iyam ucyate bodhipakṣyā bhāvanā //
body.translated_text: Thus, whoever practices the thirty-seven <s>dharmas</s> conducive to awakening in this manner and in this sequence — this is called the cultivation of the factors conducive to awakening.

body.text:
(II)-A-II-13-a Ms.92a7M, Sh.331-1, W.M02-4, P.148b5, D.121a5, N.128a4, Co,125b1, Ch.445b29
tatra bhāvanāphalaṃ katamat / āha / catvāri śrāmaṇyaphalāni / srota-āpattiphalaṃ sakṛdāgāmiphalam anāgāmiphalam agraphalam arhattvam /
body.translated_text: (II)-A-II-13-a — Therein, what is the fruit of cultivation? It is said: The four fruits of the ascetic life — the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>), the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>), the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>), and the final fruit, <s>arhatship</s> (<s>arhattvaphala</s>).

body.text: tatra katamac chrāmaṇyam, katamat phalam / āha / mārgaḥ, kleśaprahāṇaṃ phalam / api ca pūrvotpannasya mārgasya paścād utpanno mārgaḥ phalaṃ madhyo viśiṣṭo vā sadṛśo vā / punas tatra kena kāraṇena catvāri vyavasthāpitāni / āha / caturvidhakleśaprahāṇapratipakṣatayā //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the ascetic life and what is the fruit? It is said: The path is the ascetic life; the abandonment of afflictions is the fruit. Moreover, a path that arises subsequently to a previously arisen path is its fruit — whether middling, distinguished, or equal. Furthermore, for what reason are four [fruits] established? It is said: By virtue of being antidotes to the fourfold abandonment of afflictions.

body.text:
-II-13-a-(1) Ms.92b1R, Sh.332-3, P.148b7, D.121a7, N.128a6, Co.125b3, Ch.445c5
tadyathā nirvastukānāṃ kleśānām apāyagamanīyānām apāyagamanahetubhūtānāṃ prahāṇāt pratipakṣotpādāc ca srota-āpattiphalaṃ vyavasthāpitam / trayāṇāṃ tu saṃyojanānāṃ prahāṇād vyavasthāpitaṃ bhagavatā triṣu pakṣeṣu, gṛhipakṣe, durākhyātadharmavinayapakṣe svākhyātadharmavinayapakṣe ca, trayāṇāṃ saṃyojanānāṃ mārgotpattaye vibandhakaratvāt /
body.translated_text: -II-13-a-(1) — Namely, from the abandonment of afflictions that have no substantial basis, that lead to the lower realms, that serve as causes for going to the lower realms — and from the arising of the antidote — the fruit of stream-entry is established. From the abandonment of the three fetters it has been established by the <s>Bhagavat</s> in three contexts: the context of householders, the context of a badly proclaimed doctrine and discipline, and the context of a well-proclaimed doctrine and discipline — because the three fetters obstruct the arising of the path in [these three contexts].

body.text: tatra gṛhipakṣe satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ, yayāyam ādita eva na prayujyata ity ādita uttrāsikā satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, in the context of householders, the view of the transient collection (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), by which one does not engage [in the path] from the very start — this is the initially frightening view of the transient collection.

body.text: durākhyāte dharmavinaye śīlavrataparāmarśaḥ, uccalito 'pi mithyāṃ pratipādayati yenāryamārgo notpadyate /
body.translated_text: In a badly proclaimed doctrine and discipline, the grasping at moral conduct and vows (<s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>), by which even one who has been stirred [to practice] proceeds wrongly, so that the noble path does not arise.

body.text: svākhyāte dharmavinaye vicikitsā, tatroccalitaś ca bhavati, na ca mithyāpratipanno 'pi tv anabhyāsāt tasya yāvad yathābhūtadarśanaṃ na bhavati jñeye vastuni tāvat kāṅkṣā vimatayo vibandhakarā bhavanti (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 240
the arising of the path.

body.translated_text: In a well-proclaimed doctrine and discipline, doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>), for even one who has been stirred [to practice] and has not gone wrong, but due to lack of practice, as long as the seeing of the knowable object as it truly is has not occurred, there remain hesitation and uncertainty that obstruct

body.text: anena tāvat kāraṇena srota-āpattiphalavyavasthānam //
body.translated_text: By this reasoning, then, the establishment of the fruit of stream-entry is [made].

body.text:
-II-13-a-(2) Ms. 92b4R, Sh.333-1, P.149a5, D.121b5, N.128b4, Co.126a1, Ch.445c17
tasyāsya srota-āpannasya paraṃ sapta bhavā avaśiṣṭā bhavanti / sa cāsya janmaprabandho yadā ca janmaprābandhikān kleśān prajahāti devabhavasaṃgṛhītān manuṣyabhavasaṃgṛhītāṃś ca, yeṣāṃ prahāṇāt param ekaṃ devabhavam abhinirvartayaty ekaṃ manuṣyabhavam / tasmin samaye sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ vyavasthāpyate //
body.translated_text: -II-13-a-(2) — For this stream-enterer, at most seven existences remain. And when one abandons the afflictions belonging to the continuum of births — those included in divine existence and those included in human existence — through whose abandonment one generates only one more divine existence and one more human existence, at that time the fruit of once-returning is established.

body.text:
-II-13-a-(3) Ms.92b5R, Sh.333-7, P.149a7, D.121b6, N.128b5, Co.126a2, Ch.445c21
yadā tu devabhavam eva kevalam abhinirvartayati, ihapratyāgamajanmikaṃ kleśaṃ prahāya, tadānāgāmiphalaṃ vyavasthāpyate //
body.translated_text: -II-13-a-(3) — But when one generates only a divine existence, having abandoned the afflictions connected with return to this [human] world, at that time the fruit of non-returning is established.

body.text:
-II-13-a-(4) Ms.92b6L, Sh.333-9, P.149a7, D.121b7, N.128b6, Co.126a3, Ch.445c23
sarvabhavopapattisaṃvartanīyakleśaprahāṇād agraphalam arhattvaphalaṃ vyavasthāpyate //
body.translated_text: -II-13-a-(4) — From the abandonment of all afflictions that lead to rebirth in any existence, the final fruit, the fruit of <s>arhatship</s>, is established.

body.text:
-II-13-a-(5) Ms.92b6L, Sh.334-1, P.149a7, D.121b7, N.128b6, Co.126a3, Ch.445c24
tat punaḥ sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ trayāṇām saṃyojanānāṃ prahāṇād rāgadveṣamohānāṃ ca tanutvād bhagavatā vyavasthāpitam, pañcānām avarabhāgīyānāṃ saṃyojanānāṃ prahāṇād anāgāmiphalam, paryādāya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhattvaphalam / idam ucyate bhāvanāphalam //
body.translated_text: -II-13-a-(5) — Furthermore, the fruit of once-returning has been established by the <s>Bhagavat</s> through the abandonment of the three fetters and the attenuation of passion, aversion, and delusion; the fruit of non-returning through the abandonment of the five lower fetters; and the fruit of <s>arhatship</s> through the complete and exhaustive abandonment of all afflictions. This is called the fruit of cultivation.

body.text:
-II-13-b Ms.92b7L, Sh.334-6, P.149b2, D.122a2, N.129a1, Co.126a5, Ch.445c28
tatra ye rāgadveṣamohamānavitarkacariteṣu pudgaleṣu pūrvaṃ tāvac (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 242

children.text: ) caritaviśodhana ālambane caritaṃ viśodhayitavyaṃ tataḥ paścāc cittasthitim adhigacchanti / teṣāṃ pratiniyatam eva tad ālambanam avaśyaṃ tais tenālambanena prayoktavyam /
children.translated_text: the conduct should be purified through the object for purifying conduct, and then afterward they attain mental stability. For them, that particular object is definitely [required]; they must necessarily practice with that object.

body.translated_text: -II-13-b — Therein, for persons of passionate, hateful, deluded, conceited, and discursive temperament, first

body.text: samabhāgacaritasya tu yatra priyārohitā tatra tena prayoktavyaṃ kevalaṃ cittasthitaye, na tu caritaviśuddhaye / yathā samabhāgacarita evaṃ mandarajasko veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: But for a person of balanced temperament, one should practice wherever there is delight, solely for mental stability, not for the purification of conduct. As with a person of balanced temperament, so should one of mild defilements be understood.

body.text: ayaṃ tv eṣāṃ viśeṣḥ / rāgādicaritaḥ prayujyamānaś cireṇādhigantā bhavati, samabhāgacarito nāticireṇa, mandarajaskas tv āśu tvaritatvaritaṃ cittasthitim adhigacchati //
body.translated_text: But this is the distinction among them: one of passionate and other temperaments, when practicing, attains [stability] after a long time; one of balanced temperament, not too long; but one of mild defilements attains mental stability quickly and swiftly.

body.text:
-II-13-b-(1) Ms.93a2L, Sh.334-16, P.149b6, D.122a6, N.129a5, Co.126b1, Ch.446a8
tatroktāni pūrvaṃ rāgādicaritānāṃ pudgalānāṃ liṅgāni / samabhāgacaritasya pudgalasya mandarajaskasya ca katamāni liṅgāni / āha / samabhāgacaritasya pudgalasya sarvāṇi tāni liṅgāni saṃvidyante yāni rāgādicaritānām, tāni rāgādīni tu nādhimātrāṇi na pradhānāni yathā rāgādicaritānām / samaprāptāni tāni bhavanti, pratyayeṣu satsu prajñāyante //
body.translated_text: -II-13-b-(1) — Therein, the marks of persons of passionate and other temperaments have been previously stated. What are the marks of a person of balanced temperament and of one with mild defilements? It is said: For a person of balanced temperament, all those marks that belong to those of passionate and other temperaments are present, but those passions and so forth are not intense or predominant as they are for those of passionate and other temperaments. They are equally present and manifest when conditions are present.

body.text:
-II-13-b-(2) Ms.93a3L, Sh.335-2, P.149b8, D.122a7, N.129a7, Co.126b3, Ch.446a13
tatra mandarajaskasya pudgalasya liṅgāni / anāvṛto bhavaty ādiśuddhasaṃbhārasaṃbhṛtaḥ / prasādabahulo medhāvī puṇyavān guṇānvitaś ca bhavati //
body.translated_text: -II-13-b-(2) — Therein, the marks of a person with mild defilements: one is unobstructed, endowed with initially pure provisions; one is abundant in faith, intelligent, meritorious, and endowed with good qualities.

body.text:
-II-13-b-(2)-i Ms.93a3M, Sh.335-5, W.*102-18, P.150a1, D.122b1, N.129b1, Co.126b4, Ch.446a16
tatra trīṇy āvaraṇāni karmāvaraṇaṃ kleśāvaraṇaṃ vipākāvaraṇam /
body.translated_text: -II-13-b-(2)-i — Therein, there are three obstacles: the obstacle of <s>karma</s> (action), the obstacle of afflictions, and the obstacle of karmic ripening.

body.text: tatra karmāvaraṇaṃ pañcānantaryāṇi karmāṇi / yac cānyad api kiṃcit karma saṃcetanīyaṃ gurukarma vipakvavipākaṃ mārgotpattaye nibandhakārakam /
body.translated_text: Therein, the obstacle of <s>karma</s> consists of the five actions of immediate retribution, and whatever other intentional, weighty <s>karma</s> whose result has ripened and which obstructs the arising of the path.

body.text: tatra kleśāvaraṇaṃ tīvrakleśatāyatakleśatā ca / yā dṛṣṭe dharme caritaviśodhanenālambanaviśodhanena na śakyate viśodhayitum /
body.translated_text: Therein, the obstacle of afflictions consists of intense affliction and prolonged affliction, which cannot be purified in this very life by means of purifying conduct through the object or by purifying the object.

body.text: tatra vipākāvaraṇaṃ yatrāryamārgasyāpravṛttir apracāra upapattyāyatane, tatra vā vipākam abhinirvartayati / yatra vāryamārgasya pravṛttiḥ pracāraḥ, tatropapanno jaḍo bhavaty eḍamūko hastasaṃvācikaḥ, apratibalo bhavati subhāṣitadurbhāṣitānāṃ dharmāṇām artham ājñātum //
body.translated_text: Therein, the obstacle of karmic ripening: one generates a karmic result in a realm of rebirth where the noble path does not function or operate; or, having been reborn where the noble path does function and operate, one is dull, mute, one who communicates only by hand-gestures, and incapable of understanding the meaning of well-spoken and ill-spoken <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text:
-II-13-b-(2)-ii Ms.93a5M, Sh.335-17, P.150a5, D.122b5, N.129a4, Co.126b7, Ch.446a27
tatrādiśuddhiḥ śīlaṃ ca suviśuddhaṃ dṛṣṭiś ca ṛjvī /
body.translated_text: -II-13-b-(2)-ii — Therein, initial purity [means] moral conduct that is well-purified and views that are straight.

body.text: tatra śīlaṃ suviśuddhaṃ daśabhiḥ kāraṇair veditavyam /
body.translated_text: Therein, moral conduct is well-purified — this should be understood by ten causes.

body.text: tatra dṛṣṭyṛjutā, śraddhāṃ saṃprayogāt, adhimuktisaṃprayogāt, vigatamāyāśāṭhyatayā, sucintitadharmārthasya niḥkāṅkṣānirvicikitsāprayoganiryāṇatayā / (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 246

body.translated_text: Therein, straightness of views — through being associated with faith, through being associated with conviction, through being free from deception and guile, and through having well-reflected on the meaning of <s>dharmas</s> with freedom from doubt, freedom from uncertainty, and progress toward deliverance.

body.text: yā dṛṣṭiḥ śraddhayā saṃprayuktā, asmād dharmavinayād asaṃhāryā bhavati /
body.translated_text: A view that is associated with faith is unshakeable from this doctrine and discipline.

body.text: adhimuktyā ca saṃprayuktā, buddhānāṃ buddhaśrāvakāṇāṃ ca, acintyam anubhāvam, acintyāni copapattyāyatanāni, gambhīrāṃ ca deśanām, avyākṛtavastu cādhimucyate, nottrasati, na saṃtrāsam āpadyate /
body.translated_text: Associated with conviction — one is convinced of, and does not become fearful or terrified by, the inconceivable power of the <s>Buddhas</s> and the disciples of the <s>Buddha</s>, the inconceivable realms of rebirth, the profound teaching, and the undetermined matters.

body.text: vigatamāyāśāṭhyā ca yā dṛṣṭiḥ, yayā ṛjuko bhavati / ṛjukajātīyo yathānuśiṣṭaś ca pratipadyate, yathābhūtaṃ cātmānam āviṣkaroti /
body.translated_text: A view that is free from deception and guile — by which one is straightforward, of a straightforward nature, and one practices as instructed, and reveals oneself as one truly is.

body.text: dharmāṇāṃ vānityatām ārabhya duḥkhatāṃ śūnyatām anātmatām arthaḥ suvicintito bhavati sutulitaḥ sūpaparīkṣitaḥ, yaddhetor ayaṃ niḥkāṅkṣo bhavati nirvicikitsaḥ, dvedhāpathāpagato viśeṣāya paraiti /
body.translated_text: The meaning of <s>dharmas</s> regarding impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self has been well-reflected upon, well-weighed, well-examined — on account of which one is free from doubt, free from uncertainty, has departed from the fork in the road, and progresses toward distinction.

body.text: itīyaṃ caturākārā dṛṣṭir yathoddiṣṭā dṛṣṭyṛjutety ucyate //
body.translated_text: Thus this fourfold view, as described, is called straightness of views.

body.text:
-II-13-b-(2)-iii Ms.93a8M, Sh.336-19, P.150b3, D.123a3, N.130a3, Co.127a5, Ch.446b12
tatra saṃbhārasaṃbhṛtatā, vistareṇa saṃbhāraḥ pūrvam eva nirdiṣṭaḥ / samāsataḥ punaś caturvidho bhavati / puṇyasaṃbhāro jñānasaṃbhāraḥ pūrvako dṛṣṭadhārmikaś ca /
body.translated_text: -II-13-b-(2)-iii — Therein, being endowed with provisions: the provisions have previously been described in detail. In summary, they are fourfold: the provision of merit, the provision of knowledge, the prior [provision], and the provision pertaining to the present life.

body.text: tatra puṇyasaṃbhāro yenāpy etarhy ānulomikāḥ pariṣkārāḥ pracurā bhavanti pradakṣiṇāḥ, kalyāṇamitrāṇi ca pratilabhate, anantarāyaś ca prayuktasya bhavati /
body.translated_text: Therein, the provision of merit — by which even now the favorable circumstances are abundant and auspicious, one obtains spiritual friends, and when one practices, there are no obstacles.

body.text: tatra jñānasaṃbhāro yena medhāvī bhavati, pratibalaḥ subhāṣitadurbhāṣitānāṃ (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 248

children.text: ) dharmāṇām artham ājñātum, lābhī bhavaty ānulomikāyā dharmadeśanāyāḥ, arthadeśanāyāḥ, avavādānuśāsanyāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>dharmas</s>, and one obtains concordant teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, teaching of the meaning, and instruction and admonition.

body.translated_text: Therein, the provision of knowledge — by which one is intelligent, capable of understanding the meaning of well-spoken and ill-spoken

body.text: tatra pūrvako yenaitarhi paripakvānīndriyāṇi labhate pūrvakuśalamūlopacayāt /
body.translated_text: Therein, the prior [provision] — by which one now obtains ripened faculties through the accumulation of prior wholesome roots.

body.text: tatra dṛṣṭadhārmikas tadyathā kuśalo dharmacchandaḥ, tathā paripakvendriyasya śīlasaṃvara indriyasaṃvara iti vistareṇa pūrvavat //
body.translated_text: Therein, the provision pertaining to the present life — such as the wholesome desire for the <s>Dharma</s>; and for one whose faculties are ripened, the moral restraint, the sense-restraint — and so on in detail as before.

body.text:
-II-13-b-(2)-iv Ms.93b2R, Sh.337-14, P.150b8, D.123a6, N.130a7, Co.127b2, Ch.446b22
tatra prasādabahulatā, na śāstari kāṅkṣati na vicikitsati prasīdaty adhimucyate, yathā śāstary evaṃ dharme śikṣāyām / iti vistareṇa pūrvavat //
body.translated_text: -II-13-b-(2)-iv — Therein, abundance of faith: one does not doubt or waver regarding the Teacher, one has faith and is convinced — as regarding the Teacher, so regarding the <s>Dharma</s> and the training — and so on in detail as before.

body.text:
-II-13-b-(2)-v Ms.93b3M, Sh.337-17, P.151a1, D.123a7, N.130b1, Co.127b3, Ch.446b25
tatra medhā yayāśu dharmam udgṛhṇāti, cireṇa dharmam arthaṃ ca na vismārayati, āśu dharmam arthaṃ ca pratividhyati //
body.translated_text: -II-13-b-(2)-v — Therein, intelligence (<s>medhā</s>): by which one quickly grasps the <s>Dharma</s>, does not forget the <s>Dharma</s> and its meaning for a long time, and quickly penetrates the <s>Dharma</s> and its meaning.

body.text:
-II-13-b-(2)-vi Ms.93b3R, Sh.338-1, P.151a2, D.123b1, N.130b1, Co.127b4, Ch.446b27
tatra kṛtapuṇyatā yayābhirūpo bhavati darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko dīrghāyur bhavati, ādeyavākyo maheśākhyo jñāto bhavati mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarādīnām, satkṛto gurukṛtaś ca rājādīnām //
body.translated_text: -II-13-b-(2)-vi — Therein, meritoriousness: by which one is handsome, attractive, inspiring confidence, long-lived, of persuasive speech, well-known, renowned as greatly meritorious, a recipient of robes and so forth, and honored and respected by kings and others.

body.text:
-II-13-b-(2)-vii Ms.93b4M, Sh.338-5, W.102-26, P.151a4, D.123b2, N.130b3, Co.127b5, Ch.446c2
tatra guṇānvita iti guṇā alpecchatādayo veditavyāḥ, yathoktāḥ śramaṇālaṃkāre, tair ayaṃ prakṛtyaiva samanvāgato bhavati /
body.translated_text: Therein, 'endowed with qualities' — the qualities should be understood as fewness of desires and so forth, as stated in the [section on] the ornament of the ascetic. He is by nature endowed with those.

body.text: itīmāny evaṃbhāgīyāni mandarajaskasya pudgalasya liṅgāni veditavyāni //
body.translated_text: These and similar are to be understood as the marks of a person with little dust [of defilements]. //

body.text:
(II)-A-II-14-a Ms.93b5L, Sh.338-9, W.*103-1, P.151a5, D.123b3, N.130b4, Co.127b6, Ch.446c6
tatra ṣaṭ pudgalaparyāyāḥ / katame ṣaṭ / tadyathā śramaṇo brāhmaṇo brahmacārī bhikṣur yatiḥ pravrajitaś ceti //
body.translated_text: Therein, there are six synonymous designations of persons (<s>pudgalaparyāya</s>). What six? Namely: <s>śramaṇa</s> (ascetic), <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate), <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk), <s>yati</s> (striver), and <s>pravrajita</s> (one gone forth). //

body.text:
-II-14-a-(1) Ms.93b5M, Sh.338-11, W.*103-7, P.151a6, D.123b4, N.130b5, Co.127b7, Ch.446c8
tatra catvāraḥ śramaṇāḥ / mārgajinaḥ, mārgadeśikaḥ, mārgajīvī, mārgadūṣī ca /
body.translated_text: Therein, there are four kinds of <s>śramaṇas</s>: the path-conqueror (<s>mārgajina</s>), the path-guide (<s>mārgadeśika</s>), the path-liver (<s>mārgajīvin</s>), and the path-corrupter (<s>mārgadūṣin</s>).

body.text: tatra yaḥ sugataḥ sa mārgajinaḥ, yo dharmavādī sa mārgadeśikaḥ, yaḥ supratipannaḥ sa mārgajīvī, yo mithyāpratipannaḥ sa mārgadūṣī /
body.translated_text: Therein, one who has gone well (<s>sugata</s>) is the path-conqueror. One who teaches the <s>Dharma</s> is the path-guide. One who practices well is the path-liver. One who practices wrongly is the path-corrupter.

body.text: sugataś cocyate yo 'śeṣaṃ rāgadveṣamohakṣayam anuprāptaḥ / dharmavādī yo rāgadveṣamohavinayāya dharmaṃ deśayati / supratipanno yo rāgadveṣamohavinayāya pratipannaḥ / duḥśīlapāpadharmā mithyāpratipannaḥ /
body.translated_text: The Well-Gone (<s>Sugata</s>) is one who has attained the complete destruction of passion, aversion, and delusion. A teacher of the <s>Dharma</s> is one who teaches the <s>Dharma</s> for the taming of passion, aversion, and delusion.
