One who practices well is one who is engaged in practice for the taming of passion, aversion, and delusion. One of bad moral conduct and evil <s>dharmas</s> is a wrong practitioner.

body.text: api ca śaikṣāśaikṣā mārgajinā ity ucyante, darśanabhāvanāprahātavyānāṃ kleśānāṃ vijayāt /
body.translated_text: Moreover, learners (<s>śaikṣa</s>) and those beyond learning (<s>aśaikṣa</s>) are called path-conquerors, because of their victory over the afflictions to be abandoned by seeing and by cultivation.

body.text: tatra tathāgato bodhisattvāś cāyatyāṃ bodhāya pratipannāḥ / śrāvakāś ca sūtradharā vinayadharā mātṛkādharāś ca, ye sāṃketikaṃ dharmavinayaṃ dhārayanti, dharmanetrīṃ pravartayanti / ima ucyante mārgadeśikāḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, the <s>Tathāgata</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s> who are engaged in practice for future awakening, and <s>śrāvakas</s> who hold the <s>sūtras</s>, who hold the <s>Vinaya</s>, and who hold the <s>Mātṛkā</s> (Abhidharma) — who maintain the conventional <s>Dharma</s>-<s>Vinaya</s> and set in motion the guides of the <s>Dharma</s> — these are called path-guides.

body.text: tatra ye pṛthagjanakalyāṇakā ātmahitāya pratipannā lajjināḥ kaukṛtikāḥ śikṣākāmāḥ / aprāptasya prāptaye, anadhigatasyādhigamāya, asākṣātkṛtasya sākṣātkriyāyai prayuktā, bhavyāś ca pratibalā yāvad asākṣātkṛtasya (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 252
) experienced — these are called path-livers.

body.translated_text: Therein, those ordinary persons who are virtuous (<s>pṛthagjanakalyāṇaka</s>), who are engaged in practice for their own benefit, who are conscientious, who feel remorse, who desire the training, who are engaged for the attainment of what has not been attained, for the realization of what has not been realized, for the direct experience of what has not been directly experienced, who are capable and competent up to the direct experience of what has not been directly

body.text: apy eṣām ūṣmā yenema āryasya prajñendriyasyotpattaye na mṛtā jīvantīty ucyante / tenocyante mārgajīvina iti /
body.translated_text: Moreover, the warmth by which they, for the arising of the noble faculty of wisdom (<s>prajñendriya</s>), are not dead but living — therefore they are called path-livers.

body.text: tatra yo 'yaṃ pudgalo duḥśīlaḥ pāpadharmā yāvad abrahmacārī brahmacāripratijñaḥ / ayam ucyate mārgadūṣī / dūṣito 'nena mārgo bhavati mūlata āditaḥ / yenāyam abhavyo bhavaty apratibalaḥ, abhājanabhūto mārgasyotpattaye, satyāṃ saṃvidyamānāyāṃ mārgadeśanāyāṃ sati saṃvidyamāne 'dhigame / tasmān mārgadūṣīty ucyate /
body.translated_text: Therein, whatever person is of bad moral conduct and evil <s>dharmas</s>, and so on up to: one who is not celibate while professing celibacy — this one is called a path-corrupter. The path has been corrupted by him from the root, from the beginning. By which he becomes incapable, incompetent, unfit for the arising of the path, even when the path-teaching exists and is present, even when realization exists and is present. Therefore he is called a path-corrupter.

body.text: idaṃ ca saṃdhāyoktaṃ bhagavatā / iha prathamaḥ śramaṇaḥ, iha yāvac caturthaḥ, śūnyāḥ parapravādāḥ śramaṇair brāhmaṇaiś ca / yatrāryāṣṭāṅgo mārgaḥ prajñāyate tatra prathamaśramaṇas tatra yāvac caturtha iti //
body.translated_text: And it is with reference to this that the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said: 'Here is the first <s>śramaṇa</s>, here up to the fourth. Other doctrines are empty of <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>. Wherever the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅga mārga</s>) is discerned, there is the first <s>śramaṇa</s>, there up to the fourth.' //

body.text:
-II-14-a-(2) Ms. 94a2R, Sh.340-6, W. 103-20, P.152a2, D.124a7, N.131b1, Co.128b3, Ch.447a6
tatra trayo brāhmaṇāḥ / tadyathā jātibrāhmaṇaḥ, saṃjñābrāhmaṇaḥ, pratipattibrāhmaṇaś ca /
body.translated_text: Therein, there are three kinds of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>: namely, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> by birth (<s>jātibrāhmaṇa</s>), a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> by designation (<s>saṃjñābrāhmaṇa</s>), and a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> by practice (<s>pratipattibrāhmaṇa</s>).

body.text: tatra jātibrāhmaṇaḥ, yo 'yaṃ brāhmaṇakule jāto yonijo mātṛsaṃbhūtaḥ, upeto mātṛtaḥ pitṛtaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> by birth is one who is born in a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> family, born from the womb, produced by the mother, descended from both mother and father.

body.text: tatra saṃjñābrāhmaṇa iti loke nāma bhavati saṃjñā samajñā prajñaptir vyavahāraḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> by designation is one who has in the world a name, a designation, a common designation, an appellation, a conventional usage.

body.text: tatra pratipattibrāhmaṇaḥ, yo 'tyantaniṣṭho bhavati kṛtārthaḥ / vāhitā bhavanty anena pāpakā akuśalā dharmāḥ / yathoktaṃ na kāryaṃ brāhmaṇasyāsti kṛtārtho brāhmaṇaḥ smṛta iti //
body.translated_text: Therein, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> by practice is one who has reached the absolute culmination, who has accomplished his purpose. Evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> have been washed away by him. As it is said: 'A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> has nothing to be done; a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is remembered as one whose purpose is accomplished.' //

body.text:
-II-14-a-(3) Ms.94a4M, Sh,341-3, P.152a4, D.124b2, N.131b3, Co.128b5, Ch.447a13
tatra trayo brahmacāriṇaḥ / tadyathā viratisamādāyī tadantaraprahāyī tadatyantaprahāyī ca /
body.translated_text: Therein, there are three kinds of <s>brahmacārins</s> (celibates): namely, one who undertakes abstinence (<s>viratisamādāyin</s>), one who abandons [sensuality] temporarily (<s>tadantaraprahāyin</s>), and one who abandons it definitively (<s>tadatyantaprahāyin</s>).

body.text: tatra viratisamādāyī, yo brahmacaryād maithunadharmāt prativirato bhavati samādattaśikṣaḥ / tatra tadantaraprahāyī, yo laukikena mārgeṇa kāmavītarāgaḥ pṛthagjanaḥ / tatra tadatyantaprahāyī, tadyathānāgāmī, arhan vā punaḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, one who undertakes abstinence is one who refrains from the sexual act in the holy life, having undertaken the training. Therein, one who abandons temporarily is an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) who has attained dispassion from sensual desires through the worldly path. Therein, one who abandons definitively is a non-returner (<s>anāgāmin</s>) or an <s>arhat</s>. //

body.text:
-II-14-a-(4) Ms.94a5L, Sh.341-10, P.152a7, D.124b4, N.131b6, Co.128b7, Ch.447a19
tatra pañca bhikṣavaḥ / bhikṣatīti bhikṣuḥ, pratijñābhikṣuḥ, saṃjñābhikṣuḥ, bhinnakleśatvād bhikṣuḥ, jñapticaturthena karmaṇopasaṃpādito bhikṣuḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, there are five kinds of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks): a <s>bhikṣu</s> because he begs (<s>bhikṣati</s>), a <s>bhikṣu</s> by profession, a <s>bhikṣu</s> by designation, a <s>bhikṣu</s> because his afflictions are broken, and a <s>bhikṣu</s> who has been ordained by a formal act with a fourth motion. //

body.text:
-II-14-a-(5) Ms.94a5R, Sh.341-13, P.152a8, D.124b5, N.131b7, Co.129a1, Ch.447a21
tatra trayo yatayaḥ / dauḥśīlyasaṃyamād yatiḥ, yo 'kuśalāt kāyavākkarmaṇaḥ prativirataḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, there are three kinds of <s>yatis</s> (strivers): a <s>yati</s> through restraint from bad moral conduct — one who refrains from unwholesome bodily and verbal action.

body.text: viṣayasaṃyamād yatiḥ, ya indriyair guptadvāraḥ, ārakṣitasmṛtir nipakasmṛtir vistareṇa pūrvavat /
body.translated_text: A <s>yati</s> through restraint of sense objects — one who has guarded doors of the sense faculties, with guarded mindfulness, with vigilant mindfulness — in detail as before.

body.text: kleśasaṃyamād yatiḥ, yasya darśanabhāvanāprahātavyāḥ kleśāḥ prahīṇāḥ, (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 256

children.text: ) utpannotpannaṃ ca chandavitarkaṃ vyāpādavihiṃsāvitarkam, abhidhyāvyāpādamithyādṛṣṭikrodhopanāhamrakṣapradāśādīny āpāyikāni sthānāni nairayikāṇi durgatigāmīny aśramaṇakārakāṇy utpannotpannāni, nādhivāsayati prajahāti vinodayati vyantīkaroti / so 'yaṃ dvividhaḥ kleśasaṃyamo bhavati / paryavasthānasaṃyamaḥ, anuśayasaṃyamaś ca //
children.translated_text: ) and whatever arisen desires and thoughts, ill-will and thoughts of harm, covetousness, ill-will, wrong view, anger, grudge, concealment, spite, and similar states leading to the lower realms, hellish, leading to evil destinies, destructive of the ascetic life — whatever has arisen, one does not tolerate, one abandons, removes, and eliminates it. This restraint of afflictions is twofold: restraint of active afflictions (<s>paryavasthānasaṃyama</s>) and restraint of latent tendencies (<s>anuśayasaṃyama</s>). //

body.translated_text: A <s>yati</s> through restraint of afflictions — one whose afflictions to be abandoned by seeing and by cultivation have been abandoned,

body.text:
-II-14-a-(6) Ms.94a7M, Sh.342-2, P.152b5, D.125a3, N.132a4, Co.129a6, Ch.447b2
tatra dvau pravrajitau / svākhyātadharmavinayo durākhyātadharmavinayaś ca /
body.translated_text: Therein, there are two kinds of those gone forth (<s>pravrajita</s>): one in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s>-<s>Vinaya</s> and one in a poorly proclaimed <s>dharma</s>-<s>vinaya</s>.

body.text: tatra svākhyātadharmavinayaḥ / bhikṣubhikṣuṇī śikṣamāṇā śrāmaṇeraśrāmaṇerī, api ca pravrājayaty ātmanaḥ pāpakān akuśalān dharmān, sa pravrajita ity ucyate paramārthataḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s>-<s>Vinaya</s>: a <s>bhikṣu</s>, <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, <s>śikṣamāṇā</s>, <s>śrāmaṇera</s>, and <s>śrāmaṇerī</s>. Moreover, one who drives out one's own evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> — that one is called 'gone forth' in the ultimate sense.

body.text: tatra durākhyātadharmavinayaḥ / tadyathā tīrthikaparivrājo nirgrantho vā parivrājakaḥ pāṇḍuraka iti, yo vā punar anyo 'py evaṃbhāgīyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, in the poorly proclaimed <s>dharma</s>-<s>vinaya</s>: namely, a non-Buddhist wandering ascetic (<s>tīrthikaparivrājaka</s>), or a <s>Nirgrantha</s> (Jain) wanderer, or a <s>Pāṇḍuraka</s>, or any other of this kind.

body.text: tenāha śramaṇo brāhmaṇo brahmacārī bhikṣur yatiḥ pravrajita iti pudgalaparyāyāḥ //
body.translated_text: Therefore he has said: <s>śramaṇa</s>, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>brahmacārin</s>, <s>bhikṣu</s>, <s>yati</s>, and <s>pravrajita</s> — these are the synonymous designations of persons. //

body.text:
-II-14-b Ms.94a9L, Sh.342-11, W.*104-33, P.153a1, D.125a6, N.132b1, Co.129b2, Ch.447b13
tatrāṣṭau pudgalāḥ / catvāri pudgalavyavasthānanidānāni /
body.translated_text: Therein, there are eight persons. And four grounds for the determination of persons.

body.text: katame 'ṣṭau pudgalāḥ / tadyathā samartho 'samarthaḥ / upāyajño 'nupāyajñaḥ / sātatiko 'sātatikaḥ / kṛtaparicayo 'kṛtaparicayaś ceti /
body.translated_text: What are the eight persons? Namely: capable (<s>samartha</s>) and incapable (<s>asamartha</s>); skilled in means (<s>upāyajña</s>) and unskilled in means (<s>anupāyajña</s>); persistent (<s>sātatika</s>) and non-persistent (<s>asātatika</s>); experienced (<s>kṛtaparicaya</s>) and inexperienced (<s>akṛtaparicaya</s>).

body.text: tatra catvāri pudgalavyavasthānanidānāni, eṣām evāṣṭānāṃ pudgalānāṃ vyavasthānāya catvāri prabhedanidānāni bhavanti / tadyathendriyaprabhedaḥ paripakvendriyo 'paripakvendriyaś ca / yogaprabhedo yogajño 'yogajñaś ca / prayogabhedaḥ sātatyasatkṛtya na sātatyasatkṛtya prayuktaś ca / kālaprabhedo dīrghakālabhāvitamārgo na dīrghakālabhāvitamārgaś ca /
body.translated_text: Therein, the four grounds for the determination of persons — for the determination of these very eight persons, there are four grounds of differentiation: namely, differentiation of faculties — one with mature faculties and one with immature faculties. Differentiation of yoga — one knowledgeable in yoga and one not knowledgeable in yoga. Differentiation of application — one engaged persistently and earnestly, and one not engaged persistently and earnestly. Differentiation of time — one whose path has been cultivated for a long time, and one whose path has not been cultivated for a long time.

body.text: itīme catvāraḥ prabhedāḥ kathaṃ nidānāni bhavanty aṣṭānāṃ pudgalānāṃ vyavasthānāya / tatra yaḥ paripakvendriyo 'yaṃ samarthaḥ / aparipakvendriyo 'samarthaḥ / yogajña upāyajñakuśalaḥ / ayogajño 'nupāyajñakuśala ity arthaḥ / sātatyasatkṛtya prayogī sātatiko nipaka ity ucyate / asātatyasatkṛtya prayogy asātatiko 'nipaka ity ucyate / dīrghakālabhāvitamārgaḥ kṛtaparicayaḥ / na dīrghakālabhāvitamārgo 'kṛtaparicayaḥ /
body.translated_text: How are these four differentiations grounds for the determination of the eight persons? Therein, one with mature faculties is capable. One with immature faculties is incapable. One knowledgeable in yoga is skilled in means. One not knowledgeable in yoga is unskilled in means — this is the meaning. One engaged persistently and earnestly is called persistent and vigilant. One not engaged persistently and earnestly is called non-persistent and non-vigilant. One whose path has been cultivated for a long time is experienced. One whose path has not been cultivated for a long time is inexperienced.

body.text: ity evam indriyaprabhedena yogaprayogakālaprabhedenāṣṭānāṃ pudgalānāṃ vyavasthānam /
body.translated_text: Thus, through differentiation of faculties, yoga, application, and time, the determination of the eight persons is established.

body.text: yo yāvat pudgalo 'paripakvendriyaḥ, sa tāvad upāyajño 'pi sātatiko 'pi kṛtaparicayo 'pi, nārādhako bhavati nyāyyasya dharmasya kuśalasya /
body.translated_text: As long as a person has immature faculties, even if he is skilled in means, persistent, and experienced, he does not succeed in the just, wholesome <s>dharma</s>.

body.text: tatra paripakvendriyaś ced bhavati na copāyajño bhavati, nārādhako bhavati /
body.translated_text: Therein, even if one has mature faculties but is not skilled in means, one does not succeed.

body.text: paripakvendriyo bhavaty upāyajño na satatiko na kṣiprābhijño bhavati /
body.translated_text: Even if one has mature faculties and is skilled in means but is not persistent, one does not become one of swift realization.

body.text: tatra paripakvendriyo bhavaty upāyajño sātatiko na kṛtaparicayaḥ, na tāvat kṛtasvārtho bhavati kṛtakṛtyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, even if one has mature faculties, is skilled in means, and is persistent but not experienced, one has not yet accomplished one's own purpose and fulfilled one's task.

body.text: yataś ca paripakvendriyo bhavaty upāyajñaḥ sātatikaḥ kṛtaparicayaś ca bhavati, evaṃ sa ārādhako bhavati, kṣiprābhijñaś ca, kṛtasvakārthaś ca bhavati kṛtakṛtyaḥ //
body.translated_text: But when one has mature faculties, is skilled in means, is persistent, and is experienced — thus one succeeds, becomes one of swift realization, and has accomplished one's own purpose and fulfilled one's task. //

body.text:
(II)-A-II-15 Ms.94b5L, Sh.343-10, W.*105-1, P.153b5, D.126a1, N.133a4, Co.130a4, Ch.447c15
tatra catvāro mārāḥ saṃbahulāni mārakarmāṇi veditavyāni yoginā yogaprayuktena / te ca parijñāya parivarjayitavyāḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, four <s>Māras</s> (evil ones) and numerous activities of <s>Māra</s> should be understood by a <s>yogin</s> engaged in practice. And having fully understood them, they should be avoided.

body.text: tatra catvāro mārāḥ / tadyathā skandhamāraḥ, kleśamāraḥ, maraṇamāraḥ, devaputramāraś ca / pañcopādānaskandhāḥ skandhamāraḥ / traidhātukāvacarāḥ kleśāḥ kleśamāraḥ / teṣāṃ teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ tasmāt tasmāt sattvanikāyād yan maraṇaṃ kālakriyā maraṇamāraḥ / yo 'sya kuśalapakṣaprayuktasya skandhakleśamṛtyusamatikramāya kāmadhātūpapanno devaputra aiśvaryaprāptaḥ, antarāyam upasaṃharati vyākṣepakaraṇe, ayam ucyate devaputramāraḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, the four <s>Māras</s>: namely, the <s>Māra</s> of the aggregates (<s>skandhamāra</s>), the <s>Māra</s> of the afflictions (<s>kleśamāra</s>), the <s>Māra</s> of death (<s>maraṇamāra</s>), and <s>Māra</s> the divine son (<s>devaputramāra</s>). The five aggregates of clinging are the <s>Māra</s> of the aggregates. The afflictions pertaining to the three realms are the <s>Māra</s> of the afflictions. The death, the passing away, of those various beings from those various classes of beings is the <s>Māra</s> of death. And that divine son born in the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>) who has attained sovereignty, who, when one is engaged in the wholesome side for transcending the aggregates, afflictions, and death, creates obstacles by causing distraction — this is called <s>Māra</s> the divine son.

body.text:
tatra yatra ca mriyate, yena ca mriyate, yaś cāsau mṛtyuḥ, yena ca mṛtyuṃ na samatikrāmaty antarāyikena vastunā / ity etad adhikṛtya catvāro mārā vyavasthāpitāḥ /
tatra pañcasūpādānaskandheṣu jāteṣu vartamāneṣu mriyate / kleśāj janayaty āyatyām, jātaś ca mriyate / cyutiś ca cyavanatā sattvānāṃ jīvitendriyanirodhaḥ kālakriyā svabhāvata eva mṛtyuḥ / devaputramāraś ca maraṇasamatikramāya prayuktasyāntarāyam upasaṃharati / yena naiva vā śaknoti maraṇadharmatāṃ samatikramitum, kālāntareṇa vā samatikrāmati /
body.translated_text:
Therein, where one dies, and by what one dies, and what that death is, and by what obstructive factor one does not transcend death — in reference to this, the four <s>Māras</s> have been established.
Therein, when the five aggregates of clinging have arisen and are present, one dies — in the aggregates. Due to the afflictions, one generates [a new existence] in the future, and having been born, one dies. And the falling away, the actual departing of beings, the cessation of the life faculty, the passing away — that is death by its own nature. And <s>Māra</s> the divine son creates obstacles for one engaged in transcending the nature of death — by which one either cannot transcend the nature of death at all, or transcends it only after a long time.

body.text: tatrāvaśagato mārasya bhavati laukikamārgavītarāgaḥ pṛthagjana (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 264

children.text: ) ihasthas tatropapanno vā / vaśagataḥ punar yo 'vītarāgaḥ / tatra yo 'vītaragaḥ, sa eva hastagato yathākāmakaraṇīyaḥ / vītarāgo vā punar baddho mārabandhanaiḥ, aparimukto mārapāśaiḥ, yasmāt sa punar apy āgantā imāṃ dhātum //
children.translated_text: ) whether remaining here or reborn there. But one who has not attained dispassion is in <s>Māra's</s> grasp. Therein, one who has not attained dispassion is the very one in [<s>Māra's</s>] hand, to be done with as [<s>Māra</s>] pleases. And one who has attained dispassion [through the worldly path] is still bound by <s>Māra's</s> bonds, not freed from <s>Māra's</s> snares, since he will again return to this realm. //

body.translated_text: Therein, an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) who has attained dispassion through the worldly path is under <s>Māra's</s> power,

body.text:
(II)-A-II-16 Ms.94b9M, Sh.345-22, P.154a6, D.126b2, N.133b5, Co.130b6, Ch.448a7
tatra mārakarmāṇi, yasya kasyacit kuśalo dharmacchandaḥ samutpanno naiṣkramyopasaṃhitaḥ kāmagredham adhipatiṃ kṛtvā pravartate, veditavyaṃ mārakarmaitad iti /
body.translated_text: Therein, the activities of <s>Māra</s>: whenever a wholesome desire for the <s>Dharma</s> connected with renunciation has arisen for anyone, [if] it proceeds under the dominance of greed for sensual pleasures — this should be understood as an activity of <s>Māra</s>.

body.text: indriyair guptadvārasya viharataḥ, yasya rañjanīyeṣu rūpeṣu śabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyadharmeṣu nimittagrāhitāyām anuvyañjanagrāhitāyāṃ cittaṃ praskandati, veditavyaṃ mārakarmaitad iti /
body.translated_text: For one dwelling with the sense-doors guarded — if, with regard to delightful forms, sounds, smells, tastes, tangibles, and <s>dharmas</s>, the mind rushes out through grasping at the sign and grasping at the secondary characteristics — this should be known as <s>Māra's</s> activity.

body.text: evaṃ bhojaneṣu mātrajñasya viharataḥ, praṇīteṣu raseṣu chandarāgam anunayena cittaṃ praskandati bhaktavaiṣamye /
body.translated_text: Likewise, for one dwelling with moderation in food — if, with regard to exquisite tastes, the mind rushes out with desire-and-passion-and-affection, toward imbalanced eating — this should be known as <s>Māra's</s> activity.

body.text: evaṃ pūrvarātrāpararātraṃ jāgarikāyogam anuyuktasya viharataḥ, nidrāsukhe, śayanasukhe, pārśvasukhe cittaṃ praskandati, veditavyaṃ mārakarmaitad iti /
body.translated_text: Likewise, for one dwelling devoted to the practice of wakefulness in the first and last watches of the night — if the mind rushes out toward the pleasure of sleep, the pleasure of lying down, the pleasure of reclining — this should be known as <s>Māra's</s> activity.

body.text: tathā saṃprajānadvihāriṇo viharataḥ, abhikramapratikramādiṣu śiśum udāravarṇaṃ rañjanīyaṃ mātṛgrāmaṃ dṛṣṭvāyoniśo nimittagrāheṇa cittaṃ praskandati / lokacitrāṇi vā dṛṣṭvā cittaṃ praskandati / bahvarthatāyāṃ bahukṛtyatāyāṃ cittaṃ praskandati / tadyathā gṛhasthapravrajitaiḥ saṃsargarāmatāyāṃ pāpamitraiḥ sahaikavyavasitāyāṃ dṛṣṭyanumataye cittaṃ praskandati / veditavyaṃ mārakarmaitad iti /
body.translated_text: Likewise, for one dwelling with clear comprehension — if, while going forward and returning, upon seeing a young woman of excellent complexion, delightful, the mind rushes out through unwise grasping at the sign; or upon seeing the spectacles of the world, the mind rushes out; or the mind rushes out toward being occupied with many concerns and many duties — such as delight in socializing with householders and renunciants, or toward being inclined in agreement with evil companions and their views — this should be known as <s>Māra's</s> activity.

body.text: tathā buddhe dharme saṃghe, duḥkhe samudaye nirodhe mārge, ihaloke paraloke, kāṅkṣā vimataya utpadyante, veditavyaṃ mārakarmaitad iti /
body.translated_text: Likewise, when doubts and uncertainties arise regarding the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, the <s>Saṅgha</s>, regarding suffering, origin, cessation, and path, regarding this world and the next — this should be known as <s>Māra's</s> activity.

body.text: araṇyagato vā, vṛkṣamūlagato vā, śūnyāgāragato vā, mahāntaṃ bhayabhairavaṃ paśyati / uttrāsakaraṃ romaharṣaṇam, brāhmaṇaveṣeṇa vā, manuṣyaveṣeṇa vā, amanuṣyaveṣeṇa vā, kaścid upasaṃkramyāyoniśaḥ śuklapakṣād vicchindayati kṛṣṇapakṣe ca samādāpayati, veditavyaṃ mārakarmaitad iti /
body.translated_text: Or, having gone to the forest, to the root of a tree, or to an empty dwelling, one sees great fear and terror — something terrifying and hair-raising. Or someone approaches in the guise of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, or in human guise, or in non-human guise, and unwisely severs one from the bright side and induces one to take up the dark side — this should be known as <s>Māra's</s> activity.

body.text: yadā lābhasatkāre cittaṃ praskandati, mātsarye mahecchatāyām asaṃtuṣṭau krodhopanāhakuhanālapanādiṣu śramaṇālaṃkāravipakṣeṣu dharmeṣu cittaṃ praskandati, veditavyaṃ mārakarmaitad iti /
body.translated_text: When the mind rushes out toward gain and honor, toward selfishness, great desire, discontent, anger, grudge-bearing, hypocrisy, flattery, and other such <s>dharmas</s> that are opposed to the ornament of the ascetic — this should be known as <s>Māra's</s> activity.

body.text: itīmāny evaṃbhāgīyāni mārakarmāṇi veditavyāni tāni caturṇāṃ mārāṇāṃ yathāyogam //
body.translated_text: Thus these and similar activities should be known as the activities of <s>Māra</s>, and they belong to the four <s>Māras</s> as appropriate.

body.text:
(II)-A-II-17 Ms.95a5R, Sh.347-9, W.*105-8, P.155a3, D.127a6, N.134b2, Co.131b2, Ch.448b4
tatra tribhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ samyakprayuktasyāpy ārambho viphalo bhavati / tadyathā indriyasamudāgamena, anulomāvavādena, samādhidurbalatayā ca /
body.translated_text: Therein, through three causes, even for one who is rightly engaged, the effort becomes fruitless — namely: through the maturation of faculties, through conforming instruction, and through weakness of concentration.

body.text: indriyāṇi cen na samudāgatāni, ānulomikaś cāvavādo bhavati, samādhiś ca kevalavān, evam asyārambho viphalo bhavati /
body.translated_text: If the faculties have not matured, even though the instruction is conforming and the concentration is merely present — thus one's effort becomes fruitless.

body.text: indriyāṇi cen na samudāgatāni bhavanti, avavādaś ca nānulomiko bhavati, samādhiś ca balavān bhavati, evārambho viphalaḥ /
body.translated_text: If the faculties have not matured and the instruction is not conforming, even though the concentration is strong — thus the effort is fruitless.

body.text: indriyāṇi cet samudāgatāni, nāvavādaś cānulomiko bhavati, samādhiś ca durbalo bhavati, evārambho viphalaḥ /
body.translated_text: If the faculties have matured but the instruction is not conforming and the concentration is weak — thus the effort is fruitless.

body.text: indriyāṇi cet samudāgatāni bhavanti, ānulomikaś cāvavādo bhavati, samādhiś ca durbalo bhavati, evārambho viphalaḥ /
body.translated_text: If the faculties have matured and the instruction is conforming but the concentration is weak — thus the effort is fruitless.

children.text: indriyāṇi cet samudāgatāni bhavanti, ānulomikaś cāvavādaḥ, samādhiś ca balavān, evam asyārambhaḥ saphalo bhavati /
children.translated_text: If the faculties have matured, the instruction is conforming, and the concentration is strong — thus one's effort becomes fruitful.

children.text: ebhis tribhiḥ kāraṇair viphalo bhavati, tribhir eva kāraṇaiḥ saphalaḥ //
children.translated_text: Through these three causes it becomes fruitless; through these same three causes it becomes fruitful.

body.text: // uddānam //
body.translated_text: Summary verses:

body.text: pudgalās tadvyavasthānam atha ālambanena ca /

children.text: avavādaś ca śikṣā ca tathā śikṣānulomikāḥ /
children.translated_text: instruction, and training; and <s>dharmas</s> in conformity with training;

children.text: yogabhraṃśaś ca yogaś ca manaskāraś ca yoginaḥ /
children.translated_text: falling away from yoga, and yoga; and the mental attentions of the practitioner;
the tasks, cultivation, fruit, and the types of persons;

children.text: māraś ca mārakarmāṇi ārambho viphalo bhavet //
children.translated_text: <s>Māra</s>, and <s>Māra's</s> activities; and the effort that becomes fruitless.

body.translated_text: Persons, and their classification; and objects of meditation;

body.text: // yogācārabhūmau śrāvakabhūmisaṃgṛhītāyāṃ dvitīyaṃ yogasthānam //
body.translated_text: In the <s>Yogācārabhūmi</s>, within the <s>Śrāvakabhūmi</s>, the second stage of yoga [is complete].

body.text:
Appendix I
Asamāhitā bhūmiḥ
body.translated_text: Appendix I: The Non-Concentrated Stage (<s>Asamāhitā Bhūmi</s>)

body.text:
Ms. B*a1L-B*a6L, P. 181b7-182b7, D. 159a6-160a4, Ch. 344b19-c15, Del. 134-136.
asamāhitā bhūmiḥ katamā / sā samāsato dvādaśākārā veditavyā /
body.translated_text: What is the non-concentrated stage? In brief, it should be understood as having twelve aspects.

body.text: asty asamāhitā bhūmiḥ svabhāvato 'samāhitā tadyathā pañca vijñānakāyāḥ /
body.translated_text: There is a non-concentrated stage that is non-concentrated by its own nature — namely, the five consciousness-groups.

body.text: asty asamāhitā bhūmiḥ prasrabdhivaikalyāt tadyathā kāmāvacārāś cittacaitasikā dharmāḥ, satyām api cittaikāgratāyāṃ te cittacaitasikā dharmā na prasrabdhyupagūḍhāḥ pravartante, iti yena sā asamāhitety ucyate /
body.translated_text: There is a non-concentrated stage due to the deficiency of tranquility (<s>prasrabdhi</s>) — namely, the mental and mental-concomitant <s>dharmas</s> belonging to the desire realm. Even though one-pointedness of mind exists, those mental and mental-concomitant <s>dharmas</s> do not proceed enveloped by tranquility — therefore it is called non-concentrated.

body.text: asty asamāhitā bhūmir anārambhāt tadyathā kāmopabhoginām adhyavasitānāṃ kāmeṣu kāmān upabhuñjānānām /
body.translated_text: There is a non-concentrated stage due to non-commencement — namely, for those who enjoy sensual pleasures and are intent on sensual pleasures, consuming sensual pleasures.

body.text: asty asamāhitā bhūmir vikṣepāt tadyathādikarmikāṇāṃ samādhiprayuktānāṃ pañcasu kāmaguṇeṣv anuvikṣipte 'nuvisṛte cetasi /
body.translated_text: There is a non-concentrated stage due to distraction — namely, for beginners engaged in concentration, whose mind is scattered and dispersed toward the five strands of sensual pleasure.

body.text: asty asamāhitā bhūmiḥ saṃkṣepāt tadyathādikarmikāṇām eva samādhiprayuktānām adhyātmam abhisaṃkṣipte cetasi styānamiddhābhibhavataḥ /
body.translated_text: There is a non-concentrated stage due to contraction — namely, for those very beginners engaged in concentration, whose mind is contracted internally, being overwhelmed by sloth-and-torpor.

body.text: asty asamāhitā bhūmir apratilambhāt tadyathā teṣām euādikarmikāṇāṃ samādhiprayuktānāṃ vikṣepasaṃkṣepānupakliṣṭe 'pi cetasy alabdhamanaskārāṇāṃ ye cittacaitasikā dharmāḥ /
body.translated_text: There is a non-concentrated stage due to non-attainment — namely, for those very beginners engaged in concentration, whose mind, even though not afflicted by distraction or contraction, has not attained [proper] mental attention — [referring to] their mental and mental-concomitant <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: asty asamāhitā bhūmir aparipūrṇatvāt tadyathā labdhamanaskārāṇām alabdhaprayoganiṣṭhāmanaskārāṇām alabdhatatphalānāṃ ca /
body.translated_text: There is a non-concentrated stage due to incompleteness — namely, for those who have attained mental attention but have not attained the mental attention of the culmination of practice and have not attained its fruit.

body.text: asty asamāhitā bhūmiḥ saṃkleśāt tadyathā labdhaprayoganiṣṭhāphalamanaskārāṇām anyatamānyatamenāsvādādikenopakleśenopakliṣṭe cetasi /
body.translated_text: There is a non-concentrated stage due to defilement — namely, for those who have attained the mental attention of the culmination of practice and its fruit, when the mind is defiled by some contamination such as relishing and the like.

body.text: asty asamāhitā bhūmir avaśitvāt tadyathā labdhaprayoganiṣṭhāphalamanaskārāṇām (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> II 278

even with undefiled minds, who have not attained mastery over the signs of entering, abiding in, and emerging from attainment — who do not obtain [these] at will, without difficulty, and without trouble.

body.translated_text: There is a non-concentrated stage due to lack of mastery — namely, for those who have attained the mental attention of the culmination of practice and its fruit,

body.text: asty asamāhitā bhūmir aviśuddhes tadyathā nikāmākṛcchrākisaralābhinām api laukikasamāpattṝṇām asamudghātitakleśānuśayāś cittacaitasikā dharmāḥ /
body.translated_text: There is a non-concentrated stage due to impurity — namely, for those who obtain at will, without difficulty, and without trouble, but who have worldly attainments — [referring to] their mental and mental-concomitant <s>dharmas</s> whose latent tendencies of defilement have not been uprooted.

body.text: asty asamāhitā bhūmir vyutthānāt tadyathā pratilabdhāt samādher vyutthitasyāparihīṇasya /
body.translated_text: There is a non-concentrated stage due to emergence — namely, for one who has emerged from a previously attained concentration and has not fallen away [from it].

body.text: asty asamāhitā bhūmiḥ parihāṇes tadyathā pratilabdhāt samādheḥ parihīṇasya //
body.translated_text: There is a non-concentrated stage due to falling away — namely, for one who has fallen away from a previously attained concentration.

body.text: yogācārabhūmāv asamāhitā bhūmiḥ samāptā // //
body.translated_text: In the <s>Yogācārabhūmi</s>, the non-concentrated stage is complete.

body.text:
Appendix II
Śrutamayī bhūmiḥ
body.translated_text: Appendix II: The Stage Born of Hearing (<s>Śrutamayī Bhūmi</s>)

body.text:
A. I-1 P.209a1,D.182b2, N.195b3, Ch.354a6
[chos bdun po 'di dag ni bden pa yaṅ dag pa ji lta ba bźin du mṅon par rtogs śiṅ rnam par grol ba yoṅs su rdsogs par 'gyur ba yin te / lhag mthoṅ gi phyogs gsum ste / chos rnam par 'byed pa daṅ / brtson 'grus daṅ / dga' ba daṅ / źi gnas kyi phyogs gsum ste / śin tu sbyaṅs pa daṅ / tiṅ ṅe 'dzin daṅ / btaṅ sñoms daṅ / gcig ni źi gnas daṅ / lhag mthoṅ gi phyogs te / 'di sta ste dran pa'o //
body.translated_text: [These seven <s>dharmas</s> lead to the full realization of the truths as they really are and to the complete accomplishment of liberation. There are three belonging to the side of insight (<s>vipaśyanā</s>): investigation of <s>dharmas</s>, energy, and joy. And three belonging to the side of calm (<s>śamatha</s>): tranquility, concentration, and equanimity. And one belongs to both the side of calm and insight: namely, mindfulness.]

body.text:
A. I-2 P.209a3, D.182b3, N.195b5, Ch.354a10
dbaṅ po daṅ / 'bras bu daṅ / rnam par thar ba las gaṅ zag bdun du rnam par bźag par rig par bya ste / źugs pa'i lam la dbaṅ po rtul po daṅ / dbaṅ po rnon po dad pa daṅ / chos kyi rjes su 'braṅ ba gñis daṅ / 'bras bu'i lam la / de gñis ñid dad pas mos pa daṅ / lta bas thob pa daṅ / sñoms par 'jug pa'i sgrib pa las ni rnam par grol la / ñon moṅs pa'i sgrib pa las ni rnam par ma grol ba ste / lus kyi mṅon sum du byed pa daṅ / ñon moṅs pa'i sgrib pa las ni rnam par grol la / sñoms par 'jug pa'i sgrib pa las ni rnam par ma grol ba ste / śes rab kyis rnam par grol ba daṅ / sñoms par 'jug pa daṅ / ñon moṅs pa gñi ga'i sgrib pa las rnam par grol ba ste / gñi ga'i cha las rnam par grol ba'o //
body.translated_text: [By faculties, fruits, and liberations, seven persons are classified: On the path of entry, those with dull faculties and those with keen faculties — the faith-follower and the <s>dharma</s>-follower — [these are] two. On the path of fruition, those same two: the one who is liberated through faith and the one who has attained through view. One who is liberated from the obstacle to attainment but not from the obstacle of defilement — the one who witnesses with the body. One who is liberated from the obstacle of defilement but not from the obstacle to attainment — the one liberated by wisdom. And one who is liberated from both obstacles of attainment and defilement — the one liberated in both ways.]

body.text:
A. I-3 P.209a7, D.182b6, N.196a1, Ch.354a16
rgyu gsum po rnam pa bdun po 'di dag ni naṅ gi sems mñam par 'jog ciṅ / yaṅ dag par sems rtse gcig tu byed par 'gyur ba ste / 'jug par byed pa daṅ / gnas pa daṅ mthun pa daṅ / sdud par byed pa'o //
body.translated_text: [These three causes, in seven modes, internally settle the mind and truly bring about one-pointedness: the cause of engagement, the cause of abiding and conforming, and the cause of collecting.]

body.text: 'jig rten pa'i yaṅ dag pa'i lta ba sbyin pa yod do / źes bya ba la sogs pa'i rnam pa daṅ / de dag ñid la brten nas khyim gyi gnas ni kun tu (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> II 286

children.text: ) gnod pa'o // khyim ni skyon yin no / źes bya ba la sogs pa'i rnam pa ste / mṅon par byuṅ ba daṅ ldan pa'i yaṅ dag pa'i rtog pa ni 'jug par byed pa'o) //
children.translated_text: the right thought accompanied by renunciation is the cause of engagement.]

body.translated_text: [The worldly right view, in the mode of 'there is giving' and so forth, and relying on those very [views], the mode of 'the household life is entirely harmful,' 'the household is a fault,' and so forth —

body.text: źugs zin nas yaṅ dag pa'i ṅag daṅ / las daṅ 'tsho ba yaṅ dag par blaṅs pa ni gnas pa daṅ mthun pa'o //
body.translated_text: [Having entered, the undertaking of right speech, right action, and right livelihood is the cause of abiding and conforming.]

body.text: 'jug par byed pa'i rgyu daṅ / gnas pa daṅ mthun pa'i rgyu de'i 'og tu tshul bźin yid la byed pa daṅ ldan pa na yaṅ dag pa'i rtsol ba daṅ / dran pa gaṅ yin pa de ni sdud par byed pa'i rgyu yin par rig par bya'o //
body.translated_text: [After the cause of engagement and the cause of abiding and conforming, when one is endowed with wise attention, whatever right effort and mindfulness there is — that should be understood as the cause of collecting.]

body.text:
A. I-4 P.209b3, D.183a2, N.196a5, Ch.354a23 ' '
'dod pa la ñe bar spyod pa rnams ni 'di lta bu'i phyir nor sogs par 'dod de / 'di ltar bde ba 'dod pa kho na'i phyir yin la / bde ba bdun po 'di dag ni 'phags pa'i nor bdun las byuṅ ba ste / de dag ni phal pa'i nor kun tu bsags pa thams cad kyis thob par mi 'gyur ba ste /
body.translated_text: [Those who pursue sensual pleasures desire wealth and so forth for this purpose: namely, solely for the purpose of happiness. But these seven kinds of happiness arise from the seven noble treasures, and cannot be obtained by any accumulation of worldly wealth:]

body.text: dad pa daṅ ldan pa'i bde ba daṅ / bde 'gror skye ba las byuṅ ba daṅ / bdag gi cha ma yin pa la ltos nas / kha na ma tho ba kun tu mi spyod pas 'gyod pa med pa las byuṅ ba daṅ / de bźin du gźan gyis smad pa la ltos pa daṅ / chos daṅ don legs par rtogs pa daṅ ldan pa'i bde ba daṅ / phyi ma la yo byad daṅ mi ldan pa med pa las byuṅ ba daṅ / don dam pa rtogs pa las byuṅ ba'i bde ba ste / rnam pa du ma kha na ma tho ba med pa'i bde ba 'di dag ni / 'jig rten pa'i nor kun tu bsags pa las rnam pa thams cad kyi thams cad du thob par mi 'gyur te / gźan du na tshe 'di ñid la yo byad kyis mi brel ba las byuṅ ba tsam du zad la de yaṅ kha na ma tho ba daṅ bcas pa yin no //
body.translated_text: [The happiness of being endowed with faith; that born of rebirth in a good destination; that born of non-remorse through not engaging in blameworthy conduct, considering what is not one's own domain; likewise, considering others' censure; the happiness endowed with proper understanding of <s>Dharma</s> and meaning; that born of not lacking requisites in the future; and the happiness born of realizing the ultimate truth. These various kinds of blameless happiness cannot in every way be obtained from the accumulation of worldly wealth. Otherwise, [what can be obtained] amounts merely to happiness born of not lacking requisites in this very life — and even that is accompanied by blameworthiness.]

body.text:
A. I-5 P.209b8, D. 183a6, N. 196b2, Ch.354b4
bdun po 'di dag ni bdud daṅ ñon moṅs pa'i phyogs kyi stobs yin te / bstan pa la gnod par byed pa daṅ / ṅan 'gror 'gro ba'i ñes par spyod pa kun (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> II 288

children.text: ) tu spyod pa daṅ / bdag gi cha ma yin par mi lta ste / bar du gcod pa'i chos bsten pa daṅ / gźan gyis smad pa las mi lta ste / bar du gcod pa'i chos bsten pa daṅ / dge ba daṅ / mi dge ba daṅ / kha na ma tho ba daṅ bcas pa daṅ / kha na ma tho ba med pa daṅ / ṅan pa daṅ / bzaṅ po daṅ / nag po daṅ / dkar po'i rab tu dbye ba daṅ bcas pa'i rten ciṅ 'brel bar 'byuṅ ba'i chos rnams mi rtogs pa daṅ / ser sna'i dri mas zil gyis non pa'i sems kyis / snod spyad daṅ / yo byad maṅ po 'chaṅ ba daṅ / blun źiṅ blo chuṅ la śin tu rmoṅs pa'o /
children.translated_text: ) [Tibetan passage:] ...and does not see it as not belonging to one's own share; practicing obstructive <s>dharmas</s>, and not seeing [the fault] in being criticized by others; practicing obstructive <s>dharmas</s>; not understanding the <s>dharmas</s> of dependent origination that include the distinctions of wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and excellent, dark and bright; and, with a mind overwhelmed by the stain of jealousy, holding many vessels, utensils, and possessions; and being foolish, of little intelligence, and deeply confused.

body.translated_text: [These seven are powers of <s>Māra</s> and the side of defilement: those that harm the teaching, and all the misconduct that leads to lower rebirths

body.text: bdud daṅ ñon moṅs pa'i phyogs kyi stobs 'di dag zil gyis mnan pa daṅ / rnam par bstsal ba'i phyir 'phags pa'i chos 'dul ba la dad pa la sogs pa'i stobs bdun po kho na yod par rig par bya'o //
body.translated_text: It should be understood that the seven powers of faith and so forth in the noble <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> exist precisely for the purpose of overcoming and dispelling these powers belonging to the side of <s>Māra</s> and the afflictions.

body.text:
A. I-6,-7 P.210a5, D.183b2, N.196b5, Ch.354b11
don dam pa'i chos mya ṅan las 'das pa'i mi mthun pa'i phyogs kyi chos bdun po 'di dag ni dam pa'i chos yoṅs su 'grib ciṅ / nub par 'gyur ba ste / de dag kyaṅ rgud pa rnam pa gsum du 'dus te /
body.translated_text: These seven <s>dharmas</s> that are the adverse side of the ultimate <s>Dharma</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s> — through these the true <s>Dharma</s> diminishes and disappears. They are comprised in three kinds of decline:

body.text: ñe bar spyad pa rgud pa daṅ / lhag pa'i bsaṃ pa rgud pa daṅ / sbyor ba rgud pa'o /
body.translated_text: the decline of conduct, the decline of superior intention, and the decline of application.

body.text: de la chos gos la sogs pa bzaṅ po 'dod pa daṅ / maṅ po 'dod pa daṅ / de las byuṅ ba'i loṅs spyod ni ñe bar spyad pa rgud pa'o /
body.translated_text: Therein, the desire for fine robes and so forth, the desire for many, and the enjoyment arising therefrom — this is the decline of conduct.

body.text: lam daṅ lam gyi 'bras bu mya ṅan las 'das pa la / mṅon par yid mi ches pa ni lhag pa'i bsam pa rgud pa'o //]
body.translated_text: [The lack of deep conviction in the path, the fruit of the path, and <s>nirvāṇa</s> — this is the decline of superior intention.]

body.text:
Ms.15b6L, P.210a7, D.183b4, N.197a1, Ch.354b16
kausīdyaṃ muṣitasmṛtitā vikṣiptacittatā dauṣprajñaṃ prayogavipattiḥ /
body.translated_text: Laziness, confused mindfulness, distracted mind, poor wisdom, and failure of application.

body.text: tatra upabhogavipattir lobhākuśalamūlapakṣyā / āśayaprayogavipattiḥ punar mohākuśalamūlapakṣyā / etadviparyayeṇa śuklapakṣo veditavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, the decline of enjoyment belongs to the side of the unwholesome root of greed. The decline of intention and application belongs to the side of the unwholesome root of delusion. By the reverse of this, the bright side should be understood.

body.text:
A. I-8 Ms.15b6R, P.210b1, D183b6, N.197a2, Ch.354b19
sapteme dharmāḥ paramārthanirvāṇapakṣyāḥ saddharmāparihāṇāya cirasthitikatāyai saṃvartante / śrutamayī prajñā, cintāmayī, bhāvanāmayī prajñā, āśrayasya viṣamapariharaṇatā, samyagāmiṣadharmaparyeṣṭiḥ, nirabhimānatā, satkārārhānarheṣu satkaraṇāsatkaraṇāya pudgalapravicayaḥ /
body.translated_text: These seven <s>dharmas</s> belong to the side of ultimate <s>nirvāṇa</s> and conduce to the non-decline and long-lasting stability of the true <s>Dharma</s>: wisdom born of hearing, wisdom born of reflection, wisdom born of cultivation, the removal of the unevenness of the basis, the proper seeking of material <s>dharma</s> requisites, freedom from conceit, and the discernment of persons worthy and unworthy of honor.

body.text: tatra śrutam avyutpannasyārthasya vyutpattaye, cintā suniścitārthābhyūhanatāyai, bhāvanā kleśaprahāṇāya, āśrayasya viṣamaparihāraḥ prahāṇakṣamakarmaṇyatāyai, samyagāmiṣadharmaparyeṣaṇā kṣiprābhijñatāyai, nirabhimānatāvaramātrādhigamāsaṃtuṣṭaye, pudgalavicayo jñātamahāpuṇyādīnām aspṛhaṇatāyai, alpecchādīnāṃ ca spṛhaṇatāyai //
body.translated_text: Therein, hearing is for the comprehension of meaning not yet understood; reflection is for the thorough ascertainment of meaning with well-established certainty; cultivation is for the abandonment of afflictions; the removal of the unevenness of the basis is for the workability and capacity for abandonment; the proper seeking of material <s>dharma</s> requisites is for swiftness of higher knowledge; freedom from conceit is for non-contentment with merely the lower attainment; the discernment of persons is for not yearning after those known to be of great merit and the like, and for yearning after those of few desires and the like.

body.text:
A. I-9 Ms.16a2M, P.210b7, D.184a3, N.197a7, Ch.354c2
saptemāni sattvānām upapattyāyatanāni yeṣu sattvānāṃ vijñānāni pravāhataḥ saṃmukhīkurvante / apāyān asaṃjñisattvān naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanaṃ sthāpayitvā /
body.translated_text: These are the seven abodes of arising of sentient beings, in which the consciousnesses of sentient beings move in continuity — excluding the lower realms, the unconscious beings, and the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.

body.text: nirvitpadasthānabhūtatvād apāyā na vijñānasthitiḥ, ekāntena tatra vijñānasyāsamudācārān nāsaṃjñisattvāḥ / samudācārāsamudācārato 'naikāntikatvān na naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanam /
body.translated_text: Since the lower realms are not a place of <s>nirvāṇa</s> in their true nature, they are not an abode of consciousness. Since consciousness does not at all occur there, the unconscious beings are not [an abode of consciousness]. And since, from the standpoint of occurrence and non-occurrence [of consciousness], it is not definitive one way — the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is not [an abode of consciousness].

body.text: tatra kāyavisabhāgatā kāyanānātvaṃ saṃjñāvisabhāgatā saṃjñanānātvam, etadviparyayād ekatvakāyatā, ekatvasaṃjñitā ca veditavyā /
body.translated_text: Therein, dissimilarity of body means diversity of body; dissimilarity of perception means diversity of perception. By the reverse of this, oneness of body and oneness of perception should be understood.

body.text: tatra brahmalokād arvāg visabhāgakāyavicitrarūpakāyātmabhāvaprasavā / brahmaloke punas tatprathamābhinirvṛttā ye teṣām evaṃ bhavati / "brahmaṇā vayaṃ sṛṣṭāḥ" / brahmaṇo 'py evaṃ bhavati / "mayaite sṛṣṭā" itīyaṃ teṣāṃ saṃjñāsabhāgatā /
body.translated_text: Therein, below the <s>Brahma</s>-world, there is the production of bodies of diverse and varied forms due to dissimilar bodies. In the <s>Brahma</s>-world, those who are first born there think: "We have been created by <s>Brahmā</s>." And <s>Brahmā</s> too thinks: "These have been created by me" — this is their similarity of perception.

body.text: dvitīyadhyānād ūrdhvam sarve 'rciḥsaṃnibhakāyatvād ekatvakāyāḥ / ābhāsvare punar devanikāye pūrvapaścād upapannānāṃ bhayābhayasaṃjñā brahmalokadahārcirdarśanāt teṣāṃ visabhāgasaṃjñā veditavyā //
body.translated_text: Above the second <s>dhyāna</s>, all have bodies similar to rays of light, hence they have oneness of body. But in the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> (radiant) divine realm, those born earlier and later have perceptions of fear and fearlessness due to seeing the flames of the fire burning the <s>Brahma</s>-world — their dissimilarity of perception should be understood.

body.text:
A. I-10 Ms.16a5L, P.211a6, D.184b2, N.197b6, Ch.354c17
saptabhiḥ sattvānāṃ dauṣṭhulyaiḥ sarvakleśapakṣyadauṣṭhulyasaṃgraho veditavyaḥ, hīnadhātukarāgadveṣapakṣyam, madhyapraṇītadhāturāgapakṣyam / hīnamadhyapraṇītadhātukamānāvidyādṛṣṭivicikitsāpakṣyaṃ ca dauṣṭhulyam //
body.translated_text: By seven unsuitabilities of beings, the collection of all unsuitability belonging to the side of afflictions should be understood: unsuitability belonging to the side of desire and aversion of the lower realm, unsuitability belonging to the side of attachment of the middle and superior realms, and unsuitability belonging to the side of pride, ignorance, wrong views, and doubt of the lower, middle, and superior realms.

body.text:
A. I-11 Ms.16a5R, P.211a8, D.184b3, N.198a1, Ch.354c20
saptabhir ākārair itobāhyakānāṃ durākhyāto dharmavinayaḥ sadoṣo veditavyaḥ / vyutpattidoṣeṇa, cāritradoṣeṇa, sanniśrayadoṣeṇa, saṃkalpadoṣeṇa, vyavasāyadoṣeṇa, adhicittadoṣeṇa, adhiprajñadoṣeṇa /
body.translated_text: By seven aspects, the ill-proclaimed <s>dharmavinaya</s> of outsiders should be understood as faulty: by the fault of learning, by the fault of conduct, by the fault of the support, by the fault of intention, by the fault of resolution, by the fault of the higher mind, and by the fault of the higher wisdom.

body.text: kiṃcāpītobāhyakaḥ śrutam udgṛhṇāti / tat punaś caturviparyāsānukūlatvād upārambheti / vādapratimokṣānuśaṃsakathāpratyupasthāpanatvāc ca tatkṛtā vyutpattiḥ sadoṣā / śīlam ācārājīvavipattiparigṛhītatvāt svayaṃ vānairyāṇikatvāt sadoṣam / mitraṃ viparītamārgadeśikatvāt sadoṣam / (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> II 294

children.text: ) viveko mithyāsaṃkalpopahatacittatvāt sadoṣaḥ / vyavasāya upāyavirahitatvāt sadoṣaḥ / adhicittaṃ muṣitasmṛtes tṛṣṇāmānāvidyāvicikitsottarādhyāyitvāt sadoṣam / adhiprajñaṃ dvāṣaṣṭibhir dṛṣṭigatair upahatatvāt sadoṣam /
children.translated_text: ) Seclusion is faulty because the mind is afflicted by wrong intentions. Resolution is faulty because it is devoid of [proper] method. The higher mind is faulty because, with confused mindfulness, it follows after craving, pride, ignorance, and doubt in their subsequent phases. The higher wisdom is faulty because it is afflicted by the sixty-two wrong views.

body.translated_text: Although the outsider grasps what has been heard, that [hearing] proceeds in conformity with the four perverted views and is established for the purpose of debate, the benefit of <s>Prātimokṣa</s> rhetoric, and the presentation of praise — therefore the learning produced thereby is faulty. Moral conduct is faulty because it is seized by corruption of conduct, livelihood, and comportment, or because it is itself non-conducive to liberation. The friend is faulty because of being a guide to the wrong path.

body.text: etadviparyayeṇa svākhyāte dharmavinaya etāny eva saptavastūni nirdoṣāṇi veditavyāni //
body.translated_text: By the reverse of this, in the well-proclaimed <s>dharmavinaya</s>, these very seven matters should be understood as faultless.

body.text:
A. I-12 Ms.16a8M, P.211b7, D.185a1, N.198a6, Ch.355a4
sapteme bhikṣūṇām utpannasyādhikaraṇasya vyupaśamāya saṃvartante / śeṣaṃ tadyathā vastusaṃgrahaṇyām //
body.translated_text: These seven conduce to the settlement of a disciplinary case that has arisen among <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks). The remainder is as in the <s>Vastusaṃgrahaṇī</s>.

body.text: tatremāni saptety adhikaraṇāni / saṃmukhāpattivyutpādanādhikaraṇam, atītasaṃmuṣitāpattivyutpādanādhikaraṇam, asvatantryāpattivyutpādanādhikaraṇam, āpattivimarśādhikaraṇam, [ltuṅ ba gtan la 'bebs pas rtsod ba daṅ / bdag ñid kyis ltuṅ ba la 'gyod pa rtsod ba daṅ /] pakṣāparapakṣavyavasthitayor anyo'nyam āpatticodanāpakarṣaṇādhikaraṇam // //
body.translated_text: Therein, these seven disciplinary cases are: the case of establishing an offense committed in one's presence, the case of establishing a past and forgotten offense, the case of establishing an offense committed without one's own control, the case of investigating an offense, [the case of settling an offense, the case of personal remorse for an offense,] and the case of mutual accusation and refutation of offenses by two parties established on opposing sides.

body.text: saptakair buddhavacane jñeyādhiṣṭhānam // //
body.translated_text: This is the knowable basis in groups of seven in the word of the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.text:
A. II-1 Ms.16b2L, P,212a3, D.185a3, N.198b2, Ch.355a11
aṣṭabhir aṅgaiḥ saṃgṛhītā bhikṣor niravaśeṣasaṃprayojanaprahāṇāya tisro bhāvanā veditavyāḥ / śīlabhāvanā, samādhibhāvanā, prajñābhāvanā ca / samyagvākkarmāntājīvaiḥ śīlabhāvanā, samyaksmṛtisamādhibhyāṃ samādhibhāvanā, samyagdṛṣṭisaṃkalpavyāyāmaiḥ prajñābhāvanā //
body.translated_text: The three cultivations, comprised by the eight limbs, should be understood as [leading to] the abandonment of all remaining connections for a <s>bhikṣu</s>: the cultivation of moral conduct, the cultivation of concentration, and the cultivation of wisdom. The cultivation of moral conduct [is accomplished] by right speech, right action, and right livelihood; the cultivation of concentration by right mindfulness and right concentration; the cultivation of wisdom by right view, right intention, and right effort.

body.text:
A. II-2 Ms.16b2R, P.212a5, D.185a5, N.198b4, Ch.355a20
saphalam samyakprayogam adhipatiṃ kṛtvā vyavadānapakṣyāṇām aṣṭānāṃ pudgalānāṃ vyavasthānaṃ veditavyam / pratipannakānāṃ caturṇāṃ phalasthānāṃ caturṇām //
body.translated_text: Taking fruitful right application as the predominant factor, the classification of eight persons belonging to the purification side should be understood: four who are practicing and four who are established in the fruit.

body.text:
A. II-3 Ms.16b3L, P.212a6, D.185a7, N.198b5, Ch.355a21
dve ime dāne aṣṭākāre veditavye, sadoṣaṃ ca dānaṃ nirdoṣaṃ ca dānam /
body.translated_text: These two kinds of giving should be understood in eight aspects: a gift with fault and a gift without fault.

body.text: tatra sadoṣaṃ saptākāram, ekākāraṃ punar nirdoṣam / asti dānaṃ kausīdyopahatatvāt sadoṣam / asty akāmakārāt sadoṣaṃ sāmiṣadoṣasya dāridrabhītasyeśvarābhilāṣiṇaḥ / asty atītasāpekṣyatayā sadoṣam / asty anāgatābhinandanatayā sadoṣam / asty avajñādoṣāt sadoṣam / asti jñātābhilāṣadoṣāt sadoṣam / asty upabhogābhilāṣāt sadoṣam /
body.translated_text: Therein, a gift with fault has seven aspects, while a gift without fault has one aspect. There is a gift that is faulty due to being afflicted by laziness. There is one faulty due to not being done freely — that of one fearful of poverty, with the fault of material desire, wishing for lordship. There is one faulty due to regard for the past. There is one faulty due to delight in the future. There is one faulty due to the fault of contempt. There is one faulty due to the fault of desire for fame. There is one faulty due to desire for enjoyment.

body.text: nirdoṣaṃ punar dānaṃ nirvāṇaparināmitaṃ tatsaṃbhārabhṛtam / nirāmiṣacetaso 'pi sugatigamanāyāpi mahābhogatāyā api saṃvartate //
body.translated_text: A faultless gift, however, is one dedicated to <s>nirvāṇa</s>, bearing [the merit of] its equipment. Even for one with a mind free from material desires, it conduces to rebirth in a good destination and to great enjoyment.

body.text:
A. II-4,-5 Ms.16b4R, P.212b3, D.185b2, N.199a2, Ch.355b6
catvāri sthānāny adhiṣṭhāyāṣṭasu kāleṣu kausīdyaṃ prāviṣkurvan vīryam anārabhamāno veditavyaḥ, kusīdajātīyo 'yaṃ pudgalo 'nārabdhavīryajātīya iti /
body.translated_text: Relying on four conditions, at eight times, one who manifests laziness and does not arouse energy should be understood: "This person is of a lazy type, of a type that has not aroused energy."

body.text: piṇḍapātasanniśrayam itikaraṇīyaṃ cārikavikramaṇaṃ dhātuvaiṣamyaṃ ca / itīmāni catvāri sthānāny adhiṣṭhāya praṇītaprabhūtabhojanakāyagauravakāle, parīttalūhabhojanakāyaklamakāle, itikaraṇīye prayoktukāmasya balānurakṣaṇakāle, itikaraṇīyaṃ kṛtavataḥ śramakāle, cārikāṃ viprakramitukāmasya balānurakṣaṇakāle, abhiprakrāntasyādhvapariśramakāle, vyādhitasya vyādhiduḥkhasannipātakāle, vyādhivyutthitasya śramyāgamanāśaṅkākāle, iti kusīdajātīyaḥ pudgalaḥ / yāvat kausīdyopadhiṃ na labhate, tāvad asya vīryamātrakaṃ prajñāyate / yadā kausīdyopadhiṃ labhate tadā tvaritatvaritaṃ kausīdyaṃ prāviṣkaroti / tasmāt kusīdajātīya ity ucyate / etadviparyayeṇa catvāry evaitāni sthānāny adhiṣṭhāya, eṣv evāṣṭasu kāleṣu vīryam ārabhamāṇaḥ, abhibhūya kausīdyam ārabdhavīryajātīyaḥ pudgalo veditavyaḥ / sa labhamāno 'pi kausīdyopadhiṃ vīryam ārabhate / prāg evālabhamānaḥ / tasmād ārabdhavīryajātīya ity ucyate //
body.translated_text: [The four conditions are:] dependence on the alms-round, required duties, walking tours, and imbalance of the humors. These are the four conditions. Relying on these, [one becomes lazy] at: the time of bodily heaviness after eating abundant, excellent food; the time of bodily fatigue after eating meager, poor food; the time of preserving strength when wishing to engage in required duties; the time of exhaustion after completing required duties; the time of preserving strength when wishing to set out on a walking tour; the time of fatigue from the journey after having set out; the time of the onset of suffering from illness when sick; and the time of apprehension about fatigue returning when recovering from illness. Thus is a lazy-type person. So long as one does not encounter an occasion for laziness, a mere trace of energy is apparent. But when one encounters an occasion for laziness, one very quickly manifests laziness. Therefore one is called 'lazy-type.' By the reverse of this, relying on these very four conditions, at these very eight times, one who arouses energy, having overcome laziness — such a person should be understood as of the type that has aroused energy. Even when encountering an occasion for laziness, one arouses energy — how much more so when not encountering one. Therefore one is called 'of the type that has aroused energy.'

body.text:
A. II-6 Ms.16b8L, P.213a2, D.186a1, N.199b1, Ch.355b21
aṣṭāv ime samyakpraṇidhānaparigṛhītā iṣṭopapattihetavaḥ / kāmeṣv abhyupapattikodayakāmānāṃ sarveṇa ca sarvaṃ kāmavivekam anabhilaṣatām aṣṭaprakāreṣṭopapattyāyatanopapattaye saṃvartante / manuṣyadurbhagapraṇihitaṃ parīttaṃ dānamayaṃ śīlamayam / evaṃ manuṣyasubhagacāturmahārājakāyikatrāyastriṃśayāmatuṣitanirmāṇaratiparanirmitavaśavartidevapraṇihitaṃ parīttaṃ dānamayaṃ ca śīlamayam //
body.translated_text: These eight causes of desired rebirth, comprised by right aspiration — for those who, amid sensual pleasures, produce the arising of desire for sensual pleasures and do not at all long for the complete separation from sensual pleasures — conduce to rebirth in eight kinds of desired realms: aspiration for [rebirth as] an unfortunate human, [produced by] meager giving and moral conduct; similarly, aspiration for [rebirth as] a fortunate human, in the realm of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> (Four Great Kings), <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-three), <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> (Delighting in Creation), and <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> (Controlling Others' Creations) gods, [each produced by] meager giving and moral conduct.

body.text:
A. II-7 Ms.17a1R, P.213a5, D.186a3, N.199b3, Ch.355b25
caturbhiḥ kāraṇair manuṣyeṣu catasṛṇāṃ tathāgatasya parṣadāṃ vyavasthānaṃ veditavyam / tribhiḥ kāraṇair devabhūtānāṃ catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ vyavasthānaṃ veditavyam / agryābhidhānabhūtatvāt, dakṣiṇīyasamantatvāt, aparādhīnabhogavṛttitvāt, samutsṛṣṭabhogavṛttitvāt, ebhiś caturbhiḥ kāraṇair manuṣyabhūtānāṃ catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ vyavasthānaṃ veditavyam / bhūmibhāgasanniśritaparyantatvāt, kāmadhātuparyantatvāt, vāksaṃskāraparyantatvāt / devabhūtānāṃ catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ vyavasthānaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text: The classification of the four assemblies of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (Thus-gone One) among humans should be understood by four reasons; the classification of the four assemblies among those who have become gods should be understood by three reasons. By being in truth the foremost, by being everywhere worthy of offerings, by having an independent mode of livelihood, and by having a relinquished mode of livelihood — by these four reasons the classification of the four assemblies among humans should be understood. By being limited to a region of the world, by being limited to the desire realm, and by being limited to verbal formations — the classification of the four assemblies among those who have become gods should be understood.

body.text:
A. II-8 Ms.17a3L, P.213b1, D.186a6, N.199b6, Ch.355c2
triṣu laukikeṣu sthāneṣu vartamāno lokaḥ satatasamitam aṣṭābhir dharmaiḥ spṛśyate / icchāyām, vyavasāye, pratyaye ca / icchāyāṃ vartamāno lābhenāpi spṛśyate, alābhenāpi / vyavasāye vartamāno parābhimate vā parānabhimate vā, parokṣāgatena varṇāvarṇavādena spṛśyate, saṃmukhānugatena vā / pratyaye vartamānaḥ pūrvake dṛṣṭadhārmike vā sukhapratyaye duḥkhapratyaye vā sukhaduḥkhābhyām spṛśyate //
body.translated_text: A being moving in three worldly situations is constantly and continuously touched by eight <s>dharmas</s> — in desire, in endeavor, and in circumstance. Moving in desire, one is touched by gain and by non-gain. Moving in endeavor, one is touched either by the esteem or the disesteem of others — by talk of praise or blame that comes indirectly, or that comes face to face. Moving in circumstance, one is touched by happiness and suffering — [arising] from a prior cause, experienced in this visible life, or from a cause of happiness or a cause of suffering.

body.text:
A. II-9 Ms.17a4M, P,213b4, D.186b1, N.200a1, Ch.355c7
aṣṭāv ime 'nāgāminām arhatāṃ vādhimokṣā āryaprabhāvamahāvihārābhinirhārāya saṃvartante / avibhūyādhyātmaṃ rūpasaṃjñāṃ bahirasaṃkliṣṭarūpādhimokṣaḥ / vibhūyādhyātmaṃ rūpasaṃjñāṃ dvitīyaḥ / śubhāśubhādvayarūpaparamopekṣādhimokṣaḥ / itīme trayo 'dhimokṣāḥ sarvarūpavaśitvāyāryarddhinirhārāya (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> II 302

children.text: ) saṃvartante / yeyam ṛddhir asādhāraṇā sarvapṛthagjanaiḥ / ākāśānantādhimokṣaḥ, vijñānānantādhimokṣaḥ, ākiñcanādhimokṣaḥ, naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanādhimokṣaḥ, sūkṣmasūkṣmasvarasavāhicittādhimokṣaś ca, itīme pañcādhimokṣā anupūrveṇa suparikarmakṛtāḥ saṃjñāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiparamavihāranirhārāya saṃvartante //
children.translated_text: — that supernatural power which is unshared with all ordinary persons. The resolve of infinite space, the resolve of infinite consciousness, the resolve of nothingness, the resolve of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, and the resolve of extremely subtle mind that proceeds with the current of its own nature — these five resolves, when well-practiced in sequence, conduce to the accomplishment of the supreme abiding in the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling.

body.translated_text: These eight resolves (<s>adhimokṣa</s>) of <s>anāgāmins</s> (non-returners) and <s>arhats</s> conduce to the accomplishment of noble powers and great abidings. Without having overcome the internal perception of form, the resolve regarding external, undefiled forms. Having overcome the internal perception of form — the second. The resolve of supreme equanimity regarding forms that are neither fair nor foul — beyond the duality. These three resolves conduce to mastery over all form and to the accomplishment of noble supernatural powers

body.text:
A. II-10 Ms.17a6M, P.214a1, D.186b5, N.200a6, Ch.355c16
yāni ca rūpāṇi paśyati yathā ca paśyati, triṣu vimokṣeṣu prathameṣu prayukta iti vimokṣatrayaprayogamārgaṃ saṃjānāti, aṣṭāv abhibhvāyatanāni veditavyāni / tatra parīttāni mahadgatāni suvarṇadurvarṇāni hīnapraṇītāni rūpāṇi paśyati bahirdhāsamāhitagocarāṇy ābhāsaprāptāni / samādhigocarālambanena manasikāreṇānābhāsagatāyām abhibhūya, śamathākāreṇa tāni samādhigocarāni [śes so / lhag mthoṅ gi rnam pas ni mthoṅ ste / tiṅ ṅe 'dzin gyi spyod yul de dag ji ltar] jānāti paśyati / yathā tāni tena vimṛṣṭāni bhavanty upalakṣitāni tathā saṃjñiteṣu bahirdhāsamādhigocareṣu bhavati / evaṃ tāni rupāṇi paśyati /
body.translated_text: Whatever forms one sees and however one sees [them], when engaged in the first three liberations — thus one recognizes the path of practice of the three liberations. The eight <s>abhibhvāyatanas</s> (bases of mastery) should be understood. Therein, one sees forms externally — limited, great, well-colored, ill-colored, inferior, excellent — forms that have come within the range of the concentrated mind, that have come into appearance. By attending with the mental attention of the object of concentration, and having mastered [forms] that have not come into appearance — by the mode of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding), those objects of concentration [one knows]; and by the mode of <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) one sees — thus one knows and sees those objects of concentration. As those [forms] have been examined and discerned by that [practitioner], so it is with the externally designated objects of concentration. Thus one sees those forms.

body.text: aṣṭakair buddhavacanajñeyādhiṣṭhānaṃ samāptam //
body.translated_text: The section on the bases of knowledge of the <s>Buddha's</s> word in groups of eight is complete.

body.text:
A. IIl-1 Ms.17a8R, P.214a6, D.187a1, N.200b3, Ch.355c26
navānāṃ saṃyojanānāṃ vyavasthānaṃ veditavyam / vastusaṃgrahaṇyām /
body.translated_text: The classification of the nine fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>) should be understood — as in the <s>Vastusaṃgrahaṇī</s>.

body.text:
A. IIl-2 Ms.17b1L, P.214a7, D.187a2, N.200b4, Ch.355c27
navemāny upapattyāyatanāni yeṣūpapannānāṃ sattvānāṃ tatra tatra samānasaṃvāsatā prajñāyate / sthāpayitvāpāyān pūrvasmin nirvitpadasthānabhūtatvāt //
body.translated_text: These are the nine realms of rebirth (<s>upapattyāyatana</s>), in which beings who have been reborn are recognized as dwelling together in the same abode — excluding the lower realms, because they are not established places [in the sense intended] here.

body.text: navakair buddhavacanajñeyādhiṣṭhānaṃ samāptam // //
body.translated_text: The section on the bases of knowledge of the <s>Buddha's</s> word in groups of nine is complete.

body.text:
A. IV-1 Ms. 17b1 R, P.214a8, D. 187a3, N.200b5, Ch.356a1
daśabhiḥ kṛtsnāyatanair vimokṣāṇāṃ kāryapariniṣpattir veditavyā / śeṣaṃ vimokṣābhibhvāyatanakṛtsnāyatanānāṃ tadyathā vastusaṃgrahaṇyām /
body.translated_text: Through the ten <s>kṛtsnāyatanas</s> (bases of totality), the completion of the function of the liberations should be understood. The remainder regarding the liberations, the bases of mastery, and the bases of totality — as in the <s>Vastusaṃgrahaṇī</s>.

body.text:
A. IV-2 Ms.17b2L, P.214b2, D.187a4, N.200b6, Ch.356a3
daśabhir aśaikṣair aṅgaiḥ pañcānām aśaikṣāṇāṃ skandhānāṃ saṃgraho veditavyaḥ / śīlasamādhiprajñāvimuktivimuktijñānadarśanaskandhānām //
body.translated_text: Through the ten factors of the beyond-trainee (<s>aśaikṣa</s>), the inclusion of the five aggregates of the beyond-trainee should be understood — [namely, the aggregates of] moral conduct, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation.

body.text: daśakair buddhavacane jñeyādhiṣṭhānaṃ samāptam //
body.translated_text: The section on the bases of knowledge of the <s>Buddha's</s> word in groups of ten is complete.

body.text: samāptaṃ ca buddhavacanajñeyādhiṣṭhānam // //
body.translated_text: And the bases of knowledge of the <s>Buddha's</s> word are complete.

body.text:
B. Ms.17b2R, P.214b4, D.187a5, N.201a1, Ch.356a8
cikitsā katamā, sā caturākārā veditavyā / tadyathābādhakauśalyam, ābādhasamutthānakauśalyam, utpannasyābādhasya prahāṇakauśalyam, prahīṇasyābādhasyāyātyām anutpādakauśalyam / eṣāṃ ca kauśalyānāṃ vibhaṅgo yathā sūtram eva veditavyaḥ // //
body.translated_text: What is medicine (<s>cikitsā</s>)? It should be understood as having four aspects: namely, skill in [recognizing] illness, skill in [recognizing] the origin of illness, skill in the abandonment of arisen illness, and skill in the non-arising of abandoned illness in the future. And the analysis of these skills should be understood just as in the <s>Sūtra</s>.
[Section marker]

body.text:
D. Ms.23a3L, P.228b6, D.199b2, N.214a2, Ch.360c21
śabdavidyā katamā / sā ṣaḍākārā draṣṭavyā / dharmaprajñaptivyavasthānataḥ / arthaprajñaptivyavasthānataḥ / pudgalaprajñaptivyavasthānataḥ / kālaprajñaptivyavasthānataḥ / saṃkhyāprajñaptivyavasthānataḥ / sakhilādhikaraṇavyavasthānataś ca //
body.translated_text: What is the science of language (<s>śabdavidyā</s>)? It should be seen as having six aspects: through the classification of the designation of <s>dharmas</s>, through the classification of the designation of meaning, through the classification of the designation of persons, through the classification of the designation of time, through the classification of the designation of number, and through the classification of the inclusive basis.

body.text: uddānam //
body.translated_text: Summary verse:

body.text:
dharmārthapudgalaḥ kālāḥ saṃkhyādhikaraṇaṃ ca yat /
sakhilaṃ tad adhiṣṭhānaṃ śabdasyeha samāsataḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s>, meaning, person, time, number, and the inclusive basis — these, in brief, are the bases of language.

body.text:
D.I. Ms.23a4L, P.229a1, D.199b4, N.214a4, Ch.360c28
tatra dharmaprajñaptivyavasthānaṃ nāmakāyapadakāyavyañjanakāyāḥ / pañcaguṇayuktaś ca śabdaḥ / agrāmyalaghvojasvī saṃbaddhaḥ svarthaś ca /
body.translated_text: Therein, the classification of the designation of <s>dharmas</s> is: noun-groups, sentence-groups, and phoneme-groups. And speech endowed with five qualities: not vulgar, light, vigorous, connected, and conveying its own meaning.

body.text:
D.II. Ms.23a4R, P.229a2, D.199b5, N.214a5, Ch.361a2
tatrārthaprajñaptivyavasthānaṃ daśākāraṃ veditavyam / indriyavyavasthānataḥ / mahābhūtavyavasthānataḥ / karmavyavasthānataḥ / paryeṣaṇāvyavasthānataḥ / adharmavyavasthānataḥ / dharmavyavasthānataḥ / saṃpattivyavasthānataḥ / vipattivyavasthānataḥ / upabhogavyavasthānataḥ / anurakṣaṇāvyavasthānataś ca //
body.translated_text: Therein, the classification of the designation of meaning should be understood as having ten aspects: through the classification of faculties, through the classification of great elements, through the classification of actions, through the classification of seeking, through the classification of <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness), through the classification of <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), through the classification of success, through the classification of failure, through the classification of enjoyment, and through the classification of protection.

body.text: uddānam //
body.translated_text: Summary verse:

body.text:
cakṣurādi pṛthivyādi kāyakarmādi caiṣaṇā /
adharmadharmasaṃpattivipadbhogānurakṣaṇā /
body.translated_text: The eye and so forth, earth and so forth, bodily action and so forth, seeking; <s>adharma</s>, <s>dharma</s>, success, failure, enjoyment, and protection.

body.text:
D.II-1 Ms.23a5R, P.229b5, D.199b7, N.214b1, Ch.361a8
tatrendriyavyavasthānatas tadyathā darśanārthaḥ śravaṇārtho jighraṇārthaḥ svādanārthaḥ sparśanārtho vijānanārthaś ca /
body.translated_text: Therein, through the classification of faculties: namely, for the purpose of seeing, for the purpose of hearing, for the purpose of smelling, for the purpose of tasting, for the purpose of touching, and for the purpose of cognizing.

body.text:
D.II-2 Ms.23a6M, P.229b6, D.200a1, N.214b2, Ch.361a9
tatra mahābhūtavyavasthānataḥ / tadyathā pratiṣṭhādyarthaḥ / abhiṣyandanādyarthaḥ, dīpādyarthaḥ / kampanādyarthaś ca //
body.translated_text: Therein, through the classification of great elements: namely, for the purpose of support and so forth, for the purpose of cohesion and so forth, for the purpose of illumination and so forth, and for the purpose of motion and so forth.

body.text:
D.II-3 Ms.23a6R, P.229b7, D.200a2, N.214b2, Ch.361a10 * 1 ḥ i
tatra karmavyavasthānataḥ / tadyathā gamanādyartho bhāṣaṇādyarthaḥ / cetanāsmṛtibuddhyādyarthaś ca //
body.translated_text: Therein, through the classification of actions: namely, for the purpose of going and so forth, for the purpose of speaking and so forth, and for the purpose of volition, mindfulness, understanding, and so forth.

body.text:
D.II-4 Ms.23a7L, P.229b8, D.200a2, N.214b3, Ch.361a11
tatraiṣaṇāvyavasthānataḥ / tadyathā mārgaṇādyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, through the classification of seeking: namely, for the purpose of searching and so forth.

body.text:
D.II-5 Ms.23a7L, P.230a1, D.200a3, N.214b3, Ch.361a12
tatrādharmavyavasthānataḥ / tadyathā hiṃsāsteyādyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, through the classification of <s>adharma</s>: namely, for the purpose of harming, stealing, and so forth.

body.text:
D.II-6 Ms.23a7M, P.230a1, D.200a3, N.214b4, Ch.361a12
tatra dharmavyavasthānataḥ / tadyathā dānasaṃyamādyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, through the classification of <s>dharma</s>: namely, for the purpose of giving, restraint, and so forth.

body.text:
D.II-7 Ms.23a7M, P.230a2, D.200a3, N.214b4, Ch.361a13
tatra saṃpattivyavasthānataḥ / tadyathā prāptiprītiharṣādyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, through the classification of success: namely, for the purpose of attainment, delight, joy, and so forth.

body.text:
D.II-8 Ms.23a7R, P.230a3, D.200a4, N.214b5, Ch.361a13
tatra vipattivyavasthānataḥ / tadyathā nāśabhayadainyādyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, through the classification of failure: namely, for the purpose of loss, fear, misery, and so forth.

body.text:
D.II-9 Ms.23a8L, P.230a3, D.200a4, N.214b5, Ch.361a14
tatropabhogavyavasthānataḥ / tadyathā bhojanapānācchādanāliṅganopacārādyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, through the classification of enjoyment: namely, for the purpose of eating, drinking, clothing, embracing, engaging, and so forth.

body.text:
D.11-10 Ms.23a8L, P.230a4, D.200a5, N.214b6, Ch.361a15
tatrānurakṣaṇāvyavasthānataḥ / tadyathā pālanaposaṇabharaṇādyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, through the classification of protection: namely, for the purpose of guarding, nourishing, maintaining, and so forth.

body.text: api khalu ṣaḍbhir ākāraiḥ samāsato 'rtho veditavyaḥ / svabhāvārtho hetvarthaḥ phalārthaḥ kriyārtho viśeṣasaṃyogārthaḥ pravṛttyarthaś ca /
body.translated_text: Moreover, in brief, meaning should be understood through six aspects: the meaning of own-nature, the meaning of cause, the meaning of fruit, the meaning of action, the meaning of special conjunction, and the meaning of activity.

body.text: uddānam //
body.translated_text: Summary verse:

body.text: svabhāvahetutatkāryatatkriyāyogavṛttibhiḥ /
body.translated_text: Through own-nature, cause, its effect, its action, conjunction, and activity.

body.text:
D.III. Ms.23b1L, P,230a6, D.200a6, N.214b7, Ch.361a21
tatra pudgalaprajñaptivyavasthānam / strīpuṃnapuṃsakavyavasthānataḥ / prathamamadhyamottamapuruṣavyavasthānataś ca //
body.translated_text: Therein, the classification of the designation of persons: through the classification of feminine, masculine, and neuter. And through the classification of first, middle, and last person.

body.text:
D.IV. Ms.23b1M, P,230a7, D.200a7, N.215a1, Ch.361a24
tatra kālaprajñāptivyavasthānam / trividhaḥ kālo 'tīto 'tītaviśiṣṭaḥ, anāgato 'nāgataviśiṣṭaḥ, vartamāno vartamānaviśiṣṭaś ca /
body.translated_text: Therein, the classification of the designation of time: Time is threefold — past, characterized by the past; future, characterized by the future; present, characterized by the present.

body.text:
D.V. Ms.23b1R, P,230a8, D.200a7, N.215a2, Ch.361a27
tatra saṃkhyāprajñaptivyavasthānam / trividhā saṃkhyā / ekasaṃkhyā dvisaṃkhyā bahusaṃkhyā ca /
body.translated_text: Therein, the classification of the designation of number: Number is threefold — singular number, dual number, and plural number.

body.text:
D.VI. Ms.23b2L, P.230b1, D.200b1, N.215a2, Ch.361a29
tatrādhikaraṇavyavasthānam / khilavyavasthānaṃ ca / pañcādhikaraṇāni sandhināmasamāsas taddhitam ākhyātaṃ ca / khilaṃ punar dhātupāṭhādi tad ubhayam api samasya sakhilam adhikaraṇam ity ucyate /
body.translated_text: Therein, the classification of the basis. And the classification of the <s>khila</s> (supplement): There are five bases — <s>sandhi</s> (juncture), <s>nāmasamāsa</s> (nominal compound), <s>taddhita</s> (secondary derivation), and <s>ākhyāta</s> (verb). The <s>khila</s> (supplement) is the list of roots (<s>dhātupāṭha</s>) and so forth. Both of these taken together are called the inclusive basis.

body.text:
E. Ms.23b2R, P.230b2, D.200b2, N.215a4, Ch.361b4
tatra śilpakarmasthānavidyā katamā / samāsato dvādaśākāraṃ śilpaṃ / tatra yaj jñānaṃ sā śilpakarmasthānavidyety ucyate / dvādaśākāraṃ śilpaṃ katamat / tadyathā kṛṣiśilpaṃ vaṇijyaśilpaṃ rājapauruṣyaśilpaṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> II 312

children.text: ) lipigaṇanasaṃkhyāmudrāśilpaṃ naimittikaśilpaṃ mantriśilpaṃ ghaṭānaśilpaṃ saṃjananaśilpaṃ vānaśilpaṃ saṃyojanaśilpaṃ pākaśilpam gāndharvaśilpaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: the art of writing, calculation, reckoning, and seals; the art of divination; the art of counsel; the art of warfare; the art of procreation; the art of weaving; the art of combining; the art of cooking; and the art of music and performance.

body.translated_text: Therein, what is the knowledge of arts and crafts (<s>śilpakarmasthānavidyā</s>)? In brief, there are twelve arts. The knowledge regarding those is called the knowledge of arts and crafts. What are the twelve arts? Namely: the art of agriculture, the art of commerce, the art of royal service,

body.text: // yogācārabhūmau śrutamayī bhūmiḥ //
body.translated_text: In the <s>Yogācārabhūmi</s>: the stage born of hearing.

body.text:
Appendix III
cintāmayī bhūmiḥ
body.translated_text: Appendix III: The Stage Born of Reflection (<s>Cintāmayī Bhūmi</s>)

body.text:
Ms.23b4L, P.230b6, D.200b5, N.215a6, Ch.361b11
cintāmayī bhūmiḥ katamā / sā samāsatas tryākārā veditavyā / svabhāvaviśuddhito jñeyapravicayato dharmapravicayataś ca //
body.translated_text: What is the stage born of reflection? In brief, it should be understood as having three aspects: through the purity of own-nature, through the investigation of the knowable, and through the investigation of <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text:
A. Ms.23b4M, P.230b7, D.200b5, N.215a7, Ch.361b18
tatra svabhāvaviśuddhiḥ katamā / sā navākārā veditavyā / yathāpi tad ekatyo yathāśrutān yathāparyāptān dharmān ekākī rahogataś cintayati / acintyaṃ parivarjayitvā cintyaṃ cintayati / kālāpadeśamahāpadeśaṃ ca parijānāti / arthapratisaraṇaś ca cintayati, na vyañjanapratisaraṇaḥ / kiṃcic ca śraddhayādhimucyate, kiṃcit prajñayā vyavacārayati dṛḍhaṃ ca cintayati / sthiraṃ ca cintayati / pratanuṃ ca cintayati / tāṃ ca cintāṃ paryavasānagatāṃ karoti, nāntarāviṣādam āpadyate / ity anayā navākārayā viśuddhyā suviśuddhā cintety ucyate //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the purity of own-nature? It should be understood as having nine aspects. Just as here someone, alone and secluded, reflects upon <s>dharmas</s> as heard and as learned. Avoiding what should not be contemplated, one contemplates what should be contemplated. One understands the reference to time and the great reference. One reflects relying on meaning, not relying on the letter. Some things one accepts through faith; some things one ascertains through wisdom. One reflects firmly. One reflects steadily. One reflects subtly. And one brings that reflection to its completion, and does not fall into discouragement midway. Through this purity in nine aspects, the reflection is called well-purified.

body.text:
B. Ms.23b6L, P.231a3, D.201a1, N.215b4, Ch.361d ḥ .0
tatra jñeyapravicayaḥ katamaḥ / yaḥ parīkṣyasyārthasya pravicayaḥ / parīkṣyo 'rthaḥ katamaḥ / sac ca sato 'sac cāsataḥ parīkṣyo 'rtha ity ucyate //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the investigation of the knowable? The investigation of the object to be examined. What is the object to be examined? The existent of the existent and the non-existent of the non-existent — this is called the object to be examined.

body.text:
B. I. Ms.23b6M, P.231a5, D.201a2, N.215b5, Ch.361c4 't
parīkṣyaṃ sadvastu katamat / tat pañcavidhaṃ draṣṭavyam / svalakṣaṇasat sāmānyalakṣaṇasat saṃketalakṣaṇasad dhetulakṣaṇasat phalalakṣaṇasac ca //
body.translated_text: What is the existent object to be examined? It should be seen as fivefold: existent by its own characteristic (<s>svalakṣaṇasat</s>), existent by its general characteristic (<s>sāmānyalakṣaṇasat</s>), existent by convention (<s>saṃketalakṣaṇasat</s>), existent by its characteristic of being a cause (<s>hetulakṣaṇasat</s>), and existent by its characteristic of being an effect (<s>phalalakṣaṇasat</s>).

body.text:
B. I-1 Ms.23b7L, P,231a6, D.201a3, N.215b6,Ch.361c7
svalakṣaṇasat katamat / tat trividhaṃ draṣṭavyam / paramārthalakṣaṇasan nimittalakṣaṇasad vartamāṇalakṣaṇasac ca /
body.translated_text:
B. I-1 Ms.23b7L, P.231a6, D.201a3, N.215b6, Ch.361c7
What is the existent characterized by its own characteristic (<s>svalakṣaṇasat</s>)? It should be seen as threefold: the existent characterized by ultimate reality (<s>paramārthalakṣaṇasat</s>), the existent characterized by a sign (<s>nimittalakṣaṇasat</s>), and the existent characterized by the present (<s>vartamāṇalakṣaṇasat</s>).
