body.text: paramārthalakṣaṇasat katamat / yo nirabhilapyo 'rthaḥ sarvadharmeṣu lokottarajñānagocaro 'vyavasthāpyalakṣaṇaḥ /
body.translated_text: What is the existent characterized by ultimate reality? That which is an inexpressible object, the domain of supramundane knowledge in all <s>dharmas</s>, whose characteristic cannot be established [in words].

body.text: nimittasat katamat / tac caturbhir ākārair draṣṭavyam / yatra nāmopalabhyate / vastūpalabhyate / tac ca nāma tasmin vastuni na vyabhicarati bhrāntivyabhicārato vānityavyabhicārato vā / tac ca nāma tasmin vastuny avyāhataṃ pravartate / na kvacid anuvartate kvacid vyāvartate /
body.translated_text: What is the existent characterized by a sign (<s>nimittasat</s>)? It should be seen in four aspects: where a name is found; a thing is found; and that name does not deviate from that thing — either through the deviation of delusion or through the deviation of impermanence; and that name operates unimpededly with respect to that thing — it does not apply in one case and not apply in another.

body.text: vartamānasat katamat / yad utpannaṃ hetuphalabhūtaṃ ca / tad etat sarvam ekadhyam abhisaṃkṣipya svalakṣaṇasad ity ucyate //
body.translated_text: What is the existent characterized by the present (<s>vartamānasat</s>)? That which has arisen and is in the state of being a cause and effect. All of this, combined together, is called the existent characterized by its own characteristic.

body.text:
B. I-2 Ms.23b8R, P.231b2, D.201a7,N.216a3, Ch.361c16
sāmānyalakṣaṇasat katamat / tad api pañcavidhaṃ draṣṭavyam / jātisāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ kṛtyānuṣṭhānasāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ sarvasaṃskārasāmānyalakṣaṇam sarvasāsravasāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ sarvadharmasāmānyalakṣaṇam ca /
body.translated_text:
B. I-2 Ms.23b8R, P.231b2, D.201a7, N.216a3, Ch.361c16
What is the existent characterized by a general characteristic (<s>sāmānyalakṣaṇasat</s>)? It too should be seen as fivefold: the general characteristic of class (<s>jātisāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>), the general characteristic of functional activity (<s>kṛtyānuṣṭhānasāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>), the general characteristic of all conditioned things (<s>sarvasaṃskārasāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>), the general characteristic of all that is with outflows (<s>sarvasāsravasāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>), and the general characteristic of all <s>dharmas</s> (<s>sarvadharmasāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>).

body.text: jātisāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ katamat / rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ svajātiḥ / saikadhyam abhisaṃkṣipya jātisāmānyalakṣaṇam ity ucyate /
body.translated_text: What is the general characteristic of class? The own-class of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — that, combined together, is called the general characteristic of class.

body.text: kṛtyānuṣṭhānasāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ katamat / kuśalasāsravā dharmā iṣṭaphalābhinirvṛttau kṛtyānuṣṭhānasāmānyalakṣaṇena sāmānyalakṣaṇāḥ / yathā (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 322

children.text: ) kuśalā dharmā iṣṭaphalābhinirvṛttāv evam akuśalā dharmā aniṣṭaphalābhinirvṛttau, smṛtyupasthānāni samyakprahāṇāny ṛddhipādānīndriyāṇi balāni bodhyaṅgāni mārgāṅgāni bodhipakṣyadharmā bodhiprāptau kṛtyānuṣṭhānasāmānyalakṣaṇena sāmānyalakṣaṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: wholesome <s>dharmas</s> [function] in the production of desirable results, so unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> in the production of undesirable results; the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), the right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), the bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), the faculties (<s>indriya</s>), the powers (<s>bala</s>), the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), the path factors (<s>mārgāṅga</s>) — the <s>dharmas</s> conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣyadharma</s>) have a general characteristic of functional activity in the attainment of awakening.

body.translated_text: What is the general characteristic of functional activity? Wholesome <s>dharmas</s> with outflows have a general characteristic of functional activity in the production of desirable results. Just as

body.text: sarvasaṃskārasāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ katamat / anityatā sarvasaṃskārāṇām / sarvasāsravasāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ katamat / duḥkhatā sarvasāsrāvāṇām / sarvadharmasāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ katamat / śūnyatā nairātmyaṃ ca sarvadharmāṇām / tad idam ucyate sāmānyalakṣaṇam //
body.translated_text: What is the general characteristic of all conditioned things? The impermanence of all conditioned things. What is the general characteristic of all that is with outflows? The suffering of all that is with outflows. What is the general characteristic of all <s>dharmas</s>? The emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) and selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>) of all <s>dharmas</s>. This is called the general characteristic.

body.text:
B. I-3 Ms.24a3R, P.232a2, D.201b5, N.216b1, Ch.362a1
saṃketalakṣaṇaṃ katamat / yatra ṣaḍvidho vādaḥ pravartate tat saṃketalakṣaṇaṃ veditavyam / ṣaḍvidho vādaḥ katamaḥ / svāmisaṃbandhayukto vādaḥ, tattadanyānyavarjito vādaḥ, sāṃketiko vādaḥ, sāṃghātiko vādaḥ, asarvatrago vādaḥ, manityaś ca vādaḥ //
body.translated_text:
B. I-3 Ms.24a3R, P.232a2, D.201b5, N.216b1, Ch.362a1
What is the characteristic of convention (<s>saṃketalakṣaṇa</s>)? Where the sixfold discourse operates — that should be understood as the characteristic of convention. What is the sixfold discourse? Discourse connected with ownership (<s>svāmisaṃbandhayukta</s>), discourse excluding what is that of this and what is other of another (<s>tattadanyānyavarjita</s>), conventional discourse (<s>sāṃketika</s>), composite discourse (<s>sāṃghātika</s>), non-universal discourse (<s>asarvatraga</s>), and impermanent discourse (<s>anitya</s>).

body.text:
B. I-3-a Ms.24a4M, P.232a5, D.201 b7, N.216b4, Ch.362a5
svāmisaṃbandhayukto vādaḥ katamaḥ / yo vādaḥ svāmisaṃbandhena lakṣaṇapratyavagamyo bhavati / nāntareṇa svāmisaṃbandham / tadyathā "jātir" ity uktaḥ "kasyeyaṃ jātir" iti, svāmisaṃbandham apekṣate vādaḥ / rūpasya jātir vedanāyāḥ saṃjñāyāḥ saṃskārāṇāṃ vijñānasya jātir no tu "rūpam" ity ukte "kasyedaṃ rūpam" iti svāmisaṃbandham apekṣate vādaḥ /
body.translated_text:
B. I-3-a Ms.24a4M, P.232a5, D.201b7, N.216b4, Ch.362a5
What is discourse connected with ownership? A discourse that is to be understood through the connection with an owner — not apart from the connection with an owner. For example, when 'class' (<s>jāti</s>) is stated, [one asks] 'whose class is this?' — the discourse requires the connection with an owner. The class of form, the class of feeling, of perception, of formations, of consciousness. But when 'form' is stated, [one does not ask] 'whose form is this?' — the discourse does not require the connection with an owner.

body.text: yathā jātir evaṃ jarā sthitir anityataivaṃbhāgīyāś cittaviprayuktāḥ saṃskārā yathāyogaṃ veditavyāḥ / ayam ucyate svāmisaṃbandhayukto vādaḥ / sa ca (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 324
where that operates — that should be understood as the characteristic of convention.

body.translated_text: As with class, so aging, persistence, impermanence, and similar <s>dharmas</s> dissociated from mind (<s>cittaviprayukta saṃskāra</s>) should be understood analogously. This is called discourse connected with ownership. And

body.text:
B. I-3-b Ms.24a6L, P.232b1, D.202a3, N.216b4, Ch.362a12
tattadanyānyavarjito vādaḥ katamaḥ / yo vādo naiva tena tasya naivānyenānyasya nirdeśāya bhavati / sa tattadanyānyavarjita ity ucyate /
body.translated_text:
B. I-3-b Ms.24a6L, P.232b1, D.202a3, N.216b4, Ch.362a12
What is discourse excluding what is that of this and what is other of another? A discourse that designates neither that of this by this, nor another of another by another — that is called 'excluding what is that of this and what is other of another.'

body.text: yas tenaiva tasya vyapadeśāya vādaḥ sa dravyalakṣaṇe 'pi vartate saṃketalakṣaṇe 'pi / yaś cānyenānyasya vyapadeśāya vādaḥ so 'pi dravyalakṣaṇe 'pi vartate saṃketalakṣaṇe 'pi / yaś cāyaṃ naiva tena tasya naivānyenānyasya vyapadeśāya vāda ekāṃśena saṃketalakṣaṇa eva pravartate /
body.translated_text: A discourse that designates that very thing of that very thing — that operates both in the characteristic of substance (<s>dravyalakṣaṇa</s>) and in the characteristic of convention. And a discourse that designates another of another — that too operates in both the characteristic of substance and the characteristic of convention. But a discourse that designates neither that of this by this nor another of another — that, in one respect, operates exclusively in the characteristic of convention.

body.text: katamaś ca tena tasyaiva vyapadeśāya vādo dravyalakṣaṇe pravartate / tadyathā pṛthivyāḥ kāṭhinyam ity yo vādaḥ / kathaṃ saṃketalakṣaṇe 'pi pravartate / aśmano māṇḍalyam ity yo vādaḥ / yathā pṛthivyāḥ kāṭhinyam aśmano māṇḍalyam evam apāṃ dravatvaṃ tailasya piṇḍas tejasa auṣṇyam agner arci vāyoḥ samudīraṇatvam anilasya vegaḥ /
body.translated_text: What discourse designating that of that very thing operates in the characteristic of substance? For example, the discourse 'hardness of earth.' How does it operate in the characteristic of convention? For example, the discourse 'roundness of a stone.' As with hardness of earth and roundness of a stone, so fluidity of water, drop of oil, heat of fire, flame of a fire, mobility of wind, and velocity of a breeze.

body.text: katham anyenānyasya vyapadeśāya vādo dravye sati vartate / tadyathā cakṣuṣor vijñānaṃ kāyasya sparśa ity evamādi / kathaṃ prajñaptisati / tadyathā buddhadattasya guṇamitrasya vā bhojanaṃ pānaṃ yānaṃ vastram alaṃkāra ity evamādi /
body.translated_text: How does a discourse designating another of another operate in the case of substance? For example, 'consciousness of the eyes,' 'touch of the body,' and so forth. How in the case of conventional designation? For example, '<s>Buddhadatta's</s> or <s>Guṇamitra's</s> food, drink, vehicle, clothing, ornament,' and so forth.

body.text: kathaṃ naiva tena tasya nāpy anyenānyasya vyapadeśāya vāda ekāntena saṃketalakṣaṇa eva pravartate / tadyathā gṛhasya dvāraṃ gṛhasya kuḍyaṃ kumbhasya mukhaṃ kumbhasya pārśvaṃ senāyā ratho vanasya vṛkṣaḥ śatasya daśakaṃ daśakasya tṛkam ity evamādi /
body.translated_text: How does a discourse designating neither that of this nor another of another operate exclusively in the characteristic of convention? For example, 'the door of a house,' 'the wall of a house,' 'the mouth of a pot,' 'the side of a pot,' 'the chariot of an army,' 'the tree of a forest,' 'the decade of a hundred,' 'the triad of a decade,' and so forth.

body.text: ayam ucyate tattadanyānyavarjito vādaḥ //
body.translated_text: This is called discourse excluding what is that of this and what is other of another.

body.text:
B. I-3-c Ms.24b2L, P.233a2, D.202b3, N.217b1, Ch.362a29
sāṃketiko vādaḥ katamaḥ / ṣaḍvidhanimittalakṣaṇe vyāvahārikaḥ svabhāvaprajñaptivādaḥ / ṣaḍvidhaṃ nimittalakṣaṇaṃ katamat / vastulakṣaṇaṃ vijñeyalakṣaṇaṃ śubhādilakṣaṇam anugrahādilakṣaṇaṃ vyavahāranimittalakṣaṇam mithyāpratipattyādinimittalakṣaṇaṃ ca /
body.translated_text:
B. I-3-c Ms.24b2L, P.233a2, D.202b3, N.217b1, Ch.362a29
What is conventional discourse (<s>sāṃketika vāda</s>)? The conventional designation of own-nature operating in the sixfold sign-characteristic. What is the sixfold sign-characteristic? The characteristic of a thing (<s>vastulakṣaṇa</s>), the characteristic of the knowable (<s>vijñeyalakṣaṇa</s>), the characteristic of the pleasant and so forth (<s>śubhādilakṣaṇa</s>), the characteristic of benefit and so forth (<s>anugrahādilakṣaṇa</s>), the sign-characteristic of convention (<s>vyavahāranimittalakṣaṇa</s>), and the sign-characteristic of wrong practice and so forth (<s>mithyāpratipattyādinimittalakṣaṇa</s>).

body.text: vastulakṣaṇaṃ katamat / yad vijñānena gṛhṇāti /
body.translated_text: What is the characteristic of a thing? That which consciousness apprehends.

body.text: vijñeyalakṣaṇaṃ katamat / yan manaskāreṇa vijñānasyotpattaye saṃvartate / śubhādilakṣaṇaṃ katamat / yat sparśena gṛhṇāti /
body.translated_text: What is the characteristic of the knowable? That which, through mental attention, conduces to the arising of consciousness. What is the characteristic of the pleasant and so forth? That which contact apprehends.

body.text: anugrahādilakṣaṇaṃ katamat / yad vedanayā gṛhṇāti /
body.translated_text: What is the characteristic of benefit and so forth? That which feeling apprehends.

body.text: vyavahāranimittalakṣaṇaṃ katamat / yat saṃjñayā gṛhṇāti /
body.translated_text: What is the sign-characteristic of convention? That which perception apprehends.

body.text: mithyāpratipattyādinimittalakṣaṇaṃ katamat / yac cetanayā gṛhṇāti //
body.translated_text: What is the sign-characteristic of wrong practice and so forth? That which volition (<s>cetanā</s>) apprehends.

body.text:
B. I-3-d Ms.24b4L, P.233a7, D.202b7, N.217b6, Ch.362b7
sāṃghātiko vādaḥ katamaḥ / yaḥ prabhūteṣu samagreṣu samuditeṣu svabhāvavyavasthānavādaḥ / tadyathādhyātmaṃ rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñāneṣv ātmādivādo bahirdhā vā rūpagandharasaspraṣṭavyeṣu tathā tathā sanniviṣṭeṣu gṛhakumbhasenāvanādivādaḥ //
body.translated_text:
B. I-3-d Ms.24b4L, P.233a7, D.202b7, N.217b6, Ch.362b7
What is composite discourse (<s>sāṃghātika vāda</s>)? The discourse that establishes own-nature when many [things] are assembled together. For example, internally, in form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — discourse of self and so forth; or externally, in forms, scents, tastes, and tangibles arranged in such and such a way — discourse of house, pot, army, forest, and so forth.

body.text:
B. I-3-e Ms.24b4R, P.233b2, D.203a2, N.218a1, Ch.362b11
asarvatrago vādaḥ katamaḥ / yo vādaḥ kvacid anuvartate, kvacid vyāvartate / tadyathā gṛhe gṛhavādo grāmanagararāṣṭrādibhyo vyāvartate / kumbhe kumbhavādo ghaṭaghaṭīśarāvādibhyo vyāvartate / senāvādaḥ pṛthakstrīpuruṣadārakadārikādibhyo vyāvartate / vanavādaḥ pṛthagvṛkṣamūlagaṇḍapatrapuṣpaphalādibhyo vyāvartate //
body.translated_text:
B. I-3-e Ms.24b4R, P.233b2, D.203a2, N.218a1, Ch.362b11
What is non-universal discourse (<s>asarvatraga vāda</s>)? A discourse that applies in one case and does not apply in another. For example, the discourse 'house' in a house does not apply to a village, city, country, and so forth. The discourse 'pot' in a pot does not apply to a jar, a small jar, a bowl, and so forth. The discourse 'army' does not apply to individual women, men, boys, girls, and so forth. The discourse 'forest' does not apply to individual trees, roots, trunks, leaves, flowers, fruits, and so forth.

body.text:
B. I-3-f Ms.24b6L, P.233b5, D.203a4, N.218a3, Ch.362b18
anityo vādaḥ katamaḥ / sa caturbhir ākārair draṣṭavyaḥ / bhedato 'bhedato 'bhisaṃskārataḥ pariṇāmataś ca /
body.translated_text:
B. I-3-f Ms.24b6L, P.233b5, D.203a4, N.218a3, Ch.362b18
What is impermanent discourse (<s>anitya vāda</s>)? It should be seen in four aspects: through breaking, through non-breaking, through fabrication, and through transformation.

body.text: kathaṃ bhedataḥ / tadyathā kumbhe bhagne yaḥ kumbha iti vādaḥ so 'vahīyate / kapālavādaḥ prādurbhavati /
body.translated_text: How through breaking? For example, when a pot is broken, the discourse 'pot' ceases and the discourse 'sherd' comes into being.

body.text: katham abhedataḥ / tadyathā nānādravyasamavāyavihite cūrṇe vā dhūpe vā yo nānādravyavādaḥ so 'vahīyate / dhūpacūrṇavādaḥ prādurbhavati /
body.translated_text: How through non-breaking? For example, when powder or incense is compounded from various substances, the discourse of the various substances ceases, and the discourse 'incense' or 'powder' comes into being.

body.text: katham abhisaṃskārataḥ / tadyathānabhisaṃskṛte suvarṇapiṇḍe harṣakaṭakakeyūrādyā abhisaṃskārapariṇate yaḥ suvarṇapiṇḍavādaḥ so 'vahīyate / harṣakaṭakakeyūravādaḥ prādurbhavati /
body.translated_text: How through fabrication? For example, when an unfabricated lump of gold is fashioned into a necklace, bracelet, armlet, and so forth, the discourse 'lump of gold' ceases, and the discourse 'necklace,' 'bracelet,' 'armlet' comes into being.

body.text: kathaṃ pariṇāmataḥ / tadyathā pariṇate bhojanapāne yo bhojanapānavādaḥ so 'vahīyate / uccāraprasrāvavādaḥ prādurbhavati /
body.translated_text: How through transformation? For example, when food and drink have been transformed, the discourse 'food and drink' ceases, and the discourse 'feces and urine' comes into being.

body.text: ity ayam evaṃbhāgīyo 'nityo vādo veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Such an impermanent discourse of this kind should be understood.

body.text: ity ayaṃ ṣaḍvidho vādo yatra pravartate tat saṃketalakṣaṇaṃ veditavyam / idam ucyate saṃketalakṣaṇam //
body.translated_text: This sixfold discourse — where it operates, that should be understood as the characteristic of convention. This is called the characteristic of convention.

body.text:
B. I-4 Ms.24b8M, P.234a4, D.203b2, N.218b2, Ch.362b28
hetulakṣaṇaṃ katamat / tat samāsataḥ pañcavidhaṃ draṣṭavyam / iṣṭahetur aniṣṭahetuḥ puṣṭihetuḥ pravṛttihetur nivṛttihetuś ca /
body.translated_text:
B. I-4 Ms.24b8M, P.234a4, D.203b2, N.218b2, Ch.362b28
What is the characteristic of cause (<s>hetulakṣaṇa</s>)? In brief, it should be seen as fivefold: the cause of the desirable (<s>iṣṭahetu</s>), the cause of the undesirable (<s>aniṣṭahetu</s>), the cause of augmentation (<s>puṣṭihetu</s>), the cause of occurrence (<s>pravṛttihetu</s>), and the cause of cessation (<s>nivṛttihetu</s>).

body.text: iṣṭahetuḥ katamaḥ / kuśalasāsravā dharmāḥ /
body.translated_text: What is the cause of the desirable? Wholesome <s>dharmas</s> with outflows.

body.text: aniṣṭahetuḥ katamaḥ / akuśalā dharmāḥ /
body.translated_text: What is the cause of the undesirable? Unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: puṣṭihetuḥ katamaḥ / pūrvotpannāḥ kuśalākuśalāvyākṛtā dharmā āsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtāḥ paścādutpannānāṃ kuśalākuśalāvyākṛtānāṃ dharmāṇām uttarottarāṇāṃ puṣṭatarāṇāṃ puṣṭatamānāṃ puṣṭihetur ity ucyante //
body.translated_text: What is the cause of augmentation? Previously arisen wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate <s>dharmas</s>, when practiced, cultivated, and made much of, are called the cause of augmentation for subsequently arisen wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate <s>dharmas</s> that are progressively more augmented and most augmented.

body.text: pravṛttihetuḥ katamaḥ / yena bījena yayā vāsanayā yena sahāyena yeṣāṃ dharmānāṃ pravṛttir bhavati sa teṣāṃ pravṛttihetur ity ucyate /
body.translated_text: What is the cause of occurrence? Whatever seed, whatever latent impression, whatever companion by means of which <s>dharmas</s> come into occurrence — that is called their cause of occurrence.

body.text: nivṛttihetuḥ katamaḥ / saṃskāranivṛtteḥ saṃkleśanivṛtteḥ sarvaupaśamiko mārgaḥ pārinirvāṇikaḥ saṃbodhigāmī sasaṃbhāraḥ saprayogaḥ sotpattikaḥ saniṣpattiko nivṛttihetur ity ucyate /
body.translated_text: What is the cause of cessation? The path that leads to the complete pacification of conditioned things and the cessation of defilements — the path that leads to <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, that conduces to awakening, together with its accumulations, its preliminary practice, its arising, and its accomplishment — that is called the cause of cessation.

body.text: idaṃ samastaṃ hetulakṣaṇaṃ vistareṇa vibhāgaḥ punar hetuphalacintāyāṃ draṣṭavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: This is the complete characteristic of cause. Its detailed analysis should be seen in the investigation of cause and effect.

body.text:
B. I-5 Ms.25a3L, P.234b2, D.203b7, N.218b7, Ch.362c11
phalalakṣaṇaṃ katamat / yad asmāt pañcavidhād dhetor utpannaṃ prāptaṃ siddhaṃ niṣpannaṃ pravṛttaṃ tat phalalakṣaṇaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text:
B. I-5 Ms.25a3L, P.234b2, D.203b7, N.218b7, Ch.362c11
What is the characteristic of result (<s>phalalakṣaṇa</s>)? Whatever has arisen from this fivefold cause, been obtained, accomplished, brought to completion, and occurred — that should be understood as the characteristic of result.

body.text:
B. II. Ms.25a3M, P.234b3, D.204a1, N.219a1, Ch.362c14
parīkṣyam asadvastu katamat / tad api pañcalakṣaṇaṃ draṣṭavyam / anutpannāsan niruddhāsad itaretarāsat paramārthāsad atyantāsac ca /
body.translated_text:
B. II. Ms.25a3M, P.234b3, D.204a1, N.219a1, Ch.362c14
What is the non-existent to be examined (<s>parīkṣyam asadvastu</s>)? It too should be seen as having five characteristics: the non-existent due to non-arising (<s>anutpannāsat</s>), the non-existent due to cessation (<s>niruddhāsat</s>), the mutually non-existent (<s>itaretarāsat</s>), the non-existent in the ultimate sense (<s>paramārthāsat</s>), and the absolutely non-existent (<s>atyantāsat</s>).

body.text: anutpannāsat katamat / anāgatāḥ saṃskārāḥ /
body.translated_text: What is the non-existent due to non-arising? Future conditioned things.

body.text: niruddhāsat katamat / atītāḥ saṃskārāḥ /
body.translated_text: What is the non-existent due to cessation? Past conditioned things.

body.text: itaretarāsat katamat / yad itaralakṣaṇenetareṣāṃ dharmāṇāṃ virahitatā avidyamānatā, itaradharmāsamavadhānatā vā punar itareṣāṃ dharmāṇām /
body.translated_text: What is the mutually non-existent? The absence, the non-existence, of other <s>dharmas</s> in the characteristic of one; or the non-conjunction of one with the other <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: paramārthāsat katamat / vyāvahārikeṇa svabhāvaprajñaptivādena yaḥ svabhāvo vyavasthāpitaḥ /
body.translated_text: What is the non-existent in the ultimate sense? The own-nature that is established by the conventional designation of own-nature through conventional discourse.

body.text: atyantāsat katamat / vandhyāputrādi yat kiṃcid evaṃbhāgīyam //
body.translated_text: What is the absolutely non-existent? The son of a barren woman and whatever is of this kind.

body.text:
B. III. Ms.25a5L, P.234b7, D.204a4, N.219a5, Ch.362c21
api khalu pañcavidhāstitā pañcavidhaiva nāstitā //
body.translated_text:
B. III. Ms.25a5L, P.234b7, D.204a4, N.219a5, Ch.362c21
Moreover, the fivefold existence is indeed [matched by] a fivefold non-existence.

body.text:
B. IIl-1 Ms.25a5M, P.234b7, D.204a4, N.219a5, Ch.362c21
pañcavidhāstitā katamā / pariniṣpannalakṣaṇāstitā paratantralakṣaṇāstitā parikalpitalakṣaṇāstitā viśeṣalakṣaṇāstitā avaktavyalakṣaṇāstitā ca /
body.translated_text:
B. III-1 Ms.25a5M, P.234b7, D.204a4, N.219a5, Ch.362c21
What is the fivefold existence? The existence characterized by the fully accomplished (<s>pariniṣpannalakṣaṇāstitā</s>), the existence characterized by the dependent (<s>paratantralakṣaṇāstitā</s>), the existence characterized by the imagined (<s>parikalpitalakṣaṇāstitā</s>), the existence characterized by distinction (<s>viśeṣalakṣaṇāstitā</s>), and the existence characterized by the inexpressible (<s>avaktavyalakṣaṇāstitā</s>).

body.text: tatra prathamā pāramārthikaṃ lakṣaṇam /
body.translated_text: Therein, the first is the ultimate characteristic (<s>pāramārthika lakṣaṇa</s>).

body.text: anu dvitīyā pratītyasamutpannalakṣaṇam /
body.translated_text: Following it, the second is the characteristic of being dependently originated (<s>pratītyasamutpanna lakṣaṇa</s>).

body.text: anu tṛtīyā saṃketalakṣaṇam /
body.translated_text: Following it, the third is the conventional characteristic (<s>saṃketa lakṣaṇa</s>).

body.text: anu caturthy adhvalakṣaṇaṃ jātilakṣaṇaṃ jarālakṣaṇaṃ sthitilakṣaṇam anityalakṣaṇaṃ duḥkhalakṣaṇaṃ śūnyalakṣaṇaṃ nairātmyalakṣaṇaṃ vastulakṣaṇaṃ vijñeyalakṣaṇaṃ grāhyalakṣaṇaṃ śubhādilakṣaṇam anugrahādilakṣaṇaṃ vyavahāranimittalakṣaṇaṃ mithyāpratipattyādinimittalakṣaṇam ity evaṃbhāgīyaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ viśeṣalakṣaṇaṃ veditavyam /
body.translated_text: Following it, the fourth comprises the specific characteristics (<s>viśeṣa lakṣaṇa</s>): the characteristic of time (<s>adhva</s>), the characteristic of birth (<s>jāti</s>), the characteristic of aging (<s>jarā</s>), the characteristic of persistence (<s>sthiti</s>), the characteristic of impermanence (<s>anitya</s>), the characteristic of suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>), the characteristic of emptiness (<s>śūnya</s>), the characteristic of non-self (<s>nairātmya</s>), the characteristic of things (<s>vastu</s>), the characteristic of the knowable (<s>vijñeya</s>), the characteristic of the graspable (<s>grāhya</s>), the characteristic of pleasant and so forth (<s>śubhādi</s>), the characteristic of benefit and so forth (<s>anugraha</s>), the characteristic as a sign for conventional usage (<s>vyavahāranimitta</s>), and the characteristic as a sign for wrong practice and so forth (<s>mithyāpratipatti</s>) — these and similar specific characteristics should be understood.

body.text: anu pañcamā caturākārayā avaktavyatayā avaktavyalakṣaṇam / asattvāt tadyathā pudgalaḥ skandhebhyo 'nyo 'nanya iti / gambhīratvān nirabhilapyadharmatā, acintyas tathāgatānāṃ dharmakāyaḥ, acintyo buddhaviṣayaḥ / tathā bhavati tathāgataḥ paraṃmaraṇād ity evamādi / anarthopasaṃhitatvāt tadyathā ye te dharmā adharmārthabrahmacaryopasaṃhitās te 'bhisaṃbuddhā api noktā bhagavatā / tathādharmalakṣaṇavyavasthānatas tadyathā tathatā saṃskārebhyo 'nyānanyatvenāvaktavyā //
body.translated_text: Following it, the fifth is the characteristic of the inexpressible (<s>avaktavya lakṣaṇa</s>), through a fourfold inexpressibility: (1) Due to non-existence — for example, the person (<s>pudgala</s>) is inexpressible as either identical with or different from the aggregates. (2) Due to profundity — the nature of <s>dharmas</s> as inexpressible, the inconceivable <s>Dharmakāya</s> of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the inconceivable domain of the <s>Buddhas</s> — such as 'Does the <s>Tathāgata</s> exist after death?' and similar [questions]. (3) Due to being connected with what is purposeless — such as those <s>dharmas</s> connected with non-<s>Dharma</s>-purpose and non-holy-life-purpose, which even though fully understood by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, were not spoken. (4) Due to the determination of the characteristic of <s>dharmas</s> as such — for example, suchness (<s>tathatā</s>) is inexpressible as either identical with or different from conditioned things (<s>saṃskāra</s>). //

body.text:
B. IIl-2 Ms.25b1M, P.235b7, D.204b4, N.219b6, Ch.363a8
pañcavidhā nāstitā katamā / paramārthalakṣaṇanāstitā svatantralakṣaṇanāstitā sarveṇa sarvaṃ svalakṣaṇanāstitā aviśeṣalakṣaṇanāstitā vaktavyalakṣaṇanāstitā ca // //
body.translated_text: What is the fivefold non-existence? Non-existence of the ultimate characteristic, non-existence of the independent characteristic, non-existence of the own-characteristic in every way, non-existence of the undifferentiated characteristic, and non-existence of the expressible characteristic. // //

body.text:
Appendix IV
Ābhiprāyikārthagāthānirdeśa
body.translated_text: Appendix IV: Exposition of Verses with Intentional Meaning (<s>Ābhiprāyikārthagāthānirdeśa</s>)

children.translated_text: (1) 'O you who have reached perfection in the trainings, destroyer of all doubts,

children.text: śikṣāṃ prabrūhi me pṛṣṭo yā ca śikṣāsu śikṣaṇā // iti //
children.translated_text: tell me, when asked, about the training and the practice of the trainings.' //

body.text: brahmaṇā bhagavān sarvaśikṣāpadaparyantaprāptitaś ca svārthasaṃpadam asādhāraṇām ārabhyotpannotpannasarvasattvasaṃśayacchedakatvena cāsādhāraṇāṃ parārthapratipattim ārabhya stutipūrvaṃ pṛṣṭaḥ "kāḥ kiyatyaś ca śikṣāḥ, kathaṃ ca tāsu śikṣitavyam" //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> was asked by <s>Brahmā</s>, with praise as a preface, with reference to the unsurpassed personal accomplishment through having reached the endpoint of all training rules, and with reference to the unsurpassed practice for the benefit of others through being a cutter of all doubts of beings as they arise: 'What are the trainings, how many are they, and how should one train in them?' //

body.text:
A. I-2 Ms1*a1R, MsG.26b1M, P.245b1, D.212b7, N.229a1, Ch.367a13
tato bhagavān bahukṛtyatābhīṣaṇā alasajātīyānāṃ protsāhanābhiprāyaḥ sarvaśikṣāḥ samasya saṃkṣepatas tisṛbhiḥ śikṣābhir nirdiśati /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, with the intention of encouraging those of lazy disposition through the manifold urgency of duties, encompassing all trainings, briefly indicates them by means of three trainings:

children.translated_text: (2) 'The higher moral conduct, the higher mind, and the higher wisdom, O good sir,

children.text: tisraḥ śikṣāḥ samāsena śṛṇu yā tāsu śikṣaṇā // iti //
children.translated_text: are the three trainings in brief. Listen to the practice of them.' //

body.text: tatra śīlacittaprajñā adhikṛtya vikṣiptacittasya avikṣepāyogopadeśato 'dhiśīlaṃśikṣayā, asamāhitacittasya samādhānāyogopadeśato 'dhicittaṃśikṣayā, samāhitāvimuktacittasya vimokṣāyogopadeśato 'dhiprajñaṃśikṣayā ca, yoginām sarvakṛtyaparisamāpteḥ, tāsv eva tisṛṣu śikṣāsv antarṇīyābhiprāyato bhagavatā deśitāḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, with reference to moral conduct, mind, and wisdom: for one with a scattered mind, through the instruction in the yoga of non-distraction — [this is] the training in higher moral conduct (<s>adhiśīla</s>). For one with an unconcentrated mind, through the instruction in the yoga of concentration — [this is] the training in higher mind (<s>adhicitta</s>). For one with a concentrated but unliberated mind, through the instruction in the yoga of liberation — [this is] the training in higher wisdom (<s>adhiprajñā</s>). Because through these three trainings alone the entire task of <s>yogins</s> is completed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> has taught them with the intention that they encompass all. //

body.text:
A. I-3 Ms 1*a3M, MsG.26b1R, P.245b7, D.213a4, N.229a5, Ch.367a22
tāsu punaḥ śikṣaṇā yena yogena tāḥ śikṣā niṣpādayati / tatra
body.translated_text: And the practice of those trainings is the method by which one accomplishes those trainings. Therein:

children.translated_text: (3) 'One should be endowed with six factors, possessed of the happiness of four abidings,
and should always be purified in the four-aspected knowledge regarding the four [truths].' //

body.text: anayā gāthayā yathākramaṃ tāsāṃ tisṛṇāṃ śikṣāṇāṃ prayogaṃ darśayati / "ṣaḍaṅgasaṃpanna" ity adhiśīlaṃśikṣām adhikṛtya śikṣāṇāṃ ṣaḍaṅgāni / śīlavān viharati, prātimokṣasaṃvarasaṃvṛtaḥ, ācārasaṃpannaḥ, gocarasaṃpannaḥ, aṇumātreṣv avadyeṣu bhayadarśī, samādāya śikṣate śikṣāpadeṣv ity ebhiś ca ṣaḍbhir aṅgaiś caturvidhā śīlaviśuddhiḥ paridīpitā/
body.translated_text: By this verse, he shows the practice of the three trainings in sequence. 'Endowed with six factors' — with reference to the training in higher moral conduct, the six factors of the training are: one dwells virtuous, restrained by the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint, endowed with [proper] conduct, endowed with [proper] resort, seeing danger in the slightest faults, and undertaking and training in the training rules — and by these six factors, the fourfold purity of moral conduct is illuminated.

body.text: tatra "śīlavān viharatī"ty adhikṛtya "prātimokṣasaṃvarasaṃvṛta" ity anena nairyāṇikaśīlatā viśuddhiḥ, mokṣādhikārikaṃ hi nairyāṇikam / "ācāragocarasaṃpanna" ity etābhyām anutkṛṣṭaśīlatā viśuddhiḥ / "aṇumātreṣv avadyeṣu bhayadarśī"ti niśchidraśīlatā viśuddhiḥ / "samādāya śikṣate śikṣāpadeṣv" ity aviparyastaśīlatā viśuddhiḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, with reference to 'one dwells virtuous' — by 'restrained by the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint,' the purity of conduct leading to liberation (<s>nairyāṇika śīlatā</s>) [is indicated], for what leads to liberation is the <s>prātimokṣa</s>. By 'endowed with [proper] conduct and resort,' the purity of not transgressing moral conduct is [indicated]. By 'seeing danger in the slightest faults,' the purity of flawless moral conduct is [indicated]. By 'undertaking and training in the training rules,' the purity of non-erroneous moral conduct is [indicated].

body.text: evaṃ ṣaḍaṅgasaṃpannatayādhiśīlaṃśikṣāprayogaṃ niśritya "catuḥsthitisukhānvita" ity adhicittaṃśikṣāprayogaṃ darśayati /
body.translated_text: Thus, relying on the practice of the training in higher moral conduct through being endowed with six factors, by 'possessed of the happiness of four abidings,' he shows the practice of the training in higher mind.

body.text: catvāri dhyānāni caturvidhā cittasthitiḥ, sā ca dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihāratvāt sukhety ucyate /
body.translated_text: The four <s>dhyānas</s> are the fourfold abiding of mind, and that is called 'happiness' because of its being a happy dwelling in this very life.

body.text: "caturṣu caturākārajñānaśuddhaḥ sadā bhaved" ity adhiprajñaṃśikṣām adhikṛtyāha / caturṣu duḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgasatyeṣv ekaikasminn anityādicaturākārajñānaśuddhiprabhāṣitatvād adhiprajñaṃśikṣāyāḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Should always be purified in the four-aspected knowledge regarding the four [truths]' — this is said with reference to the training in higher wisdom. Because the purity of four-aspected knowledge beginning with impermanence is proclaimed with respect to each of the four truths of suffering, origination, cessation, and path — [this pertains to] the training in higher wisdom. //

children.translated_text: (4) 'One should be well-established in the root, delighting in the pacification of the mind,
conjoined with the noble view and disjoined from the evil view.' //

body.text: anayā gāthayā śikṣātrayasya krameṇotpattiṃ darśayati / mūlaṃ hy adhiśīlaṃ (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 344
) the first training. Because the other two follow from it.

body.translated_text: By this verse, he shows the sequential arising of the triad of trainings. For the root is the higher moral conduct,

body.text: tataḥ śīlavato 'vipratisārādyanupūrvyā cittasamādhānābhiratyā dvitīyā /
body.translated_text: Then, for the virtuous one, through the sequence of non-remorse and so forth, by delight in the concentration of mind — the second [training].

body.text: tataḥ samāhitacittasya yathābhūtadarśanād āryadṛṣṭisaṃyogataḥ pāpadṛṣṭiviyogataś ca tṛtīyā //
body.translated_text: Then, for one with a concentrated mind, through seeing as it truly is, by conjunction with the noble view and disjunction from evil view — the third [training]. //

children.text: (5) ādiśuddho dhyānarataḥ satye ca kuśalo bhavet /
children.translated_text: (5) 'One should be pure at the beginning, delighting in meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), and skilled in truth.'

children.text: utpādayed varjayec ca bṛṃhayet satyam eva ca // iti //
children.translated_text: 'One should generate, avoid, and augment the truth itself.' //

body.text: anayā gāthayā tāsām eva tisṛṇāṃ śikṣāṇāṃ yathākramaṃ śuddhiviśeṣaṃ darśayati / tatra "ādiśuddha" iti prathamāyāḥ / "dhyānarata" iti dvitīyāyāḥ / "satye ca kuśala" iti tṛtīyāyāḥ / tat punaḥ "satyakauśalyam utpādayed" iti mārgasatyasyotpādanāt / "varjayed" iti duḥkhasamudayasatyayor varjanāt / "bṛṃhayed" iti nirodhasatyasya punaḥ punar mṛdumadhyādhimātrakleśaprahāṇanirodhena brṃhaṇāt /
body.translated_text: By this verse, he shows the distinctive purity of those very three trainings in sequence. Therein, 'pure at the beginning' pertains to the first. 'Delighting in meditation' pertains to the second. 'Skilled in truth' pertains to the third. Furthermore, 'one should generate skill in truth' — through the generation of the truth of the path. 'One should avoid' — through the avoidance of the truths of suffering and origination. 'One should augment' — through augmenting the truth of cessation by the progressive abandonment of mild, middling, and intense afflictions.

children.translated_text: (6) 'In the three training-bases, there are four destinations.'

children.text: vivarjayitvā dve gatī dve gatī samudānayet // iti //
children.translated_text: 'Having avoided two destinations, one should cultivate two destinations.' //

body.text: anayā gāthayā śīlacittaprajñākhyeṣu śikṣādhiṣṭhāneṣu śikṣāṇāṃ saṃpādanavipādanād, yathāsaṃbhavaṃ tatphalabhūtā yāś catasro gatayaḥ,
body.translated_text: By this verse, [he shows that] through the accomplishment or non-accomplishment of the trainings in the three training-bases called moral conduct, mind, and wisdom, there are four destinations as their respective fruits:

body.text: kāmadhātau devamanuṣyasaṃgṛhītā sugatir adhiśīlasaṃpattiphalā, kāmadhātāv eva tadanyagatisaṃgṛhītādhiśīlavipattiphalā durgatiḥ, rūpārūpyadhātau devagatisaṃgṛhītādhicittaphalā ūrdhvagatiḥ, traidhātukāparyāpannā cādhiprajñaphalā nirvāṇagatiḥ /
body.translated_text: A good destination included among gods and humans in the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>), which is the fruit of accomplishing higher moral conduct. An evil destination included among other destinies in the desire realm, which is the fruit of failing in higher moral conduct. An upward destination included among the gods of the form and formless realms, which is the fruit of higher mind. And the destination of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, not included in the three realms, which is the fruit of higher wisdom.

body.text: etābhyo gatibhya ādye dve sugatidurgatī varjayitvā, uttare dve ūrdhvagatinirvāṇagatī samudānayel laukikalokottarābhyāṃ mārgābhyām ity etad darśayati //
body.translated_text: Having avoided the first two of these destinations — the good destination and the evil destination — one should cultivate the latter two — the upward destination and the destination of <s>nirvāṇa</s> — by means of the worldly and supramundane paths. This is what he shows. //

body.text:
A. II Ms. 1 *b5R, MsG.26b3M, P.247a7, D.214b1 N.230b5, Ch.367c7
(7) dve dvayapratyupasthāne ekā nirvāṇagāminī / anupūrvopaniṣadabhinnasaṃbhinnabhāvitā // iti //
body.translated_text:
(7) 'By pairs, the two are supports [for the third]; one leads to <s>nirvāṇa</s>;
gradually as prerequisites, they should be cultivated separately and combined.' //

body.text: asyāṃ gāthāyāṃ yathādhiśīlādhicittaśikṣayoḥ prathamāyāś cānupūrveṇādhicittādhiprajñaśikṣādvayopaniṣadbhāvena pratyupasthānam / madhyamāyāś cādhiprajñadhyānasaṃvarasaṃgṛhītādhiśīlaśikṣā dvayopaṇiṣadbhāvena pratyupasthānam / uttamāyāś caikasyā nirvāṇopaniṣadbhāvena pratyupasthānam / vyastasamastānaṃ ca yathāsaṃbhavaṃ bhāvanām / tad darśayati //
body.translated_text: In this verse, just as the trainings in higher moral conduct and higher mind — the first, in sequence, through being a prerequisite for the pair of trainings in higher mind and higher wisdom, is a support. The middle, through being a prerequisite for the pair of higher wisdom and the moral-conduct training included in <s>dhyāna</s> restraint, is a support. And the highest, alone, through being a prerequisite for <s>nirvāṇa</s>, is a support. And the cultivation of them separately and combined, as appropriate — this he shows. //

children.text: (8) niṣkaukṛtyo bhaved ādau paścāc ca sukhito yataḥ /
children.translated_text: (8) 'One should first be free from remorse, and afterward be happy;

children.text: ādyāsau sarvaśikṣāṇāṃ yatra śikṣeta paṇḍitaḥ // iti //
children.translated_text: this first of all trainings is that in which a wise person should train.' //

body.text: anayā gāihayā yathādhiśīlaṃśikṣā avipratisārādyānupūrvyā, uttaropaniṣadbhāvena vartate / tad darśayati //
body.translated_text: By this verse, he shows how the training in higher moral conduct, through the sequence of non-remorse and so forth, functions as a prerequisite for the higher [trainings]. //

children.translated_text: (9) 'By which one should purify knowledge, endowed with the arising of the wholesome,

children.text: madhyāsau sarvaśikṣāṇāṃ yatra śikṣeta paṇḍitaḥ // iti //
children.translated_text: this middle of all trainings is that in which a wise person should train.' //

body.text: adhicittaṃśikṣāyā bhāvanāmayaviśiṣṭakuśalamūlotpattyādyānupūrvyā (

children.translated_text: Śbh II 348
) [functions as] a prerequisite for the highest training — this he shows. //

body.translated_text: The training in higher mind, through the sequence of the arising of distinguished wholesome roots born of cultivation,

children.text: (10) yato vimocayec cittaṃ prapañcaṃ ca nirodhayet /
children.translated_text: (10) 'By which one should liberate the mind and cease conceptual proliferation (<s>prapañca</s>),

children.text: śreṣṭhāsau sarvaśikṣāṇāṃ yatra śikṣeta paṇḍitaḥ // iti //
children.translated_text: this best of all trainings is that in which a wise person should train.' //

body.text: adhiprajñaṃśikṣāyā nirvāṇopaniṣattvāc chreṣṭhatvaṃ darśayati //
body.translated_text: He shows the supremacy of the training in higher wisdom through its being a prerequisite for <s>nirvāṇa</s>. //

children.translated_text: (11) 'The practice leading to impurity, and that leading to a good destination —

children.text: ādyā pratipad ukteyaṃ sā ca niṣkevalā matā // iti //
children.translated_text: this first practice has been stated; and it is considered to be self-sufficient.' //

body.text: yathādhiśīlaṃśikṣā vipāditā durgatihetuḥ, saṃpāditā ca sugatihetuḥ, kevalāpi ca vinottarābhyāṃ śikṣābhyāṃ śakyate saṃpādayitum / tad darśayati //
body.translated_text: He shows how the training in higher moral conduct, when failed, is a cause for evil destinies; when accomplished, a cause for good destinies; and can be accomplished by itself alone, without the other two trainings. //

children.translated_text: (12) 'The practice leading to purification but not leading to the definitive end of everything —

children.text: madhyā pratipad ukteyaṃ māpi niṣkevalā matā // iti //
children.translated_text: this middle practice has been stated; and it is not to be considered self-sufficient.' //

body.text: yathā madhyamā pratipat kāmadhātuvairāgyaviśuddhyā viśuddhagāminī, ūrdhvadhātvavairāgyāt kāmarāgānuśayasya cātyanta [ma phyin pa'i phyir / thams cad gtan du rnam par dag par 'gro ba ma yin pa daṅ / ji ltar mchog med ciṅ daṅ po med par 'ba' źig gis 'grub par mi 'gyur ba de ston to //]
body.translated_text: He shows how the middle practice, through purification by dispassion from the desire realm, leads to purification; [but] since, through dispassion from the upper realms, the latent tendency of desire for sensual pleasures [does not reach] its definitive end [— therefore it is not all-sufficient, and cannot be accomplished by itself alone without the first. This he shows. //]

body.text:
A. II-4-c Ms-, MsG.26b5L, P.248a4, D.215a4, N.231b1, Ch.368a2
(13) viśuddhagāminī pratipad yā sarvātyantagāminī /

children.text: śreṣṭhā pratipad ukteyaṃ sa naivādvayakevala // [ces bya ba ni /
children.translated_text: this best practice has been stated; and it too is not self-sufficient as just one of two.' //

body.translated_text: (13) 'The practice leading to purification that leads to the definitive end of everything —

body.text: khams gsum pa'i 'dod chags daṅ bral ba daṅ / bag la ñal yaṅ gtan phyin pa daṅ ji ltar mchog de thams cad gtan du 'gro ba yin la / sṅa ma gñis med par yaṅ gcig pus 'grub par mi 'gyur ba de ston to //]
body.translated_text: [Because through dispassion from all three realms, even the latent tendencies reach their definitive end, and it is the best since it leads definitively to everything. And yet it cannot be accomplished alone without the prior two. This he shows. //]

body.text:
A. IIl-1 Ms.2*a4L, MsG.26b5M, P.248a6, D.215a5, N.231 b3, Ch.368a5
(14a) śikṣeta yo na śikṣeta ubhau tau paṇḍitau matau /
body.translated_text: (14a) 'One who trains, and one who does not train — both are considered wise.'

body.text: zes bya ba'i tshigs su bcad pa phyed kyis ni bslab pa gsum po 'di dag la bslab pa rnams yaṅ dag par slob kyi / log par mi
body.translated_text: By this half-verse, those who properly train in these three trainings and do not wrongly

body.text: śikṣaṇāt paṇḍitalakṣaṇaṃ darśayati /
body.translated_text: train — he shows the mark of a wise person.

body.text: (14b) śikṣeta yo na śikṣeta ubhau tau bālasaṃmatau // iti //
body.translated_text: (14b) 'One who trains, and one who does not train — both are considered fools.' //

body.text: uttarārdhena mithyāśikṣāṇāṃ naiva ca śikṣāṇāṃ bālalakṣaṇaṃ darśayati //
body.translated_text: By the latter half, he shows the characteristics of the foolish — those who train wrongly and those who do not train at all.

children.translated_text: (15) Through the abandonment of possessions, through the removal of unsuitability,

children.text: pratyakṣatvāc ca jñeyasya śikṣādānaṃ tridhā bhavet // iti //
children.translated_text: and through the direct perception of the knowable — the undertaking of training is threefold.

body.text: yasya gṛhakalatrādiparigṛhītaparityāgād yasya samādhivipakṣasya dauṣṭhulyasya prahāṇād yasya ca catuḥsatyalakṣaṇasya jñeyatattvasya pratyakṣīkaraṇād yathākramaṃ śikṣātrayaṃ saṃpadyate, tad darśayati //
body.translated_text: For one whose household, wife, and other possessions are abandoned, for one whose unsuitability that opposes concentration is eliminated, and for one whose knowable reality characterized by the four truths is directly perceived — in this order, the threefold training is accomplished. This he shows.

body.text:
A. IIl-3 Ms.2*a5M, MsG.26b5R, P.248b3, D.215b1, N.231b7, Ch.368a16
(16a) sālambanānālambanāḥ sūkṣmaudārikasaṃhitāḥ // iti //
body.translated_text:
A. III-3 Ms.2*a5M, MsG.26b5R, P.248b3, D.215b1, N.231b7, Ch.368a16
(16a) With support and without support; endowed with the subtle and the coarse.

body.text: anena gāthārdhenottamayoḥ prathamāyāś ca yathākramaṃ sālambanānālambanatvena sūkṣmaudārikatvena prabhedaṃ darśayati //
body.translated_text: By this half-verse, he shows the distinction of the highest and the first [trainings] in their order — as having support and being without support, as being subtle and coarse.

body.text: (16b) samādānaprāvivekyaghoṣa-ābhogasaṃhṛtāḥ // iti //
body.translated_text: (16b) Characterized by undertaking, by seclusion, and by the voice of instruction.

body.text: uttarārdhena prathamamadhyamottamānāṃ yathākramaṃ pratijñānābhinirhṛtatvaṃ kāyacittavivekābhinirhṛtatvaṃ paraghoṣādhyātmayoniśomanaskārābhinirhṛtatvaṃ ca darśayati //
body.translated_text: By the latter half, he shows that the first, middle, and highest [trainings] are respectively brought about by commitment, brought about by physical and mental seclusion, and brought about by the voice of others and by inward wise attention.

children.text: (17) ekā ekā bhavec chikṣā sadvitīyāparā bhavet /
children.translated_text: (17) One training stands alone; another has a second companion;

children.text: ekā syāt satṛtīyaiva tā budhaḥ samatikramet // iti //
children.translated_text: one has a third as well — the wise one transcends them all.

body.text: prathamām ekāṃ kevalām upadarśayati / madhyamā tu na vinā tām, uttamā na vinā te / tābhyaś ca samatikramo 'śaikṣasyārhato veditavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: He shows that the first stands alone by itself. But the middle does not exist without it, and the highest does not exist without those two. And the transcendence of all three should be understood as belonging to the <s>aśaikṣa</s> (one beyond training), the <s>arhat</s>.

children.translated_text: (18) One whose morality is unbroken, who has undertaken the trainings,
whose conduct is blameless, who avoids the five places.

body.text: "abhraṣṭaśīlaḥ śikṣāsv" iti śīlavān viharatīty etad darśayati / "pratijñopagato bhaved" iti pratimokṣasaṃvarasaṃvṛtatvam / "agarhitasamācāra"' ity ācārāvipattim / "pañcasthānavivarjita" iti gocarāvipattim / pañcasthānāni bhikṣor agocaraḥ, rājakulaṃ ghoṣaḥ pānāgāraṃ veśaś caṇḍālakaṭhinaṃ ca / tatra ghoṣaḥ sūnā draṣṭavyā / tatrodghoṣaurabhrikādibhir abhyastāvadyaṃ pāpakarmorabhrādivadhaḥ kriyate //
body.translated_text: "One whose morality is unbroken in the trainings" — this shows that one dwells endowed with moral virtue. "Who has undertaken" shows restraint by the <s>prātimokṣa</s> (code of liberation) vow. "Whose conduct is blameless" shows non-failure in conduct. "Who avoids the five places" shows non-failure in domain. The five places that are not the domain of a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) are: the royal court, the slaughterhouse, the tavern, the brothel, and the <s>caṇḍāla</s> (outcaste) settlement. Therein, "slaughterhouse" should be understood as the place of killing — where butchers and others habitually commit the sinful act of slaughtering rams and other [animals].

body.text:
A. IV-2 Ms.2*b1L, MsG.26b6R, P.249a5, D.216a2, N.232b1, Ch.368b4
(19a) anāpattātha vyutthātā niṣkaukṛtyo 'tha kaukṛtī / iti //
body.translated_text:
A. IV-2 Ms.2*b1L, MsG.26b6R, P.249a5, D.216a2, N.232b1, Ch.368b4
(19a) One who has not transgressed, and one who rises [from transgression]; one free from remorse, and one who has remorse.

body.text: aṇumātreṣv avadyeṣu bhayadarśitāṃ darśayati / tatra yathā vyutthātā tathā niṣkaukṛtyaḥ, yathā kaukṛtī tathānāpattā //
body.translated_text: He shows fearful regard for even the slightest faults. Therein, just as one rises [from transgression], so one is free from remorse; and just as one has remorse, so one has not transgressed.

body.text: (19b) śikṣām āgamayet tatra pratipadyeta bhāvataḥ // iti //
body.translated_text: (19b) One should master the training therein and practice it in reality.

body.text: samādāya śikṣate śikṣāpadeṣv iti, etad darśayati //
body.translated_text: This shows that having undertaken [the rules], one trains in the training precepts.

children.text: (20) pratyākhyānaṃ na kurvīta jīvitārthaṃ na nāśayet /
children.translated_text: (20) One should not renounce [the training]; one should not destroy it for the sake of livelihood;

children.text: pratipattau sthito nityaṃ pravṛttavinayo bhavet // iti //
children.translated_text: always established in practice, one should be well-disciplined in conduct.

body.text: anayā gāthayā caturbhiḥ padair yathākramaṃ dhruvaśīlatāṃ dṛḍhaśīlatāṃ sātatakāritāṃ sātatavartitāṃ ca darśayati //
body.translated_text: By this verse, with its four quarters, he shows in order: steadfast morality, firm morality, constant practice, and constant behavior.

body.text:
A. IV-4 Ms.2*b2M, MsG.26b7M, P.249b1, D.216a4, N.232b4, Ch.368b10
(21a) pratijñāṃ śodhayet pūrvam ājīvam api śodhayet / iti /
body.translated_text:
A. IV-4 Ms.2*b2M, MsG.26b7M, P.249b1, D.216a4, N.232b4, Ch.368b10
(21a) One should purify one's commitment, and one should also purify one's livelihood.

body.text: anena gāthārdhena ācārājīvaviśuddhiṃ darśayati / ācārasya hi pratijñāpūrvakam ācaraṇam iti pratijñety ucyate /
body.translated_text: By this half-verse, he shows the purity of conduct and livelihood. For conduct is practiced on the basis of commitment — therefore it is called 'commitment.'

body.text: (21b) antadvayaṃ varjayitvā praṇidhānaṃ vivarjayet // iti //
body.translated_text: (21b) Having avoided the two extremes, one should avoid [wrong] aspiration.

body.text: kāmasukhallikānuyogāntātmaklamathānuyogāntayoḥ svargādipraṇidhānasya ca vivarjanāc chīlaviśuddhim eva darśayati //
body.translated_text: He shows the purity of morality through the avoidance of the two extremes — the extreme of pursuit of sensual pleasure and the extreme of self-mortification — and through the avoidance of aspiration for heaven and the like.

children.translated_text: (22) One should never covet <s>dharmas</s> that create obstacles;
one should not tolerate <s>dharmas</s> that agitate the mind when they arise.

body.text: anayā gāthayā, indriyāguptadvāratādīnāṃ śikṣāviśuddhyantarāyakarāṇām aguṇadarśitvenānadhyavasānāt / akuśalānāṃ ca kāmavyāpādavitarkādīnāṃ manaḥsaṃkṣobhakarāṇām utpannānām anadhivāsanena śikṣāviśuddhiṃ darśayati //
body.translated_text: By this verse: through not pursuing those that create obstacles to the purity of training — such as unguardedness of the sense-doors and the like — by seeing their disadvantages; and through not tolerating unwholesome [states] that agitate the mind — such as thoughts of sensual desire, ill-will, and so forth — when they have arisen, he shows the purity of training.

children.translated_text: (23) Neither too withdrawn nor too forward, always with well-established mindfulness,

children.text: mūlasāmantakaiḥ śuddhaṃ brahmacaryaṃ cared api // iti //
children.translated_text: one should practice the holy life, pure in its root and proximate [precepts].

body.text: mandakaukṛtyāsthānakaukṛtyavivarjanayā smṛtisaṃpramoṣavivarjanayā ca niṣṭhākālaprayogakālayor brahmacaryaśuddhiṃ paridīpayati //
body.translated_text: He illuminates the purity of the holy life at the times of culmination and practice — through avoiding lax remorse and groundless remorse, and through avoiding the loss of mindfulness.

children.translated_text: (24) One should be of aroused energy, always of firm exertion,
and one should cultivate non-negligence, well-established in its five aspects.

body.text: saṃnāhaprayogāvyāvartyavīryatayā pañcavidhāpramādaniṣevaṇatayā ca śikṣāviśuddhiviśeṣam evaṃ darśayati / tatra pañcāṅgo 'pramādo 'tītānāgatapratyutpannapūrvakālakaraṇīyasahānucaraḥ //
body.translated_text: He thus shows the distinction of the purity of training through the unshakeable energy of preparation and application, and through the cultivation of fivefold non-negligence. Therein, fivefold non-negligence is that which accompanies what is to be done in the past, future, present, and earlier times.

children.translated_text: (25) One should be one whose good qualities are concealed, and likewise one whose faults are revealed;

children.text: lūhena vā praṇītena tuṣṭaḥ syāc cīvarādinā //
children.translated_text: one should be content with robes and so forth, whether coarse or fine.

children.text: (26) alpena vartayed yātrāṃ lūhenāpi ca vartayet /
children.translated_text: (26) One should maintain one's livelihood with little, and even with what is coarse;
one should adopt the <s>dhūta</s> (ascetic) qualities for the sake of peace, free from afflictions.

body.text: etābhyāṃ gāthābhyāṃ jñātrakāmatāyā mahecchatāsaṃtuṣṭihetubhūtāyāḥ, tayoś ca mahecchatāsaṃtuṣṭyoḥ śikṣāviśuddhivibandhahetvoḥ parivarjanena śikṣāviśuddhiṃ darśayati //
body.translated_text: By these two verses, he shows the purity of training through the avoidance of desire for fame — which is the cause of great desire and discontent — and through the avoidance of those very great desire and discontent, which are causes of obstruction to the purity of training.

children.translated_text: (27) One should be endowed with proper deportment and should know moderation in accepting;

children.text: tadarthaṃ kalpitām īryāṃ kuryān naiva kathaṃcana // iti //
children.translated_text: one should never engage in deportment contrived for that purpose [of gain].

body.text: īryāpathasaṃpattyā pareṣām akuhanārthayā pratigrahamātrajñatayā ca yāvad brahmacaryavāsāj jīvitasthityupakaraṇopādānāc chikṣāviśuddhim eva darśayati //
body.translated_text: He shows the purity of training through proper deportment — for the purpose of not deceiving others — through knowing moderation in accepting, and through obtaining the means of sustaining life as long as one lives the holy life.

children.text: (28) ātmanaś ca guṇān bhūtān na lapen nāpi lāpayet /
children.translated_text: (28) One should not speak of one's own true virtues, nor have others speak of them;

children.text: tān guṇān atha cārthitvaṃ nimittena na darśayet //
children.translated_text: one should not display those virtues or one's neediness by hints.
(29) One should not make requests from others by causing obstruction;

children.text: dharmaṇopagataṃ lābhaṃ lābheneha na saṃcayet // iti //
children.translated_text: one should not accumulate gain upon gain that has been obtained in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: etābhyāṃ gāthābhyāṃ lapanānaimittikatānaiṣpeśikatālābhenalābhaniścikīrṣukatāparivarjanena śikṣāviśuddhiviśeṣaṃ darśayati //
body.translated_text: By these two verses, he shows the distinction of the purity of training through the avoidance of flattery, hinting, indirect suggestion, and the desire to accumulate gain upon gain.

children.translated_text: (30) One should never covet gain or honor in any way;
one should not cling to views of superimposition or denial.

body.text: lābhasatkārāgṛddhatayā pañcavidhakudṛṣṭyanabhiniveśataś ca viśuddhiviśeṣaṃ darśayati //
body.translated_text: He shows the distinction of purity through non-covetousness regarding gain and honor, and through non-attachment to the five types of wrong views.

children.text: (31) lokāyatāṃs tathā mantrān nirarthān na parāmṛśet /
children.translated_text: (31) One should not engage with <s>lokāyata</s> (materialist texts) and meaningless <s>mantras</s>;

children.text: apārthaṃ dhārayen naiva utsadaṃ pātracīvaram // iti //
children.translated_text: one should never keep excess bowls and robes for no purpose.

body.text: kudṛṣṭihetūnām itobāhyakakuśāstrāṇāṃ pañcopādānaskandhavipratibandhārthena lokāyatakṛtānām aparāmarṣataḥ, lābhasatkāragṛddhihetoś ca utsadapātracīvaradhāraṇasya parivarjanato hetuviśuddhyā śikṣāviśuddhiṃ darśayati //
body.translated_text: He shows the purity of training through not engaging with <s>lokāyata</s> texts — those heterodox texts that are causes of wrong views and that obstruct the five aggregates of clinging — and through the avoidance of keeping excess bowls and robes, which is a cause of covetousness for gain and honor; thus through purity of cause.

children.translated_text: (32) One should not associate intimately with householders, which increases afflictions;

children.text: āryais tu sahasaṃsargaṃ kuryāj jñānaviśodhanam // iti //
children.translated_text: but one should associate with the noble ones, which purifies knowledge.

body.text: vipakṣahetoḥ pratipakṣahetoś ca varjanāt sevanāc ca viśuddhiṃ darśayati //
body.translated_text: He shows purity through avoidance of the cause of the adverse side and through cultivation of the cause of the antidote side.

children.translated_text: (33) One should not make a friend of a family that causes sorrow and disturbance;

children.text: duḥkhasya janakān kleśān utpannān nādhivāsayet // iti //
children.translated_text: one should not tolerate afflictions that generate suffering when they arise.

body.text: yathā gṛhasthaiḥ sahasaṃsargaḥ śokavyākṣepaṃ kṛtvā kleśavivardhano duḥkhahetuḥ, yathā cāryasaṃsargo duḥkhajanakakleśotpannānadhivāsanayā pratipakṣahetuḥ, tad darśayati //
body.translated_text: He shows how intimate association with householders causes sorrow and disturbance, increases afflictions, and is a cause of suffering; and how association with the noble ones, through not tolerating afflictions that generate suffering when they arise, is the cause of the antidote.

children.text: (34) śraddhādeyaṃ na bhuñjīta kathaṃcic ca kṣatavrataḥ /
children.translated_text: (34) One should not consume what is given in faith while having broken vows;

children.text: pratyākhyānaṃ na kurvīta saddharmasya kathaṃcana // iti //
children.translated_text: one should never reject the true <s>Dharma</s> in any way.

body.text: lābhasatkārānabhigṛddheḥ kudṛṣṭyanabhiniveśasya ca śraddhādeyāvinipātanena saddharmāpratikṣepaṇena cāyatyām api kāmādhyavasānakudṛṣṭyutpādahetuparivarjanato viśuddhiviśeṣaṃ darśayati //
body.translated_text: He shows the distinction of purity through non-covetousness regarding gain and honor and through non-attachment to wrong views — by not falling away from what is given in faith and by not rejecting the true <s>Dharma</s> — thus avoiding even in the future the causes for the arising of desire-attachment and wrong views.

children.text: (35) pareṣāṃ skhalite doṣe anābhogaḥ sukhī bhavet /
children.translated_text: (35) Regarding others' stumbling into faults, one should be unconcerned and happy;

children.text: ātmanaḥ skhalitaṃ doṣaṃ jñātvā vivṛṇuyāt punaḥ // iti //
children.translated_text: knowing one's own stumbling into faults, one should reveal them again.

body.text: pareṣāṃ ca doṣadarśanābhogavivarjanena, svakuśalapakṣāvikṣepasaumanasyotpattyā, ātmadoṣaparijñānāviṣkaraṇena ca nirabhimānatayā śikṣāviśuddhiṃ darśayati //
body.translated_text: He shows the purity of training through avoiding the inclination to see others' faults, through the arising of gladness from not being distracted from one's own wholesome side, and through recognizing and disclosing one's own faults — thus through being free from pride.

children.translated_text: (36) And having incurred a transgression, one should remedy it in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>;
in matters requiring one's own effort, one should be skilled and self-reliant.

body.text: āpattivyutthānataḥ parebhyaś copasthānaparicaryāsvīkaraṇakāmatāparivarjanato 'pi viśuddhiṃ darśayati //
body.translated_text: He shows purity through rising from transgressions and through avoiding the desire to have others serve and attend to oneself.

children.text: (37) buddhānāṃ śrāvakāṇāṃ ca anubhāvaṃ ca deśanām /
children.translated_text: (37) The power and teaching of the <s>Buddhas</s> and their <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) —
one who has faith and sees blame [in transgression] should never deny them in any way.

body.text: śraddhāsaṃpattyā abhyākhyāne cāvadyadarśitayā viśuddhiḥ paridīpitā //
body.translated_text: Purity is illuminated through the accomplishment of faith and through seeing blame in denial.

children.translated_text: (38) Regarding <s>dharmas</s> that are very profound and beyond the range of reasoning,

children.text: paurāṇam āgamaṃ tyaktvā svadṛṣṭiṃ na parāmṛśet // iti //
children.translated_text: one should not, abandoning the ancient <s>āgama</s> (tradition), cling to one's own view.

body.text: svayaṃdṛṣṭiparāmarṣasthāyitvaparivarjanato 'pi viśuddhiviśeṣaḥ paridīpitaḥ //
body.translated_text: The distinction of purity is illuminated through the avoidance of persistent clinging to one's own views.

children.translated_text: (39) One should dwell in seclusion, in a bed and seat in a remote place;
one should cultivate wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, with firm energy and exertion.

body.text: kāyacittasya vyavakṛṣṭatayā samādhyanukūlaśayanāsanāsevanatayā akuśalavitarkavarjitaikāntaśukladharmabhāvanayā layauddhatyādyupakleśānabhibhavanīyatvena ca susaṃnaddhaprayogatayādhicittaṃśikṣaṇopāyaviśeṣaṃ darśayati //
body.translated_text: by showing the special method of training in higher mind through the withdrawal of body and mind, through frequenting seats and beds conducive to concentration, through the cultivation of exclusively bright <s>dharmas</s> while avoiding unwholesome thoughts, and through well-girded effort characterized by not being overcome by contaminations such as sinking and restlessness.

children.translated_text: [Manuscript and edition references]
(40) One without desire becomes one in whom desire has arisen; one without hostility becomes one who condemns;

children.text: nirmiddhaś caiva middhīva kāle śānto na ca sthitaḥ //
children.translated_text: free from torpor, one becomes as if torpid; at the [right] time at peace, yet not [firmly] established.
(41) Free from remorse, yet having remorse; free from doubt, yet doubting;

children.text: sarvathā sarvadā yukto bhavet saṃyakprayogavān // iti //
children.translated_text: in every way, at all times, one should be engaged, one who practices correctly.

body.text: ābhyāṃ gāthābhyārh* kāmacchandavyāpādastyānamiddhauddhatyakawkṛtyavicikitsānivaraṇaparivarjanāt kuśaladharmacchandikatayā kāmavidūṣaṇena, kuśalapakṣaprayogakalyatānimittaṃ ca kāle middhaniṣevaṇena, cittaṃ śamayataś ca līyamāne citte tadāśaṅkini vā prasadanīyanimittamanasikārāc chamānavasthitatvena, cāragatasya ca prāg āpattes tadanadhyācārataḥ sakaukṛtyatayā, uttarottaraviśeṣākāṅkṣaṇatayā ca satkṛtyasātatyena ca saṃyakprayuktasya cādhicittaṃśikṣāviśuddhiṃ darśayati //
body.translated_text: By these two verses, one shows the purification of the training in higher mind through: avoiding the hindrances of sensual desire, ill-will, sloth-and-torpor, restlessness-and-remorse, and doubt; through being desirous of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>; through condemning sensual pleasures; through sleeping at the [right] time with the sign of fitness for effort in the wholesome side; through the mental attention of a gladdening sign when one who is calming the mind finds it sinking or suspects sinking, [resulting in] being established in a calm state; through having remorse when one who has been engaged in conduct has, prior to an offense, not committed that transgression; and through continuous and respectful aspiration for ever higher distinction in one who is rightly engaged.

children.translated_text: [Manuscript and edition references]
(42) One who impels, one who awakens, and likewise another who binds;
one who is suggestive, one who fondles, and likewise another who dallies;

children.text: (43) niṣpīḍanaś ca paramaḥ snehanaḥ kalpa ucyate /
children.translated_text: (43) one who presses, and the supreme fondling — this is called the sequence

children.text: kāmarāgasya janakas taṃ budhaḥ parivarjayet // iti //
children.translated_text: that generates desire for sensual pleasure; the wise one should avoid it.

body.text: atrāṣṭavidhasya vikalpasya maithunarāgajanakasyādāv ārabhya krameṇotpadyamānasya yāvan niṣṭhāgamanataḥ parivarjanayā śikṣāviśuddhiviśeṣaḥ paridīpitaḥ /
body.translated_text: Here, the special purification of the training is illuminated through the avoidance of the eightfold conceptualization that generates desire for sexual intercourse, arising gradually from the beginning in sequence, up to its culmination.

body.text: tatra nudano vikalpo yo rañjanīye vastuny ayoniśomanaskārasaṃprayuktaś cittasya prerakaḥ / bodhano yas tasminn eva vastuni prabuddharāgaparyavasthānasaṃprayuktaḥ / (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> II 366

children.text: ) saṃyojanas tasyaiva vastunaḥ paryeṣakaḥ / naimittikas tasminn eva vastuni vicitraśubhanimittagrahakaḥ / snehanaḥ prāpte tasmin vastuny adhyavasānasaṃprayuktaḥ / vilasano yas tasminn eva vastuni vicitraparibhogābhilāṣanānāmukhapravṛttaḥ / niṣpīḍano yo dvayadvayendriyasamāpattikāle / paramasnehano yo 'śucivipramokṣakāle //
children.translated_text: The 'binding' is that which seeks out that very object. The 'suggestive' is that which, toward that very object, grasps at various signs of beauty. The 'fondling' is that which, upon obtaining that object, is connected with resolve. The 'dallying' is that which, toward that very object, proceeds through various modes of desire for enjoyment. The 'pressing' is that at the time of the coming together of the two sense-faculties. The 'supreme fondling' is that at the time of the discharge of impurity.

body.translated_text: Therein, the 'impelling' conceptualization is that which, connected with unwise attention toward a delightful object, impels the mind. The 'awakening' is that which, toward that very object, is connected with the aroused obsessive manifestation of passion.

children.translated_text: [Manuscript and edition references]
(44) Sensual pleasures cause no satisfaction; likewise they are shared by many;
they are causes of <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness); and likewise they increase craving.
(45) They should be avoided by the virtuous; they quickly reach destruction;

children.text: pratyayeṣv āśritāḥ kāmāḥ pramādasya ca bhūmayaḥ // iti //
children.translated_text: sensual pleasures depend on conditions; and they are the grounds of heedlessness.

body.text: aṣṭābhir ākārair dṛṣṭe dharme saṃparāye ca yathāyogaṃ kāmānām ādīnavadarśanena kāmacchandaprahāṇopāyaṃ darśayati //
body.translated_text: By eight modes, showing the danger of sensual pleasures in the present life and in future lives as appropriate, one shows the means of abandoning sensual desire.

children.translated_text: [Manuscript and edition references]
(46) Sensual pleasures are like a skeleton; and likewise comparable to a lump of flesh;
they are like a torch of straw; and likewise comparable to a fire-pit;
(47) they are comparable to a poisonous snake; and likewise comparable to a dream;
they are like borrowed ornaments; and likewise comparable to fruit on a tree.

body.text: (48a) evaṃ kāmān parijñāya nābhigṛdhyet kathaṃcana // iti //
body.translated_text: (48a) Thus, having fully understood sensual pleasures, one should not crave them in any way.

body.text: atra pūrvoktānām aṣṭānām atṛptikaratvādināṃ kāmeṣv ādīnavānām sarvalokasiddhair upamopanyāsair ādīnavatvaṃ darśayati / ye nāmaivaṃ bahuṣv āviṣkṛtādīnavāḥ kathaṃ nāma teṣu paṇḍito gṛdhyed iti saṃdarśanārtham /
body.translated_text: Here, one shows the dangerous nature of the previously stated eight — beginning with causing no satisfaction — among the dangers of sensual pleasures, through similes that are established in the entire world. The purpose is to demonstrate: 'How could a wise person crave those [pleasures] whose dangers have been so extensively revealed?'

body.text: tatrātṛptikarakāḥ karaṅkasadṛṣatvāt / bahusādhāraṇā māṃsapeśyupamatvāt / adharmahetavas tṛṇolkāsādṛśyenātyaktādahanapratyupasthānatayā / tṛṣṇāvivardhanā agnikhadopamatayā tṛṣṇāsaṃjananasādharmyeṇa / (

children.translated_text: <s>Śbh</s> II 368

children.text: ) satāṃ varjanīyā āśīviṣopamatayā / kṣipraṃ vilayagāminaḥ svapnopamatayā / pratyayāśritā yācñālaṃkārasadṛśatayā / pramādabhūmayo vṛkṣāgraphalopamatayā //
children.translated_text: They should be avoided by the virtuous — because they are comparable to a poisonous snake. They quickly reach destruction — because they are comparable to a dream. They depend on conditions — because they are like borrowed ornaments. They are grounds of heedlessness — because they are comparable to fruit at the top of a tree.

body.translated_text: Therein, they cause no satisfaction — because they are like a skeleton. They are shared by many — because they are comparable to a lump of flesh. They are causes of <s>adharma</s> — by similarity to a torch of straw, through the imminent burning that is not relinquished. They increase craving — by comparison to a fire-pit, through the resemblance of generating craving.

children.translated_text: [Manuscript and edition references]

children.text: (48b) saddharmaṃ śṛṇuyān nityaṃ cintayed bhāvayed api /
children.translated_text: (48b) One should always hear the true <s>Dharma</s>, and also reflect upon and cultivate it.
(49) Seeing the peaceful and the sublime first, one should become one exclusively devoted to cultivation;

children.text: vijahya kleśadauṣṭhulyaṃ prahāṇe ca rato bhavet //
children.translated_text: having abandoned the unsuitability of defilements, one should delight in abandonment.
(50) One should be an investigator; regarding the sign, one should become supreme in application;

children.text: kuryāc ca kāmavairāgyaṃ rūpavairāgyam eva ca //
children.translated_text: one should bring about dispassion from sensual desires and also dispassion from form.
(51) One should bring about the realization of the truths and also complete dispassion;

children.text: dṛṣṭe dharme ca nirvāyāt tathā upadhi saṃkṣayāt // iti //
children.translated_text: one should attain <s>nirvāṇa</s> in this very life, and also through the destruction of the substrates.

body.text: atra lakṣaṇapratisaṃvedyādibhiḥ saptabhir manaskārair laukikalokottaramārgaviśuddhyā sopadhinirupadhinirvāṇaphalādhiprajñaṃśikṣāviśuddhiḥ paridīpitā /
body.translated_text: Here, the purification of the training in higher wisdom, through the fruit of the worldly and supramundane path purification by means of the seven mental attentions beginning with the mental attention that perceives characteristics, [leading to] <s>nirvāṇa</s> with and without remainder, is illuminated.

body.text: tatra lakṣaṇapratisaṃvedī saddharmaśravaṇacintanavacanena paridīpitaḥ / adhimokṣiko bhāvanāvacanena / tadadhimuktibhāvanataḥ / śāntaudārikadarśī prāg iti prāvivekyaḥ / bhāvanaikāntiko bhaved iti ratisaṃgrāhakaḥ / mīmāṃsakaḥ syān nimitta iti mīmāṃsāmanaskāraḥ / prayogaparamo bhaved iti prayoganiṣṭhaḥ / kuryāc ca kāmavairāgyaṃ rūpavairāgyam eva ca / satyābhisamayaṃ kuryāt sarvavairāgyam eva ceti laukikalokottaraprayoganiṣṭhāphalaṃ ca //
body.translated_text: Therein, 'perceiving characteristics' is illuminated by the words 'hearing, reflecting on, and [mastering] the true <s>Dharma</s>.' 'Resolving' is illuminated by the word 'cultivation' — from the cultivation of that resolve. 'Seeing the peaceful and the sublime first' is the mental attention of seclusion. 'One should become exclusively devoted to cultivation' is the mental attention of delight. 'One should be an investigator regarding the sign' is the mental attention of investigation. 'One should become supreme in application' is the mental attention of the culmination of practice. 'One should bring about dispassion from sensual desires, dispassion from form, the realization of the truths, and also complete dispassion' — this is the fruit of the worldly and supramundane culmination of practice.

body.text: // ābhiprāyikārthagāthānirdeśaḥ samāptaḥ //
body.translated_text: The exposition of the verses with hidden meaning is complete.
